"""Sparse displayed or latent liquidity can make a given volume surprise coincide with an unusually large price move, but OHLCV data cannot identify whether that excess impact reflects liquidity scarcity, information, news, or temporary withdrawal of liquidity. The factor therefore treats impact elasticity as an empirical conditioning variable rather than a causal estimate and tests whether directionally confirmed, high-volume events with unusually high pre-event impact sensitivity continue over the next six daily bars. Continuation versus reversal, and whether the elasticity term adds value beyond standard volume, close-location, and range signals, are empirical questions rather than assumed implications of dealer inventory behavior."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _percentile_rank_eligible(
    values: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Ascending average-tie percentile ranks on the eligible cross-section."""
    masked = values.where(eligible)
    ranks = masked.rank(axis=1, method="average", ascending=True)
    counts = masked.count(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan)
    denominator = counts - 1.0
    result = ranks.sub(1.0, axis=0).div(denominator, axis=0)
    single_name = counts.eq(1.0)
    if single_name.any():
        result.loc[single_name] = 0.5
    return result.where(eligible)


def _lagged_elasticity_event_components(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute strictly lagged rolling winsorized OLS event statistics.

    At each row t the regression sample is exactly the preceding 60 bars.
    Volume and range medians are themselves shifted by one bar, so neither
    event normalization nor regression inputs use current-bar information.
    """
    previous_close = close.shift(1)
    positive_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
    median_volume = positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=1).median().shift(1)

    valid_return = (
        close.gt(0.0)
        & previous_close.gt(0.0)
        & volume.gt(0.0)
        & median_volume.gt(0.0)
    )
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        log_return = np.log(close / previous_close)
        x = np.log(volume / median_volume)
        y = np.log(np.maximum(log_return.abs(), 0.0001))
    x = x.where(valid_return)
    y = y.where(valid_return)

    valid_range = high.gt(low) & close.gt(0.0)
    range_ratio = ((high - low) / close).where(valid_range)
    median_range = range_ratio.where(range_ratio > 0.0).rolling(
        20, min_periods=1
    ).median().shift(1)

    index = close.index
    columns = close.columns
    n_rows, n_cols = close.shape
    beta_out = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    z_out = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    event_valid_out = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=bool)

    x_values = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    y_values = y.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    close_values = close.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    previous_values = previous_close.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    volume_values = volume.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    median_volume_values = median_volume.to_numpy(dtype=float)

    # Each iteration is vectorized across names; only the causal time origin
    # advances. This preserves the exact per-date winsorization requested.
    for t in range(60, n_rows):
        x_window = x_values[t - 60 : t]
        y_window = y_values[t - 60 : t]
        candidate_valid = np.isfinite(x_window) & np.isfinite(y_window)
        candidate_count = candidate_valid.sum(axis=0)
        usable_columns = np.flatnonzero(candidate_count >= 40)
        if usable_columns.size == 0:
            continue

        x_sample = x_window[:, usable_columns]
        y_sample = y_window[:, usable_columns]
        valid_sample = candidate_valid[:, usable_columns]

        # All retained columns have at least 40 observations, avoiding an
        # all-NaN quantile while retaining missing candidate observations.
        x_low = np.nanquantile(x_sample, 0.05, axis=0)
        x_high = np.nanquantile(x_sample, 0.95, axis=0)
        y_low = np.nanquantile(y_sample, 0.05, axis=0)
        y_high = np.nanquantile(y_sample, 0.95, axis=0)

        x_winsor = np.where(
            valid_sample, np.minimum(np.maximum(x_sample, x_low), x_high), np.nan
        )
        y_winsor = np.where(
            valid_sample, np.minimum(np.maximum(y_sample, y_low), y_high), np.nan
        )

        count = candidate_count[usable_columns].astype(float)
        x_mean = np.nansum(x_winsor, axis=0) / count
        y_mean = np.nansum(y_winsor, axis=0) / count
        x_centered = x_winsor - x_mean
        y_centered = y_winsor - y_mean
        denominator = np.nansum(x_centered * x_centered, axis=0)
        numerator = np.nansum(x_centered * y_centered, axis=0)
        beta = numerator / np.where(denominator > 0.0, denominator, np.nan)
        intercept = y_mean - beta * x_mean

        residuals = y_winsor - intercept - beta * x_winsor
        residual_median = np.nanmedian(residuals, axis=0)
        mad = np.nanmedian(np.abs(residuals - residual_median), axis=0)
        residual_scale = np.maximum(1.4826 * mad, 0.05)

        current_valid = (
            np.isfinite(close_values[t, usable_columns])
            & (close_values[t, usable_columns] > 0.0)
            & np.isfinite(previous_values[t, usable_columns])
            & (previous_values[t, usable_columns] > 0.0)
            & np.isfinite(volume_values[t, usable_columns])
            & (volume_values[t, usable_columns] > 0.0)
            & np.isfinite(median_volume_values[t, usable_columns])
            & (median_volume_values[t, usable_columns] > 0.0)
        )
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            current_x = np.log(
                volume_values[t, usable_columns] / median_volume_values[t, usable_columns]
            )
            current_return = np.log(
                close_values[t, usable_columns] / previous_values[t, usable_columns]
            )
            current_y = np.log(np.maximum(np.abs(current_return), 0.0001))

        current_x = np.minimum(np.maximum(current_x, x_low), x_high)
        current_y = np.minimum(np.maximum(current_y, y_low), y_high)
        z_score = (current_y - intercept - beta * current_x) / residual_scale
        z_score = np.clip(z_score, -5.0, 5.0)

        beta_out[t, usable_columns] = beta
        z_out[t, usable_columns] = z_score
        event_valid_out[t, usable_columns] = current_valid & np.isfinite(beta) & np.isfinite(z_score)

    beta_frame = pd.DataFrame(beta_out, index=index, columns=columns)
    z_frame = pd.DataFrame(z_out, index=index, columns=columns)
    event_valid_frame = pd.DataFrame(event_valid_out, index=index, columns=columns)
    return beta_frame, z_frame, x, range_ratio, median_range, event_valid_frame


@register_factor
class NonlinearImpactElasticityVolumeSurprise(BaseFactor):
    """Lagged OHLC impact elasticity conditioned on confirmed volume surprises."""

    factor_id = "nonlinear_impact_elasticity_volume_surprise"
    name = "Lagged OHLC Impact Elasticity Event"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Directional volume-surprise events weighted by a strictly lagged, "
        "winsorized OHLC impact-elasticity regression and excess-impact residual."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        beta, z_score, volume_surprise, range_ratio, median_range, event_valid = (
            _lagged_elasticity_event_components(close, high, low, volume)
        )

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            log_return = np.log(close / previous_close)
        direction = np.sign(log_return).where(log_return.notna(), 0.0)

        valid_range = high.gt(low) & close.gt(0.0)
        close_location = (2.0 * (close - low) / (high - low) - 1.0).where(valid_range)
        confirmation = (direction * close_location).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)

        range_median_valid = median_range.gt(0.0) & range_ratio.gt(0.0)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            relative_range = range_ratio / median_range
        range_gate = relative_range.ge(0.5) & relative_range.le(3.0)

        eligible = (
            event_valid
            & beta.gt(0.0)
            & valid_range
            & range_median_valid
            & volume_surprise.notna()
            & z_score.notna()
        )

        beta_rank = _percentile_rank_eligible(beta, eligible)
        z_rank = _percentile_rank_eligible(z_score, eligible)
        volume_rank = _percentile_rank_eligible(volume_surprise.clip(-3.0, 3.0), eligible)

        score = direction * range_gate.astype(float) * (
            0.35 * beta_rank + 0.35 * z_rank + 0.20 * volume_rank + 0.10 * confirmation
        )
        return score.where(eligible, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Lagged OHLC Impact Elasticity Event
programs.trading_idea: Sparse displayed or latent liquidity can make a given volume surprise coincide with an unusually large price move, but OHLCV data cannot identify whether that excess impact reflects liquidity scarcity, information, news, or temporary withdrawal of liquidity. The factor therefore treats impact elasticity as an empirical conditioning variable rather than a causal estimate and tests whether directionally confirmed, high-volume events with unusually high pre-event impact sensitivity continue over the next six daily bars. Continuation versus reversal, and whether the elasticity term adds value beyond standard volume, close-location, and range signals, are empirical questions rather than assumed implications of dealer inventory behavior.
programs.description: All quantities at date t are computed from completed daily bars; no current-bar observation enters the pre-event regression, its volume benchmarks, or its residual scale. Define r_i = ln(close_i / close_{i-1}). For every i, define mV_i as the median positive volume over bars i-20 through i-1, and x_i = ln(volume_i / mV_i). Define y_i = ln(max(abs(r_i), 0.0001)). To estimate the pre-event elasticity at t, use candidate bars i = t-60,...,t-1 only, retaining observations with positive close_i, positive close_{i-1}, positive volume_i, and positive mV_i. Require at least 40 valid candidate observations. Winsorize x_i and y_i separately to their candidate-sample 5th and 95th percentiles, then estimate the ordinary-least-squares regression y_i^W = a_t + b_t x_i^W + e_i; b_t is the strictly lagged OHLC impact-elasticity estimate. Define the pre-event residual scale s_t = max(1.4826 * median_i(abs(e_i - median_j(e_j))), 0.05). For the current event, require positive close_t, close_{t-1}, volume_t, and mV_t; form x_t and y_t using the same definitions and clip each to the corresponding pre-event winsor limits. The standardized excess-impact residual is z_t = (y_t^W - a_t - b_t*x_t^W) / s_t, clipped to [-5,5]. Define volume surprise v_t = clip(x_t, -3, 3). Define the directional OHLC proxy d_t = sign(r_t), with d_t = 0 when r_t = 0; this is explicitly a price-direction proxy, not observed signed order flow. For a valid nonzero daily range high_t > low_t, define close-location q_t = 2*(close_t-low_t)/(high_t-low_t)-1 and directional confirmation g_t = max(0, d_t*q_t). Define range ratio h_t = (high_t-low_t)/close_t and mH_t as the median positive h over t-20,...,t-1; require positive mH_t and set the range-quality gate I_t = 1 when 0.5 <= h_t/mH_t <= 3.0, otherwise 0. Names with invalid or zero volume, price, range, required medians, fewer than 40 regression observations, or nonpositive b_t are ineligible. Among eligible names each date, let R_t(.) denote ascending cross-sectional percentile rank, mapped to [0,1], with average ranks for ties. The final signed score is S_t = d_t * I_t * [0.35*R_t(b_t) + 0.35*R_t(z_t) + 0.20*R_t(v_t) + 0.10*g_t]. Positive scores are long candidates and negative scores are short candidates. At the close of t, compute S_t; rebalance at the next daily-bar open into equal-weight top and bottom deciles of eligible names, dollar-neutral where both sides contain sufficient names, and hold each daily vintage for six bars with overlapping vintages. The factor must be evaluated against fixed ablations using the same event eligibility and rebalance timing: abnormal-volume only S_volume = d_t*R_t(v_t); close-location only S_close = d_t*g_t; and range/volatility only S_range = d_t*I_t*R_t(h_t/mH_t). Incremental efficacy requires the full score to outperform these ablations after the harness applies conservative executable-cost assumptions; the available fields do not contain spreads, quotes, or realized execution costs, so the factor itself makes no claim of cost-adjusted profitability.

programs.code:
"""The signal targets short-lived common price-pressure episodes rather than attempting to infer a specific ETF, dealer, or rebalancing counterparty. A sector-wide volume-participation surge followed by an immediately observable collapse in participation, while return commonality remains elevated rather than releasing, is interpreted as exhaustion of urgent basket-like trading demand. The payoff is a narrowly defined cross-sectional reversal within the affected sector: recent residual losers are bought and residual leaders are shorted after the participation shock has already cooled."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_labels(sector: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Return static sector-to-column-position mapping, ignoring unlabeled names."""
    groups: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
    for column_number, column in enumerate(sector.columns):
        observed = sector.iloc[:, column_number].dropna()
        if not observed.empty:
            # Sector is documented as static, so its first observed label is safe.
            label = str(observed.iloc[0])
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(column_number)
    return {
        label: np.asarray(positions, dtype=int)
        for label, positions in groups.items()
    }


def _observable_basket_flow_signal(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Construct causal, sector-neutral six-bar basket-flow exhaustion sleeves."""
    positive_bar = (close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0)
    dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(positive_bar)

    # The 18-observation minimum respects the explicit eligible-universe rule
    # while never treating a missing or nonpositive bar as a valid observation.
    valid_count = positive_bar.astype(float).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
    adv20 = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=18).mean()
    eligible = (valid_count >= 18.0) & (adv20 >= 5_000_000.0)

    # Current dollar participation relative to the trailing, strictly prior
    # twenty bars.  A median based on fewer than 18 valid observations is not
    # considered observable enough to define a participation shock.
    prior_median = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=18).median()
    q = dollar_volume / prior_median.where(prior_median > 0.0)

    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    ret = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0
    ret3 = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()

    group_positions = _sector_labels(sector)
    n_rows, n_columns = close.shape
    output = np.zeros((n_rows, n_columns), dtype=float)

    eligible_array = eligible.to_numpy(dtype=bool)
    q_array = q.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    ret3_array = ret3.to_numpy(dtype=float)

    previous_b: dict[str, float] = {label: np.nan for label in group_positions}
    previous_c: dict[str, float] = {label: np.nan for label in group_positions}

    # Each item is (sector, final formation-row index, long columns, short columns).
    # A sleeve formed after close t is represented from row t through t+5; a
    # next-open execution engine consequently holds it for exactly six bars.
    active: list[tuple[str, int, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]] = []

    for row in range(n_rows):
        active = [sleeve for sleeve in active if sleeve[1] >= row]
        occupied_sectors = {sleeve[0] for sleeve in active}

        current_b: dict[str, float] = {}
        current_c: dict[str, float] = {}
        current_members: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

        for label, sector_columns in group_positions.items():
            members = sector_columns[eligible_array[row, sector_columns]]
            if members.size < 15:
                continue

            # Invalid q observations are excluded rather than forward-filled.
            q_values = q_array[row, members]
            q_valid = np.isfinite(q_values)
            q_members = members[q_valid]
            if q_members.size < 15:
                continue
            current_b[label] = float(np.mean(q_array[row, q_members] >= 1.5))

            # Pairwise complete 10-bar correlations among eligible members.
            # A pair is valid only when all ten return observations are present;
            # constant-return pairs naturally produce NaN and are excluded.
            correlation_window = ret.iloc[row - 9 : row + 1, members] if row >= 9 else None
            if correlation_window is None or correlation_window.shape[0] != 10:
                continue
            corr = correlation_window.corr(min_periods=10).to_numpy(dtype=float)
            upper = np.triu(np.ones((members.size, members.size), dtype=bool), k=1)
            pair_values = corr[upper]
            valid_pairs = pair_values[np.isfinite(pair_values)]
            possible_pairs = members.size * (members.size - 1) // 2
            required_pairs = int(np.ceil(0.80 * possible_pairs))
            if valid_pairs.size < required_pairs:
                continue

            current_c[label] = float(np.mean(valid_pairs))
            current_members[label] = members

        # The correlation quintile is evaluated only across sectors that have
        # both an eligible membership and sufficiently observed correlations.
        if current_c:
            c_rank = pd.Series(current_c, dtype=float).rank(pct=True)
            high_commonality = {
                label for label, value in c_rank.items() if value >= 0.80
            }
        else:
            high_commonality = set()

        for label in high_commonality:
            if label in occupied_sectors:
                continue
            if label not in current_b or label not in current_members:
                continue

            b_now = current_b[label]
            b_previous = previous_b.get(label, np.nan)
            c_now = current_c[label]
            c_previous = previous_c.get(label, np.nan)
            cooling = (
                np.isfinite(b_previous)
                and b_previous >= 0.60
                and b_now <= 0.35
                and b_now <= b_previous - 0.20
            )
            commonality_persistent = (
                np.isfinite(c_previous) and c_now >= c_previous - 0.01
            )
            if not (cooling and commonality_persistent):
                continue

            members = current_members[label]
            three_bar = ret3_array[row, members]
            valid_return = np.isfinite(three_bar)
            candidates = members[valid_return]
            candidate_returns = three_bar[valid_return]
            if candidates.size < 15:
                continue

            sector_mean = float(np.mean(candidate_returns))
            residual = candidate_returns - sector_mean
            side_size = candidates.size // 5
            if side_size < 3:
                continue

            order = np.argsort(residual, kind="mergesort")
            longs = candidates[order[:side_size]]
            shorts = candidates[order[-side_size:]]
            if longs.size < 3 or shorts.size < 3:
                continue

            active.append((label, row + 5, longs, shorts))
            occupied_sectors.add(label)

        # Update state only after all current-t entry tests have used t-1 state.
        for label in group_positions:
            previous_b[label] = current_b.get(label, np.nan)
            previous_c[label] = current_c.get(label, np.nan)

        # Equal gross allocation across simultaneously active sector sleeves;
        # every sleeve has equal long and short dollar exposure.
        if active:
            sleeve_scale = 1.0 / len(active)
            for _, _, longs, shorts in active:
                output[row, longs] += 0.5 * sleeve_scale / longs.size
                output[row, shorts] -= 0.5 * sleeve_scale / shorts.size

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    """Sector-neutral reversal after correlated basket-flow participation cools."""

programs.name: Observable Basket-Flow Exhaustion
programs.trading_idea: The signal targets short-lived common price-pressure episodes rather than attempting to infer a specific ETF, dealer, or rebalancing counterparty. A sector-wide volume-participation surge followed by an immediately observable collapse in participation, while return commonality remains elevated rather than releasing, is interpreted as exhaustion of urgent basket-like trading demand. The payoff is a narrowly defined cross-sectional reversal within the affected sector: recent residual losers are bought and residual leaders are shorted after the participation shock has already cooled.
programs.description: At each close t, form the eligible universe using only listed fields: a stock must have positive close and volume on at least 18 of the preceding 20 bars and 20-bar average dollar volume, mean(close*volume over t-19 through t), of at least USD 5m. Short candidates additionally require USD 10m 20-bar average dollar volume as an in-scope liquidity/borrow-capacity proxy; actual stock-loan availability is not observable in this feed and must be confirmed by execution outside the factor calculation. A sector is eligible only if it contains at least 15 such stocks. Define daily return r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. For each eligible sector, compute C_s,t as the mean of all available pairwise 10-bar Pearson correlations of constituent daily returns over t-9 through t; require at least 80% of the sector's possible pairs to have valid correlations. Define each stock's volume shock q_i,t = (close_i,t*volume_i,t) / median(close_i,t-k*volume_i,t-k, k=1,...,20), with invalid or nonpositive denominators excluded. Sector participation B_s,t is the fraction of eligible constituents with q_i,t >= 1.5. A sector enters the exhaustion state at t only when all conditions are known at t: (1) B_s,t-1 >= 0.60, showing broad participation on the preceding bar; (2) B_s,t <= 0.35 and B_s,t <= B_s,t-1 - 0.20, an observable one-bar cooling event; (3) C_s,t is in the cross-sector top quintile among eligible sectors at t; and (4) C_s,t >= C_s,t-1 - 0.01, so correlation has not materially released. Condition (4) makes this explicitly non-overlapping with a correlation-release trade: this factor cannot enter after a meaningful decline in commonality and does not use a correlation-release/repricing state. For every entering sector, calculate trailing 3-bar sector-relative return a_i,t = sum(r_i,t-2:t) minus the equal-weighted sector mean of sum(r_j,t-2:t), using only eligible constituents. Rank a_i,t within the sector at formation. Buy the bottom quintile of residual returns and short the top quintile, requiring at least three names on each side; use equal weights within each side. Each active sector receives equal gross exposure, with equal long and short dollar exposure, so every sector sleeve is dollar neutral and the aggregate portfolio is sector neutral. Signals are formed after the close t, entered at the next bar's open, and held for exactly 6 daily bars before exit; do not open another sleeve in the same sector while its prior 6-bar sleeve remains active. Missing prices, volumes, correlations, or insufficient sector membership invalidate that stock or sector rather than being forward-filled. The factor uses no fundamental quality or valuation overlay, avoiding the prior factor's fundamental-dispersion payoff construction; turnover cooling is the indispensable, independently measured entry condition.

"""Sector-shock-conditioned repair of high-elasticity residual moves.

Mechanism: synchronized peer moves establish a common shock state.  A large
beta-adjusted residual with unusually high return-per-volume impact is treated
as transient liquidity depletion, so the factor fades that residual rather
than extrapolating its direction.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Return one static group label per column without changing panel shape."""
    filled = frame.ffill().bfill()
    if filled.empty:
        return pd.Series(index=frame.columns, dtype=object)
    return filled.iloc[0]


def _sector_elasticity_repair(ret: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal leave-one-out shock, beta-residual, and impact-surprise score."""
    valid = ret.notna()
    count = valid.astype(float).sum(axis=1)
    total = ret.sum(axis=1, skipna=True)
    total_abs = ret.abs().sum(axis=1, skipna=True)

    peer_count = valid.astype(float).rsub(count, axis=0)
    peer_sum = ret.rsub(total, axis=0)
    peer_abs = ret.abs().rsub(total_abs, axis=0)
    peer = (peer_sum / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(peer_count >= 7.0)

    paired = ret.notna() & peer.notna()
    x_ret = ret.where(paired)
    y_peer = peer.where(paired)
    n = paired.astype(float).rolling(60, min_periods=40).sum().shift(1)
    mean_x = x_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean().shift(1)
    mean_y = y_peer.rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean().shift(1)
    mean_xy = (x_ret * y_peer).rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean().shift(1)
    mean_y2 = (y_peer * y_peer).rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean().shift(1)
    cov_xy = mean_xy - mean_x * mean_y
    var_y = mean_y2 - mean_y * mean_y
    beta = (cov_xy / var_y.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(n >= 40.0).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

    residual = ret - beta * peer
    residual_sigma = residual.rolling(60, min_periods=40).std().shift(1)
    residual_z = (residual / residual_sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

    prior_peer_std = peer.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
    shock_size = (peer.abs() / prior_peer_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 4.0)
    coherence = (peer_sum.abs() / peer_abs.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    agree = ret.mul(np.sign(peer)).gt(0.0).astype(float)
    own_agree = agree
    peer_agree = own_agree.rsub(agree.sum(axis=1), axis=0)
    breadth = (peer_agree / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    shock_gate = breadth * coherence * (shock_size / 3.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    positive_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
    prior_volume = positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).median().shift(1)
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        volume_surprise = np.log(volume / prior_volume)
        impact_y = np.log(ret.abs().clip(lower=0.0001))
    volume_surprise = volume_surprise.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    impact_y = impact_y.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    impact_valid = volume_surprise.notna() & impact_y.notna()
    vx = volume_surprise.where(impact_valid)
    iy = impact_y.where(impact_valid)
    ix_mean = vx.rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean().shift(1)
    iy_mean = iy.rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean().shift(1)
    ix_var = (vx * vx).rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean().shift(1) - ix_mean * ix_mean
    ixiy_cov = (vx * iy).rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean().shift(1) - ix_mean * iy_mean
    impact_beta = (ixiy_cov / ix_var.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
    impact_fit = iy_mean + impact_beta * (volume_surprise - ix_mean)
    impact_error = impact_y - impact_fit
    impact_scale = impact_error.rolling(60, min_periods=40).std().shift(1)
    impact_z = (impact_error / impact_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

    elastic_gate = (impact_z / 3.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    participation_gate = (volume_surprise / 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    score = -residual_z * shock_gate * elastic_gate * participation_gate
    return score.where(peer_count >= 7.0)


@register_factor
class SectorShockElasticityResidualRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sector_shock_elasticity_residual_repair"
    name = "Sector Shock Elasticity Residual Repair"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Fades standardized sector-beta residuals only during coherent peer shocks "
        "when the residual is accompanied by elevated participation and excess "
        "return-per-volume impact."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        labels = _static_labels(data["sector"])
        ret = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns, dtype=float)

        for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
            columns = labels.index[labels == label]
            if len(columns) < 8:
                continue
            raw = _sector_elasticity_repair(ret.loc[:, columns], volume.loc[:, columns])
            eligible = raw.notna().sum(axis=1) >= 8
            ranked = raw.where(eligible, np.nan).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
            mapped = 2.0 * ranked - 1.0
            mapped = mapped.sub(mapped.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
            output.loc[:, columns] = mapped.fillna(0.0)

        return output.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Sector Shock Elasticity Residual Repair
programs.trading_idea: A coherent sector shock supplies a common-price-discovery state in which a stock's beta-adjusted residual is more likely to reflect temporary dislocation than a distinct fundamental repricing. Within that state, a large residual accompanied by unusually high volume and excess return-per-volume impact identifies liquidity being consumed disproportionately in the outlying name; the realized negative direction of Parent A is consistent with an exhausted liquidity vacuum rather than durable information. The interaction has edge because Parent B identifies synchronized peer-shock repair but intentionally excludes high-participation names, while Parent A detects fragile impact events without determining whether the move is idiosyncratic or embedded in a common shock.
programs.description: Computes a lagged sector-beta residual during broad, sign-coherent leave-one-out sector shocks, then fades residuals only when the name has both elevated volume and an unusually large return magnitude relative to its own trailing volume-impact relationship. Scores are ranked and demeaned within sector.

programs.code:
"""A large, synchronized sector move can temporarily compress cross-sectional price formation, leaving some names with unusually large deviations from their pre-existing sector-return relationship. This construction does not claim to identify ETF or basket flow uniquely; instead, it tests whether residual moves made during coherent peer shocks, without elevated single-name trading participation, are more likely to mean-revert than residual moves occurring in ordinary conditions. It should be evaluated as an incremental, cost-adjusted sector-beta-residual reversal signal relative to standard industry-neutral reversal and existing peer-shock factors."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_rolling_sum(frame: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing sum through t-1, with missing observations excluded."""
    return frame.rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum().shift(1)


def _prior_rolling_count(frame: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing valid-observation count through t-1."""
    return frame.notna().astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=1).sum().shift(1)


def _sector_residual_score(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute the causal leave-one-out peer-shock reversal score for one sector."""
    valid_ret = ret.notna()
    valid_float = valid_ret.astype(float)

    sector_count = valid_float.sum(axis=1)
    sector_sum = ret.sum(axis=1, skipna=True)
    sector_abs_sum = ret.abs().sum(axis=1, skipna=True)

    peer_count = valid_float.rsub(sector_count, axis=0)
    peer_sum = ret.rsub(sector_sum, axis=0)
    peer_abs_sum = ret.abs().rsub(sector_abs_sum, axis=0)

    # The leave-one-out benchmark is intentionally unavailable without seven
    # contemporaneously valid peers.
    peer_return = (peer_sum / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(peer_count >= 7.0)

    paired = ret.notna() & peer_return.notna()
    paired_float = paired.astype(float)
    x = ret.where(paired)
    y = peer_return.where(paired)

    n_obs = _prior_rolling_sum(paired_float, 60)
    sum_x = _prior_rolling_sum(x, 60)
    sum_y = _prior_rolling_sum(y, 60)
    sum_xy = _prior_rolling_sum(x * y, 60)
    sum_y2 = _prior_rolling_sum(y * y, 60)
    sum_x2 = _prior_rolling_sum(x * x, 60)

    safe_n = n_obs.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    centered_xy = sum_xy - (sum_x * sum_y / safe_n)
    centered_y2 = sum_y2 - (sum_y * sum_y / safe_n)
    beta = (centered_xy / centered_y2.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
        (n_obs >= 40.0) & (centered_y2 > 0.0)
    ).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

    # Residual volatility is computed over the same historical paired sample,
    # using the date-t beta against each prior sector return.
    residual_sum = sum_x - beta * sum_y
    residual_sq_sum = sum_x2 - 2.0 * beta * sum_xy + beta * beta * sum_y2
    residual_ss = residual_sq_sum - (residual_sum * residual_sum / safe_n)
    sigma = np.sqrt(
        (residual_ss / (n_obs - 1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
            (n_obs >= 40.0) & (residual_ss > 0.0)
        )
    )

    current_residual = ret - beta * peer_return
    z_residual = (current_residual / sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

    # Breadth uses the count of peer returns agreeing with the sign of each
    # name's own leave-one-out benchmark.  Separate sign counts avoid any
    # accidental inclusion of the stock itself.
    positive_count = (ret > 0.0).sum(axis=1)
    negative_count = (ret < 0.0).sum(axis=1)
    zero_count = ((ret == 0.0) & valid_ret).sum(axis=1)

    own_positive = (ret > 0.0).astype(float)
    own_negative = (ret < 0.0).astype(float)
    own_zero = ((ret == 0.0) & valid_ret).astype(float)
    peer_positive = own_positive.rsub(positive_count, axis=0)
    peer_negative = own_negative.rsub(negative_count, axis=0)
    peer_zero = own_zero.rsub(zero_count, axis=0)

    benchmark_sign = np.sign(peer_return)
    agreeing_peers = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(
            benchmark_sign.to_numpy() > 0.0,
            peer_positive.to_numpy(),
            np.where(
                benchmark_sign.to_numpy() < 0.0,
                peer_negative.to_numpy(),
                peer_zero.to_numpy(),
            ),
        ),
        index=ret.index,
        columns=ret.columns,
    )
    breadth = (agreeing_peers / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(peer_count >= 7.0)

    coherence = (peer_sum.abs() / peer_abs_sum.replace(0.0, np.nan)).fillna(0.0)

    prior_sector_count = _prior_rolling_count(peer_return, 20)
    prior_sector_std = peer_return.rolling(20, min_periods=1).std().shift(1)
    shock_z = (peer_return.abs() / prior_sector_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
        (prior_sector_count >= 15.0) & (prior_sector_std > 0.0)
    )
    shock_scale = breadth * coherence.clip(0.0, 1.0) * (shock_z / 3.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    positive_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
    prior_volume_count = _prior_rolling_count(positive_volume, 20)
    prior_volume_mean = positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=1).mean().shift(1)
    relative_volume = (volume / prior_volume_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
        prior_volume_count >= 15.0
    )
    low_volume_scale = (2.0 - relative_volume).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    return -z_residual * shock_scale * low_volume_scale


def _static_sector_labels(sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Extract one static sector label per ticker without changing panel shape."""
    labels = sector.ffill().bfill()
    if labels.empty:
        return pd.Series(index=sector.columns, dtype=object)
    return labels.iloc[0]


@register_factor
class CommonShockBetaOvershootRepair(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-neutral reversal of low-participation residual overshoots during coherent peer shocks."""

    factor_id = "common_shock_beta_overshoot_repair"
    name = "Synchronized Sector Residual Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Ranks negative standardized stock-sector residuals within sectors only "
        "when a broad coherent leave-one-out sector shock occurs and the stock's "
        "own trading volume is below its recent norm."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        ret = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        labels = _static_sector_labels(sector)
        output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns, dtype=float)

        for sector_name in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
            columns = labels.index[labels == sector_name]
            if len(columns) < 8:
                continue

            raw = _sector_residual_score(ret.loc[:, columns], volume.loc[:, columns])
            eligible_count = raw.notna().sum(axis=1)
            raw = raw.where(eligible_count >= 8, np.nan)

            percentile = raw.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True)
            mapped = 2.0 * percentile - 1.0
            mapped = mapped.sub(mapped.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
            output.loc[:, columns] = mapped

        return output

"""The revised mechanism does not interpret elevated pre-report volatility as evidence that a public estimate revision contains superior private information. Instead, idiosyncratic range-variance acceleration is treated as a price-discovery and adverse-selection warning: when a stock has already experienced unusually rapid volatility acceleration relative to its sector, the information motivating a subsequent consensus change may already be reflected in price and implementation costs are likely elevated. The factor therefore seeks late-quarter estimate revisions only where sector-adjusted variance acceleration is subdued, consistent with slower diffusion of public analyst information into constrained institutional portfolios over the subsequent six sessions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _report_age(reset: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return bars elapsed since the latest point-in-time report reset."""
    n_rows, n_cols = reset.shape
    positions = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(np.arange(n_rows, dtype=float)[:, None], (n_rows, n_cols)),
        index=reset.index,
        columns=reset.columns,
    )
    latest_reset = positions.where(reset).ffill()
    return positions - latest_reset


def _finite_change_reset(actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify actual-value updates relative to the preceding available value."""
    prior_available = actual.ffill().shift(1)
    current_valid = actual.notna() & ~actual.isin([np.inf, -np.inf])
    prior_valid = prior_available.notna() & ~prior_available.isin([np.inf, -np.inf])
    return current_valid & prior_valid & actual.ne(prior_available)


def _normalized_revision(
    estimate: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    lag: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute a lagged estimate revision with a causal cross-sectional floor."""
    prior = estimate.shift(lag)
    valid = (
        eligible
        & estimate.notna()
        & prior.notna()
        & ~estimate.isin([np.inf, -np.inf])
        & ~prior.isin([np.inf, -np.inf])
    )
    prior_abs = prior.abs().where(valid)
    cross_sectional_floor = 0.01 * prior_abs.median(axis=1)
    denominator = prior.abs().where(
        prior.abs().ge(cross_sectional_floor, axis=0),
        cross_sectional_floor,
        axis=0,
    ).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    revision = ((estimate - prior) / denominator).where(valid)
    return revision.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _sector_acceleration_zscore(
    q: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Calculate sector robust z-scores, falling back to the eligible universe."""
    q_valid = q.where(eligible)
    universe_median = q_valid.median(axis=1)
    universe_mad = q_valid.sub(universe_median, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1)

    labels = sector.ffill().iloc[-1].astype(object)
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "__UNKNOWN_SECTOR__")
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=q.index, columns=q.columns, dtype=float)

    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        group_q = q_valid.loc[:, members]
        group_count = group_q.notna().sum(axis=1)
        group_median = group_q.median(axis=1)
        group_mad = group_q.sub(group_median, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1)
        use_group = group_count.ge(5)
        location = group_median.where(use_group, universe_median)
        dispersion = group_mad.where(use_group, universe_mad)
        output.loc[:, members] = group_q.sub(location, axis=0).div(
            1.4826 * dispersion + 1e-12,
            axis=0,
        )

    return output.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class ReportClockVarianceAccelerationRevision(BaseFactor):
    """Late-quarter revisions screened for sector-relative range-variance acceleration."""

    factor_id = "report_clock_variance_acceleration_revision"
    name = "Late-Clock Revision Diffusion with Variance-Completion Screen"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks late-quarter EPS and revenue consensus revisions, then attenuates "
        "them when Parkinson range variance has accelerated unusually rapidly "
        "relative to the stock's sector."
    )
    window_length = 90
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "sector",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        if close.empty:
            return close.astype(float)

        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]

        reset = _finite_change_reset(eps_actual) | _finite_change_reset(revenue_actual)
        age = _report_age(reset)
        eligible = age.ge(35) & age.le(65)

        eps_revision = _normalized_revision(eps_estimate, eligible, 21)
        revenue_revision = _normalized_revision(revenue_estimate, eligible, 21)

        eps_score = 2.0 * eps_revision.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        revenue_score = 2.0 * revenue_revision.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        revision_score = 0.60 * eps_score + 0.40 * revenue_score

        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        valid_range = high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0)
        range_ratio = high.where(valid_range) / low.where(valid_range)
        range_variance = np.log(range_ratio).pow(2) / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))

        short_variance = range_variance.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        long_variance = range_variance.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        acceleration = np.log((short_variance + 1e-12) / (long_variance + 1e-12))
        acceleration = acceleration.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        zscore = _sector_acceleration_zscore(acceleration, eligible, data["sector"])
        attenuation = zscore.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0) / 2.0
        signal = revision_score * (1.0 - attenuation)

        valid_signal = eligible & revision_score.notna() & zscore.notna()
        return signal.where(valid_signal, 0.0).fillna(0.0).reindex(
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

programs.description: At each close t, reset the reporting clock to age 0 whenever either epsActual or revenueActual is finite and differs from its immediately preceding available daily value; if both update on the same date, this is one reset with no field priority required. Report age is the number of daily bars since the most recent reset, and names are eligible only for ages 35 through 65 inclusive. Compute 21-bar estimate changes for both epsEstimate and revenueEstimate as (x_t - x_t-21) / max(abs(x_t-21), 0.01 times the cross-sectional median of abs(x_t-21) among valid names); require both estimates to be valid at t and t-21. Convert each normalized change to its same-date cross-sectional percentile rank among eligible names, map each rank to [-1,1], and define the signed revision score as 0.60 times the EPS score plus 0.40 times the revenue score. For volatility, define daily Parkinson range variance v_t = ln(high_t/low_t)^2 / (4 ln(2)), requiring positive high and low. Define q_i,t = ln((mean(v_i,t-4:t) + 1e-12) / (mean(v_i,t-19:t) + 1e-12)). Within each sector on each date, subtract the sector median q and divide by 1.4826 times the sector median absolute deviation plus 1e-12; if a sector has fewer than five valid names, use the full eligible-universe median and MAD instead. Let a_i,t = min(max(z_i,t, 0), 2) / 2, where z is this sector-adjusted acceleration score. The final factor is revision_score_i,t times (1 - a_i,t): positive revisions with low idiosyncratic acceleration are long signals and negative revisions with low acceleration are short signals, while high-acceleration names are continuously downweighted rather than treated as stronger information signals. Signals use only data available by the close of t and are executed at the next session's open; performance is measured over the fixed subsequent six daily bars.

"""Revision-conditioned unfinished peer-shock transmission."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _labels(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    if frame.empty:
        return pd.Series(index=frame.columns, dtype=object)
    return frame.ffill().bfill().iloc[0].reindex(frame.columns)


def _loo_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns, dtype=float)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels == label]
        if len(cols) <= minimum:
            continue
        group = values.loc[:, cols]
        valid = group.notna().astype(float)
        total = group.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        peer_total = group.fillna(0.0).rsub(total, axis=0)
        peer_count = valid.rsub(count, axis=0)
        output.loc[:, cols] = peer_total.div(peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(peer_count >= minimum)
    return output


@register_factor
class RevisionConditionedPeerShockReceiverGap(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "revision_conditioned_peer_shock_receiver_gap"
    name = "Revision-Conditioned Peer Shock Receiver Gap"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Fundamental revisions select unfinished beta-adjusted peer-shock "
        "catch-up gaps, using volume-confirmed industry cascade intensity as "
        "the information-transmission state."
    )
    window_length = 70
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry", "epsEstimate"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry = _labels(data["industry"])
        estimate = data["epsEstimate"]

        ret = np.log(close.where(close.gt(0.0)).div(close.shift(1).where(close.shift(1).gt(0.0))))
        peer_ret = _loo_mean(ret, industry, 5)

        beta = ret.rolling(60, min_periods=35).cov(peer_ret).div(
            peer_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=35).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).shift(1).clip(-2.5, 2.5)

        own_three = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        peer_three = peer_ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        expected_three = beta * peer_three
        receiver_gap = expected_three - own_three

        prior_estimate = estimate.shift(21)
        revision = estimate.sub(prior_estimate).div(prior_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        revision = revision.clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        revision_rank = 2.0 * revision.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume.gt(0.0)))
        volume_mean = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean().shift(1)
        volume_std = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
        volume_z = log_volume.sub(volume_mean).div(volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        abnormal = ret - beta * peer_ret
        abnormal_std = abnormal.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
        abnormal_z = abnormal.div(abnormal_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        event = (
            np.sign(abnormal) * abnormal_z.abs().clip(upper=3.0)
        ).where(volume_z.ge(0.5), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        peer_event = _loo_mean(event.ewm(alpha=0.25, adjust=False).mean(), industry, 5)
        peer_abs_event = _loo_mean(event.abs().ewm(alpha=0.25, adjust=False).mean(), industry, 5)
        coherence = peer_event.abs().div(peer_abs_event.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        aligned_cascade = (np.sign(revision_rank) * peer_event).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
        unresolved = (np.sign(revision_rank) * receiver_gap).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.15)
        low_participation = (1.0 - volume_z.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)).fillna(0.0)

        signal = revision_rank * unresolved * aligned_cascade * coherence * low_participation
        valid = revision_rank.notna() & receiver_gap.notna() & peer_event.notna() & beta.notna()
        return signal.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)
programs.name: Revision-Conditioned Peer Shock Receiver Gap
programs.trading_idea: A synchronized peer shock is not necessarily a mechanical overshoot: when it is reinforced by a same-signed analyst revision, a low-participation stock that has lagged its beta-implied peer move is more plausibly an unfinished information receiver. The child therefore treats Parent A's residual displacement as a catch-up gap only when Parent B's revision-and-cascade state validates the direction, rather than indiscriminately fading residuals. This interaction separates informative cross-excitation from basket-flow noise: peer moves alone cannot establish the direction's fundamental content, while revisions alone cannot identify whether industry information is actively propagating.
programs.description: Ranks a signed analyst-revision signal multiplied by the remaining beta-adjusted industry-return gap, only when a coherent, volume-confirmed peer event cascade agrees with the revision and the stock has below-normal own participation. Industry leave-one-out returns provide the common-shock state and a trailing beta converts the peer move into the stock-specific expected response.

"""Elasticity-gated sector disclosure backlog.

Mechanism: peer earnings news is transmitted across economically related names,
but the short-horizon receiver response is amplified when the receiver has a
historically high, pre-existing price-volume impact elasticity.  A receiver's
own contemporaneous relative reaction is removed because high-impact moves
originating in the receiver can be transient liquidity dislocations rather
than durable information adoption.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_sector_mean(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
    minimum_peers: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Leave-one-out sector mean using only contemporaneously eligible peers."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels.eq(label)]
        group_values = values.loc[:, cols].where(eligible.loc[:, cols], 0.0)
        group_valid = eligible.loc[:, cols].astype(float)
        total = group_values.sum(axis=1)
        count = group_valid.sum(axis=1)
        loo_total = group_values.rsub(total, axis=0)
        loo_count = group_valid.rsub(count, axis=0)
        mean = loo_total.div(loo_count.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
        result.loc[:, cols] = mean.where(
            eligible.loc[:, cols] & loo_count.ge(float(minimum_peers))
        )
    return result


def _cross_sectional_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robust daily cross-sectional standardisation with finite-value guards."""
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lo = clean.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
    hi = clean.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
    clipped = clean.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    std = clipped.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(std, axis=0)


def _lagged_impact_elasticity(
    close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Pre-event rolling slope of log absolute return on log volume surprise.

    Both regression channels are shifted one bar before estimation, so the
    elasticity used at t is known before t's disclosure mark and return.
    """
    previous_close = close.shift(1)
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        ret = np.log(close / previous_close)
    volume_base = volume.rolling(15, min_periods=8).median().shift(1)
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        x = np.log(volume / volume_base)
        y = np.log(ret.abs().clip(lower=0.0001))
    valid = (
        close.gt(0.0)
        & previous_close.gt(0.0)
        & volume.gt(0.0)
        & volume_base.gt(0.0)
        & np.isfinite(x)
        & np.isfinite(y)
    )
    x = x.where(valid).clip(-3.0, 3.0).shift(1)
    y = y.where(valid).clip(-8.0, 0.0).shift(1)
    covariance = x.rolling(20, min_periods=12).cov(y)
    variance = x.rolling(20, min_periods=12).var()
    return (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 3.0)


def _rolling_sector_loading(
    own_return: pd.DataFrame, peer_return: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Strictly lagged trailing sector beta with a moderate warm-up."""
    x = peer_return.shift(1)
    y = own_return.shift(1)
    valid = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    xv = x.where(valid, 0.0)
    yv = y.where(valid, 0.0)
    count = valid.astype(float).rolling(30, min_periods=15).sum()
    sx = xv.rolling(30, min_periods=15).sum()
    sy = yv.rolling(30, min_periods=15).sum()
    sxx = (xv * xv).rolling(30, min_periods=15).sum()
    sxy = (xv * yv).rolling(30, min_periods=15).sum()
    numerator = sxy - sx * sy / count
    denominator = sxx - sx * sx / count
    return (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 2.0)


@register_factor
class PeerImpulseElasticityBacklog(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "peer_impulse_elasticity_backlog"
    name = "Elasticity-Gated Peer Impulse Backlog"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Leave-one-out sector disclosure impulse scaled by lagged receiver "
        "impact elasticity and historical sector loading, net of the "
        "receiver's recent sector-adjusted reaction."
    )
    window_length = 35
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        labels = data["sector"].iloc[0].copy()

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        own_return = close / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        own_return = own_return.where(np.isfinite(own_return))
        eligible = np.isfinite(own_return)

        peer_return = _leave_one_out_sector_mean(
            own_return, eligible, labels, 2
        )

        eps_event = np.isfinite(eps_surprise) & (
            ~np.isfinite(eps_surprise.shift(1))
            | eps_surprise.ne(eps_surprise.shift(1))
        )
        revenue_event = np.isfinite(revenue_surprise) & (
            ~np.isfinite(revenue_surprise.shift(1))
            | revenue_surprise.ne(revenue_surprise.shift(1))
        )
        event = eps_event | revenue_event

        eps_valid = np.isfinite(eps_surprise) & eps_estimate.abs().gt(0.0)
        revenue_valid = (
            np.isfinite(revenue_surprise) & revenue_estimate.abs().gt(0.0)
        )
        eps_mark = (eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs()).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        revenue_mark = (
            revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs()
        ).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        component_count = eps_valid.astype(float) + revenue_valid.astype(float)
        surprise_mark = (
            eps_mark.where(eps_valid, 0.0)
            + revenue_mark.where(revenue_valid, 0.0)
        ).div(component_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        volume_base = volume.rolling(15, min_periods=8).mean().shift(1)
        abnormal_volume = (volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        disclosure_mark = (
            surprise_mark * abnormal_volume
        ).where(event & component_count.gt(0.0) & eligible, 0.0)

        peer_mark = _leave_one_out_sector_mean(
            disclosure_mark, eligible, labels, 2
        ).fillna(0.0)
        intensity = peer_mark.copy()
        decay = np.exp(-np.log(2.0) * np.arange(1, 7, dtype=float) / 2.5)
        for lag, weight in enumerate(decay, start=1):
            intensity = intensity + peer_mark.shift(lag).fillna(0.0) * weight
        intensity = intensity / (1.0 + float(decay.sum()))

        loading = _rolling_sector_loading(own_return, peer_return)
        elasticity = _lagged_impact_elasticity(close, volume)
        elasticity_z = _cross_sectional_zscore(elasticity).clip(-2.0, 2.0)
        elasticity_gate = (1.0 + 0.35 * elasticity_z).clip(0.25, 1.75)

        sector_response = peer_return.rolling(3, min_periods=2).sum()
        own_response = own_return.rolling(3, min_periods=2).sum()
        response_residual = own_response - loading * sector_response

        impulse = intensity * loading * elasticity_gate
        impulse_z = _cross_sectional_zscore(impulse)
        response_z = _cross_sectional_zscore(response_residual)
        score = impulse_z - 0.60 * response_z

        valid = (
            eligible
            & np.isfinite(peer_return)
            & np.isfinite(loading)
            & np.isfinite(elasticity)
            & np.isfinite(score)
        )
        return score.where(valid, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Elasticity-Gated Peer Impulse Backlog
programs.trading_idea: Peer earnings disclosures create a signed sector information impulse, but its six-day transmission should be strongest in receivers with historically high price-volume impact elasticity: scarce risk-bearing capacity makes externally generated sector demand move those names more per unit participation. Parent A's contradicted continuation sign is reconciled by explicitly removing the receiver's already-priced relative move: a high-impact move initiated in the name itself is often a transient liquidity event and reverses, whereas high elasticity amplifies an unabsorbed peer-originated impulse when the receiver has not yet reacted. The interaction therefore targets externally sourced information diffusion through a liquidity-sensitive receiver, rather than either generic peer drift or generic impact-event continuation alone.
programs.description: Computes leave-one-out sector disclosure-surprise intensity, scales it by a lagged rolling elasticity of absolute return to volume surprise and the stock's historical sector loading, then subtracts the stock's recent sector-adjusted response. High values identify liquidity-sensitive firms that have lagged a positive peer-information impulse; low values identify analogous negative or already-overreacted receivers.

programs.code:
"""The revised mechanism is sector-level common-shock propagation rather than an assumed delayed execution of individually underreacting constituents. A broad sector move accompanied by unusual sector activity and a discrete rise in within-sector return synchronization is treated as evidence that the move is dominated by a common information or common-flow shock, which may continue to diffuse over the next several daily bars. The trade is directionally aligned with the peer-derived sector impulse, but it does not select stocks because they exhibited a beta-adjusted response deficit, low own volume, or a presumed need to catch up."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _winsorized_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectionally winsorize valid close-to-close returns at each date."""
    prior = close.shift(1)
    valid = (close > 0.0) & (prior > 0.0)
    raw = (close / prior - 1.0).where(valid)
    lower = raw.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = raw.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return raw.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _sector_peer_statistics(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    activity_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute date-by-date leave-one-out impulse, breadth, and activity."""
    impulse = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    breadth = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    activity = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)

    for t in range(len(ret.index)):
        labels = sector.iloc[t]
        valid = eligible.iloc[t] & labels.notna() & ret.iloc[t].notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue

        for label in pd.unique(labels.loc[valid]):
            members = np.flatnonzero((labels == label).to_numpy() & valid.to_numpy())
            n_members = len(members)
            if n_members < 13:
                continue

            values = ret.iloc[t, members].to_numpy(dtype=float)
            total = float(np.sum(values))
            loo_impulse = (total - values) / float(n_members - 1)
            impulse.iloc[t, members] = loo_impulse

            signs = np.sign(values)
            for local_i, col_i in enumerate(members):
                peer_mask = np.ones(n_members, dtype=bool)
                peer_mask[local_i] = False
                peer_signs = signs[peer_mask]
                target_sign = np.sign(loo_impulse[local_i])
                breadth.iloc[t, col_i] = float(np.mean(peer_signs == target_sign))

                ratio_values = activity_ratio.iloc[t, members].to_numpy(dtype=float)
                peer_ratio = ratio_values[peer_mask]
                peer_ratio = peer_ratio[np.isfinite(peer_ratio)]
                if peer_ratio.size:
                    activity.iloc[t, col_i] = float(np.median(peer_ratio))

    return impulse, breadth, activity


def _sector_synchronization_delta(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute current five-day versus prior-sixty-day pairwise correlation jump."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    n_dates = len(ret.index)

    for t in range(n_dates):
        if t < 60:
            continue
        labels = sector.iloc[t]
        current_eligible = eligible.iloc[t] & labels.notna()
        if not current_eligible.any():
            continue

        for label in pd.unique(labels.loc[current_eligible]):
            members = np.flatnonzero(
                (labels == label).to_numpy() & current_eligible.to_numpy()
            )
            if len(members) < 12:
                continue

            recent = ret.iloc[max(0, t - 4):t + 1, members]
            baseline = ret.iloc[t - 60:t, members]
            recent_corr = recent.corr(min_periods=4).to_numpy(dtype=float)
            base_corr = baseline.corr(min_periods=50).to_numpy(dtype=float)
            upper = np.triu_indices(len(members), k=1)
            recent_pairs = recent_corr[upper]
            base_pairs = base_corr[upper]

            # The specification requires every pair to meet its observation rule.
            if not (np.isfinite(recent_pairs).all() and np.isfinite(base_pairs).all()):
                continue

            delta = float(np.mean(recent_pairs) - np.mean(base_pairs))
            out.iloc[t, members] = delta

    return out


def _trailing_beta(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """OLS slope on observations t-60 through t-1, requiring 50 valid pairs."""
    y_lag = y.shift(1)
    x_lag = x.shift(1)
    pair_count = (y_lag.notna() & x_lag.notna()).rolling(60, min_periods=60).sum()
    x_mean = x_lag.rolling(60, min_periods=60).mean()
    y_mean = y_lag.rolling(60, min_periods=60).mean()
    covariance = (x_lag * y_lag).rolling(60, min_periods=60).mean() - x_mean * y_mean
    variance = (x_lag * x_lag).rolling(60, min_periods=60).mean() - x_mean * x_mean
    return (covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(pair_count >= 50)


def _sector_impulse_volatility(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.Series:
    """Trailing volatility of the contemporaneous eligible equal-weight market."""
    sector_mean = ret.where(eligible).mean(axis=1)
    return sector_mean.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=50).std()


def _portfolio_vintages(
    raw_signal: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    market_beta: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build sector-balanced, market-beta-hedged daily vintages and overlap six of them."""
    vintage = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=raw_signal.index, columns=raw_signal.columns)

    for t in range(len(raw_signal.index)):
        signal_row = raw_signal.iloc[t]
        label_row = sector.iloc[t]
        positive_sectors: list[tuple[object, np.ndarray]] = []
        negative_sectors: list[tuple[object, np.ndarray]] = []

        valid_labels = label_row.notna()
        for label in pd.unique(label_row.loc[valid_labels]):
            members = np.flatnonzero((label_row == label).to_numpy())
            pos = members[signal_row.iloc[members].to_numpy(dtype=float) > 0.0]
            neg = members[signal_row.iloc[members].to_numpy(dtype=float) < 0.0]
            if len(pos):
                positive_sectors.append((label, pos))
            if len(neg):
                negative_sectors.append((label, neg))

        # A new vintage exists only when both books span at least two sectors.
        if len(positive_sectors) < 2 or len(negative_sectors) < 2:
            continue

        weights = np.zeros(raw_signal.shape[1], dtype=float)
        for _, members in positive_sectors:
            weights[members] = 1.0 / (len(positive_sectors) * len(members))
        for _, members in negative_sectors:
            weights[members] = -1.0 / (len(negative_sectors) * len(members))

        beta_row = market_beta.iloc[t].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        portfolio_beta = float(np.nansum(weights * beta_row))
        basket = np.flatnonzero(eligible.iloc[t].to_numpy())
        if len(basket) and np.isfinite(portfolio_beta):
            # Equal-weight eligible-stock market basket is the hedge instrument.
            weights[basket] -= portfolio_beta / float(len(basket))

        vintage.iloc[t] = weights

    return vintage.rolling(6, min_periods=1).mean().fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class SectorBasketCompletionResponseDeficit(BaseFactor):
    """Sector common-shock continuation portfolio with synchronization confirmation."""

    factor_id = "sector_basket_completion_response_deficit"
    name = "Sector Synchronization Shock Continuation"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "A sector-balanced continuation portfolio triggered by broad peer return "
        "impulses, unusual peer activity, and a discrete rise in within-sector "
        "return synchronization; it contains no focal-stock response-deficit term."
    )
    window_length = 81
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)
        sector = data["sector"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        ret = _winsorized_returns(close)
        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where((close > 0.0) & (volume >= 0.0))

        valid_return_count = ret.notna().rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
        median_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        nonzero_volume_count = (volume > 0.0).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
        eligible = (
            (close > 0.0)
            & ret.notna()
            & (valid_return_count >= 20)
            & (median_dollar_volume >= 1_000_000.0)
            & (nonzero_volume_count >= 15)
            & sector.notna()
        )

        prior_dv_median = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median().shift(1)
        activity_ratio = dollar_volume / prior_dv_median.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        impulse, breadth, activity = _sector_peer_statistics(
            ret, eligible, sector, activity_ratio
        )
        delta_sync = _sector_synchronization_delta(ret, eligible, sector)

        # Beta is audit/control-only: it never enters a realized-response score.
        sector_beta = _trailing_beta(ret, impulse)
        market_return = ret.where(eligible).mean(axis=1)
        market_panel = pd.DataFrame(
            np.tile(market_return.to_numpy()[:, None], (1, close.shape[1])),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        market_beta = _trailing_beta(ret, market_panel)

        # For each sector, the volatility is of its equal-weight eligible return.
        sector_vol = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for t in range(len(close.index)):
            labels = sector.iloc[t]
            valid = eligible.iloc[t] & labels.notna()
            for label in pd.unique(labels.loc[valid]):
                members = np.flatnonzero((labels == label).to_numpy() & valid.to_numpy())
                if len(members) < 13:
                    continue
                sector_history = ret.iloc[:, members].where(eligible.iloc[:, members]).mean(axis=1)
                value = sector_history.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=50).std().iloc[t]
                sector_vol.iloc[t, members] = value

        z_impulse = impulse / sector_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        capped_z = z_impulse.abs().clip(upper=3.0)
        capped_sync = (delta_sync / 0.10).clip(upper=3.0)
        raw_signal = np.sign(impulse) * capped_z * capped_sync

        signal_mask = (
            eligible
            & (impulse != 0.0)
            & (z_impulse.abs() >= 1.5)
            & (breadth >= 0.70)
            & (activity >= 1.20)
            & (delta_sync >= 0.10)
            & (sector_beta > 0.0)
            & (sector_beta < 2.0)
        )
        raw_signal = raw_signal.where(signal_mask, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        return _portfolio_vintages(raw_signal, eligible, sector, market_beta).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Sector Synchronization Shock Continuation
programs.trading_idea: The revised mechanism is sector-level common-shock propagation rather than an assumed delayed execution of individually underreacting constituents. A broad sector move accompanied by unusual sector activity and a discrete rise in within-sector return synchronization is treated as evidence that the move is dominated by a common information or common-flow shock, which may continue to diffuse over the next several daily bars. The trade is directionally aligned with the peer-derived sector impulse, but it does not select stocks because they exhibited a beta-adjusted response deficit, low own volume, or a presumed need to catch up.
programs.description: All calculations are made after close on date t and use only data available by that close; entry is no earlier than open(t+1). Let r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. On every date, winsorize r_i,t cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th percentiles across stocks with valid close_t and close_t-1. Sector is the static data['sector'] label; stocks with missing sector, nonpositive close, or fewer than 20 valid daily observations are excluded. Liquidity eligibility requires median(close_i,u * volume_i,u) over u=t-19,...,t to be at least USD 1,000,000 and at least 15 nonzero-volume observations in that window. No fundamental or estimate field is used, hence no non-price point-in-time screen is required. For each eligible stock i in sector s, require at least 12 other eligible sector peers. Define the leave-one-out sector impulse I_i,t = mean_{j in s, j != i}(r_j,t). Define leave-one-out breadth B_i,t = mean_{j in s, j != i}[1(sign(r_j,t) = sign(I_i,t))], with sign(0)=0; if I_i,t=0 the stock is not eligible for a signal. Define dollar volume DV_j,t = close_j,t * volume_j,t and peer-relative sector activity A_i,t = median_{j in s, j != i}[DV_j,t / median(DV_j,u), u=t-20,...,t-1]. Thus activity uses only contemporaneous peer participation relative to each peer's own trailing baseline, not the focal stock's relative volume. For auditability, estimate each stock's sector beta beta_i,t by OLS slope of r_i,u on I_i,u over u=t-60,...,t-1, requiring at least 50 valid paired observations; this beta is used only for portfolio market-exposure control and is not used to define a response deficit or rank a stock by its realized return. Define sector synchronization C_s,t as the mean of all pairwise Pearson correlations of winsorized daily returns among eligible sector stocks over u=t-4,...,t, provided at least 12 stocks and every pair has at least 4 valid observations. Define the pre-signal synchronization baseline Cbar_s,t = mean of the same pairwise correlations over u=t-60,...,t-1, requiring at least 50 valid observations. Let DeltaC_s,t = C_s,t - Cbar_s,t. Define sector impulse volatility sigma_s,t as the standard deviation of the equal-weight sector return mean_{j in s}(r_j,u) over u=t-60,...,t-1, with at least 50 observations, and Z_i,t = I_i,t / sigma_s,t. A stock receives raw signal S_i,t = sign(I_i,t) * min(abs(Z_i,t), 3) * min(DeltaC_s,t / 0.10, 3) only when abs(Z_i,t) >= 1.5, B_i,t >= 0.70, A_i,t >= 1.20, DeltaC_s,t >= 0.10, and 0 < beta_i,t < 2; otherwise S_i,t = 0. The score therefore depends on peer shock magnitude, breadth, abnormal peer activity, and a contemporaneous jump in sector return synchronization. It deliberately contains no term involving r_i,t - beta_i,t*I_i,t, no residual-response ranking, and no focal-name volume-participation deficit, so it is not a monotone transformation of an industry-loading/participation-deficit catch-up signal. For portfolio construction, among nonzero signals rank stocks by S_i,t; long the positive-signal half and short the negative-signal half, with equal gross capital allocated to each active sector and equal weights within each sector side. If fewer than two sectors are active on either side, hold no new vintage. Scale long and short books to equal gross exposure. Estimate each stock's market beta over the same t-60,...,t-1 window against the equal-weight return of all liquidity-eligible stocks, and hedge the resulting portfolio beta using that equal-weight eligible-stock market basket; the hedge is entered at open(t+1) as well. Do not sector-neutralize, because sector common-shock continuation is the intended exposure. Each daily signal vintage is held from open(t+1) through close(t+6), with overlapping six-bar vintages equally weighted.
