from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _report_age(eps_actual: pd.DataFrame, revenue_actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bars since the latest observed quarterly report-state change."""
    eps_state = eps_actual.ffill()
    revenue_state = revenue_actual.ffill()
    eps_change = eps_state.notna() & eps_state.shift(1).notna() & eps_state.ne(eps_state.shift(1))
    revenue_change = (
        revenue_state.notna()
        & revenue_state.shift(1).notna()
        & revenue_state.ne(revenue_state.shift(1))
    )
    report_change = eps_change | revenue_change
    rows, cols = eps_actual.shape
    clock = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(np.arange(rows, dtype=float)[:, None], (rows, cols)),
        index=eps_actual.index,
        columns=eps_actual.columns,
    )
    last_report = clock.where(report_change).ffill()
    return clock - last_report


def _estimate_revision(estimate: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Twenty-one-bar estimate innovation with a cross-sectional scale floor."""
    prior = estimate.shift(21)
    scale_floor = prior.abs().median(axis=1).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=1e-6) * 0.02
    denominator = prior.abs().where(prior.abs().ge(scale_floor, axis=0), scale_floor, axis=0)
    valid = eligible & estimate.notna() & prior.notna()
    return estimate.sub(prior).div(denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(valid)


def _loo_peer_intensity(
    intensity: pd.DataFrame,
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
    minimum_peers: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Leave-one-out signed and absolute industry cascade intensity."""
    peer_signed = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=intensity.index, columns=intensity.columns)
    peer_absolute = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=intensity.index, columns=intensity.columns)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=intensity.index, columns=intensity.columns)

    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels == label]
        if len(cols) <= minimum_peers:
            continue
        group_valid = valid.loc[:, cols]
        group = intensity.loc[:, cols].where(group_valid, 0.0)
        count = group_valid.astype(float).sum(axis=1)
        total = group.sum(axis=1)
        absolute_total = group.abs().sum(axis=1)

        excluded_count = group_valid.astype(float).rsub(count, axis=0)
        excluded_signed = group.rsub(total, axis=0)
        excluded_absolute = group.abs().rsub(absolute_total, axis=0)

        peer_signed.loc[:, cols] = excluded_signed.div(excluded_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
            excluded_count.ge(minimum_peers)
        )
        peer_absolute.loc[:, cols] = excluded_absolute.div(excluded_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
            excluded_count.ge(minimum_peers)
        )
        peer_count.loc[:, cols] = excluded_count

    return peer_signed, peer_absolute, peer_count


@register_factor
class ReportVetoedPeerCriticalitySnapback(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "report_vetoed_peer_criticality_snapback"
    name = "Report-Vetoed Peer Criticality Snapback"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Fades a high-participation, terminally stretched peer-cascade response "
        "only when a late-quarter estimate revision contradicts the cascade direction."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        safe_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))
        log_close = np.log(safe_close)
        ret = log_close.diff()
        log_volume = np.log1p(safe_volume)

        report_age = _report_age(data["epsActual"], data["revenueActual"])
        report_window = report_age.ge(25.0) & report_age.le(70.0)
        eps_revision = _estimate_revision(data["epsEstimate"], report_window)
        revenue_revision = _estimate_revision(data["revenueEstimate"], report_window)
        revision = (
            0.65 * (2.0 * eps_revision.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0)
            + 0.35 * (2.0 * revenue_revision.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0)
        )

        market_ret = ret.mean(axis=1)
        abnormal = ret.sub(market_ret, axis=0)
        abnormal_mean = abnormal.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        abnormal_std = abnormal.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        abnormal_z = abnormal.sub(abnormal_mean).div(abnormal_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        volume_std = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        volume_z = log_volume.sub(volume_mean).div(volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        valid_event = abnormal_z.notna() & volume_z.notna() & labels.notna().to_numpy()[None, :]
        marked_event = (
            np.sign(abnormal_z)
            * abnormal_z.abs().clip(upper=3.0)
            * (volume_z - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        ).where(valid_event, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        own_intensity = marked_event.ewm(alpha=0.25, adjust=False).mean()

        peer_signed, peer_absolute, peer_count = _loo_peer_intensity(
            own_intensity, valid_event, labels, 5
        )
        coherence = peer_signed.abs().div(peer_absolute.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        trend_mean = log_close.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        trend_std = log_close.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        extension = log_close.sub(trend_mean).div(trend_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        dollar_volume = (safe_close * safe_volume).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        recent_turnover = dollar_volume.rolling(4, min_periods=4).mean()
        prior_turnover = dollar_volume.shift(4).rolling(12, min_periods=10).mean()
        participation = np.log(recent_turnover.div(prior_turnover)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        cascade_strength = peer_signed.abs().rank(axis=1, pct=True) * coherence
        extension_strength = extension.abs().rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        participation_strength = participation.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        cascade_extension_aligned = peer_signed.mul(extension).gt(0.0)
        fundamental_veto = revision.mul(peer_signed).lt(0.0)
        raw = revision * cascade_strength * extension_strength * participation_strength
        usable = (
            report_window
            & revision.notna()
            & peer_count.ge(5.0)
            & peer_signed.notna()
            & coherence.notna()
            & extension.abs().ge(0.9)
            & participation.gt(0.0)
            & cascade_extension_aligned
            & fundamental_veto
            & raw.notna()
        )

        signal = raw.where(usable).rank(axis=1, pct=True).sub(0.5)
        return signal.where(usable, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).reindex(
            index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        ).astype(float)

"""A public earnings disclosure by one firm can reveal an industry-specific operating-state change that is not fully incorporated into comparable firms immediately, particularly during clustered reporting periods when analysts must map heterogeneous disclosures into relative single-name implications. The signal is restricted to liquid receivers that have neither issued a fresh report nor moved in the direction already implied by price-confirmed peer disclosures; this is an observable underreaction condition rather than an assertion that low turnover alone identifies investor inattention. The expected six-bar return follows the signed, price-confirmed peer information as the receiver closes its industry-relative pricing gap."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_value(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag point-in-time releases or revisions using only the prior bar."""
    previous = value.shift(1)
    return value.notna() & (previous.isna() | value.ne(previous))


def _static_labels(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
    """Extract static group labels, assigning unique groups to missing labels."""
    labels = frame.ffill().bfill().iloc[0].astype(object).to_numpy(copy=True)
    for pos, ticker in enumerate(frame.columns):
        if pd.isna(labels[pos]):
            labels[pos] = "__missing_group_" + str(ticker)
        else:
            labels[pos] = str(labels[pos])
    return labels


def _industry_relative_return(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    industry_labels: np.ndarray,
    horizon: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing return less equal-weight same-industry return excluding self."""
    own_return = close / close.shift(horizon) - 1.0
    values = own_return.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    result = np.full(values.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)

    for industry in np.unique(industry_labels):
        members = np.flatnonzero(industry_labels == industry)
        group_values = values[:, members]
        valid = np.isfinite(group_values)
        group_sum = np.where(valid, group_values, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        group_count = valid.sum(axis=1)

        for local_pos, column_pos in enumerate(members):
            own_valid = valid[:, local_pos]
            denominator = group_count - own_valid.astype(int)
            numerator = group_sum - np.where(own_valid, values[:, column_pos], 0.0)
            benchmark = np.divide(
                numerator,
                denominator,
                out=np.full(len(close.index), np.nan, dtype=float),
                where=denominator > 0,
            )
            result[:, column_pos] = values[:, column_pos] - benchmark

    return pd.DataFrame(result, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)


def _confirmed_peer_relay(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    event_score: pd.DataFrame,
    event_base_close: pd.DataFrame,
    industry_labels: np.ndarray,
    sector_labels: np.ndarray,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute receiver-specific leave-two-out, price-confirmed peer disclosures.

    Each peer carries only its most recent eligible event from the preceding
    five bars.  The sector benchmark is recomputed from that peer's event base
    and excludes both the disclosing peer and the prospective receiver.
    """
    close_values = close.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    score_values = event_score.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    base_values = event_base_close.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = close_values.shape
    output = np.zeros((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=float)

    industry_members = {
        group: np.flatnonzero(industry_labels == group)
        for group in np.unique(industry_labels)
    }
    sector_members = {
        group: np.flatnonzero(sector_labels == group)
        for group in np.unique(sector_labels)
    }

    for row in range(n_rows):
        current_close = close_values[row]
        current_score = score_values[row]
        current_base = base_values[row]
        peer_valid = (
            np.isfinite(current_score)
            & np.isfinite(current_base)
            & (current_base != 0.0)
            & np.isfinite(current_close)
        )

        if not peer_valid.any():
            continue

        for industry, receivers in industry_members.items():
            candidate_peers = receivers[peer_valid[receivers]]
            if len(candidate_peers) < 3:
                continue

            peer_sector_returns: dict[int, tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, float]] = {}
            for peer in candidate_peers:
                sector_indices = sector_members[sector_labels[peer]]
                sector_close = current_close[sector_indices]
                sector_return = sector_close / current_base[peer] - 1.0
                sector_valid = np.isfinite(sector_return)
                peer_own_return = current_close[peer] / current_base[peer] - 1.0
                peer_sector_returns[int(peer)] = (
                    sector_return,
                    sector_valid,
                    float(peer_own_return),
                )

            for receiver in receivers:
                contributions: list[float] = []

                for peer in candidate_peers:
                    if peer == receiver:
                        continue

                    sector_indices = sector_members[sector_labels[peer]]
                    sector_return, sector_valid, peer_own_return = peer_sector_returns[int(peer)]
                    include = sector_valid.copy()

                    peer_location = np.flatnonzero(sector_indices == peer)
                    if len(peer_location):
                        include[peer_location[0]] = False
                    receiver_location = np.flatnonzero(sector_indices == receiver)
                    if len(receiver_location):
                        include[receiver_location[0]] = False

                    count = int(include.sum())
                    if count <= 0:
                        continue

                    sector_benchmark = float(sector_return[include].mean())
                    confirmation_return = peer_own_return - sector_benchmark
                    peer_sign = np.sign(current_score[peer])
                    confirmation_sign = np.sign(confirmation_return)

                    if peer_sign != 0.0 and peer_sign == confirmation_sign:
                        contribution = float(current_score[peer] * abs(confirmation_return))
                        if np.isfinite(contribution):
                            contributions.append(contribution)

                if len(contributions) < 3:
                    continue

                contribution_array = np.asarray(contributions, dtype=float)
                absolute_total = float(np.abs(contribution_array).sum())
                if absolute_total <= 0.0:
                    continue

                positive_mass = float(contribution_array[contribution_array > 0.0].sum())
                negative_mass = float(-contribution_array[contribution_array < 0.0].sum())
                dominant_mass = max(positive_mass, negative_mass)

                if dominant_mass >= (2.0 / 3.0) * absolute_total:
                    output[row, receiver] = float(contribution_array.mean())

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)


@register_factor
class AttentionBottleneckPeerDisclosureRelay(BaseFactor):
    """Price-confirmed peer disclosures relayed to liquid, underreacting industry receivers."""

    factor_id = "attention_bottleneck_peer_disclosure_relay"
    name = "Confirmed Peer-Disclosure Underreaction"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Signed, price-confirmed same-industry earnings-disclosure relay for "
        "liquid receivers without a fresh report whose industry-relative price "
        "has not yet moved in the peer-implied direction."
    )
    window_length = 25
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "industry",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]

        industry_labels = _static_labels(data["industry"])
        sector_labels = _static_labels(data["sector"])

        eps_fresh = _fresh_value(eps_actual)
        revenue_fresh = _fresh_value(revenue_actual)
        fresh_disclosure = eps_fresh | revenue_fresh

        prior_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        eps_scaled = eps_surprise / prior_close
        revenue_scaled = revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)

        eps_component = (2.0 * eps_scaled.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0).where(
            eps_fresh & eps_surprise.notna() & eps_scaled.notna()
        )
        revenue_component = (2.0 * revenue_scaled.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0).where(
            revenue_fresh & revenue_surprise.notna() & revenue_scaled.notna()
        )

        component_count = (
            eps_component.notna().astype(float) + revenue_component.notna().astype(float)
        )
        event_score_raw = (eps_component.fillna(0.0) + revenue_component.fillna(0.0))
        event_score_raw = event_score_raw / component_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        eligible_event = component_count > 0.0

        # Forward fill only five bars: at t this is the latest eligible e in [t-5, t].
        latest_event_score = event_score_raw.where(eligible_event).ffill(limit=5)
        latest_event_base = prior_close.where(eligible_event).ffill(limit=5)

        peer_score = _confirmed_peer_relay(
            close,
            latest_event_score,
            latest_event_base,
            industry_labels,
            sector_labels,
        )

        no_recent_receiver_disclosure = (
            fresh_disclosure.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).max() == 0.0
        )

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(close.notna() & volume.notna())
        adv20 = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        liquid = adv20.rank(axis=1, pct=True) >= 0.30

        current_volume = volume.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        prior_volume = volume.shift(3).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        volume_ratio = current_volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        attention_gate = (volume_ratio <= 1.0) & (volume_ratio >= 0.25)

        receiver_industry_return = _industry_relative_return(close, industry_labels, 3)
        price_gap_gate = peer_score * receiver_industry_return <= 0.0

        valid = (
            no_recent_receiver_disclosure
            & liquid
            & attention_gate
            & price_gap_gate
            & peer_score.ne(0.0)
        )
        return peer_score.where(valid, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Confirmed Peer-Disclosure Underreaction
programs.trading_idea: A public earnings disclosure by one firm can reveal an industry-specific operating-state change that is not fully incorporated into comparable firms immediately, particularly during clustered reporting periods when analysts must map heterogeneous disclosures into relative single-name implications. The signal is restricted to liquid receivers that have neither issued a fresh report nor moved in the direction already implied by price-confirmed peer disclosures; this is an observable underreaction condition rather than an assertion that low turnover alone identifies investor inattention. The expected six-bar return follows the signed, price-confirmed peer information as the receiver closes its industry-relative pricing gap.
programs.description: At each decision-bar close t, define a fresh peer disclosure for stock i as the latest bar e in [t-5, t] on which either epsActual or revenueActual becomes newly available or changes versus e-1, with a non-null corresponding epsSurprise or revenueSurprise. For that disclosure, form a point-in-time surprise score s_i as the mean of available cross-sectional percentile-rank transforms on event bar e of epsSurprise_i / close_i(e-1) and revenueSurprise_i / abs(revenueEstimate_i); names with zero or missing denominators are omitted from that component. Compute trailing-only return confirmation r_i from close_i(e-1) to close_i(t), less the equal-weight sector return over the same interval excluding i and the receiver. Retain the peer contribution only when sign(s_i) equals sign(r_i), and define its signed contribution as s_i times abs(r_i). For receiver j, aggregate only same-industry stocks i != j, using one latest eligible event per peer; the leave-one-out peer score is the equal-weight mean of retained contributions. Require at least three contributing peers and require the dominant contribution sign to represent at least two-thirds of total absolute contribution; otherwise set the score to zero. Exclude receiver j from every industry and sector benchmark. The receiver must have no fresh EPS or revenue disclosure in [t-5, t], must pass a liquidity screen of 20-day average dollar volume close*volume at or above the contemporaneous cross-sectional 30th percentile, and must not exhibit an extreme volume drought. Its attention/underreaction gate is current 3-day average volume divided by the preceding non-overlapping 20-day average volume <= 1.0, together with sign(peer_score) times the receiver's 3-day industry-relative return <= 0, where industry-relative return is receiver return minus equal-weight same-industry return excluding the receiver. The final signal is the signed peer score when all gates pass and zero otherwise. It is timestamped after the close of t and traded no earlier than the next bar open, so all event data and return confirmation are available at decision time. Relative to the existing peer-readthrough factor, this version is intended to isolate price-confirmed peer information and a liquid receiver's measurable industry-relative underreaction, rather than a peer signal conditioned on supply-unwind dynamics; incremental exposure versus peer-readthrough and standalone earnings-surprise drift should be tested directly.

"""Late-quarter revisions received through an unfinished industry event cascade."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _loo_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels == label]
        if len(cols) <= minimum:
            continue
        group = values.loc[:, cols]
        valid = group.notna().astype(float)
        total = group.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        peer_total = group.fillna(0.0).rsub(total, axis=0)
        peer_count = valid.rsub(count, axis=0)
        output.loc[:, cols] = peer_total.div(peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(peer_count >= minimum)
    return output


def _report_age(actual_eps: pd.DataFrame, actual_revenue: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    eps_prior = actual_eps.ffill().shift(1)
    rev_prior = actual_revenue.ffill().shift(1)
    eps_reset = actual_eps.notna() & eps_prior.notna() & actual_eps.ne(eps_prior)
    rev_reset = actual_revenue.notna() & rev_prior.notna() & actual_revenue.ne(rev_prior)
    reset = eps_reset | rev_reset
    rows, cols = actual_eps.shape
    position = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(np.arange(rows, dtype=float)[:, None], (rows, cols)),
        index=actual_eps.index,
        columns=actual_eps.columns,
    )
    latest = position.where(reset).ffill()
    return position - latest


def _revision(estimate: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    prior = estimate.shift(21)
    valid = eligible & estimate.notna() & prior.notna()
    floor = prior.abs().median(axis=1).mul(0.01)
    denominator = prior.abs().where(prior.abs().ge(floor, axis=0), floor, axis=0)
    return estimate.sub(prior).div(denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(valid)


def _sector_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    universe_median = values.median(axis=1)
    universe_mad = values.sub(universe_median, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels == label]
        group = values.loc[:, cols]
        count = group.notna().sum(axis=1)
        median = group.median(axis=1).where(count.ge(5), universe_median)
        mad = group.sub(group.median(axis=1), axis=0).abs().median(axis=1)
        mad = mad.where(count.ge(5), universe_mad)
        output.loc[:, cols] = group.sub(median, axis=0).div(1.4826 * mad + 1e-12, axis=0)
    return output


@register_factor
class ReportClockPeerCascadeRevisionReceiver(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "report_clock_peer_cascade_revision_receiver"
    name = "Peer-Cascade Revision Receiver"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Late-quarter estimate revisions are traded only when aligned with a "
        "coherent beta-adjusted industry event cascade that the stock has not "
        "yet absorbed, with a sector variance-acceleration completion screen."
    )
    window_length = 90
    inputs = [
        "close", "high", "low", "volume", "industry", "sector",
        "epsActual", "revenueActual", "epsEstimate", "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry_labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        sector_labels = data["sector"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        age = _report_age(data["epsActual"], data["revenueActual"])
        eligible = age.ge(35.0) & age.le(65.0)
        eps_rev = _revision(data["epsEstimate"], eligible)
        revenue_rev = _revision(data["revenueEstimate"], eligible)
        revision_score = (
            0.60 * (2.0 * eps_rev.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0)
            + 0.40 * (2.0 * revenue_rev.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0)
        )

        prior_close = close.shift(1).where(close.shift(1).gt(0.0))
        ret = np.log(close.where(close.gt(0.0)).div(prior_close))
        industry_ret = _loo_mean(ret, industry_labels, 5)
        beta = ret.rolling(60, min_periods=30).cov(industry_ret).div(
            industry_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=30).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).shift(1).clip(-2.0, 2.0)
        abnormal = ret - beta * industry_ret
        abnormal_z = abnormal.div(abnormal.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan))

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume.gt(0.0)))
        volume_mean = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean().shift(1)
        volume_std = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().shift(1)
        volume_z = log_volume.sub(volume_mean).div(volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        price_range = high - low
        clv = (2.0 * close - high - low).div(price_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
        event = (
            np.sign(abnormal) * abnormal_z.abs().clip(upper=3.0)
            * (0.5 + 0.5 * np.sign(abnormal) * clv)
        ).where(abnormal_z.abs().ge(1.5) & volume_z.ge(1.0), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        own_intensity = event.ewm(alpha=0.20, adjust=False).mean()
        peer_intensity = _loo_mean(own_intensity, industry_labels, 5)
        peer_absolute = _loo_mean(own_intensity.abs(), industry_labels, 5)
        coherence = peer_intensity.abs().div(peer_absolute.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        peer_gap = (peer_intensity - own_intensity) * coherence

        range_variance = np.log(high.where(high.gt(0.0)).div(low.where(low.gt(0.0)))).pow(2) / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))
        acceleration = np.log(
            (range_variance.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean() + 1e-12).div(
                range_variance.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean() + 1e-12
            )
        )
        variance_z = _sector_zscore(acceleration.where(eligible), sector_labels)
        completion_penalty = variance_z.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0).div(2.0)

        alignment = (np.sign(revision_score) * peer_gap).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0).div(2.0)
        signal = revision_score * alignment * (1.0 - completion_penalty)
        valid = eligible & revision_score.notna() & peer_gap.notna() & variance_z.notna()
        return signal.where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)
programs.name: Peer-Cascade Revision Receiver
programs.trading_idea: Late-quarter analyst revisions are most actionable over six sessions when an economically linked peer cascade has already begun in the same direction but the receiver itself has not yet absorbed that information. The industry event state supplies a cross-excitation clock, while the report-clock revision supplies the stock-specific fundamental direction; suppressing names with fast sector-relative variance acceleration avoids cases where the receiver has already undergone costly adverse-selection-driven price discovery. Neither parent alone distinguishes a public revision that is merely slow from one that is being actively validated and transmitted through an unfinished peer-information cascade.
programs.description: Ranks late-quarter EPS and revenue estimate revisions and activates them only when a coherent, beta-adjusted leave-one-out industry event intensity points in the same direction and exceeds the stock's own event intensity. The signal is attenuated when Parkinson range-variance acceleration is high relative to the sector.

"""A synchronized, high-participation residual-price shock across several liquid peers is more likely to represent shared industry information or correlated order-flow excitation than an isolated firm-specific move. Individual receivers with normal-to-muted trading activity may update more slowly because the industry impulse has not yet generated comparable receiver-side participation. The signal therefore follows the signed peer impulse only when it is corroborated by multiple independently shocked peers and when the receiver remains liquid but has not experienced abnormal own-volume assimilation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_market_return(ret: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Construct same-bar equal-weight market returns excluding each ticker."""
    valid = ret.notna()
    row_sum = ret.sum(axis=1, skipna=True)
    row_count = valid.sum(axis=1)

    loo_sum = ret.mul(-1.0).add(row_sum, axis=0)
    loo_count = valid.astype(float).mul(-1.0).add(row_count, axis=0)
    loo_market = loo_sum / loo_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return loo_market.where(loo_count > 0.0)


def _industry_peer_impulse(
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    liquid: pd.DataFrame,
    shock: pd.DataFrame,
    capped_z: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute causal, leave-one-out industry shock means and receiver gates."""
    impulse = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=capped_z.index, columns=capped_z.columns)
    receiver_gate = pd.DataFrame(False, index=capped_z.index, columns=capped_z.columns)

    for row_pos in range(len(capped_z.index)):
        labels = industry.iloc[row_pos]
        liquid_row = liquid.iloc[row_pos].fillna(False).astype(float)
        shock_row = shock.iloc[row_pos].fillna(False).astype(float)
        z_row = capped_z.iloc[row_pos]
        shock_contribution = z_row.where(shock_row > 0.0, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        liquid_by_industry = liquid_row.groupby(labels).sum()
        shocks_by_industry = shock_row.groupby(labels).sum()
        signed_z_by_industry = shock_contribution.groupby(labels).sum()

        total_liquid = labels.map(liquid_by_industry).fillna(0.0)
        total_shocks = labels.map(shocks_by_industry).fillna(0.0)
        total_signed_z = labels.map(signed_z_by_industry).fillna(0.0)

        peer_liquid = total_liquid - liquid_row
        peer_shocks = total_shocks - shock_row
        peer_signed_z = total_signed_z - shock_contribution
        peer_impulse = peer_signed_z / peer_shocks.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        valid_receiver = (
            labels.notna()
            & (liquid_row > 0.0)
            & (peer_liquid >= 8.0)
            & (peer_shocks >= 3.0)
        )

        impulse.iloc[row_pos] = peer_impulse.to_numpy()
        receiver_gate.iloc[row_pos] = valid_receiver.to_numpy()

    return impulse, receiver_gate


@register_factor
class IndustryReceiverAttentionDeficitRelay(BaseFactor):
    """Industry shock relay for liquid receivers with muted own participation."""

    factor_id = "industry_receiver_attention_deficit_relay"
    name = "Synchronized Industry Shock Relay"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Uses leave-one-out market residual shocks among liquid industry peers "
        "to identify receiver stocks whose own trading participation has not yet "
        "fully assimilated a corroborated industry-level impulse."
    )
    window_length = 121
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        ret = (close / close.shift(1) - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        loo_market = _leave_one_out_market_return(ret)

        prior_ret = ret.shift(1)
        prior_market = loo_market.shift(1)
        pair_count = (prior_ret.notna() & prior_market.notna()).rolling(
            60, min_periods=40
        ).sum()
        covariance = prior_ret.rolling(60, min_periods=40).cov(prior_market)
        market_variance = prior_market.rolling(60, min_periods=40).var()
        beta = covariance / market_variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta = beta.where(pair_count >= 40.0)

        residual = (ret - beta * loo_market).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        prior_residual = residual.shift(1)
        residual_count = prior_residual.rolling(60, min_periods=40).count()
        residual_mean = prior_residual.rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean()
        residual_std = prior_residual.rolling(60, min_periods=40).std()
        residual_z = (residual - residual_mean) / residual_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        capped_z = residual_z.where(residual_count >= 40.0).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        prior_dollar_median = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(
            20, min_periods=20
        ).median()
        liquid = prior_dollar_median >= 5_000_000.0
        high_participation = dollar_volume >= (1.5 * prior_dollar_median)
        shock = liquid & high_participation & (capped_z.abs() >= 2.0)

        peer_impulse, receiver_gate = _industry_peer_impulse(
            industry, liquid, shock, capped_z
        )

        prior_volume_median = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        volume_denominator = prior_volume_median.clip(lower=1.0)
        volume_surprise = (volume / volume_denominator).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).clip(lower=0.5, upper=3.0)
        attention_multiplier = (1.0 / volume_surprise).clip(lower=0.5, upper=2.0)

        score = (peer_impulse * attention_multiplier).clip(lower=-8.0, upper=8.0)
        return score.where(receiver_gate, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Synchronized Industry Shock Relay
programs.trading_idea: A synchronized, high-participation residual-price shock across several liquid peers is more likely to represent shared industry information or correlated order-flow excitation than an isolated firm-specific move. Individual receivers with normal-to-muted trading activity may update more slowly because the industry impulse has not yet generated comparable receiver-side participation. The signal therefore follows the signed peer impulse only when it is corroborated by multiple independently shocked peers and when the receiver remains liquid but has not experienced abnormal own-volume assimilation.
programs.description: Use the static `industry` taxonomy only. At each completed daily bar t, define each stock return as close[t] / close[t-1] - 1. For every stock, construct a leave-one-out equal-weight market return from all other valid-universe stocks and estimate a no-intercept market beta using covariance(return, leave-one-out market return) / variance(leave-one-out market return) over the prior 60 completed bars, requiring at least 40 valid observations; the current idiosyncratic residual is return[t] - beta[t] * leave-one-out market return[t]. Standardize this residual using its own prior 60 completed residuals, excluding t, requiring 40 observations, and cap the resulting residual z-score to [-4, 4]. A stock is an eligible shock peer only if its trailing-20-bar median dollar volume, computed as median(close * volume) over bars t-20 through t-1, is at least USD 5 million; its current volume is at least 1.5 times that same prior-20-bar median; and its absolute capped residual z-score is at least 2.0. For each receiver, exclude the receiver itself from every industry aggregate and retain the receiver only when its industry contains at least 8 other eligible liquid peers and at least 3 qualifying shock peers on t. The peer impulse is the equal-weight mean of the qualifying shock peers' capped signed residual z-scores; no market-cap, volume, or residual-magnitude weighting is used. The receiver must also have trailing-20-bar median dollar volume of at least USD 5 million. Define its own volume-surprise ratio as volume[t] divided by its prior-20-bar median volume, floor the denominator at 1 share-equivalent unit to avoid division by zero, winsorize the ratio to [0.5, 3.0], and set the attention multiplier to 1 / clipped-volume-surprise, capped to [0.5, 2.0]. The final score is peer impulse times the attention multiplier, capped to [-8, 8]. All quantities use the completed bar t only; the score is formed after that bar closes and may be traded no earlier than the next executable bar.

programs.code:
"""Late-report estimate revisions conditioned on confirmed peer disclosure cascades.

Mechanism: public peer earnings surprises create a marked, self-decaying industry
information intensity.  A receiver is tradable only when its own late-quarter
revision agrees with that intensity but its relative price has not yet caught up.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return static industry labels, isolating tickers with unavailable labels."""
    labels = frame.ffill().iloc[-1].astype(object).to_numpy(copy=True)
    for position, ticker in enumerate(frame.columns):
        if pd.isna(labels[position]):
            labels[position] = "__isolated_" + str(ticker)
        else:
            labels[position] = str(labels[position])
    return labels


def _leave_one_out(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: np.ndarray, minimum: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal same-date leave-one-out group mean and observed peer count."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    counts = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in np.unique(labels):
        positions = np.flatnonzero(labels == label)
        if len(positions) <= minimum:
            continue
        group = values.iloc[:, positions]
        observed = group.notna().astype(float)
        total = group.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1)
        count = observed.sum(axis=1)
        peer_total = group.rsub(total, axis=0)
        peer_count = observed.rsub(count, axis=0)
        result.iloc[:, positions] = peer_total.div(peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0).where(peer_count >= minimum)
        counts.iloc[:, positions] = peer_count
    return result, counts


def _fresh_update(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time update flag, including the first available observation."""
    previous = value.shift(1)
    return value.notna() & (previous.isna() | value.ne(previous))


def _report_age(eps_actual: pd.DataFrame, revenue_actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Number of bars elapsed since the last observable reporting update."""
    update = _fresh_update(eps_actual) | _fresh_update(revenue_actual)
    clock = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(np.arange(len(eps_actual), dtype=float)[:, None], eps_actual.shape),
        index=eps_actual.index,
        columns=eps_actual.columns,
    )
    last_update = clock.where(update).ffill()
    return clock - last_update


def _relative_revision(estimate: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robust twenty-one-bar estimate revision, using only public trailing values."""
    prior = estimate.shift(21)
    floor = prior.abs().median(axis=1).mul(0.02)
    denominator = prior.abs().where(prior.abs().ge(floor, axis=0), floor, axis=0)
    valid = eligible & estimate.notna() & prior.notna() & denominator.gt(0.0)
    return estimate.sub(prior).div(denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0).where(valid)


@register_factor
class LateRevisionConfirmedDisclosurePhaseRelay(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "late_revision_confirmed_disclosure_phase_relay"
    name = "Late Revision Confirmed Disclosure Relay"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Late-quarter receiver revisions aligned with a leave-one-out, "
        "price-confirmed peer disclosure intensity, gated by an unfinished "
        "industry-relative receiver response."
    )
    window_length = 90
    inputs = [
        "close", "volume", "industry", "epsActual", "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise", "revenueEstimate",
        "epsEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        labels = _static_labels(data["industry"])

        log_return = np.log(close.where(close.gt(0.0)).div(close.shift(1)))
        industry_return, return_peer_count = _leave_one_out(log_return, labels, 4)
        abnormal_return = log_return - industry_return
        abnormal_scale = abnormal_return.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        abnormal_z = abnormal_return.div(abnormal_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume.ge(0.0)))
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        volume_scale = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        volume_z = log_volume.sub(volume_mean).div(volume_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        eps_fresh = _fresh_update(data["epsActual"])
        revenue_fresh = _fresh_update(data["revenueActual"])
        eps_scaled = data["epsSurprise"].div(close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        revenue_scaled = data["revenueSurprise"].div(data["revenueEstimate"].abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        eps_rank = 2.0 * eps_scaled.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        revenue_rank = 2.0 * revenue_scaled.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        surprise_count = (eps_fresh & eps_rank.notna()).astype(float) + (revenue_fresh & revenue_rank.notna()).astype(float)
        surprise = eps_rank.where(eps_fresh).fillna(0.0).add(revenue_rank.where(revenue_fresh).fillna(0.0))
        surprise = surprise.div(surprise_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        confirmed = surprise.notna() & abnormal_z.notna() & volume_z.notna() & return_peer_count.ge(4.0)
        signed_confirmation = np.sign(surprise) * np.sign(abnormal_z)
        disclosure_mark = (
            surprise.abs().clip(upper=1.0)
            * abnormal_z.abs().clip(upper=3.0)
            * (volume_z - 0.25).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
            * np.sign(surprise)
        ).where(confirmed & signed_confirmation.gt(0.0))

        history = abnormal_z.notna().astype(float).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum().ge(15.0)
        own_intensity = disclosure_mark.fillna(0.0).ewm(alpha=0.20, adjust=False).mean().where(history)
        peer_intensity, peer_count = _leave_one_out(own_intensity, labels, 4)

        age = _report_age(data["epsActual"], data["revenueActual"])
        late_window = age.ge(30.0) & age.le(75.0)
        eps_revision = _relative_revision(data["epsEstimate"], late_window)
        revenue_revision = _relative_revision(data["revenueEstimate"], late_window)
        revision_count = eps_revision.notna().astype(float) + revenue_revision.notna().astype(float)
        revision = (
            0.60 * eps_revision.fillna(0.0) + 0.40 * revenue_revision.fillna(0.0)
        ).div(revision_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        receiver_relative = close.div(close.shift(3)).sub(1.0)
        industry_relative, _ = _leave_one_out(receiver_relative, labels, 4)
        own_gap = receiver_relative - industry_relative
        direction = np.sign(revision)
        backlog = direction * (peer_intensity - own_intensity)
        price_unpaid = direction * own_gap.le(0.0)

        valid = (
            late_window
            & revision.notna()
            & peer_intensity.notna()
            & peer_count.ge(4.0)
            & history
            & revision.mul(peer_intensity).gt(0.0)
            & backlog.gt(0.0)
            & price_unpaid
        )
        raw = revision * backlog.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).div(1.0 + own_intensity.abs())
        signal = 2.0 * raw.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        return signal.where(valid, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).astype(float)

Peer disclosure marks establish that the information shock is fundamental rather than a purely technical volume event, and the receiver's revision supplies a stock-specific direction and susceptibility state. This interaction targets the intermediate contagion phase in which public peer news is validated by prices but the economically aligned, unreleased receiver has not yet completed repricing.

"""Late-clock revision-conditioned terminal participation overshoot reversal."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _report_age(reset: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bars since the most recent causally observed report-value update."""
    rows, cols = reset.shape
    positions = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(np.arange(rows, dtype=float)[:, None], (rows, cols)),
        index=reset.index,
        columns=reset.columns,
    )
    return positions - positions.where(reset).ffill()


def _update_reset(actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify public actual-value changes without using future observations."""
    prior = actual.ffill().shift(1)
    finite_now = actual.notna() & np.isfinite(actual)
    finite_prior = prior.notna() & np.isfinite(prior)
    return finite_now & finite_prior & actual.ne(prior)


def _trend_residual_zscore(close: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Terminal residual from a trailing log-price linear trend, in residual SDs."""
    log_price = np.log(close.where(close > 0.0))
    time = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(np.arange(len(close), dtype=float)[:, None], close.shape),
        index=close.index,
        columns=close.columns,
    )
    sum_t = time.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_t2 = (time * time).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_y = log_price.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_y2 = (log_price * log_price).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_ty = (time * log_price).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    denominator = window * sum_t2 - sum_t * sum_t
    slope = (window * sum_ty - sum_t * sum_y) / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    intercept = (sum_y - slope * sum_t) / float(window)
    fitted_now = intercept + slope * time
    residual = log_price - fitted_now
    sse = sum_y2 - intercept * sum_y - slope * sum_ty
    residual_std = np.sqrt(sse.clip(lower=0.0) / float(window - 2))
    return (residual / residual_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _normalized_revision(estimate: pd.DataFrame, age_ok: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal estimate change scaled by the prior published estimate magnitude."""
    prior = estimate.shift(lag)
    valid = age_ok & estimate.notna() & prior.notna() & np.isfinite(estimate) & np.isfinite(prior)
    scale = prior.abs().where(valid)
    floor = 0.01 * scale.median(axis=1)
    denominator = scale.where(scale.ge(floor, axis=0), floor, axis=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return ((estimate - prior) / denominator).where(valid).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class LateClockRevisionTerminalOvershoot(BaseFactor):
    """Fade revision-aligned terminal price extensions with accelerating participation."""

    factor_id = "late_clock_revision_terminal_overshoot"
    name = "Late-Clock Revision Terminal Overshoot"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Fades a revision-aligned log-trend extension only during the late report clock, "
        "when dollar-volume participation accelerates but range-variance discovery remains calm."
    )
    window_length = 45
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        if close.empty:
            return close.astype(float)

        reset = _update_reset(data["epsActual"]) | _update_reset(data["revenueActual"])
        age = _report_age(reset)
        late_clock = age.ge(35.0) & age.le(70.0)

        eps_revision = _normalized_revision(data["epsEstimate"], late_clock, 21)
        revenue_revision = _normalized_revision(data["revenueEstimate"], late_clock, 21)
        eps_direction = 2.0 * eps_revision.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        revenue_direction = 2.0 * revenue_revision.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        revision_direction = 0.6 * eps_direction + 0.4 * revenue_direction

        trend_z = _trend_residual_zscore(close, 30)
        dollar_volume = (close * data["volume"]).where((close > 0.0) & (data["volume"] > 0.0))
        recent_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        prior_volume = dollar_volume.shift(5).rolling(15, min_periods=15).mean()
        volume_acceleration = np.log(recent_volume / prior_volume).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        participation_rank = volume_acceleration.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        valid_range = high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0)
        range_variance = (np.log(high.where(valid_range) / low.where(valid_range)) ** 2) / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))
        short_variance = range_variance.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        long_variance = range_variance.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        variance_acceleration = np.log((short_variance + 1e-12) / (long_variance + 1e-12))
        variance_rank = variance_acceleration.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        calmness = 1.0 - variance_rank

        aligned_extension = revision_direction * trend_z > 0.0
        eligible = (
            late_clock
            & revision_direction.notna()
            & trend_z.notna()
            & participation_rank.ge(0.60)
            & calmness.ge(0.40)
            & trend_z.abs().ge(0.80)
            & aligned_extension
        )
        signal = -trend_z * participation_rank * calmness
        return signal.where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.trading_idea: Late-quarter consensus revisions provide a signed public-information state, while a trend-residual extension with accelerating participation identifies a self-exciting terminal order-flow episode. The child fades only those critical price extensions that run in the same direction as the revision and occur while range-variance acceleration remains subdued: delayed institutional reaction can initially validate the news, but a volume-backed terminal extension is more likely to exhaust marginal liquidity than to represent fresh information. Neither parent alone distinguishes ordinary calm revision diffusion from the final crowded overshoot of that diffusion.
programs.description: Computes a late-report-clock EPS/revenue revision direction, then fades a same-direction rolling log-price trend residual when dollar-volume participation accelerates and sector-unconditioned range variance remains calm. The signal is zero outside the late-quarter revision state or when price and revision do not align.

"""The revised mechanism is not mechanical cross-excitation from one stock to another, but delayed incorporation of unusually high-volume, industry-relevant information after removing the market and realized industry return. A stock is a candidate receiver only when its industry peers have recently generated signed abnormal return-volume events, its own industry-neutral response remains below the historically estimated response associated with such peer intensity, and it has not itself generated a large event that would indicate that the information is already incorporated. The strategy is active only when the rolling, strictly pre-signal relation between peer event intensity and subsequent industry-neutral returns is positive; otherwise the signal is set to zero rather than assuming continuation over reversal."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_mean(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    observed: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
    min_peers: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal same-date leave-one-out industry mean and peer-count mask."""
    safe_labels = labels.fillna("__missing_industry__")
    observed_float = observed.astype(float)
    group_sum = values.where(observed, 0.0).T.groupby(safe_labels, sort=False).sum().T
    group_count = observed_float.T.groupby(safe_labels, sort=False).sum().T

    mapped_sum = group_sum.reindex(columns=safe_labels.to_numpy())
    mapped_count = group_count.reindex(columns=safe_labels.to_numpy())
    mapped_sum.columns = values.columns
    mapped_count.columns = values.columns

    peer_sum = mapped_sum - values.where(observed, 0.0)
    peer_count = mapped_count - observed_float
    peer_mean = peer_sum / peer_count.where(peer_count >= min_peers)
    return peer_mean, peer_count


def _finite_exponential_mark(
    marks: pd.DataFrame,
    decay: float,
    length: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Fixed finite exponential kernel, valid only after a complete history."""
    weighted = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=marks.index, columns=marks.columns)
    for lag in range(length):
        weighted = weighted + (decay ** lag) * marks.shift(lag).fillna(0.0)

    complete = marks.notna().astype(float).rolling(length, min_periods=length).sum() == length
    return weighted.where(complete), complete


def _pooled_rolling_slope(
    predictor: pd.DataFrame,
    response: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series]:
    """Trailing pooled OLS slope with intercept, using only contemporaneous pairs."""
    pair = predictor.notna() & response.notna()
    x = predictor.where(pair, 0.0)
    y = response.where(pair, 0.0)

    daily_n = pair.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    daily_x = x.sum(axis=1)
    daily_y = y.sum(axis=1)
    daily_xx = (x * x).sum(axis=1)
    daily_xy = (x * y).sum(axis=1)

    n = daily_n.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sx = daily_x.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sy = daily_y.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sxx = daily_xx.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sxy = daily_xy.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()

    denominator = sxx - (sx * sx) / n.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    numerator = sxy - (sx * sy) / n.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    beta = numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return beta, n


def _industry_standardized_rank(
    raw: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize, percentile-rank, and standardize independently by industry."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=raw.index, columns=raw.columns)
    safe_labels = labels.fillna("__missing_industry__")

    for industry_name in pd.unique(safe_labels):
        columns = safe_labels.index[safe_labels == industry_name]
        subset = raw.loc[:, columns]
        lower = subset.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
        upper = subset.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
        clipped = subset.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        percentile = clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        mean_rank = percentile.mean(axis=1)
        std_rank = percentile.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        result.loc[:, columns] = percentile.sub(mean_rank, axis=0).div(std_rank, axis=0)

    return result


@register_factor
class MarkedPeerExcitationResponseDeficit(BaseFactor):
    """Industry-neutral deficit after marked peer return-volume events."""

    factor_id = "marked_peer_excitation_response_deficit"
    name = "Industry-Neutral Peer Event Response Deficit"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks stocks within industry by their shortfall versus the historically "
        "positive pooled response to recent, signed high-volume peer events, "
        "while suppressing names with their own event saturation."
    )
    window_length = 280
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry_frame = data["industry"]
        output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        # Industry is static metadata. Using the first available panel row avoids
        # any future-dependent label construction; names without an initial label
        # remain ineligible through the dynamic validity masks below.
        labels = industry_frame.iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        static_label_valid = labels.notna()
        current_label_valid = industry_frame.notna() & static_label_valid

        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        safe_volume = volume.where(volume >= 0.0)
        log_return = np.log(safe_close / safe_close.shift(1))
        log_volume = np.log1p(safe_volume)

        base_valid = (
            safe_close.notna()
            & safe_volume.notna()
            & current_label_valid
            & log_return.notna()
        )
        prior_valid_count = base_valid.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
        market_eligible = base_valid & (prior_valid_count >= 20.0)
        market_return = log_return.where(market_eligible).mean(axis=1)
        market_adjusted = log_return.sub(market_return, axis=0)

        prior_x = market_adjusted.shift(1)
        prior_v = log_volume.shift(1)
        mean_x = prior_x.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        std_x = prior_x.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std(ddof=0)
        mean_v = prior_v.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        std_v = prior_v.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std(ddof=0)

        event_eligible = (
            base_valid
            & market_return.notna().to_numpy()[:, None]
            & std_x.gt(0.0)
            & std_v.gt(0.0)
            & mean_x.notna()
            & mean_v.notna()
        )
        z_return = (market_adjusted - mean_x) / std_x.where(std_x > 0.0)
        z_volume = (log_volume - mean_v) / std_v.where(std_v > 0.0)
        event_mark = (
            np.sign(z_return)
            * (z_return.abs() - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
            * (z_volume - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        ).where(event_eligible)

        peer_event, peer_event_count = _leave_one_out_mean(
            event_mark,
            event_mark.notna() & current_label_valid,
            labels,
            5,
        )
        peer_intensity, peer_history_complete = _finite_exponential_mark(
            peer_event,
            0.80,
            20,
        )

        own_saturation, own_history_complete = _finite_exponential_mark(
            event_mark.abs(),
            0.80,
            20,
        )

        # At endpoint u this is the realized simple return over u-5,...,u.
        # Pairing it with P shifted six bars makes it the required outcome for
        # the peer signal observed at u-6, without any negative shift.
        six_log_sum = log_return.rolling(6, min_periods=6).sum()
        six_return = np.exp(six_log_sum) - 1.0
        six_observed = six_return.notna() & current_label_valid
        six_peer_return, _ = _leave_one_out_mean(six_return, six_observed, labels, 5)
        completed_response = six_return - six_peer_return

        # At t, these shifts expose completed endpoints t-252 through t-1,
        # corresponding exactly to signal dates t-258 through t-7.
        historical_predictor = peer_intensity.shift(7)
        historical_response = completed_response.shift(1)
        beta, observation_count = _pooled_rolling_slope(
            historical_predictor,
            historical_response,
            252,
        )
        active = beta.gt(0.0) & beta.notna() & observation_count.ge(1000.0)

        five_log_sum = log_return.rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
        five_return = np.exp(five_log_sum) - 1.0
        five_observed = five_return.notna() & current_label_valid
        five_peer_return, _ = _leave_one_out_mean(five_return, five_observed, labels, 5)
        realized_response = five_return - five_peer_return

        implied = peer_intensity.mul(beta, axis=0)
        deficit = (implied - realized_response) / (1.0 + own_saturation)
        usable = (
            active.to_numpy()[:, None]
            & peer_history_complete
            & own_history_complete
            & deficit.notna()
            & peer_event_count.ge(5.0)
        )
        ranked_input = deficit.where(usable)
        standardized = _industry_standardized_rank(ranked_input, labels)
        return standardized.where(usable, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Industry-Neutral Peer Event Response Deficit
programs.trading_idea: The revised mechanism is not mechanical cross-excitation from one stock to another, but delayed incorporation of unusually high-volume, industry-relevant information after removing the market and realized industry return. A stock is a candidate receiver only when its industry peers have recently generated signed abnormal return-volume events, its own industry-neutral response remains below the historically estimated response associated with such peer intensity, and it has not itself generated a large event that would indicate that the information is already incorporated. The strategy is active only when the rolling, strictly pre-signal relation between peer event intensity and subsequent industry-neutral returns is positive; otherwise the signal is set to zero rather than assuming continuation over reversal.
programs.description: At each close t, define log return r_i,t = log(close_i,t / close_i,t-1). Define the market return m_t as the equal-weighted return of tickers with valid close, volume, and industry data on t and at least 20 prior valid observations. For each stock define market-adjusted return x_i,t = r_i,t - m_t. Using only days t-20 through t-1, compute mu_x_i,t and sigma_x_i,t as the trailing mean and standard deviation of x, and compute mu_v_i,t and sigma_v_i,t from log(1 + volume). Define abnormal-return z-score zR_i,t = (x_i,t - mu_x_i,t) / sigma_x_i,t and abnormal-volume z-score zV_i,t = (log(1 + volume_i,t) - mu_v_i,t) / sigma_v_i,t; observations with zero or missing trailing standard deviation are ineligible. The signed event mark is E_i,t = sign(zR_i,t) * min(max(abs(zR_i,t) - 1, 0), 3) * min(max(zV_i,t - 1, 0), 3), so an event requires both an unusually large signed market-adjusted return and unusually high volume. The peer universe for stock i is all eligible stocks in i's static industry excluding i, requiring at least five peers. Let peer mark P_i,t = sum from k=0 to 19 of 0.80^k times the leave-one-out industry-average event mark E_peer(i),t-k. This fixed 20-day exponential kernel is not estimated on the evaluation sample. To map peer intensity into an implied six-day receiver return, estimate a single pooled rolling slope beta_t using only completed historical observations s from t-258 through t-7: regress Y_i,s on P_i,s with an intercept, where Y_i,s is stock i's cumulative return from s+1 through s+6 minus the equal-weighted cumulative return of its leave-one-out industry peers over those same six days. Thus every dependent-variable realization used in beta_t was fully known before t. Set implied remaining industry-neutral return I_i,t = beta_t * P_i,t. If beta_t is nonpositive, unavailable, or estimated from fewer than 1,000 stock-day observations, set all scores to zero. Measure realized receiver response R_i,t as stock i's cumulative return from t-4 through t minus the leave-one-out industry-peer cumulative return over t-4 through t. Measure own-event saturation A_i,t = sum from k=0 to 19 of 0.80^k * abs(E_i,t-k). The raw signed deficit is D_i,t = (I_i,t - R_i,t) / (1 + A_i,t): positive peer events with insufficient relative receiver appreciation produce positive scores, while negative peer events with insufficient relative receiver decline produce negative scores. Each day, winsorize D at the cross-sectional 2nd and 98th percentiles and rank it within industry; the final factor is the cross-sectional standardized within-industry rank, with high scores bought and low scores sold. Signals use the complete close and volume of day t, are formed only after the t close, and are traded no earlier than t+1; no full-sample parameter fitting is permitted.

programs.code:
"""Concentrated peer-event cascades with empirically validated response backlogs.

Mechanism: a localized industry event cascade is informative only when peer-event
intensity has historically transmitted into positive subsequent industry-relative
returns.  The factor buys receivers whose realized relative response remains below
their causally learned response to a concentrated peer shock.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _recursive_intensity(events: pd.DataFrame, decay: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponentially decayed marked-event intensity."""
    values = events.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    output = np.zeros_like(values, dtype=float)
    state = np.zeros(values.shape[1], dtype=float)
    for t in range(values.shape[0]):
        state = decay * state + values[t]
        output[t] = state
    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=events.index, columns=events.columns)


def _peer_statistics(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    minimum_peers: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Leave-one-out peer mean, absolute-intensity Herfindahl, and count."""
    peer_mean = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    concentration = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)

    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        columns = labels.index[labels == label]
        if len(columns) <= 1:
            continue
        eligible = valid.loc[:, columns].astype(float)
        group_values = values.loc[:, columns].where(eligible.astype(bool), 0.0)
        total = group_values.sum(axis=1)
        total_abs = group_values.abs().sum(axis=1)
        total_sq = (group_values.abs() ** 2).sum(axis=1)
        total_count = eligible.sum(axis=1)

        excluded = group_values.rsub(total, axis=0)
        excluded_abs = group_values.abs().rsub(total_abs, axis=0)
        excluded_sq = (group_values.abs() ** 2).rsub(total_sq, axis=0)
        excluded_count = eligible.rsub(total_count, axis=0)

        mean = excluded.div(excluded_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        herfindahl = excluded_sq.div((excluded_abs ** 2).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        peer_mean.loc[:, columns] = mean.where(excluded_count >= minimum_peers)
        concentration.loc[:, columns] = herfindahl.where(excluded_count >= minimum_peers)
        peer_count.loc[:, columns] = excluded_count

    return peer_mean, concentration, peer_count


def _rolling_slope(
    predictor: pd.DataFrame,
    response: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
    minimum_count: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing per-name OLS slope with intercept and pairwise missing handling."""
    paired = predictor.notna() & response.notna()
    x = predictor.where(paired, 0.0)
    y = response.where(paired, 0.0)
    count = paired.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_count).sum()
    sx = x.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_count).sum()
    sy = y.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_count).sum()
    sxx = (x * x).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_count).sum()
    sxy = (x * y).rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_count).sum()
    denominator = sxx - sx * sx.div(count.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    numerator = sxy - sx * sy.div(count.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    return numerator.div(denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(count >= minimum_count)


@register_factor
class ConcentratedPeerEfficacyBacklog(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "concentrated_peer_efficacy_backlog"
    name = "Concentrated Peer Efficacy Backlog"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks concentrated leave-one-out industry event cascades by the gap "
        "between a causally learned peer-response implication and the receiver's "
        "already realized industry-relative return."
    )
    window_length = 110
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        safe_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))
        ret = np.log(safe_close.div(safe_close.shift(1)))
        log_volume = np.log1p(safe_volume)
        valid = ret.notna() & log_volume.notna() & labels.notna().to_numpy()[None, :]

        market_return = ret.where(valid).mean(axis=1)
        abnormal = ret.sub(market_return, axis=0)
        prior_abnormal = abnormal.shift(1)
        prior_volume = log_volume.shift(1)
        abnormal_mean = prior_abnormal.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        abnormal_std = prior_abnormal.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        volume_mean = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        volume_std = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()

        z_return = abnormal.sub(abnormal_mean).div(abnormal_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        z_volume = log_volume.sub(volume_mean).div(volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        event = (
            np.sign(z_return)
            * (z_return.abs() - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
            * (z_volume - 0.75).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        ).where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        own_intensity = _recursive_intensity(event, 0.80)
        history_valid = valid.astype(float).rolling(20, min_periods=15).sum().ge(15.0)
        peer_intensity, herfindahl, peer_count = _peer_statistics(
            own_intensity, labels, history_valid, 5
        )

        diffuse_floor = 1.0 / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        concentration = (
            herfindahl.sub(diffuse_floor)
            .div((1.0 - diffuse_floor).replace(0.0, np.nan))
            .clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        )

        five_return = ret.rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
        peer_five, _, five_count = _peer_statistics(
            five_return, labels, five_return.notna() & valid, 5
        )
        realized_response = five_return - peer_five

        six_return = ret.rolling(6, min_periods=6).sum()
        peer_six, _, six_count = _peer_statistics(
            six_return, labels, six_return.notna() & valid, 5
        )
        completed_response = six_return - peer_six

        historical_predictor = peer_intensity.shift(7)
        historical_response = completed_response.shift(1)
        efficacy = _rolling_slope(historical_predictor, historical_response, 80, 50)
        efficacy = efficacy.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

        own_saturation = _recursive_intensity(event.abs(), 0.80)
        implied_response = efficacy * peer_intensity
        backlog = (implied_response - realized_response).div(1.0 + own_saturation)
        raw = concentration * backlog

        usable = (
            valid
            & peer_count.ge(5.0)
            & five_count.ge(5.0)
            & six_count.ge(5.0)
            & efficacy.gt(0.0)
            & raw.notna()
        )
        ranked = raw.where(usable).rank(axis=1, pct=True).sub(0.5)
        return ranked.where(usable, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
