"""This is a single-sided short signal, not a symmetric leader/laggard composite. A prior sector leader that experiences a high-participation, wide-range selloff closing near its low while an independently measured leave-one-out peer basket continues to advance is treated as a non-receiver of an ongoing sector demand impulse. The mandatory peer-impulse condition is intended to separate stock-specific adverse reassessment or distribution from a sector-wide reversal; the factor forecasts negative six-bar returns for selected names and is executed no earlier than the next bar."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_transform(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, operation: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Apply a cross-sectional transform independently within static sectors."""
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform(operation).T


def _sector_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Ascending average-tie ranks within each date-sector cross-section."""
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(method="average", ascending=True).T


@register_factor
class SectorImpulseNonreceiverDistribution(BaseFactor):
    """Short prior leaders suffering idiosyncratic distribution despite sector demand."""

    factor_id = "sector_impulse_nonreceiver_distribution"
    name = "Leave-One-Out Sector Impulse Non-Receiver"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Binary short-selection signal for prior sector leaders whose severe, "
        "high-participation distribution day contrasts with positive leave-one-out "
        "sector peer returns and breadth."
    )
    window_length = 66
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector_frame = data["sector"]

        # Sector is explicitly static. Filling labels only resolves sparse feed
        # representation and does not introduce a time-varying market datum.
        sector_labels = sector_frame.ffill().bfill().iloc[0]

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        daily_range = (high - low) / close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_range = daily_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()

        close_recent_positive = (
            close.rolling(21, min_periods=21).min() > 0.0
        )
        volume_recent_positive = (
            volume.rolling(21, min_periods=21).min() > 0.0
        )

        eligible = (
            close_recent_positive
            & volume_recent_positive
            & (close.shift(65) > 0.0)
            & (close.shift(5) > 0.0)
            & close.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & (high > low)
            & (prior_volume > 0.0)
            & (prior_range > 0.0)
            & sector_labels.notna()
        )

        leadership_return = close.shift(5) / close.shift(65).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        interruption_return = close / close.shift(5).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        abnormal_volume = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        range_ratio = daily_range / prior_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = (close - low) / (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        eligible_float = eligible.astype(float)
        sector_count = _sector_transform(eligible_float, sector_labels, "sum")
        peer_count = sector_count - eligible_float

        eligible_leadership = leadership_return.where(eligible)
        sector_leadership_sum = _sector_transform(
            eligible_leadership, sector_labels, "sum"
        )
        peer_leadership = (
            sector_leadership_sum - eligible_leadership
        ) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_leadership = leadership_return - peer_leadership

        leadership_rank = _sector_rank(eligible_leadership, sector_labels)
        leadership_percentile = leadership_rank / sector_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        eligible_interruption = interruption_return.where(eligible)
        sector_interruption_sum = _sector_transform(
            eligible_interruption, sector_labels, "sum"
        )
        peer_return = (
            sector_interruption_sum - eligible_interruption
        ) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        positive_interruption = (
            (interruption_return > 0.0) & eligible
        ).astype(float)
        sector_positive_count = _sector_transform(
            positive_interruption, sector_labels, "sum"
        )
        peer_breadth = (
            sector_positive_count - positive_interruption
        ) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        valid_peer_set = eligible & (peer_count >= 8.0)
        selected = (
            valid_peer_set
            & (leadership_percentile >= 0.70)
            & (relative_leadership > 0.0)
            & (interruption_return <= -0.05)
            & (abnormal_volume >= 1.50)
            & (range_ratio >= 1.50)
            & (close_location <= 0.25)
            & (peer_return >= 0.01)
            & (peer_breadth >= 0.60)
        )

        # Ineligible names and sectors without eight leave-one-out peers are
        # outside the signal universe; valid eligible names receive binary D.
        return selected.astype(float).where(valid_peer_set)

programs.trading_idea: This is a single-sided short signal, not a symmetric leader/laggard composite. A prior sector leader that experiences a high-participation, wide-range selloff closing near its low while an independently measured leave-one-out peer basket continues to advance is treated as a non-receiver of an ongoing sector demand impulse. The mandatory peer-impulse condition is intended to separate stock-specific adverse reassessment or distribution from a sector-wide reversal; the factor forecasts negative six-bar returns for selected names and is executed no earlier than the next bar.
programs.description: At the close of bar t, form the signal using only bars dated t or earlier; earliest execution is at t+1. A stock i is eligible only if close is positive and non-missing at t-65, t-20 through t, and t-5; volume is positive and non-missing at t-20 through t; high, low, and close are non-missing at t; high_t > low_t; and the following prior-20-bar averages are positive: mean(volume[t-20:t-1]) and mean((high-low)/close[t-1] over bars t-20:t-1). Define E_t as all eligible stocks. For stock i, define P_i,t as eligible stocks in E_t with the same static sector label as i, excluding i. Require at least 8 leave-one-out peers, |P_i,t| >= 8; otherwise i receives NaN. Define prior leadership return LRet_i,t = close_i,t-5 / close_i,t-65 - 1. For every j in the same eligible sector, compute LRet_j,t identically. Define leadership percentile LPct_i,t as the ascending fractional rank of LRet_i,t among all eligible stocks in i's sector, using average ranks for ties divided by the sector eligible count. Define relative prior leadership RelLead_i,t = LRet_i,t - mean(LRet_j,t for j in P_i,t). A stock is a prior leader only if LPct_i,t >= 0.70 and RelLead_i,t > 0. Define interruption return IR_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-5 - 1. Define abnormal-volume ratio AV_i,t = volume_i,t / mean(volume_i,t-20:t-1). Define daily range ratio Range_i,t = ((high_i,t-low_i,t)/close_i,t-1) / mean((high_i,s-low_i,s)/close_i,s-1 for s=t-20,...,t-1). Define close location CL_i,t = (close_i,t-low_i,t)/(high_i,t-low_i,t). For each peer j, define peer interruption return IR_j,t = close_j,t / close_j,t-5 - 1. Define leave-one-out peer return PeerRet_i,t = mean(IR_j,t for j in P_i,t) and peer breadth PeerBreadth_i,t = count(IR_j,t > 0 for j in P_i,t)/|P_i,t|. The binary factor is D_i,t = 1 if, jointly: prior-leader conditions hold; IR_i,t <= -0.05; AV_i,t >= 1.50; Range_i,t >= 1.50; CL_i,t <= 0.25; PeerRet_i,t >= 0.01; and PeerBreadth_i,t >= 0.60. Otherwise D_i,t = 0 for eligible stocks. No laggard-rebound counterpart is included. Aggregation is a strict logical AND rather than a tunable weighted composite: selected stocks are the D=1 cross-section and are the short side. The concrete distinction from sector_rank_interrupt_distribution_unwind is that this construction requires a quantitatively positive, leave-one-out sector impulse simultaneously in both equal-weight peer return and peer breadth, while defining leadership exclusively from the completed t-65 to t-5 interval and the interruption exclusively from t-5 to t; it does not infer sector support from a broad sector rank or use a symmetric reversal leg.

"""Peer earnings read-through conditioned on cash-confirmation state.

Mechanism: coherent peer EPS events transmit industry information to non-reporting
receivers.  The receiver follows that information only when its own cash conversion
and revenue-estimate state corroborate the shock; expensive EPS optimism unsupported
by cash instead turns the peer catalyst into an extrapolation-reversal setup.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _finite(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return df.astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _peer_eps_impulse(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_actual: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal coherent peer-event impulse and non-reporter recipient mask."""
    ret = close.pct_change()
    prior_actual = eps_actual.shift(1)
    update = eps_actual.notna() & (prior_actual.isna() | eps_actual.ne(prior_actual))
    fresh = update & eps_surprise.notna() & ret.notna() & industry.notna()

    impulse = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    recipient = pd.DataFrame(False, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    for timestamp in close.index:
        labels = industry.loc[timestamp]
        valid_labels = labels.dropna()
        row_ret = ret.loc[timestamp]
        row_surprise = eps_surprise.loc[timestamp]
        row_fresh = fresh.loc[timestamp]
        row_update = update.loc[timestamp]
        shocks: dict[object, float] = {}

        for label, members in valid_labels.groupby(valid_labels).groups.items():
            names = list(members)
            event_names = [name for name in names if bool(row_fresh.loc[name])]
            if len(event_names) < 3:
                continue
            event_ret = row_ret.loc[event_names]
            event_surprise = row_surprise.loc[event_names]
            mean_ret = event_ret.mean()
            if not np.isfinite(mean_ret) or mean_ret == 0.0:
                continue
            direction = float(np.sign(mean_ret))
            return_agreement = (np.sign(event_ret) == direction).mean()
            surprise_agreement = (np.sign(event_surprise) == direction).mean()
            if return_agreement >= (2.0 / 3.0) and surprise_agreement >= (2.0 / 3.0):
                shocks[label] = float(mean_ret)

        if not shocks:
            continue
        cutoff = pd.Series([abs(x) for x in shocks.values()]).quantile(0.60)
        for label, shock in shocks.items():
            if not np.isfinite(cutoff) or abs(shock) < cutoff:
                continue
            names = labels.index[(labels == label) & (~row_update)]
            if len(names) > 0:
                impulse.loc[timestamp, names] = shock
                recipient.loc[timestamp, names] = True

    return impulse, recipient


def _centered_rank(value: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robust cross-sectional centered rank restricted to a valid universe."""
    masked = value.where(mask).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lo = masked.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    hi = masked.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    clipped = masked.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)
    return clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True).sub(0.5)


@register_factor
class PeerCashStateExtrapolationSwitch(BaseFactor):
    """Switch peer-event continuation into reversal when cash evidence conflicts."""

    factor_id = "peer_cash_state_extrapolation_switch"
    name = "Peer Shock Cash-State Switch"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks delayed non-reporter responses to coherent industry EPS events after "
        "switching peer-news continuation into a fade when cash conversion, revenue "
        "revisions, valuation, and EPS narrative are mutually inconsistent."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "marketCap",
        "evToSales",
        "epsActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "netIncome",
        "operatingCashFlow",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _finite(data["close"])
        volume = _finite(data["volume"])
        market_cap = _finite(data["marketCap"])
        ev_to_sales = _finite(data["evToSales"])
        eps_actual = _finite(data["epsActual"])
        eps_surprise = _finite(data["epsSurprise"])
        eps_estimate = _finite(data["epsEstimate"])
        revenue_estimate = _finite(data["revenueEstimate"])
        net_income = _finite(data["netIncome"])
        operating_cash_flow = _finite(data["operatingCashFlow"])
        industry = data["industry"]

        peer_impulse, peer_recipient = _peer_eps_impulse(
            close, eps_actual, eps_surprise, industry
        )
        direction = np.sign(peer_impulse)
        ret = close.pct_change()

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0))
        prior_median_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).median().shift(1)
        abnormal_volume = dollar_volume / prior_median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        lag_close = close.shift(1)
        eps_lag = eps_estimate.shift(63)
        revenue_lag = revenue_estimate.shift(63)
        income_lag = net_income.shift(63)
        cash_lag = operating_cash_flow.shift(63)

        eligible = (
            peer_recipient
            & close.gt(5.0)
            & lag_close.gt(0.0)
            & market_cap.gt(0.0)
            & ev_to_sales.gt(0.0)
            & eps_estimate.notna()
            & eps_lag.notna()
            & revenue_estimate.notna()
            & revenue_lag.notna()
            & net_income.gt(0.0)
            & income_lag.gt(0.0)
            & operating_cash_flow.notna()
            & cash_lag.notna()
        )

        eps_revision = (eps_estimate - eps_lag) / lag_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        revenue_revision = (revenue_estimate - revenue_lag) / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        cash_change = (
            operating_cash_flow / net_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            - cash_lag / income_lag.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        valuation = np.log(ev_to_sales.where(ev_to_sales.gt(0.0)))

        rank_eps = _centered_rank(eps_revision, eligible)
        rank_revenue = _centered_rank(revenue_revision, eligible)
        rank_cash = _centered_rank(cash_change, eligible)
        rank_value = _centered_rank(valuation, eligible)

        peer_abs = peer_impulse.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        underreaction = (direction * ret) <= (0.50 * peer_abs)
        early_assimilation = (direction * ret > 0.0) & abnormal_volume.ge(1.0)

        cash_revenue_alignment = direction * (rank_cash + rank_revenue) / 2.0
        positive_peer_narrative_fragility = (
            (direction > 0.0).astype(float)
            * (rank_eps - rank_revenue - rank_cash + rank_value)
        )
        state_switch = cash_revenue_alignment - positive_peer_narrative_fragility

        active = (
            eligible
            & underreaction
            & early_assimilation
            & abnormal_volume.notna()
            & state_switch.notna()
        )
        raw_score = (
            direction
            * peer_abs
            * state_switch
            * abnormal_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        ).where(active)

        output = raw_score.rank(axis=1, pct=True).where(raw_score.notna(), 0.0)
        return output.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Coherent peer EPS-surprise shocks create a read-through signal, but recipients need not react in the same direction: the peer-information move should continue when the recipient's own cash conversion and revenue-estimate state corroborate that direction. When a positive peer shock reaches an expensive recipient with an EPS-upgrade narrative but deteriorating cash realization and unconfirmed revenue, peer news instead intensifies extrapolation bias and should be faded; the symmetric logic applies to negative shocks resisted by strong cash and revenue evidence. Thus the child uses Parent A's delayed industry information transmission as the catalyst and Parent B's cash-versus-headline state as a directional switch, identifying continuation versus correction rather than treating all peer underreaction alike.
programs.description: The factor detects coherent same-day industry EPS-surprise baskets, selects non-reporting recipients that have underreacted but begun to trade in the peer direction on elevated turnover, and then applies a cash/revenue-confirmation versus expensive EPS-narrative switch. High scores indicate peer-news continuation supported by the recipient's own fundamental state, while low scores indicate likely narrative-extrapolation reversal.

"""Investors and news-driven strategies initially extrapolate the sign of an earnings or revenue surprise, but often underweight whether the reported result is supported by improving cash conversion rather than receivables or inventory accumulation. Go long disappointing headline reports accompanied by a material improvement in cash conversion and short positive headline reports accompanied by a material deterioration in cash conversion, as fundamental investors process the quality of the result over the following week. The inefficiency persists because fast headline traders, passive flows, and constrained benchmarked investors react to the salient surprise, whereas detailed working-capital reconciliation is slower and costly to perform."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _update_mask(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify point-in-time fundamental step updates using only t and t-1."""
    previous = df.shift(1)
    return df.notna() & previous.notna() & df.ne(previous)


def _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise median/MAD score with standard-deviation fallback."""
    median = df.median(axis=1)
    centered = df.sub(median, axis=0)
    mad = centered.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    fallback = df.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad.where(mad > 1.0e-12, fallback)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 1.0e-12)
    return centered.div(scale, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _event_change_score(
    level: pd.DataFrame,
    event: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Standardize fresh quarterly changes against prior observed changes.

    The rolling dispersion is calculated only from prior report-to-report moves,
    rather than treating the many forward-filled daily observations as data.
    """
    change = level.diff().where(event)
    history = change.rolling(lookback, min_periods=2).std()
    scaled = change / history.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    # Early in a company's history there may be fewer than two prior updates.
    # Raw day changes are then still normalized cross-sectionally below.
    usable = scaled.where(scaled.notna(), change)
    return _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(usable)


@register_factor
class CashCycleHeadlineConflictAssimilation(BaseFactor):
    """Headline-surprise conflict with newly reported cash-conversion quality."""

    factor_id = "cashcycle_headline_conflict_assimilation"
    name = "Cash-Cycle Headline Conflict"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Activated on fresh quarterly reports, this factor identifies disagreement "
        "between standardized EPS/revenue headline surprises and cash-conversion "
        "quality. It is positive for negative surprises with improving cash "
        "realization and negative for positive surprises with worsening cash "
        "realization, with operating-cash-flow direction as confirmation."
    )
    window_length = 504
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "cashConversionCycle",
        "operatingCashFlow",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        cash_cycle = data["cashConversionCycle"]
        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"]

        eps_event = _update_mask(eps_surprise)
        revenue_event = _update_mask(revenue_surprise)
        headline_event = eps_event | revenue_event
        cash_cycle_event = _update_mask(cash_cycle)
        ocf_event = _update_mask(operating_cash_flow)

        eps_z = _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(eps_surprise)
        revenue_z = _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(revenue_surprise)
        headline_count = eps_z.notna().astype(float) + revenue_z.notna().astype(float)
        headline = (eps_z.fillna(0.0) + revenue_z.fillna(0.0)).div(
            headline_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        # A decline in days outstanding/inventory net of payables is an improvement.
        cash_cycle_change = _event_change_score(cash_cycle, cash_cycle_event, 504)
        cash_realization = -cash_cycle_change

        # OCF confirmation is intentionally directional: it supplements the detailed
        # working-capital measure without allowing different company sizes to dominate.
        ocf_direction = np.sign(operating_cash_flow.diff()).where(ocf_event, 0.0)
        quality = 0.80 * cash_realization + 0.20 * ocf_direction

        # Retain only genuine disagreement.  A negative headline paired with positive
        # quality is long; a positive headline paired with negative quality is short.
        opposition = (-np.sign(headline) * quality).clip(lower=0.0)
        conflict = -headline * opposition

        active = headline_event & cash_cycle_event & headline.notna() & quality.notna()
        result = conflict.where(active, 0.0)
        result = result.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return result.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

"""Peer-echo cash-quality contrarian factor.

Mechanism: headline traders extrapolate an earnings surprise more aggressively when
liquid industry leaders move in the same direction.  When that consensus narrative
conflicts with newly disclosed cash-conversion quality, the reinforced initial
reaction is prone to a near-term correction.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _update_mask(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally identify a new point-in-time fundamental observation."""
    prior = value.shift(1)
    return value.notna() & prior.notna() & value.ne(prior)


def _robust_cs_zscore(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional median/MAD standardization with a standard-dev fallback."""
    location = value.median(axis=1)
    centered = value.sub(location, axis=0)
    mad_scale = 1.4826 * centered.abs().median(axis=1)
    std_scale = value.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad_scale.where(mad_scale.gt(1.0e-12), std_scale)
    scale = scale.where(scale.gt(1.0e-12))
    return centered.div(scale, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _event_change_quality(level: pd.DataFrame, event: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Standardize report-to-report changes using only trailing disclosed history."""
    change = level.diff().where(event)
    history = change.rolling(378, min_periods=2).std()
    normalized = change.div(history.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    normalized = normalized.where(normalized.notna(), change)
    return _robust_cs_zscore(normalized)


def _liquid_peer_impulse(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Leave-self-out three-bar return of liquid industry leaders.

    Leader eligibility is determined from prior trailing dollar volume, avoiding
    contemporaneous selection on the current response.  The peer return is scaled
    by each recipient's own trailing volatility.
    """
    safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
    ret = safe_close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
    three_bar = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
    dollar_adv = (close * volume).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
    own_vol = ret.shift(1).rolling(30, min_periods=12).std()

    labels = industry.ffill().iloc[-1].astype(object)
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "__UNKNOWN__")
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    for _, member_index in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        members = list(member_index)
        if len(members) < 2:
            continue
        adv_block = dollar_adv.loc[:, members]
        leader = adv_block.rank(axis=1, pct=True).ge(0.65) & adv_block.gt(0.0)
        weights = adv_block.where(leader, 0.0)
        weighted_return = weights * three_bar.loc[:, members]
        total_weight = weights.sum(axis=1)
        total_return = weighted_return.sum(axis=1)

        peer_weight = total_weight.to_frame().reindex(columns=members).sub(weights)
        peer_return = total_return.to_frame().reindex(columns=members).sub(weighted_return)
        peer_mean = peer_return.div(peer_weight.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        output.loc[:, members] = peer_mean.div(own_vol.loc[:, members])

    return output.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class PeerEchoCashqualityContrarian(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "peer_echo_cashquality_contrarian"
    name = "Peer-Echo Cash-Quality Contrarian"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Fresh headline-surprise versus cash-conversion conflicts are traded only "
        "when leave-self-out liquid industry leaders reinforce the headline's "
        "direction, identifying an extrapolative peer echo."
    )
    window_length = 378
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "cashConversionCycle",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].astype(float)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].astype(float)
        cash_cycle = data["cashConversionCycle"].astype(float)

        eps_event = _update_mask(eps_surprise)
        revenue_event = _update_mask(revenue_surprise)
        headline_event = eps_event | revenue_event
        cash_event = _update_mask(cash_cycle)

        eps_z = _robust_cs_zscore(eps_surprise)
        revenue_z = _robust_cs_zscore(revenue_surprise)
        count = eps_z.notna().astype(float) + revenue_z.notna().astype(float)
        headline = (eps_z.fillna(0.0) + revenue_z.fillna(0.0)).div(
            count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        # A decline in the cash-conversion cycle is an improvement in realization.
        cash_quality = -_event_change_quality(cash_cycle, cash_event)
        opposition = (-np.sign(headline) * cash_quality).clip(lower=0.0)
        fundamental_conflict = -headline * opposition

        peer_impulse = _liquid_peer_impulse(
            close,
            data["volume"].astype(float),
            data["industry"],
        )
        headline_concordance = peer_impulse.mul(np.sign(headline))
        echo_strength = headline_concordance.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).div(3.0)

        active = headline_event & cash_event & headline.notna() & cash_quality.notna()
        signal = (fundamental_conflict * echo_strength).where(active, 0.0)
        return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).reindex(
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

programs.trading_idea: A reported earnings or revenue surprise can be mispriced when it conflicts with the contemporaneous change in cash conversion: weak headlines with improving cash realization and strong headlines with worsening realization are particularly vulnerable to reversal. The child factor activates this conflict only when liquid industry peers are moving in the headline-consistent direction, indicating that peer read-through and momentum traders are reinforcing the salient narrative rather than evaluating its accounting quality. This interaction creates a short-horizon edge neither parent has alone: cash-cycle disagreement identifies the hidden fundamental contradiction, while leader-peer confirmation identifies when the market has most aggressively extrapolated the wrong headline.

Scale it by a leave-self-out, liquidity-weighted industry-leader return impulse only when that peer impulse agrees with the headline direction.

programs.code:
"""Cash-conversion conflict repaired after peer-supported headline extrapolation.

A report's accounting-quality contradiction is most actionable when the immediate
headline reaction is reinforced by industry momentum, because peer flow makes the
salient interpretation temporarily more crowded than the cash-flow interpretation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _update_mask(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    previous = values.shift(1)
    return values.notna() & previous.notna() & values.ne(previous)


def _robust_cs_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    clean = values.where(np.isfinite(values))
    median = clean.median(axis=1)
    centered = clean.sub(median, axis=0)
    mad_scale = centered.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    std_scale = clean.std(axis=1, ddof=0)
    scale = mad_scale.where(mad_scale.gt(1.0e-10), std_scale)
    return centered.div(scale.where(scale.gt(1.0e-10)), axis=0)


def _industry_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date industry mean, requiring at least three observable members."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for _, member_index in labels.groupby(labels, sort=False).groups.items():
        members = list(member_index)
        block = values.loc[:, members]
        count = block.notna().sum(axis=1)
        average = block.mean(axis=1).where(count.ge(3))
        result.loc[:, members] = np.repeat(average.to_numpy()[:, None], len(members), axis=1)
    return result


@register_factor
class CashcyclePeerExtrapolationRepair(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cashcycle_peer_extrapolation_repair"
    name = "Cash-Cycle Peer Extrapolation Repair"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Trades fresh headline/cash-cycle conflicts only while stock-specific and "
        "industry price momentum continue to extrapolate the contradictory headline."
    )
    window_length = 42
    inputs = ["close", "industry", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise", "cashConversionCycle"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        cash_cycle = data["cashConversionCycle"]

        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].astype(object).copy()
        missing = labels.isna()
        if missing.any():
            labels.loc[missing] = ["__single_" + str(x) for x in labels.index[missing]]

        eps_event = _update_mask(eps_surprise)
        revenue_event = _update_mask(revenue_surprise)
        headline_event = eps_event | revenue_event
        cash_event = _update_mask(cash_cycle)

        eps_z = _robust_cs_zscore(eps_surprise)
        revenue_z = _robust_cs_zscore(revenue_surprise)
        available = eps_z.notna().astype(float) + revenue_z.notna().astype(float)
        headline = (eps_z.fillna(0.0) + revenue_z.fillna(0.0)).div(available.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        cash_change = cash_cycle.diff().where(cash_event)
        quality = -_robust_cs_zscore(cash_change)
        conflict = (-headline * quality).where(headline.mul(quality).lt(0.0))
        fresh = headline_event & cash_event & conflict.notna()

        # Preserve the report-state direction through the week in which delayed
        # fundamental reconciliation is expected, without using future observations.
        active_conflict = conflict.where(fresh).ffill(limit=4)
        active_headline = headline.where(fresh).ffill(limit=4)

        returns = close.pct_change()
        stock_move = close.pct_change(3)
        industry_daily = _industry_mean(returns, labels)
        industry_move = industry_daily.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
        residual_move = stock_move - industry_move

        residual_scale = residual_move.rolling(21, min_periods=10).std()
        industry_scale = industry_move.rolling(21, min_periods=10).std()
        residual_z = residual_move.div(residual_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        industry_z = industry_move.div(industry_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        # Both the idiosyncratic reaction and the peer basket must have moved in
        # the salient-headline direction; otherwise there is no crowded narrative
        # for the cash-quality signal to repair.
        idio_extrapolation = (np.sign(active_headline) * residual_z).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        peer_extrapolation = (np.sign(active_headline) * industry_z).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        raw = active_conflict * idio_extrapolation * peer_extrapolation

        active = active_conflict.notna() & idio_extrapolation.gt(0.0) & peer_extrapolation.gt(0.0)
        score = _robust_cs_zscore(raw.where(active)).where(active, 0.0)
        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).reindex(
            index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        ).astype(float)

A negative surprise with improving cash conversion becomes especially attractive when both the stock and its industry have sold off, while a positive surprise with worsening conversion is most fragile after a peer-supported rally. """Analysts can update a firm's active-quarter revenue consensus before fully incorporating the earnings impact implied by the firm's pre-existing unit economics. The signal converts the sales-consensus revision into an explicitly per-share, after-tax EPS revision using a predetermined historical contribution-margin proxy, then trades the residual between that implied EPS revision and the observed EPS-consensus revision. A positive residual indicates EPS consensus has revised less upward than the sales revision mechanically implies; the symmetric negative residual identifies EPS consensus that has revised less downward than implied."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _clean_numeric(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Replace non-finite numeric observations with missing values."""
    return df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _trailing_tax_rate(
    income_before_tax: pd.DataFrame,
    income_tax_expense: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute a causal 63-bar eligible-tax mean, defaulting only with no history."""
    pretax_safe = income_before_tax.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    tax_ratio = (income_tax_expense / pretax_safe).clip(0.0, 0.50)
    eligible = (
        (income_before_tax > 0.0)
        & (revenue > 0.0)
        & (income_before_tax > 0.01 * revenue)
        & tax_ratio.notna()
    )
    eligible_tax = tax_ratio.where(eligible)
    tax_mean = eligible_tax.rolling(63, min_periods=1).mean()
    eligible_count = eligible_tax.rolling(63, min_periods=1).count()
    return tax_mean.where(eligible_count > 0.0, 0.25)


def _winsorized_sector_rank(
    signal: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize each date cross-sectionally, then percentile-rank within sector."""
    lower = signal.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    upper = signal.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    winsorized = signal.T.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=1).T

    # Sector is static in this feed.  Using the first available row avoids any
    # dependence on future market or estimate observations.
    sector_labels = sector.iloc[0].astype(object).where(
        sector.iloc[0].notna(), "__unknown_sector__"
    )
    return winsorized.T.groupby(sector_labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True).T


@register_factor
class CostStructureEstimatePassthroughGap(BaseFactor):
    """Revenue-revision EPS passthrough residual ranked within sector."""

    factor_id = "cost_structure_estimate_passthrough_gap"
    name = "Margin-Implied EPS Revision Residual"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional sector rank of the price-normalized gap between an "
        "after-tax, contribution-margin-implied EPS revision from active-quarter "
        "sales consensus and the observed active-quarter EPS consensus revision."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsEstimate",
        "sharesOutstanding",
        "grossMargin",
        "sgaToRevenue",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "revenue",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _clean_numeric(data["close"])
        revenue_estimate = _clean_numeric(data["revenueEstimate"])
        eps_estimate = _clean_numeric(data["epsEstimate"])
        shares = _clean_numeric(data["sharesOutstanding"])
        gross_margin = _clean_numeric(data["grossMargin"])
        sga_to_revenue = _clean_numeric(data["sgaToRevenue"])
        income_before_tax = _clean_numeric(data["incomeBeforeTax"])
        income_tax_expense = _clean_numeric(data["incomeTaxExpense"])
        revenue = _clean_numeric(data["revenue"])

        gross_mean = gross_margin.rolling(63, min_periods=42).mean()
        sga_mean = sga_to_revenue.rolling(63, min_periods=42).mean()
        tax_rate = _trailing_tax_rate(
            income_before_tax, income_tax_expense, revenue
        )
        incremental_margin = (
            (gross_mean - sga_mean) * (1.0 - tax_rate)
        ).clip(-0.25, 0.60)

        revenue_revision = revenue_estimate - revenue_estimate.shift(21)
        eps_revision = eps_estimate - eps_estimate.shift(21)
        implied_eps_revision = revenue_revision * incremental_margin / shares.replace(
            0.0, np.nan
        )
        raw_gap = (implied_eps_revision - eps_revision) / close.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        endpoint_fields = [
            revenue_estimate,
            eps_estimate,
            close,
            shares,
            gross_margin,
            sga_to_revenue,
            income_before_tax,
            income_tax_expense,
            revenue,
        ]
        valid = pd.DataFrame(True, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for field in endpoint_fields:
            valid = valid & field.notna() & field.shift(21).notna()

        valid = (
            valid
            & (close > 0.0)
            & (shares > 0.0)
            & gross_mean.notna()
            & sga_mean.notna()
            & tax_rate.notna()
        )
        raw_gap = raw_gap.where(valid)

        ranked = _winsorized_sector_rank(raw_gap, data["sector"])
        return ranked.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: Analysts can update a firm's active-quarter revenue consensus before fully incorporating the earnings impact implied by the firm's pre-existing unit economics. The signal converts the sales-consensus revision into an explicitly per-share, after-tax EPS revision using a predetermined historical contribution-margin proxy, then trades the residual between that implied EPS revision and the observed EPS-consensus revision. A positive residual indicates EPS consensus has revised less upward than the sales revision mechanically implies; the symmetric negative residual identifies EPS consensus that has revised less downward than implied.
programs.description: At date t, use the feed's single point-in-time latest active fiscal-quarter consensus series for revenueEstimate and epsEstimate, requiring both estimates, close, sharesOutstanding, grossMargin, sgaToRevenue, incomeBeforeTax, incomeTaxExpense, and their t-21-bar values to be valid. The fixed revision window is 21 daily bars: dR = revenueEstimate_t - revenueEstimate_(t-21) and dEPS = epsEstimate_t - epsEstimate_(t-21). To avoid a dimensionally invalid dollar-versus-per-share comparison, convert dR into implied per-share EPS change: implied_dEPS = dR * m_t / sharesOutstanding_t. The predetermined incremental after-tax margin m_t is computed as clip((mean_63d(grossMargin) - mean_63d(sgaToRevenue)) * (1 - tax_t), -0.25, 0.60), where each 63-day mean requires at least 42 valid observations; tax_t is the 63-day mean of clip(incomeTaxExpense / incomeBeforeTax, 0, 0.50) using only observations with positive incomeBeforeTax greater than 1% of revenue, and defaults to 0.25 only when no eligible tax observation exists. This construction uses no revenue, EPS, or margin denominator that can become unstable near zero; names with nonpositive sharesOutstanding or close are excluded. Define the raw signal as G = (implied_dEPS - dEPS) / close_t, which is an earnings-yield-revision residual. Each day, winsorize G cross-sectionally at the 5th and 95th percentiles and rank it within sector; go long the highest-ranked names and short the lowest-ranked names, so the sign is symmetric for positive and negative revenue revisions. The active-period rule is the feed-defined latest-quarter consensus available at each date; observations with missing endpoint estimates are excluded rather than filled, preventing stale or unavailable estimate histories from entering the 21-bar revision. This is not an exact duplicate of cash_backed_upgrade_inventory_discount or translation_resolution_delivery_impulse: those signals use cash-conversion or subsequent delivery confirmation around revisions, whereas this signal is the contemporaneous, price-normalized residual of an explicitly specified revenue-to-after-tax-EPS mapping using gross margin, SG&A intensity, tax, and point-in-time shares.

"""Peer earnings disclosures can provide economically relevant, directionally signed information about near-term demand and operating conditions for firms with the same industry exposure that have not yet reported. The revised mechanism does not assume that peer news creates a separate valuation, cash-flow, anchoring, or overhead-supply unwind; it predicts that non-reporting peers move in the direction of a coherent, public industry-level earnings-and-revenue surprise. This shortens the causal chain to information propagation and avoids imposing an unsupported universally negative sign."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_event_scores(
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    reporter_quality: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute causal daily industry mean-surprise events and broadcast them.

    A valid event has at least three usable reporters, a two-thirds directional
    sign consensus, and an absolute mean quality-adjusted surprise of 0.15.
    Each row is independent and only contains information available on that bar.
    """
    output = np.full(reporter_quality.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)

    for row_number in range(len(reporter_quality.index)):
        industry_row = industry.iloc[row_number]
        quality_row = reporter_quality.iloc[row_number]

        observations = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "industry": industry_row,
                "quality": quality_row,
            }
        ).dropna(subset=["industry", "quality"])

        if observations.empty:
            continue

        observations["positive"] = (observations["quality"] > 0.0).astype(float)
        observations["negative"] = (observations["quality"] < 0.0).astype(float)

        grouped = observations.groupby("industry").agg(
            count=("quality", "count"),
            mean_quality=("quality", "mean"),
            positive=("positive", "sum"),
            negative=("negative", "sum"),
        )

        consensus = (
            (grouped["positive"] / grouped["count"] >= (2.0 / 3.0))
            | (grouped["negative"] / grouped["count"] >= (2.0 / 3.0))
        )
        valid = (
            (grouped["count"] >= 3.0)
            & consensus
            & (grouped["mean_quality"].abs() >= 0.15)
        )

        valid_means = grouped.loc[valid, "mean_quality"]
        if not valid_means.empty:
            output[row_number, :] = industry_row.map(valid_means).to_numpy(dtype=float)

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=reporter_quality.index, columns=reporter_quality.columns)


@register_factor
class DirectionalPeerFundamentalReadthrough(BaseFactor):
    """Signed industry earnings-surprise propagation to non-reporting peers."""

    factor_id = "peer_readthrough_model_risk_supply_unwind"
    name = "Directional Peer Fundamental Readthrough"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks non-reporting firms by the signed mean earnings and revenue "
        "surprise of a coherent same-industry reporter group, subject to a "
        "five-bar own-report blackout."
    )
    window_length = 6
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        industry = data["industry"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex(
            index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        )
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex(
            index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        )

        prior_eps_surprise = eps_surprise.shift(1)
        prior_revenue_surprise = revenue_surprise.shift(1)
        eps_report = eps_surprise.notna() & (
            prior_eps_surprise.isna() | eps_surprise.ne(prior_eps_surprise)
        )
        revenue_report = revenue_surprise.notna() & (
            prior_revenue_surprise.isna()
            | revenue_surprise.ne(prior_revenue_surprise)
        )
        reporter_flag = eps_report | revenue_report

        usable = (
            np.isfinite(eps_estimate)
            & np.isfinite(revenue_estimate)
            & np.isfinite(eps_surprise)
            & np.isfinite(revenue_surprise)
            & (eps_estimate.abs() > 0.0)
            & (revenue_estimate.abs() > 0.0)
            & reporter_flag
        )

        normalized_eps = (eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs()).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        normalized_revenue = (revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs()).clip(-0.25, 0.25)

        eps_percentile = normalized_eps.where(usable).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        revenue_percentile = normalized_revenue.where(usable).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        reporter_quality = 0.5 * eps_percentile + 0.5 * revenue_percentile - 0.5

        industry_score = _industry_event_scores(industry, reporter_quality)

        recent_own_reports = (
            reporter_flag.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum().eq(0.0)
        )
        eligible = recent_own_reports & industry_score.notna()
        raw_receiver_score = industry_score.where(eligible)

        ranked = 2.0 * raw_receiver_score.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        return ranked.where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0).astype(float)

An industry event is valid only when at least three usable reporters exist, at least two-thirds have the same sign of q, and abs(mean(q))>=0.15. Its signed readthrough statistic is I=mean(q) across those reporters; direction is explicitly used, unlike the original absolute-informativeness trigger. Orders are formed only after bar t has closed and entered at the next tradable bar's open, t+1, so same-day close, volume, and after-close report information is never used for same-day execution. The original EPS-optimism, revenue-growth, cash-realization, valuation, and volume-cost-basis/overhead-inventory gates are intentionally removed: no epsEstimate revision, revenueGrowth, incomeQuality/freeCashFlow proxy, peRatio/earningsYield valuation metric, or price-volume inventory measure enters the score. This implementation fingerprint is therefore a signed, minimum-three-reporter, industry-mean surprise propagation signal with a fixed own-report blackout, rather than an interaction of peer shocks with receiver revisions, cash quality, valuation, or reference-price overhang.

The original EPS-optimism, revenue-growth, cash-realization, valuation, and volume-cost-basis/overhead-inventory gates are intentionally removed: no epsEstimate revision, revenueGrowth, incomeQuality/freeCashFlow proxy, peRatio/earningsYield valuation metric, or price-volume inventory measure enters the score. This implementation fingerprint is therefore a signed, minimum-three-reporter, industry-mean surprise propagation signal with a fixed own-report blackout, rather than an interaction of peer shocks with receiver revisions, cash quality, valuation, or reference-price overhang.

"""Cash-quality disagreement timed by post-report pressure exhaustion.

Mechanism: headline-oriented traders react rapidly to earnings and revenue surprises,
while cash-conversion reconciliation is slower.  A headline-consistent move that was
volume-supported but has already lost participation is more likely temporary when the
new cash-cycle information contradicts the headline interpretation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_update(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time report availability/update mask, including a first observation."""
    previous = values.shift(1)
    return values.notna() & (previous.isna() | values.ne(previous))


def _robust_cs_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date median/MAD standardization with a standard-deviation fallback."""
    median = values.median(axis=1)
    centered = values.sub(median, axis=0)
    mad_scale = centered.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    std_scale = values.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad_scale.where(mad_scale > 1.0e-12, std_scale)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 1.0e-12)
    return centered.div(scale, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class CashcycleConflictPressureRelease(BaseFactor):
    """Time cash-quality disagreement after headline-flow participation fades."""

    factor_id = "cashcycle_conflict_pressure_release"
    name = "Cash-Quality Pressure Release"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Three bars after a fresh report, trades the cash-conversion interpretation "
        "only when the two-bar headline-consistent price response had elevated "
        "participation but current turnover and price extension have faded."
    )
    window_length = 30
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "cashConversionCycle",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].copy()
        high = data["high"].reindex_like(close)
        low = data["low"].reindex_like(close)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(close)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        cash_cycle = data["cashConversionCycle"].reindex_like(close)

        valid_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        previous_close = valid_close.shift(1)
        ret = valid_close.div(previous_close.where(previous_close > 0.0)).sub(1.0)
        bar_range = (high.sub(low)).div(previous_close.where(previous_close > 0.0))
        bar_range = bar_range.clip(lower=0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        eps_event = _fresh_update(eps_surprise)
        revenue_event = _fresh_update(revenue_surprise)
        headline_event = eps_event | revenue_event
        cash_event = _fresh_update(cash_cycle)

        eps_z = _robust_cs_zscore(eps_surprise)
        revenue_z = _robust_cs_zscore(revenue_surprise)
        headline_count = eps_z.notna().astype(float) + revenue_z.notna().astype(float)
        headline = eps_z.fillna(0.0).add(revenue_z.fillna(0.0)).div(
            headline_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        # A declining cash-conversion cycle is an improvement in cash realization.
        cash_change = cash_cycle.diff().where(cash_event)
        cash_quality = -_robust_cs_zscore(cash_change)

        # At t, the report was available at t-3 and the market had two full bars
        # (t-2 and t-1) to express the salient headline reaction.
        report_headline = headline.shift(3)
        report_quality = cash_quality.shift(3)
        report_active = headline_event.shift(3).fillna(False) & cash_event.shift(3).fillna(False)

        prior_volume_median = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        abnormal_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0).div(
            prior_volume_median.where(prior_volume_median > 0.0)
        )
        abnormal_volume = abnormal_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=8.0)

        response_return = ret.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum().shift(1)
        response_volume = abnormal_volume.rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean().shift(1)
        response_range = bar_range.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum().shift(1)
        pressure = response_return.abs().mul(response_volume)
        pressure_rank = pressure.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        # Current lower participation and limited fresh extension indicate that the
        # headline-flow episode is completing rather than continuing.
        fade = (1.0 - abnormal_volume.div(response_volume.where(response_volume > 0.0))).clip(
            lower=0.0, upper=1.0
        )
        stabilized = ret.abs().le(0.5 * response_range.where(response_range > 0.0))
        headline_aligned_move = response_return.mul(report_headline).gt(0.0)

        conflict = (-report_headline.mul(report_quality)).clip(lower=0.0)
        eligible = (
            report_active
            & report_headline.notna()
            & report_quality.notna()
            & headline_aligned_move
            & response_volume.gt(1.0)
            & pressure_rank.gt(0.60)
            & fade.gt(0.0)
            & stabilized.fillna(False)
        )

        score = np.sign(report_quality) * conflict * pressure_rank * fade
        score = score.where(eligible, 0.0)
        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).reindex_like(close).astype(float)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_update(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    previous = values.shift(1)
    return values.notna() & (previous.isna() | values.ne(previous))


def _robust_cs_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    median = values.median(axis=1)
    centered = values.sub(median, axis=0)
    mad = centered.abs().median(axis=1).mul(1.4826)
    fallback = values.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad.where(mad > 1.0e-12, fallback).where(lambda x: x > 1.0e-12)
    return centered.div(scale, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _trailing_tax_rate(
    pretax: pd.DataFrame, tax: pd.DataFrame, revenue: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ratio = tax.div(pretax.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 0.50)
    eligible = (pretax > 0.0) & (revenue > 0.0) & (pretax > 0.01 * revenue)
    observed = ratio.where(eligible)
    mean = observed.rolling(63, min_periods=1).mean()
    count = observed.rolling(63, min_periods=1).count()
    return mean.where(count > 0.0, 0.25)


@register_factor
class MarginRevisionCashcycleExhaustion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "margin_revision_cashcycle_exhaustion"
    name = "Margin Revision Cash-Cycle Exhaustion"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Reverses a margin-implied EPS-consensus residual only when a fresh "
        "cash-conversion update contradicts the revenue revision and the "
        "revision-aligned price response loses abnormal-volume support."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsEstimate",
        "sharesOutstanding",
        "grossMargin",
        "sgaToRevenue",
        "incomeBeforeTax",
        "incomeTaxExpense",
        "revenue",
        "cashConversionCycle",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].reindex_like(close)
        low = data["low"].reindex_like(close)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_est = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eps_est = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        shares = data["sharesOutstanding"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        gross_margin = data["grossMargin"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sga_ratio = data["sgaToRevenue"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        pretax = data["incomeBeforeTax"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        tax = data["incomeTaxExpense"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue = data["revenue"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cash_cycle = data["cashConversionCycle"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        gross_mean = gross_margin.rolling(63, min_periods=42).mean()
        sga_mean = sga_ratio.rolling(63, min_periods=42).mean()
        tax_rate = _trailing_tax_rate(pretax, tax, revenue)
        contribution_margin = ((gross_mean - sga_mean) * (1.0 - tax_rate)).clip(-0.25, 0.60)

        revenue_revision = revenue_est.sub(revenue_est.shift(21))
        eps_revision = eps_est.sub(eps_est.shift(21))
        implied_eps = revenue_revision.mul(contribution_margin).div(shares.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        margin_gap = implied_eps.sub(eps_revision).div(close.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        revision_event = _fresh_update(revenue_est) | _fresh_update(eps_est)
        cash_event = _fresh_update(cash_cycle)
        cash_quality = -_robust_cs_zscore(cash_cycle.diff().where(cash_event))
        revision_z = _robust_cs_zscore(revenue_revision.where(revision_event))

        previous_close = close.where(close > 0.0).shift(1)
        ret = close.div(previous_close).sub(1.0)
        bar_range = high.sub(low).div(previous_close).clip(lower=0.0)
        prior_median_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        abnormal_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0).div(prior_median_volume.where(prior_median_volume > 0.0))
        abnormal_volume = abnormal_volume.clip(0.0, 8.0)

        report_gap = margin_gap.shift(3)
        report_revision = revision_z.shift(3)
        report_quality = cash_quality.shift(3)
        report_active = revision_event.shift(3).fillna(False) & cash_event.shift(3).fillna(False)

        response_return = ret.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum().shift(1)
        response_volume = abnormal_volume.rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean().shift(1)
        response_range = bar_range.rolling(2, min_periods=2).sum().shift(1)
        pressure = response_return.abs().mul(response_volume)
        pressure_rank = pressure.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        fade = (1.0 - abnormal_volume.div(response_volume.where(response_volume > 0.0))).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        stabilized = ret.abs().le(0.5 * response_range.where(response_range > 0.0))

        headline_aligned = response_return.mul(report_revision).gt(0.0)
        cash_conflict = (-report_revision.mul(report_quality)).clip(lower=0.0)
        valid_gap = report_gap.notna() & report_gap.replace(0.0, np.nan).notna()
        eligible = (
            report_active
            & valid_gap
            & report_revision.notna()
            & report_quality.notna()
            & headline_aligned
            & response_volume.gt(1.0)
            & pressure_rank.gt(0.60)
            & fade.gt(0.0)
            & stabilized.fillna(False)
        )

        score = (-report_gap) * cash_conflict * pressure_rank * fade
        score = score.where(eligible, 0.0)
        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).reindex_like(close).astype(float)

programs.code:
"""The signal isolates a specific disconfirmation event rather than treating any interruption in momentum as bearish: an established industry price leader must both underperform its industry recently and receive a comparatively weak fresh EPS-consensus update. This joint condition indicates that the price narrative supporting the leader is no longer confirmed by contemporaneously available fundamental expectations, creating scope for a short repricing as extrapolative holders reassess. The symmetric long leg requires an established laggard, recent relative improvement, and a superior fresh revision, identifying improving fundamentals before relative-price catch-up is complete."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Percentile-rank each row within static industry peer groups."""
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True).T


def _industry_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast same-day equal-weighted industry means to constituent names."""
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T


def _industry_eligible_count(
    eligible: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast same-day eligible peer counts to constituent names."""
    return (
        eligible.astype(float)
        .T.groupby(labels, sort=False)
        .transform("sum")
        .T
    )


def _cross_sectional_winsorize(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally winsorize each day's available cross section at 5/95 percent."""
    lower = values.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    upper = values.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    return values.clip(lower=lower, axis=0).clip(upper=upper, axis=0)


def _top_candidates(
    candidates: pd.DataFrame, conviction: pd.DataFrame, ascending: bool
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Select at most twenty candidates per day with deterministic tie handling."""
    candidate_conviction = conviction.where(candidates)
    order = candidate_conviction.rank(axis=1, ascending=ascending, method="first")
    return candidates & order.le(20)


@register_factor
class IndustryEarningsAnchorLeadershipUnwind(BaseFactor):
    """Industry leadership failures jointly confirmed by fresh EPS revisions."""

    factor_id = "industry_earnings_anchor_leadership_unwind"
    name = "Anchored Leadership Failure"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Three-way industry-relative gate: established leaders with recent "
        "relative weakness and weak fresh EPS revisions are short candidates, "
        "while established laggards with relative improvement and strong fresh "
        "revisions are long candidates. Positions are capped at twenty names "
        "per side and require at least five names on both sides."
    )
    window_length = 127
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry", "epsEstimate"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]

        # Industry is static by contract. Using the first bar avoids any
        # dependence on later observations while retaining its ticker alignment.
        industry_labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        dollar_volume = close * volume
        complete_price_history = close.rolling(127, min_periods=127).count().eq(127)
        liquid = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().ge(1_000_000.0)
        base_eligible = close.gt(5.0) & complete_price_history & liquid

        eligible_count = _industry_eligible_count(base_eligible, industry_labels)
        industry_ok = eligible_count.ge(8.0)
        eligible = base_eligible & industry_ok

        prior_return = close.div(close.shift(126).replace(0.0, np.nan)).sub(1.0)
        leadership_rank = _industry_rank(prior_return.where(eligible), industry_labels)

        recent_return = close.div(close.shift(5).replace(0.0, np.nan)).sub(1.0)
        industry_recent_return = _industry_mean(
            recent_return.where(eligible), industry_labels
        )
        relative_recent_return = recent_return.sub(industry_recent_return)
        relative_rank = _industry_rank(
            relative_recent_return.where(eligible), industry_labels
        )

        prior_estimate = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        estimate_change = eps_estimate.sub(prior_estimate)
        fresh_revision = (
            eps_estimate.notna()
            & prior_estimate.notna()
            & estimate_change.abs().gt(0.0)
        )
        revision = estimate_change.div(close.abs().clip(lower=1.0))
        revision = revision.where(eligible & fresh_revision)
        winsorized_revision = _cross_sectional_winsorize(revision)
        revision_rank = _industry_rank(winsorized_revision, industry_labels)

        short_candidates = (
            eligible
            & fresh_revision
            & leadership_rank.ge(0.67)
            & relative_rank.le(0.33)
            & revision_rank.le(0.33)
        )
        long_candidates = (
            eligible
            & fresh_revision
            & leadership_rank.le(0.33)
            & relative_rank.ge(0.67)
            & revision_rank.ge(0.67)
        )

        long_selected = _top_candidates(long_candidates, revision_rank, ascending=False)
        short_selected = _top_candidates(short_candidates, revision_rank, ascending=True)

        both_sides_available = (
            long_candidates.sum(axis=1).ge(5)
            & short_candidates.sum(axis=1).ge(5)
        )
        score = long_selected.astype(float).sub(short_selected.astype(float))
        return score.mul(both_sides_available.astype(float), axis=0).fillna(0.0)
