"""A large negative opening jump that remains unrepaired through the completed session, closes near the session low, and occurs on unusually high volume is treated as evidence of unresolved sell-side pressure rather than a corrected auction mispricing. The mechanism is asymmetric downside-order excitation: a sharp decline can trigger risk-limit reductions, stop-loss activity, margin-related selling, and execution of pre-existing sell programs, while the failed intraday recovery indicates that natural buyers did not absorb the supply. The factor therefore shorts names with fresh, high-participation downside jump stress and takes the opposite side in names without such stress, entered only after the session has closed."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_winsorized_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize each date at 1/99 percentiles, then use population z-scores."""
    lower = values.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = values.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    clipped = values.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    std = clipped.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(std, axis=0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class AsymmetricDownsideJumpPersistence(BaseFactor):
    """Fresh high-volume downside auction stress with failed intraday repair."""

    factor_id = "asymmetric_downside_jump_persistence"
    name = "Downside Auction Stress Persistence"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Shorts fresh, unusually large downside opening gaps that fail to recover, "
        "close near the low, and arrive with abnormal participation; the negative "
        "score is strongest when the event is not part of repeated prior gap stress."
    )
    window_length = 26
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1).where(close.shift(1) > 0.0)
        safe_open = open_.where(open_ > 0.0)
        safe_high = high.where(high > 0.0)
        safe_low = low.where(low > 0.0)

        gap = np.log(safe_open / prior_close)
        log_range_sq = np.log(safe_high / safe_low).pow(2)
        sigma = log_range_sq.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().pow(0.5)
        sigma = sigma.where(sigma > 0.0)

        jump = (-gap / sigma).clip(lower=0.0)

        prior_volume_mean = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        abnormal_volume = volume / prior_volume_mean.where(prior_volume_mean > 0.0)

        recovery = (close - open_) / (prior_close - open_).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        session_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        location = (close - low) / session_range

        expansion = gap.abs() / sigma
        prior_expansion_event = expansion.ge(1.0).where(expansion.notna())
        repeated_count = (
            prior_expansion_event.shift(1)
            .astype(float)
            .rolling(5, min_periods=5)
            .sum()
        )
        freshness = 1.0 - repeated_count / 5.0

        valid = (
            gap.notna()
            & sigma.notna()
            & abnormal_volume.notna()
            & recovery.notna()
            & location.notna()
            & freshness.notna()
            & np.isfinite(jump)
            & np.isfinite(abnormal_volume)
            & np.isfinite(recovery)
            & np.isfinite(location)
            & (volume >= 0.0)
        )

        ranked_jump = jump.where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        ranked_volume = abnormal_volume.where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        qualifies = (
            valid
            & (gap < 0.0)
            & (jump >= 1.5)
            & (ranked_jump >= 0.80)
            & (abnormal_volume >= 1.25)
            & (ranked_volume >= 0.70)
            & (recovery <= 0.25)
            & (location <= 0.35)
        )

        recovery_component = 1.0 - recovery.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        raw_stress = (
            freshness
            * ((ranked_jump - 0.80) / 0.20)
            * ((ranked_volume - 0.70) / 0.30)
            * recovery_component
            * (1.0 - location)
        ).where(qualifies, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        standardized_stress = _cross_sectional_winsorized_zscore(raw_stress)
        return (-standardized_stress).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A large negative opening jump that remains unrepaired through the completed session, closes near the session low, and occurs on unusually high volume is treated as evidence of unresolved sell-side pressure rather than a corrected auction mispricing. The mechanism is asymmetric downside-order excitation: a sharp decline can trigger risk-limit reductions, stop-loss activity, margin-related selling, and execution of pre-existing sell programs, while the failed intraday recovery indicates that natural buyers did not absorb the supply. The factor therefore shorts names with fresh, high-participation downside jump stress and takes the opposite side in names without such stress, entered only after the session has closed.
programs.description: At end of day t, using only completed-session data, define the opening gap g_t = log(open_t / close_{t-1}) and the prior-20-session intraday range-volatility estimate sigma_t = sqrt(mean_{i=t-20}^{t-1}[log(high_i / low_i)^2]). Define downside jump magnitude J_t = max(0, -g_t / sigma_t). Define the intraday gap-recovery fraction rho_t = (close_t - open_t) / (close_{t-1} - open_t) for g_t < 0, and the close-location statistic L_t = (close_t - low_t) / max(high_t - low_t, epsilon). Define abnormal-volume ratio V_t = volume_t / mean_{i=t-20}^{t-1}(volume_i). Compute cross-sectional percentile ranks qJ_t and qV_t for J_t and V_t among names with valid observations. A name qualifies as downside stress only if J_t >= 1.5, qJ_t >= 0.80, V_t >= 1.25, qV_t >= 0.70, rho_t <= 0.25, and L_t <= 0.35. To isolate a fresh innovation rather than an established multi-day repricing, define repeated-expansion count N_t = sum_{i=t-5}^{t-1} I(|log(open_i / close_{i-1})| / sigma_i >= 1.0), and apply freshness multiplier P_t = 1 - N_t / 5. For qualifying names, raw stress is A_t = P_t * ((qJ_t - 0.80) / 0.20) * ((qV_t - 0.70) / 0.30) * (1 - clip(rho_t, 0, 1)) * (1 - L_t); otherwise A_t = 0. Winsorize A_t cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th percentiles, standardize it cross-sectionally, and set the tradable score to -z(A_t). Thus lower scores are short candidates and higher scores are long candidates. Form the signal after close_t is known, enter at the next executable bar, and hold for six subsequent daily bars.

"""A sharp selloff immediately following a newly available non-negative earnings and revenue surprise is more plausibly a temporary liquidity dislocation than a pure bad-news discovery event, particularly when the firm is not financially fragile. Elevated downside range volatility and unusual trading activity identify a state in which adverse-order-flow amplification can temporarily dominate the contemporaneous fundamental disclosure. The signal buys the names where intraday closes are beginning to move away from the lows, consistent with same-day absorption rather than a fully persistent downward-information state."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _finite_frame(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Replace non-finite panel values with NaN."""
    return frame.where(np.isfinite(frame))


def _winsorized_percentile(
    frame: pd.DataFrame, missing_rank: float = 0.5
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectionally winsorize finite observations and average-rank ties."""
    clean = _finite_frame(frame)
    lower = clean.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = clean.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    clipped = clean.where(clean.ge(lower, axis=0), lower, axis=0)
    clipped = clipped.where(clipped.le(upper, axis=0), upper, axis=0)
    ranked = clipped.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True)
    return ranked.fillna(missing_rank)


def _cross_sectional_liquidity_gate(adv: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return one for available names at or above the daily 60th ADV percentile."""
    clean = _finite_frame(adv)
    available = clean.notna() & clean.gt(0.0)
    threshold = clean.where(available).quantile(0.60, axis=1)
    return available & clean.ge(threshold, axis=0)


@register_factor
class SolventPositiveEventDislocationReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Positive-surprise selloff reversal conditioned on liquidity and solvency."""

    factor_id = "solvent_positive_event_dislocation_reversal"
    name = "Solvent Positive-Event Dislocation Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Ranks temporary downside dislocations after fresh positive EPS and "
        "non-negative revenue surprises, requiring top-quintile liquidity and "
        "discounting financially fragile firms."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "debtToEquity",
        "interestCoverage",
        "currentRatio",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _finite_frame(data["close"])
        high = _finite_frame(data["high"])
        low = _finite_frame(data["low"])
        volume = _finite_frame(data["volume"])

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        three_bar_return = close / close.shift(3).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        downside = (-three_bar_return).clip(lower=0.0)
        downside_valid = (
            close.notna()
            & close.shift(3).notna()
            & close.shift(3).ne(0.0)
        )
        downside_rank = _winsorized_percentile(
            downside.where(downside_valid), missing_rank=0.5
        )

        range_a = high - low
        range_b = (high - previous_close).abs()
        range_c = (low - previous_close).abs()
        true_range = pd.concat([range_a, range_b, range_c], axis=0).groupby(level=0).max()
        normalized_tr = true_range / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tr_valid = (
            high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & previous_close.notna()
            & previous_close.gt(0.0)
            & normalized_tr.notna()
        )
        normalized_tr = normalized_tr.where(tr_valid)
        fast_vol = normalized_tr.pow(2).rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean().pow(0.5)
        slow_vol = normalized_tr.pow(2).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().pow(0.5)
        volatility_stress = (fast_vol / slow_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        volatility_rank = _winsorized_percentile(volatility_stress, missing_rank=0.5)

        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = (close - low) / bar_range
        flat_bar = high.eq(low) & high.notna() & low.notna() & close.notna()
        close_location = close_location.where(~flat_bar, 0.5)
        close_location = close_location.where(
            high.notna() & low.notna() & close.notna()
        )
        recent_location = close_location.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        prior_location = close_location.shift(3).rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        low_repair = (recent_location - prior_location).clip(lower=0.0)
        repair_rank = _winsorized_percentile(low_repair, missing_rank=0.5)

        prior_volume_mean = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        activity = volume / prior_volume_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        activity_valid = volume.notna() & prior_volume_mean.gt(0.0)
        activity_rank = _winsorized_percentile(
            activity.where(activity_valid), missing_rank=0.5
        )

        dollar_volume = close * volume
        adv = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        liquidity_gate = _cross_sectional_liquidity_gate(adv).astype(float)

        eps_surprise = _finite_frame(data["epsSurprise"])
        revenue_surprise = _finite_frame(data["revenueSurprise"])
        eps_previous = eps_surprise.shift(1)
        revenue_previous = revenue_surprise.shift(1)
        event_gate = (
            eps_surprise.notna()
            & eps_previous.notna()
            & revenue_surprise.notna()
            & revenue_previous.notna()
            & eps_surprise.ne(eps_previous)
            & revenue_surprise.ne(revenue_previous)
            & eps_surprise.gt(0.0)
            & revenue_surprise.ge(0.0)
        ).astype(float)

        leverage_rank = _winsorized_percentile(_finite_frame(data["debtToEquity"]))
        coverage_rank = _winsorized_percentile(-_finite_frame(data["interestCoverage"]))
        liquidity_rank = _winsorized_percentile(-_finite_frame(data["currentRatio"]))
        fragility = (leverage_rank + coverage_rank + liquidity_rank) / 3.0

        dislocation = (
            0.30 * downside_rank
            + 0.25 * volatility_rank
            + 0.20 * activity_rank
            + 0.25 * repair_rank
        )
        raw_score = event_gate * liquidity_gate * (1.0 - fragility) * dislocation
        return _winsorized_percentile(raw_score, missing_rank=0.5)
programs.name: Solvent Positive-Event Dislocation Reversal
programs.trading_idea: A sharp selloff immediately following a newly available non-negative earnings and revenue surprise is more plausibly a temporary liquidity dislocation than a pure bad-news discovery event, particularly when the firm is not financially fragile. Elevated downside range volatility and unusual trading activity identify a state in which adverse-order-flow amplification can temporarily dominate the contemporaneous fundamental disclosure. The signal buys the names where intraday closes are beginning to move away from the lows, consistent with same-day absorption rather than a fully persistent downward-information state.
programs.description: All quantities are computed separately for each ticker at signal-date close t, using only bars dated t or earlier and point-in-time fundamental fields available at t. Define one-bar return r_t = close_t / close_(t-1) - 1. Define downside shock D_t = max(0, -(close_t / close_(t-3) - 1)). Define normalized true range TR_t = max(high_t-low_t, abs(high_t-close_(t-1)), abs(low_t-close_(t-1))) / close_(t-1). Fast range volatility is VF_t = sqrt(mean(TR^2 over t-2 through t)); slow range volatility is VS_t = sqrt(mean(TR^2 over t-19 through t)); volatility stress is V_t = max(0, VF_t / VS_t - 1). Define close location CL_t = (close_t-low_t)/(high_t-low_t), with CL_t = 0.5 when high_t equals low_t. Define away-from-low repair L_t = max(0, mean(CL over t-2 through t) - mean(CL over t-5 through t-3)). Define activity A_t = volume_t / mean(volume over t-20 through t-1), provided the denominator is positive. Define 20-day dollar-volume liquidity ADV_t = mean(close*volume over t-19 through t), and let Q_t equal 1 only when ADV_t is at or above that date's cross-sectional 60th percentile among available names; otherwise Q_t = 0. Define a hard contemporaneous disclosure gate E_t = 1 only if epsSurprise_t differs from epsSurprise_(t-1), revenueSurprise_t differs from revenueSurprise_(t-1), epsSurprise_t > 0, and revenueSurprise_t >= 0; otherwise E_t = 0. This gate uses the point-in-time availability-date steps of the surprise fields and does not infer a later confirmation. Financial fragility is F_t = [R(debtToEquity_t) + R(-interestCoverage_t) + R(-currentRatio_t)]/3, where R(x) is the cross-sectional percentile rank after winsorizing finite observations of x at the 1st and 99th percentiles; a missing fundamental component receives rank 0.5. Thus high F means high leverage, weak interest coverage, and weak liquidity. For each date, winsorize finite values of D, V, A, and L at the cross-sectional 1st and 99th percentiles, then convert each to percentile ranks RD, RV, RA, and RL using average ranks for ties. If a required OHLCV history is unavailable, or if volume history is invalid, set that component rank to 0.5; if ADV is unavailable, set Q to 0. The raw score is S_t = E_t * Q_t * (1-F_t) * (0.30*RD_t + 0.25*RV_t + 0.20*RA_t + 0.25*RL_t). The factor value is the cross-sectional percentile rank of winsorized S_t; names with no qualifying fresh positive event or insufficient liquidity receive S_t = 0. Rebalance once per day after the signal-date close, enter eligible high-score names at the next bar's open, and hold for six daily bars before exit; no centered window, future-bar confirmation, or future return-derived state is used. The explicit differentiator from the named pressure/repair factors is the mandatory E_t hard gate and the solvency penalty (1-F_t): this is not a standalone selloff, range-stress, turnover, or close-repair score. Exact duplication would require another factor to use the same jointly necessary condition of a newly updated positive EPS surprise, newly updated non-negative revenue surprise, top-40-percent dollar-volume eligibility, and the specified three-component point-in-time fragility penalty.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _transition_entropy(states: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal 20-bar entropy of adjacent return-volume state transitions."""
    values = states.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    output = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    columns = np.arange(n_cols)
    normalizer = np.log(81.0)

    for end in range(19, n_rows):
        window = values[end - 19:end + 1]
        counts = np.full((n_cols, 81), 0.25, dtype=float)
        retained = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=int)
        for offset in range(19):
            previous = window[offset]
            current = window[offset + 1]
            valid = np.isfinite(previous) & np.isfinite(current)
            if valid.any():
                transition = previous[valid].astype(int) * 9 + current[valid].astype(int)
                np.add.at(counts, (columns[valid], transition), 1.0)
                retained[valid] += 1
        eligible = retained >= 12
        if eligible.any():
            probs = counts[eligible] / counts[eligible].sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
            output[end, eligible] = -(probs * np.log(probs)).sum(axis=1) / normalizer

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=states.index, columns=states.columns)


def _cross_sectional_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Daily winsorized cross-sectional z-score, retaining a numeric panel."""
    lower = values.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = values.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    clipped = values.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    std = clipped.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(std, axis=0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class EntropyGatedDownsideAuctionAftershock(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "entropy_gated_downside_auction_aftershock"
    name = "Entropy-Gated Downside Auction Aftershock"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Shorts failed high-volume downside opening auctions when their pre-event "
        "return-volume path shows low transition entropy and persistent negative pressure."
    )
    window_length = 45
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        open_ = data["open"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)

        prior_close = close.shift(1).where(close.shift(1) > 0.0)
        safe_open = open_.where(open_ > 0.0)
        safe_high = high.where(high > 0.0)
        safe_low = low.where(low > 0.0)

        daily_return = close / prior_close - 1.0
        positive_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
        prior_median_volume = positive_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        relative_volume = volume / prior_median_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        return_state = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(daily_return.to_numpy() < 0.0, 0.0,
                     np.where(daily_return.to_numpy() > 0.0, 2.0, 1.0)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        volume_state = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(relative_volume.to_numpy() <= 0.80, 0.0,
                     np.where(relative_volume.to_numpy() <= 1.20, 1.0, 2.0)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        state_valid = (
            np.isfinite(daily_return)
            & np.isfinite(relative_volume)
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & (close > 0.0)
        )
        states = (return_state * 3.0 + volume_state).where(state_valid)
        entropy = _transition_entropy(states)

        signed_pressure = (
            daily_return * relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        ).where(state_valid).rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
        prior_sell_pressure = (-signed_pressure.shift(1)).clip(lower=0.0)
        prior_low_entropy = (1.0 - entropy.shift(1)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        gap = np.log(safe_open / prior_close)
        range_sigma = np.log(safe_high / safe_low).pow(2).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().pow(0.5)
        range_sigma = range_sigma.where(range_sigma > 0.0)
        downside_jump = (-gap / range_sigma).clip(lower=0.0)

        prior_volume_mean = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        abnormal_volume = volume / prior_volume_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        recovery = (close - safe_open) / (prior_close - safe_open).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        location = (close - safe_low) / (safe_high - safe_low).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        valid_event = (
            np.isfinite(gap)
            & np.isfinite(downside_jump)
            & np.isfinite(abnormal_volume)
            & np.isfinite(recovery)
            & np.isfinite(location)
            & prior_sell_pressure.notna()
            & prior_low_entropy.notna()
        )
        jump_rank = downside_jump.where(valid_event).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        volume_rank = abnormal_volume.where(valid_event).rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        auction_stress = (
            ((jump_rank - 0.80) / 0.20).clip(lower=0.0)
            * ((volume_rank - 0.70) / 0.30).clip(lower=0.0)
            * (1.0 - recovery.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0))
            * (1.0 - location.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0))
        )
        qualifies = (
            valid_event
            & (gap < 0.0)
            & (downside_jump >= 1.5)
            & (abnormal_volume >= 1.25)
            & (recovery <= 0.25)
            & (location <= 0.35)
            & (prior_sell_pressure > 0.0)
        )

        sell_rank = prior_sell_pressure.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        entropy_rank = prior_low_entropy.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        continuation_gate = sell_rank * entropy_rank
        raw_signal = (-auction_stress * continuation_gate).where(qualifies, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        return _cross_sectional_zscore(raw_signal).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

"""The revised mechanism is persistent downside stress rather than a claim of critical slowing down. Following a material selloff, elevated range volatility that remains high on both fast and slow filters, together with serial dependence in range, can indicate that forced selling, margin pressure, or uncertainty has not yet been resolved. This should be most damaging for firms with high net-debt burdens relative to cash-generating capacity, because weaker financing capacity can prolong deleveraging pressure; the signal is explicitly tested for incremental value beyond ordinary downside momentum, volatility, sector weakness, and leverage."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _rolling_valid_lag1_autocorr(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Lag-one Pearson autocorrelation from the latest 20 valid observations.

    Invalid range observations are omitted before forming consecutive pairs.
    Nineteen adjacent pairs are therefore used once twenty valid observations
    have accumulated.  Each calculation is trailing and causal.
    """
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)

    for column in values.columns:
        series = values[column].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).dropna()
        if len(series) < 20:
            continue

        current = series.iloc[1:]
        previous = series.shift(1).iloc[1:]
        autocorr = current.rolling(19, min_periods=19).corr(previous)
        output.loc[autocorr.index, column] = autocorr

    return output


def _cross_sectional_winsorized_rank(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Daily 5/95-percentile winsorization followed by percentile ranking."""
    clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lower = clean.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    upper = clean.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    clipped = clean.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    return clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True)


def _sector_residual(
    score: pd.DataFrame,
    sector_labels: pd.Series,
    minimum_names: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract same-date sector means only where a sector has enough names."""
    grouped_score = score.T.groupby(sector_labels, sort=False)
    sector_mean = grouped_score.transform("mean").T
    sector_count = score.notna().astype(float).T.groupby(
        sector_labels, sort=False
    ).transform("sum").T
    return (score - sector_mean).where(sector_count >= float(minimum_names))


@register_factor
class DownsideCriticalSlowingStressSpread(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-neutral bearish score for persistent post-selloff range stress."""

    factor_id = "downside_critical_slowing_stress_spread"
    name = "Persistent Downside Stress Spread"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Ranks sector-neutral post-selloff stress created by persistent range "
        "volatility, range autocorrelation, and net-debt fragility; higher "
        "scores are short signals."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "totalDebt", "cash", "ebitda", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        valid_range = (high > 0.0) & (low > 0.0)
        range_ratio = (high / low).where(valid_range)
        log_range = np.log(range_ratio).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        range_variance = (log_range * log_range).where(log_range.notna())

        # adjust=False initializes each series at its first valid observation;
        # ignore_na=True carries the recursive state across an invalid bar.
        fast_variance = range_variance.ewm(
            alpha=0.30, adjust=False, ignore_na=True, min_periods=1
        ).mean()
        slow_variance = range_variance.ewm(
            alpha=0.06, adjust=False, ignore_na=True, min_periods=1
        ).mean()

        valid_observation_count = range_variance.notna().cumsum()
        sufficient_range_history = valid_observation_count >= 60

        autocorr = _rolling_valid_lag1_autocorr(log_range)
        inertia_ratio = np.log(
            slow_variance / fast_variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        log_fast_variance = np.log(fast_variance).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        ac_rank = _cross_sectional_winsorized_rank(autocorr)
        ir_rank = _cross_sectional_winsorized_rank(inertia_ratio)
        fast_rank = _cross_sectional_winsorized_rank(log_fast_variance)
        persistence = 0.40 * ac_rank + 0.30 * ir_rank + 0.30 * fast_rank
        persistence = persistence.where(sufficient_range_history & valid_range)

        five_bar_return = close / close.shift(5) - 1.0
        downside_gate = (five_bar_return <= -0.08).astype(float)

        debt = data["totalDebt"]
        cash = data["cash"]
        ebitda = data["ebitda"]
        required_fundamentals = debt.notna() & cash.notna() & ebitda.notna()

        positive_ebitda_nd = ((debt - cash) / ebitda.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
            ebitda > 0.0
        )
        positive_ebitda_nd = positive_ebitda_nd.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        positive_ebitda_p95 = positive_ebitda_nd.quantile(0.95, axis=1)

        net_debt_fragility = positive_ebitda_nd.where(
            ebitda > 0.0,
            positive_ebitda_p95,
            axis=0,
        ).where(required_fundamentals)
        fragility_rank = _cross_sectional_winsorized_rank(net_debt_fragility)

        raw_score = (downside_gate * persistence * fragility_rank).where(
            required_fundamentals
        )

        # Apply the stated tradability universe before sector neutralization so
        # ineligible securities do not affect sector means or final ranks.
        trailing_dollar_volume = (close * volume).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        tradable = (close >= 5.0) & (trailing_dollar_volume >= 5_000_000.0)
        eligible_score = raw_score.where(tradable)

        # Sector is static in this feed, so the first timestamp supplies the
        # contemporaneously available group label for each ticker.
        sector_labels = data["sector"].iloc[0]
        sector_residual = _sector_residual(eligible_score, sector_labels, 5)

        final_rank = sector_residual.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return (2.0 * final_rank - 1.0).where(sector_residual.notna())

Following a material selloff, elevated range volatility that remains high on both fast and slow filters, together with serial dependence in range, can indicate that forced selling, margin pressure, or uncertainty has not yet been resolved. This should be most damaging for firms with high net-debt burdens relative to cash-generating capacity, because weaker financing capacity can prolong deleveraging pressure; the signal is explicitly tested for incremental value beyond ordinary downside momentum, volatility, sector weakness, and leverage.
programs.description: For each stock, define daily log range r_t = ln(high_t / low_t) and q_t = r_t^2, using only observations with positive high and low. Require at least 60 valid daily observations. Compute fast and slow EWMA range variances recursively as v_fast,t = 0.70*v_fast,t-1 + 0.30*q_t and v_slow,t = 0.94*v_slow,t-1 + 0.06*q_t, initialized from the first valid q observation. Compute AC_t as the ordinary Pearson lag-1 autocorrelation of r over the most recent 20 valid bars, using the 19 paired observations (r_t,r_t-1). Define the slow-to-fast variance ratio IR_t = ln(v_slow,t / v_fast,t). Define the five-bar downside-shock gate D_t = 1 when close_t / close_t-5 - 1 <= -0.08, and D_t = 0 otherwise. On each date, winsorize AC_t, IR_t, and ln(v_fast,t) independently at the cross-sectional 5th and 95th percentiles, then convert each to a cross-sectional percentile rank in [0,1]. Define persistence stress B_t = 0.40*rank(AC_t) + 0.30*rank(IR_t) + 0.30*rank(ln(v_fast,t)); the positive v_fast term ensures that a high slow/fast ratio is interpreted as sustained elevated volatility rather than merely calm volatility. Define net-debt fragility ND_t = (totalDebt_t - cash_t) / ebitda_t when cash, totalDebt, and EBITDA are available and EBITDA is positive. For EBITDA <= 0, set ND_t to the same-date 95th percentile of ND among positive-EBITDA firms; for missing cash, debt, or EBITDA, set the factor to missing rather than imputing. Winsorize ND_t at its daily 5th and 95th percentiles and map it to a daily percentile rank F_t in [0,1]. The pre-neutralization bearish stress score is G_t = D_t*B_t*F_t. Sector-neutralize G_t by subtracting its same-date sector mean, requiring at least five valid names in a sector, then percentile-rank the residual across the eligible universe and linearly scale it to [-1,1]. Higher final scores are short signals. Evaluation must report incremental six-bar predictive performance after controlling for: five-bar stock downside return and 20-bar drawdown, 20-bar close-return volatility and range volatility, five-bar equal-weight sector return, debtToEquity, cashRatio, and the net-debt/EBITDA fragility rank. A tradable implementation must exclude stocks below $5 in closing price or below $5 million in trailing-20-bar average dollar volume, apply 75 bp one-way trading costs to both legs, and charge a 3% annualized borrow cost to the short leg; results should be reported both before and after these assumptions.

"""Cadenced idiosyncratic repair elasticity.

Mechanism: an idiosyncratic downside variance shock is more likely to reverse when it
terminates an orderly volume-participated sell cadence and current downside impact
collapses despite elevated participation, indicating supply absorption rather than
new fundamental information.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, sectors: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date sector mean, with a small-group fallback left missing."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for timestamp in values.index:
        row = values.loc[timestamp]
        labels = sectors.loc[timestamp]
        valid = row.notna() & labels.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        means = row[valid].groupby(labels[valid]).mean()
        counts = row[valid].groupby(labels[valid]).count()
        eligible = counts[counts >= 3].index
        mapped = labels.map(means).where(labels.isin(eligible))
        result.loc[timestamp] = mapped
    return result


def _fresh_update(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time change flag, including the first observed report."""
    previous = values.shift(1)
    return values.ne(previous) & (values.notna() | previous.notna())


@register_factor
class CadencedIdiosyncraticRepairElasticity(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cadenced_idiosyncratic_repair_elasticity"
    name = "Cadenced Idiosyncratic Repair Elasticity"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks repaired idiosyncratic downside shocks by the interaction of prior "
        "regular sell participation and contemporaneous collapse in downside impact."
    )
    window_length = 41
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)

        prior_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        log_return = np.log(close / prior_close).where(close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0))

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1)
        volume_base = prior_volume.rolling(15, min_periods=10).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vrel = (volume / volume_base).clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0)
        log_vrel = np.log1p(vrel)

        # Parent A state: persistent negative, participation-weighted pressure
        # whose magnitude is regular rather than a single isolated liquidation.
        sell_pressure = (-log_return).clip(lower=0.0) * log_vrel.fillna(0.0)
        prior_pressure = sell_pressure.shift(1)
        pressure_mean = prior_pressure.rolling(5, min_periods=3).mean()
        pressure_std = prior_pressure.rolling(5, min_periods=3).std(ddof=0)
        negative_share = log_return.shift(1).lt(0.0).rolling(5, min_periods=3).mean()
        cadence = (
            negative_share.fillna(0.0)
            * pressure_mean.fillna(0.0)
            / (pressure_std.fillna(0.0) + 0.002)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)

        # Parent B state: signed close-to-close variance innovation net of the
        # same-bar Parkinson range variance, residualized from sector movement.
        valid_range = high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0) & high.ge(low)
        log_range = np.log(high / low).where(valid_range & high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0))
        park_var = log_range.pow(2) / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))
        q = (np.sign(log_return) * (log_return.pow(2) - park_var)).where(
            log_return.notna() & park_var.notna()
        )
        q_prior = q.shift(1)
        q_mean = q_prior.rolling(35, min_periods=18).mean()
        q_std = q_prior.rolling(35, min_periods=18).std(ddof=1)
        z = ((q - q_mean) / q_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0)
        sector_z = _sector_mean(z, data["sector"])
        idio_z = (z - sector_z.fillna(0.0)).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0)
        downside_innovation = (-idio_z).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)

        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        clv = ((close - low) / bar_range).where(valid_range & high.gt(low))
        recovery = (2.0 * (clv - 0.5)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        downside_excursion = ((open_ - low) / open_.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0)
        impact = downside_excursion / log_vrel.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_impact = impact.shift(1).rolling(5, min_periods=3).median()
        impact_collapse = (
            prior_impact / impact.clip(lower=1e-5) - 1.0
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)

        fresh_event = (
            _fresh_update(data["epsSurprise"])
            | _fresh_update(data["revenueSurprise"])
            | _fresh_update(data["epsSurprise"]).shift(1).fillna(False)
            | _fresh_update(data["revenueSurprise"]).shift(1).fillna(False)
        )
        information_weight = (~fresh_event).astype(float)

        raw = (
            cadence
            * downside_innovation.fillna(0.0)
            * vrel.fillna(0.0).clip(upper=4.0)
            * recovery
            * impact_collapse
            * information_weight
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=100.0)

        valid = close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0)
        score = rank(raw.where(valid)).fillna(0.5)
        return score.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _transition_entropy(states: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal 20-bar entropy of adjacent three-state return-volume transitions."""
    values = states.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    output = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    col_ids = np.arange(n_cols)
    log_count = np.log(9.0)

    for end in range(19, n_rows):
        window = values[end - 19:end + 1]
        counts = np.full((n_cols, 9), 0.25, dtype=float)
        retained = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=int)
        for offset in range(19):
            previous = window[offset]
            current = window[offset + 1]
            valid = np.isfinite(previous) & np.isfinite(current)
            if valid.any():
                transition = previous[valid].astype(int) * 3 + current[valid].astype(int)
                np.add.at(counts, (col_ids[valid], transition), 1.0)
                retained[valid] += 1
        eligible = retained >= 12
        if eligible.any():
            probability = counts[eligible] / counts[eligible].sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
            output[end, eligible] = -(probability * np.log(probability)).sum(axis=1) / log_count

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=states.index, columns=states.columns)


def _downside_variance_repair(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal downside close/range variance disagreement and repaired-close gate."""
    previous_close = close.shift(1)
    valid_return = close.gt(0.0) & previous_close.gt(0.0)
    log_return = np.log(close.where(valid_return) / previous_close.where(valid_return))

    valid_range = high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0) & high.ge(low)
    log_range = np.log(high.where(valid_range) / low.where(valid_range))
    range_variance = (log_range * log_range / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))).fillna(0.0)
    close_variance = log_return.pow(2).fillna(0.0)
    downside = log_return.lt(0.0)

    down_close = close_variance.where(downside, 0.0).ewm(halflife=10, adjust=False).mean()
    down_range = range_variance.where(downside, 0.0).ewm(halflife=10, adjust=False).mean()
    total = (down_close + down_range).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    dislocation = ((down_close - down_range) / total).clip(lower=0.0)

    width = (high - low).where(valid_range)
    close_location = ((close - low) / width.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    close_location = close_location.fillna(0.5)

    clean_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    baseline = clean_volume.ewm(halflife=20, adjust=False).mean().shift(1)
    abnormal_volume = (clean_volume / baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(0.0, 3.0)
    repair = dislocation * close_location * abnormal_volume.fillna(0.0)
    return repair, log_return


@register_factor
class CadencedDownsideVarianceRepairReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cadenced_downside_variance_repair_reversal"
    name = "Cadenced Downside Variance Repair"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Ranks repaired downside close-versus-range variance dislocations only when "
        "they occur within low-entropy, persistent negative return-volume pressure."
    )
    window_length = 40
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)

        repair, log_return = _downside_variance_repair(close, high, low, volume)

        positive_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))
        volume_base = positive_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        relative_volume = volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        valid = log_return.notna() & relative_volume.notna() & volume.gt(0.0)

        states = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(
                log_return.to_numpy() < 0.0,
                0.0,
                np.where(log_return.to_numpy() > 0.0, 2.0, 1.0),
            ),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        ).where(valid)
        entropy = _transition_entropy(states)

        signed_pressure = (
            log_return * relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        ).where(valid).rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
        mechanical_selling = (-signed_pressure).clip(lower=0.0)
        regularity = (1.0 - entropy).clip(lower=0.0)

        raw = (repair * mechanical_selling * regularity).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        return rank(raw)

"""This is a deliberately narrow proxy for the imbalance of recently transacted volume above versus below the current price, rather than a claim to observe the outstanding shareholder cost basis. A large recent above-price volume imbalance identifies a potential short-horizon downside-liquidity asymmetry: a further decline can activate stop-loss, margin, tax-loss, and adverse-selection selling among recently established positions, consistent with asymmetric excitation of downward orders. The hypothesis predicts lower subsequent six-bar returns for stocks with more decayed volume above the current close, conditional on cross-sectional ranking; it should be evaluated jointly with subsequent volume, downside volatility, and price impact rather than interpreted solely as a disposition-effect test."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _decayed_reference_price_skew(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int = 60,
    half_life: float = 20.0,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally aggregate decayed volume whose bar reference price is above/below close."""
    above = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    below = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    current_valid = close.notna() & np.isfinite(close) & close.gt(0.0)
    decay_rate = np.log(2.0) / half_life

    for lag in range(lookback):
        bar_high = high.shift(lag)
        bar_low = low.shift(lag)
        bar_close = close.shift(lag)
        bar_volume = volume.shift(lag)
        reference_price = (bar_high + bar_low + bar_close) / 3.0

        valid = (
            current_valid
            & bar_volume.notna()
            & np.isfinite(bar_volume)
            & bar_volume.gt(0.0)
            & reference_price.notna()
            & np.isfinite(reference_price)
            & reference_price.gt(0.0)
        )
        weighted_volume = bar_volume * np.exp(-decay_rate * lag)
        above = above + weighted_volume.where(
            valid & reference_price.gt(close), 0.0
        )
        below = below + weighted_volume.where(
            valid & reference_price.lt(close), 0.0
        )

    total = above + below
    return ((above - below) / total.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(total.gt(0.0))


@register_factor
class DecayedVolumeReferencePriceSkew(BaseFactor):
    """Negative ranked skew of decayed volume transacted above current close."""

    factor_id = "prospect_costbasis_supply_skew"
    name = "Decayed Volume Reference-Price Skew"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "At each close, computes a 60-bar, 20-bar-half-life volume imbalance "
        "between reference-price volume above and below the current close, then "
        "negates its cross-sectional percentile rank."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        skew = _decayed_reference_price_skew(
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["close"],
            data["volume"],
        )
        rank_pct = skew.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True)
        return -(rank_pct - 0.5)

The tradable factor is -score_t, so stocks with disproportionately recent volume transacted above the current close receive more-negative expected-return scores.

"""A downward traverse through a historically high-turnover price region is treated not as a literal investor inventory ledger, but as a public reference-price breach that can coincide with one-sided liquidity demand and reduced displayed-liquidity resilience. The negative-return prediction is restricted to breaches completed with unusually high trading volume and a close near the bar low, conditions consistent with unresolved sell-side pressure rather than an intraday dip that was absorbed. Because a breach can also mark selling exhaustion and support, this is explicitly an incremental conditional activation signal whose sign and value must be tested after controlling for the existing prospect_costbasis_supply_skew factor."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _barrier_activation(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute a causal, exponentially decayed volume-at-price breach signal."""
    close_values = close.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    high_values = high.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    low_values = low.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    volume_values = volume.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)

    n_rows, n_cols = close_values.shape
    output = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    typical_price = (high_values + low_values + close_values) / 3.0

    # At t, observations t-126 through t-1 have ages 126 through 1.
    ages = np.arange(126, 0, -1, dtype=float)
    decay = np.exp(-np.log(2.0) * ages / 21.0)[:, None]

    prior_volume = (
        volume.shift(1)
        .rolling(20, min_periods=20)
        .mean()
        .to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    )
    epsilon = 1.0e-12

    for t in range(126, n_rows):
        previous_close = close_values[t - 1]
        current_close = close_values[t]
        current_high = high_values[t]
        current_low = low_values[t]
        current_volume = volume_values[t]
        average_volume = prior_volume[t]

        width = 0.005 * previous_close
        hist_tp = typical_price[t - 126 : t]
        hist_volume = volume_values[t - 126 : t]

        valid_width = np.isfinite(width) & (width > 0.0)
        valid_history = (
            np.isfinite(hist_tp)
            & np.isfinite(hist_volume)
            & (hist_volume >= 0.0)
            & valid_width[None, :]
        )
        weighted_volume = np.where(valid_history, hist_volume * decay, 0.0)
        total_profile = weighted_volume.sum(axis=0)

        scaled_price = np.zeros_like(hist_tp, dtype=float)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            np.divide(
                hist_tp,
                width[None, :],
                out=scaled_price,
                where=valid_history,
            )
        bin_centers = np.rint(scaled_price) * width[None, :]

        crossed_down = (
            np.isfinite(current_close)
            & np.isfinite(previous_close)
            & (current_close < previous_close)
        )
        crossed_bins = (
            valid_history
            & (bin_centers >= current_close[None, :])
            & (bin_centers < previous_close[None, :])
            & crossed_down[None, :]
        )
        crossed_mass = np.where(crossed_bins, weighted_volume, 0.0).sum(axis=0)

        bar_range = current_high - current_low
        valid_range = np.isfinite(bar_range) & (bar_range > 0.0)
        close_location = np.full(n_cols, 0.5, dtype=float)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            np.divide(
                current_high - current_close,
                bar_range,
                out=close_location,
                where=valid_range,
            )
        close_location = np.clip(close_location, 0.0, 1.0)

        relative_volume = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
        valid_average = np.isfinite(average_volume) & (average_volume >= 0.0)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            np.divide(
                current_volume,
                average_volume + epsilon,
                out=relative_volume,
                where=np.isfinite(current_volume) & valid_average,
            )
        relative_volume = np.minimum(np.maximum(relative_volume, 0.0), 5.0)

        eligible = (
            valid_width
            & np.isfinite(current_close)
            & np.isfinite(previous_close)
            & np.isfinite(current_high)
            & np.isfinite(current_low)
            & np.isfinite(current_volume)
            & valid_average
            & (total_profile > epsilon)
        )
        activation = np.full(n_cols, np.nan, dtype=float)
        activation[eligible] = (
            crossed_mass[eligible]
            / (total_profile[eligible] + epsilon)
            * relative_volume[eligible]
            * close_location[eligible]
        )
        output[t] = activation

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)


@register_factor
class FreshCostbasisBarrierActivation(BaseFactor):
    """Negative ranked activation of high-turnover reference-price breaches."""

    factor_id = "fresh_costbasis_barrier_activation"
    name = "Residual Downside Barrier Activation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Negative cross-sectional rank of a causal 126-bar exponentially "
        "decayed volume-at-price barrier breach, activated only by high "
        "relative volume and closes near the daily low."
    )
    window_length = 127
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        activation = _barrier_activation(
            close,
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["volume"],
        )

        lower = activation.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = activation.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        winsorized = activation.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        score = -rank(winsorized)
        return score.where(activation.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)

"""A large close-to-close decline accompanied by abnormally high trading participation is treated as confirmed asymmetric downward order pressure, rather than as an inferred low-volume liquidity vacuum. High relative volume makes the move more consistent with active repricing, institutional de-risking, or information-driven selling that may take several sessions to complete. The signal is made idiosyncratic by removing the contemporaneous equal-weight industry-average pressure score, so it does not simply short broad industry selloffs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _winsorize_cross_section(
    score: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize eligible scores independently on each date."""
    masked = score.where(eligible)
    lower = masked.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = masked.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _industry_residual(
    score: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove same-date industry means only for groups with five valid names."""
    labels = industry.iloc[0].copy()
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "__MISSING_INDUSTRY__")

    residual = score.copy()
    for label in pd.unique(labels):
        columns = labels.index[labels == label]
        group_score = score.loc[:, columns]
        group_eligible = eligible.loc[:, columns]

        valid_count = group_eligible.sum(axis=1)
        group_mean = group_score.where(group_eligible).mean(axis=1)
        demeaned = group_score.sub(group_mean, axis=0)
        use_demeaned = (valid_count >= 5).astype(float)

        adjusted = (
            demeaned.mul(use_demeaned, axis=0)
            + group_score.mul(1.0 - use_demeaned, axis=0)
        )
        residual.loc[:, columns] = adjusted

    return residual


@register_factor
class IdioDownsidePressureConfirmation(BaseFactor):
    """Short idiosyncratic, high-volume downside pressure after confirmed selling."""

    factor_id = "idio_downside_pressure_confirmation"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Downside Pressure Confirmation"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Negative cross-sectional exposure to stocks with unusually large "
        "close-to-close declines confirmed by positive abnormal volume, after "
        "removing contemporaneous industry-average downside pressure."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_close = (close > 0.0) & (previous_close > 0.0)
        log_return = np.log(
            close.where(close > 0.0) / previous_close.where(previous_close > 0.0)
        ).where(valid_close)

        prior_abs_return = log_return.abs().shift(1)
        return_count = prior_abs_return.rolling(20, min_periods=20).count()
        return_median = prior_abs_return.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        valid_return_history = (return_count == 20) & (return_median > 0.0)

        downside = (-log_return).clip(lower=0.0)
        downside_shock = (downside / return_median).clip(upper=5.0)

        positive_prior_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0).shift(1)
        volume_count = positive_prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).count()
        volume_median = positive_prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        valid_volume_history = (volume_count == 20) & (volume_median > 0.0)

        log_relative_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume > 0.0) / volume_median)
        participation = log_relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

        eligible = (
            valid_close
            & valid_return_history
            & valid_volume_history
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & downside_shock.notna()
            & participation.notna()
        )

        raw_pressure = (downside_shock * participation).where(eligible)
        winsorized_pressure = _winsorize_cross_section(raw_pressure, eligible)
        residual = _industry_residual(
            winsorized_pressure, eligible, data["industry"]
        ).where(eligible)

        return (-rank(residual)).where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Idiosyncratic Downside Pressure Confirmation
programs.trading_idea: A large close-to-close decline accompanied by abnormally high trading participation is treated as confirmed asymmetric downward order pressure, rather than as an inferred low-volume liquidity vacuum. High relative volume makes the move more consistent with active repricing, institutional de-risking, or information-driven selling that may take several sessions to complete. The signal is made idiosyncratic by removing the contemporaneous equal-weight industry-average pressure score, so it does not simply short broad industry selloffs.
programs.description: After bar t closes, compute r_t = log(close_t / close_{t-1}). Define downside shock D_t = min(5, max(-r_t, 0) / median(|r_{t-20}|,...,|r_{t-1}|)); require 20 valid prior return observations and a strictly positive denominator. Define participation confirmation P_t = min(3, max(log(volume_t / median(volume_{t-20},...,volume_{t-1})), 0)); require 20 valid positive prior-volume observations. The raw pressure score is S_t = D_t * P_t, so an ordinary-volume or below-normal-volume decline receives zero confirmation. Cross-sectionally winsorize S_t at the eligible-universe 1st and 99th percentiles, subtract the contemporaneous equal-weight mean score of the stock's industry when that industry has at least 5 eligible names, then percentile-rank the resulting industry residual across all eligible stocks. Take negative exposure to the highest-ranked residuals. The signal is formed only after the complete daily bar, including close and volume, is known and is executed no earlier than the next executable bar. Formula-level distinction from range_volume_elasticity_breakout: this construction uses only close-to-close downside returns and positive abnormal-volume confirmation; it contains no intraday range, range-to-volume elasticity ratio, weak-volume condition, or inferred liquidity-withdrawal measure.

programs.code:
"""Turnover-anchor breach pressure confirmed by reclaim rejection and sell excitation.

Mechanism: an initial high-participation break through a recent turnover-weighted
reference price is informative only when subsequent attempts to reclaim that
reference fail while negative return-volume pressure persists.  This distinguishes
unresolved one-sided liquidation from a volume-driven exhaustion low.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_turnover_anchor(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal trailing volume-weighted typical-price anchor, excluding bar t."""
    typical = (high + low + close) / 3.0
    prior_volume = volume.shift(1).where(volume.shift(1) >= 0.0)
    weighted_price = typical.shift(1) * prior_volume
    numerator = weighted_price.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    denominator = prior_volume.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    return numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _near_low(high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One near the bar low and zero near the high, with safe zero-range handling."""
    bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return ((high - close) / bar_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)


@register_factor
class AnchoredBreachRejectionExcitation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "anchored_breach_rejection_excitation"
    name = "Anchored Breach Rejection Excitation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Negative rank of high-volume breaks below a causal turnover-weighted "
        "anchor when three subsequent bars reject reclaim attempts and retain "
        "negative return-volume excitation."
    )
    window_length = 44
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        anchor = _prior_turnover_anchor(high, low, close, volume, 40)
        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        volume_ratio = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # The initiating break is fixed at b=t-3 so all confirmation bars are known.
        anchor_b = anchor.shift(3)
        close_b = close.shift(3)
        previous_close_b = close.shift(4)
        volume_ratio_b = volume_ratio.shift(3)
        initial_low_close = _near_low(high.shift(3), low.shift(3), close_b)

        fresh_break = (
            anchor_b.notna()
            & (previous_close_b >= anchor_b)
            & (close_b < anchor_b)
        )
        break_depth = ((anchor_b - close_b) / anchor_b.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0)
        initial_pressure = (
            break_depth
            * volume_ratio_b.clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
            * initial_low_close
        )

        return_series = close.pct_change()
        rejection_terms = []
        excitation_terms = []
        weights = [0.2, 0.3, 0.5]

        # At t these are bars b+1, b+2, and b+3, respectively.
        for price_shift, weight in zip([2, 1, 0], weights):
            bar_high = high.shift(price_shift)
            bar_low = low.shift(price_shift)
            bar_close = close.shift(price_shift)
            bar_volume_ratio = volume_ratio.shift(price_shift)
            bar_return = return_series.shift(price_shift)

            # A reclaim probe must reach toward the old anchor, then close below it.
            probe_proximity = (bar_high / anchor_b.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(
                lower=0.0, upper=1.0
            )
            rejection_depth = (
                (anchor_b - bar_close) / anchor_b.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            ).clip(lower=0.0)
            rejection_terms.append(
                weight * probe_proximity * rejection_depth * _near_low(bar_high, bar_low, bar_close)
            )

            negative_impulse = (-bar_return).clip(lower=0.0)
            excitation_terms.append(
                weight * negative_impulse * bar_volume_ratio.clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
            )

        reclaim_rejection = rejection_terms[0] + rejection_terms[1] + rejection_terms[2]
        downside_excitation = excitation_terms[0] + excitation_terms[1] + excitation_terms[2]
        pressure = initial_pressure * reclaim_rejection * downside_excitation

        active_score = pressure.where(fresh_break & pressure.notna())
        return (-rank(active_score)).where(active_score.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Anchored Breach Rejection Excitation
programs.trading_idea: A high-participation break below a turnover-weighted reference price is ambiguous by itself because it may be either forced-liquidation continuation or capitulatory exhaustion. The child activates only when the next three bars repeatedly approach the broken reference yet reject below it with low-close outcomes, and when negative return-volume pressure remains elevated. This interaction identifies a self-exciting sell-side state in which attempted demand replenishment fails, an observable distinction that Parent A's initial breach and Parent B's reclaim pattern alone do not fully make.
programs.description: Builds a causal 40-bar volume-weighted price anchor, detects a fresh high-volume downside crossing three bars earlier, and ranks the combined intensity of subsequent failed reclaim attempts, low-close rejection, and negative return-volume excitation. The returned score is negative for names with the strongest unresolved downside pressure.

programs.code:
"""Industry-relative revision drift conditioned on downside execution pressure.

Mechanism: estimate revisions contain delayed information, but their incorporation is
slower when asymmetric return-volume selling pressure masks the revision in the
short-run price path.  Revision signs that conflict with recent relative returns are
therefore magnified only in names experiencing elevated downside pressure.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_demean(values: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise industry demeaning with singleton labels for missing industries."""
    labels = industry.reindex(columns=values.columns).iloc[0].astype(object).copy()
    missing = labels.isna()
    if missing.any():
        labels.loc[missing] = [
            "__singleton_" + str(ticker) for ticker in labels.index[missing]
        ]
    peer_mean = values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("mean").T
    return values - peer_mean


@register_factor
class RevisionDisplacementPressureMask(BaseFactor):
    """Revision disagreement whose price assimilation is masked by sell pressure."""

    factor_id = "revision_displacement_pressure_mask"
    name = "Revision Displacement Under Downside Pressure"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks industry-relative EPS and revenue estimate changes, amplified when "
        "their sign conflicts with recent industry-relative returns during elevated "
        "downside return-volume and weak-close pressure."
    )
    window_length = 25
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        safe_cap = market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # Estimate changes are point-in-time observations.  Scaling makes the two
        # estimate channels comparable without fitting a cross-sectional model.
        eps_change = (eps_estimate - eps_estimate.shift(21)) / safe_close
        revenue_change = (revenue_estimate - revenue_estimate.shift(21)) / safe_cap
        eps_component = rank(eps_change.fillna(0.0)) - 0.5
        revenue_component = rank(revenue_change.fillna(0.0)) - 0.5
        revision = _industry_demean(0.5 * (eps_component + revenue_component), industry)
        revision_signal = rank(revision.fillna(0.0)) - 0.5

        # Relative-return disagreement captures whether the revision has already
        # been incorporated into price.  Positive gap means recent relative weakness.
        ret10 = close / close.shift(10).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        relative_return = _industry_demean(ret10, industry)
        return_gap = rank((-relative_return).fillna(0.0)) - 0.5

        # A broad, causal proxy for Parent A's downside execution state: negative
        # returns receive more weight on high-volume, weak-close bars.
        daily_return = close / close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(volume.gt(0.0))
        adv20 = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=5).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        volume_multiple = (dollar_volume / adv20).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0).fillna(0.0)
        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        weak_close = ((high - close) / bar_range).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.5)
        downside_mark = (-daily_return).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        pressure = (
            downside_mark * volume_multiple * (0.5 + weak_close)
        ).rolling(5, min_periods=3).mean()
        pressure_state = rank(pressure.fillna(0.0))

        # Contradiction is positive for upgrades with weak prices and downgrades
        # with strong prices.  Downside pressure raises the weight of that gap but
        # is bounded so one noisy price sequence cannot reverse a revision signal.
        revision_sign = np.sign(revision_signal)
        contradiction = revision_sign * return_gap
        multiplier = (1.0 + 1.5 * pressure_state * contradiction).clip(0.25, 1.75)
        score = revision_signal * multiplier

        return rank(score.fillna(0.0)).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)
programs.name: Revision Displacement Under Downside Pressure
programs.trading_idea: Industry-relative estimate revisions are most underpriced when recent return-volume selling pressure obscures their information content. A positive idiosyncratic revision combined with weak relative price action is a delayed-good-news setup, while a negative revision combined with relative strength identifies news that the market has not yet fully incorporated. The interaction adds edge because revision displacement alone cannot distinguish already-assimilated news from price-dislocated news, and downside-pressure measures alone cannot distinguish informational selling from temporary execution pressure.
programs.description: The signal forms an industry-relative composite of EPS- and revenue-estimate changes, then magnifies it when its sign conflicts with the stock's recent industry-relative return under high downside return-volume and weak-close pressure. It returns a broad cross-sectional rank with neutral fallback values for sparse estimate histories.

"""An idiosyncratic negative overnight repricing followed by no intraday repair and a close near the session low is a directly observable confirmation that selling pressure remained one-sided through the full daily session. Rather than identifying an unobservable liquidity-withdrawal counterparty, the factor treats this pattern as a reduced-form bad-news-amplification and short-horizon underreaction signal: price discovery may remain incomplete when a negative information shock is confirmed rather than reversed. The prediction is a negative return over the six sessions beginning at the next executable open."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _complete_ohlcv_history(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal availability mask requiring complete OHLCV history through t."""
    observed = (
        open_.notna()
        & high.notna()
        & low.notna()
        & close.notna()
        & volume.notna()
    )
    return observed.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum().eq(window)


@register_factor
class UnrepairedOvernightBadnewsLiquidityDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks liquid names with confirmed idiosyncratic downside overnight gaps."""

    factor_id = "unrepaired_overnight_badnews_liquidity_drift"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Downside Gap Confirmation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "At each completed close, ranks liquid stocks whose idiosyncratic "
        "negative overnight gap was not repaired intraday and whose close "
        "remained near the session low; high scores are expected to underperform."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        history_ok = _complete_ohlcv_history(open_, high, low, close, volume, 61)

        dollar_volume = close * volume
        prior_adv20 = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        liquidity_cutoff = prior_adv20.where(history_ok).quantile(0.30, axis=1)
        liquid = prior_adv20.ge(liquidity_cutoff, axis=0) & prior_adv20.notna()
        eligible = history_ok & liquid

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        gap = open_.div(prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)).sub(1.0)
        median_gap = gap.where(eligible).median(axis=1)
        relative_gap = gap.sub(median_gap, axis=0)
        negative_idiosyncratic_gap = eligible & gap.lt(median_gap, axis=0)

        downside_gap = (-relative_gap).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.10).div(0.10)
        downside_gap = downside_gap.where(negative_idiosyncratic_gap, 0.0)

        gap_amount = prior_close.sub(open_).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        repair = close.sub(open_).div(gap_amount).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        repair_failure = 1.0 - repair
        repair_failure = repair_failure.where(negative_idiosyncratic_gap, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        session_range = high.sub(low)
        close_weakness = 1.0 - close.sub(low).div(session_range.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        close_weakness = close_weakness.where(session_range.ne(0.0), 0.5)
        close_weakness = close_weakness.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        score = downside_gap * repair_failure * close_weakness
        ranked = rank(score.where(eligible))
        signal = ranked.where(negative_idiosyncratic_gap, 0.0)
        return signal.fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Idiosyncratic Downside Gap Confirmation
programs.trading_idea: An idiosyncratic negative overnight repricing followed by no intraday repair and a close near the session low is a directly observable confirmation that selling pressure remained one-sided through the full daily session. Rather than identifying an unobservable liquidity-withdrawal counterparty, the factor treats this pattern as a reduced-form bad-news-amplification and short-horizon underreaction signal: price discovery may remain incomplete when a negative information shock is confirmed rather than reversed. The prediction is a negative return over the six sessions beginning at the next executable open.
programs.description: At the completed close of day t, define each stock's overnight gap as g_i,t = open_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. Define the contemporaneous market gap as the cross-sectional median g across eligible stocks, and define idiosyncratic downside gap d_i,t = clip(-(g_i,t - median(g_t)), 0, 0.10) / 0.10. A stock is eligible only if it has non-missing OHLCV observations for days t-60 through t and its prior-20-day average dollar volume, mean(close*volume from t-20 through t-1), is at or above the 30th cross-sectional percentile among stocks with the required history. For stocks with g_i,t < median(g_t), define intraday repair as r_i,t = clip((close_i,t - open_i,t) / (close_i,t-1 - open_i,t), 0, 1), and define repair failure f_i,t = 1 - r_i,t. Define close weakness w_i,t = 1 - (close_i,t - low_i,t) / (high_i,t - low_i,t); if high equals low, set w_i,t = 0.5. The raw downside-confirmation score is s_i,t = d_i,t * f_i,t * w_i,t; stocks without a negative idiosyncratic gap receive no signal. Cross-sectionally rank s among eligible stocks into [0,1], with the highest-ranked names expected to underperform. No inverse-relative-volume term is used: volume is used only for the fixed ex-ante liquidity screen, avoiding an interpretation of low volume as uniquely identifying liquidity withdrawal. The signal is computed only after day t closes, entered no earlier than day t+1 open, and evaluated from that next-session open through the close of day t+6.
