programs.trading_idea: A repaired opening gap is usually interpreted as temporary liquidity pressure, but its meaning changes when the recent range-volume relation indicates that depth is being withdrawn: repeated closes at the repair-side bar edge can reflect the terminal execution of a one-sided inventory program rather than durable information. Balance-sheet resilience distinguishes a repaired downside gap in a solvent firm from genuine distress, while fragility makes repaired upside gaps more likely to be short-covering or thin-book support. The interaction carries edge because the gap repair supplies the intraday reversal event and solvency interpretation, while the accelerating inverse range-volume elasticity identifies the depleted-liquidity regime in which that apparent repair is most likely exhausted and subsequently reversed.
programs.description: Computes asymmetrically solvency-weighted opening-gap repairs and retains them only when a strengthening inverse range-volume elasticity and repeated repair-side edge closes indicate liquidity depletion. Higher scores represent stronger repaired-downside/solvent episodes and are expected to reverse downward over the next six bars.

programs.code:
"""This is an explicitly observable OHLCV impact-transition hypothesis, not a claim that displayed depth or a metaorder is identified from daily bars. A stock that moves from an unusually high range-per-dollar-volume session to an unusually low-impact but still high-volume session, while closing persistently on the same side of its daily ranges, may be in a temporary price-discovery deceleration rather than a completed reversal. The hypothesis is that the signed terminal-price pressure in this narrowly defined two-day transition predicts same-direction returns over the following six bars; the sign is empirical and can be rejected if absorption or distribution dominates."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _baseline_impact_percentiles(impact: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute t-1 and t impact percentiles against the common t-61:t-2 baseline."""
    values = impact.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    prior_percentile = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    current_percentile = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)

    # At t, Python slice [t-61:t-1] contains exactly observations t-61 through t-2.
    for t in range(61, n_rows):
        baseline = values[t - 61 : t - 1]
        valid_count = np.isfinite(baseline).sum(axis=0)
        enough_history = valid_count >= 45

        previous_value = values[t - 1]
        current_value = values[t]
        previous_count = np.sum(baseline <= previous_value[None, :], axis=0)
        current_count = np.sum(baseline <= current_value[None, :], axis=0)

        denominator = np.where(enough_history, valid_count, np.nan)
        prior_percentile[t] = previous_count / denominator
        current_percentile[t] = current_count / denominator

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(prior_percentile, index=impact.index, columns=impact.columns),
        pd.DataFrame(current_percentile, index=impact.index, columns=impact.columns),
    )


@register_factor
class DepthReplenishmentTransitionExecutionDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Directional drift after a high-impact to low-impact, high-volume transition."""

    factor_id = "depth_replenishment_transition_execution_drift"
    name = "Impact-Transition Directional Drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks signed close-location pressure only for names transitioning from "
        "an unusually high prior-day range-per-dollar-volume impact to an "
        "unusually low current-day impact with abnormal volume and persistent "
        "open-to-close directional agreement."
    )
    window_length = 62
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        price_range = high - low
        relative_range = price_range / close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        dollar_volume = volume * close

        bar_valid = (
            (close > 0.0)
            & (open_ > 0.0)
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & (high > low)
            & (relative_range >= 0.001)
        )
        impact = (relative_range / dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(bar_valid)
        impact = impact.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        prior_pct, current_pct = _baseline_impact_percentiles(impact)
        high_prior_impact = prior_pct >= 0.80
        low_current_impact = current_pct <= 0.20

        positive_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
        prior_volume_median = positive_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=1).median()
        abnormal_volume = volume >= (1.5 * prior_volume_median)

        clv = (
            (2.0 * close - high - low) / price_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        open_to_close = (close / open_.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )

        prior_clv = clv.shift(1)
        prior_open_to_close = open_to_close.shift(1)
        persistent_terminal_direction = (clv * prior_clv) > 0.0
        current_terminal_pressure = clv.abs() >= 0.5
        current_direction_agrees = (clv * open_to_close) > 0.0
        prior_direction_agrees = (prior_clv * prior_open_to_close) > 0.0

        overnight_gap = (open_ / close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        acceptable_gap = overnight_gap.abs() <= 0.05

        eligible = (
            bar_valid
            & bar_valid.shift(1).fillna(False)
            & high_prior_impact
            & low_current_impact
            & abnormal_volume
            & current_terminal_pressure
            & persistent_terminal_direction
            & current_direction_agrees
            & prior_direction_agrees
            & acceptable_gap
        )

        volume_ratio = volume / prior_volume_median.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        raw_signal = clv * np.log(volume_ratio)
        raw_signal = raw_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # Ranking occurs only inside the eligible transition cross-section.
        return rank(raw_signal.where(eligible)).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Impact-Transition Directional Drift
programs.trading_idea: This is an explicitly observable OHLCV impact-transition hypothesis, not a claim that displayed depth or a metaorder is identified from daily bars. A stock that moves from an unusually high range-per-dollar-volume session to an unusually low-impact but still high-volume session, while closing persistently on the same side of its daily ranges, may be in a temporary price-discovery deceleration rather than a completed reversal. The hypothesis is that the signed terminal-price pressure in this narrowly defined two-day transition predicts same-direction returns over the following six bars; the sign is empirical and can be rejected if absorption or distribution dominates.
programs.description: At signal-date close t, define relative range R_s = (high_s - low_s) / close_s and intraday dollar volume DV_s = volume_s * close_s. Define impact I_s = R_s / DV_s. A bar is valid only when close_s > 0, open_s > 0, volume_s > 0, high_s > low_s, and R_s >= 0.001; zero-volume, zero-range, and sub-10-basis-point-range bars are excluded rather than divided through. For both I_(t-1) and I_t, use the same pre-transition baseline of valid impacts from t-61 through t-2, requiring at least 45 valid observations. The prior-day high-impact condition is that the empirical percentile of I_(t-1) within that baseline is at least 80%; the current low-impact condition is that the empirical percentile of I_t within the same baseline is at most 20%, where percentile is the fraction of baseline observations less than or equal to the evaluated impact. Current volume must be abnormal: volume_t must be at least 1.5 times the median positive volume from t-20 through t-1. Define close-location CLV_s = (2*close_s - high_s - low_s) / (high_s - low_s). Retain only transitions where abs(CLV_t) >= 0.5, CLV_t and CLV_(t-1) have the same nonzero sign, and both CLV_t*(close_t/open_t - 1) and CLV_(t-1)*(close_(t-1)/open_(t-1) - 1) are positive, ensuring that terminal range location agrees with each day's open-to-close direction. Exclude observations with abs(open_t / close_(t-1) - 1) > 0.05. The raw signal is CLV_t * ln(volume_t / median(volume_(t-20:t-1))); cross-sectionally rank this raw signal only among eligible transition names on date t, with high ranks long and low ranks short. No sector or industry residualization is applied. The signal is known after the close of t, enters at the next bar's open, and is evaluated through the close of t+6.

programs.code:
"""This is a reduced-form test of whether an idiosyncratic close-to-close move is less likely to persist when it occurs during a broad same-industry trading episode but the stock's own dollar-turnover response is unusually small relative to its market-capacity-adjusted peers. The prediction is not that ETF flow, dealer inventory, or displayed depth is observed; rather, conditional on broad peer participation, a residual move unsupported by proportional own trading activity is treated as a lower-information price displacement and is expected to reverse over the next six daily bars. The signal fades positive unsupported residual moves and buys negative unsupported residual moves."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _winsorize_cross_section(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally winsorize each date's available cross section at 1/99 percentiles."""
    lower = df.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = df.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return df.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _leave_one_out_quantile(values: np.ndarray, quantile: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the linear-interpolated quantile after removing each observation."""
    n = len(values)
    result = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype=float)
    if n < 2:
        return result

    ordered = np.sort(values)
    positions = np.searchsorted(ordered, values, side="left")
    reduced_n = n - 1
    h = (reduced_n - 1) * quantile
    lo = int(np.floor(h))
    hi = int(np.ceil(h))
    weight = h - lo

    lo_index = lo + (lo >= positions)
    hi_index = hi + (hi >= positions)
    result = (1.0 - weight) * ordered[lo_index] + weight * ordered[hi_index]
    return result


def _peer_statistics(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    dollar_turnover: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    capacity_turnover: pd.DataFrame,
    abnormal_turnover: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute causal daily leave-one-out industry peer statistics."""
    index = ret.index
    columns = ret.columns
    peer_return = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    synchronization = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    peer_capacity_turnover = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    peer_at_percentile = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)

    for row_number, timestamp in enumerate(index):
        ret_row = ret.iloc[row_number]
        dt_row = dollar_turnover.iloc[row_number]
        cap_row = market_cap.iloc[row_number]
        ind_row = industry.iloc[row_number]
        cat_row = capacity_turnover.iloc[row_number]
        at_row = abnormal_turnover.iloc[row_number]

        core = (
            ret_row.notna()
            & (dt_row > 0.0)
            & cap_row.notna()
            & (cap_row > 0.0)
            & ind_row.notna()
        )
        if not core.any():
            continue

        core_columns = columns[core.to_numpy()]
        frame = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "industry": ind_row.loc[core_columns],
                "return": ret_row.loc[core_columns].astype(float),
                "cap": cap_row.loc[core_columns].astype(float),
            },
            index=core_columns,
        )
        frame["cap_return"] = frame["cap"] * frame["return"]
        grouped = frame.groupby("industry", sort=False)

        total_cap = grouped["cap"].transform("sum")
        total_cap_return = grouped["cap_return"].transform("sum")
        group_size = grouped["cap"].transform("count").astype(float)
        loo_count = group_size - 1.0
        loo_cap = total_cap - frame["cap"]
        loo_return = (total_cap_return - frame["cap_return"]) / loo_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        positive = (frame["return"] > 0.0).astype(float)
        negative = (frame["return"] < 0.0).astype(float)
        positive_count = positive.groupby(frame["industry"], sort=False).transform("sum")
        negative_count = negative.groupby(frame["industry"], sort=False).transform("sum")
        same_positive = positive_count - positive
        same_negative = negative_count - negative
        same_sign = pd.Series(
            np.where(loo_return > 0.0, same_positive, same_negative),
            index=frame.index,
            dtype=float,
        )
        sync = same_sign / loo_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        peer_return.iloc[row_number, columns.get_indexer(core_columns)] = loo_return.to_numpy()
        synchronization.iloc[row_number, columns.get_indexer(core_columns)] = sync.to_numpy()
        peer_count.iloc[row_number, columns.get_indexer(core_columns)] = loo_count.to_numpy()

        cat_valid_columns = core_columns[
            cat_row.loc[core_columns].notna().to_numpy()
        ]
        if len(cat_valid_columns) > 0:
            cat_frame = pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "industry": ind_row.loc[cat_valid_columns],
                    "cap": cap_row.loc[cat_valid_columns].astype(float),
                    "cat": cat_row.loc[cat_valid_columns].astype(float),
                },
                index=cat_valid_columns,
            )
            cat_frame["cap_cat"] = cat_frame["cap"] * cat_frame["cat"]
            cat_grouped = cat_frame.groupby("industry", sort=False)
            cat_cap_sum = cat_grouped["cap"].transform("sum")
            cat_value_sum = cat_grouped["cap_cat"].transform("sum")
            loo_cat = (cat_value_sum - cat_frame["cap_cat"]) / (
                cat_cap_sum - cat_frame["cap"]
            ).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            peer_capacity_turnover.iloc[
                row_number, columns.get_indexer(cat_valid_columns)
            ] = loo_cat.to_numpy()

        at_valid_columns = core_columns[
            at_row.loc[core_columns].notna().to_numpy()
        ]
        if len(at_valid_columns) > 0:
            at_frame = pd.DataFrame(
                {"industry": ind_row.loc[at_valid_columns]},
                index=at_valid_columns,
            )
            for _, group in at_frame.groupby("industry", sort=False):
                group_columns = group.index
                values = at_row.loc[group_columns].astype(float).to_numpy()
                cutoffs = _leave_one_out_quantile(values, 0.80)
                peer_at_percentile.iloc[
                    row_number, columns.get_indexer(group_columns)
                ] = cutoffs

    return peer_return, synchronization, peer_capacity_turnover, peer_at_percentile, peer_count


@register_factor
class CapacityMatchedPeerCrossimpactEcho(BaseFactor):
    """Reversal signal for weak own-turnover responses to synchronized peer flow."""

    factor_id = "capacity_matched_peer_crossimpact_echo"
    name = "Peer-Flow Capacity Mismatch Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks negative idiosyncratic returns times a positive capacity-normalized "
        "turnover shortfall versus synchronized same-industry peers."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        returns = close.pct_change()
        dollar_turnover = close * volume
        positive_turnover = dollar_turnover.where(dollar_turnover > 0.0)
        prior_turnover_mean = positive_turnover.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        abnormal_turnover = dollar_turnover / prior_turnover_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        abnormal_turnover = _winsorize_cross_section(abnormal_turnover)

        capacity_turnover = abnormal_turnover / np.sqrt(market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0))
        (
            peer_return,
            synchronization,
            peer_capacity_turnover,
            peer_at_percentile,
            peer_count,
        ) = _peer_statistics(
            returns,
            dollar_turnover,
            market_cap,
            industry,
            capacity_turnover,
            abnormal_turnover,
        )

        residual_return = returns - peer_return
        mismatch = np.log(
            (peer_capacity_turnover + 1.0e-12)
            / (capacity_turnover + 1.0e-12)
        )
        mismatch = _winsorize_cross_section(mismatch)

        base_valid = (
            returns.notna()
            & (dollar_turnover > 0.0)
            & market_cap.notna()
            & (market_cap > 0.0)
            & industry.notna()
            & (peer_count >= 5.0)
            & peer_return.notna()
            & capacity_turnover.notna()
            & peer_capacity_turnover.notna()
            & abnormal_turnover.notna()
        )
        nonzero_peer_return = peer_return.abs() > 0.0
        peer_move_median = peer_return.abs().where(base_valid & nonzero_peer_return).median(axis=1)
        sufficiently_broad_move = peer_return.abs().ge(peer_move_median, axis=0)

        active = (
            base_valid
            & (synchronization >= 0.60)
            & nonzero_peer_return
            & sufficiently_broad_move
            & (mismatch > 0.0)
            & peer_at_percentile.notna()
            & (abnormal_turnover <= peer_at_percentile)
        )

        raw_score = (-residual_return * mismatch).where(active)
        winsorized_score = _winsorize_cross_section(raw_score)
        ranked_score = winsorized_score.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return ranked_score.where(active, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

The prediction is not that ETF flow, dealer inventory, or displayed depth is observed; rather, conditional on broad peer participation, a residual move unsupported by proportional own trading activity is treated as a lower-information price displacement and is expected to reverse over the next six daily bars. The signal fades positive unsupported residual moves and buys negative unsupported residual moves.
programs.description: At the close of day t, define stock return r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1 and dollar turnover DT_i,t = close_i,t * volume_i,t. The peer universe for stock i is all other stocks with the same industry label, a valid return at t, positive DT at t, and non-missing positive marketCap at t; require at least 5 such peers. Define the leave-one-out industry return P_i,t as the market-cap-weighted mean of peer returns, using weights marketCap_j,t, and residual return E_i,t = r_i,t - P_i,t. Define peer synchronization B_i,t as the fraction of eligible peers whose return has the same sign as P_i,t; require B_i,t >= 0.60 and abs(P_i,t) > 0. Define abnormal turnover AT_i,t = DT_i,t / mean(DT_i,t-20 through DT_i,t-1), requiring 20 prior positive daily-turnover observations; values are winsorized cross-sectionally each day to the 1st and 99th percentiles. Define capacity-normalized abnormal turnover CAT_i,t = AT_i,t / sqrt(marketCap_i,t), and define the peer benchmark CATpeer_i,t as the market-cap-weighted mean CAT among eligible peers. The capacity mismatch is M_i,t = log((CATpeer_i,t + 1e-12) / (CAT_i,t + 1e-12)), winsorized daily to the 1st/99th percentiles. Suppress a potential stock-specific volume shock by setting the signal to zero whenever AT_i,t exceeds the 80th percentile of AT among the eligible same-industry peer universe on day t. The raw score is S_i,t = -E_i,t * M_i,t, retained only when B_i,t >= 0.60, abs(P_i,t) is at or above the cross-sectional median of nonzero abs(P_i,t) values among valid stocks, and M_i,t > 0; otherwise it is zero. Finally winsorize S cross-sectionally to the 1st/99th percentiles and rank it cross-sectionally, with higher scores indicating expected positive six-bar forward returns. All quantities use information available at the close of t; positions are entered no earlier than t+1, and evaluation uses returns from t+1 onward only.

"""Resilience-modulated signed-pressure polarity under repaired-gap exhaustion.

Mechanism: compressed-range, high-activity signed pressure usually reflects an
unresolved execution schedule.  A polarity flip is applied only when a repaired
opening gap, repair-side close persistence, and accelerating inverse
range-volume elasticity identify terminal liquidity depletion; balance-sheet
resilience distinguishes credible downside repairs from fragile upside support.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_resilience(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time resilience composite with a neutral fallback for sparse filings."""
    cash_ratio = data["cashRatio"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    debt_assets = data["debtToAssets"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    operating_cf = data["operatingCashFlow"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    market_cap = data["marketCap"].replace([0.0, np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    coverage = data["interestCoverage"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    components = [
        cash_ratio.rank(axis=1, pct=True),
        (-debt_assets).rank(axis=1, pct=True),
        (operating_cf / market_cap).rank(axis=1, pct=True),
        coverage.rank(axis=1, pct=True),
    ]
    total = sum(component.fillna(0.0) for component in components)
    count = sum(component.notna().astype(float) for component in components)
    return (total / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).fillna(0.5).clip(0.0, 1.0)


def _inverse_range_volume_elasticity(
    log_volume: pd.DataFrame, log_range: pd.DataFrame, lookback: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal trailing estimate of -Cov(log range, log volume)/Var(log volume)."""
    covariance = log_volume.rolling(lookback, min_periods=10).cov(log_range)
    variance = log_volume.rolling(lookback, min_periods=10).var()
    return covariance.mul(-1.0).div(variance.replace(0.0, np.nan))


@register_factor
class ResilienceModulatedPressureRepairPolarity(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "resilience_modulated_pressure_repair_polarity"
    name = "Resilience-Modulated Pressure Repair Polarity"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Lagged signed abnormal-volume pressure is continued in compressed, active "
        "conditions but polarity-flipped when a resilience-weighted repaired-gap "
        "exhaustion state indicates terminal liquidity depletion."
    )
    window_length = 24
    inputs = [
        "open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "cashRatio",
        "debtToAssets", "operatingCashFlow", "marketCap", "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_price = data["open"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        bar_range = high - low
        normalized_range = (bar_range / previous_close).where(previous_close.gt(0.0))
        close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        close_location = close_location.clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)

        volume_base = volume.shift(2).rolling(15, min_periods=8).median()
        prior_volume_ratio = volume.shift(1) / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_pressure = close_location.shift(1) * np.log1p(
            prior_volume_ratio.where(prior_volume_ratio.ge(0.0))
        )
        prior_pressure = prior_pressure.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        range_base = normalized_range.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).median()
        activity_base = volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=8).median()
        range_ratio = normalized_range / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        activity_ratio = volume / activity_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        compression = (1.0 - range_ratio).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
        activity = np.log(activity_ratio.where(activity_ratio.gt(0.0))).clip(0.0, 1.5)
        activity = (activity / 1.5).fillna(0.0)
        continuation_weight = (0.20 + 0.80 * compression) * (0.20 + 0.80 * activity)

        gap = open_price / previous_close - 1.0
        intraday_return = close / open_price.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        repair_fraction = (-intraday_return / gap.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        repair_direction = (-np.sign(gap)).fillna(0.0)

        gap_salience = (gap.abs() / range_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 2.0) / 2.0
        repair_edge = (close_location * repair_direction).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        prior_repair_edge = (close_location.shift(1) * repair_direction).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        persistent_repair_edge = repair_edge * (0.5 + 0.5 * prior_repair_edge.fillna(0.0))

        log_volume = np.log(activity_ratio.where(activity_ratio.gt(0.0)))
        log_range = np.log(range_ratio.where(range_ratio.gt(0.0)))
        elasticity = _inverse_range_volume_elasticity(log_volume, log_range, 15)
        elasticity_acceleration = elasticity - elasticity.shift(3)
        elasticity_strength = elasticity.where(elasticity.gt(0.0)).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        acceleration_strength = elasticity_acceleration.where(
            elasticity_acceleration.gt(0.0)
        ).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        depletion = (elasticity_strength.fillna(0.0) * acceleration_strength.fillna(0.0))

        resilience = _cross_sectional_resilience(data)
        solvency_weight = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(gap.to_numpy() < 0.0, resilience.to_numpy(), 1.0 - resilience.to_numpy()),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

        pressure_repair_alignment = (np.sign(prior_pressure) * repair_direction).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        exhaustion_state = (
            repair_fraction.fillna(0.0)
            * gap_salience.fillna(0.0)
            * persistent_repair_edge.fillna(0.0)
            * depletion
            * solvency_weight
            * pressure_repair_alignment.fillna(0.0)
        ).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        polarity = 1.0 - 2.0 * exhaustion_state
        raw = prior_pressure * continuation_weight * polarity
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        score = 2.0 * raw.rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5) - 1.0
        return score.where(close.notna(), 0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Resilience-Modulated Pressure Repair Polarity
programs.trading_idea: Compressed-range, abnormal-volume signed pressure normally indicates an incompletely absorbed directional execution program and should continue. However, when that pressure is aligned with a repaired opening gap, closes repeatedly at the repair-side edge, and inverse range-volume elasticity is accelerating, the same pressure more likely marks terminal liquidity depletion and should reverse. Solvency determines whether a downside repair is credible non-distress buying support, while fragility makes upside repairs more likely to be transient short-covering; thus the child identifies when Parent A's continuation mechanism should be polarity-flipped by Parent B's exhaustion state.
programs.description: The factor starts with lagged close-location abnormal-volume pressure, softly weighted by current range compression and activity. It reverses that pressure only in a resilience-weighted repaired-gap exhaustion regime identified by repair completion, repair-side closes, and accelerating inverse range-volume elasticity.

programs.code:
"""This is an incremental execution-pressure proxy, not a claim that daily OHLCV identifies a metaorder or displayed-depth replenishment. The hypothesis is that repeated, unusually high participation sessions that close persistently near one end of an unusually compressed daily range can indicate unresolved directional trading pressure, conditional on the absence of a recent earnings-release surprise and a large contemporaneous price shock. If that pressure is persistent rather than fully informational, the sign of the footprint should predict six-bar continuation; if it is instead auction flow, balanced trading, or news-driven repricing, the conditioning rules should reduce its contribution."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_winsorize(
    values: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize each row at eligible-name 1st and 99th percentiles."""
    masked = values.where(eligible)
    lower = masked.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = masked.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _earnings_event_flag(surprise: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag newly available or revised point-in-time surprise observations."""
    previous = surprise.shift(1)
    return surprise.notna() & (previous.isna() | surprise.ne(previous))


@register_factor
class LatentParticipationImpactSuppressionDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Conditioned low-impact participation footprint aggregated over five sessions."""

    factor_id = "latent_participation_impact_suppression_drift"
    name = "Conditioned Low-Impact Participation Drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks a five-session, decay-weighted signed participation footprint: "
        "high-volume closes near a compressed range edge, attenuated after "
        "large price shocks and excluded around mechanically detected earnings events."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        price_valid = close.gt(0.0) & previous_close.gt(0.0)
        bar_valid = price_valid & high.notna() & low.notna() & high.ge(low)

        ratio = (close / previous_close).where(price_valid)
        log_return = np.log(ratio).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        bar_range = high - low
        normalized_range = (bar_range / previous_close).where(bar_valid)
        normalized_range = normalized_range.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        range_valid = normalized_range.notna()

        close_location = pd.DataFrame(
            np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns, dtype=float
        )
        positive_range = bar_valid & bar_range.gt(0.0)
        close_location = close_location.where(~positive_range, 0.0)
        close_location = close_location.where(
            ~positive_range,
            2.0 * (close - low) / bar_range - 1.0,
        )
        zero_range = bar_valid & bar_range.eq(0.0)
        close_location = close_location.where(~zero_range, 0.0)
        close_location = close_location.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)

        valid_volume = volume.gt(0.0)
        mean_volume = volume.where(valid_volume).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        abnormal_participation = np.log(volume / mean_volume)
        abnormal_participation = abnormal_participation.clip(lower=0.0)
        abnormal_participation = abnormal_participation.where(
            valid_volume & mean_volume.gt(0.0)
        )

        range_percentile = normalized_range.rolling(60, min_periods=60).rank(pct=True)
        compression = 1.0 - range_percentile

        shock_denominator = log_return.abs().clip(lower=0.0001)
        shock_weight = (0.03 / shock_denominator).clip(upper=1.0)
        shock_weight = shock_weight.where(log_return.notna())

        eps_event = _earnings_event_flag(data["epsSurprise"])
        revenue_event = _earnings_event_flag(data["revenueSurprise"])
        event_flag = eps_event | revenue_event
        contaminated = event_flag.rolling(3, min_periods=1).max().fillna(0.0).gt(0.0)

        component_valid = (
            close_location.notna()
            & abnormal_participation.notna()
            & compression.notna()
            & shock_weight.notna()
            & range_valid
        )

        raw_footprint = (
            close_location * abnormal_participation * compression * shock_weight
        ).where(component_valid)
        raw_footprint = raw_footprint.where(~contaminated, 0.0)

        clipped_footprint = _cross_sectional_winsorize(
            raw_footprint, component_valid
        )
        clipped_footprint = clipped_footprint.where(~contaminated, 0.0)

        weights = np.array([0.70 ** j for j in range(5)], dtype=float)
        schedule_score = pd.DataFrame(
            0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns, dtype=float
        )
        for lag, weight in enumerate(weights):
            schedule_score = schedule_score + weight * clipped_footprint.shift(lag)
        schedule_score = schedule_score / float(weights.sum())

        five_day_valid = component_valid.rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum().eq(5)
        schedule_score = schedule_score.where(five_day_valid)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0))
        average_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        dollar_volume_valid = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).count().eq(20)
        liquidity_cutoff = average_dollar_volume.where(dollar_volume_valid).quantile(
            0.30, axis=1
        )
        liquid = average_dollar_volume.ge(liquidity_cutoff, axis=0) & dollar_volume_valid

        eligible = schedule_score.notna() & ~contaminated & liquid
        clipped_score = _cross_sectional_winsorize(schedule_score, eligible)
        final_rank = clipped_score.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return (2.0 * final_rank - 1.0).where(eligible)
programs.name: Conditioned Low-Impact Participation Drift
programs.trading_idea: This is an incremental execution-pressure proxy, not a claim that daily OHLCV identifies a metaorder or displayed-depth replenishment. The hypothesis is that repeated, unusually high participation sessions that close persistently near one end of an unusually compressed daily range can indicate unresolved directional trading pressure, conditional on the absence of a recent earnings-release surprise and a large contemporaneous price shock. If that pressure is persistent rather than fully informational, the sign of the footprint should predict six-bar continuation; if it is instead auction flow, balanced trading, or news-driven repricing, the conditioning rules should reduce its contribution.
programs.description: At each signal date t, use only observations available through the close of bar t and trade no earlier than bar t+1. Define daily log return r_t = log(close_t / close_{t-1}) and normalized range q_t = (high_t - low_t) / close_{t-1}; observations with nonpositive or missing close_t or close_{t-1} are invalid. Define close location clv_t = 2*(close_t-low_t)/(high_t-low_t)-1 when high_t>low_t, and clv_t=0 for zero-range bars. Define abnormal participation a_t = max(0, log(volume_t / mean(volume_{t-19:t}))), requiring 20 valid positive-volume observations including t. Define p_t as the inclusive trailing 60-observation empirical percentile of q_t within q_{t-59:t}, requiring 60 valid ranges; range-compression weight is c_t=1-p_t. Define return-shock weight d_t=min(1, 0.03/max(abs(r_t), 0.0001)), so returns of 3% or less receive weight 1 and larger shocks are proportionally downweighted. An earnings-event flag e_t equals 1 if either epsSurprise_t or revenueSurprise_t is non-null and differs from its immediately preceding available daily value, including a transition from null to non-null; otherwise e_t=0. A date is event-contaminated when max(e_t,e_{t-1},e_{t-2})=1. For every non-event-contaminated date s, compute raw footprint x_s=clv_s*a_s*c_s*d_s; otherwise set x_s=0. Winsorize x_s cross-sectionally each date at the 1st and 99th percentiles among eligible names. Form the fixed five-session execution-schedule score S_t=(sum from j=0 to 4 of 0.70^j*x_{t-j})/(sum from j=0 to 4 of 0.70^j), requiring valid component inputs for all five dates. The eligible cross-sectional universe at t consists of names with valid S_t, no event contamination at t, and 20-day average dollar volume mean(close_s*volume_s for s=t-19...t) at or above the cross-sectional 30th percentile among names with valid 20-day dollar-volume histories. Winsorize S_t at the eligible-universe 1st/99th percentiles, then assign the final factor as the eligible-universe percentile rank of S_t mapped to [-1,1]. Positive values are long and negative values are short. Relative to the named concealed-flow parents, this is explicitly an incremental conditioned variant: its score is algebraically defined by a 60-day within-stock range percentile, a fixed 3% shock attenuation, a mechanically detected three-bar post-surprise exclusion, and a normalized five-bar 0.70-decay aggregation. It should be admitted only if it retains incremental alpha after neutralization against the cited low-impact/participation parent factors and after realistic turnover and trading-cost tests.

"""Cadenced opening-extension rejection after accelerated impact pressure.

Mechanism: a repaired opening gap is interpreted as terminal execution exhaustion only
when it extends an accelerating sequence of same-signed, unusually high price-impact
events.  The completed opening rejection distinguishes absorption of a pressured
schedule from a routine one-bar auction reversal.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _accelerating_cadence(impact: pd.DataFrame, event: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Emit a signed cadence score on the third same-signed event.

    For each ticker, the score is nonzero only if the last two qualifying events
    occurred within 20 bars and the interval into the current event shortened.
    All event times used at a row are contemporaneous or earlier.
    """
    values = impact.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    flags = event.to_numpy(dtype=bool)
    output = np.zeros_like(values, dtype=float)

    for col in range(values.shape[1]):
        positive_events = []
        negative_events = []
        for row in range(values.shape[0]):
            value = values[row, col]
            if not flags[row, col] or not np.isfinite(value) or value == 0.0:
                continue
            history = positive_events if value > 0.0 else negative_events
            if len(history) >= 2:
                first = history[-2]
                second = history[-1]
                first_gap = second - first
                second_gap = row - second
                if (
                    row - first <= 20
                    and first_gap > 0
                    and second_gap > 0
                    and second_gap < first_gap
                ):
                    acceleration = (first_gap - second_gap) / (first_gap + second_gap)
                    output[row, col] = np.sign(value) * acceleration
            history.append(row)

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=impact.index, columns=impact.columns)


@register_factor
class CadenceConfirmedOpeningExtensionReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cadence_confirmed_opening_extension_reversal"
    name = "Cadenced Opening Extension Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks opening gaps that extend an accelerating same-signed impact cadence "
        "but repair intraday on elevated participation; repaired downside extensions "
        "are positive and repaired upside extensions are negative."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        open_price = data["open"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        participation = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        daily_return = close / previous_close - 1.0
        daily_range = (high - low) / previous_close

        valid_impact = (
            previous_close.notna()
            & prior_volume.gt(0.0)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & daily_return.notna()
            & daily_range.ge(0.0)
        )
        impact = (
            np.sign(daily_return)
            * daily_range
            / participation.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).where(valid_impact)
        impact = impact.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        impact_cutoff = impact.abs().rolling(60, min_periods=40).quantile(0.80).shift(1)
        event = valid_impact & impact.abs().gt(impact_cutoff)
        cadence = _accelerating_cadence(impact, event)

        gap = open_price / previous_close - 1.0
        intraday_return = close / open_price.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        repair = (-intraday_return / gap.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        same_direction_extension = np.sign(gap).eq(np.sign(cadence)) & gap.ne(0.0)

        participation_score = participation.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        raw = (
            -np.sign(cadence)
            * gap.abs()
            * repair
            * cadence.abs()
            * participation_score
        )
        confirmed = (
            cadence.ne(0.0)
            & same_direction_extension
            & repair.ge(0.5)
            & participation.ge(1.0)
            & raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).notna()
        )
        raw = raw.where(confirmed, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        lower = raw.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
        upper = raw.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
        clipped = raw.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        scored = rank(clipped)
        return scored.sub(scored.mean(axis=1), axis=0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Cadenced Opening Extension Reversal
programs.trading_idea: The factor treats an opening-gap repair as informative only when it occurs at the terminal point of an accelerating sequence of unusually high price impact events, rather than as an isolated daily reversal. Repeated same-signed impact events with shortening inter-event times proxy for increasingly urgent execution or thinning available liquidity; an opening extension in that direction that is then repaired on abnormal participation indicates that the remaining scheduled pressure was absorbed rather than discovered as durable information. The interaction has edge because gap repair alone confounds ordinary auction noise with exhaustion, while impact cadence alone cannot distinguish unresolved informed flow from a final failed extension.
programs.description: Measures accelerating same-signed high-impact event cadence, then scores an opening gap in that direction which is substantially repaired by the close on elevated participation. Positive values represent repaired downside extensions after sell-pressure cadence; negative values represent repaired upside extensions after buy-pressure cadence.

"""This is a falsifiable daily-bar proxy for failed directional price probes, not a direct measurement of limit-order replenishment. A downside move accompanied by repeated lower-range rejection, elevated relative turnover, and only a volatility-normalized modest cumulative decline may indicate that selling pressure failed to achieve durable price displacement; the symmetric upside pattern may indicate failed buying pressure. The predicted six-day effect is reversal, but the hypothesis should fail when the apparent rejection reflects persistent informed trading, earnings/news repricing, stop cascades, or a regime of sustained directional flow."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _wick_persistence_score(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute the causal failed-probe score using completed-bar OHLCV only."""
    bar_range = high - low
    valid_range = bar_range > 0.0
    safe_range = bar_range.where(valid_range, np.nan)

    lower_wick = ((pd.DataFrame(np.minimum(open_.to_numpy(), close.to_numpy()), index=close.index, columns=close.columns) - low) / safe_range)
    upper_wick = ((high - pd.DataFrame(np.maximum(open_.to_numpy(), close.to_numpy()), index=close.index, columns=close.columns)) / safe_range)
    close_location = (2.0 * close - high - low) / safe_range

    lower_wick = lower_wick.where(valid_range, 0.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    upper_wick = upper_wick.where(valid_range, 0.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    close_location = close_location.where(valid_range, 0.0).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)

    prior_volume_baseline = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    valid_volume = prior_volume_baseline.notna() & (prior_volume_baseline > 0.0) & volume.notna()
    volume_excess = (volume / prior_volume_baseline - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
    volume_excess = volume_excess.where(valid_volume, 0.0)

    lower_contribution = volume_excess * lower_wick * (1.0 + close_location) / 2.0
    upper_contribution = volume_excess * upper_wick * (1.0 - close_location) / 2.0

    valid_bar = valid_range & valid_volume & open_.notna() & high.notna() & low.notna() & close.notna()
    lower_persistence = lower_contribution.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
    upper_persistence = upper_contribution.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
    valid_persistence = valid_bar.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum() == 3

    close_return = close / close.shift(1) - 1.0
    mean_abs_return = close_return.abs().rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    displacement = (close / close.shift(3) - 1.0) / mean_abs_return.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    valid_displacement = mean_abs_return.notna() & (mean_abs_return > 0.0) & close.shift(3).notna()

    downside_probe = (-displacement).clip(lower=0.0) * np.exp(-(-displacement).clip(lower=0.0))
    upside_probe = displacement.clip(lower=0.0) * np.exp(-displacement.clip(lower=0.0))
    score = lower_persistence * downside_probe - upper_persistence * upside_probe

    valid_score = valid_persistence & valid_displacement
    return score.where(valid_score, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class LiquidityReplenishmentWickPersistence(BaseFactor):
    """Failed directional probes with persistent high-turnover wick rejection."""

    factor_id = "liquidity_replenishment_wick_persistence"
    name = "Directional Probe Failure"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Causal daily-bar proxy for failed directional probes: persistent "
        "relative-volume lower-wick rejection after modest downside displacement "
        "is positive, with an symmetric negative signal for failed upside probes."
    )
    window_length = 23
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        return _wick_persistence_score(
            data["open"],
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            close,
            data["volume"],
        )
programs.name: Directional Probe Failure
programs.trading_idea: This is a falsifiable daily-bar proxy for failed directional price probes, not a direct measurement of limit-order replenishment. A downside move accompanied by repeated lower-range rejection, elevated relative turnover, and only a volatility-normalized modest cumulative decline may indicate that selling pressure failed to achieve durable price displacement; the symmetric upside pattern may indicate failed buying pressure. The predicted six-day effect is reversal, but the hypothesis should fail when the apparent rejection reflects persistent informed trading, earnings/news repricing, stop cascades, or a regime of sustained directional flow.
programs.description: At the close of completed daily bar t, define range R_t = high_t - low_t. If R_t <= 0, set that bar's wick components to zero. Otherwise define lowerWick_t = (min(open_t, close_t) - low_t) / R_t, upperWick_t = (high_t - max(open_t, close_t)) / R_t, and closeLocation_t = (2*close_t - high_t - low_t) / R_t. Thus closeLocation is +1 at the high and -1 at the low. Define the abnormal-volume baseline as mean(volume_{t-20}, ..., volume_{t-1}); require all 20 prior volume observations to be present and the baseline to be positive. Let volumeExcess_t = min(max(volume_t / baseline_t - 1, 0), 2). Define downside-rejection contribution L_t = volumeExcess_t * lowerWick_t * (1 + closeLocation_t) / 2 and upside-rejection contribution U_t = volumeExcess_t * upperWick_t * (1 - closeLocation_t) / 2. Require three valid completed bars and form persistence measures P_L,t = mean(L_{t-2}, L_{t-1}, L_t) and P_U,t = mean(U_{t-2}, U_{t-1}, U_t). Define daily close return r_i = close_i / close_{i-1} - 1 and require 20 valid returns through t. Define normalized three-day displacement D_t = (close_t / close_{t-3} - 1) / mean(|r_{t-19}|, ..., |r_t|). If the denominator is zero or unavailable, set the signal to zero. With g(x) = max(x, 0) * exp(-x), the signed raw score is S_t = P_L,t * g(-D_t) - P_U,t * g(D_t). This gives positive scores only to persistent, elevated-volume lower-wick rejection after a modest downside probe, and negative scores only to the symmetric upside-probe failure; very large normalized moves are down-weighted by exp(-abs(D_t)). Missing required history produces a zero/untradable score rather than an imputed signal. Compute S_t only after bar t is fully complete; enter at the next tradable session's open (t+1) and evaluate the long-high-score/short-low-score portfolio from that next-session execution through the close six daily bars later.

"""Phase-confirmed opening-repair execution backlog.

Mechanism: an apparent intraday repair of an opening gap can be temporary when
recent abnormal participation led price in the original overnight-gap direction.
The lagged volume-to-price state acts as a proxy for unfinished scheduled flow,
while balance-sheet resilience separates transient liquidity repairs from a
plausible fundamental distress interpretation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _resilience_score(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Available-component cross-sectional balance-sheet resilience score."""
    cash_ratio = data["cashRatio"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    debt_assets = data["debtToAssets"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    market_cap = data["marketCap"].replace([0.0, np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    coverage = data["interestCoverage"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    components = [
        cash_ratio.rank(axis=1, pct=True),
        (-debt_assets).rank(axis=1, pct=True),
        (operating_cash_flow / market_cap).rank(axis=1, pct=True),
        coverage.rank(axis=1, pct=True),
    ]
    available = sum(component.notna().astype(float) for component in components)
    total = sum(component.fillna(0.0) for component in components)
    return (total / available.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(available >= 2.0)


def _volume_leads_gap_direction(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    gap_sign: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal evidence that abnormal volume led displacement in gap direction."""
    bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    displacement = ((close - open_) / bar_range).clip(-2.0, 2.0)

    valid_volume = volume.where(volume.ge(0.0))
    log_volume = np.log1p(valid_volume)
    baseline = log_volume.rolling(15, min_periods=15).mean().shift(1)
    scale = log_volume.rolling(15, min_periods=15).std(ddof=0).shift(1)
    volume_surprise = ((log_volume - baseline) / scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

    lead_alignment = (volume_surprise.shift(1) * displacement).rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
    return lead_alignment * gap_sign


@register_factor
class PhaseConfirmedOpeningRepairBacklog(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "phase_confirmed_opening_repair_backlog"
    name = "Phase-Confirmed Opening Repair Backlog"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks solvency-conditioned opening-gap repairs, activated only when a "
        "causal lagged abnormal-volume/price sequence supports the original gap "
        "direction and therefore indicates an unfinished execution backlog."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "cashRatio",
        "debtToAssets",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "marketCap",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        safe_open = open_.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        gap = open_ / previous_close - 1.0
        intraday_return = close / safe_open - 1.0
        repair = (-intraday_return / gap.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        abnormal_volume = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        volume_rank = abnormal_volume.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        resilience = _resilience_score(data)
        gap_sign = np.sign(gap)
        phase_support = _volume_leads_gap_direction(
            open_, high, low, close, volume, gap_sign
        )
        phase_gate = phase_support.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        downside_weight = resilience
        upside_weight = 1.0 - resilience
        signed_repair = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(gap.lt(0.0), downside_weight, -upside_weight),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        ).where(gap.ne(0.0))

        raw = gap.abs() * repair * volume_rank * signed_repair * phase_gate
        valid = (
            gap.notna()
            & repair.notna()
            & volume_rank.notna()
            & resilience.notna()
            & phase_gate.notna()
            & raw.notna()
        )
        percentile = raw.where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return (2.0 * percentile - 1.0).where(valid)

Balance-sheet resilience distinguishes a solvent-name downside repair from immediate distress, while fragility identifies upside repairs more likely to reflect short-covering or thin liquidity; the phase condition then asks whether recent participation still validates the original overnight direction. This interaction carries edge neither parent has alone because a repaired gap without prior execution-state confirmation is ambiguous, while a volume-price phase pattern without an observable auction-style rejection has no clear near-term resolution point.

programs.code:
"""Phase-matured opening-auction repair conditioned on financial resilience.

A repaired opening gap becomes informative when a completed price-volume phase
loop indicates that the preceding activity was an active inventory-transfer
state rather than ordinary noise.  The loop's magnitude is used as confidence,
while repair direction is resolved by auction rejection and balance-sheet
resilience.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _phase_maturity(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal magnitude of a completed volume/displacement phase loop."""
    valid = (
        open_.notna()
        & high.notna()
        & low.notna()
        & close.notna()
        & volume.notna()
        & volume.ge(0.0)
    )
    bar_range = high - low
    displacement = (close - open_) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    displacement = displacement.where(valid)
    displacement = displacement.where(~(valid & bar_range.eq(0.0)), 0.0).clip(-2.0, 2.0)

    log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(valid))
    baseline = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().shift(1)
    scale = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std(ddof=0).shift(1)
    surprise = (log_volume - baseline) / scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    surprise = surprise.where(valid).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

    complete = (
        (displacement.notna() & surprise.notna())
        .rolling(8, min_periods=8)
        .sum()
        .eq(8)
    )
    increment = displacement.shift(1) * surprise - surprise.shift(1) * displacement
    area = increment.rolling(7, min_periods=7).sum() / 28.0
    return area.abs().where(complete)


def _resilience(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Available-component cross-sectional solvency score."""
    cash_ratio = data["cashRatio"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    debt_assets = data["debtToAssets"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    market_cap = data["marketCap"].replace([0.0, np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    coverage = data["interestCoverage"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    components = [
        cash_ratio.rank(axis=1, pct=True),
        (-debt_assets).rank(axis=1, pct=True),
        (operating_cash_flow / market_cap).rank(axis=1, pct=True),
        coverage.rank(axis=1, pct=True),
    ]
    available = sum(x.notna().astype(float) for x in components)
    total = sum(x.fillna(0.0) for x in components)
    return (total / available.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(available >= 2.0)


@register_factor
class PhaseMaturedAuctionRepairResilience(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "phase_matured_auction_repair_resilience"
    name = "Phase-Matured Auction Repair"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Signed opening-gap repair, conditioned on balance-sheet resilience, "
        "current participation, and the maturity of a completed causal "
        "price-volume phase loop."
    )
    window_length = 28
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "cashRatio",
        "debtToAssets",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "marketCap",
        "interestCoverage",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        safe_open = open_.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        gap = open_ / previous_close - 1.0
        intraday_return = close / safe_open - 1.0
        repair = (-intraday_return / gap.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume.ge(0.0)))
        vol_mean = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().shift(1)
        vol_std = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std(ddof=0).shift(1)
        vol_surprise = ((log_volume - vol_mean) / vol_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        participation = vol_surprise.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        maturity = _phase_maturity(open_, high, low, close, volume)
        maturity_rank = maturity.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        resilience = _resilience(data)

        repair_direction = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(gap.lt(0.0), resilience, -(1.0 - resilience)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        ).where(gap.ne(0.0))

        raw = gap.abs() * repair * participation * maturity_rank * repair_direction
        valid = (
            gap.notna()
            & repair.notna()
            & participation.notna()
            & maturity_rank.notna()
            & resilience.notna()
            & raw.notna()
        )
        percentile = raw.where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return (2.0 * percentile - 1.0).where(valid)

programs.trading_idea: An opening gap repaired into the close is directionally ambiguous unless it occurs after a mature, abnormal volume-price loop: the loop identifies an actively absorbed execution state rather than ordinary intraday noise. Parent A's unstable directional orientation is therefore used as a state-confidence measure (loop magnitude), not as a standalone directional forecast; Parent B's repaired auction supplies the direction and near-term resolution point. Resilient names with repaired downside gaps are more likely to sustain the repair, while financially fragile names with repaired upside gaps are more likely to fail, and this distinction should matter most when a preceding participation loop confirms that inventory was genuinely transferred.
programs.description: Ranks the signed direction of an opening-gap repair, weighted by current abnormal participation and the magnitude of a completed causal price-volume oriented-area loop. The repair direction is conditioned on a cross-sectional balance-sheet resilience score so downside repairs are favored in resilient firms and upside repairs are faded in fragile firms.

"""Reported changes in shares outstanding are not identified tradable-float or offering events, but newly public share-count expansion versus contraction can still condition the interpretation of subsequent price-volume pressure. A positive disclosed share-count change paired with persistent weak price pressure is consistent with supply pressure, while a contraction paired with positive pressure is consistent with a favorable reduction in marginal equity supply; the opposite combinations indicate that observed pressure is offsetting the accounting-share signal. The claim is explicitly a conditional share-count-change and daily price/volume-pressure hypothesis, not evidence of underwriter distribution or dealer inventory."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_winsorize(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Clip each date's valid cross section at its 1st and 99th percentiles."""
    lower = frame.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = frame.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return frame.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _share_change_events(shares: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return disclosed share changes only when the available value changes.

    The input is ordinarily a point-in-time forward-filled step function.  The
    lagged forward fill also handles occasional missing intervals without using
    future observations.
    """
    previous_available = shares.ffill().shift(1)
    valid_pair = shares.gt(0.0) & previous_available.gt(0.0)
    changed = shares.ne(previous_available)

    event_change = shares / previous_available - 1.0
    return event_change.where(changed, 0.0).where(valid_pair)


def _pressure_score(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute the causal five-bar close-location signed-volume pressure."""
    price_range = high - low
    close_location = ((close - low) / price_range - 0.5).where(high.gt(low), 0.0)

    prior_volume_mean = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    relative_volume = volume / prior_volume_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    daily_pressure = (close_location * relative_volume).where(prior_volume_mean.gt(0.0))

    return daily_pressure.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()


@register_factor
class FloatShockResilienceInventorySort(BaseFactor):
    """Conditional share-count changes confirmed or offset by price-volume pressure."""

    factor_id = "float_shock_resilience_inventory_sort"
    name = "Share-Change Pressure Confirmation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional interaction of newly disclosed share-count changes and "
        "five-bar close-location signed-volume pressure; positive scores identify "
        "expansion with weak pressure or contraction with strong pressure."
    )
    window_length = 25
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sharesOutstanding"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        share_change = _share_change_events(data["sharesOutstanding"])
        winsorized_change = _cross_sectional_winsorize(share_change)
        change_rank = 2.0 * winsorized_change.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0

        pressure = _pressure_score(
            close,
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["volume"],
        )
        winsorized_pressure = _cross_sectional_winsorize(pressure)
        pressure_rank = 2.0 * winsorized_pressure.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0

        return (-change_rank * pressure_rank).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.trading_idea: Reported changes in shares outstanding are not identified tradable-float or offering events, but newly public share-count expansion versus contraction can still condition the interpretation of subsequent price-volume pressure. A positive disclosed share-count change paired with persistent weak price pressure is consistent with supply pressure, while a contraction paired with positive pressure is consistent with a favorable reduction in marginal equity supply; the opposite combinations indicate that observed pressure is offsetting the accounting-share signal. The claim is explicitly a conditional share-count-change and daily price/volume-pressure hypothesis, not evidence of underwriter distribution or dealer inventory.
programs.description: At each date t after the close, identify the latest sharesOutstanding observation S_t and its immediately preceding distinct non-null point-in-time observation S_prev for each ticker. Define disclosed share change g_t = (S_t / S_prev) - 1 only from the first bar on which S_t differs from the previously available value, and set g_t = 0 on all other bars; require S_t > 0 and S_prev > 0, otherwise leave missing. Winsorize g_t cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th percentiles, then compute G_t as its cross-sectional percentile rank transformed to [-1,1] by 2*rank(g_t)-1. Compute a fixed 5-bar pressure score using only bars through t: daily close-location CL_i = ((close_i-low_i)/(high_i-low_i))-0.5 when high_i>low_i, otherwise 0; daily signed-volume pressure P_i = CL_i * (volume_i / mean(volume_{i-20:i-1})), requiring a positive 20-bar prior-volume mean and otherwise missing. Let Pbar_t be the arithmetic mean of P_i over i=t-4 through t, requiring all five observations; winsorize Pbar_t cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th percentiles and convert it to [-1,1] using 2*cross-sectional-percentile-rank(Pbar_t)-1. The final score is -G_t * PbarRank_t: it is positive for share-count expansion with weak/negative pressure and for contraction with strong/positive pressure, and negative for expansion with strong pressure or contraction with weak pressure. The signal is formed after the close of t and may be executed no earlier than the next executable bar open; missing inputs produce a missing score.

programs.code:
"""This revision does not interpret reported weighted-average shares outstanding as contemporaneous inventory that dealers must absorb. Instead, it treats a newly public share-count revision as an information event only when it is directionally corroborated by a newly public net-stock-issuance cash-flow figure, identifying a disclosed external-equity-flow state rather than option dilution, splits, or an accounting-only share-count revision. The expected six-bar effect is positive for verified repurchase states and negative for verified issuance states, after removing contemporaneous exposure to return-volume pressure, turnover, and range-per-volume liquidity measures."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _previous_share_event_distance(change: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return bars since the prior observed share-count change, causally."""
    positions = np.broadcast_to(
        np.arange(len(change.index), dtype=float)[:, None], change.shape
    )
    position_frame = pd.DataFrame(positions, index=change.index, columns=change.columns)
    previous_event = position_frame.where(change).ffill().shift(1)
    return position_frame - previous_event


def _standardized_cross_sectional_residual(
    score: pd.DataFrame,
    pressure: pd.DataFrame,
    turnover: pd.DataFrame,
    impact: pd.DataFrame,
    log_market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Residualize each event cross-section against liquidity controls and industries."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=score.index, columns=score.columns)

    for row in range(len(score.index)):
        mask = eligible.iloc[row].fillna(False).to_numpy(dtype=bool)
        if int(mask.sum()) < 20:
            continue

        y = score.iloc[row, mask].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        p = pressure.iloc[row, mask].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        a = turnover.iloc[row, mask].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        imp = impact.iloc[row, mask].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        size = log_market_cap.iloc[row, mask].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        labels = industry.iloc[row, mask].astype(str).to_numpy()

        finite = (
            np.isfinite(y)
            & np.isfinite(p)
            & np.isfinite(a)
            & np.isfinite(imp)
            & np.isfinite(size)
        )
        if int(finite.sum()) < 20:
            continue

        y = y[finite]
        p = p[finite]
        a = a[finite]
        imp = imp[finite]
        size = size[finite]
        labels = labels[finite]

        categories = np.unique(labels)
        columns = [np.ones(len(y)), p, a, imp, size]
        for category in categories[1:]:
            columns.append((labels == category).astype(float))
        design = np.column_stack(columns)

        try:
            coefficients = np.linalg.lstsq(design, y, rcond=None)[0]
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            continue

        residual = y - design @ coefficients
        residual_std = float(np.std(residual))
        if not np.isfinite(residual_std) or residual_std <= 1e-12:
            continue

        original_columns = np.flatnonzero(mask)
        valid_columns = original_columns[finite]
        output.iloc[row, valid_columns] = residual / residual_std

    return output


@register_factor
class SharecountEventElasticityRecoveryGate(BaseFactor):
    """Cash-flow-verified share-count disclosure residual."""

    factor_id = "sharecount_event_elasticity_recovery_gate"
    name = "Verified Equity-Flow Disclosure Residual"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Standardized residual of directionally cash-flow-verified share-count "
        "disclosure events after contemporaneous turnover, pressure, impact, "
        "size, and industry controls."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = [
        "sharesOutstanding",
        "netStockIssuance",
        "marketCap",
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        shares = data["sharesOutstanding"]
        issuance = data["netStockIssuance"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        previous_shares = shares.shift(1)
        valid_share_pair = (
            np.isfinite(shares)
            & np.isfinite(previous_shares)
            & shares.gt(0.0)
            & previous_shares.gt(0.0)
        )
        share_change = valid_share_pair & shares.ne(previous_shares)
        share_ratio = (shares / previous_shares).where(valid_share_pair)
        q = np.log(share_ratio)
        prior_event_distance = _previous_share_event_distance(share_change)

        previous_issuance = issuance.shift(1)
        issuance_ratio = issuance / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        valid_issuance_event = (
            np.isfinite(issuance)
            & np.isfinite(previous_issuance)
            & issuance.ne(previous_issuance)
            & np.isfinite(market_cap)
            & market_cap.gt(0.0)
            & np.isfinite(issuance_ratio)
            & issuance_ratio.abs().ge(0.002)
        )

        share_event = (
            share_change
            & q.abs().ge(0.005)
            & q.abs().le(np.log(1.5))
            & prior_event_distance.ge(45.0)
            & prior_event_distance.le(180.0)
            & valid_issuance_event
            & np.sign(q).eq(np.sign(issuance_ratio))
        )
        raw_score = (-np.sign(q) * q.abs().clip(upper=0.10)).where(share_event)

        trailing_volume = (
            volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))
            .shift(1)
            .rolling(20, min_periods=15)
            .median()
        )
        valid_volume_count = (
            volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))
            .shift(1)
            .notna()
            .rolling(20, min_periods=15)
            .sum()
        )
        abnormal_turnover = volume / trailing_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        open_price = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        valid_prices = close.gt(0.0) & open_price.gt(0.0)
        intrabar_return = np.log((close / open_price).where(valid_prices))
        pressure = np.sign(intrabar_return) * np.log1p(abnormal_turnover)

        range_value = ((high - low) / close.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(close.gt(0.0))
        trailing_range = range_value.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        impact = range_value / (abnormal_turnover + 0.01)
        log_market_cap = np.log(market_cap.where(market_cap.gt(0.0)))

        tradable = (
            valid_volume_count.ge(15.0)
            & abnormal_turnover.ge(0.5)
            & abnormal_turnover.le(3.0)
            & range_value.le(3.0 * trailing_range)
        )
        usable_controls = (
            np.isfinite(pressure)
            & np.isfinite(abnormal_turnover)
            & np.isfinite(impact)
            & np.isfinite(log_market_cap)
            & industry.notna()
        )
        eligible = share_event & tradable & usable_controls & raw_score.notna()

        masked_pressure = pressure.where(eligible)
        lower_pressure = masked_pressure.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
        upper_pressure = masked_pressure.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
        winsorized_pressure = pressure.clip(
            lower=lower_pressure, upper=upper_pressure, axis=0
        )

        return _standardized_cross_sectional_residual(
            raw_score,
            winsorized_pressure,
            abnormal_turnover,
            impact,
            log_market_cap,
            industry,
            eligible,
        )
