"""The revised mechanism is not that raw EPS-to-revenue surprise elasticity is itself a durable operating-leverage estimate. Instead, it isolates the residual between delivered EPS news and the EPS implication of pre-release consensus co-revisions, then trades it only when contemporaneous operating-margin, cash-conversion, and working-capital evidence support the residual's sign. The expected continuation arises when analysts must revise profitability and cash-realization assumptions after a report, while the completed report-day return indicates that the directional implication was not already fully absorbed."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _finite_mask(*frames: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the aligned mask on which every supplied numeric frame is finite."""
    mask = pd.DataFrame(True, index=frames[0].index, columns=frames[0].columns)
    for frame in frames:
        mask = mask & frame.notna() & np.isfinite(frame)
    return mask


def _carry_post_close_events(event_score: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Carry a report-day score from the next bar through the sixth bar."""
    carried = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=event_score.index, columns=event_score.columns)
    for lag in range(1, 7):
        decay = 1.0 - (lag - 1) / 6.0
        carried = carried + event_score.shift(lag).fillna(0.0) * decay
    return carried


@register_factor
class DeliveredElasticityCalibrationResponseGap(BaseFactor):
    """Post-close residual earnings-news drift confirmed by cash and margins."""

    factor_id = "delivered_elasticity_calibration_response_gap"
    name = "Cash-Confirmed Delivery Residual Drift"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks post-close EPS delivery residuals versus pre-report consensus "
        "elasticity only when margin, cash-conversion, and working-capital "
        "evidence confirm the residual and report-day absorption is incomplete."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingMargin",
        "incomeQuality",
        "workingCapital",
        "revenue",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        operating_margin = data["operatingMargin"]
        income_quality = data["incomeQuality"]
        working_capital = data["workingCapital"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]

        eps_est_t1 = eps_estimate.shift(1)
        eps_est_t21 = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        revenue_est_t1 = revenue_estimate.shift(1)
        revenue_est_t21 = revenue_estimate.shift(21)

        eps_revision = (eps_est_t1 - eps_est_t21) / eps_est_t21.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        revenue_revision = (revenue_est_t1 - revenue_est_t21) / revenue_est_t21.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        beta = (eps_revision / revenue_revision.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        standardized_eps = (eps_surprise / eps_est_t1.abs().clip(lower=0.01)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        standardized_revenue = (
            revenue_surprise / revenue_est_t1.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        ).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        delivery_residual = (standardized_eps - beta * standardized_revenue).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        operating_margin_lag = operating_margin.shift(63)
        income_quality_lag = income_quality.shift(63)
        working_capital_lag = working_capital.shift(63)
        revenue_lag = revenue.shift(63)

        delta_margin = operating_margin - operating_margin_lag
        delta_income_quality = income_quality - income_quality_lag
        normalized_wc = working_capital / revenue.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        normalized_wc_lag = working_capital_lag / revenue_lag.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        delta_working_capital = normalized_wc - normalized_wc_lag

        confirmation = (
            (delta_margin / 0.02).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
            + 0.5 * delta_income_quality.clip(-1.0, 1.0)
            - 0.5 * (delta_working_capital / 0.05).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        )

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        report_return = close / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        absorption = 1.0 - (
            (np.sign(delivery_residual) * report_return)
            .clip(lower=0.0)
            .clip(upper=0.10)
            / 0.10
        )

        eps_changed = eps_actual.notna() & (
            eps_actual.shift(1).isna() | eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1))
        )
        revenue_changed = revenue_actual.notna() & (
            revenue_actual.shift(1).isna() | revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1))
        )
        fresh_report = eps_changed | revenue_changed

        revision_valid = _finite_mask(
            eps_est_t1,
            eps_est_t21,
            revenue_est_t1,
            revenue_est_t21,
            eps_revision,
            revenue_revision,
            beta,
        ) & revenue_revision.abs().ge(0.01)
        surprise_valid = _finite_mask(
            eps_surprise,
            revenue_surprise,
            standardized_eps,
            standardized_revenue,
            delivery_residual,
        ) & standardized_revenue.abs().ge(0.01)
        confirmation_valid = _finite_mask(
            operating_margin,
            operating_margin_lag,
            income_quality,
            income_quality_lag,
            working_capital,
            working_capital_lag,
            revenue,
            revenue_lag,
            delta_margin,
            delta_income_quality,
            delta_working_capital,
            confirmation,
        )
        absorption_valid = _finite_mask(close, prior_close, report_return, absorption)
        report_fields_valid = _finite_mask(
            eps_actual,
            revenue_actual,
            eps_surprise,
            revenue_surprise,
        )

        eligible = (
            fresh_report
            & report_fields_valid
            & revision_valid
            & surprise_valid
            & confirmation_valid
            & absorption_valid
            & confirmation.abs().ge(0.25)
            & np.sign(delivery_residual).eq(np.sign(confirmation))
            & np.sign(delivery_residual).eq(np.sign(delta_margin))
        )

        event_score = (
            delivery_residual * confirmation.abs() * absorption
        ).where(eligible, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        carried_score = _carry_post_close_events(event_score)

        ranked = rank(carried_score)
        return ranked.where(carried_score.ne(0.0), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Cash-Confirmed Delivery Residual Drift
programs.trading_idea: The revised mechanism is not that raw EPS-to-revenue surprise elasticity is itself a durable operating-leverage estimate. Instead, it isolates the residual between delivered EPS news and the EPS implication of pre-release consensus co-revisions, then trades it only when contemporaneous operating-margin, cash-conversion, and working-capital evidence support the residual's sign. The expected continuation arises when analysts must revise profitability and cash-realization assumptions after a report, while the completed report-day return indicates that the directional implication was not already fully absorbed.
programs.description: Let t be a fresh report date: epsActual[t] and revenueActual[t] must be non-null, epsSurprise[t] and revenueSurprise[t] must be non-null, and at least one of epsActual[t] or revenueActual[t] must differ from its value at t-1. All report-date quantities are used only after close[t] is known. Pre-report consensus revisions use only the 20-bar window ending at t-1: rE = (epsEstimate[t-1]-epsEstimate[t-21]) / max(abs(epsEstimate[t-21]), 0.01), and rR = (revenueEstimate[t-1]-revenueEstimate[t-21]) / max(abs(revenueEstimate[t-21]), 1000000). The pre-report calibration coefficient is beta = winsorize(rE / rR, -5, 5), but the event is discarded unless abs(rR) >= 0.01. Delivered standardized surprises are sE = winsorize(epsSurprise[t] / max(abs(epsEstimate[t-1]), 0.01), -3, 3) and sR = winsorize(revenueSurprise[t] / max(abs(revenueEstimate[t-1]), 1000000), -3, 3); discard the event unless abs(sR) >= 0.01. The economically scaled delivery residual is D = winsorize(sE - beta*sR, -3, 3), rather than an unbounded ratio of EPS and revenue surprises. Cash-and-operations confirmation is measured over the prior approximately quarterly 63-bar lookback: dOM = operatingMargin[t]-operatingMargin[t-63], dIQ = incomeQuality[t]-incomeQuality[t-63], and dWC = workingCapital[t]/max(abs(revenue[t]), 1000000) - workingCapital[t-63]/max(abs(revenue[t-63]), 1000000). Define Q = clip(dOM/0.02, -1, 1) + 0.5*clip(dIQ, -1, 1) - 0.5*clip(dWC/0.05, -1, 1). Retain an event only when sign(D)=sign(Q), abs(Q)>=0.25, and sign(D)=sign(dOM); otherwise assign zero. This requires positive residuals to coincide with improving operating margin, improving cash conversion, and/or reduced working-capital cash consumption, while negative residuals require deterioration on those dimensions. Any missing input to the event, revision, confirmation, or absorption calculation produces no trade. Report-day absorption is based on the completed close-to-close return R0 = close[t]/close[t-1]-1: A = 1 - clip(max(0, sign(D)*R0)/0.10, 0, 1). The post-close event score is S_t = D*abs(Q)*A. It is first executable at the next bar, t+1, never on report date t. At each bar u from t+1 through t+6, carry S_t with linear decay S_t*(1-(u-t-1)/6); exit after the sixth executable bar. If multiple eligible report events remain active, sum their decayed scores before cross-sectionally ranking the resulting signal.

programs.code:
"""A large sector-wide move can initially transmit through baskets and correlated risk repricing before investors fully differentiate firms by their capacity to absorb the implied operating or financing stress. Conditional on an objectively large sector move, resilient firms whose five-day return has lagged their sector should outperform weaker or relative-overresponding peers after a positive shock; after a negative shock, resilient firms with relatively smaller declines should outperform fragile firms with disproportionately large declines. The hypothesis is specifically incremental: the interaction must predict six-day returns after controlling for both sector-relative reversal and the standalone resilience composite."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_winsorize(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Clip each date's cross-section at its trailing-date 1st/99th percentiles."""
    clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lower = clean.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = clean.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return clean.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _sector_shock_scores(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    gross_margin: pd.DataFrame,
    sga_to_revenue: pd.DataFrame,
    current_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_to_equity: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Implement contemporaneous sector shock sorting using only date-t data."""
    safe_close = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    five_day_return = safe_close / safe_close.shift(5) - 1.0
    five_day_return = five_day_return.where((safe_close > 0.0) & (safe_close.shift(5) > 0.0))

    gross_margin = _cross_sectional_winsorize(gross_margin)
    sga_to_revenue = _cross_sectional_winsorize(sga_to_revenue)
    current_ratio = _cross_sectional_winsorize(current_ratio)
    debt_to_equity = _cross_sectional_winsorize(debt_to_equity)

    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns, dtype=float)

    for row_number in range(len(close.index)):
        labels = sector.iloc[row_number]
        stock_return = five_day_return.iloc[row_number]
        gm = gross_margin.iloc[row_number]
        sga = sga_to_revenue.iloc[row_number]
        liquidity = current_ratio.iloc[row_number]
        leverage = debt_to_equity.iloc[row_number]

        valid_return = stock_return.notna() & labels.notna()
        resilience_eligible = (
            labels.notna()
            & gm.notna()
            & sga.notna()
            & liquidity.notna()
            & leverage.notna()
        )

        score = pd.Series(np.nan, index=close.columns, dtype=float)
        score.loc[valid_return & resilience_eligible] = 0.0

        if not valid_return.any():
            output.iloc[row_number] = score
            continue

        sector_observations = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "sector": labels.loc[valid_return],
                "stock_return": stock_return.loc[valid_return],
            }
        )
        sector_summary = sector_observations.groupby("sector", sort=False)["stock_return"].agg(
            ["mean", "count"]
        )
        eligible_sector_return = sector_summary.loc[
            sector_summary["count"] >= 5, "mean"
        ]

        if eligible_sector_return.empty:
            output.iloc[row_number] = score
            continue

        sector_abs_rank = eligible_sector_return.abs().rank(pct=True)
        shocked_sector_return = eligible_sector_return.loc[sector_abs_rank >= (2.0 / 3.0)]

        if shocked_sector_return.empty:
            output.iloc[row_number] = score
            continue

        sector_return_by_stock = labels.map(eligible_sector_return)
        abnormal_response = stock_return - sector_return_by_stock
        abnormal_rank = abnormal_response.groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True) - 0.5

        ranked_gm = gm.where(resilience_eligible).groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True) - 0.5
        ranked_sga = -(sga.where(resilience_eligible))
        ranked_sga = ranked_sga.groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True) - 0.5
        ranked_liquidity = (
            liquidity.where(resilience_eligible).groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True) - 0.5
        )
        ranked_leverage = -(leverage.where(resilience_eligible))
        ranked_leverage = ranked_leverage.groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True) - 0.5

        resilience = (ranked_gm + ranked_sga + ranked_liquidity + ranked_leverage) / 4.0
        shock_direction = labels.map(np.sign(shocked_sector_return))
        shocked_stock = labels.isin(shocked_sector_return.index)
        active = shocked_stock & resilience_eligible & abnormal_rank.notna()

        score.loc[active] = resilience.loc[active] - (
            shock_direction.loc[active] * abnormal_rank.loc[active]
        )
        output.iloc[row_number] = score

    return output


@register_factor
class SectorShockCostAbsorptionSort(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks resilient firms by their relative response to large sector shocks."""

    factor_id = "sector_shock_cost_absorption_sort"
    name = "Sector Shock Resilience Response"
    category = "other"
    description = (
        "Within objectively shocked sectors, favors high-resilience firms that "
        "lag positive sector shocks or avoid disproportionate declines in negative shocks."
    )
    window_length = 5
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "grossMargin",
        "sgaToRevenue",
        "currentRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return _sector_shock_scores(
            data["close"],
            data["sector"],
            data["grossMargin"],
            data["sgaToRevenue"],
            data["currentRatio"],
            data["debtToEquity"],
        )
programs.name: Sector Shock Resilience Response
programs.trading_idea: A large sector-wide move can initially transmit through baskets and correlated risk repricing before investors fully differentiate firms by their capacity to absorb the implied operating or financing stress. Conditional on an objectively large sector move, resilient firms whose five-day return has lagged their sector should outperform weaker or relative-overresponding peers after a positive shock; after a negative shock, resilient firms with relatively smaller declines should outperform fragile firms with disproportionately large declines. The hypothesis is specifically incremental: the interaction must predict six-day returns after controlling for both sector-relative reversal and the standalone resilience composite.
programs.description: At each rebalance date t, form five-day simple returns r_i = close_t / close_{t-5} - 1 for stocks with valid positive closes at t and t-5. For each sector with at least five eligible stocks, compute the equal-weighted sector return R_s as the mean of r_i. Rank absolute sector returns across eligible sectors using percentile ranks and define a sector as shocked when its absolute-return percentile rank is at least 2/3; define shock direction S_s = sign(R_s). Stocks in unshocked sectors receive no signal. For each stock in a shocked sector, calculate abnormal response A_i = r_i - R_s, then convert A_i to a within-sector percentile rank and center it to a [-0.5, 0.5] scale. Construct a point-in-time resilience score Q_i from grossMargin, sgaToRevenue, currentRatio, and debtToEquity. Winsorize each component cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th percentiles on date t; within each sector convert grossMargin and currentRatio to ascending percentile ranks, and sgaToRevenue and debtToEquity to descending percentile ranks, then center each rank to [-0.5, 0.5]. Q_i is the equal-weighted average of the four centered component ranks. A stock is eligible only if all four resilience fields are available at t; missing values produce NaN rather than an imputed signal. The signed factor is Score_i = Q_i - S_s * A_i. Thus, after a positive shock, the score is highest for resilient sector laggards and lowest for fragile relative overresponders; after a negative shock, it is highest for resilient stocks with relatively small declines and lowest for fragile stocks with disproportionately negative abnormal responses. Test a sector-neutral implementation that, within each shocked sector, buys the highest-score quintile and shorts the lowest-score quintile with equal gross sector weights.

programs.code:
"""The signal tests a narrowly defined conditional mean-reversion mechanism: following an observable decline from an unusually high level of within-sector return commonality, firms with stronger pre-existing fundamental characteristics but recent sector-relative underperformance may recover relative to weaker firms with sector-relative outperformance. The correlation-state transition, rather than a generic sector return shock, is a necessary condition for trading. The hypothesis does not assume that every correlation decline is caused by passive-flow unwinding; it is a reduced-form test of whether temporary common-price formation is followed by six-day re-differentiation conditional on point-in-time fundamentals."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_correlation_state(
    close: pd.DataFrame, columns: pd.Index
) -> pd.Series:
    """Compute causal 20-return mean pairwise correlation for one sector.

    A constituent enters a date's correlation universe only when all 21 closes
    needed for the 20 close-to-close returns are present.  The loop is over
    dates, while each correlation is a vectorized matrix calculation over the
    eligible constituent panel.
    """
    sector_close = close.loc[:, columns]
    index = sector_close.index
    correlation = pd.Series(np.nan, index=index, dtype=float)

    complete_close = (
        sector_close.notna()
        .rolling(21, min_periods=21)
        .sum()
        .eq(21)
    )
    sector_return = (
        sector_close / sector_close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    )

    for position in range(20, len(index)):
        members = complete_close.iloc[position].to_numpy(dtype=bool)
        if int(members.sum()) < 8:
            continue

        return_window = sector_return.iloc[position - 19 : position + 1, :]
        values = return_window.iloc[:, members].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        finite_members = np.isfinite(values).all(axis=0)
        values = values[:, finite_members]
        if values.shape[1] < 8:
            continue

        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
            matrix = np.corrcoef(values, rowvar=False)
        pair_values = matrix[np.triu_indices(matrix.shape[0], k=1)]
        pair_values = pair_values[np.isfinite(pair_values)]
        if pair_values.size:
            correlation.iloc[position] = float(pair_values.mean())

    return correlation


def _release_state(close: pd.DataFrame, columns: pd.Index) -> pd.Series:
    """Identify a high-correlation to lower-correlation transition causally."""
    current = _sector_correlation_state(close, columns)
    previous = current.shift(1)
    historical_high = previous.rolling(126, min_periods=63).quantile(0.75)
    threshold = historical_high.clip(lower=0.35)

    return (
        historical_high.notna()
        & previous.notna()
        & current.notna()
        & (previous >= threshold)
        & (current <= previous - 0.10)
    )


def _clean_fundamental(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Keep only finite contemporaneously available fundamental observations."""
    return frame.astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class CorrelationReleaseFundamentalDispersionRepri(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-neutral fundamental re-differentiation after correlation release."""

    factor_id = "correlation_release_fundamental_dispersion_repri"
    name = "Causal Correlation-Release Repricing"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Equal-capital aggregate of six causal sector-neutral vintages that "
        "buy fundamentally strong five-day sector laggards and short weak "
        "sector leaders only after a high within-sector correlation releases."
    )
    window_length = 147
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
        "roic",
        "incomeQuality",
        "debtToAssets",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        index = close.index
        columns = close.columns

        # Sector is static in this feed.  Taking its first row avoids using a
        # future financial observation while preserving the supplied mapping.
        sector_labels = data["sector"].iloc[0].reindex(columns)
        valid_sector_labels = sector_labels.dropna()
        sector_names = pd.unique(valid_sector_labels)

        fcf_yield = _clean_fundamental(data["freeCashFlowYield"])
        roic = _clean_fundamental(data["roic"])
        income_quality = _clean_fundamental(data["incomeQuality"])
        debt_to_assets = _clean_fundamental(data["debtToAssets"])

        five_day_return = close / close.shift(5).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        vintage = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)

        for sector_name in sector_names:
            sector_columns = sector_labels.index[sector_labels == sector_name]
            if len(sector_columns) == 0:
                continue

            released = _release_state(close, sector_columns)

            # Each directional percentile is calculated only against the
            # contemporaneously non-missing fundamental observations in sector.
            sector_fcf = fcf_yield.loc[:, sector_columns].rank(axis=1, pct=True)
            sector_roic = roic.loc[:, sector_columns].rank(axis=1, pct=True)
            sector_iq = income_quality.loc[:, sector_columns].rank(axis=1, pct=True)
            sector_debt = (-debt_to_assets.loc[:, sector_columns]).rank(
                axis=1, pct=True
            )
            fundamental_ranks = pd.concat(
                [sector_fcf, sector_roic, sector_iq, sector_debt],
                keys=["fcf", "roic", "iq", "debt"],
                axis=1,
            )

            # Reconstruct the four-field mean without any imputation.
            rank_sum = sector_fcf + sector_roic + sector_iq + sector_debt
            rank_count = (
                sector_fcf.notna().astype(int)
                + sector_roic.notna().astype(int)
                + sector_iq.notna().astype(int)
                + sector_debt.notna().astype(int)
            )
            anchor = (rank_sum / rank_count.replace(0, np.nan)).where(
                rank_count >= 3
            )

            sector_five_day = five_day_return.loc[:, sector_columns]
            sector_mean_return = sector_five_day.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
            relative_return = sector_five_day.sub(sector_mean_return, axis=0)
            eligible = anchor.notna() & relative_return.notna()
            relative_rank = relative_return.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
            score = (anchor - relative_rank).where(eligible)

            sector_vintage = pd.DataFrame(
                0.0, index=index, columns=sector_columns, dtype=float
            )
            release_positions = np.flatnonzero(released.to_numpy(dtype=bool))

            for position in release_positions:
                row_score = score.iloc[position].dropna()
                member_count = len(row_score)
                if member_count < 10:
                    continue

                side_count = max(2, int(np.floor(0.20 * member_count)))
                long_order = row_score.rank(method="first", ascending=False)
                short_order = row_score.rank(method="first", ascending=True)
                long_members = long_order.index[long_order <= side_count]
                short_members = short_order.index[short_order <= side_count]

                # Sector allocations are finalized after all active sectors are
                # known at this date, so store unit long/short side weights now.
                sector_vintage.loc[index[position], long_members] = 1.0 / side_count
                sector_vintage.loc[index[position], short_members] = -1.0 / side_count

            # A nonzero row denotes a tradable released sector.  Dividing each
            # such row by the number of active sectors gives +/-0.5/S gross-side
            # allocation after the global half-gross multiplier below.
            active = sector_vintage.abs().sum(axis=1).gt(0.0)
            if active.any():
                vintage.loc[:, sector_columns] = sector_vintage

        active_sector_count = pd.Series(0, index=index, dtype=float)
        for sector_name in sector_names:
            sector_columns = sector_labels.index[sector_labels == sector_name]
            if len(sector_columns):
                active_sector_count += vintage.loc[:, sector_columns].abs().sum(axis=1).gt(0.0)

        vintage = vintage.div(active_sector_count.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
        vintage = (0.5 * vintage).fillna(0.0)

        # Signals at t through t-5 are the six simultaneously live vintages at
        # the next open; normalize by the number actually available in startup.
        live = vintage.rolling(6, min_periods=1).mean()
        return live.reindex(index=index, columns=columns).fillna(0.0).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: The signal tests a narrowly defined conditional mean-reversion mechanism: following an observable decline from an unusually high level of within-sector return commonality, firms with stronger pre-existing fundamental characteristics but recent sector-relative underperformance may recover relative to weaker firms with sector-relative outperformance. The correlation-state transition, rather than a generic sector return shock, is a necessary condition for trading. The hypothesis does not assume that every correlation decline is caused by passive-flow unwinding; it is a reduced-form test of whether temporary common-price formation is followed by six-day re-differentiation conditional on point-in-time fundamentals.
programs.description: At each close t, define daily close-to-close returns r[i,u] = close[i,u] / close[i,u-1] - 1. A sector is correlation-eligible at t only if it has at least 8 constituents with non-missing closes for every date from t-20 through t. For each eligible sector s, compute C[s,t] as the equally weighted mean of all distinct pairwise Pearson correlations of member returns over the 20 observations t-19 through t. Let H[s,t] be the 75th percentile of valid historical C[s,u] values over u in t-126 through t-1, requiring at least 63 valid observations. Sector s is in a causal correlation-release state at t if C[s,t-1] >= max(H[s,t], 0.35) and C[s,t] <= C[s,t-1] - 0.10. No future low-correlation confirmation is used. For stocks in a released sector, form four point-in-time fundamental percentile ranks within sector at t: freeCashFlowYield (higher is better), roic (higher is better), incomeQuality (higher is better), and debtToAssets (lower is better). Each rank uses only non-missing contemporaneously available values in that sector; a stock must have at least 3 of the 4 valid inputs, and its fundamental anchor Q is the mean of its available directional percentile ranks. Compute each stock's five-day sector-relative return A = (close[t] / close[t-5] - 1) minus the equal-weighted five-day return of all sector members with both required closes. Convert A to a within-sector percentile rank R among signal-eligible stocks. The stock score is S = Q - R: high scores are fundamentally stronger firms that lagged their sector over the preceding five days, while low scores are fundamentally weaker firms that outperformed. A released sector is tradable only if it has at least 10 signal-eligible stocks. Within each tradable released sector, buy the top k = max(2, floor(0.20*n)) scores and short the bottom k scores, equally weighted within each side. Each sector receives equal gross allocation, with +0.5/S total long weight and -0.5/S total short weight across S active sectors, making every vintage dollar-neutral and sector-dollar-neutral. The signal is observed after close t, entered at open t+1, and each vintage is held through open t+7, producing the required six-bar open-to-open forward return. A new qualifying vintage may be initiated daily; the live portfolio is the equal-capital aggregate of overlapping six-bar vintages. Missing prices prevent correlation or return eligibility; missing fundamental fields are handled only through the stated three-of-four anchor rule, with no filling or backward shifting. Incrementality is pre-specified for evaluation rather than used in calc: report factor-return correlation, constituent overlap, and an incremental regression of this portfolio's daily returns on sector_shock_cost_absorption_sort, resilient_industry_pressure_differentiation_j_j, and sector_relative_intermediate_momentum. The intended distinction is that this factor must be inactive without the contemporaneously observed high-correlation-to-lower-correlation transition, even if a sector has experienced a large common return impulse.

"""A large, broad, low-residual-dispersion industry move can temporarily dominate stock-specific price formation even without proving a particular ETF or dealer-flow counterparty. When a stock's completed-day industry-relative move is opposite to its established 21-day industry-relative direction, the move is treated as a conditional relative-price dislocation rather than as a post-event \"release\" signal. The hypothesis is that the prior relative-price direction contains slower-moving idiosyncratic information that reasserts itself over the next six daily bars after contemporaneous common-mode compression."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_common_mode_components(
    returns: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute causal daily industry medians, residuals, dispersion, and breadth."""
    index = returns.index
    columns = returns.columns
    median_panel = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    residual_panel = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    dispersion_panel = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    breadth_panel = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)

    if not isinstance(industry, pd.DataFrame) or industry.empty:
        return median_panel, residual_panel, dispersion_panel, breadth_panel

    # Industry is static by contract.  Taking its last supplied observation is
    # robust to sparse synthetic panels while not changing a static classification.
    labels = industry.reindex(index=index, columns=columns).ffill().iloc[-1]
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna() & (labels.astype(str) != ""))

    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        group_columns = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(group_columns) == 0:
            continue

        group_returns = returns.loc[:, group_columns]
        valid = np.isfinite(group_returns)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        group_median = group_returns.where(valid).median(axis=1).where(count >= 10)
        group_residual = group_returns.sub(group_median, axis=0).where(valid)
        group_dispersion = group_residual.std(axis=1, ddof=0).where(count >= 10)

        direction = np.sign(group_median)
        same_sign = group_returns.mul(direction, axis=0).gt(0.0).astype(float)
        group_breadth = same_sign.where(valid).sum(axis=1).div(count).where(count >= 10)

        repeated_median = np.repeat(group_median.to_numpy()[:, None], len(group_columns), axis=1)
        repeated_dispersion = np.repeat(group_dispersion.to_numpy()[:, None], len(group_columns), axis=1)
        repeated_breadth = np.repeat(group_breadth.to_numpy()[:, None], len(group_columns), axis=1)

        median_panel.loc[:, group_columns] = repeated_median
        residual_panel.loc[:, group_columns] = group_residual
        dispersion_panel.loc[:, group_columns] = repeated_dispersion
        breadth_panel.loc[:, group_columns] = repeated_breadth

    return median_panel, residual_panel, dispersion_panel, breadth_panel


@register_factor
class ContemporaneousCommonModeAnchorOpposition(BaseFactor):
    """Industry-compression residual reversal against a prior relative-price anchor."""

    factor_id = "common_mode_compression_anchor_release"
    name = "Contemporaneous Common-Mode Anchor Opposition"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Scores stocks whose 21-day industry-relative anchor is opposed by a "
        "same-day high-breadth, low-residual-dispersion industry shock."
    )
    window_length = 42
    inputs = ["close", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        if not isinstance(close, pd.DataFrame):
            return pd.DataFrame()

        safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        daily_returns = safe_close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
        daily_returns = daily_returns.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        industry_move, residual, dispersion, breadth = _industry_common_mode_components(
            daily_returns, industry
        )

        # All anchor and baseline quantities explicitly stop at t-1.
        anchor = residual.shift(1).rolling(21, min_periods=21).sum()
        move_baseline = industry_move.abs().shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        dispersion_baseline = dispersion.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()

        score = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns, dtype=float)

        if not isinstance(industry, pd.DataFrame) or industry.empty:
            return score

        labels = industry.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).ffill().iloc[-1]
        labels = labels.where(labels.notna() & (labels.astype(str) != ""))

        for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
            group_columns = labels.index[labels == group]
            if len(group_columns) == 0:
                continue

            group_anchor = anchor.loc[:, group_columns]
            anchor_scale = group_anchor.abs().median(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

            group_move = industry_move.loc[:, group_columns[0]]
            group_dispersion = dispersion.loc[:, group_columns[0]]
            group_breadth = breadth.loc[:, group_columns[0]]
            group_move_baseline = move_baseline.loc[:, group_columns[0]]
            group_dispersion_baseline = dispersion_baseline.loc[:, group_columns[0]]

            eligible = (
                group_move_baseline.gt(0.0)
                & group_dispersion_baseline.gt(0.0)
                & group_move.abs().ge(1.5 * group_move_baseline)
                & group_breadth.ge(0.75)
                & group_dispersion.gt(0.0)
                & group_dispersion.le(0.60 * group_dispersion_baseline)
            )

            group_residual = residual.loc[:, group_columns]
            anchor_magnitude = group_anchor.abs().div(anchor_scale, axis=0).clip(upper=3.0)
            residual_magnitude = group_residual.abs().div(group_dispersion, axis=0).clip(upper=3.0)
            raw_score = np.sign(group_anchor) * anchor_magnitude * residual_magnitude

            opposition = group_anchor.mul(group_residual).lt(0.0)
            valid_event = opposition & eligible.to_numpy()[:, None]
            score.loc[:, group_columns] = raw_score.where(valid_event, 0.0)

        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

For industry g, compute m(g,u) as the cross-sectional median return of stocks in g with valid returns, requiring at least 10 valid stocks. Define the stock residual e(i,u)=r(i,u)-m(g,u). The pre-t anchor uses only information through t-1: A(i,t)=sum from u=t-21 through t-1 of e(i,u). Using completed bar t only, define industry breadth B(g,t) as the fraction of valid stocks whose return has the same sign as m(g,t), define residual dispersion D(g,t) as the cross-sectional standard deviation of e(i,t), and define Q(g,t)=median of abs(m(g,u)) and H(g,t)=median of D(g,u) over u=t-20 through t-1. For stocks in eligible industries with A(i,t)*e(i,t)<0, assign S(i,t)=sign(A(i,t))*min(abs(A(i,t))/median_g(abs(A(j,t))),3)*min(abs(e(i,t))/D(g,t),3); otherwise assign zero. Thus positive scores are stocks with positive prior residual anchors that were pulled down relative to industry on t, while negative scores are the symmetric short candidates. Form the portfolio after close t, execute at t+1 open, long the top quintile and short the bottom quintile of S among eligible stocks with equal gross exposure by industry, and measure realized returns only from t+1 open through t+6 close. This differs from correlation-release factors because it enters during the observable same-day high-breadth, low-dispersion compression event and does not require a subsequently observed correlation decline, episode endpoint, turnover cooling, or release condition.

programs.code:
"""The signal targets sessions in which an unusually large, high-range trading process finishes near one intraday endpoint even though the close remains close to the prior close. This conjunction is interpreted more narrowly than as proof of residual metaorder inventory: it identifies a completed-bar state in which substantial intraday price discovery and participation occurred, but the final close-side imbalance was not reflected in net close-to-close displacement. A high-endpoint session is hypothesized to retain positive short-horizon drift and a low-endpoint session negative drift because close-side demand or supply survived the two-sided intraday trading process; the hypothesis is explicitly conditional and should be tested for incremental value against existing intrabar-pressure factors."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_robust_stats(values: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Trailing prior-window median and MAD, excluding the current bar."""
    prior = values.shift(1)
    median = prior.rolling(window, min_periods=window).median()
    mad = prior.rolling(window, min_periods=window).apply(
        lambda x: np.median(np.abs(x - np.median(x))), raw=True
    )
    return median, mad


def _prior_complete(valid: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Require every observation in t-window through t-1 to be valid."""
    return valid.shift(1).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum().eq(window)


@register_factor
class EndpointVolumeImpedanceDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Endpoint imbalance after unusually intense, high-range participation."""

    factor_id = "endpoint_volume_impedance_drift"
    name = "Endpoint Participation-Imbalance Drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-neutral endpoint direction following jointly abnormal volume and "
        "intraday range, conditional on muted close-to-close displacement."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        finite_current = (
            np.isfinite(open_)
            & np.isfinite(high)
            & np.isfinite(low)
            & np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
        )
        current_valid = (
            finite_current
            & close.gt(0.0)
            & previous_close.gt(0.0)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & high.gt(low)
        )

        intraday_range = high - low
        normalized_range = (intraday_range / previous_close).where(current_valid)
        range_valid = np.isfinite(normalized_range) & normalized_range.gt(0.0)
        volume_valid = np.isfinite(volume) & volume.gt(0.0)
        history_complete = _prior_complete(volume_valid & range_valid, 20)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(current_valid)
        median_dollar_volume = (
            dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        )

        base_eligible = (
            current_valid
            & history_complete
            & np.isfinite(median_dollar_volume)
            & median_dollar_volume.gt(0.0)
        )
        liquidity_percentile = median_dollar_volume.where(base_eligible).rank(
            axis=1, pct=True
        )
        liquid = (
            base_eligible
            & median_dollar_volume.ge(1_000_000.0)
            & liquidity_percentile.ge(0.30)
        )

        log_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume_valid))
        log_range = np.log(normalized_range.where(range_valid))
        volume_median, volume_mad = _prior_robust_stats(log_volume, 20)
        range_median, range_mad = _prior_robust_stats(log_range, 20)

        volume_scale = 1.4826 * volume_mad
        range_scale = 1.4826 * range_mad
        z_volume = (log_volume - volume_median) / volume_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z_range = (log_range - range_median) / range_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z_volume = z_volume.clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)
        z_range = z_range.clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0)

        close_location = (
            2.0 * (close - low) / intraday_range.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        ).where(current_valid)
        muted_displacement = (
            (close / previous_close - 1.0).abs().le(0.25 * normalized_range)
        )

        active = (
            liquid
            & np.isfinite(z_volume)
            & np.isfinite(z_range)
            & close_location.abs().ge(0.60)
            & z_volume.ge(1.0)
            & z_range.ge(1.0)
            & muted_displacement
        )
        raw = (close_location * np.minimum(z_volume, z_range)).where(active)

        lower = raw.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = raw.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        winsorized = raw.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        scaled_rank = 2.0 * winsorized.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0

        # Sector is static in this feed; grouping only active names avoids
        # treating non-traded names as zero-valued sector observations.
        groups = sector.iloc[0]
        sector_values = scaled_rank.where(active)
        sector_mean = sector_values.T.groupby(groups, sort=False).transform("mean").T
        sector_count = active.astype(float).T.groupby(groups, sort=False).transform("sum").T
        sector_residual = scaled_rank - sector_mean

        return sector_residual.where(active & sector_count.gt(1.0), 0.0).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: The signal targets sessions in which an unusually large, high-range trading process finishes near one intraday endpoint even though the close remains close to the prior close. This conjunction is interpreted more narrowly than as proof of residual metaorder inventory: it identifies a completed-bar state in which substantial intraday price discovery and participation occurred, but the final close-side imbalance was not reflected in net close-to-close displacement. A high-endpoint session is hypothesized to retain positive short-horizon drift and a low-endpoint session negative drift because close-side demand or supply survived the two-sided intraday trading process; the hypothesis is explicitly conditional and should be tested for incremental value against existing intrabar-pressure factors.
programs.description: At completed daily bar t, define dollar volume as close*volume and define normalized intraday range q_t=(high_t-low_t)/close_{t-1}. A stock is liquid and eligible only if: close_t and close_{t-1} are positive and finite; open_t, high_t, low_t, close_t, and volume_t are finite; volume_t>0; high_t>low_t; it has valid positive volume and valid positive normalized range observations on each of the prior 20 bars t-20 through t-1; and its 20-bar median dollar volume over t-20 through t-1 is at least USD 1,000,000 and ranks at or above the 30th cross-sectional percentile among otherwise valid stocks on t. Let v_t=log(volume_t) and r_t=log(q_t). For each variable separately, compute its rolling prior-20-bar median and median absolute deviation using only t-20 through t-1, then compute robust abnormality zV_t=(v_t-median(v))/(1.4826*MAD(v)) and zR_t=(r_t-median(r))/(1.4826*MAD(r)); observations with zero or missing MAD are excluded. Winsorize zV_t and zR_t to [-3,3]. Define close location CL_t=2*(close_t-low_t)/(high_t-low_t)-1, which lies in [-1,1]. Retain a signal only when |CL_t|>=0.60, zV_t>=1.00, zR_t>=1.00, and |close_t/close_{t-1}-1|<=0.25*q_t. The raw signed score is CL_t*min(zV_t,zR_t), so endpoint direction determines sign while the weaker of abnormal participation and abnormal range determines intensity. Cross-sectionally winsorize raw scores at the 1st and 99th percentiles among eligible names, convert them to percentile ranks scaled to [-1,1], and sector-neutralize by subtracting the equal-weight mean scaled rank of each sector on that date; sectors with one eligible stock receive a zero sector residual. Missing, zero-volume, halted, zero-range, invalid-price, or insufficient-history observations receive no score and are not traded. The t bar is used only after it is complete; portfolio formation and return measurement begin at the harness's next executable t+1 session convention, never at the t close.

"""This is an incremental conditioning test on post-earnings-announcement drift, not a claim that daily entropy directly identifies hidden institutional orders. A positive or negative earnings surprise may diffuse more persistently when trading is both active and directionally organized after the disclosure, consistent with correlated attention and order-flow response rather than stale, low-participation price persistence. The signal therefore requires above-normal participation and low transition entropy, and tests whether this condition adds predictive power beyond the surprise, initial reaction, momentum, volatility, liquidity, revisions, and event timing."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date median/MAD standardisation, retaining only finite inputs."""
    finite = frame.where(np.isfinite(frame))
    median = finite.median(axis=1)
    mad = finite.sub(median, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return finite.sub(median, axis=0).div(mad, axis=0)


def _transition_entropy(state: pd.DataFrame, n_states: int, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal Laplace-smoothed first-order conditional transition entropy."""
    previous = state.shift(1)
    valid_transition = state.notna() & previous.notna()

    counts: list[list[pd.DataFrame]] = []
    total = None
    for origin in range(n_states):
        row: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
        for destination in range(n_states):
            indicator = (
                ((previous == origin) & (state == destination))
                .astype(float)
                .where(valid_transition)
            )
            count = indicator.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
            row.append(count)
            total = count if total is None else total + count
        counts.append(row)

    entropy = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=state.index, columns=state.columns)
    augmented_total = total + float(n_states * n_states)
    for origin in range(n_states):
        row_total = counts[origin][0]
        for destination in range(1, n_states):
            row_total = row_total + counts[origin][destination]

        augmented_row_total = row_total + float(n_states)
        for destination in range(n_states):
            augmented_count = counts[origin][destination] + 1.0
            joint_probability = augmented_count / augmented_total
            conditional_probability = augmented_count / augmented_row_total
            entropy = entropy - joint_probability * np.log(conditional_probability)

    return entropy / np.log(float(n_states))


@register_factor
class EntropyConditionedSurprisePolarity(BaseFactor):
    """Scores fresh surprise reactions only when active trading has low transition entropy."""

    factor_id = "entropy_conditioned_surprise_polarity"
    name = "Participation-Conditioned Surprise Drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Fresh earnings or revenue surprise polarity scaled by inverse six-state "
        "return-volume transition entropy, active only for above-normal-volume "
        "names with a same-direction initial reaction in the lowest entropy tail."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = close / prior_close - 1.0

        volume_baseline = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        relative_volume = volume / volume_baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        lower_return = ret.rolling(60, min_periods=60).quantile(0.33)
        upper_return = ret.rolling(60, min_periods=60).quantile(0.67)
        valid_return_state = ret.notna() & lower_return.notna() & upper_return.notna()
        return_state = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(ret < lower_return, -1.0, np.where(ret > upper_return, 1.0, 0.0)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        ).where(valid_return_state)

        upper_volume = relative_volume.rolling(60, min_periods=60).quantile(0.67)
        valid_volume_state = relative_volume.notna() & upper_volume.notna()
        volume_state = (relative_volume > upper_volume).astype(float).where(valid_volume_state)

        combined_state = ((return_state + 1.0) * 2.0 + volume_state).where(
            return_state.notna() & volume_state.notna()
        )
        normalized_entropy = _transition_entropy(combined_state, 6, 60)

        eps_z = _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(data["epsSurprise"])
        revenue_z = _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(data["revenueSurprise"])
        available_components = eps_z.notna().astype(float) + revenue_z.notna().astype(float)
        surprise_composite = (eps_z.fillna(0.0) + revenue_z.fillna(0.0)).where(
            available_components > 0.0
        )
        surprise_direction = np.sign(surprise_composite)

        prior_available_composite = surprise_composite.ffill().shift(1)
        fresh_surprise = (
            surprise_composite.notna()
            & prior_available_composite.notna()
            & surprise_composite.ne(prior_available_composite)
            & surprise_direction.ne(0.0)
        )

        reaction_agrees = np.sign(ret).eq(surprise_direction) & np.sign(ret).ne(0.0)
        low_entropy = rank(normalized_entropy).le(0.30)
        eligible = relative_volume.gt(1.0)

        inverse_entropy = 1.0 / normalized_entropy.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        active = fresh_surprise & eligible & low_entropy & reaction_agrees
        score = (surprise_direction * inverse_entropy).where(active, 0.0)
        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

The signal therefore requires above-normal participation and low transition entropy, and tests whether this condition adds predictive power beyond the surprise, initial reaction, momentum, volatility, liquidity, revisions, and event timing.
programs.description: At each daily close t, compute one-day return r_t = close_t / close_{t-1} - 1 and trailing relative volume RV_t = volume_t / mean(volume_{t-20},...,volume_{t-1}); use only prior observations in the denominator. Define a three-valued return state {-1,0,+1} from r_t relative to each stock's trailing 60-day return thresholds: -1 if r_t is below its trailing 33rd percentile, +1 if above its trailing 67th percentile, and 0 otherwise. Define a two-valued volume state {0,1}: 1 if RV_t exceeds its trailing 60-day 67th percentile and 0 otherwise. The combined six-state sequence is used to estimate first-order transition entropy over the trailing 60 completed daily transitions, with Laplace pseudocount 1 applied to every origin-to-destination transition; normalized entropy is Shannon conditional entropy divided by log(6). Eligible names must have current RV above 1.0, preventing low entropy caused solely by inactive or stale trading. Surprise direction is s_t = sign(z_cs(epsSurprise_t) + z_cs(revenueSurprise_t)), where each z_cs is a same-date cross-sectional robust standardization among finite observations using median and MAD; a component is omitted when unavailable, and the composite requires at least one available component. A surprise is fresh only when the current point-in-time composite differs from its prior available value: fresh_t = 1 when s_t is nonzero and the composite surprise value at t differs from its forward-filled value at t-1; no ex-post event labels are used. Initial reaction is the cumulative close-to-close return from t-1 through t, measured only after the current daily bar has closed; require its sign to agree with s_t. Form the score after that close as s_t multiplied by inverse normalized entropy, but only for fresh eligible names whose normalized entropy is in the lowest 30% cross-sectional tail on date t, current RV is above 1.0, and reaction sign agrees with surprise sign; otherwise score is zero. Use the fixed parameters: 20-day volume baseline, 60-day state thresholds and entropy history, three return states, two volume states, Laplace pseudocount 1, and 30% entropy cutoff. Evaluate incremental forecasting power versus a PEAD baseline using surprise level, surprise change, prior 20-day momentum, trailing 20-day return volatility, log relative volume, market capitalization, and days since the latest surprise change as controls.

"""This replaces the unsupported assumption that isolated flow in financially fragile firms is non-informational and about to reverse. An idiosyncratic return-volume acceleration is treated as continuation only when it occurs on the public update of a positive or negative earnings-surprise signal and is directionally consistent with that surprise. Sector-concordant activity is excluded: the intended mechanism is delayed incorporation of firm-specific public information and its local order-flow cross-excitation, not liquidity provision against broad sector news or presumed forced liquidation."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_sector_median(
    activity_acceleration: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return each name's same-sector leave-one-out median acceleration."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(
        np.nan,
        index=activity_acceleration.index,
        columns=activity_acceleration.columns,
        dtype=float,
    )

    # Sector is static in this feed, so its first aligned row defines the
    # cross-sectional peer partition without using any price or event future.
    labels = sector.iloc[0]
    valid_labels = labels.dropna()

    for label in pd.unique(valid_labels):
        members = valid_labels.index[valid_labels == label]
        if len(members) < 4:
            continue

        group_activity = activity_acceleration.loc[:, members]
        for ticker in members:
            peers = group_activity.drop(columns=ticker)
            peer_count = peers.notna().sum(axis=1)
            peer_median = peers.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
            result.loc[:, ticker] = peer_median.where(peer_count >= 3)

    return result


@register_factor
class EventConfirmedIdiosyncraticFlowContinuation(BaseFactor):
    """Earnings-confirmed, sector-isolated return-volume acceleration continuation."""

    factor_id = "event_confirmed_idiosyncratic_flow_continuation"
    name = "Event-Confirmed Idiosyncratic Flow Continuation"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks earnings-surprise-consistent return-volume acceleration only on "
        "public surprise updates, after removing same-sector peer activity and "
        "suppressing sector-concordant accelerations."
    )
    window_length = 26
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "epsSurprise", "epsEstimate", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        ret = close.pct_change()

        # The baseline is strictly prior volume: t-20 through t-1.
        prior_volume_baseline = volume.shift(1).rolling(
            20, min_periods=20
        ).mean()
        volume_ratio = volume / prior_volume_baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        volume_ratio = volume_ratio.clip(upper=5.0)
        activity = ret * volume_ratio

        # The comparison mean is strictly prior activity: t-5 through t-1.
        prior_activity_mean = activity.shift(1).rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        acceleration = activity - prior_activity_mean

        previous_surprise = surprise.shift(1)
        report_update = surprise.notna() & (
            previous_surprise.isna() | surprise.ne(previous_surprise)
        )

        normalized_surprise = surprise / estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        surprise_rank = normalized_surprise.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True)
        event_direction = 2.0 * surprise_rank - 1.0

        sector_median = _leave_one_out_sector_median(acceleration, sector)
        idiosyncratic_acceleration = acceleration - sector_median

        eligible = (
            report_update
            & event_direction.notna()
            & event_direction.ne(0.0)
            & idiosyncratic_acceleration.notna()
            & (event_direction * idiosyncratic_acceleration > 0.0)
            & (event_direction * sector_median <= 0.0)
        )

        signed_strength = (event_direction * idiosyncratic_acceleration).where(eligible)
        eligible_rank = signed_strength.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True)
        score = (np.sign(event_direction) * eligible_rank).where(eligible, 0.0)

        return score.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: This replaces the unsupported assumption that isolated flow in financially fragile firms is non-informational and about to reverse. An idiosyncratic return-volume acceleration is treated as continuation only when it occurs on the public update of a positive or negative earnings-surprise signal and is directionally consistent with that surprise. Sector-concordant activity is excluded: the intended mechanism is delayed incorporation of firm-specific public information and its local order-flow cross-excitation, not liquidity provision against broad sector news or presumed forced liquidation.
programs.description: All inputs are observed through the signal-date close; the portfolio is formed after that close and evaluated over the fixed next 6 daily bars. For stock i on date t, define r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. Define the prior-volume baseline b_i,t as the arithmetic mean of volume_i over t-20 through t-1, requiring all 20 observations and b_i,t > 0. Define signed return-volume activity a_i,t = r_i,t * min(volume_i,t / b_i,t, 5), and define acceleration d_i,t = a_i,t - mean(a_i,t-5,...,a_i,t-1), requiring all five prior activity observations. Define the public-report-update flag g_i,t = 1 only when epsSurprise_i,t is nonmissing and either epsSurprise_i,t-1 is missing or epsSurprise_i,t differs from epsSurprise_i,t-1; otherwise g_i,t = 0. This uses the feed's point-in-time availability stamp and never waits for later flow extinction or a later reversal. For names with nonmissing epsSurprise and nonzero epsEstimate, define q_i,t = epsSurprise_i,t / abs(epsEstimate_i,t). Let e_i,t = 2 * percentile_rank(q_i,t) - 1, where percentile ranks are computed cross-sectionally among valid q observations on date t, using average ranks for ties. For each stock, compute m_i,t as the median d_j,t of valid same-sector peer stocks j excluding i; require at least three such peers. Define idiosyncratic acceleration x_i,t = d_i,t - m_i,t. A name is eligible only if g_i,t = 1, e_i,t is nonzero, x_i,t is available, e_i,t * x_i,t > 0, and e_i,t * m_i,t <= 0. The last condition is the exact sector-concordance suppression rule: an earnings-consistent sector-directional acceleration suppresses the signal rather than being interpreted as firm-specific information. For eligible names define w_i,t = e_i,t * x_i,t. The final score is sign(e_i,t) times the percentile rank of w_i,t among eligible names on that date; all ineligible or missing-input names receive zero. Fixed pre-registered parameters are a 20-bar prior-volume baseline, a 5-bar prior-activity mean, volume-ratio clipping at 5, and a minimum of three valid sector peers. Before admission, the finalized expression should be mechanically checked for exact identity against existing factors.

"""Buffer-conditioned fade of muted sector-peer pressure.

Mechanism: aligned peer and receiver pressure with little receiver close impact can
represent either slow information diffusion or temporary inventory absorption.  A
strong cash and liquidity buffer makes absorption and subsequent price repair more
likely, so the factor fades the peer-pressure direction only in buffered receivers.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_pressure(
    pressure: pd.DataFrame, sector_labels: pd.Series
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-bar leave-one-out sector mean using only contemporaneously valid peers."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=pressure.index, columns=pressure.columns)
    labels = sector_labels.reindex(pressure.columns)

    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        columns = labels.index[labels == label]
        if len(columns) < 4:
            continue
        block = pressure.loc[:, columns]
        count = block.notna().sum(axis=1)
        total = block.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        loo = block.rsub(total, axis=0).div(count - 1, axis=0)
        loo = loo.where(block.notna() & count.ge(4).to_numpy()[:, None])
        output.loc[:, columns] = loo
    return output


def _sector_neutral_percentile(
    score: pd.DataFrame, valid: pd.DataFrame, sector_labels: pd.Series
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rank valid scores within adequately populated sectors; invalid names are neutral."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=score.index, columns=score.columns, dtype=float)
    labels = sector_labels.reindex(score.columns)

    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        columns = labels.index[labels == label]
        if len(columns) < 8:
            continue
        block = score.loc[:, columns]
        block_valid = valid.loc[:, columns]
        count = block_valid.sum(axis=1)
        mean = block.where(block_valid).mean(axis=1)
        demeaned = block.sub(mean, axis=0)
        eligible = block_valid & count.ge(8).to_numpy()[:, None]
        ranked = demeaned.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True, method="average")
        output.loc[:, columns] = (2.0 * ranked - 1.0).fillna(0.0)
    return output


@register_factor
class BufferedPeerAbsorptionFade(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "buffered_peer_absorption_fade"
    name = "Buffered Peer-Absorption Fade"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-neutral fade of coherent peer directional pressure when an aligned "
        "receiver has a muted price response and a strong balance-sheet liquidity buffer."
    )
    window_length = 30
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "cashRatio",
        "currentRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
        "netDebtToEbitda",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sector_labels = data["sector"].iloc[0]

        price_valid = close.notna() & high.notna() & low.notna() & high.gt(low)
        clv = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / (high - low)).where(price_valid)

        positive_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))
        volume_count = positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).count()
        volume_median = positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).median()
        volume_valid = volume.gt(0.0) & volume_count.ge(10) & volume_median.gt(0.0)
        relative_volume = (volume / volume_median).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        pressure = (clv * relative_volume).where(price_valid & volume_valid)

        peer_pressure = _leave_one_out_pressure(pressure, sector_labels)
        peer_count = peer_pressure.rolling(3, min_periods=3).count()
        peer_impulse = peer_pressure.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean().clip(-2.0, 2.0)
        peer_valid = peer_count.eq(3) & peer_impulse.notna()

        own_count = pressure.rolling(2, min_periods=2).count()
        own_pressure = pressure.rolling(2, min_periods=2).mean()
        aligned_participation = (
            own_pressure.mul(np.sign(peer_impulse)).clip(0.0, 3.0) / 3.0
        ).where(own_count.eq(2) & peer_valid)

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        log_return = np.log(close / prior_close).where(
            close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0)
        )
        return_sigma = log_return.rolling(20, min_periods=12).std()
        normalized_range = ((high - low) / prior_close).where(
            high.ge(low) & prior_close.gt(0.0)
        )
        muted_response = (
            (1.0 - log_return.abs() / (normalized_range + 1.0e-6)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
            * (1.0 - log_return.abs() / (2.0 * return_sigma + 1.0e-6)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        )
        muted_valid = muted_response.notna() & return_sigma.gt(0.0)

        cash_ratio = data["cashRatio"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        current_ratio = data["currentRatio"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        debt_to_equity = data["debtToEquity"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        net_debt_to_ebitda = data["netDebtToEbitda"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        buffer_valid = (
            cash_ratio.notna()
            & current_ratio.notna()
            & debt_to_equity.notna()
            & net_debt_to_ebitda.notna()
            & debt_to_equity.ge(0.0)
        )

        buffer_strength = (
            0.30 * rank(cash_ratio.clip(0.0, 10.0).where(buffer_valid))
            + 0.25 * rank(current_ratio.clip(0.0, 10.0).where(buffer_valid))
            + 0.25 * (1.0 - rank(debt_to_equity.clip(0.0, 10.0).where(buffer_valid)))
            + 0.20 * (1.0 - rank(net_debt_to_ebitda.clip(-5.0, 10.0).where(buffer_valid)))
        ).where(buffer_valid)

        strong_buffer = buffer_strength.ge(0.55)
        valid = (
            peer_valid
            & aligned_participation.notna()
            & muted_valid
            & strong_buffer
        )

        # The negative sign deliberately fades the peer-pressure direction.
        raw_score = (
            -peer_impulse
            * aligned_participation
            * muted_response
            * buffer_strength.pow(2.0)
        ).where(valid)

        return _sector_neutral_percentile(raw_score, valid, sector_labels).astype(float)
programs.name: Buffered Peer-Absorption Fade
programs.trading_idea: A coherent sector-peer pressure impulse is informative only when the receiver is participating in the same directional flow yet its close-to-close response is muted. In financially well-buffered firms, this combination is more plausibly temporary inventory absorption or benchmark-driven flow than an unpriced financing shock: cash capacity permits natural buyers and liquidity providers to absorb the pressure, so the apparent impact deficit subsequently reverses in the direction opposite the peer impulse. The interaction has edge because peer pressure supplies a timely cross-excitation trigger while the balance-sheet buffer distinguishes reversible absorption from the constrained-flow cases that a peer-impact signal alone cannot separate; the negative realized signs of both parents motivate this economically grounded fade rather than an unsupported continuation interpretation.
programs.description: Computes leave-one-out sector directional relative-volume pressure, requires aligned receiver pressure and a muted receiver price response, then fades that signed impulse only in names with strong cash, liquidity, and low-leverage buffers. The final score is sector-neutralized so it represents idiosyncratic buffered absorption rather than a sector directional bet.

programs.code:
"""Surprise-impact saturation phase switch in organized participation regimes.

Mechanism: low transition entropy and elevated participation identify coordinated
order-flow states, but their implication depends on the event response elasticity.
A modest reaction per unit of fresh fundamental surprise is under-assimilation,
whereas an extreme aligned reaction per unit of surprise is feedback saturation
and is expected to reverse over the next several bars.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_release(actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """True where a reported value becomes newly available or is revised."""
    return actual.notna() & actual.ne(actual.shift(1))


def _event_zscore(
    surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    estimate: pd.DataFrame,
    event: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional event-date standardized surprise with tail clipping."""
    raw = surprise.div(estimate.abs().where(estimate.abs().gt(0.0)))
    raw = raw.where(np.isfinite(raw))
    valid = raw.where(event)
    enough = valid.count(axis=1).ge(15)

    lo = valid.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    hi = valid.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    clipped = valid.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    scale = clipped.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(scale, axis=0).where(enough, axis=0)


def _pre_event_transition_entropy(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Six-state, trailing first-order entropy using only states through t-1."""
    prior_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ret = close.div(prior_close).sub(1.0)
    vol_base = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    rel_vol = volume.div(vol_base)

    lower = ret.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=60).quantile(0.33)
    upper = ret.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=60).quantile(0.67)
    valid_ret = ret.notna() & lower.notna() & upper.notna()
    ret_state = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(ret.lt(lower), 0.0, np.where(ret.gt(upper), 2.0, 1.0)),
        index=close.index,
        columns=close.columns,
    ).where(valid_ret)

    vol_cut = rel_vol.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=60).quantile(0.67)
    vol_state = rel_vol.gt(vol_cut).astype(float).where(rel_vol.notna() & vol_cut.notna())
    state = (ret_state * 2.0 + vol_state).where(ret_state.notna() & vol_state.notna())
    previous = state.shift(1)
    valid_transition = state.notna() & previous.notna()

    counts = []
    for origin in range(6):
        row = []
        for destination in range(6):
            indicator = ((previous.eq(float(origin))) & (state.eq(float(destination)))).astype(float)
            row.append(indicator.where(valid_transition).shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=60).sum())
        counts.append(row)

    total = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    entropy = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    for origin in range(6):
        row_total = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for destination in range(6):
            total = total + counts[origin][destination]
            row_total = row_total + counts[origin][destination]
        for destination in range(6):
            joint = (counts[origin][destination] + 1.0) / (total + 36.0)
            conditional = (counts[origin][destination] + 1.0) / (row_total + 6.0)
            entropy = entropy - joint * np.log(conditional)

    return entropy / np.log(6.0)


@register_factor
class SurpriseImpactSaturationPhaseSwitch(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "surprise_impact_saturation_phase_switch"
    name = "Surprise Impact Saturation Phase Switch"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Fresh standardized surprise polarity switches from continuation to reversal "
        "as its aligned volatility-normalized price response becomes excessive, "
        "conditional on active low-entropy return-volume flow."
    )
    window_length = 121
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        eps_event = _fresh_release(data["epsActual"])
        revenue_event = _fresh_release(data["revenueActual"])
        eps_z = _event_zscore(data["epsSurprise"], data["epsEstimate"], eps_event)
        revenue_z = _event_zscore(
            data["revenueSurprise"], data["revenueEstimate"], revenue_event
        )

        available = eps_z.notna().astype(float) + revenue_z.notna().astype(float)
        surprise = eps_z.fillna(0.0).add(revenue_z.fillna(0.0)).div(
            available.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        fresh = eps_event | revenue_event

        prior_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        reaction = close.div(prior_close).sub(1.0)
        prior_volatility = reaction.shift(1).rolling(30, min_periods=20).std()
        standardized_reaction = reaction.abs().div(prior_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        volume_base = volume.shift(1).rolling(30, min_periods=20).mean()
        relative_volume = volume.div(volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        entropy = _pre_event_transition_entropy(close, volume)

        surprise_size = surprise.abs()
        elasticity = standardized_reaction.div(surprise_size.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        phase_score = (1.25 - elasticity.clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)) / 1.25
        signed_score = np.sign(surprise) * phase_score

        moderate_news = surprise_size.ge(0.50) & surprise_size.le(2.50)
        aligned = np.sign(reaction).eq(np.sign(surprise)) & np.sign(reaction).ne(0.0)
        active_flow = relative_volume.gt(1.15)
        organized_flow = rank(entropy).le(0.35)
        eligible = fresh & moderate_news & aligned & active_flow & organized_flow

        return signed_score.where(eligible, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
