"""The signal does not infer dealer inventory or signed order flow from daily bars. Instead, it identifies an observable, temporary price-participation feedback pattern: directional range-normalized price pressure and relative-volume shocks move in opposite phases, the relative dominance of the two alternates day to day, and that oscillation decays after a material directional displacement. This pattern is interpreted as a candidate transient-flow state rather than new information, so the trade takes the opposite side of the preceding displacement."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _orbit_statistics(
    impact: pd.DataFrame,
    volume_shock: pd.DataFrame,
    log_return: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute eight-bar causal anti-phase, alternation, decay, direction, and displacement."""
    index = impact.index
    columns = impact.columns
    n_rows, n_cols = impact.shape

    impact_values = impact.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    shock_values = volume_shock.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    return_values = log_return.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)

    phase = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    alternation = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    decay = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    direction = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    displacement = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)

    for t in range(7, n_rows):
        i_window = impact_values[t - 7 : t + 1]
        q_window = shock_values[t - 7 : t + 1]
        r_window = return_values[t - 7 : t + 1]

        valid = (
            np.isfinite(i_window).all(axis=0)
            & np.isfinite(q_window).all(axis=0)
            & np.isfinite(r_window).all(axis=0)
        )
        if not valid.any():
            continue

        i_std = np.std(i_window, axis=0, ddof=1)
        q_std = np.std(q_window, axis=0, ddof=1)
        valid &= (i_std > 0.0) & (q_std > 0.0)

        signed_displacement = np.sum(r_window, axis=0)
        d = np.sign(signed_displacement)
        valid &= np.isfinite(signed_displacement) & (d != 0.0)
        if not valid.any():
            continue

        u_window = i_window * d[None, :]
        u_mean = np.mean(u_window, axis=0)
        q_mean = np.mean(q_window, axis=0)
        u_std = np.std(u_window, axis=0, ddof=1)

        u_centered = u_window - u_mean[None, :]
        q_centered = q_window - q_mean[None, :]
        phase_denom = np.sqrt(
            np.sum(u_centered * u_centered, axis=0)
            * np.sum(q_centered * q_centered, axis=0)
        )
        valid &= np.isfinite(phase_denom) & (phase_denom > 0.0)
        if not valid.any():
            continue

        corr_u_q = np.sum(u_centered * q_centered, axis=0) / phase_denom

        z_u = u_centered / u_std[None, :]
        z_q = q_centered / q_std[None, :]
        x = z_u - z_q

        x_lag = x[:-1]
        x_now = x[1:]
        x_lag_centered = x_lag - np.mean(x_lag, axis=0)[None, :]
        x_now_centered = x_now - np.mean(x_now, axis=0)[None, :]
        alternation_denom = np.sqrt(
            np.sum(x_lag_centered * x_lag_centered, axis=0)
            * np.sum(x_now_centered * x_now_centered, axis=0)
        )
        valid &= np.isfinite(alternation_denom) & (alternation_denom > 0.0)
        if not valid.any():
            continue

        corr_x_lag = (
            np.sum(x_lag_centered * x_now_centered, axis=0) / alternation_denom
        )
        early_amplitude = np.mean(np.abs(x[:3]), axis=0)
        late_amplitude = np.mean(np.abs(x[-3:]), axis=0)
        decay_value = np.clip(
            1.0 - late_amplitude / (early_amplitude + 0.0001), 0.0, 1.0
        )

        phase[t, valid] = -corr_u_q[valid]
        alternation[t, valid] = -corr_x_lag[valid]
        decay[t, valid] = decay_value[valid]
        direction[t, valid] = d[valid]
        displacement[t, valid] = np.abs(signed_displacement[valid])

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(phase, index=index, columns=columns),
        pd.DataFrame(alternation, index=index, columns=columns),
        pd.DataFrame(decay, index=index, columns=columns),
        pd.DataFrame(direction, index=index, columns=columns),
        pd.DataFrame(displacement, index=index, columns=columns),
    )


@register_factor
class CausalAntiPhasePressureOrbitReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Reverses material displacements accompanied by decaying anti-phase pressure-volume oscillation."""

    factor_id = "anti_phase_pressure_orbit_reversal"
    name = "Causal Anti-Phase Pressure Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional reversal signal for names whose eight-bar directional "
        "range-normalized pressure and relative-volume shocks are anti-phased, "
        "alternate in dominance across adjacent bars, and decay after a material "
        "observed displacement."
    )
    window_length = 28
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        bar_range = high - low
        range_fraction = bar_range / prior_close

        valid_price = (
            (close > 0.0)
            & (prior_close > 0.0)
            & bar_range.notna()
            & (bar_range >= 0.0)
        )
        close_location = ((close - low) / bar_range).where(bar_range > 0.0, 0.5)
        close_location = close_location.where(bar_range >= 0.0)

        log_return = np.log(close / prior_close).where(valid_price)
        confirmation = (
            1.0 + np.sign(log_return) * (2.0 * close_location - 1.0)
        ) / 2.0
        impact = (
            (log_return / (range_fraction + 0.0001)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
            * confirmation
        ).where(valid_price)

        prior_volume_mean = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        valid_volume = (volume > 0.0) & (prior_volume_mean > 0.0)
        volume_shock = np.log(volume / prior_volume_mean).where(valid_volume)

        phase, alternation, decay, direction, displacement = _orbit_statistics(
            impact,
            volume_shock,
            log_return,
        )

        phase_strength = ((phase - 0.20) / 0.80).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        alternation_strength = ((alternation - 0.10) / 0.90).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        eligible = (
            phase.notna()
            & alternation.notna()
            & decay.notna()
            & direction.notna()
            & displacement.notna()
        )
        displacement_rank = displacement.where(eligible).rank(
            axis=1, pct=True, ascending=True
        )
        setup_strength = (
            0.50 * phase_strength + 0.30 * alternation_strength + 0.20 * decay
        ) * displacement_rank
        setup_strength = setup_strength.where(eligible)

        setup_rank = setup_strength.rank(axis=1, pct=True, ascending=True)
        return (-direction * setup_rank).where(eligible)

programs.trading_idea: The signal does not infer dealer inventory or signed order flow from daily bars. Instead, it identifies an observable, temporary price-participation feedback pattern: directional range-normalized price pressure and relative-volume shocks move in opposite phases, the relative dominance of the two alternates day to day, and that oscillation decays after a material directional displacement. This pattern is interpreted as a candidate transient-flow state rather than new information, so the trade takes the opposite side of the preceding displacement.
programs.description: All quantities at date t use only completed daily bars dated t or earlier. Let r_s=ln(close_s/close_{s-1}), R_s=(high_s-low_s)/close_{s-1}, and CL_s=(close_s-low_s)/(high_s-low_s). For zero-range bars set CL_s=0.5; require positive close, prior close, high-low nonnegative, and volume. Define directional close confirmation m_s=(1+sign(r_s)*(2*CL_s-1))/2, with sign(0)=0, and signed range-normalized impact i_s=clip(r_s/(R_s+0.0001),-3,3)*m_s. Define the causal relative-volume shock q_s=ln(volume_s/mean(volume_{s-20},...,volume_{s-1})); the volume baseline excludes the current bar. A stock is eligible only when all inputs needed for q and the most recent eight observations of i and q are finite, the 20-day baseline volume is positive, and the within-eight-bar standard deviations of i and q are positive. Let S_t=sum(r_{t-7},...,r_t), d_t=sign(S_t), and u_s=d_t*i_s for s=t-7,...,t. Thus u is impact expressed in the direction of the already-observed eight-day displacement. On these eight bars calculate P_t=-corr(u_s,q_s), the contemporaneous anti-phase statistic. Standardize each series using its own eight-bar mean and sample standard deviation, zU_s=(u_s-mean(u))/sd(u) and zQ_s=(q_s-mean(q))/sd(q), and define x_s=zU_s-zQ_s. Calculate A_t=-corr(x_s,x_{s-1}) over s=t-6,...,t; this is the explicit alternation statistic and is high only when the relative dominance of price pressure versus participation switches across adjacent days. Define early oscillation amplitude E_t=mean(|x_{t-7}|,|x_{t-6}|,|x_{t-5}|) and late amplitude L_t=mean(|x_{t-2}|,|x_{t-1}|,|x_t|), then D_t=clip(1-L_t/(E_t+0.0001),0,1). Convert the phase measures continuously: p_t=clip((P_t-0.20)/0.80,0,1) and a_t=clip((A_t-0.10)/0.90,0,1). The raw setup strength is H_t=(0.50*p_t+0.30*a_t+0.20*D_t)*CSRank_t(|S_t|), where CSRank is the same-date ascending percentile rank among eligible stocks; missing or ineligible names receive NaN. The final directed factor is F_t=-d_t*CSRank_t(H_t). Hence positive-displacement names with strong causal anti-phase, alternating, decaying oscillations receive negative scores, and negative-displacement names receive positive scores. This differs from a generic low-volume reversal rule because low volume, weak impact, or a large move alone cannot score highly without both negative price-volume phase correlation and negative first-order autocorrelation in the standardized pressure-versus-participation gap. No future turning point, completed cycle, or future amplitude observation is used. Cross-sectional ranking is over the eligible universe without sector neutralization.

"""Abnormal trading participation can reflect either informed order-flow arrival, which may persist, or temporary liquidity-demand pressure, which may reverse. Rather than assuming that a low-entropy return-volume state implies continuation, the signal estimates the historically realized signed next-day outcome conditional on the current return-volume state. A state is bullish only when its strictly historical transition record predicts a relatively positive next signed return; predictable reversal states receive negative scores."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


_TRANSITION_WINDOW = 126
_DIRICHLET_STRENGTH = 12.0


def _return_volume_state(close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Create causal signed-return and return-volume state codes."""
    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    ret = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0

    # The current return is normalized only by volatility observable before t.
    prior_volatility = ret.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
    return_valid = ret.notna() & prior_volatility.notna() & (prior_volatility > 0.0)

    return_state = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    return_state = return_state.mask(ret > 0.5 * prior_volatility, 1.0)
    return_state = return_state.mask(ret < -0.5 * prior_volatility, -1.0)
    return_state = return_state.where(return_valid)

    # Shift first so the participation baseline contains exactly t-20 through t-1.
    prior_volume_mean = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    volume_ratio = volume / prior_volume_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    volume_valid = volume.notna() & (volume >= 0.0) & volume_ratio.notna()

    volume_state = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    volume_state = volume_state.mask(volume_ratio < 0.8, 0.0)
    volume_state = volume_state.mask(volume_ratio > 1.5, 2.0)
    volume_state = volume_state.where(volume_valid)

    # Nine origin states: return {-1, 0, +1} x volume {low, normal, high}.
    state_code = ((return_state + 1.0) * 3.0 + volume_state).where(
        return_state.notna() & volume_state.notna()
    )
    return return_state, state_code


def _transition_forecast(return_state: pd.DataFrame, state_code: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Estimate a trailing, shrinkage-stabilized conditional transition edge."""
    # A row at t represents the fully observed transition from origin t-1 to
    # destination t. Therefore the rolling window ending at t contains no
    # information from the unobserved t-to-t+1 transition.
    origin = state_code.shift(1)
    destination = return_state
    valid_transition = origin.notna() & destination.notna()
    valid_marker = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=origin.index, columns=origin.columns).where(valid_transition)
    total = valid_marker.rolling(_TRANSITION_WINDOW, min_periods=_TRANSITION_WINDOW).sum()

    destination_counts: dict[int, pd.DataFrame] = {}
    for dest in (-1, 0, 1):
        observations = (destination == float(dest)).astype(float).where(valid_transition)
        destination_counts[dest] = observations.rolling(
            _TRANSITION_WINDOW, min_periods=_TRANSITION_WINDOW
        ).sum()

    pooled_expectation = (
        destination_counts[1] - destination_counts[-1]
    ) / total.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    enough_history = total.eq(float(_TRANSITION_WINDOW)) & state_code.notna()
    score = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=state_code.index, columns=state_code.columns)

    for state in range(9):
        origin_observations = (origin == float(state)).astype(float).where(valid_transition)
        origin_count = origin_observations.rolling(
            _TRANSITION_WINDOW, min_periods=_TRANSITION_WINDOW
        ).sum()

        posterior_expectation = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=state_code.index, columns=state_code.columns)
        for dest in (-1, 0, 1):
            joint_observations = (
                ((origin == float(state)) & (destination == float(dest)))
                .astype(float)
                .where(valid_transition)
            )
            joint_count = joint_observations.rolling(
                _TRANSITION_WINDOW, min_periods=_TRANSITION_WINDOW
            ).sum()
            pooled_frequency = destination_counts[dest] / total.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            posterior_count = joint_count + _DIRICHLET_STRENGTH * pooled_frequency
            posterior_expectation = posterior_expectation + float(dest) * posterior_count

        posterior_expectation = posterior_expectation / (origin_count + _DIRICHLET_STRENGTH).replace(
            0.0, np.nan
        )
        current_state = state_code.eq(float(state)) & enough_history
        score = score.where(~current_state, posterior_expectation - pooled_expectation)

    return score.where(enough_history, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class CausalVolumeStateEntropyContinuation(BaseFactor):
    """Historical return-volume transition edge for continuation versus reversal."""

    factor_id = "causal_volume_state_entropy_continuation"
    name = "Causal Volume-State Transition Forecast"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Maps the current nine-bin return-volume state to its strictly historical "
        "Dirichlet-shrunk next signed-return expectation, less the stock's pooled "
        "trailing unconditional expectation."
    )
    window_length = 146
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        return_state, state_code = _return_volume_state(close, volume)
        return _transition_forecast(return_state, state_code).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Causal Volume-State Transition Forecast
programs.trading_idea: Abnormal trading participation can reflect either informed order-flow arrival, which may persist, or temporary liquidity-demand pressure, which may reverse. Rather than assuming that a low-entropy return-volume state implies continuation, the signal estimates the historically realized signed next-day outcome conditional on the current return-volume state. A state is bullish only when its strictly historical transition record predicts a relatively positive next signed return; predictable reversal states receive negative scores.
programs.description: For each stock, define the current return state using close-to-close return relative to its prior 20-bar realized return volatility: +1 when return exceeds +0.5 volatility units, -1 when below -0.5 volatility units, and 0 otherwise. Define the volume state from current volume divided by the mean volume over bars t-20 through t-1: low below 0.8, normal from 0.8 to 1.5, and high above 1.5. The resulting 3-by-3 return-volume state at t is mapped to a posterior conditional expectation of the next signed-return state, estimated from the trailing 126 historical transitions whose destination dates are no later than t; thus, at t, only transitions with origins through t-1 and destinations through t are used, never the t-to-t+1 transition. For each state, estimate P(next state = +1), P(next state = 0), and P(next state = -1) with a fixed Dirichlet shrinkage of 12 pseudo-observations allocated according to the stock's pooled destination-state frequencies in the same 126-transition window; if insufficient valid history exists, assign a neutral score of zero. The factor is E[next signed state | current return-volume state] minus the pooled unconditional E[next signed state], so positive values forecast a more positive next-day directional outcome than the stock's recent baseline and negative values forecast reversal or downside. The posterior shrinkage, fixed bins, 20-bar normalizations, and 126-transition lookback are pre-specified to prevent sparse-state and discretization tuning.

programs.code:
"""The signal measures whether unusual trading participation systematically precedes, rather than follows, directional daily price displacement. A positive timing asymmetry is interpreted as a state in which information processing or portfolio-flow transmission remains incomplete after participation rises, while a negative asymmetry indicates the analogous downside state. This is not treated as a unique identifier of concealed order flow; it is a conditional proxy for delayed incorporation whose efficacy must be assessed net of event, volatility, and trading-cost exposure."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_neutral_percentile(
    raw_signal: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Demean eligible signals by same-day sector median, then percentile rank."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=raw_signal.index, columns=raw_signal.columns)

    for row_pos, timestamp in enumerate(raw_signal.index):
        values = raw_signal.iloc[row_pos]
        labels = sector.iloc[row_pos]
        eligible = values.notna() & labels.notna()

        if not eligible.any():
            continue

        eligible_values = values.loc[eligible]
        eligible_labels = labels.loc[eligible]
        sector_counts = eligible_labels.groupby(eligible_labels, sort=False).transform("size")
        sector_medians = eligible_values.groupby(eligible_labels, sort=False).transform("median")

        valid_sector = sector_counts >= 3
        demeaned = (eligible_values - sector_medians).where(valid_sector)
        ranked = demeaned.rank(pct=True)
        output.loc[timestamp, ranked.index] = ranked

    return output


@register_factor
class DailyVolumeReturnTimingDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-neutral rank of five-day volume-return timing-loop drift."""

    factor_id = "lag_antisymmetric_volume_return_loop_drift"
    name = "Daily Volume-Return Timing Drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Measures the antisymmetric lag relationship between abnormal daily "
        "trading participation and standardized close-to-close returns, then "
        "sector-neutralizes the five-day timing-loop average before ranking it "
        "cross-sectionally."
    )
    window_length = 27
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        safe_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)

        log_return = np.log(safe_close / safe_close.shift(1))
        log_volume = np.log1p(safe_volume)

        prior_volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        prior_volume_std = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std(ddof=0)
        abnormal_volume = (log_volume - prior_volume_mean) / prior_volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        prior_return_std = log_return.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std(ddof=0)
        standardized_return = log_return / prior_return_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        loop_term = (
            abnormal_volume.shift(1) * standardized_return
            - standardized_return.shift(1) * abnormal_volume
        )
        raw_signal = loop_term.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()

        close_history_valid = (
            safe_close.notna().rolling(27, min_periods=27).sum().eq(27)
        )
        volume_history_valid = (
            safe_volume.notna().rolling(27, min_periods=27).sum().eq(27)
        )
        loop_history_valid = loop_term.notna().rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum().eq(5)

        eligible_raw = raw_signal.where(
            close_history_valid & volume_history_valid & loop_history_valid
        )
        eligible_raw = eligible_raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        return _sector_neutral_percentile(eligible_raw, sector)
programs.name: Daily Volume-Return Timing Drift
programs.trading_idea: The signal measures whether unusual trading participation systematically precedes, rather than follows, directional daily price displacement. A positive timing asymmetry is interpreted as a state in which information processing or portfolio-flow transmission remains incomplete after participation rises, while a negative asymmetry indicates the analogous downside state. This is not treated as a unique identifier of concealed order flow; it is a conditional proxy for delayed incorporation whose efficacy must be assessed net of event, volatility, and trading-cost exposure.
programs.description: Use daily bars only. At the close of day t, define the completed close-to-close log return r_t = log(close_t / close_{t-1}). Define x_t = log(1 + volume_t), and define abnormal volume v_t = (x_t - mean(x_{t-20}, ..., x_{t-1})) / std(x_{t-20}, ..., x_{t-1}). Standardize returns causally as q_t = r_t / std(r_{t-20}, ..., r_{t-1}). Compute the one-day antisymmetric timing interaction for each of the five completed days i in {t-4, ..., t}: l_i = v_{i-1} * q_i - q_{i-1} * v_i. The raw signal is the arithmetic mean of these five l_i values. The eligible cross-sectional universe at t consists of stocks with positive volume, non-missing close and volume observations, and valid inputs for every required observation from t-26 through t; stocks with zero rolling standard deviation or any undefined input are excluded. Sector neutralization is mandatory: subtract the cross-sectional median raw signal of the stock's sector, using only eligible stocks and only sectors with at least three eligible constituents; otherwise exclude the stock. The submitted factor value is the cross-sectional percentile rank of this sector-demeaned signal among all remaining eligible stocks, with higher ranks denoting stronger upward timing asymmetry and lower ranks stronger downward timing asymmetry. The signal is calculated solely after the completed close at t and may be traded no earlier than the next executable daily bar/session.

programs.code:
"""Disclosure drift after exhausted idiosyncratic pressure and confirmed absorption.

Mechanism: a fundamental catalyst has a more durable short-horizon effect when an
opposing thin-liquidity impact episode has failed to extend, and the first
post-disclosure session subsequently absorbs unusual turnover without delivering
a commensurate signed response.  The first condition identifies released
inventory pressure; the second identifies public information still being
assimilated.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _release_mask(actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time first observation or reported-value revision mask."""
    prior = actual.shift(1)
    return actual.notna() & (prior.isna() | actual.ne(prior))


def _event_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame, event: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robust same-date normalization among names reporting that field."""
    observed = values.where(event)
    center = observed.median(axis=1)
    mad = observed.sub(center, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1)
    count = observed.count(axis=1)
    scale = (1.4826 * mad).where(count.ge(5))
    return observed.sub(center, axis=0).div(scale.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0).clip(-3.0, 3.0)


def _sector_residual(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date sector demean, with universe demean for small sectors."""
    output = values.sub(values.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels.eq(group)]
        if len(cols) < 4:
            continue
        block = values.loc[:, cols]
        counts = block.count(axis=1)
        group_mean = block.mean(axis=1)
        residual = block.sub(group_mean, axis=0)
        output.loc[:, cols] = residual.where(counts.ge(4), output.loc[:, cols])
    return output


def _sigmoid(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    clipped = values.clip(-30.0, 30.0)
    return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-clipped))


@register_factor
class DisclosureExhaustionAbsorptionReleaseMemory(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "disclosure_exhaustion_absorption_release_memory"
    name = "Disclosure Exhaustion Absorption Release"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "A decayed disclosure-surprise signal requiring both a failed opposing "
        "thin-impact extension at the release and high-turnover, muted response "
        "in the first post-release session."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        open_price = data["open"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        labels = data["sector"].iloc[0]

        eps_event = _release_mask(eps_actual) & eps_surprise.notna()
        revenue_event = _release_mask(revenue_actual) & revenue_surprise.notna()
        event = eps_event | revenue_event
        eps_z = _event_zscore(eps_surprise, eps_event)
        revenue_z = _event_zscore(revenue_surprise, revenue_event)
        available = eps_z.notna().astype(float) + revenue_z.notna().astype(float)
        joint_z = (eps_z.fillna(0.0) + revenue_z.fillna(0.0)).div(available.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        catalyst = np.tanh(joint_z / 2.0)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0))
        normal_volume = dollar_volume.shift(2).rolling(20, min_periods=12).mean()
        participation = dollar_volume.div(normal_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        bar_range = (high - low).where(high.ge(low) & close.gt(0.0))
        bar_direction = np.sign(close - open_price)
        thin_impact = (
            bar_direction
            * bar_range.div(close.replace(0.0, np.nan))
            .div(participation.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        ).where(participation.gt(0.0) & participation.le(1.0))

        impact_median = thin_impact.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=25).median()
        impact_mad = thin_impact.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=25).apply(
            lambda x: np.nanmedian(np.abs(x - np.nanmedian(x))), raw=True
        )
        impact_z = thin_impact.sub(impact_median).div(1.4826 * impact_mad + 1e-8).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        impact_residual = _sector_residual(impact_z, labels)
        prior_impact = impact_residual.shift(1)

        failed_downside = prior_impact.lt(-1.0) & low.ge(low.shift(1))
        failed_upside = prior_impact.gt(1.0) & high.le(high.shift(1))
        failed_extension = failed_downside | failed_upside
        repair_direction = -np.sign(prior_impact)
        exhaustion_strength = prior_impact.abs().sub(1.0).clip(0.0, 3.0).div(3.0)
        aligned_release = np.sign(catalyst).eq(repair_direction) & catalyst.notna()
        release_state = (catalyst * exhaustion_strength).where(event & failed_extension & aligned_release)

        session_return = close.div(open_price.replace(0.0, np.nan)).sub(1.0)
        sector_return = _sector_residual(session_return, labels)
        pre_volatility = session_return.shift(2).rolling(20, min_periods=12).std(ddof=0)
        signed_response = (
            np.sign(joint_z.shift(1))
            * sector_return.div(pre_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        )
        response_shortfall = joint_z.shift(1).abs() - signed_response
        muted_response = _sigmoid(response_shortfall)
        high_participation = _sigmoid(np.log(participation.replace(0.0, np.nan)) * 2.0)

        confirmed_pulse = (
            release_state.shift(1) * muted_response * high_participation
        ).where(release_state.shift(1).notna())
        memory = (
            confirmed_pulse.fillna(0.0)
            + 0.75 * confirmed_pulse.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
            + 0.55 * confirmed_pulse.shift(2).fillna(0.0)
            + 0.40 * confirmed_pulse.shift(3).fillna(0.0)
            + 0.30 * confirmed_pulse.shift(4).fillna(0.0)
        ) / 3.0

        neutral_memory = _sector_residual(memory, labels).fillna(0.0)
        return (rank(neutral_memory) - 0.5).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Disclosure Exhaustion Absorption Release
programs.trading_idea: A joint earnings and revenue surprise is most likely to drift over the next week when it arrives immediately after an opposing thin-participation idiosyncratic impact shock has failed to extend, indicating that temporary inventory pressure has already exhausted. The child then requires the first post-release session to show high turnover but muted surprise-aligned impact, distinguishing unresolved information absorption from a fully priced catalyst. This interaction carries edge because exhaustion identifies a cleared mechanical obstacle while abnormal-volume underreaction identifies a remaining fundamental repricing backlog; either condition alone can instead describe a generic reversal or an uninformative quiet response.
programs.description: The signal forms a release-state surprise only when a prior sector-residual thin-impact extreme fails to extend in the catalyst direction, then activates a decayed memory only if the following session has high relative dollar volume and an insufficient sector-adjusted response. It cross-sectionally ranks the sector-neutral signed unresolved-release memory.

programs.code:
"""The signal tests a narrowly defined conditional form of post-disclosure underreaction: a joint earnings and revenue surprise is more likely to drift when unusually large event-day participation occurs without a commensurate intraday price range. High turnover alone is not interpreted as proof of absorption or inefficient pricing; rather, the tradable hypothesis is the specific interaction of signed joint news, abnormal participation, and muted initial impact. The proposed mechanism is that a liquid, two-sided event market can initially accommodate substantial reallocations while fundamental interpretation and follow-on institutional positioning occur over subsequent sessions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_disclosure(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag values that first appear or differ from the prior available bar."""
    previous = value.shift(1)
    return value.notna() & (previous.isna() | value.ne(previous))


def _cross_sectional_percentile(
    value: pd.DataFrame, universe: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-day percentile rank restricted to the valid trading universe."""
    return value.where(universe).rank(axis=1, pct=True)


@register_factor
class JointDisclosureParticipationImpactInteraction(BaseFactor):
    """Joint disclosure surprise weighted by abnormal participation and muted impact."""

    factor_id = "disclosure_participation_range_decoupling_h6"
    name = "Joint Disclosure Participation-Impact Interaction"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Event-only signed joint earnings and revenue surprise, amplified when "
        "event-day participation is abnormal but the intraday range remains low."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        completed_median_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(
            20, min_periods=20
        ).median()

        valid_ohlcv = (
            open_.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & close.notna()
            & volume.notna()
            & (close > 0.0)
            & (high > 0.0)
            & (low > 0.0)
            & (volume > 0.0)
        )
        universe = (
            valid_ohlcv
            & completed_median_dollar_volume.notna()
            & (completed_median_dollar_volume >= 5_000_000.0)
        )

        eps_rank = _cross_sectional_percentile(eps_surprise, universe)
        revenue_rank = _cross_sectional_percentile(revenue_surprise, universe)
        eps_signed_rank = 2.0 * eps_rank - 1.0
        revenue_signed_rank = 2.0 * revenue_rank - 1.0

        same_direction = (
            ((eps_signed_rank > 0.0) & (revenue_signed_rank > 0.0))
            | ((eps_signed_rank < 0.0) & (revenue_signed_rank < 0.0))
        )
        joint_surprise = ((eps_signed_rank + revenue_signed_rank) / 2.0).where(
            same_direction, 0.0
        )

        participation = (
            dollar_volume / completed_median_dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.25, upper=4.0)
        participation_rank = _cross_sectional_percentile(participation, universe)

        raw_log_range = np.log(high / low).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        floored_range = raw_log_range.clip(lower=0.002).where(universe)
        range_lower = floored_range.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
        range_upper = floored_range.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
        winsorized_range = floored_range.clip(
            lower=range_lower, upper=range_upper, axis=0
        )
        inverse_impact_rank = _cross_sectional_percentile(
            1.0 / winsorized_range.replace(0.0, np.nan), universe
        )

        fresh_joint_event = (
            _fresh_disclosure(eps_actual)
            & _fresh_disclosure(revenue_actual)
            & eps_surprise.notna()
            & revenue_surprise.notna()
        )
        eligible_event = fresh_joint_event & universe

        score = joint_surprise * participation_rank * inverse_impact_rank
        return score.where(eligible_event, 0.0).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: The signal tests a narrowly defined conditional form of post-disclosure underreaction: a joint earnings and revenue surprise is more likely to drift when unusually large event-day participation occurs without a commensurate intraday price range. High turnover alone is not interpreted as proof of absorption or inefficient pricing; rather, the tradable hypothesis is the specific interaction of signed joint news, abnormal participation, and muted initial impact. The proposed mechanism is that a liquid, two-sided event market can initially accommodate substantial reallocations while fundamental interpretation and follow-on institutional positioning occur over subsequent sessions.
programs.description: At each daily close t, assign a fresh joint disclosure event only when both epsActual and revenueActual are non-null and newly available or changed versus t-1, with both epsSurprise and revenueSurprise available at t. The score is formed only after the t close and is traded no earlier than t+1. Use the cross-sectional universe of names with valid OHLCV, positive close and volume, and median trailing 20 completed-bar dollar volume (close times volume from t-20 through t-1) of at least USD 5 million. Standardize epsSurprise and revenueSurprise separately by same-day cross-sectional percentile rank within that universe, transform each rank to [-1,1], and define joint surprise as their average only when both transformed surprises have the same sign; otherwise set the event score to zero. Define abnormal participation as event-day dollar volume divided by trailing-20-bar median dollar volume, winsorize this ratio to [0.25, 4.0], and convert it to a same-day cross-sectional percentile rank. Define initial impact exclusively as intraday log range max(log(high/low), 0.002), winsorize it at the same-day 5th and 95th percentiles, and calculate its inverse-impact percentile rank using 1/range; the 20 bp floor prevents near-zero-range instability. The final event-only factor is joint surprise multiplied by abnormal-participation rank multiplied by inverse-impact rank; non-event names receive zero or NaN. Thus, the tested effect is explicitly surprise times high abnormal participation times low initial intraday impact, not an unconstrained standalone PEAD or volume-range ratio.

programs.code:
"""Investors and news-driven strategies initially extrapolate the sign of an earnings or revenue surprise, but often underweight whether the reported result is supported by improving cash conversion rather than receivables or inventory accumulation. Go long disappointing headline reports accompanied by a material improvement in cash conversion and short positive headline reports accompanied by a material deterioration in cash conversion, as fundamental investors process the quality of the result over the following week. The inefficiency persists because fast headline traders, passive flows, and constrained benchmarked investors react to the salient surprise, whereas detailed working-capital reconciliation is slower and costly to perform."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _update_mask(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify point-in-time fundamental step updates using only t and t-1."""
    previous = df.shift(1)
    return df.notna() & previous.notna() & df.ne(previous)


def _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise median/MAD score with standard-deviation fallback."""
    median = df.median(axis=1)
    centered = df.sub(median, axis=0)
    mad = centered.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    fallback = df.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad.where(mad > 1.0e-12, fallback)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 1.0e-12)
    return centered.div(scale, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _event_change_score(
    level: pd.DataFrame,
    event: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Standardize fresh quarterly changes against prior observed changes.

    The rolling dispersion is calculated only from prior report-to-report moves,
    rather than treating the many forward-filled daily observations as data.
    """
    change = level.diff().where(event)
    history = change.rolling(lookback, min_periods=2).std()
    scaled = change / history.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    # Early in a company's history there may be fewer than two prior updates.
    # Raw day changes are then still normalized cross-sectionally below.
    usable = scaled.where(scaled.notna(), change)
    return _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(usable)


@register_factor
class CashCycleHeadlineConflictAssimilation(BaseFactor):
    """Headline-surprise conflict with newly reported cash-conversion quality."""

    factor_id = "cashcycle_headline_conflict_assimilation"
    name = "Cash-Cycle Headline Conflict"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Activated on fresh quarterly reports, this factor identifies disagreement "
        "between standardized EPS/revenue headline surprises and cash-conversion "
        "quality. It is positive for negative surprises with improving cash "
        "realization and negative for positive surprises with worsening cash "
        "realization, with operating-cash-flow direction as confirmation."
    )
    window_length = 504
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "cashConversionCycle",
        "operatingCashFlow",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        cash_cycle = data["cashConversionCycle"]
        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"]

        eps_event = _update_mask(eps_surprise)
        revenue_event = _update_mask(revenue_surprise)
        headline_event = eps_event | revenue_event
        cash_cycle_event = _update_mask(cash_cycle)
        ocf_event = _update_mask(operating_cash_flow)

        eps_z = _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(eps_surprise)
        revenue_z = _robust_cross_sectional_zscore(revenue_surprise)
        headline_count = eps_z.notna().astype(float) + revenue_z.notna().astype(float)
        headline = (eps_z.fillna(0.0) + revenue_z.fillna(0.0)).div(
            headline_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        # A decline in days outstanding/inventory net of payables is an improvement.
        cash_cycle_change = _event_change_score(cash_cycle, cash_cycle_event, 504)
        cash_realization = -cash_cycle_change

        # OCF confirmation is intentionally directional: it supplements the detailed
        # working-capital measure without allowing different company sizes to dominate.
        ocf_direction = np.sign(operating_cash_flow.diff()).where(ocf_event, 0.0)
        quality = 0.80 * cash_realization + 0.20 * ocf_direction

        # Retain only genuine disagreement.  A negative headline paired with positive
        # quality is long; a positive headline paired with negative quality is short.
        opposition = (-np.sign(headline) * quality).clip(lower=0.0)
        conflict = -headline * opposition

        active = headline_event & cash_cycle_event & headline.notna() & quality.notna()
        result = conflict.where(active, 0.0)
        result = result.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return result.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

"""Peer-echo cash-quality contrarian factor.

Mechanism: headline traders extrapolate an earnings surprise more aggressively when
liquid industry leaders move in the same direction.  When that consensus narrative
conflicts with newly disclosed cash-conversion quality, the reinforced initial
reaction is prone to a near-term correction.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _update_mask(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally identify a new point-in-time fundamental observation."""
    prior = value.shift(1)
    return value.notna() & prior.notna() & value.ne(prior)


def _robust_cs_zscore(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional median/MAD standardization with a standard-dev fallback."""
    location = value.median(axis=1)
    centered = value.sub(location, axis=0)
    mad_scale = 1.4826 * centered.abs().median(axis=1)
    std_scale = value.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad_scale.where(mad_scale.gt(1.0e-12), std_scale)
    scale = scale.where(scale.gt(1.0e-12))
    return centered.div(scale, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _event_change_quality(level: pd.DataFrame, event: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Standardize report-to-report changes using only trailing disclosed history."""
    change = level.diff().where(event)
    history = change.rolling(378, min_periods=2).std()
    normalized = change.div(history.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    normalized = normalized.where(normalized.notna(), change)
    return _robust_cs_zscore(normalized)


def _liquid_peer_impulse(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Leave-self-out three-bar return of liquid industry leaders.

    Leader eligibility is determined from prior trailing dollar volume, avoiding
    contemporaneous selection on the current response.  The peer return is scaled
    by each recipient's own trailing volatility.
    """
    safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
    ret = safe_close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
    three_bar = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()
    dollar_adv = (close * volume).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
    own_vol = ret.shift(1).rolling(30, min_periods=12).std()

    labels = industry.ffill().iloc[-1].astype(object)
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "__UNKNOWN__")
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    for _, member_index in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        members = list(member_index)
        if len(members) < 2:
            continue
        adv_block = dollar_adv.loc[:, members]
        leader = adv_block.rank(axis=1, pct=True).ge(0.65) & adv_block.gt(0.0)
        weights = adv_block.where(leader, 0.0)
        weighted_return = weights * three_bar.loc[:, members]
        total_weight = weights.sum(axis=1)
        total_return = weighted_return.sum(axis=1)

        peer_weight = total_weight.to_frame().reindex(columns=members).sub(weights)
        peer_return = total_return.to_frame().reindex(columns=members).sub(weighted_return)
        peer_mean = peer_return.div(peer_weight.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        output.loc[:, members] = peer_mean.div(own_vol.loc[:, members])

    return output.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class PeerEchoCashqualityContrarian(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "peer_echo_cashquality_contrarian"
    name = "Peer-Echo Cash-Quality Contrarian"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Fresh headline-surprise versus cash-conversion conflicts are traded only "
        "when leave-self-out liquid industry leaders reinforce the headline's "
        "direction, identifying an extrapolative peer echo."
    )
    window_length = 378
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "cashConversionCycle",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].astype(float)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].astype(float)
        cash_cycle = data["cashConversionCycle"].astype(float)

        eps_event = _update_mask(eps_surprise)
        revenue_event = _update_mask(revenue_surprise)
        headline_event = eps_event | revenue_event
        cash_event = _update_mask(cash_cycle)

        eps_z = _robust_cs_zscore(eps_surprise)
        revenue_z = _robust_cs_zscore(revenue_surprise)
        count = eps_z.notna().astype(float) + revenue_z.notna().astype(float)
        headline = (eps_z.fillna(0.0) + revenue_z.fillna(0.0)).div(
            count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        # A decline in the cash-conversion cycle is an improvement in realization.
        cash_quality = -_event_change_quality(cash_cycle, cash_event)
        opposition = (-np.sign(headline) * cash_quality).clip(lower=0.0)
        fundamental_conflict = -headline * opposition

        peer_impulse = _liquid_peer_impulse(
            close,
            data["volume"].astype(float),
            data["industry"],
        )
        headline_concordance = peer_impulse.mul(np.sign(headline))
        echo_strength = headline_concordance.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).div(3.0)

        active = headline_event & cash_event & headline.notna() & cash_quality.notna()
        signal = (fundamental_conflict * echo_strength).where(active, 0.0)
        return signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).reindex(
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

programs.trading_idea: A reported earnings or revenue surprise can be mispriced when it conflicts with the contemporaneous change in cash conversion: weak headlines with improving cash realization and strong headlines with worsening realization are particularly vulnerable to reversal. The child factor activates this conflict only when liquid industry peers are moving in the headline-consistent direction, indicating that peer read-through and momentum traders are reinforcing the salient narrative rather than evaluating its accounting quality. This interaction creates a short-horizon edge neither parent has alone: cash-cycle disagreement identifies the hidden fundamental contradiction, while leader-peer confirmation identifies when the market has most aggressively extrapolated the wrong headline.
programs.description: On fresh surprise and cash-conversion updates, compute the signed contradiction between standardized headline news and cash-cycle improvement. Scale it by a leave-self-out, liquidity-weighted industry-leader return impulse only when that peer impulse agrees with the headline direction.

"""The revised mechanism is cross-sectional underreaction rather than an ambiguous volume-contraction interpretation. Stocks with strong, risk-adjusted intermediate returns relative to sector peers may continue to outperform because investors and analysts update valuations gradually and because relative-performance information diffuses more slowly than broad sector or market news. Skipping the most recent bar avoids defining the signal from the same very-short-run price pressure that can reverse over the next few days."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_percentile_rank(
    quality: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rank eligible quality scores within static sector groups at each date."""
    labels = sector.ffill().bfill().iloc[0]
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=quality.index, columns=quality.columns)

    known_labels = labels[labels.notna()]
    for label in pd.unique(known_labels):
        columns = labels.index[labels == label]
        group_quality = quality.loc[:, columns]
        group_count = group_quality.notna().sum(axis=1)
        group_rank = group_quality.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        result.loc[:, columns] = group_rank.where(group_count >= 5, np.nan)

    return result


@register_factor
class SectorRelativeIntermediateMomentum(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-relative, volatility-normalized lagged intermediate momentum."""

    factor_id = "sector_relative_intermediate_momentum"
    name = "Sector-Relative Lagged Momentum"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Within-sector percentile rank of a stock's lagged 10-bar log return, "
        "normalized by its trailing 10-bar return volatility and restricted to "
        "liquid, sufficiently large names."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        finite_close = pd.DataFrame(
            np.isfinite(close.to_numpy(dtype=float)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        valid_close = finite_close & (close > 0.0)
        safe_close = close.where(valid_close)

        # This t-2 to t-12 endpoint return deliberately excludes the latest
        # two bars, avoiding very-short-run price pressure in the signal.
        log_close = np.log(safe_close)
        lagged_return = log_close.shift(2) - log_close.shift(12)

        one_bar_log_return = log_close.diff()
        volatility = (
            one_bar_log_return.rolling(10, min_periods=10).std(ddof=1).shift(2)
        )
        volatility_floor = 0.005 * np.sqrt(10.0)
        risk_scale = (volatility * np.sqrt(10.0)).clip(lower=volatility_floor)
        quality = lagged_return / risk_scale
        quality = quality.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # Require every close from t-12 through t to be observed and positive.
        close_history_count = valid_close.astype(float).rolling(
            13, min_periods=13
        ).sum()
        complete_close_history = close_history_count == 13.0

        finite_volume = pd.DataFrame(
            np.isfinite(volume.to_numpy(dtype=float)),
            index=volume.index,
            columns=volume.columns,
        )
        valid_volume = finite_volume & (volume >= 0.0)
        dollar_volume = close * volume
        finite_dollar_volume = pd.DataFrame(
            np.isfinite(dollar_volume.to_numpy(dtype=float)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        valid_dollar_volume = valid_close & valid_volume & finite_dollar_volume
        observed_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.where(valid_dollar_volume)

        valid_dollar_count = valid_dollar_volume.astype(float).rolling(
            21, min_periods=21
        ).sum()
        dollar_volume_sum = observed_dollar_volume.rolling(
            21, min_periods=1
        ).sum()
        mean_dollar_volume = dollar_volume_sum / valid_dollar_count.replace(
            0.0, np.nan
        )
        liquid = (valid_dollar_count >= 18.0) & (mean_dollar_volume >= 1_000_000.0)

        finite_market_cap = pd.DataFrame(
            np.isfinite(market_cap.to_numpy(dtype=float)),
            index=market_cap.index,
            columns=market_cap.columns,
        )
        sufficiently_large = finite_market_cap & (market_cap >= 100_000_000.0)

        eligible = complete_close_history & liquid & sufficiently_large
        eligible_quality = quality.where(eligible)
        sector_rank = _sector_percentile_rank(eligible_quality, sector)
        return (sector_rank - 0.5).astype(float)
programs.name: Sector-Relative Lagged Momentum
programs.trading_idea: The revised mechanism is cross-sectional underreaction rather than an ambiguous volume-contraction interpretation. Stocks with strong, risk-adjusted intermediate returns relative to sector peers may continue to outperform because investors and analysts update valuations gradually and because relative-performance information diffuses more slowly than broad sector or market news. Skipping the most recent bar avoids defining the signal from the same very-short-run price pressure that can reverse over the next few days.
programs.description: At the end of daily bar t, use only closes through t to compute each stock's lagged 10-bar log return R_i,t = log(close[t-2] / close[t-12]). Compute sigma_i,t as the sample standard deviation of the ten one-bar log returns from t-12 to t-2, and form Q_i,t = R_i,t / max(sigma_i,t * sqrt(10), 0.005 * sqrt(10)). Eligible stocks must have positive valid closes for t-12 through t, at least 18 valid observations of close*volume over t-20 through t, mean 21-bar dollar volume of at least USD 1,000,000, and positive marketCap of at least USD 100,000,000 at t. Within each sector, assign Q a percentile rank among eligible names; the tradable score is percentile_rank(Q within sector) minus 0.5, with sectors having fewer than five eligible names assigned NaN. All quantities are evaluated after bar t closes, and no future spike, completed pattern, high/low range, or subsequent volume behavior is selected or confirmed. Missing or nonpositive closes, invalid volume, and zero/undefined volatility make the name ineligible; the fixed volatility floor prevents near-zero-volatility names from dominating. Gaps are not separately classified: they enter only through observed close-to-close returns, while open, high, and low are deliberately unused. There is no market-shock exclusion because no market-index field is available; sector-relative ranking removes common sector direction but does not claim to identify or avoid market-wide shocks. This is distinct from the listed in-book volume/return continuation factors because it contains no abnormal-volume measure, volume-decay condition, signed volume-return interaction, intrabar close-location statistic, range compression, event gate, or inferred liquidity/absorption state; operationally it is solely a sector-relative, volatility-normalized, lagged-return ranking.

"""Sector-relative price/fundamental disagreement catch-up factor.

Mechanism: peer-relative price trends that conflict with a firm's cash-realization
and revenue-expectation state are more likely to be temporary extrapolation than
information. Improving cash fundamentals in a sector laggard support catch-up,
while deteriorating cash fundamentals in a sector leader support repricing down.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_rank(value: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank within static sector groups."""
    labels = sector.ffill().bfill().iloc[0]
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=value.index, columns=value.columns)
    valid_labels = labels.dropna()

    for label in pd.unique(valid_labels):
        members = labels.index[labels == label]
        group = value.loc[:, members]
        count = group.notna().sum(axis=1)
        ranked = group.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        result.loc[:, members] = ranked.where(count >= 5)

    return result


def _finite(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return df.astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class SectorCashDisagreementCatchup(BaseFactor):
    """Trade price/fundamental disagreement among sector peers."""

    factor_id = "sector_cash_disagreement_catchup"
    name = "Sector Cash-Disagreement Catch-Up"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks sector-relative cash and revenue-state improvement among stocks whose "
        "lagged sector-relative momentum disagrees with that fundamental state; long "
        "improving laggards and short deteriorating leaders."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "sector",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "netIncome",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _finite(data["close"])
        volume = _finite(data["volume"])
        market_cap = _finite(data["marketCap"])
        cash_flow = _finite(data["operatingCashFlow"])
        net_income = _finite(data["netIncome"])
        revenue_estimate = _finite(data["revenueEstimate"])
        sector = data["sector"]

        valid_close = close.gt(0.0)
        log_close = np.log(close.where(valid_close))
        lagged_return = log_close.shift(2) - log_close.shift(12)
        return_vol = log_close.diff().rolling(10, min_periods=10).std().shift(2)
        risk_adjusted_momentum = lagged_return / return_vol.clip(lower=0.005)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(valid_close & volume.gt(0.0))
        mean_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(21, min_periods=15).mean()
        liquid = mean_dollar_volume.ge(1_000_000.0)

        prior_cash_flow = cash_flow.shift(63)
        prior_income = net_income.shift(63)
        prior_revenue_estimate = revenue_estimate.shift(63)
        cash_conversion = cash_flow / net_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_conversion = prior_cash_flow / prior_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        cash_change = cash_conversion - prior_conversion
        revenue_revision = (
            revenue_estimate - prior_revenue_estimate
        ) / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        eligible = (
            valid_close
            & market_cap.ge(100_000_000.0)
            & liquid
            & risk_adjusted_momentum.notna()
            & cash_change.notna()
            & revenue_revision.notna()
        )

        momentum_rank = _sector_rank(risk_adjusted_momentum.where(eligible), sector)
        cash_rank = _sector_rank(cash_change.where(eligible), sector)
        revenue_rank = _sector_rank(revenue_revision.where(eligible), sector)

        momentum_state = momentum_rank - 0.5
        fundamental_state = ((cash_rank - 0.5) + (revenue_rank - 0.5)) / 2.0
        disagreement = momentum_state * fundamental_state < 0.0

        raw_score = (
            fundamental_state * momentum_state.abs()
        ).where(disagreement & fundamental_state.notna() & momentum_state.notna())

        output = raw_score.rank(axis=1, pct=True).sub(0.5)
        return output.where(raw_score.notna(), 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Sector Cash-Disagreement Catch-Up
programs.trading_idea: Sector-relative intermediate winners are not automatically continuation candidates at a six-bar horizon: the parent evidence suggests that recently successful relative-price narratives can become extrapolated when operating cash evidence fails to validate them. This child trades the interaction rather than either signal alone: it buys sector-relative laggards whose cash conversion and revenue-estimate state are improving, and shorts sector-relative leaders whose cash conversion and revenue-estimate state are deteriorating. The edge comes from identifying a temporary disagreement between slowly updated fundamental evidence and already-extended peer-relative prices, creating a catch-up/repricing channel that pure momentum and cash-state signals cannot isolate.
programs.description: Computes sector-relative lagged, volatility-normalized momentum and a sector-relative cash-conversion plus revenue-estimate state. It activates only when the price trend and fundamental state disagree, ranking fundamentally improving laggards above fundamentally weakening leaders.
