"""Cash-verified industry earnings-news diffusion to non-reporting peers.

Mechanism: an industry surprise is more informative for unreported peers when the
reporters' earnings surprise is corroborated by improving cash conversion in the
same direction.  Cash confirmation filters headline EPS narratives that are more
likely to reverse before peer fundamentals can be assimilated.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_coherent_events(
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    reporter_score: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast coherent same-day industry reporter scores to all constituents.

    An industry event needs two reporters and a two-thirds sign consensus.  Each
    row is computed independently, hence uses only information available that day.
    """
    values = np.full(reporter_score.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)

    for row_num in range(len(reporter_score.index)):
        labels = industry.iloc[row_num]
        scores = reporter_score.iloc[row_num]
        observations = pd.DataFrame({"industry": labels, "score": scores}).dropna()
        if observations.empty:
            continue

        observations["positive"] = (observations["score"] > 0.0).astype(float)
        observations["negative"] = (observations["score"] < 0.0).astype(float)
        grouped = observations.groupby("industry").agg(
            count=("score", "count"),
            mean_score=("score", "mean"),
            positive=("positive", "sum"),
            negative=("negative", "sum"),
        )
        coherent = (
            (grouped["count"] >= 2.0)
            & (
                (grouped["positive"] / grouped["count"] >= 2.0 / 3.0)
                | (grouped["negative"] / grouped["count"] >= 2.0 / 3.0)
            )
        )
        valid_scores = grouped.loc[coherent, "mean_score"]
        if not valid_scores.empty:
            values[row_num, :] = labels.map(valid_scores).to_numpy(dtype=float)

    return pd.DataFrame(values, index=reporter_score.index, columns=reporter_score.columns)


@register_factor
class CashVerifiedPeerSurpriseDiffusion(BaseFactor):
    """Propagate cash-validated industry surprise information to delayed peers."""

    factor_id = "cash_verified_peer_surprise_diffusion_delay"
    name = "Cash-Verified Peer Surprise Diffusion"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks non-reporting firms by a decayed, coherent same-industry earnings "
        "and revenue surprise whose sign is validated by reporters' cash-conversion "
        "change."
    )
    window_length = 69
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "netIncome",
        "operatingCashFlow",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        industry = data["industry"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        eps_est = data["epsEstimate"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        rev_est = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        rev_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        income = data["netIncome"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        cashflow = data["operatingCashFlow"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        prior_eps = eps_surprise.shift(1)
        prior_rev = rev_surprise.shift(1)
        eps_event = eps_surprise.notna() & (prior_eps.isna() | eps_surprise.ne(prior_eps))
        rev_event = rev_surprise.notna() & (prior_rev.isna() | rev_surprise.ne(prior_rev))
        report_event = eps_event | rev_event

        eps_component = (eps_surprise / eps_est.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        rev_component = (
            4.0 * rev_surprise / rev_est.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        surprise_count = eps_component.notna().astype(float) + rev_component.notna().astype(float)
        signed_surprise = (eps_component.fillna(0.0) + rev_component.fillna(0.0)).div(
            surprise_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        conversion = cashflow / income.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        conversion_change = (conversion - conversion.shift(63)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        cash_alignment = np.tanh(2.0 * conversion_change)

        # A positive surprise needs improving conversion; a negative surprise needs
        # worsening conversion.  Reliability remains bounded in [0, 1].
        surprise_sign = np.sign(signed_surprise)
        reliability = 0.5 * (1.0 + surprise_sign * cash_alignment)
        reporter_score = (signed_surprise * reliability).where(
            report_event
            & signed_surprise.notna()
            & conversion_change.notna()
            & industry.notna()
        )

        industry_event = _industry_coherent_events(industry, reporter_score)
        carried_event = industry_event.fillna(0.0).ewm(
            halflife=2.0, adjust=False, min_periods=1
        ).mean()

        own_report_blackout = report_event.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum().eq(0.0)
        eligible = own_report_blackout & industry.notna()
        raw_signal = carried_event.where(eligible)
        ranked = 2.0 * raw_signal.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        return ranked.where(eligible, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Cash-Verified Peer Surprise Diffusion
programs.trading_idea: Industry earnings surprises should propagate to unreported peers only when the reporters' earnings news is corroborated by improving cash conversion, because cash-backed surprises are more likely to reveal genuine common demand rather than accounting timing or headline extrapolation. The interaction separates credible peer information from the cash-unconfirmed narratives that Parent B identifies as prone to reversal, while retaining Parent A's cross-firm information-diffusion channel. This should create a more persistent six-bar receiver signal: long non-reporting peers after cash-verified positive industry disclosures and short them after cash-verified negative disclosures.
programs.description: The factor forms fresh reporter-level EPS/revenue surprise scores, scales each by whether the direction of the surprise agrees with the reporter's quarter-over-quarter operating-cash-flow conversion change, and aggregates coherent signals within industry. It exponentially carries the industry impulse to peers that have not themselves reported in the prior six bars, then cross-sectionally ranks the signed receiver signal.

programs.code:
"""This is a deliberately narrow proxy for the imbalance of recently transacted volume above versus below the current price, rather than a claim to observe the outstanding shareholder cost basis. A large recent above-price volume imbalance identifies a potential short-horizon downside-liquidity asymmetry: a further decline can activate stop-loss, margin, tax-loss, and adverse-selection selling among recently established positions, consistent with asymmetric excitation of downward orders. The hypothesis predicts lower subsequent six-bar returns for stocks with more decayed volume above the current close, conditional on cross-sectional ranking; it should be evaluated jointly with subsequent volume, downside volatility, and price impact rather than interpreted solely as a disposition-effect test."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _decayed_reference_price_skew(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int = 60,
    half_life: float = 20.0,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally aggregate decayed volume whose bar reference price is above/below close."""
    above = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    below = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    current_valid = close.notna() & np.isfinite(close) & close.gt(0.0)
    decay_rate = np.log(2.0) / half_life

    for lag in range(lookback):
        bar_high = high.shift(lag)
        bar_low = low.shift(lag)
        bar_close = close.shift(lag)
        bar_volume = volume.shift(lag)
        reference_price = (bar_high + bar_low + bar_close) / 3.0

        valid = (
            current_valid
            & bar_volume.notna()
            & np.isfinite(bar_volume)
            & bar_volume.gt(0.0)
            & reference_price.notna()
            & np.isfinite(reference_price)
            & reference_price.gt(0.0)
        )
        weighted_volume = bar_volume * np.exp(-decay_rate * lag)
        above = above + weighted_volume.where(
            valid & reference_price.gt(close), 0.0
        )
        below = below + weighted_volume.where(
            valid & reference_price.lt(close), 0.0
        )

    total = above + below
    return ((above - below) / total.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(total.gt(0.0))


@register_factor
class DecayedVolumeReferencePriceSkew(BaseFactor):
    """Negative ranked skew of decayed volume transacted above current close."""

    factor_id = "prospect_costbasis_supply_skew"
    name = "Decayed Volume Reference-Price Skew"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "At each close, computes a 60-bar, 20-bar-half-life volume imbalance "
        "between reference-price volume above and below the current close, then "
        "negates its cross-sectional percentile rank."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        skew = _decayed_reference_price_skew(
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["close"],
            data["volume"],
        )
        rank_pct = skew.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True)
        return -(rank_pct - 0.5)
programs.name: Decayed Volume Reference-Price Skew
programs.trading_idea: This is a deliberately narrow proxy for the imbalance of recently transacted volume above versus below the current price, rather than a claim to observe the outstanding shareholder cost basis. A large recent above-price volume imbalance identifies a potential short-horizon downside-liquidity asymmetry: a further decline can activate stop-loss, margin, tax-loss, and adverse-selection selling among recently established positions, consistent with asymmetric excitation of downward orders. The hypothesis predicts lower subsequent six-bar returns for stocks with more decayed volume above the current close, conditional on cross-sectional ranking; it should be evaluated jointly with subsequent volume, downside volatility, and price impact rather than interpreted solely as a disposition-effect test.
programs.description: At close t, use exactly the 60 completed daily bars t-59 through t, inclusive, and compute only from OHLCV available through close t; execution is no earlier than the open of t+1. For each lag k in {0,...,59}, assign decay weight w_k = exp(-ln(2)*k/20), corresponding to a fixed 20-bar half-life. Define bar price p_(t-k) = (high_(t-k) + low_(t-k) + close_(t-k))/3. For each ticker, retain an observation only when volume_(t-k) is finite and strictly positive, p_(t-k) is finite and strictly positive, and close_t is finite and strictly positive; otherwise its contribution is zero. Using the feed's supplied OHLC prices as-is (including its corporate-action treatment), classify each retained bar before normalization: above-volume A_t = sum[w_k*volume_(t-k)*1(p_(t-k)>close_t)], below-volume B_t = sum[w_k*volume_(t-k)*1(p_(t-k)<close_t)], and equal-price volume receives zero weight in both legs. Form the bounded skew S_t = (A_t-B_t)/(A_t+B_t) only if A_t+B_t>0, otherwise NaN. Cross-sectionally rank S_t among finite observations at t using ascending percentile rank, then center it as score_t = rank_pct(S_t)-0.5; no range, return-shock, volatility, sector, or liquidity attenuation is applied. The tradable factor is -score_t, so stocks with disproportionately recent volume transacted above the current close receive more-negative expected-return scores.

programs.code:
"""A downward traverse through a historically high-turnover price region is treated not as a literal investor inventory ledger, but as a public reference-price breach that can coincide with one-sided liquidity demand and reduced displayed-liquidity resilience. The negative-return prediction is restricted to breaches completed with unusually high trading volume and a close near the bar low, conditions consistent with unresolved sell-side pressure rather than an intraday dip that was absorbed. Because a breach can also mark selling exhaustion and support, this is explicitly an incremental conditional activation signal whose sign and value must be tested after controlling for the existing prospect_costbasis_supply_skew factor."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _barrier_activation(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute a causal, exponentially decayed volume-at-price breach signal."""
    close_values = close.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    high_values = high.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    low_values = low.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    volume_values = volume.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)

    n_rows, n_cols = close_values.shape
    output = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    typical_price = (high_values + low_values + close_values) / 3.0

    # At t, observations t-126 through t-1 have ages 126 through 1.
    ages = np.arange(126, 0, -1, dtype=float)
    decay = np.exp(-np.log(2.0) * ages / 21.0)[:, None]

    prior_volume = (
        volume.shift(1)
        .rolling(20, min_periods=20)
        .mean()
        .to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    )
    epsilon = 1.0e-12

    for t in range(126, n_rows):
        previous_close = close_values[t - 1]
        current_close = close_values[t]
        current_high = high_values[t]
        current_low = low_values[t]
        current_volume = volume_values[t]
        average_volume = prior_volume[t]

        width = 0.005 * previous_close
        hist_tp = typical_price[t - 126 : t]
        hist_volume = volume_values[t - 126 : t]

        valid_width = np.isfinite(width) & (width > 0.0)
        valid_history = (
            np.isfinite(hist_tp)
            & np.isfinite(hist_volume)
            & (hist_volume >= 0.0)
            & valid_width[None, :]
        )
        weighted_volume = np.where(valid_history, hist_volume * decay, 0.0)
        total_profile = weighted_volume.sum(axis=0)

        scaled_price = np.zeros_like(hist_tp, dtype=float)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            np.divide(
                hist_tp,
                width[None, :],
                out=scaled_price,
                where=valid_history,
            )
        bin_centers = np.rint(scaled_price) * width[None, :]

        crossed_down = (
            np.isfinite(current_close)
            & np.isfinite(previous_close)
            & (current_close < previous_close)
        )
        crossed_bins = (
            valid_history
            & (bin_centers >= current_close[None, :])
            & (bin_centers < previous_close[None, :])
            & crossed_down[None, :]
        )
        crossed_mass = np.where(crossed_bins, weighted_volume, 0.0).sum(axis=0)

        bar_range = current_high - current_low
        valid_range = np.isfinite(bar_range) & (bar_range > 0.0)
        close_location = np.full(n_cols, 0.5, dtype=float)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            np.divide(
                current_high - current_close,
                bar_range,
                out=close_location,
                where=valid_range,
            )
        close_location = np.clip(close_location, 0.0, 1.0)

        relative_volume = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
        valid_average = np.isfinite(average_volume) & (average_volume >= 0.0)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            np.divide(
                current_volume,
                average_volume + epsilon,
                out=relative_volume,
                where=np.isfinite(current_volume) & valid_average,
            )
        relative_volume = np.minimum(np.maximum(relative_volume, 0.0), 5.0)

        eligible = (
            valid_width
            & np.isfinite(current_close)
            & np.isfinite(previous_close)
            & np.isfinite(current_high)
            & np.isfinite(current_low)
            & np.isfinite(current_volume)
            & valid_average
            & (total_profile > epsilon)
        )
        activation = np.full(n_cols, np.nan, dtype=float)
        activation[eligible] = (
            crossed_mass[eligible]
            / (total_profile[eligible] + epsilon)
            * relative_volume[eligible]
            * close_location[eligible]
        )
        output[t] = activation

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)


@register_factor
class FreshCostbasisBarrierActivation(BaseFactor):
    """Negative ranked activation of high-turnover reference-price breaches."""

    factor_id = "fresh_costbasis_barrier_activation"
    name = "Residual Downside Barrier Activation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Negative cross-sectional rank of a causal 126-bar exponentially "
        "decayed volume-at-price barrier breach, activated only by high "
        "relative volume and closes near the daily low."
    )
    window_length = 127
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        activation = _barrier_activation(
            close,
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["volume"],
        )

        lower = activation.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = activation.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        winsorized = activation.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        score = -rank(winsorized)
        return score.where(activation.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)

programs.code:
"""A large close-to-close decline accompanied by abnormally high trading participation is treated as confirmed asymmetric downward order pressure, rather than as an inferred low-volume liquidity vacuum. High relative volume makes the move more consistent with active repricing, institutional de-risking, or information-driven selling that may take several sessions to complete. The signal is made idiosyncratic by removing the contemporaneous equal-weight industry-average pressure score, so it does not simply short broad industry selloffs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _winsorize_cross_section(
    score: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize eligible scores independently on each date."""
    masked = score.where(eligible)
    lower = masked.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = masked.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _industry_residual(
    score: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove same-date industry means only for groups with five valid names."""
    labels = industry.iloc[0].copy()
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "__MISSING_INDUSTRY__")

    residual = score.copy()
    for label in pd.unique(labels):
        columns = labels.index[labels == label]
        group_score = score.loc[:, columns]
        group_eligible = eligible.loc[:, columns]

        valid_count = group_eligible.sum(axis=1)
        group_mean = group_score.where(group_eligible).mean(axis=1)
        demeaned = group_score.sub(group_mean, axis=0)
        use_demeaned = (valid_count >= 5).astype(float)

        adjusted = (
            demeaned.mul(use_demeaned, axis=0)
            + group_score.mul(1.0 - use_demeaned, axis=0)
        )
        residual.loc[:, columns] = adjusted

    return residual


@register_factor
class IdioDownsidePressureConfirmation(BaseFactor):
    """Short idiosyncratic, high-volume downside pressure after confirmed selling."""

    factor_id = "idio_downside_pressure_confirmation"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Downside Pressure Confirmation"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Negative cross-sectional exposure to stocks with unusually large "
        "close-to-close declines confirmed by positive abnormal volume, after "
        "removing contemporaneous industry-average downside pressure."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_close = (close > 0.0) & (previous_close > 0.0)
        log_return = np.log(
            close.where(close > 0.0) / previous_close.where(previous_close > 0.0)
        ).where(valid_close)

        prior_abs_return = log_return.abs().shift(1)
        return_count = prior_abs_return.rolling(20, min_periods=20).count()
        return_median = prior_abs_return.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        valid_return_history = (return_count == 20) & (return_median > 0.0)

        downside = (-log_return).clip(lower=0.0)
        downside_shock = (downside / return_median).clip(upper=5.0)

        positive_prior_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0).shift(1)
        volume_count = positive_prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).count()
        volume_median = positive_prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        valid_volume_history = (volume_count == 20) & (volume_median > 0.0)

        log_relative_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume > 0.0) / volume_median)
        participation = log_relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

        eligible = (
            valid_close
            & valid_return_history
            & valid_volume_history
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & downside_shock.notna()
            & participation.notna()
        )

        raw_pressure = (downside_shock * participation).where(eligible)
        winsorized_pressure = _winsorize_cross_section(raw_pressure, eligible)
        residual = _industry_residual(
            winsorized_pressure, eligible, data["industry"]
        ).where(eligible)

        return (-rank(residual)).where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A large close-to-close decline accompanied by abnormally high trading participation is treated as confirmed asymmetric downward order pressure, rather than as an inferred low-volume liquidity vacuum. High relative volume makes the move more consistent with active repricing, institutional de-risking, or information-driven selling that may take several sessions to complete. The signal is made idiosyncratic by removing the contemporaneous equal-weight industry-average pressure score, so it does not simply short broad industry selloffs.
programs.description: After bar t closes, compute r_t = log(close_t / close_{t-1}). Define downside shock D_t = min(5, max(-r_t, 0) / median(|r_{t-20}|,...,|r_{t-1}|)); require 20 valid prior return observations and a strictly positive denominator. Define participation confirmation P_t = min(3, max(log(volume_t / median(volume_{t-20},...,volume_{t-1})), 0)); require 20 valid positive prior-volume observations. The raw pressure score is S_t = D_t * P_t, so an ordinary-volume or below-normal-volume decline receives zero confirmation. Cross-sectionally winsorize S_t at the eligible-universe 1st and 99th percentiles, subtract the contemporaneous equal-weight mean score of the stock's industry when that industry has at least 5 eligible names, then percentile-rank the resulting industry residual across all eligible stocks. Take negative exposure to the highest-ranked residuals. The signal is formed only after the complete daily bar, including close and volume, is known and is executed no earlier than the next executable bar. Formula-level distinction from range_volume_elasticity_breakout: this construction uses only close-to-close downside returns and positive abnormal-volume confirmation; it contains no intraday range, range-to-volume elasticity ratio, weak-volume condition, or inferred liquidity-withdrawal measure.

"""This is a narrowly defined short-horizon reversal signal, not a direct measure of liquidity-provider inventory or forced selling. A stock that experiences an unusually high-volume negative daily return but closes materially above its intraday low has partially reversed its same-day downside move; conditional on the selloff and abnormal participation, this geometry may identify temporary price pressure whose residual component mean-reverts over the next six sessions. The factor uses only the downside-rejection leg because upside fades need not be economically symmetric under short-sale constraints and asymmetric incorporation of bad news."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _winsorized_cross_sectional_rank(
    raw_signal: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize each date at valid 2nd/98th-percentile values, then rank."""
    lower = raw_signal.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
    upper = raw_signal.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
    winsorized = raw_signal.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    return rank(winsorized)


@register_factor
class DownsideTailAbsorptionReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks high-volume downside bars that reject their intraday lows."""

    factor_id = "downside_tail_absorption_reversal"
    name = "High-Volume Downside Rejection Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of abnormal-volume negative-return bars that "
        "close well above their intraday lows, identifying temporary downside "
        "price pressure expected to reverse over the next six sessions."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        daily_return = close / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0

        bar_range = high - low
        lower_tail_rejection = (close - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # Shift first so the current bar's participation cannot enter its own
        # abnormal-volume benchmark.
        prior_mean_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        relative_volume = volume / prior_mean_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        required_valid = (
            close.notna()
            & previous_close.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & volume.notna()
            & (bar_range > 0.0)
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & prior_mean_volume.notna()
            & (prior_mean_volume > 0.0)
        )

        downside_pressure = (-daily_return).clip(lower=0.0)
        raw_downside = (
            downside_pressure
            * lower_tail_rejection
            * np.log1p(relative_volume)
        )

        # Non-negative-return bars are valid observations but carry no
        # downside-pressure signal; malformed or unavailable observations are
        # retained as NaN and therefore excluded from the cross section.
        raw_signal = raw_downside.where(daily_return < 0.0, 0.0)
        raw_signal = raw_signal.where(required_valid)

        return _winsorized_cross_sectional_rank(raw_signal)

A stock that experiences an unusually high-volume negative daily return but closes materially above its intraday low has partially reversed its same-day downside move; conditional on the selloff and abnormal participation, this geometry may identify temporary price pressure whose residual component mean-reverts over the next six sessions. The factor uses only the downside-rejection leg because upside fades need not be economically symmetric under short-sale constraints and asymmetric incorporation of bad news.

Compute relative volume RV_t = volume_t / mean(volume_{t-20:t-1}), requiring a strictly positive 20-prior-bar mean volume and setting the observation to NaN otherwise; current-day volume is excluded from the denominator. Define downside pressure D_t = max(-r_t, 0). The raw signal is S_t = D_t * L_t * log(1 + RV_t), with S_t set to zero when r_t >= 0, volume_t <= 0, or any required input is missing. Each day, winsorize valid raw signals cross-sectionally at the 2nd and 98th percentiles, then convert them to a cross-sectional percentile rank on [0,1]; missing or invalid observations remain NaN and are not traded. No discretionary news or fundamental-disclosure exclusion is applied because no comprehensive news field is available in scope.

programs.code:
"""Narrative overhang activation: fragile earnings optimism meets loss-triggered supply.

Mechanism: an EPS-revision narrative with weak cash and revenue confirmation is
most vulnerable when decayed traded volume lies above the current price.  That
reference-price overhang supplies a nonlinear selling channel, making the
fundamental-attention correction faster than either signal alone.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _numeric(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Preserve panel alignment while making invalid numeric observations missing."""
    return df.astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _centered_rank(value: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional robust percentile rank, centered at zero."""
    masked = value.where(eligible).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lo = masked.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    hi = masked.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    clipped = masked.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)
    return clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True).sub(0.5)


def _decayed_above_price_overhang(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int = 45,
    half_life: float = 15.0,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal fraction of decayed reference-price volume above today's close."""
    above = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    below = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    valid_now = close.notna() & np.isfinite(close) & close.gt(0.0)
    decay = np.log(2.0) / half_life

    for lag in range(lookback):
        ref = (high.shift(lag) + low.shift(lag) + close.shift(lag)) / 3.0
        vol = volume.shift(lag)
        valid = (
            valid_now
            & ref.notna()
            & np.isfinite(ref)
            & ref.gt(0.0)
            & vol.notna()
            & np.isfinite(vol)
            & vol.gt(0.0)
        )
        weighted = vol * np.exp(-decay * lag)
        above = above + weighted.where(valid & ref.gt(close), 0.0)
        below = below + weighted.where(valid & ref.lt(close), 0.0)

    total = above + below
    return ((above - below) / total.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(total.gt(0.0))


@register_factor
class NarrativeCostbasisOverhangActivation(BaseFactor):
    """Short fragile EPS narratives only when loss-triggered supply is available."""

    factor_id = "narrative_costbasis_overhang_activation"
    name = "Narrative Cost-Basis Overhang Activation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks cash-unconfirmed and expensive EPS extrapolation, then activates "
        "that bearish narrative only for stocks with decayed traded-volume "
        "reference prices concentrated above the current close."
    )
    window_length = 108
    inputs = [
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "evToSales",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "netIncome",
        "operatingCashFlow",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _numeric(data["close"])
        high = _numeric(data["high"])
        low = _numeric(data["low"])
        volume = _numeric(data["volume"])
        market_cap = _numeric(data["marketCap"])
        ev_sales = _numeric(data["evToSales"])
        eps_est = _numeric(data["epsEstimate"])
        revenue_est = _numeric(data["revenueEstimate"])
        income = _numeric(data["netIncome"])
        cash_flow = _numeric(data["operatingCashFlow"])

        close_1 = close.shift(1)
        close_5 = close.shift(5)
        eps_63 = eps_est.shift(63)
        revenue_63 = revenue_est.shift(63)
        income_63 = income.shift(63)
        cash_63 = cash_flow.shift(63)

        eligible = (
            close.gt(5.0)
            & close_1.gt(0.0)
            & close_5.gt(0.0)
            & market_cap.gt(0.0)
            & ev_sales.gt(0.0)
            & eps_est.notna()
            & eps_63.notna()
            & revenue_est.notna()
            & revenue_63.notna()
            & income.gt(0.0)
            & income_63.gt(0.0)
            & cash_flow.notna()
            & cash_63.notna()
        )

        eps_revision = (eps_est - eps_63) / close_1.where(close_1.gt(0.0))
        revenue_revision = (revenue_est - revenue_63) / market_cap
        cash_conversion_change = cash_flow / income - cash_63 / income_63
        recent_reaction = np.log(close / close_5.where(close_5.gt(0.0)))
        valuation = np.log(ev_sales)

        narrative = (
            _centered_rank(eps_revision, eligible)
            - _centered_rank(revenue_revision, eligible)
            - _centered_rank(cash_conversion_change, eligible)
            + _centered_rank(recent_reaction, eligible)
            + _centered_rank(valuation, eligible)
        ) / 5.0

        overhang_raw = _decayed_above_price_overhang(high, low, close, volume)
        overhang = _centered_rank(overhang_raw, eligible)

        activation = narrative.clip(lower=0.0) * overhang.clip(lower=0.0)
        return activation.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)

programs.trading_idea: Cash-unconfirmed EPS optimism is normally corrected gradually because investors overweight the salient earnings-revision narrative relative to weak revenue confirmation and deteriorating cash conversion. The correction becomes faster when recent volume is concentrated above the current price: these optimistic holders are simultaneously sitting on losses, so a modest decline can activate stop-loss and adverse-selection selling. Neither parent alone identifies this state-dependent acceleration: the narrative signal identifies vulnerable beliefs, while the volume-reference skew identifies the mechanical supply channel that converts vulnerability into a six-bar repricing.
programs.description: Computes a cross-sectional cash-unconfirmed EPS-extrapolation score and multiplies its positive tail by a decayed volume-reference-price overhang score. High values identify expensive, recently appreciated EPS-upgrade narratives with weak cash/revenue confirmation whose recent buyers are predominantly above water only at higher prices.

"""The revised mechanism is not an attempt to identify a particular scheduled seller from daily data. It instead targets an observable asymmetric downside-liquidity state: several increasingly active negative-return bars are followed by materially lower downside price impact per unit of abnormal participation, then by a modest positive close while turnover remains elevated. This pattern is consistent with sell-side pressure becoming less price-effective as liquidity is replenished, but the portfolio is deliberately one-sided on the alpha leg because upside execution and downside liquidation need not be symmetric."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_matched_weights(
    selected_longs: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    qualifying: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Create equal-weight longs and sector-matched equal-dollar financing shorts."""
    sector_valid = sector.notna()
    short_pool = eligible & (~qualifying) & sector_valid
    preliminary_longs = selected_longs & sector_valid

    # For each name, count long and short candidates sharing its same-day sector.
    # Sector is static in this feed, but this remains valid if labels are sparse.
    short_sector_count = pd.DataFrame(
        0.0, index=sector.index, columns=sector.columns
    )
    for ticker in sector.columns:
        same_sector = sector.eq(sector[ticker], axis=0) & sector_valid
        short_sector_count = short_sector_count.add(
            same_sector.mul(short_pool[ticker].astype(float), axis=0), fill_value=0.0
        )

    # Do not retain an alpha leg in a sector where no eligible financing short exists.
    longs = preliminary_longs & short_sector_count.gt(0.0)

    long_sector_count = pd.DataFrame(
        0.0, index=sector.index, columns=sector.columns
    )
    for ticker in sector.columns:
        same_sector = sector.eq(sector[ticker], axis=0) & sector_valid
        long_sector_count = long_sector_count.add(
            same_sector.mul(longs[ticker].astype(float), axis=0), fill_value=0.0
        )

    n_longs = longs.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    long_weights = longs.astype(float).div(n_longs, axis=0).fillna(0.0)

    # Each sector's short gross equals that sector's long gross.  Thus the
    # aggregate financing basket is equal-dollar and sector matched, without
    # interpreting the short candidates as a symmetric reversal signal.
    sector_long_gross = long_sector_count.div(n_longs, axis=0)
    short_weights = (
        -sector_long_gross.div(short_sector_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    ).where(short_pool, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

    return (long_weights + short_weights).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class AsymmetricDownsideImpactDeceleration(BaseFactor):
    """Downside-impact deceleration followed by a bounded high-turnover reversal."""

    factor_id = "phase_space_impact_hysteresis_endpoint"
    name = "Asymmetric Downside Impact Deceleration"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Detects accelerating abnormal participation during negative innovations, "
        "declining downside impact over the next two sell bars, and a bounded "
        "high-turnover positive endpoint; qualifying longs are financed with "
        "sector-matched eligible non-qualifying shorts."
    )
    window_length = 25
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        safe_volume = volume.where(volume.ge(0.0))
        log_return = np.log(safe_close / safe_close.shift(1))

        # Both normalizers deliberately exclude the current bar.  Consequently,
        # z, participation, and impact at t use only information observable at t.
        return_std = log_return.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
        volume_mean = safe_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        dollar_volume = safe_close * safe_volume
        dollar_volume_mean = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()

        valid_std = return_std.gt(0.0)
        valid_volume = volume_mean.gt(0.0)
        z = log_return.div(return_std.where(valid_std))
        participation = safe_volume.div(volume_mean.where(valid_volume))
        impact = z.div(participation.clip(lower=0.25))

        valid_history = z.notna() & participation.notna() & dollar_volume_mean.gt(0.0)
        liquidity_cutoff = dollar_volume_mean.where(valid_history).quantile(0.30, axis=1)
        eligible = valid_history & dollar_volume_mean.gt(liquidity_cutoff, axis=0)

        a2 = participation.shift(2)
        a3 = participation.shift(3)
        a4 = participation.shift(4)
        z2 = z.shift(2)
        z3 = z.shift(3)
        z4 = z.shift(4)
        z1 = z.shift(1)
        i2 = impact.shift(2).abs()
        i3 = impact.shift(3).abs()
        i1 = impact.shift(1).abs()

        qualifying = (
            a4.lt(a3)
            & a3.lt(a2)
            & a2.ge(1.50)
            & z4.lt(0.0)
            & z3.lt(0.0)
            & z2.lt(0.0)
            & i2.le(0.65 * i3)
            & participation.shift(1).ge(1.25)
            & z1.lt(0.0)
            & i1.le(i2)
            & participation.ge(1.25)
            & z.gt(0.0)
            & z.le(1.00)
            & eligible
        ).fillna(False)

        q_participation = (a2 + participation.shift(1) + participation) / 3.0
        q_impact = 1.0 - i1.div(i3.clip(lower=0.01))
        q_reversal = z

        # Masking before rank makes every component a percentile exclusively
        # within the current day's qualifying cross-section.
        score = (
            0.50 * rank(q_participation.where(qualifying))
            + 0.30 * rank(q_impact.where(qualifying))
            + 0.20 * rank(q_reversal.where(qualifying))
        )
        selected_longs = qualifying & rank(score.where(qualifying)).ge(0.80)

        return _sector_matched_weights(
            selected_longs,
            eligible.fillna(False),
            qualifying,
            sector,
        ).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: The revised mechanism is not an attempt to identify a particular scheduled seller from daily data. It instead targets an observable asymmetric downside-liquidity state: several increasingly active negative-return bars are followed by materially lower downside price impact per unit of abnormal participation, then by a modest positive close while turnover remains elevated. This pattern is consistent with sell-side pressure becoming less price-effective as liquidity is replenished, but the portfolio is deliberately one-sided on the alpha leg because upside execution and downside liquidation need not be symmetric.
programs.description: At each current close t, define daily log return r_j = log(close_j / close_{j-1}). Define causal 20-bar return innovation z_j = r_j / std(r_{j-20},...,r_{j-1}) and causal abnormal participation a_j = volume_j / mean(volume_{j-20},...,volume_{j-1}); observations with a nonpositive denominator or missing history are excluded. Define signed impact I_j = z_j / max(a_j, 0.25), so negative I is standardized downside movement per unit of abnormal participation. Restrict the universe to names with valid 20-bar history and 20-bar average dollar volume mean(close*volume over t-20,...,t-1) above the cross-sectional 30th percentile. A name qualifies only if all ordered, current-close-observable conditions hold: (1) participation accelerates during the initial sell sequence, a_{t-4} < a_{t-3} < a_{t-2} and a_{t-2} >= 1.50; (2) the three initial bars are negative innovations, z_{t-4}, z_{t-3}, z_{t-2} < 0; (3) downside impact decelerates despite the participation increase, |I_{t-2}| <= 0.65*|I_{t-3}|; (4) selling remains active but impact weakens further on t-1, with a_{t-1} >= 1.25, z_{t-1} < 0, and |I_{t-1}| <= |I_{t-2}|; and (5) the current bar is an elevated-turnover, modest reversal, with a_t >= 1.25 and 0 < z_t <= 1.00. No later volume normalization, later reversal persistence, or future-bar confirmation is used. Among qualifying names, form Q = 0.50*rank_cs(mean(a_{t-2},a_{t-1},a_t)) + 0.30*rank_cs(1 - |I_{t-1}|/max(|I_{t-3}|,0.01)) + 0.20*rank_cs(z_t), where each rank is a same-day percentile rank among qualifying names. Go long the top 20% of qualifying names by Q, equally weighted. Finance the long book with an equal-dollar short basket of otherwise eligible non-qualifying names matched to the long book's sector weights; this short is a sector-neutral financing hedge, not a claimed mirror-image buy-program reversal signal. The distinguishing sequence is therefore accelerating participation first, declining negative impact on the next two still-negative bars, and only then a bounded current-bar positive innovation while participation remains high.

programs.code:
"""An opening gap that remains substantially unrefilled and closes at the directional end of the daily range is interpreted as evidence that opposing displayed liquidity did not replenish sufficiently during the session. With daily OHLCV data, this is not claimed to identify scheduled institutional execution or auction-specific order flow; it is a reduced-form proxy for persistent directional liquidity imbalance. The prediction is continuation when the imbalance persists over several sessions, while explicitly recognizing that information-driven repricing is an observationally similar alternative explanation."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import indneutralize, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _gap_imbalance_score(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute the causal daily unrefilled-opening-gap imbalance score."""
    previous_close = close.shift(1)
    valid_prices = (open_ > 0.0) & (previous_close > 0.0)
    gap = np.log((open_ / previous_close).where(valid_prices))
    gap_sign = np.sign(gap)

    intraday_range = high - low
    true_range = np.maximum(
        intraday_range,
        np.maximum((high - previous_close).abs(), (low - previous_close).abs()),
    )
    normalized_true_range = (true_range / previous_close).where(previous_close > 0.0)
    median_normalized_range = normalized_true_range.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
    magnitude = (gap.abs() / median_normalized_range.where(median_normalized_range > 0.0)).clip(
        lower=0.0, upper=3.0
    )

    upward_refill = (open_ - low) / (open_ - previous_close).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    downward_refill = (high - open_) / (previous_close - open_).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    refill = upward_refill.where(gap > 0.0, downward_refill).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

    close_location = (
        2.0 * (close - low) / intraday_range.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    ).where(intraday_range > 0.0, 0.0)
    retention = (1.0 + gap_sign * close_location) / 2.0

    daily = gap_sign * magnitude * (1.0 - refill) * retention
    nonzero_gap = gap.notna() & gap.ne(0.0)
    daily = daily.where(nonzero_gap)
    daily = daily.mask(gap.eq(0.0), 0.0)
    return daily.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class OpenGapRefillParticipationClock(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks persistent directional opening gaps whose opposing liquidity did not refill."""

    factor_id = "open_gap_refill_participation_clock"
    name = "Unrefilled Gap Liquidity Persistence"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional sector-neutral rank of the mean three-session signed "
        "opening-gap imbalance score, where large unrefilled gaps closing at "
        "their directional range extreme indicate persistent liquidity imbalance."
    )
    window_length = 22
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        daily_score = _gap_imbalance_score(
            data["open"],
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["close"],
        )
        persistence = daily_score.rolling(3, min_periods=2).mean()
        mapped_rank = 2.0 * rank(persistence) - 1.0
        neutralized = indneutralize(mapped_rank, data["sector"])
        return neutralized.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

programs.trading_idea: An opening gap that remains substantially unrefilled and closes at the directional end of the daily range is interpreted as evidence that opposing displayed liquidity did not replenish sufficiently during the session. With daily OHLCV data, this is not claimed to identify scheduled institutional execution or auction-specific order flow; it is a reduced-form proxy for persistent directional liquidity imbalance. The prediction is continuation when the imbalance persists over several sessions, while explicitly recognizing that information-driven repricing is an observationally similar alternative explanation.
programs.description: At each close t, define the signed opening gap g_t = log(Open_t / Close_{t-1}) and s_t = sign(g_t), with a zero gap assigned a score of zero. Define true range TR_t = max(High_t-Low_t, abs(High_t-Close_{t-1}), abs(Low_t-Close_{t-1})) and normalized gap magnitude m_t = min(abs(g_t) / median(TR_{t-19:t} / Close_{t-1}), 3); if the median denominator is missing or nonpositive, set the daily score to NaN. For an upward gap, refill_t = clip((Open_t-Low_t)/(Open_t-Close_{t-1}), 0, 1); for a downward gap, refill_t = clip((High_t-Open_t)/(Close_{t-1}-Open_t), 0, 1). Define close-location CLV_t = 2*(Close_t-Low_t)/(High_t-Low_t)-1 when High_t>Low_t and 0 otherwise, and directional retention r_t = (1 + s_t*CLV_t)/2. The daily imbalance score is d_t = s_t*m_t*(1-refill_t)*r_t. The factor is the arithmetic mean of valid d_t values over t-2 through t, requiring at least two valid observations; it is then converted to a cross-sectional percentile rank, mapped to [-1,1], and demeaned within sector. Positive factor exposure is long and negative exposure is short. All inputs are observed through Close_t only, and positions may be entered no earlier than t+1.

"""This is not interpreted as dealer-inventory unwinding. A sufficiently large opening-auction displacement that is fully invalidated by a close through the prior close is treated as evidence that the opening price did not represent the dominant day-long information or order-flow direction. The close-side direction is therefore the signal: crossing the reference price indicates that the market has repriced beyond the auction anchor, and the resulting information/order-flow imbalance may continue to diffuse over the following six sessions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _turnover_percentile(
    turnover: pd.DataFrame, universe: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Ascending cross-sectional average-rank percentile on valid rows only."""
    valid_turnover = turnover.where(universe)
    ranks = valid_turnover.rank(axis=1, method="average", ascending=True)
    counts = universe.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    denominator = counts.sub(1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    percentile = ranks.sub(1.0).div(denominator, axis=0)
    return percentile.where(universe)


@register_factor
class AuctionGapInvalidationContinuation(BaseFactor):
    """Close-side continuation after a fully invalidated opening-auction gap."""

    factor_id = "auction_gap_invalidation_continuation"
    name = "Auction Gap Invalidation Continuation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Signals close-side continuation after a 2%--10% opening-auction gap "
        "is fully crossed through the prior close, conditional on high same-day "
        "dollar-volume-to-market-cap participation."
    )
    window_length = 2
    inputs = ["open", "close", "volume", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_price = data["open"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        prior_close = close.shift(1)

        finite_positive = (
            np.isfinite(open_price)
            & np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(prior_close)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
            & np.isfinite(market_cap)
            & (open_price > 0.0)
            & (close > 0.0)
            & (prior_close > 0.0)
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & (market_cap > 0.0)
        )

        gap = open_price.div(prior_close) - 1.0
        close_return = close.div(prior_close) - 1.0
        turnover = close.mul(volume).div(market_cap)

        universe_count = finite_positive.sum(axis=1)
        sufficient_universe = universe_count >= 20
        participation = _turnover_percentile(turnover, finite_positive)

        invalidated_gap = (
            (gap.abs() >= 0.02)
            & (gap.abs() <= 0.10)
            & (close_return.abs() >= 0.005)
            & (np.sign(gap) * close_return < 0.0)
        )
        eligible = (
            finite_positive
            & invalidated_gap
            & (participation >= 0.70)
        )

        raw_score = np.sign(close_return) * gap.abs() * close_return.abs() * participation
        score = raw_score.where(eligible, 0.0)
        score = score.where(sufficient_universe, 0.0)
        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: This is not interpreted as dealer-inventory unwinding. A sufficiently large opening-auction displacement that is fully invalidated by a close through the prior close is treated as evidence that the opening price did not represent the dominant day-long information or order-flow direction. The close-side direction is therefore the signal: crossing the reference price indicates that the market has repriced beyond the auction anchor, and the resulting information/order-flow imbalance may continue to diffuse over the following six sessions.
programs.description: For stock i on day t, define prior close C[t-1], opening gap g[t]=O[t]/C[t-1]-1, and close return r[t]=C[t]/C[t-1]-1. A stock is eligible only when O[t], C[t], C[t-1], volume[t], and marketCap[t] are finite and strictly positive; abs(g[t]) is at least 0.02 and at most 0.10; abs(r[t]) is at least 0.005; and sign(g[t])*r[t]<0, which requires the close to cross fully through the prior-close reference level rather than merely retrace part of the opening gap. Participation is same-day turnover proxy q[t]=C[t]*volume[t]/marketCap[t]. On each t, form the cross-sectional universe of stocks satisfying the stated positive finite OHLCV and market-cap requirements. If this universe has fewer than 20 stocks, all scores are zero. Otherwise let p[t] be the percentile rank of q[t] in that universe, using ascending average ranks for ties and p=(average_rank-1)/(N-1); require p[t]>=0.70. The final score is score[t]=sign(r[t])*abs(g[t])*abs(r[t])*p[t] for eligible stocks and zero for every other stock, including any missing or invalid observation. Positive scores indicate long exposure and negative scores indicate short exposure. The signal is finalized only after the close of t; no order may use the t close for execution. Enter at the next available bar open, t+1 open, and hold through the close of t+6, a six-daily-bar forward holding convention. The distinguishing feature versus ordinary gap-refill signals is the mandatory full prior-close cross-through plus continuation in the close-side direction, rather than a partial gap retracement interpreted as a reversal.

programs.code:
"""This is a reduced-form test of whether an isolated negative opening dislocation that is substantially reversed during the same completed daily session predicts short-horizon continuation of that reversal. Daily OHLCV cannot identify auction-seller exhaustion, informed flow, or liquidity-provider inventory, so the factor makes no such attribution: it treats the pattern as observable evidence of temporary opening price pressure relative to sector peers. Elevated participation is used as a confirmation that the reversal occurred in an actively traded session rather than as proof of a particular counterparty mechanism."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _positive_finite(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Keep only finite, strictly positive numeric observations."""
    return df.where(np.isfinite(df) & df.gt(0.0))


def _sector_gap_median(
    gap: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return date-wise sector median gaps only for sectors with five names."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=gap.index, columns=gap.columns)
    labels = pd.unique(sector.to_numpy().ravel())

    for label in labels:
        if pd.isna(label):
            continue

        constituent = sector.eq(label)
        valid = constituent & gap.notna()
        usable_date = valid.sum(axis=1).ge(5)
        target = constituent & usable_date.to_numpy()[:, None]

        median = gap.where(valid).median(axis=1)
        median_panel = pd.DataFrame(
            np.broadcast_to(median.to_numpy()[:, None], gap.shape),
            index=gap.index,
            columns=gap.columns,
        )
        result = result.where(~target, median_panel)

    return result


def _cross_sectional_winsorized_rank(score: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize eligible scores by date and average-rank only broad universes."""
    eligible_count = score.notna().sum(axis=1)
    lower = score.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = score.quantile(0.99, axis=1)

    winsorized = score.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    ranked = winsorized.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True, ascending=True)
    return ranked.where(eligible_count.ge(20), np.nan)


@register_factor
class IdioOpeningSellRejectionRecovery(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks active idiosyncratic opening selloffs rejected by the close."""

    factor_id = "idio_opening_sell_rejection_recovery"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Gap-Rejection Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional percentile rank of a negative sector-adjusted opening "
        "gap that reverses strongly into the close on elevated volume, using only "
        "completed daily-bar information."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)

        safe_open = _positive_finite(open_)
        safe_high = _positive_finite(high)
        safe_low = _positive_finite(low)
        safe_close = _positive_finite(close)
        safe_volume = _positive_finite(volume)
        safe_prior_close = _positive_finite(prior_close)

        gap = (safe_open / safe_prior_close - 1.0).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        sector_gap = _sector_gap_median(gap, sector)
        idiosyncratic_gap = gap - sector_gap

        historical_range = ((safe_high - safe_low) / safe_prior_close).where(
            safe_high.ge(safe_low)
        )
        historical_range = historical_range.where(historical_range.gt(0.0))
        historical_range = historical_range.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        sigma_range = historical_range.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median().shift(1)
        vol_base = safe_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median().shift(1)

        bar_range = safe_high - safe_low
        valid_current_geometry = (
            safe_high.ge(safe_open)
            & safe_high.ge(safe_close)
            & safe_low.le(safe_open)
            & safe_low.le(safe_close)
            & bar_range.gt(0.0)
        )

        current_valid = (
            safe_open.notna()
            & safe_high.notna()
            & safe_low.notna()
            & safe_close.notna()
            & safe_volume.notna()
            & safe_prior_close.notna()
            & valid_current_geometry
            & idiosyncratic_gap.notna()
            & sigma_range.gt(0.0)
            & vol_base.gt(0.0)
        )

        dislocation = (-idiosyncratic_gap / sigma_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        reversal = ((safe_close - safe_open) / bar_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        near_high = ((safe_close - safe_low) / bar_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        participation = (safe_volume / vol_base - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)

        raw_score = (dislocation * reversal * near_high * participation).where(
            current_valid
        )
        raw_score = raw_score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        return _cross_sectional_winsorized_rank(raw_score)
programs.name: Idiosyncratic Gap-Rejection Reversal
programs.trading_idea: This is a reduced-form test of whether an isolated negative opening dislocation that is substantially reversed during the same completed daily session predicts short-horizon continuation of that reversal. Daily OHLCV cannot identify auction-seller exhaustion, informed flow, or liquidity-provider inventory, so the factor makes no such attribution: it treats the pattern as observable evidence of temporary opening price pressure relative to sector peers. Elevated participation is used as a confirmation that the reversal occurred in an actively traded session rather than as proof of a particular counterparty mechanism.
programs.description: At the close of daily bar t, define the stock gap g_i,t = open_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1, using the immediately preceding available daily close. The sector gap G_s,t is the equal-weight cross-sectional median of g_i,t among all configured ticker columns with a nonmissing positive prior close and positive open, and with the same nonmissing static sector label s; a sector observation is usable only when at least five such constituents exist. Define the idiosyncratic gap e_i,t = g_i,t - G_s,t. For each stock, define prior daily relative range r_i,u = (high_i,u - low_i,u) / close_i,u-1 and require 20 valid, strictly positive observations from u=t-20 through t-1; set sigmaRange_i,t to their median. Require 20 valid, strictly positive daily volumes over the same t-20 through t-1 window and set volBase_i,t to their median. The completed-day measures are D_i,t = clip((-e_i,t / sigmaRange_i,t), 0, 5), R_i,t = clip((close_i,t - open_i,t) / (high_i,t - low_i,t), 0, 1), N_i,t = clip((close_i,t - low_i,t) / (high_i,t - low_i,t), 0, 1), and A_i,t = clip((volume_i,t / volBase_i,t) - 1, 0, 4). The raw score is S_i,t = D_i,t * R_i,t * N_i,t * A_i,t. A stock is ineligible, and receives NaN rather than an imputed score, if any required current or historical input is missing or nonpositive, if high < max(open, close), if low > min(open, close), if high equals low, if sigmaRange or volBase is nonpositive, or if its sector lacks five valid gap observations. Thus zero-range bars, including bars that may be mechanically locked or limit-like, are excluded; the feed has no limit-status field, so nonzero-range bars are not otherwise classified as limit bars. On each date with at least 20 eligible stocks, winsorize S cross-sectionally at its 1st and 99th percentiles and convert it to an ascending percentile rank using average ranks for ties; this percentile rank is the factor value, with higher values predicting higher returns. The score is computed only after bar t has fully closed. It is entered no earlier than the next executable daily bar's open, t+1, and the six-bar forecast/holding return is measured from the t+1 open to the t+7 open; a name without a tradable next open is not entered.

programs.code:
"""A one-day, industry-relative displacement occurring with unusually high participation and no contemporaneous analyst-consensus revision is treated as a candidate temporary-liquidity shock rather than as identified uninformed flow. The proposed mechanism is that urgent execution can temporarily consume displayed and latent liquidity, leaving the closing price away from the level supported once liquidity providers and patient counterparties return. Because static estimates do not rule out private or non-consensus information, this is a conditional mean-reversion hypothesis requiring empirical validation, especially net of trading costs and relative to existing liquidity-reversal signals."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _peer_relative_return(
    stock_return: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return versus same-industry peers, falling back to sector peers.

    A peer benchmark requires at least five other non-missing names.  All
    grouping is performed independently at each completed bar, so changing
    universe membership and sparse classification data remain causal.
    """
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=stock_return.index, columns=stock_return.columns)

    for row_number in range(len(stock_return.index)):
        values = stock_return.iloc[row_number]
        industry_labels = industry.iloc[row_number]
        sector_labels = sector.iloc[row_number]

        def peer_mean(labels: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
            valid = values.notna() & labels.notna()
            output = pd.Series(np.nan, index=values.index, dtype=float)
            if not valid.any():
                return output

            grouped_values = values.loc[valid]
            grouped_labels = labels.loc[valid]
            group_sum = grouped_values.groupby(grouped_labels).transform("sum")
            group_count = grouped_values.groupby(grouped_labels).transform("count")
            peer_count = group_count - 1.0
            denominator = peer_count.where(peer_count >= 5.0)
            output.loc[grouped_values.index] = (group_sum - grouped_values) / denominator
            return output

        industry_peer_mean = peer_mean(industry_labels)
        sector_peer_mean = peer_mean(sector_labels)
        benchmark = industry_peer_mean.where(industry_peer_mean.notna(), sector_peer_mean)
        result.iloc[row_number] = (values - benchmark).to_numpy()

    return result


def _conditional_sector_rank(
    raw_pressure: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rank negative pressure by adequately populated sector or residualized pool."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=raw_pressure.index, columns=raw_pressure.columns)

    for row_number in range(len(raw_pressure.index)):
        raw_row = raw_pressure.iloc[row_number]
        sector_labels = sector.iloc[row_number]
        eligible = raw_row.notna() & sector_labels.notna()
        if not eligible.any():
            continue

        raw_eligible = raw_row.loc[eligible]
        sector_eligible = sector_labels.loc[eligible]
        sector_count = raw_eligible.groupby(sector_eligible).transform("count")
        sector_median = raw_eligible.groupby(sector_eligible).transform("median")

        # Sparse sectors are compared in the full eligible universe only after
        # removing their sector's common displacement level.
        global_rank = (-(raw_eligible - sector_median)).rank(pct=True)
        sector_rank = (-raw_eligible).groupby(sector_eligible).rank(pct=True)
        selected_rank = global_rank.where(sector_count < 10.0, sector_rank)
        result.loc[result.index[row_number], selected_rank.index] = selected_rank.to_numpy()

    return result


@register_factor
class ForecastStaticTurnoverDisplacementRepair(BaseFactor):
    """Conditional reversal after high-turnover, estimate-static relative displacement."""

    factor_id = "forecast_static_turnover_displacement_repair"
    name = "Forecast-Static Relative Flow Repair"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks negative industry-relative return pressure when turnover is "
        "abnormally high but EPS and revenue consensus estimates have remained "
        "static; pressure is ranked within sufficiently populated sectors and "
        "otherwise sector-median residualized in the full eligible universe."
    )
    window_length = 25
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "sector",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry = data["industry"]
        sector = data["sector"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]

        stock_return = close / close.shift(1) - 1.0
        relative_return = _peer_relative_return(stock_return, industry, sector)

        # The shifted rolling mean is exactly the t-20 through t-1 baseline.
        prior_volume = volume.shift(1)
        baseline_volume = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        valid_current_volume = volume.notna() & (volume >= 0.0)
        turnover = (volume / baseline_volume).where(
            valid_current_volume & (baseline_volume > 0.0)
        )
        log_turnover = np.log1p(turnover.where(turnover >= 0.0))

        # Cross-sectional winsorization is contemporaneous and does not use
        # future observations.
        turnover_cap = log_turnover.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        capped_log_turnover = log_turnover.clip(upper=turnover_cap, axis=0)

        eps_lag = eps_estimate.shift(5)
        revenue_lag = revenue_estimate.shift(5)
        eps_static = (
            eps_estimate.notna()
            & eps_lag.notna()
            & ((eps_estimate - eps_lag).abs() <= 0.001)
        )
        revenue_tolerance = np.maximum(1.0, 0.001 * revenue_lag.abs())
        revenue_static = (
            revenue_estimate.notna()
            & revenue_lag.notna()
            & ((revenue_estimate - revenue_lag).abs() <= revenue_tolerance)
        )
        estimate_static = eps_static & revenue_static

        raw_pressure = (relative_return * capped_log_turnover).where(estimate_static)
        return _conditional_sector_rank(raw_pressure, sector)

programs.description: At completed bar t, define stock return as r_t = close_t / close_{t-1} - 1. Define the industry-relative return as r_t minus the equal-weighted same-industry return at t, excluding the stock itself; if fewer than 5 non-missing peers are available, use the analogous sector-relative equal-weighted return, also excluding the stock; otherwise set the signal missing. Define daily turnover as volume_t divided by the 20-bar rolling mean of volume from t-20 through t-1, requiring at least 15 valid prior observations and positive baseline volume. Transform abnormal turnover as log(1 + turnover_t), capped at the cross-sectional 99th percentile on date t to limit isolated reporting or data errors. Define EPS-consensus change as abs(epsEstimate_t - epsEstimate_{t-5}) and revenue-consensus change as abs(revenueEstimate_t - revenueEstimate_{t-5}); an observation is estimate-static only when both current and t-5 values are non-missing, EPS change is no greater than 0.001 USD, and revenue change is no greater than max(1, 0.001 times abs(revenueEstimate_{t-5})) USD. Compute raw pressure as industry-relative return times capped log abnormal turnover, retain only estimate-static observations, and assign the factor as the cross-sectional percentile rank of negative raw pressure among eligible names on t. Rank separately within sector where at least 10 eligible names exist; otherwise rank in the full eligible universe after subtracting the sector median raw pressure. Missing prices, volume history, industry/sector peers, turnover baselines, or either required estimate observation produce a missing signal rather than an imputed estimate-static classification. All inputs are available through the completed daily bar t; portfolio formation and execution occur no earlier than t+1, never at t's close.

programs.code:
"""Reported changes in shares outstanding are not identified tradable-float or offering events, but newly public share-count expansion versus contraction can still condition the interpretation of subsequent price-volume pressure. A positive disclosed share-count change paired with persistent weak price pressure is consistent with supply pressure, while a contraction paired with positive pressure is consistent with a favorable reduction in marginal equity supply; the opposite combinations indicate that observed pressure is offsetting the accounting-share signal. The claim is explicitly a conditional share-count-change and daily price/volume-pressure hypothesis, not evidence of underwriter distribution or dealer inventory."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_winsorize(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Clip each date's valid cross section at its 1st and 99th percentiles."""
    lower = frame.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = frame.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return frame.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _share_change_events(shares: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return disclosed share changes only when the available value changes.

    The input is ordinarily a point-in-time forward-filled step function.  The
    lagged forward fill also handles occasional missing intervals without using
    future observations.
    """
    previous_available = shares.ffill().shift(1)
    valid_pair = shares.gt(0.0) & previous_available.gt(0.0)
    changed = shares.ne(previous_available)

    event_change = shares / previous_available - 1.0
    return event_change.where(changed, 0.0).where(valid_pair)


def _pressure_score(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute the causal five-bar close-location signed-volume pressure."""
    price_range = high - low
    close_location = ((close - low) / price_range - 0.5).where(high.gt(low), 0.0)

    prior_volume_mean = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    relative_volume = volume / prior_volume_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    daily_pressure = (close_location * relative_volume).where(prior_volume_mean.gt(0.0))

    return daily_pressure.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()


@register_factor
class FloatShockResilienceInventorySort(BaseFactor):
    """Conditional share-count changes confirmed or offset by price-volume pressure."""

    factor_id = "float_shock_resilience_inventory_sort"
    name = "Share-Change Pressure Confirmation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional interaction of newly disclosed share-count changes and "
        "five-bar close-location signed-volume pressure; positive scores identify "
        "expansion with weak pressure or contraction with strong pressure."
    )
    window_length = 25
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sharesOutstanding"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        share_change = _share_change_events(data["sharesOutstanding"])
        winsorized_change = _cross_sectional_winsorize(share_change)
        change_rank = 2.0 * winsorized_change.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0

        pressure = _pressure_score(
            close,
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["volume"],
        )
        winsorized_pressure = _cross_sectional_winsorize(pressure)
        pressure_rank = 2.0 * winsorized_pressure.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0

        return (-change_rank * pressure_rank).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.description: At each date t after the close, identify the latest sharesOutstanding observation S_t and its immediately preceding distinct non-null point-in-time observation S_prev for each ticker. Define disclosed share change g_t = (S_t / S_prev) - 1 only from the first bar on which S_t differs from the previously available value, and set g_t = 0 on all other bars; require S_t > 0 and S_prev > 0, otherwise leave missing.
