programs.trading_idea: This is a conditional short-horizon price-pressure hypothesis, not a claim that OHLCV identifies displayed depth, dealer inventory, or liquidity-motivated trading. A stock with unusually high realized range per traded dollar, a close near the daily low, and many peers simultaneously exhibiting elevated range-per-dollar-volume is more likely to be in a correlated adverse-price-pressure episode than in an isolated idiosyncratic move. The prediction is negative over the following six daily bars because broad peer concurrence conditions the otherwise ambiguous low-close/illiquidity observation toward continuation rather than standalone capitulation.
programs.description: At each completed daily bar, form the eligible universe of stocks with positive close, nonnegative high-low range, and positive volume. Define normalized range r=(high-low)/close and dollar volume dv=close*volume; within the eligible universe, winsorize dv to its daily 1st and 99th percentiles and set impact=r/winsorized_dv. Let I be the daily full-universe percentile rank of impact, with higher values indicating greater realized range per traded dollar. Define downside close location D=1-((close-low)/(high-low)) when high>low, and D=0.5 when high=low; thus D is 1 at the low and 0 at the high. Mark a stock as elevated-impact when I>=0.90. For each stock, compute leave-one-out elevated-impact breadth B as the fraction of eligible peers marked elevated-impact: use its industry if at least 9 eligible same-industry peers excluding itself exist; otherwise use its sector if at least 9 eligible same-sector peers excluding itself exist; otherwise use all other eligible universe members. The raw signal is S=I*B*D, and the tradable cross-sectional factor is the daily percentile rank of S among eligible stocks, with higher scores shorted and lower scores bought or used as the opposite leg. The signal is formed only after the completed daily bar and may be executed no earlier than the next tradable bar/open; liquidity, borrow availability, turnover, and transaction-cost filters are applied by the evaluation harness. Evaluation should test incremental efficacy after controlling for standalone range/volume, directional-return/impulse, and peer-shock exposures.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_component_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels == label]
        valid = eligible.loc[:, cols]
        enough = valid.sum(axis=1) >= 8
        group_values = values.loc[:, cols].where(valid)
        lower = group_values.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
        upper = group_values.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
        clipped = group_values.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        ranked = clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        out.loc[:, cols] = ranked.where(enough, np.nan)
    return out


def _sector_momentum_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels == label]
        valid = eligible.loc[:, cols]
        enough = valid.sum(axis=1) >= 10
        ranked = values.loc[:, cols].where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        out.loc[:, cols] = ranked.where(enough, np.nan)
    return out


def _sector_demeaned_zscore(score: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    demeaned = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=score.index, columns=score.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels == label]
        group = score.loc[:, cols]
        demeaned.loc[:, cols] = group.sub(group.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    dispersion = demeaned.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return demeaned.div(dispersion, axis=0)


@register_factor
class QualityPremiumGatedRankInterruptFade(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "quality_premium_gated_rank_interrupt_fade"
    name = "Quality-State Rank Interruption Fade"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "A signed, volatility-adjusted realized quality-premium state gates the "
        "fade of sector-relative medium-term leadership interrupted by a recent "
        "short-term rank deterioration."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "roic",
        "incomeQuality",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
        "assetGrowth",
        "debtGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        labels = data["sector"].iloc[0]

        roic = data["roic"].shift(1)
        income_quality = data["incomeQuality"].shift(1)
        fcf_yield = data["freeCashFlowYield"].shift(1)
        asset_growth = data["assetGrowth"].shift(1)
        debt_growth = data["debtGrowth"].shift(1)

        quality_eligible = (
            roic.notna()
            & income_quality.notna()
            & fcf_yield.notna()
            & asset_growth.notna()
            & debt_growth.notna()
        )
        quality_score = (
            _sector_component_rank(roic, quality_eligible, labels)
            + _sector_component_rank(income_quality, quality_eligible, labels)
            + _sector_component_rank(fcf_yield, quality_eligible, labels)
            + (1.0 - _sector_component_rank(asset_growth, quality_eligible, labels))
            + (1.0 - _sector_component_rank(debt_growth, quality_eligible, labels))
        ) / 5.0
        quality_score = quality_score.where(quality_eligible)

        quality_z = _sector_demeaned_zscore(quality_score, labels)
        completed_return = close.pct_change().shift(1)
        completed_quality_premium = (quality_z.shift(1) * completed_return).mean(axis=1)
        premium_mean = completed_quality_premium.rolling(15, min_periods=10).mean()
        premium_vol = completed_quality_premium.rolling(40, min_periods=25).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        quality_state = (premium_mean / premium_vol).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        quality_state = np.tanh(quality_state).fillna(0.0)

        lag_close = close.shift(1)
        daily_return = lag_close.pct_change()
        volatility = daily_return.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        normalized: dict[int, pd.DataFrame] = {}
        for horizon in (2, 5, 10, 20):
            trailing = lag_close / lag_close.shift(horizon).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
            normalized[horizon] = trailing.div(volatility * np.sqrt(float(horizon)))

        momentum_eligible = pd.DataFrame(True, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for frame in normalized.values():
            momentum_eligible = momentum_eligible & frame.notna()
        momentum_eligible = momentum_eligible & quality_score.notna()

        p2 = _sector_momentum_rank(normalized[2], momentum_eligible, labels)
        p5 = _sector_momentum_rank(normalized[5], momentum_eligible, labels)
        p10 = _sector_momentum_rank(normalized[10], momentum_eligible, labels)
        p20 = _sector_momentum_rank(normalized[20], momentum_eligible, labels)

        consensus = (p10 + p20) / 2.0
        long_interrupt = (p10 >= 0.60) & (p20 >= 0.60) & (p5 >= 0.50)
        short_interrupt = (p10 <= 0.40) & (p20 <= 0.40) & (p5 <= 0.50)
        candidate = (long_interrupt | short_interrupt) & momentum_eligible

        interruption_gap = consensus - p2
        quality_intensity = 0.5 + quality_score.clip(0.0, 1.0)
        signal = (-interruption_gap * quality_intensity).mul(quality_state, axis=0)
        return signal.where(candidate, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Quality-State Rank Interruption Fade
programs.trading_idea: The rank-interruption pattern in Parent B appears to be a crowded-leadership exhaustion signal rather than a continuation signal: stocks with strong medium-term sector leadership but a recent relative stumble tend to underperform, consistent with institutional rebalancing and delayed de-risking. This child activates that fade specifically when the lagged profitability/cash-flow/conservative-investment spread has recently earned a positive, volatility-adjusted premium, a state in which quality leadership has likely attracted allocator demand and is more vulnerable to synchronized profit-taking. When the quality premium is negative, the same interruption is instead signed as a catch-up opportunity because the allocator flow supporting quality is already unwinding; neither a static quality spread nor an unconditional rank interruption distinguishes these two flow states.

Higher values indicate expected higher six-bar returns.

"""Leader-confirmed late-quarter revision diffusion.

Mechanism: analyst revisions diffuse fastest when a liquid industry's leaders make a
same-direction, high-participation idiosyncratic move, but not when the recipient
has already undergone unusually rapid sector-relative variance acceleration.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _report_age(reset: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bars since the latest observed actual-report update, calculated causally."""
    rows, cols = reset.shape
    positions = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(np.arange(rows, dtype=float)[:, None], (rows, cols)),
        index=reset.index,
        columns=reset.columns,
    )
    latest = positions.where(reset).ffill()
    return positions - latest


def _update_reset(actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Mark a new reported actual relative to the previously available actual."""
    prior = actual.ffill().shift(1)
    finite_now = actual.notna() & ~actual.isin([np.inf, -np.inf])
    finite_prior = prior.notna() & ~prior.isin([np.inf, -np.inf])
    return finite_now & finite_prior & actual.ne(prior)


def _revision(estimate: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robustly scale a causal estimate change by its prior estimate magnitude."""
    prior = estimate.shift(lag)
    valid = eligible & estimate.notna() & prior.notna()
    valid = valid & ~estimate.isin([np.inf, -np.inf]) & ~prior.isin([np.inf, -np.inf])
    magnitude = prior.abs().where(valid)
    floor = 0.01 * magnitude.median(axis=1)
    denominator = prior.abs().where(
        prior.abs().ge(floor, axis=0), floor, axis=0
    ).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return ((estimate - prior) / denominator).where(valid).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _sector_robust_zscore(value: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-date sector robust z-score with a universe fallback for small sectors."""
    labels = sector.ffill().iloc[-1].astype(object)
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "__UNKNOWN__")
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=value.index, columns=value.columns, dtype=float)

    universe_median = value.median(axis=1)
    universe_mad = value.sub(universe_median, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1)
    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        block = value.loc[:, members]
        count = block.notna().sum(axis=1)
        median = block.median(axis=1)
        mad = block.sub(median, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1)
        use_sector = count.ge(5)
        location = median.where(use_sector, universe_median)
        dispersion = mad.where(use_sector, universe_mad)
        output.loc[:, members] = block.sub(location, axis=0).div(
            1.4826 * dispersion + 1e-12, axis=0
        )
    return output.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _leader_peer_impulse(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Leave-self-out liquid-leader residual impulse for each industry member.

    Leaders are names in the trailing-dollar-volume top tercile of their industry.
    Their current idiosyncratic returns are weighted by contemporaneous volume
    surprise, so a broad industry move does not masquerade as a transported shock.
    """
    safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ret = safe_close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
    dollar = close * volume
    adv = dollar.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
    volume_base = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
    own_sigma = ret.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=10).std()

    labels = industry.ffill().iloc[-1].astype(object)
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "__UNKNOWN__")
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns, dtype=float)

    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        if len(members) < 2:
            continue
        group_ret = ret.loc[:, members]
        group_mean = group_ret.mean(axis=1)
        residual = group_ret.sub(group_mean, axis=0)
        group_adv = adv.loc[:, members]
        cutoff = group_adv.quantile(0.67, axis=1)
        leaders = group_adv.ge(cutoff, axis=0) & group_adv.gt(0.0)
        participation = (volume.loc[:, members] / volume_base.loc[:, members]).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        weights = group_adv.where(leaders, 0.0) * participation.where(leaders, 0.0)
        weighted_residual = weights * residual
        total_weight = weights.sum(axis=1)
        total_impulse = weighted_residual.sum(axis=1)

        peer_weight = total_weight.to_frame().reindex(columns=members).sub(weights)
        peer_impulse = total_impulse.to_frame().reindex(columns=members).sub(weighted_residual)
        peer_average = peer_impulse / peer_weight.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        output.loc[:, members] = peer_average.div(own_sigma.loc[:, members]).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)

    return output


@register_factor
class LeaderConfirmedRevisionDiffusionGate(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "leader_confirmed_revision_diffusion_gate"
    name = "Leader-Confirmed Revision Diffusion"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Late-quarter consensus revisions receive greater signed weight when they "
        "agree with a high-volume idiosyncratic impulse from liquid industry peers, "
        "subject to a sector-relative variance-completion screen."
    )
    window_length = 45
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "sector",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        if close.empty:
            return close.astype(float)

        reset = _update_reset(data["epsActual"]) | _update_reset(data["revenueActual"])
        age = _report_age(reset)
        eligible = age.ge(30) & age.le(70)

        eps_change = _revision(data["epsEstimate"], eligible, 15)
        revenue_change = _revision(data["revenueEstimate"], eligible, 15)
        eps_rank = 2.0 * eps_change.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        revenue_rank = 2.0 * revenue_change.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        revision_score = 0.65 * eps_rank + 0.35 * revenue_rank

        peer_impulse = _leader_peer_impulse(close, data["volume"].astype(float), data["industry"])
        concordance = revision_score * peer_impulse
        confirmation = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-2.0 * concordance.clip(-8.0, 8.0)))

        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        valid_range = high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0)
        range_var = np.log(high.where(valid_range) / low.where(valid_range)).pow(2) / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))
        short_var = range_var.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        long_var = range_var.rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()
        acceleration = np.log((short_var + 1e-12) / (long_var + 1e-12)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        variance_z = _sector_robust_zscore(acceleration, data["sector"])
        completion_penalty = variance_z.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0).fillna(0.0) / 2.0

        signal = revision_score * confirmation * (1.0 - completion_penalty)
        return signal.where(eligible & revision_score.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0).reindex(
            index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        )

The peer impulse supplies a real-time read-through channel that a revision alone lacks, while the revision supplies a fundamental direction and report-clock context that a leader return alone lacks. The interaction is attenuated when the follower's range variance has already accelerated relative to its sector, because rapid price discovery and adverse-selection risk imply that the joint information is already incorporated.

A sector-relative Parkinson variance-acceleration screen reduces exposure where the follower has already entered an intensive price-discovery regime.

programs.code:
"""The signal targets delayed incorporation of newly released peer-specific fundamental information rather than generic industry returns. A stock is eligible only when several other firms in its static industry have newly available EPS-surprise observations whose signs and same-session returns agree, while the recipient itself has no new EPS release and has moved materially less than the peer event basket. A same-day close in the peer-information direction on elevated dollar volume is used as a confirmation gate that the recipient is beginning, rather than failing, to assimilate the peer fundamental news; the portfolio is entered only at the next session's executable open."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _peer_event_shock(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_actual: pd.DataFrame,
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Build causal same-close industry event shocks and recipient eligibility."""
    ret = close.pct_change()
    prior_actual = eps_actual.shift(1)
    actual_update = eps_actual.notna() & (
        prior_actual.isna() | eps_actual.ne(prior_actual)
    )
    fresh = (
        actual_update
        & eps_surprise.notna()
        & ret.notna()
        & industry.notna()
    )

    shock = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    eligible = pd.DataFrame(False, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

    for timestamp in close.index:
        labels = industry.loc[timestamp]
        row_ret = ret.loc[timestamp]
        row_surprise = eps_surprise.loc[timestamp]
        row_fresh = fresh.loc[timestamp]
        row_update = actual_update.loc[timestamp]

        industry_shocks: dict[object, float] = {}
        coherent_industries: list[object] = []

        for label, members in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
            member_index = list(members)
            event_names = [name for name in member_index if bool(row_fresh.loc[name])]
            count = len(event_names)
            if count < 3:
                continue

            peer_returns = row_ret.loc[event_names]
            peer_surprises = row_surprise.loc[event_names]
            peer_mean = peer_returns.mean()
            if not np.isfinite(peer_mean) or peer_mean == 0.0:
                continue

            direction = float(np.sign(peer_mean))
            return_agreement = (np.sign(peer_returns) == direction).mean()
            surprise_agreement = (np.sign(peer_surprises) == direction).mean()
            if return_agreement >= (2.0 / 3.0) and surprise_agreement >= (2.0 / 3.0):
                industry_shocks[label] = float(peer_mean)
                coherent_industries.append(label)

        if not industry_shocks:
            continue

        absolute_shocks = pd.Series(
            [abs(value) for value in industry_shocks.values()], dtype=float
        )
        threshold = absolute_shocks.quantile(0.70)
        if not np.isfinite(threshold):
            continue

        for label in coherent_industries:
            peer_mean = industry_shocks[label]
            if abs(peer_mean) < threshold:
                continue
            recipients = labels.index[(labels == label) & (~row_update)]
            if len(recipients) > 0:
                shock.loc[timestamp, recipients] = peer_mean
                eligible.loc[timestamp, recipients] = True

    return shock, eligible


def _residual_rank_and_sector_weights(
    raw_score: pd.DataFrame,
    active: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    market_cap: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize active scores, peer-adjust them, then form sector-balanced deciles."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=raw_score.index, columns=raw_score.columns)

    for timestamp in raw_score.index:
        active_row = active.loc[timestamp] & raw_score.loc[timestamp].notna()
        names = list(active_row.index[active_row])
        if len(names) < 2:
            continue

        values = raw_score.loc[timestamp, names].astype(float)
        lower = values.quantile(0.02)
        upper = values.quantile(0.98)
        clipped = values.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper)

        sectors = sector.loc[timestamp, names]
        caps = market_cap.loc[timestamp, names]
        valid = sectors.notna() & caps.notna() & np.isfinite(caps)
        names = list(valid.index[valid])
        if len(names) < 2:
            continue

        clipped = clipped.loc[names]
        sectors = sectors.loc[names]
        cap_rank = caps.loc[names].rank(pct=True, method="average")
        cap_bucket = np.ceil(cap_rank * 5.0).clip(1.0, 5.0).astype(int)
        group_key = sectors.astype(str) + "|" + cap_bucket.astype(str)
        residual = clipped - clipped.groupby(group_key).transform("mean")
        residual_rank = residual.rank(pct=True, method="average")

        long_names = list(residual_rank.index[residual_rank >= 0.90])
        short_names = list(residual_rank.index[residual_rank <= 0.10])
        if not long_names or not short_names:
            continue

        long_sectors = sectors.loc[long_names]
        short_sectors = sectors.loc[short_names]
        usable_sectors = sorted(set(long_sectors) & set(short_sectors))
        if not usable_sectors:
            continue

        sector_count = float(len(usable_sectors))
        for sector_name in usable_sectors:
            sector_longs = [name for name in long_names if long_sectors.loc[name] == sector_name]
            sector_shorts = [name for name in short_names if short_sectors.loc[name] == sector_name]
            if sector_longs:
                output.loc[timestamp, sector_longs] = 1.0 / (sector_count * len(sector_longs))
            if sector_shorts:
                output.loc[timestamp, sector_shorts] = -1.0 / (sector_count * len(sector_shorts))

    return output


@register_factor
class PeerGapAssimilationCompletionDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Peer EPS-event underreaction confirmed by directional close and volume."""

    factor_id = "peer_gap_assimilation_completion_drift"
    name = "Fundamental Peer-Gap Assimilation"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Industry EPS-surprise event baskets identify recipients still below the "
        "peer-information move; directional close location and abnormal dollar "
        "volume confirm early assimilation before a six-bar drift."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "epsActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "industry",
        "sector",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_price = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        industry = data["industry"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        ret = close.pct_change()
        peer_shock, peer_eligible = _peer_event_shock(
            close, eps_actual, eps_surprise, industry
        )
        direction = np.sign(peer_shock)

        valid_market_ret = ret.where(ret.notna())
        market_return = valid_market_ret.mean(axis=1)
        median_abs_return = valid_market_ret.abs().median(axis=1)
        broad_risk = market_return.abs() > (1.5 * median_abs_return)

        dollar_volume = (volume * close).where(
            volume.notna() & close.notna() & (volume > 0.0) & (close > 0.0)
        )
        prior_median_dollar_volume = (
            dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).median().shift(1)
        )
        abnormal_dollar_volume = dollar_volume / prior_median_dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        intraday_return = close / open_price.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        price_range = high - low
        positive_location = (close - low) / price_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        negative_location = (high - close) / price_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = positive_location.where(direction > 0.0, negative_location)

        peer_abs = peer_shock.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        recipient_underreaction = (direction * ret) <= (0.5 * peer_abs)
        confirmation = (
            (direction * intraday_return > 0.0)
            & (close_location >= 0.60)
            & (abnormal_dollar_volume >= 1.0)
        )
        ohlcv_valid = (
            open_price.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & close.notna()
            & volume.notna()
            & (price_range != 0.0)
        )
        active = (
            peer_eligible
            & recipient_underreaction
            & confirmation
            & ohlcv_valid
            & market_cap.notna()
            & (~broad_risk.reindex(close.index).fillna(True).to_numpy()[:, None])
        )

        assimilation_gap = 1.0 - (direction * ret / peer_abs)
        raw_score = direction * peer_abs * assimilation_gap * abnormal_dollar_volume.clip(upper=3.0)
        raw_score = raw_score.where(active)

        return _residual_rank_and_sector_weights(raw_score, active, sector, market_cap)

A stock is eligible only when several other firms in its static industry have newly available EPS-surprise observations whose signs and same-session returns agree, while the recipient itself has no new EPS release and has moved materially less than the peer event basket. A same-day close in the peer-information direction on elevated dollar volume is used as a confirmation gate that the recipient is beginning, rather than failing, to assimilate the peer fundamental news; the portfolio is entered only at the next session's executable open.
programs.description: At the close of session t, define each stock return as r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. A peer j is a fresh fundamental-event peer for recipient i only if j is in the same static industry, j != i, epsActual_j,t and epsSurprise_j,t are finite, and epsActual_j,t differs from epsActual_j,t-1; recipient i must have no corresponding epsActual update at t. The leave-one-out peer shock P_i,t is the equal-weighted mean of r_j,t across fresh event peers, requiring at least 3 such peers. Retain an industry event only when at least two-thirds of event peers have return signs matching sign(P_i,t), at least two-thirds have epsSurprise signs matching sign(P_i,t), and |P_i,t| is at or above the cross-sectional 70th percentile of absolute eligible industry-event shocks that day. Exclude broad-risk days when the absolute equal-weighted market return exceeds 1.5 times the cross-sectional median absolute stock return, and exclude names with missing open, high, low, close, volume, marketCap, or insufficient volume history. Recipient underreaction requires sign(P_i,t) * r_i,t <= 0.5 * |P_i,t|. Confirmation requires sign(P_i,t) * (close_i,t / open_i,t - 1) > 0, directional close location of at least 0.60, and abnormal dollar volume of at least 1.0. Directional close location is (close-low)/(high-low) for positive P and (high-close)/(high-low) for negative P; observations with high == low are excluded. Abnormal dollar volume is volume_t * close_t divided by the median daily dollar volume over sessions t-20 through t-1, requiring at least 15 valid prior observations. For confirmed names, form raw score = sign(P_i,t) * |P_i,t| * [1 - sign(P_i,t) * r_i,t / |P_i,t|] * min(abnormalDollarVolume, 3); otherwise score is zero. Winsorize nonzero scores cross-sectionally at the 2nd and 98th percentiles, demean them within sector and market-cap quintile, and rank the residuals cross-sectionally. Buy the highest residual-score decile and short the lowest decile, subject to equal sector gross exposure. All same-day OHLCV values, peer closes, and event-state changes are observed only after session t closes; the signal is therefore submitted no earlier than the next bar's open and held for the fixed six-bar forecast horizon. This differs from the existing lagged_industry_leader_receiver_score because peer information is restricted to synchronized, newly available EPS-surprise releases with explicit surprise-sign coherence, uses an equal-weighted leave-one-out event basket rather than identified price leaders, excludes recipients with their own release, and treats volume/close behavior strictly as a post-event confirmation gate rather than as a standalone continuation signal.

programs.code:
"""This is not an identification claim about scheduled execution: daily OHLCV cannot distinguish mechanical flow from informed trading. Instead, it tests whether a persistent, unusually participatory one-sided price-pressure sequence becomes progressively less price-effective while its return-volume states remain repetitive; that configuration is a candidate for transitory liquidity pressure and a subsequent partial reversal. The reversal sign is conditional and must be evaluated net of known volume-impact, entropy, impulse-response, and liquidity-resilience signals, as well as trading costs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _relative_volume(volume: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal relative volume using the preceding 20 strictly valid bars."""
    valid_volume = volume.gt(0.0) & np.isfinite(volume)
    reference_volume = volume.where(valid_volume).shift(1)
    reference_median = reference_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
    reference_count = valid_volume.astype(float).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
    valid = valid_volume & reference_count.eq(20.0) & reference_median.gt(0.0)
    return (volume / reference_median).where(valid), valid


def _transition_entropy(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, relative_volume: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Normalized entropy of trailing nine causal return-volume transitions."""
    valid = ret.notna() & np.isfinite(ret) & relative_volume.notna() & np.isfinite(relative_volume)
    positive_or_zero = ret.ge(0.0)
    high_participation = relative_volume.ge(1.0)

    state_values = np.where(
        positive_or_zero & ~high_participation,
        0.0,
        np.where(
            positive_or_zero & high_participation,
            1.0,
            np.where(~positive_or_zero & ~high_participation, 2.0, 3.0),
        ),
    )
    states = pd.DataFrame(state_values, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns).where(valid)
    complete_window = states.notna().astype(float).rolling(10, min_periods=10).sum().eq(10.0)

    entropy = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    previous = states.shift(1)
    for source_state in range(4):
        for destination_state in range(4):
            transition = (
                states.eq(destination_state) & previous.eq(source_state)
            ).astype(float)
            probability = transition.rolling(9, min_periods=9).sum() / 9.0
            safe_probability = probability.where(probability.gt(0.0), 1.0)
            entropy = entropy - probability.where(probability.gt(0.0), 0.0) * np.log(safe_probability)

    return (entropy / np.log(16.0)).where(complete_window)


@register_factor
class AbsorbedCadenceImpactDecayReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Reversal score for repetitive, absorbed one-sided participation pressure."""

    factor_id = "absorbed_cadence_impact_decay_reversal"
    name = "Low-Entropy Pressure Decay"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Scores six-bar one-sided, high-participation pressure episodes whose "
        "return-volume transition sequence is repetitive and whose directional "
        "price impact decays from the first three bars to the last three bars. "
        "Positive values identify absorbed selling and negative values identify "
        "absorbed buying; portfolio construction should residualize this score "
        "against specified volume-impact, entropy, impulse-response, and "
        "liquidity-resilience factors."
    )
    window_length = 30
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = (close / previous_close - 1.0).where(np.isfinite(close / previous_close - 1.0))
        relative_volume, relative_volume_valid = _relative_volume(volume)

        signed_participation = np.sign(ret) * relative_volume
        pressure = signed_participation.rolling(6, min_periods=6).sum()
        direction = np.sign(pressure)
        episode_count = signed_participation.notna().astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=6).sum()
        mean_participation = relative_volume.rolling(6, min_periods=6).mean()
        same_direction_count = (
            np.sign(signed_participation).eq(direction).astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=6).sum()
        )

        entropy = _transition_entropy(ret, relative_volume)

        directional_impact = (direction * ret).clip(lower=0.0) / relative_volume
        impact_prior = directional_impact.shift(3).rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        impact_recent = directional_impact.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        impact_ratio = impact_recent / impact_prior.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        impact_decay = (1.0 - impact_ratio).clip(lower=0.0)

        qualifies = (
            episode_count.eq(6.0)
            & pressure.abs().ge(3.0)
            & mean_participation.ge(1.0)
            & same_direction_count.ge(5.0)
            & entropy.le(0.50)
            & impact_prior.gt(0.0)
            & impact_recent.le(0.75 * impact_prior)
        )

        score = -direction * (pressure.abs() / 6.0) * (1.0 - entropy) * impact_decay
        score = score.where(qualifies, 0.0)
        return score.where(relative_volume_valid).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
programs.name: Low-Entropy Pressure Decay
programs.trading_idea: This is not an identification claim about scheduled execution: daily OHLCV cannot distinguish mechanical flow from informed trading. Instead, it tests whether a persistent, unusually participatory one-sided price-pressure sequence becomes progressively less price-effective while its return-volume states remain repetitive; that configuration is a candidate for transitory liquidity pressure and a subsequent partial reversal. The reversal sign is conditional and must be evaluated net of known volume-impact, entropy, impulse-response, and liquidity-resilience signals, as well as trading costs.
programs.description: All quantities are calculated after the close of date t using only bars dated t or earlier. Let r_t = close_t / close_{t-1} - 1. Define relative volume RV_t = volume_t / median(volume_{t-20},...,volume_{t-1}); require all 20 reference observations to be positive and finite, and otherwise set the signal to NaN. Define daily signed participation x_t = sign(r_t) * RV_t, with sign(0)=0. Over the fixed six-bar candidate episode t-5 through t, define signed pressure P_t = sum(x_j), episode direction s_t = sign(P_t), and require: |P_t| >= 3, mean(RV_j) >= 1, and at least five of the six x_j values have sign equal to s_t. This is a fully trailing pressure/participation screen, not a label of eventual execution completion. For return-volume transition entropy, assign each valid day j one of four states: positive-or-zero return with RV_j < 1, positive-or-zero return with RV_j >= 1, negative return with RV_j < 1, or negative return with RV_j >= 1. Using the fixed ten-day window t-9 through t, count the nine adjacent ordered state transitions, form their empirical probabilities p_ab across the 16 possible transitions, and calculate H_t = -sum(p_ab * log(p_ab)) / log(16), treating 0*log(0) as zero. Require H_t <= 0.50. Define directional impact i_j = max(0, s_t * r_j) / RV_j. Let I_prior be the mean of i_j over t-5 through t-3 and I_recent the mean over t-2 through t. Require I_prior > 0 and I_recent <= 0.75 * I_prior. The raw score is S_t = -s_t * (|P_t| / 6) * (1 - H_t) * max(0, 1 - I_recent / I_prior), and is zero when any qualification condition fails. Thus absorbed selling produces a positive score and absorbed buying a negative score. The tradable implementation must cross-sectionally residualize S_t, at the same signal date, against the contemporaneous standardized scores of causal_volume_state_entropy_continuation, range_volume_elasticity_breakout, causal_impulse_response_skew, and kalman_liquidity_resilience_impulse; sector fixed effects and log(marketCap) may additionally be neutralized. This residualization is a portfolio-construction requirement rather than an additional input to the OHLCV calculation. All windows, thresholds, and comparisons are fixed as stated; no centered windows, future episode labels, or full-sample normalizations are used.

"""The signal is a conditional liquidity-replenishment hypothesis, not an identification of closing-auction or forced-sale flow. A stock that experiences an unusually large one-day downside return, yet closes materially above its intraday low and has elevated volume, may reflect temporarily exhausted selling and subsequent liquidity-provider/fundamental-buyer absorption. The trade is restricted away from dates on which a newly public negative earnings or revenue surprise is observed, because such events are more plausibly information-driven and may continue to drift downward."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_negative_surprise(surprise: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify only the date on which a negative PIT surprise becomes new."""
    previous = surprise.shift(1)
    changed = surprise.notna() & (previous.isna() | surprise.ne(previous))
    return changed & surprise.lt(0.0)


def _sector_residual(
    raw: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Residualize each row against sufficiently populated sector medians."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=raw.index, columns=raw.columns, dtype=float)

    for row_num in range(len(raw.index)):
        values = raw.iloc[row_num]
        labels = sector.iloc[row_num]
        active_mask = eligible.iloc[row_num] & values.notna() & labels.notna()

        if not active_mask.any():
            continue

        active_values = values.loc[active_mask].astype(float)
        active_labels = labels.loc[active_mask]
        universe_median = active_values.median()

        grouped = active_values.groupby(active_labels)
        sector_median = grouped.transform("median")
        sector_count = grouped.transform("count")
        benchmark = sector_median.where(sector_count.ge(5), universe_median)
        result.loc[result.index[row_num], active_values.index] = active_values - benchmark

    return result


def _winsorize_cross_section(raw: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally winsorize each day's eligible cross-section at 1% and 99%."""
    masked = raw.where(eligible)
    lower = masked.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = masked.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return masked.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


@register_factor
class NewsVetoedFreshAuctionVarianceRepair(BaseFactor):
    """Downside recovery innovations screened for newly released bad news."""

    factor_id = "news_vetoed_fresh_auction_variance_repair"
    name = "Downside Recovery Innovation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks fresh standardized downside moves that recover above the daily "
        "range midpoint on abnormal volume, residualized against sector peers "
        "and vetoed on newly public negative earnings or revenue surprises."
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]

        finite_close = close.where(np.isfinite(close))
        finite_high = high.where(np.isfinite(high))
        finite_low = low.where(np.isfinite(low))
        finite_volume = volume.where(np.isfinite(volume))

        previous_close = finite_close.shift(1)
        ret = finite_close / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        ret = ret.where(np.isfinite(ret))

        realized_vol = np.sqrt((ret * ret).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean())
        realized_vol = realized_vol.where(np.isfinite(realized_vol))

        range_width = finite_high - finite_low
        valid_range = (
            finite_close.notna()
            & finite_high.notna()
            & finite_low.notna()
            & finite_high.gt(finite_low)
        )
        clv = 2.0 * (finite_close - finite_low) / range_width.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        clv = clv.where(valid_range, 0.0).where(np.isfinite(clv), 0.0)

        dollar_volume = finite_close * finite_volume
        valid_dollar_volume = (
            finite_close.gt(0.0)
            & finite_volume.gt(0.0)
            & dollar_volume.gt(0.0)
            & dollar_volume.notna()
        )
        dollar_volume = dollar_volume.where(valid_dollar_volume)
        median_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        abnormal_volume = dollar_volume / median_dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        abnormal_volume = abnormal_volume.clip(lower=0.25, upper=5.0)
        volume_multiplier = np.log1p(abnormal_volume)

        standardized_move = ret / realized_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        downside = (-standardized_move).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        upside = standardized_move.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        recovery = clv.clip(lower=0.0)
        upside_reversal = (-clv).clip(lower=0.0)

        base_eligible = (
            ret.notna()
            & realized_vol.notna()
            & realized_vol.gt(0.0)
            & valid_dollar_volume
            & median_dollar_volume.notna()
            & median_dollar_volume.gt(0.0)
            & abnormal_volume.notna()
            & volume_multiplier.notna()
            & sector.notna()
        )

        liquidity_cutoff = median_dollar_volume.where(base_eligible).quantile(0.20, axis=1)
        liquid_enough = median_dollar_volume.gt(liquidity_cutoff, axis=0)

        negative_news = (
            _fresh_negative_surprise(eps_surprise)
            | _fresh_negative_surprise(revenue_surprise)
        )
        eligible = base_eligible & liquid_enough & ~negative_news

        downside_raw = (downside * recovery * volume_multiplier).where(eligible)
        upside_raw = (upside * upside_reversal * volume_multiplier).where(eligible)

        downside_winsorized = _winsorize_cross_section(downside_raw, eligible)
        upside_winsorized = _winsorize_cross_section(upside_raw, eligible)

        downside_residual = _sector_residual(downside_winsorized, sector, eligible)
        upside_residual = _sector_residual(upside_winsorized, sector, eligible)

        long_candidate = eligible & downside_residual.gt(0.0) & ~upside_residual.gt(0.0)
        scores = rank(downside_residual.where(eligible))
        return scores.where(long_candidate, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

Define dollar volume DV_t = close_t*volume_t and the causal abnormal-volume ratio AV_t = DV_t / median(DV_{t-19},...,DV_t). The eligible universe at t consists of names with valid signal inputs, non-null sector labels, and trailing median dollar volume above the contemporaneous 20th percentile of eligible names; this modest liquidity screen is intended to reduce the most severe implementation-cost exposure rather than to infer auction participation. Cross-sectionally on date t, winsorize Sraw_t at the 1st and 99th percentiles. A negative-news event occurs only on t when (epsChange_t and epsSurprise_t < 0) or (revenueChange_t and revenueSurprise_t < 0). Such a name is excluded on that date; the forward-filled surprise value does not veto later dates unless a newly stamped value changes again. It is not a short signal and is not assigned a negative factor score: upside/reversal candidates are merely excluded because daily OHLCV does not establish a comparably reliable forced-buying or inventory-unwind mechanism. Signal formation occurs after the t close; a tradable implementation enters at the t+1 open and exits at the t+7 open, producing a six-daily-bar holding return open_{t+7}/open_{t+1}-1. """A large negative opening jump that remains unrepaired through the completed session, closes near the session low, and occurs on unusually high volume is treated as evidence of unresolved sell-side pressure rather than a corrected auction mispricing. The mechanism is asymmetric downside-order excitation: a sharp decline can trigger risk-limit reductions, stop-loss activity, margin-related selling, and execution of pre-existing sell programs, while the failed intraday recovery indicates that natural buyers did not absorb the supply. The factor therefore shorts names with fresh, high-participation downside jump stress and takes the opposite side in names without such stress, entered only after the session has closed."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_winsorized_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize each date at 1/99 percentiles, then use population z-scores."""
    lower = values.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = values.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    clipped = values.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    std = clipped.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(std, axis=0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class AsymmetricDownsideJumpPersistence(BaseFactor):
    """Fresh high-volume downside auction stress with failed intraday repair."""

    factor_id = "asymmetric_downside_jump_persistence"
    name = "Downside Auction Stress Persistence"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Shorts fresh, unusually large downside opening gaps that fail to recover, "
        "close near the low, and arrive with abnormal participation; the negative "
        "score is strongest when the event is not part of repeated prior gap stress."
    )
    window_length = 26
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1).where(close.shift(1) > 0.0)
        safe_open = open_.where(open_ > 0.0)
        safe_high = high.where(high > 0.0)
        safe_low = low.where(low > 0.0)

        gap = np.log(safe_open / prior_close)
        log_range_sq = np.log(safe_high / safe_low).pow(2)
        sigma = log_range_sq.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().pow(0.5)
        sigma = sigma.where(sigma > 0.0)

        jump = (-gap / sigma).clip(lower=0.0)

        prior_volume_mean = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        abnormal_volume = volume / prior_volume_mean.where(prior_volume_mean > 0.0)

        recovery = (close - open_) / (prior_close - open_).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        session_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        location = (close - low) / session_range

        expansion = gap.abs() / sigma
        prior_expansion_event = expansion.ge(1.0).where(expansion.notna())
        repeated_count = (
            prior_expansion_event.shift(1)
            .astype(float)
            .rolling(5, min_periods=5)
            .sum()
        )
        freshness = 1.0 - repeated_count / 5.0

        valid = (
            gap.notna()
            & sigma.notna()
            & abnormal_volume.notna()
            & recovery.notna()
            & location.notna()
            & freshness.notna()
            & np.isfinite(jump)
            & np.isfinite(abnormal_volume)
            & np.isfinite(recovery)
            & np.isfinite(location)
            & (volume >= 0.0)
        )

        ranked_jump = jump.where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        ranked_volume = abnormal_volume.where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        qualifies = (
            valid
            & (gap < 0.0)
            & (jump >= 1.5)
            & (ranked_jump >= 0.80)
            & (abnormal_volume >= 1.25)
            & (ranked_volume >= 0.70)
            & (recovery <= 0.25)
            & (location <= 0.35)
        )

        recovery_component = 1.0 - recovery.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        raw_stress = (
            freshness
            * ((ranked_jump - 0.80) / 0.20)
            * ((ranked_volume - 0.70) / 0.30)
            * recovery_component
            * (1.0 - location)
        ).where(qualifies, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        standardized_stress = _cross_sectional_winsorized_zscore(raw_stress)
        return (-standardized_stress).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

programs.code:
"""The revised mechanism is not an assertion that unobserved stop-losses or dealer hedges are directly identified. Instead, a first close below a recently high-participation price region, combined with moderate abnormal trading activity and a close near the daily low, is interpreted as a publicly observable adverse-selection and bad-news-amplification event: liquidity suppliers infer that selling information or urgency remains unresolved and price discovery can continue over the following week. To separate this from likely capitulation, the signal excludes exceptionally large volume spikes, which are more plausibly associated with supply exhaustion and reversal."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _barrier_failure_score(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Construct causal 20-bar decayed volume-profile barrier failures.

    The profile at row t is built exclusively from rows t-20 through t-1.
    Each daily bar's full volume is allocated to the bin containing its
    typical price, an explicit daily-bar approximation to volume-at-price.
    """
    index = close.index
    columns = close.columns
    n_rows, n_cols = close.shape
    output = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)

    high_values = high.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    low_values = low.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    close_values = close.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    volume_values = volume.to_numpy(dtype=float)

    decay_weights = np.power(0.94, np.arange(19, -1, -1, dtype=float))

    for t in range(20, n_rows):
        hist_high = high_values[t - 20:t]
        hist_low = low_values[t - 20:t]
        hist_close = close_values[t - 20:t]
        hist_volume = volume_values[t - 20:t]

        current_high = high_values[t]
        current_low = low_values[t]
        current_close = close_values[t]
        previous_close = close_values[t - 1]

        historical_valid = (
            np.isfinite(hist_high)
            & np.isfinite(hist_low)
            & np.isfinite(hist_close)
            & np.isfinite(hist_volume)
            & (hist_volume >= 0.0)
            & (hist_high >= hist_low)
        )
        current_valid = (
            np.isfinite(current_high)
            & np.isfinite(current_low)
            & np.isfinite(current_close)
            & np.isfinite(previous_close)
            & np.isfinite(volume_values[t])
            & (volume_values[t] >= 0.0)
            & (current_high > current_low)
        )

        for c in range(n_cols):
            if not current_valid[c] or not np.all(historical_valid[:, c]):
                continue

            history_low = hist_low[:, c]
            history_high = hist_high[:, c]
            history_close = hist_close[:, c]
            history_volume = hist_volume[:, c]
            history_typical = (history_high + history_low + history_close) / 3.0

            if not np.all(np.isfinite(history_typical)):
                continue

            lower_bound = float(np.min(history_low))
            upper_bound = float(np.max(history_high))
            if not np.isfinite(lower_bound) or not np.isfinite(upper_bound):
                continue
            if upper_bound <= lower_bound:
                continue

            bin_width = (upper_bound - lower_bound) / 10.0
            if not np.isfinite(bin_width) or bin_width <= 0.0:
                continue

            bin_index = np.floor((history_typical - lower_bound) / bin_width).astype(int)
            bin_index = np.clip(bin_index, 0, 9)
            decayed_volume = np.bincount(
                bin_index,
                weights=history_volume * decay_weights,
                minlength=10,
            ).astype(float)

            lower_edges = lower_bound + bin_width * np.arange(10, dtype=float)
            eligible = lower_edges > current_close[c]
            if not np.any(eligible):
                continue

            eligible_indices = np.flatnonzero(eligible)
            eligible_volume = decayed_volume[eligible_indices]
            # np.argmax selects the first maximum, implementing lower-price tie break.
            barrier_bin = eligible_indices[int(np.argmax(eligible_volume))]
            barrier = lower_edges[barrier_bin]

            fresh_breach = (
                previous_close[c] >= barrier and current_close[c] < barrier
            )
            if not fresh_breach:
                output[t, c] = 0.0
                continue

            historical_median_volume = float(np.median(history_volume))
            if (
                not np.isfinite(historical_median_volume)
                or historical_median_volume <= 0.0
            ):
                continue

            relative_volume = volume_values[t, c] / historical_median_volume
            close_location = (
                (current_close[c] - current_low[c])
                / (current_high[c] - current_low[c])
            )
            if (
                not np.isfinite(relative_volume)
                or not np.isfinite(close_location)
                or relative_volume < 1.5
                or relative_volume > 3.0
                or close_location > 0.25
            ):
                output[t, c] = 0.0
                continue

            output[t, c] = np.log(relative_volume) * (1.0 - close_location)

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=index, columns=columns)


@register_factor
class AuditableFreshBarrierFailureExcitation(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks fresh downside failures of high-participation price barriers."""

    factor_id = "fresh_costbasis_barrier_failure_excitation"
    name = "Auditable Fresh Barrier-Failure Excitation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of a causal daily-bar volume-profile barrier "
        "failure: a first close below a recently high-participation region, "
        "with moderate abnormal volume and a close near the low. Higher "
        "values denote stronger bearish adverse-selection excitation."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        raw_score = _barrier_failure_score(
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["close"],
            data["volume"],
        )
        return rank(raw_score)

For each historical bar s, define typical price P_s=(high_s+low_s+close_s)/3 and assign all volume_s to the single price bin containing P_s; this is an explicit daily-bar proxy allocation and does not claim to observe intraday volume-at-price. Divide [A,B] into exactly 10 equal-width bins, with the final bin including its upper endpoint. The decayed bin volume is V_j=sum_s volume_s*0.94^(t-1-s) for observations allocated to bin j. Among bins whose lower edge is strictly above close_t, select the bin with the greatest V_j; break ties by selecting the lower-priced bin. Its lower edge is the barrier K_t. Define a fresh breach as 1 when close_(t-1)>=K_t and close_t<K_t, evaluating both closes against the same date-t, history-derived barrier; otherwise it is 0. Define relative volume RV_t=volume_t/median(volume_(t-20),...,volume_(t-1)); require a positive finite denominator and retain only 1.5<=RV_t<=3.0. Define close-location CLV_t=(close_t-low_t)/(high_t-low_t); if high_t<=low_t, set the observation missing. Retain only CLV_t<=0.25. The raw downside-excitation score is fresh_breach_t*log(RV_t)*(1-CLV_t) for retained observations and zero for valid non-events. The reported factor is the same-date cross-sectional percentile rank of this raw score, where a higher value denotes a stronger bearish event and is expected to predict lower six-bar forward returns. Incremental validity should be assessed by cross-sectionally residualizing this score against prospect_costbasis_supply_skew, causal_impulse_response_skew, and range_volume_elasticity_breakout where those existing factor outputs are available, and by testing net returns after realistic spread, impact, and borrow costs.

programs.code:
"""A downward traverse through a historically high-turnover price region is treated not as a literal investor inventory ledger, but as a public reference-price breach that can coincide with one-sided liquidity demand and reduced displayed-liquidity resilience. The negative-return prediction is restricted to breaches completed with unusually high trading volume and a close near the bar low, conditions consistent with unresolved sell-side pressure rather than an intraday dip that was absorbed. Because a breach can also mark selling exhaustion and support, this is explicitly an incremental conditional activation signal whose sign and value must be tested after controlling for the existing prospect_costbasis_supply_skew factor."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _barrier_activation(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute a causal, exponentially decayed volume-at-price breach signal."""
    close_values = close.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    high_values = high.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    low_values = low.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    volume_values = volume.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)

    n_rows, n_cols = close_values.shape
    output = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    typical_price = (high_values + low_values + close_values) / 3.0

    # At t, observations t-126 through t-1 have ages 126 through 1.
    ages = np.arange(126, 0, -1, dtype=float)
    decay = np.exp(-np.log(2.0) * ages / 21.0)[:, None]

    prior_volume = (
        volume.shift(1)
        .rolling(20, min_periods=20)
        .mean()
        .to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    )
    epsilon = 1.0e-12

    for t in range(126, n_rows):
        previous_close = close_values[t - 1]
        current_close = close_values[t]
        current_high = high_values[t]
        current_low = low_values[t]
        current_volume = volume_values[t]
        average_volume = prior_volume[t]

        width = 0.005 * previous_close
        hist_tp = typical_price[t - 126 : t]
        hist_volume = volume_values[t - 126 : t]

        valid_width = np.isfinite(width) & (width > 0.0)
        valid_history = (
            np.isfinite(hist_tp)
            & np.isfinite(hist_volume)
            & (hist_volume >= 0.0)
            & valid_width[None, :]
        )
        weighted_volume = np.where(valid_history, hist_volume * decay, 0.0)
        total_profile = weighted_volume.sum(axis=0)

        scaled_price = np.zeros_like(hist_tp, dtype=float)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            np.divide(
                hist_tp,
                width[None, :],
                out=scaled_price,
                where=valid_history,
            )
        bin_centers = np.rint(scaled_price) * width[None, :]

        crossed_down = (
            np.isfinite(current_close)
            & np.isfinite(previous_close)
            & (current_close < previous_close)
        )
        crossed_bins = (
            valid_history
            & (bin_centers >= current_close[None, :])
            & (bin_centers < previous_close[None, :])
            & crossed_down[None, :]
        )
        crossed_mass = np.where(crossed_bins, weighted_volume, 0.0).sum(axis=0)

        bar_range = current_high - current_low
        valid_range = np.isfinite(bar_range) & (bar_range > 0.0)
        close_location = np.full(n_cols, 0.5, dtype=float)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            np.divide(
                current_high - current_close,
                bar_range,
                out=close_location,
                where=valid_range,
            )
        close_location = np.clip(close_location, 0.0, 1.0)

        relative_volume = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
        valid_average = np.isfinite(average_volume) & (average_volume >= 0.0)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            np.divide(
                current_volume,
                average_volume + epsilon,
                out=relative_volume,
                where=np.isfinite(current_volume) & valid_average,
            )
        relative_volume = np.minimum(np.maximum(relative_volume, 0.0), 5.0)

        eligible = (
            valid_width
            & np.isfinite(current_close)
            & np.isfinite(previous_close)
            & np.isfinite(current_high)
            & np.isfinite(current_low)
            & np.isfinite(current_volume)
            & valid_average
            & (total_profile > epsilon)
        )
        activation = np.full(n_cols, np.nan, dtype=float)
        activation[eligible] = (
            crossed_mass[eligible]
            / (total_profile[eligible] + epsilon)
            * relative_volume[eligible]
            * close_location[eligible]
        )
        output[t] = activation

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)


@register_factor
class FreshCostbasisBarrierActivation(BaseFactor):
    """Negative ranked activation of high-turnover reference-price breaches."""

    factor_id = "fresh_costbasis_barrier_activation"
    name = "Residual Downside Barrier Activation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Negative cross-sectional rank of a causal 126-bar exponentially "
        "decayed volume-at-price barrier breach, activated only by high "
        "relative volume and closes near the daily low."
    )
    window_length = 127
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        activation = _barrier_activation(
            close,
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["volume"],
        )

        lower = activation.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = activation.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        winsorized = activation.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        score = -rank(winsorized)
        return score.where(activation.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)

The signal is observed only after completion of bar t and is executed no earlier than the next bar.
