"""OHLCV cannot identify dealer inventory, displayed depth, or informed versus forced flow. It can, however, provide a testable proxy for directional moves occurring with unusually high normalized range relative to recent dollar-volume participation. The hypothesis is that the incremental component of a thin-participation move that repeatedly closes at the same extreme bar edge is more prone to a six-bar reversal after controlling for an ordinary directional range-volume breakout signal."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_clip(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Clip each date's valid cross section at its 1st and 99th percentiles."""
    lower = df.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = df.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return df.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _event_residual_score(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute the causal event-only residual after cross-sectional control."""
    previous_close = close.shift(1)

    bar_valid = (
        open_.gt(0.0)
        & high.gt(0.0)
        & low.gt(0.0)
        & close.gt(0.0)
        & volume.gt(0.0)
        & high.gt(low)
        & previous_close.gt(0.0)
    )

    true_range = pd.concat(
        [
            high - low,
            (high - previous_close).abs(),
            (low - previous_close).abs(),
        ],
        axis=0,
    ).groupby(level=0, sort=False).max()
    atr = (true_range / previous_close).where(bar_valid)
    dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(bar_valid)

    atr = _cross_sectional_clip(atr).where(bar_valid)
    dollar_volume = _cross_sectional_clip(dollar_volume).where(bar_valid)

    valid_history = bar_valid.rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum().eq(20)
    med_atr = atr.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
    med_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()

    x = (
        np.log(atr / med_atr.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        - np.log(dollar_volume / med_dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    close_location = (
        2.0 * (close - low) / (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
    ).where(bar_valid)

    liquid_universe_cutoff = med_dollar_volume.quantile(0.20, axis=1)
    eligible = (
        valid_history
        & med_atr.notna()
        & med_dollar_volume.notna()
        & med_dollar_volume.ge(liquid_universe_cutoff, axis=0)
    )

    recent_participation = dollar_volume.shift(2).rolling(3, min_periods=3).median()
    prior_participation = dollar_volume.shift(3).rolling(3, min_periods=3).median()

    event = (
        eligible
        & x.gt(0.0)
        & x.gt(x.shift(3))
        & close_location.abs().ge(0.80)
        & close_location.shift(1).abs().ge(0.80)
        & np.sign(close_location).eq(np.sign(close_location.shift(1)))
        & dollar_volume.lt(med_dollar_volume)
        & recent_participation.lt(prior_participation)
    )

    log_return = np.log(close / previous_close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    raw_signal = (close_location * x).where(event)
    breakout_control = (log_return * x).where(event)

    event_count = event.sum(axis=1)
    numerator = (raw_signal * breakout_control).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    denominator = (breakout_control * breakout_control).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    beta = (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(
        event_count.ge(20) & denominator.gt(0.0), 0.0
    ).fillna(0.0)

    residual = (raw_signal - breakout_control.mul(beta, axis=0)).where(event)
    lower = residual.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = residual.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    winsorized = residual.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    event_rank = winsorized.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

    return (event_rank - 0.5).where(event, 0.0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class ThinParticipationImpactExhaustion(BaseFactor):
    """Residual edge-persistence score for thin-participation directional moves."""

    factor_id = "thin_participation_impact_exhaustion"
    name = "Edge-Persistence Thin-Participation Residual"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Event-only percentile rank of the edge-persistent, high range-per-"
        "volume residual after removing an ordinary directional breakout "
        "control; positive values identify upward thin-participation moves "
        "expected to exhaust over the next six bars."
    )
    window_length = 26
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        score = _event_residual_score(
            data["open"],
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            close,
            data["volume"],
        )
        return score.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

Exclude ticker-days with nonpositive OHLC prices, nonpositive volume, high_t <= low_t, or insufficient valid history through t-19. To limit abnormal prints, clip ATR and DV independently each day to their cross-sectional 1st and 99th percentiles before further calculations. The eligible cross-sectional universe is the remaining names whose 20-bar median clipped DV is at or above the 20th cross-sectional percentile of 20-bar median clipped DV. Define the 20-bar benchmarks medATR_t = median(ATR_{t-19:t}) and medDV_t = median(DV_{t-19:t}), and define the range-per-volume dislocation x_t = log(ATR_t / medATR_t) - log(DV_t / medDV_t). Define the signed close-location e_t = 2*(close_t-low_t)/(high_t-low_t)-1. An edge-persistence event E_t occurs only when: x_t > 0; x_t > x_{t-3} (a fixed three-bar rising-dislocation comparison); abs(e_t) >= 0.80 and abs(e_{t-1}) >= 0.80; sign(e_t) = sign(e_{t-1}) (two consecutive same-side edge closes); DV_t < medDV_t; and median(DV_{t-2:t}) < median(DV_{t-5:t-3}) (a fixed three-bar fading-participation comparison). The raw edge-persistence signal is S_t = E_t * e_t * x_t. To make this distinct from a generic range-volume breakout, construct the deterministic control B_t = log(close_t/close_{t-1}) * x_t, which captures the ordinary directional return-by-range-volume dislocation. Within the eligible E_t=1 names, estimate the no-intercept cross-sectional projection coefficient beta_t = sum(S_t*B_t)/sum(B_t^2), requiring at least 20 event names and positive denominator; otherwise assign a zero signal. The submitted residual is R_t = E_t*(S_t-beta_t*B_t). Winsorize R_t at the event-group 1st and 99th percentiles, convert it to a percentile rank within event names, and set the final score to rank(R_t)-0.5; non-events receive zero. High scores represent upward edge-persistent thin-participation moves and are expected to have negative subsequent returns; low scores represent downward counterparts and are expected to have positive subsequent returns. Compute using only the completed daily bar at t, trade no earlier than the t+1 open, and measure the six-bar holding-period outcome from t+1 to t+7.

"""Peer-synchronised auction absorption conditioned on return-volume memory.

Mechanism: common peer impact identifies correlated liquidity pressure, while an
ordinary-volume refilled downside auction gap indicates that opening inventory was
absorbed.  The signal acts only when the current negative return-volume state has
historically transitioned toward positive returns.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


_HISTORY = 126


def _leave_one_out_breadth(
    elevated: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal same-date peer breadth with industry/sector/universe fallback."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=eligible.index, columns=eligible.columns)
    for i in range(len(eligible.index)):
        mask = eligible.iloc[i].astype(float)
        events = (elevated.iloc[i] & eligible.iloc[i]).astype(float)
        ind = industry.iloc[i]
        sec = sector.iloc[i]

        ind_n = mask.groupby(ind).transform("sum") - mask
        ind_e = events.groupby(ind).transform("sum") - events
        sec_n = mask.groupby(sec).transform("sum") - mask
        sec_e = events.groupby(sec).transform("sum") - events

        universe_n = mask.sum() - mask
        universe_e = events.sum() - events
        universe = universe_e / universe_n.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        sector_breadth = sec_e / sec_n.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        industry_breadth = ind_e / ind_n.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        use_industry = ind_n.ge(9.0)
        use_sector = (~use_industry) & sec_n.ge(9.0)
        breadth = universe.where(~use_sector, sector_breadth)
        breadth = breadth.where(~use_industry, industry_breadth)
        result.iloc[i] = breadth.where(eligible.iloc[i], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    return result


def _negative_state_reversal_expectation(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Dirichlet-shrunk, trailing probability of a positive next return state.

    State definitions use only current and prior observations.  Transition counts
    are shifted by one bar, so the estimate available at t is based only on
    transitions completed no later than t-1.
    """
    safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
    ret = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0
    ret_scale = ret.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
    ret_state = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    ret_state = ret_state.mask(ret.gt(0.5 * ret_scale), 1.0)
    ret_state = ret_state.mask(ret.lt(-0.5 * ret_scale), -1.0)
    ret_state = ret_state.where(ret.notna() & ret_scale.gt(0.0))

    vol_base = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    vol_ratio = volume / vol_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    vol_state = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    vol_state = vol_state.mask(vol_ratio.lt(0.8), 0.0)
    vol_state = vol_state.mask(vol_ratio.gt(1.5), 2.0)
    vol_state = vol_state.where(vol_ratio.notna() & volume.ge(0.0))

    state = ((ret_state + 1.0) * 3.0 + vol_state).where(
        ret_state.notna() & vol_state.notna()
    )
    origin = state.shift(1)
    destination = ret_state
    valid = origin.notna() & destination.notna()
    marker = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns).where(valid)
    total = marker.rolling(_HISTORY, min_periods=_HISTORY).sum().shift(1)
    plus_total = (destination.eq(1.0).astype(float).where(valid).rolling(
        _HISTORY, min_periods=_HISTORY
    ).sum().shift(1))
    minus_total = (destination.eq(-1.0).astype(float).where(valid).rolling(
        _HISTORY, min_periods=_HISTORY
    ).sum().shift(1))
    pooled = (plus_total - minus_total) / total.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    expectation = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    for code in range(9):
        count = (origin.eq(float(code)).astype(float).where(valid).rolling(
            _HISTORY, min_periods=_HISTORY
        ).sum().shift(1))
        plus = ((origin.eq(float(code)) & destination.eq(1.0)).astype(float).where(valid).rolling(
            _HISTORY, min_periods=_HISTORY
        ).sum().shift(1))
        minus = ((origin.eq(float(code)) & destination.eq(-1.0)).astype(float).where(valid).rolling(
            _HISTORY, min_periods=_HISTORY
        ).sum().shift(1))
        shrunk = ((plus - minus) + 12.0 * pooled) / (count + 12.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        expectation = expectation.where(~state.eq(float(code)), shrunk)

    active = ret_state.eq(-1.0) & total.ge(float(_HISTORY))
    return expectation.where(active, 0.0).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)


def _downside_auction_refill(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Strength of a material downside gap that refills on ordinary volume."""
    prior_close = close.shift(1)
    valid = open_.gt(0.0) & close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0) & volume.gt(0.0)
    gap = np.log((open_ / prior_close).where(valid))
    downside_gap = (-gap).clip(lower=0.0)
    refill = ((close - open_) / (prior_close - open_).replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(
        lower=0.0, upper=1.0
    )

    log_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume.gt(0.0)))
    mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
    std = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
    volume_z = (log_volume - mean) / std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ordinary = np.exp(-volume_z.clip(lower=-3.0, upper=3.0).abs())

    prior_ret = prior_close / prior_close.shift(1) - 1.0
    prior_scale = prior_ret.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
    materiality = (downside_gap / prior_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(
        lower=0.0, upper=2.0
    ) / 2.0
    return (refill * ordinary * materiality).where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class PeerSynchronizedAuctionAbsorptionMemory(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "peer_synchronized_auction_absorption_memory"
    name = "Peer-Synchronized Auction Absorption Memory"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Common peer liquidity impact and a low close identify broad pressure; "
        "a refilled downside auction gap and positive stressed-state transition "
        "memory identify absorbed pressure likely to rebound."
    )
    window_length = 146
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "industry", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        bar_range = high - low
        eligible = (
            close.gt(0.0) & high.notna() & low.notna() & volume.gt(0.0)
            & bar_range.ge(0.0)
        )

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(eligible)
        lower = dollar_volume.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = dollar_volume.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        clipped_dollar = dollar_volume.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        impact = (bar_range / close.replace(0.0, np.nan)) / clipped_dollar.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        impact_rank = impact.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        elevated = impact_rank.ge(0.90) & eligible
        breadth = _leave_one_out_breadth(
            elevated, eligible, data["industry"], data["sector"]
        )

        close_near_low = 1.0 - (close - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_near_low = close_near_low.where(bar_range.gt(0.0), 0.5).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        auction = _downside_auction_refill(data["open"], close, volume)
        reversal = _negative_state_reversal_expectation(close, volume)

        raw = (impact_rank * breadth * close_near_low * auction * reversal).where(eligible)
        return raw.rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)

programs.trading_idea: A broad industry liquidity-impact episode with closes near the low is more likely to be a correlated liquidity withdrawal or forced-risk-transfer event than firm-specific bad information. A partially refilled downside opening gap on ordinary volume identifies names where auction inventory was absorbed despite the broad pressure, while the return-volume transition table requires that the name's current stressed state has historically been followed by a positive signed return. Neither parent alone distinguishes common forced selling from informed idiosyncratic selling and then verifies that the particular return-volume state has a repeatable reversal tendency; their interaction isolates absorbed systemic pressure likely to rebound over the next six bars.
programs.description: The factor ranks stocks with elevated range-per-dollar-volume, broad leave-one-out industry or sector impact breadth, a low close, an ordinary-volume refilled downside auction gap, and a historically positive next-state expectation following the current negative return-volume state.

"""Quality-disclosure latency conditioned on allocator-flow exhaustion.

Mechanism: positive cash-backed quality updates usually drift when their initial
industry-relative reaction is muted.  A pre-existing quality-premium regime,
regular volume-confirmed buying, and a short-horizon momentum interruption
instead identify mechanical allocator completion, turning that same apparent
latency into a near-term fade.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _group_rank(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
    minimum_names: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile ranks within a static label group."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels.eq(label)].tolist()
        sample = values.loc[:, cols].where(eligible.loc[:, cols])
        enough = sample.notna().sum(axis=1).ge(minimum_names)
        lo = sample.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
        hi = sample.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
        clipped = sample.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)
        out.loc[:, cols] = clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True).where(enough, np.nan)
    return out


def _group_zscore(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
    minimum_names: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorized contemporaneous z-score within static groups."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels.eq(label)].tolist()
        sample = values.loc[:, cols].where(eligible.loc[:, cols])
        count = sample.notna().sum(axis=1)
        lo = sample.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
        hi = sample.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
        clipped = sample.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)
        mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
        scale = clipped.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        out.loc[:, cols] = clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(scale, axis=0).where(
            count.ge(minimum_names), np.nan
        )
    return out


def _latest_report_changes(
    fields: list[pd.DataFrame],
) -> tuple[list[pd.DataFrame], pd.DataFrame]:
    """Extract causal synchronous report innovations from PIT step functions."""
    changes: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    transitions: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    for field in fields:
        prior = field.ffill().shift(1)
        changed = field.notna() & prior.notna() & field.ne(prior)
        transitions.append(changed)
        changes.append(field.sub(prior))

    event = transitions[0].copy()
    for changed in transitions[1:]:
        event = event & changed
    return [change.where(event).ffill() for change in changes], event


def _leave_one_out_industry_return(
    own_return: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.Series,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return less the contemporaneous leave-one-out industry mean return."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=own_return.index, columns=own_return.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(industry.dropna()):
        cols = industry.index[industry.eq(label)].tolist()
        sample = own_return.loc[:, cols].where(eligible.loc[:, cols])
        count = sample.notna().sum(axis=1)
        total = sample.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        peers = sample.rsub(total, axis=0).div(count.sub(1), axis=0)
        out.loc[:, cols] = (sample - peers).where(count.sub(1).ge(8), np.nan)
    return out


def _cadence_regularity(states: pd.DataFrame, valid: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Low entropy of trailing signed-return/relative-volume states."""
    entropy = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=states.index, columns=states.columns)
    for state in range(9):
        probability = states.eq(float(state)).where(valid).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        entropy = entropy - probability * np.log(probability.clip(lower=1e-8))
    observed = valid.astype(float).rolling(20, min_periods=15).sum()
    normalized = entropy / np.log(9.0)
    return (1.0 - normalized).where(observed.ge(15), np.nan).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)


@register_factor
class QualityUpdateCadenceExhaustionSwitch(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "quality_update_cadence_exhaustion_switch"
    name = "Quality Update Cadence Exhaustion Switch"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Trades muted positive cash-backed quality updates as continuation unless "
        "a positive quality-premium regime and regular pre-event buying identify "
        "mechanical-demand exhaustion, in which case it fades them."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "industry",
        "roic",
        "incomeQuality",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
        "assetGrowth",
        "debtGrowth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)
        sector = data["sector"].iloc[0]
        industry = data["industry"].iloc[0]

        fields = [
            data["roic"].astype(float),
            data["incomeQuality"].astype(float),
            data["freeCashFlowYield"].astype(float),
            data["assetGrowth"].astype(float),
            data["debtGrowth"].astype(float),
        ]
        innovations, event = _latest_report_changes(fields)

        fundamental_valid = fields[0].notna()
        for field in fields[1:]:
            fundamental_valid = fundamental_valid & field.notna()

        q_roic = _group_rank(fields[0], fundamental_valid, sector, 8)
        q_income = _group_rank(fields[1], fundamental_valid, sector, 8)
        q_fcf = _group_rank(fields[2], fundamental_valid, sector, 8)
        q_assets = _group_rank(fields[3], fundamental_valid, sector, 8)
        q_debt = _group_rank(fields[4], fundamental_valid, sector, 8)
        quality_level = (
            q_roic + q_income + q_fcf + (1.0 - q_assets) + (1.0 - q_debt)
        ) / 5.0

        quality_z = _group_zscore(
            quality_level, quality_level.notna(), sector, 8
        )
        daily_return = close.pct_change()
        realized_premium = (quality_z.shift(1) * daily_return).mean(axis=1)
        premium_mean = realized_premium.rolling(15, min_periods=10).mean()
        premium_vol = realized_premium.rolling(40, min_periods=25).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        quality_state = np.tanh((premium_mean / premium_vol).clip(-3.0, 3.0)).shift(1)
        positive_state = quality_state.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)

        lag_close = close.shift(1)
        lag_return = lag_close.pct_change()
        lag_volume = volume.shift(1)
        vol = lag_return.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        short_mom = lag_close.div(lag_close.shift(2)).sub(1.0).div(vol * np.sqrt(2.0))
        medium_mom = lag_close.div(lag_close.shift(15)).sub(1.0).div(vol * np.sqrt(15.0))
        momentum_valid = short_mom.notna() & medium_mom.notna() & quality_level.notna()
        short_rank = _group_rank(short_mom, momentum_valid, sector, 8)
        medium_rank = _group_rank(medium_mom, momentum_valid, sector, 8)
        interruption = (medium_rank - short_rank).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        positive_volume = lag_volume.where(lag_volume.gt(0.0))
        typical_volume = positive_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        relative_volume = lag_volume.div(typical_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        flow_valid = lag_return.notna() & relative_volume.notna() & lag_volume.gt(0.0)
        return_state = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(lag_return.to_numpy() < 0.0, 0.0, np.where(lag_return.to_numpy() > 0.0, 2.0, 1.0)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        volume_state = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(relative_volume.to_numpy() <= 0.80, 0.0, np.where(relative_volume.to_numpy() <= 1.20, 1.0, 2.0)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        regularity = _cadence_regularity(return_state * 3.0 + volume_state, flow_valid)
        pressure = (
            lag_return * relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        ).where(flow_valid).rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum().clip(lower=0.0)
        pressure_scale = (vol * np.sqrt(5.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        pressure_strength = np.tanh(pressure.div(pressure_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0))
        exhaustion = (
            positive_state.to_frame().reindex(close.index).iloc[:, 0]
            * quality_level.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
            * interruption
            * regularity
            * pressure_strength
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        liquid = (
            close.gt(0.0)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & close.mul(volume).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean().ge(5_000_000.0)
        )
        innovation_valid = liquid & innovations[0].notna()
        for innovation in innovations[1:]:
            innovation_valid = innovation_valid & innovation.notna()
        z_roic = _group_zscore(innovations[0], innovation_valid, industry, 8)
        z_income = _group_zscore(innovations[1], innovation_valid, industry, 8)
        z_fcf = _group_zscore(innovations[2], innovation_valid, industry, 8)
        z_assets = _group_zscore(innovations[3], innovation_valid, industry, 8)
        z_debt = _group_zscore(innovations[4], innovation_valid, industry, 8)
        update_quality = 0.30 * z_roic + 0.25 * z_income + 0.20 * z_fcf - 0.15 * z_assets - 0.10 * z_debt

        six_bar_return = close.div(close.shift(6)).sub(1.0)
        relative_return = _leave_one_out_industry_return(
            six_bar_return, liquid & six_bar_return.notna(), industry
        )
        relative_z = _group_zscore(
            relative_return, relative_return.notna(), industry, 9
        )
        positive_latency = (update_quality * (-relative_z)).clip(lower=0.0)
        raw = positive_latency.mul(1.0 - 2.0 * exhaustion).where(event, 0.0)
        return raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Quality Update Cadence Exhaustion Switch
programs.trading_idea: A positive cash-backed quality update with a muted industry-relative reaction normally has a disclosure-underreaction tail because investors have not fully incorporated the new information. That continuation is unreliable when the same stock is already a quality leader in a positive quality-premium regime and displays a pre-event pattern of regular, volume-confirmed buying with a short-horizon momentum interruption: the muted reaction then reflects an exhausted allocator program rather than investor inattention. The interaction therefore switches a conventional quality-update drift trade into a six-day fade only when latent mechanical demand appears to have completed.
programs.description: The signal identifies positive synchronous quality-report innovations whose six-day industry-relative price response is muted, then multiplies that latency signal by a pre-event quality-leadership buying-exhaustion state. It is positive for unexhausted disclosure underreaction and negative when the same update arrives into regular-buying completion risk.

programs.code:
"""Distribution-confirmed sector-rank unwind.

Mechanism: a medium-horizon sector leader that breaks down on unusually intense,
low-closing trading is more likely undergoing informed distribution than a benign
liquidity interruption.  The symmetric accumulation state validates rebounds in
prior sector laggards; the prior rank supplies the crowding context absent from
stand-alone volume and range signals.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_rank(
    values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame, minimum_size: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date percentile ranks within sectors, using only current information."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    labels = sector.reindex(index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for i in range(len(values.index)):
        row = values.iloc[i]
        row_labels = labels.iloc[i]
        eligible = row.notna() & row_labels.notna()
        if not bool(eligible.any()):
            continue
        for label in pd.unique(row_labels[eligible].to_numpy()):
            mask = eligible & row_labels.eq(label)
            count = int(mask.sum())
            if count >= minimum_size:
                out.iloc[i, np.flatnonzero(mask.to_numpy())] = (
                    row[mask].rank(method="average") / float(count)
                ).to_numpy()
    return out


def _sector_residual(
    values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame, minimum_size: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Contemporaneous sector residual, retaining only adequately populated groups."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    labels = sector.reindex(index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for i in range(len(values.index)):
        row = values.iloc[i]
        row_labels = labels.iloc[i]
        eligible = row.notna() & row_labels.notna()
        if not bool(eligible.any()):
            continue
        for label in pd.unique(row_labels[eligible].to_numpy()):
            mask = eligible & row_labels.eq(label)
            count = int(mask.sum())
            if count >= minimum_size:
                group = row[mask]
                out.iloc[i, np.flatnonzero(mask.to_numpy())] = (
                    group - group.mean()
                ).to_numpy()
    return out


@register_factor
class SectorRankInterruptDistributionUnwind(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sector_rank_interrupt_distribution_unwind"
    name = "Distribution-Confirmed Rank Unwind"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Scores sector leaders whose short-term interruption is confirmed by "
        "high-participation selling, versus sector laggards whose rebound is "
        "confirmed by high-participation accumulation."
    )
    window_length = 41
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        low = data["low"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        sector = data["sector"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        daily_ret = close / close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        vol = daily_ret.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)

        normalized: dict[int, pd.DataFrame] = {}
        for horizon in (2, 10, 20):
            trailing = close / close.shift(horizon).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
            normalized[horizon] = trailing / (vol * np.sqrt(float(horizon)))

        p2 = _sector_rank(normalized[2], sector, 8)
        p10 = _sector_rank(normalized[10], sector, 8)
        p20 = _sector_rank(normalized[20], sector, 8)
        residual_day = _sector_residual(daily_ret, sector, 8)

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        relative_volume = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        true_range = (high - low) / close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_range = true_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        relative_range = true_range / prior_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        span = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        location = ((close - low) / span).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        location = location.where(span.notna(), 0.5)

        activity = (relative_volume - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        range_shock = (relative_range - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        sell_confirmation = (
            activity * range_shock * (1.0 - location) * (-residual_day / vol).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
        )
        buy_confirmation = (
            activity * range_shock * location * (residual_day / vol).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
        )

        leader_interrupt = (
            (p10 >= 0.60) & (p20 >= 0.60) & (p2 <= 0.45)
        )
        laggard_rebound = (
            (p10 <= 0.40) & (p20 <= 0.40) & (p2 >= 0.55)
        )

        leader_strength = ((p10 + p20) / 2.0 - p2).clip(lower=0.0)
        laggard_strength = (p2 - (p10 + p20) / 2.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        score = (leader_strength * sell_confirmation).where(leader_interrupt)
        score = score.where(~laggard_rebound, -laggard_strength * buy_confirmation)

        return rank(score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Distribution-Confirmed Rank Unwind
programs.trading_idea: Medium-horizon sector leadership followed by a short-term decline is not automatically a benign catch-up opportunity: when that interruption occurs with abnormal volume, abnormal range, and a close near the low, it more likely reflects informed distribution or crowded-holder liquidation. Conversely, a sector laggard's short-term rebound is credible only when high-participation accumulation closes near the high. The interaction adds edge because relative-performance ranks identify the crowded prior trend, while the bar-state identifies whether the reversal is being validated by directional liquidity demand rather than being a low-information price fluctuation; the parent momentum signal alone cannot distinguish these cases and the parent state signal lacks the prior-trend context.
programs.description: Ranks 2-, 10-, and 20-day volatility-normalized returns within sector, then scores leader interruptions accompanied by sell-side volume/range/close-location confirmation versus laggard rebounds accompanied by buy-side confirmation. Higher values denote distribution-confirmed unwind risk and are expected to precede lower six-bar sector-relative returns.

programs.code:
"""Peer earnings disclosures can provide economically relevant, directionally signed information about near-term demand and operating conditions for firms with the same industry exposure that have not yet reported. The revised mechanism does not assume that peer news creates a separate valuation, cash-flow, anchoring, or overhead-supply unwind; it predicts that non-reporting peers move in the direction of a coherent, public industry-level earnings-and-revenue surprise. This shortens the causal chain to information propagation and avoids imposing an unsupported universally negative sign."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_event_scores(
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    reporter_quality: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute causal daily industry mean-surprise events and broadcast them.

    A valid event has at least three usable reporters, a two-thirds directional
    sign consensus, and an absolute mean quality-adjusted surprise of 0.15.
    Each row is independent and only contains information available on that bar.
    """
    output = np.full(reporter_quality.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)

    for row_number in range(len(reporter_quality.index)):
        industry_row = industry.iloc[row_number]
        quality_row = reporter_quality.iloc[row_number]

        observations = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "industry": industry_row,
                "quality": quality_row,
            }
        ).dropna(subset=["industry", "quality"])

        if observations.empty:
            continue

        observations["positive"] = (observations["quality"] > 0.0).astype(float)
        observations["negative"] = (observations["quality"] < 0.0).astype(float)

        grouped = observations.groupby("industry").agg(
            count=("quality", "count"),
            mean_quality=("quality", "mean"),
            positive=("positive", "sum"),
            negative=("negative", "sum"),
        )

        consensus = (
            (grouped["positive"] / grouped["count"] >= (2.0 / 3.0))
            | (grouped["negative"] / grouped["count"] >= (2.0 / 3.0))
        )
        valid = (
            (grouped["count"] >= 3.0)
            & consensus
            & (grouped["mean_quality"].abs() >= 0.15)
        )

        valid_means = grouped.loc[valid, "mean_quality"]
        if not valid_means.empty:
            output[row_number, :] = industry_row.map(valid_means).to_numpy(dtype=float)

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=reporter_quality.index, columns=reporter_quality.columns)


@register_factor
class DirectionalPeerFundamentalReadthrough(BaseFactor):
    """Signed industry earnings-surprise propagation to non-reporting peers."""

    factor_id = "peer_readthrough_model_risk_supply_unwind"
    name = "Directional Peer Fundamental Readthrough"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks non-reporting firms by the signed mean earnings and revenue "
        "surprise of a coherent same-industry reporter group, subject to a "
        "five-bar own-report blackout."
    )
    window_length = 6
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        industry = data["industry"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex(
            index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        )
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex(
            index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        )

        prior_eps_surprise = eps_surprise.shift(1)
        prior_revenue_surprise = revenue_surprise.shift(1)
        eps_report = eps_surprise.notna() & (
            prior_eps_surprise.isna() | eps_surprise.ne(prior_eps_surprise)
        )
        revenue_report = revenue_surprise.notna() & (
            prior_revenue_surprise.isna()
            | revenue_surprise.ne(prior_revenue_surprise)
        )
        reporter_flag = eps_report | revenue_report

        usable = (
            np.isfinite(eps_estimate)
            & np.isfinite(revenue_estimate)
            & np.isfinite(eps_surprise)
            & np.isfinite(revenue_surprise)
            & (eps_estimate.abs() > 0.0)
            & (revenue_estimate.abs() > 0.0)
            & reporter_flag
        )

        normalized_eps = (eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs()).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        normalized_revenue = (revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs()).clip(-0.25, 0.25)

        eps_percentile = normalized_eps.where(usable).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        revenue_percentile = normalized_revenue.where(usable).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        reporter_quality = 0.5 * eps_percentile + 0.5 * revenue_percentile - 0.5

        industry_score = _industry_event_scores(industry, reporter_quality)

        recent_own_reports = (
            reporter_flag.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum().eq(0.0)
        )
        eligible = recent_own_reports & industry_score.notna()
        raw_receiver_score = industry_score.where(eligible)

        ranked = 2.0 * raw_receiver_score.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        return ranked.where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Directional Peer Fundamental Readthrough
programs.trading_idea: Peer earnings disclosures can provide economically relevant, directionally signed information about near-term demand and operating conditions for firms with the same industry exposure that have not yet reported. The revised mechanism does not assume that peer news creates a separate valuation, cash-flow, anchoring, or overhead-supply unwind; it predicts that non-reporting peers move in the direction of a coherent, public industry-level earnings-and-revenue surprise. This shortens the causal chain to information propagation and avoids imposing an unsupported universally negative sign.
programs.description: At each daily bar t after the close, define a reporter as a ticker for which either epsSurprise or revenueSurprise newly becomes non-null or changes from its value at t-1; this uses the point-in-time availability timestamps already supplied by the feed. A reporter is usable only when epsEstimate, revenueEstimate, epsSurprise, and revenueSurprise are finite and abs(epsEstimate)>0 and abs(revenueEstimate)>0. For each usable reporter, compute e=(epsSurprise/abs(epsEstimate)).clip(-1,1) and r=(revenueSurprise/abs(revenueEstimate)).clip(-0.25,0.25), then compute q=0.5*rank_pct(e)+0.5*rank_pct(r)-0.5, where each percentile rank is calculated cross-sectionally among that day's usable reporters and mapped to [-0.5,0.5]. The peer universe for a receiver is all usable reporters with the same non-null industry label. An industry event is valid only when at least three usable reporters exist, at least two-thirds have the same sign of q, and abs(mean(q))>=0.15. Its signed readthrough statistic is I=mean(q) across those reporters; direction is explicitly used, unlike the original absolute-informativeness trigger. Eligible receivers are tickers in a valid-event industry that are not reporters on t and had no reporter flag during t-1 through t-5, a fixed five-bar own-report blackout. The receiver score is I, cross-sectionally percentile-ranked among eligible receivers and mapped to [-1,1]; higher scores predict higher six-bar returns. Orders are formed only after bar t has closed and entered at the next tradable bar's open, t+1, so same-day close, volume, and after-close report information is never used for same-day execution. The original EPS-optimism, revenue-growth, cash-realization, valuation, and volume-cost-basis/overhead-inventory gates are intentionally removed: no epsEstimate revision, revenueGrowth, incomeQuality/freeCashFlow proxy, peRatio/earningsYield valuation metric, or price-volume inventory measure enters the score. This implementation fingerprint is therefore a signed, minimum-three-reporter, industry-mean surprise propagation signal with a fixed own-report blackout, rather than an interaction of peer shocks with receiver revisions, cash quality, valuation, or reference-price overhang.

programs.code:
"""Inventory-gated common-news impact fade.

Mechanism: a leave-one-out industry surprise cluster identifies common information,
but an aligned receiver move is transient when it traverses an abnormally thin
supply curve while substantial recent volume remains above the current price.
The resulting score is deliberately a fade: high values represent upward
common-news overshoots likely to reverse over the next six bars.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _finite(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return frame.astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _fresh_update(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    prior = value.shift(1)
    return value.notna() & (prior.isna() | value.ne(prior))


def _event_zscore(value: pd.DataFrame, event: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    sample = value.where(event)
    median = sample.median(axis=1)
    mad = sample.sub(median, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1)
    fallback = sample.std(axis=1)
    scale = (1.4826 * mad).where(mad.gt(1.0e-8), fallback)
    return sample.sub(median, axis=0).div(scale.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0).clip(-4.0, 4.0)


def _industry_sum(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum").T


def _overhead_inventory(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int = 30,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponentially decayed fraction of volume transacted above price."""
    above = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    total = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    decay = np.log(2.0) / 12.0
    valid_close = close.gt(0.0) & close.notna()

    for lag in range(lookback):
        typical = (high.shift(lag) + low.shift(lag) + close.shift(lag)) / 3.0
        traded = volume.shift(lag)
        valid = valid_close & typical.gt(0.0) & traded.gt(0.0)
        weight = traded * np.exp(-decay * lag)
        total = total + weight.where(valid, 0.0)
        above = above + weight.where(valid & typical.gt(close), 0.0)

    return above.div(total.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class InventoryGatedPeerImpactFade(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "inventory_gated_peer_impact_fade"
    name = "Inventory-Gated Peer Impact Fade"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Fades an aligned non-reporting peer response when a coherent industry "
        "surprise cluster meets abnormal return-per-volume impact and overhead "
        "cost-basis inventory."
    )
    window_length = 45
    inputs = [
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _finite(data["close"])
        high = _finite(data["high"])
        low = _finite(data["low"])
        volume = _finite(data["volume"])
        eps_surprise = _finite(data["epsSurprise"])
        revenue_surprise = _finite(data["revenueSurprise"])
        eps_estimate = _finite(data["epsEstimate"])
        revenue_estimate = _finite(data["revenueEstimate"])

        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].astype(object).copy()
        for ticker in labels.index[labels.isna()]:
            labels.loc[ticker] = "__singleton_" + str(ticker)

        eps_event = _fresh_update(eps_surprise)
        revenue_event = _fresh_update(revenue_surprise)
        release = eps_event | revenue_event

        eps_scaled = eps_surprise.div(eps_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        revenue_scaled = revenue_surprise.div(revenue_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        eps_z = _event_zscore(eps_scaled, eps_event)
        revenue_z = _event_zscore(revenue_scaled, revenue_event)
        channels = eps_event.astype(float) + revenue_event.astype(float)
        issuer_score = (eps_z.fillna(0.0) + revenue_z.fillna(0.0)).div(
            channels.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).fillna(0.0)
        issuer_score = issuer_score.where(release, 0.0)

        recent_score = issuer_score.rolling(3, min_periods=1).sum()
        recent_reporter = release.astype(float).rolling(3, min_periods=1).max()
        group_score = _industry_sum(recent_score, labels)
        group_count = _industry_sum(recent_reporter, labels)
        peer_score = group_score - recent_score
        peer_count = (group_count - recent_reporter).clip(lower=0.0)
        peer_cluster = peer_score.div(np.sqrt(peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)))
        peer_cluster = peer_cluster.where(peer_count.ge(2.0), 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_price = close.gt(0.0) & previous_close.gt(0.0)
        log_return = np.log(close.div(previous_close)).where(valid_price)

        positive_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0))
        volume_median = positive_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=10).median().shift(1)
        participation = volume.div(volume_median.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        impact = log_return.abs().div(np.sqrt(participation.clip(lower=0.05)))
        impact_mean = impact.rolling(40, min_periods=25).mean().shift(1)
        impact_std = impact.rolling(40, min_periods=25).std().shift(1)
        excess_impact = impact.sub(impact_mean).div(impact_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        excess_impact = excess_impact.clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)

        overhead = _overhead_inventory(high, low, close, volume)
        aligned = np.sign(log_return).eq(np.sign(peer_cluster)) & peer_cluster.ne(0.0)
        valid = (
            valid_price
            & volume_median.gt(0.0)
            & overhead.gt(0.15)
            & excess_impact.notna()
            & (~release)
            & aligned
        )

        raw = (np.sign(log_return) * excess_impact * overhead).where(valid)
        ranked = raw.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return ranked.where(valid, 0.5).fillna(0.5).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.5)

The interaction distinguishes genuine slow peer-information assimilation from a common-news basket-flow overshoot constrained by the receiver's local supply curve, which neither peer confirmation nor cost-basis imbalance alone can identify.

"""The signal treats volume-at-price only as an explicitly modeled proxy for the fraction of recent trading conducted above the current close, not as identified holder-level supply. A downside return innovation accompanied by a low close in an unusually wide, high-participation bar is more likely to continue when that proxy is high, consistent with asymmetric excitation of sell orders and liquidity withdrawal after losses. The factor is conditional: overhang alone and downside activity alone are not sufficient to produce a strong bearish score."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _trailing_above_price_overhang(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int = 60,
    half_life: float = 20.0,
    min_valid_bars: int = 40,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponentially weighted volume-at-price overhang proxy.

    At each decision date, each historical bar's volume is allocated uniformly
    over its observed high-low interval relative to that date's close.  The
    loop is over time only; all ticker calculations within each window are
    vectorised NumPy operations.
    """
    close_values = np.asarray(close, dtype=float)
    high_values = np.asarray(high, dtype=float)
    low_values = np.asarray(low, dtype=float)
    volume_values = np.asarray(volume, dtype=float)

    n_rows, n_columns = close_values.shape
    result = np.full((n_rows, n_columns), np.nan, dtype=float)

    # Window rows are oldest to newest, so their ages run window - 1 down to 0.
    ages = np.arange(window - 1, -1, -1, dtype=float)
    weights = np.exp2(-ages / half_life)

    for t in range(window - 1, n_rows):
        start = t - window + 1
        historical_high = high_values[start : t + 1]
        historical_low = low_values[start : t + 1]
        historical_close = close_values[start : t + 1]
        historical_volume = volume_values[start : t + 1]
        reference_close = close_values[t]

        span = historical_high - historical_low
        reference_valid = np.isfinite(reference_close)[None, :]
        valid = (
            np.isfinite(historical_high)
            & np.isfinite(historical_low)
            & np.isfinite(historical_close)
            & np.isfinite(historical_volume)
            & (historical_volume > 0.0)
            & (span >= 0.0)
            & reference_valid
        )

        above = np.zeros_like(historical_volume, dtype=float)
        below = np.zeros_like(historical_volume, dtype=float)

        nonflat = valid & (span > 0.0)
        if np.any(nonflat):
            above_fraction = np.clip(
                (historical_high - np.maximum(historical_low, reference_close[None, :]))
                / span,
                0.0,
                1.0,
            )
            below_fraction = np.clip(
                (np.minimum(historical_high, reference_close[None, :]) - historical_low)
                / span,
                0.0,
                1.0,
            )
            above[nonflat] = (historical_volume * above_fraction)[nonflat]
            below[nonflat] = (historical_volume * below_fraction)[nonflat]

        flat = valid & (span == 0.0)
        if np.any(flat):
            reference_matrix = reference_close[None, :]
            above[flat & (historical_close > reference_matrix)] = historical_volume[
                flat & (historical_close > reference_matrix)
            ]
            below[flat & (historical_close < reference_matrix)] = historical_volume[
                flat & (historical_close < reference_matrix)
            ]
            equal_close = flat & (historical_close == reference_matrix)
            above[equal_close] = 0.5 * historical_volume[equal_close]
            below[equal_close] = 0.5 * historical_volume[equal_close]

        weighted_total = np.sum(weights[:, None] * (above + below), axis=0)
        weighted_above = np.sum(weights[:, None] * above, axis=0)
        valid_count = valid.sum(axis=0)
        eligible = (valid_count >= min_valid_bars) & (weighted_total > 0.0)
        result[t, eligible] = weighted_above[eligible] / weighted_total[eligible]

    return pd.DataFrame(result, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)


def _prior_innovation(
    series: pd.DataFrame,
    minimum_observations: int = 15,
    window: int = 20,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Positive current z-innovation against the strictly prior trailing window."""
    prior = series.shift(1)
    mean = prior.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_observations).mean()
    stdev = prior.rolling(window, min_periods=minimum_observations).std(ddof=1)
    zscore = (series - mean) / stdev.where(stdev > 0.0)
    return zscore.clip(lower=0.0)


@register_factor
class TrailingOverhangExcitationHazard(BaseFactor):
    """Conditional downside hazard from cost-basis overhang and sell-order excitation."""

    factor_id = "overhang_breach_downside_branching_h6"
    name = "Trailing Overhang Excitation Hazard"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of a conditional downside hazard combining a "
        "60-bar volume-at-price overhang proxy with same-day downside, range, "
        "participation, and weak-close innovations. Higher values predict lower "
        "subsequent six-bar returns."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    expected_sign = -1

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        overhang = _trailing_above_price_overhang(close, high, low, volume)

        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        prior_close = safe_close.shift(1)
        log_return = np.log(safe_close / prior_close)

        valid_range_bar = (
            high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & close.notna()
            & (high >= low)
            & prior_close.notna()
        )
        fractional_range = ((high - low) / prior_close).where(valid_range_bar)
        log_volume = np.log(volume.where(volume > 0.0))

        downside = _prior_innovation(log_return)
        range_innovation = _prior_innovation(fractional_range)
        participation = _prior_innovation(log_volume)

        span = high - low
        valid_location_bar = high.notna() & low.notna() & close.notna() & (span >= 0.0)
        close_weakness = ((high - close) / span).where((span > 0.0) & valid_location_bar)
        close_weakness = close_weakness.mask((span == 0.0) & valid_location_bar, 0.5)

        hazard = overhang * downside * range_innovation * participation * close_weakness
        return rank(hazard)

programs.description: Decision timestamp is the close of day t; every input uses bars dated t or earlier, and the six-bar return starts after that close. Let C, H, L, and V denote close, high, low, and volume. Construct a trailing 60-bar, exponentially decayed volume-at-price proxy using s=t-59,...,t and weights w_s=2^(-(t-s)/20). For each historical bar s, allocate its observed volume uniformly over [L_s,H_s]. Given the known decision-close reference C_t, the allocated volume above C_t is A_s=V_s*max(0,min(1,(H_s-max(L_s,C_t))/(H_s-L_s))) and the allocated volume below C_t is B_s=V_s*max(0,min(1,(min(H_s,C_t)-L_s)/(H_s-L_s))). If H_s=L_s, set (A_s,B_s)=(V_s,0) when C_s>C_t, (0,V_s) when C_s<C_t, and (V_s/2,V_s/2) when C_s=C_t. Define weighted above-price overhang O_t=sum_s(w_s*A_s)/(sum_s(w_s*(A_s+B_s))); O_t is set NaN if the denominator is zero or fewer than 40 valid positive-volume bars occur in the 60-bar window. Compute r_t=log(C_t/C_{t-1}) and daily fractional range q_t=(H_t-L_t)/C_{t-1}. From the prior 20 valid observations t-20,...,t-1 only, calculate means and sample standard deviations for r, q, and log(V), requiring at least 15 observations and positive standard deviations. Define downside return innovation D_t=max(0,-(r_t-mean(r))/sd(r)), range innovation R_t=max(0,(q_t-mean(q))/sd(q)), and abnormal-participation innovation P_t=max(0,(log(V_t)-mean(log(V)))/sd(log(V))). Define close-location weakness K_t=(H_t-C_t)/(H_t-L_t), with K_t=0.5 if H_t=L_t. The raw hazard is S_t=O_t*D_t*R_t*P_t*K_t. Missing or invalid inputs produce NaN rather than imputation. The reported factor is the same-date cross-sectional ascending percentile rank of S_t among non-NaN names; higher ranks predict lower subsequent six-bar returns, so expected_sign=-1. Mechanical redundancy check before booking: compare this exact daily ranked output with prospect_costbasis_supply_skew and fresh_costbasis_barrier_activation over their common history; reject it if the expressions are identical or if the daily cross-sectional rank correlation is identically 1, and separately evaluate incremental predictive content after cross-sectionally residualizing S_t on those two booked outputs.

"""The revised mechanism is not broad volatility-targeting or risk-parity deleveraging. A negative, industry-specific volatility innovation can instead reduce single-name liquidity-provider and execution-algorithm risk capacity after the close: risk limits and volatility estimates are updated from realized returns, causing lower inventory replenishment and more cautious quote provision over the following several sessions. The factor targets downside variance shocks that are unusually large relative to the stock's own prior downside-risk history and to industry peers, while explicitly removing the component associated with abnormal-volume downside-pressure confirmation."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _daily_winsorize(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Clip each date's valid cross-section at its 1st and 99th percentiles."""
    lower = frame.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = frame.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return frame.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _valid_text_labels(labels: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify nonempty point-in-time categorical labels without coercing NaNs."""
    return labels.notna() & labels.astype(str).ne("")


def _industry_market_adjustment(
    returns: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute causal same-date market and sufficiently broad industry adjustments."""
    market = returns.where(eligible).median(axis=1)
    adjusted = returns.sub(market, axis=0)
    industry_component = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=returns.index, columns=returns.columns)

    for row_pos in range(len(returns.index)):
        valid = eligible.iloc[row_pos]
        labels = industry.iloc[row_pos]
        values = adjusted.iloc[row_pos].where(valid)
        row_component = pd.Series(0.0, index=returns.columns, dtype=float)

        for _, group_values in values.groupby(labels, sort=False):
            if group_values.count() >= 5:
                row_component.loc[group_values.index] = group_values.median()

        industry_component.iloc[row_pos] = row_component

    residual = adjusted - industry_component
    return residual.where(eligible)


def _industry_peer_surprise(
    surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Demean surprise by broad industries, using the universe median for narrow groups."""
    peer_adjusted = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=surprise.index, columns=surprise.columns)

    for row_pos in range(len(surprise.index)):
        valid = eligible.iloc[row_pos]
        labels = industry.iloc[row_pos]
        values = surprise.iloc[row_pos].where(valid)
        universe_median = values.median()
        row_peer_median = pd.Series(np.nan, index=surprise.columns, dtype=float)

        for _, group_values in values.groupby(labels, sort=False):
            group_median = group_values.median() if group_values.count() >= 5 else universe_median
            row_peer_median.loc[group_values.index] = group_median

        peer_adjusted.iloc[row_pos] = values - row_peer_median

    return peer_adjusted.where(eligible)


def _cross_sectional_control_residual(
    score: pd.DataFrame,
    control: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Residualize score on an intercept and contemporaneous control date by date."""
    valid = eligible & score.notna() & control.notna()
    q = score.where(valid)
    c = control.where(valid)

    count = valid.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    q_mean = q.sum(axis=1, min_count=1) / count
    c_mean = c.sum(axis=1, min_count=1) / count

    q_centered = q.sub(q_mean, axis=0)
    c_centered = c.sub(c_mean, axis=0)
    covariance = (q_centered * c_centered).sum(axis=1, min_count=1) / count
    variance = (c_centered * c_centered).sum(axis=1, min_count=1) / count

    beta = covariance / variance.where(variance > 1e-12)
    beta = beta.fillna(0.0)
    residual = q_centered - c_centered.mul(beta, axis=0)
    return residual.where(valid)


@register_factor
class IndustryRelativeDownsideVarianceShock(BaseFactor):
    """Industry-relative downside variance shocks orthogonalized to volume pressure."""

    factor_id = "idiosyncratic_downside_variance_targeting_feedba"
    name = "Industry-Relative Downside Variance Shock"
    category = "volatility"
    description = (
        "Ranks industry-relative downside semivariance surprises after removing "
        "their abnormal-volume downside-pressure component; high values indicate "
        "the strongest idiosyncratic volatility-capacity shock and forecast lower "
        "six-bar subsequent return."
    )
    window_length = 65
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)
        sector = data["sector"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        returns = close.div(prior_close) - 1.0
        returns = returns.where(close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0))

        prior_return_count = returns.rolling(65, min_periods=1).count().shift(1)
        prior_volume = volume.shift(1)
        prior_volume_mean = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        prior_volume_positive = (
            prior_volume.gt(0.0).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum().eq(20.0)
        )

        eligible = (
            prior_return_count.ge(65.0)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & prior_volume_positive
            & prior_volume_mean.gt(0.0)
            & _valid_text_labels(sector)
            & _valid_text_labels(industry)
        )

        raw_residual = _industry_market_adjustment(returns, eligible, industry)
        residual = _daily_winsorize(raw_residual).where(eligible)
        downside_square = residual.clip(upper=0.0).pow(2.0)

        recent_downside_variance = downside_square.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        baseline_downside_variance = (
            downside_square.shift(5).rolling(60, min_periods=48).mean()
        )

        epsilon = 1e-8
        surprise = np.log(
            (recent_downside_variance + epsilon).div(baseline_downside_variance + epsilon)
        )
        surprise = surprise.where(eligible & baseline_downside_variance.notna())

        peer_surprise = _industry_peer_surprise(surprise, eligible, industry)
        peer_surprise = _daily_winsorize(peer_surprise).where(eligible)

        severity = (-residual).div(np.sqrt(baseline_downside_variance + epsilon))
        severity = severity.clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0).where(eligible)
        raw_score = (peer_surprise * severity).where(eligible)

        abnormal_volume = np.log(volume.div(prior_volume_mean))
        abnormal_volume = abnormal_volume.clip(lower=0.0)
        control = severity * abnormal_volume
        control = _daily_winsorize(control.where(eligible)).where(eligible)

        residual_score = _cross_sectional_control_residual(raw_score, control, eligible)
        return rank(residual_score).reindex_like(close).astype(float)

Estimate the market return m_t as the cross-sectional median of eligible r_i,t. For each industry g with at least 5 eligible stocks, estimate its market-adjusted return b_g,t as median_i in g(r_i,t - m_t); set b_g,t = 0 for smaller industries. Define the causally observed industry-adjusted residual e_i,t = r_i,t - m_t - b_g,t. Winsorize e_i,t cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th percentiles separately on every date before using it in volatility calculations. Define recent downside semivariance D_i,t = mean over s=t-4,...,t of min(e_i,s, 0)^2. Define the predetermined slow downside-risk baseline B_i,t = mean over s=t-64,...,t-5 of min(e_i,s, 0)^2; require at least 48 valid observations, and use epsilon = 1e-8 only in ratios. The variance-surprise statistic is S_i,t = log((D_i,t + epsilon)/(B_i,t + epsilon)). Compute the industry-peer surprise E_i,t = S_i,t - median_j in industry g(S_j,t), falling back to the full-universe median when the industry has fewer than 5 valid S values. Winsorize E_i,t at the daily cross-sectional 1st/99th percentiles. Define contemporaneous downside-shock severity H_i,t = min(max(-e_i,t / sqrt(B_i,t + epsilon), 0), 5), and set raw variance-shock score Q_i,t = winsorized(E_i,t) * H_i,t. To differentiate the signal from idio_downside_pressure_confirmation, construct an explicit abnormal-volume downside-pressure control C_i,t = H_i,t * max(log(volume_i,t / mean(volume_i,t-20,...,t-1)), 0), winsorized daily at the 1st/99th percentiles. Each date, regress Q cross-sectionally on an intercept and C over the eligible universe and retain the residual U_i,t; this removes the portion of the variance-shock score explainable by volume-confirmed downside pressure. The final signal is the daily cross-sectional percentile rank of U_i,t, with higher rank forecasting lower subsequent return. All market, industry, volume, residual-return, semivariance, baseline, winsorization, regression, and ranking inputs use observations available through t only; trades are entered no earlier than t+1 and evaluated over the fixed six-bar horizon.

"""A negative close-to-close discontinuity that is unusually large relative to the same-day Parkinson intraday-range variance, is not shared by the stock's sector, and is followed by a strong close-location recovery is treated as a proxy for asymmetric downside liquidity demand rather than a fully confirmed repricing. High relative volume makes the event more likely to represent concentrated order-flow pressure, while the high close indicates that this pressure was not sustained through the close. The hypothesis is intentionally one-sided: it predicts a positive six-bar return after repaired idiosyncratic downside shocks and makes no symmetric claim about upside events."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _prior_rolling_mean_std(values: pd.DataFrame, window: int, min_valid: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal prior-window moments, excluding the current bar."""
    prior = values.shift(1)
    count = prior.rolling(window, min_periods=min_valid).count()
    mean = prior.rolling(window, min_periods=min_valid).mean()
    std = prior.rolling(window, min_periods=min_valid).std(ddof=1)
    valid = (count >= min_valid) & (std > 0.0)
    return (mean.where(valid), std.where(valid))

def _sector_mean(values: pd.DataFrame, sectors: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Equal-weight same-date sector mean, requiring sufficient valid names."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for timestamp in values.index:
        row = values.loc[timestamp]
        group_row = sectors.loc[timestamp]
        valid = row.notna() & group_row.notna()
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        grouped_mean = row[valid].groupby(group_row[valid]).mean()
        grouped_count = row[valid].groupby(group_row[valid]).count()
        eligible = grouped_count[grouped_count >= min_names].index
        if len(eligible) == 0:
            continue
        mapped = group_row.map(grouped_mean)
        mapped = mapped.where(group_row.isin(eligible))
        result.loc[timestamp] = mapped
    return result

def _prior_volume_ratio(volume: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Current volume divided by a strictly prior 20-bar median volume."""
    prior = volume.shift(1)
    prior_count = prior.rolling(19, min_periods=15).count()
    prior_median = prior.rolling(19, min_periods=15).median()
    denominator = prior_median.where((prior_count >= 15) & (prior_median > 0.0))
    return (volume / denominator).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)

@register_factor
class IdiosyncraticGapRecoveryClimaxReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks repaired, idiosyncratic downside gap-range liquidity shocks."""
    factor_id = 'idiosyncratic_gap_recovery_climax_reversal_j'
    name = 'Idiosyncratic Signed Gap-Range Recovery'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Cross-sectional percentile rank of repaired downside discontinuities whose signed close-to-close variance minus Parkinson range innovation is idiosyncratic to the sector, occurs on abnormal volume, and closes near the daily high.'
    window_length = 61
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume', 'sector']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        high = data['high']
        low = data['low']
        volume = data['volume']
        sector = data['sector']
        positive_prices = (close > 0.0) & (high > 0.0) & (low > 0.0)
        valid_range = positive_prices & (high >= low)
        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_return = (close > 0.0) & (prior_close > 0.0)
        log_return = np.log(close / prior_close).where(valid_return)
        park_range = np.log(high / low).where(valid_range)
        parkinson_variance = park_range * park_range / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))
        q = (np.sign(log_return) * (log_return * log_return - parkinson_variance)).where(log_return.notna() & parkinson_variance.notna())
        q_mean, q_std = _prior_rolling_mean_std(q, 60, 40)
        z = ((q - q_mean) / q_std).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0)
        sector_z = _sector_mean(z, sector, 5)
        zres = (z - sector_z).clip(lower=-5.0, upper=5.0)
        volume_ratio = _prior_volume_ratio(volume)
        range_width = (high - low).where(high > low)
        clv = ((close - low) / range_width).where(valid_range & range_width.notna())
        event = (log_return <= -0.015) & (zres <= -1.0) & (sector_z.abs() <= 0.25) & (volume_ratio >= 2.0) & (clv >= 0.75)
        recovery = (2.0 * (clv - 0.5)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        raw_score = (-zres * volume_ratio * recovery).clip(lower=0.0, upper=25.0)
        raw_score = raw_score.where(event, 0.0)
        valid_stock = log_return.notna() & zres.notna() & sector_z.notna() & volume_ratio.notna() & clv.notna()
        ranked = raw_score.where(valid_stock).rank(axis=1, pct=True, method='average')
        return ranked.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Idiosyncratic Signed Gap-Range Recovery (jitter)
programs.trading_idea: A negative close-to-close discontinuity that is unusually large relative to the same-day Parkinson intraday-range variance, is not shared by the stock's sector, and is followed by a strong close-location recovery is treated as a proxy for asymmetric downside liquidity demand rather than a fully confirmed repricing. High relative volume makes the event more likely to represent concentrated order-flow pressure, while the high close indicates that this pressure was not sustained through the close. The hypothesis is intentionally one-sided: it predicts a positive six-bar return after repaired idiosyncratic downside shocks and makes no symmetric claim about upside events.
programs.description: Signals are formed after the daily close and may be traded no earlier than the next eligible bar. For stock i on day t, define close-to-close log return r_i,t = ln(close_i,t / close_i,t-1) and Parkinson range variance p_i,t = [ln(high_i,t / low_i,t)]^2 / [4 ln(2)], using only observations with strictly positive close, high, and low. Define the signed gap-minus-range quantity q_i,t = sign(r_i,t) * (r_i,t^2 - p_i,t). Estimate its baseline from the prior 60 trading days only: mu_i,t is the mean of q_i over t-60 through t-1 and sigma_i,t is the sample standard deviation over the same window, requiring at least 40 valid observations and sigma > 0. Define z_i,t = clip((q_i,t - mu_i,t) / sigma_i,t, -5, 5). For each sector and day, compute the equal-weight mean sector_z_s,t of valid z observations, requiring at least 5 valid names in that sector; define the sector-residual shock zres_i,t = clip(z_i,t - sector_z_s,t, -5, 5). Normalize volume by the prior 20-day rolling median, requiring at least 15 valid prior observations and a positive median: vr_i,t = clip(volume_i,t / median(volume_i,t-20:t-1), 0, 5). Define close location clv_i,t = (close_i,t - low_i,t) / (high_i,t - low_i,t); when high equals low, clv is invalid. A downside-recovery event requires all of: r_i,t <= -0.015; zres_i,t <= -1.0; abs(sector_z_s,t) <= 0.25; vr_i,t >= 2.0; and clv_i,t >= 0.75. For qualifying events, set raw_score_i,t = clip((-zres_i,t) * vr_i,t * clip(2 * (clv_i,t - 0.5), 0, 1), 0, 25); otherwise set raw_score to 0. On each date, winsorize implicitly through the stated [0,25] clip and convert raw_score into a cross-sectional percentile rank across all valid stocks using average-tie ranking, with higher ranks predicting higher subsequent six-bar returns. This is mechanically distinct from open_gap_refill_participation_clock because it requires an explicit signed close-to-close variance-minus-Parkinson-range innovation, not an opening-gap refill measure; from kalman_liquidity_resilience_impulse because it uses no state-space resilience estimate and requires a sector-residual discontinuity; and from idio_downside_pressure_confirmation because it requires the joint interaction of signed gap-range innovation, weak sector confirmation, abnormal participation, and close-location repair rather than directional pressure confirmation alone.
