programs.trading_idea: An abnormal-volume neutral session followed by a directional range close is ambiguous in isolation: Parent B's failed sign suggests that unconditional close-location skew often reflects inventory completion rather than durable information. This child uses the peer-revision/relative-price-response backlog as the state variable that distinguishes genuine delayed information transfer from mechanical flow: a bullish close is trusted only when favourable peer revisions remain under-validated by the stock, with the symmetric rule for bearish states. The interaction carries edge because the candle pattern supplies the short-horizon timing of assimilation, while the leave-one-out revision-response gap supplies the reason that the directional flow is informational rather than transient.
programs.description: Ranks high-volume neutral-to-directional close transfers only when the close direction agrees with an industry-peer estimate-revision backlog relative to the stock's own recent response. It applies range, gap, and dollar-liquidity controls so the signal targets delayed assimilation rather than broad volatility shocks.

"""Cash-validated coherent upgrades entered through temporary inventory pressure.

Mechanism: a jointly positive EPS and revenue estimate revision is more credible
when the latest filing improves operating-cash conversion.  A subsequent
high-volume neutral session followed by a close near the low is treated as a
short-lived inventory discount, provided industry-relative prices have not yet
absorbed the favorable expectations update.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _clean(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _industry_relative_return(
    returns_5: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Equal-weight industry-relative return using only contemporaneously valid names."""
    masked = returns_5.where(eligible)
    grouped = masked.T.groupby(labels, sort=False)
    mean = grouped.transform("mean").T
    count = grouped.transform("count").T
    return (returns_5 - mean).where(eligible & count.ge(8))


def _cash_conversion_state(
    revenue: pd.DataFrame,
    ocf: pd.DataFrame,
    receivables: pd.DataFrame,
    inventory: pd.DataFrame,
    ccc: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal filing-to-filing cash-quality innovation, retained for 90 bars."""
    prior_revenue = revenue.shift(1)
    update = revenue.notna() & prior_revenue.notna() & revenue.ne(prior_revenue)

    margin = ocf / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    receivable_intensity = receivables / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    inventory_intensity = inventory / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    prior_margin = margin.shift(1)
    prior_receivable_intensity = receivable_intensity.shift(1)
    prior_inventory_intensity = inventory_intensity.shift(1)
    prior_ccc = ccc.shift(1)

    complete = (
        update
        & margin.notna()
        & prior_margin.notna()
        & receivable_intensity.notna()
        & prior_receivable_intensity.notna()
        & inventory_intensity.notna()
        & prior_inventory_intensity.notna()
        & ccc.notna()
        & prior_ccc.notna()
    )

    ccc_scale = prior_ccc.abs().clip(lower=10.0)
    quality_innovation = (
        (margin - prior_margin)
        - 0.50 * (receivable_intensity - prior_receivable_intensity)
        - 0.50 * (inventory_intensity - prior_inventory_intensity)
        - 0.25 * ((ccc - prior_ccc) / ccc_scale)
    ).where(complete)

    return quality_innovation.where(complete).ffill(limit=90)


@register_factor
class CashValidatedCoherentRevisionInventoryEntry(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_validated_coherent_revision_inventory_entry"
    name = "Cash-Validated Revision Inventory Entry"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Longs coherent positive EPS and revenue revisions supported by recent "
        "cash-conversion improvement when industry-relative price performance "
        "and a bearish high-volume range close indicate incomplete assimilation."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "revenue",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "receivables",
        "inventory",
        "cashConversionCycle",
        "industry",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _clean(data["close"])
        open_ = _clean(data["open"])
        high = _clean(data["high"])
        low = _clean(data["low"])
        volume = _clean(data["volume"])
        eps_estimate = _clean(data["epsEstimate"])
        revenue_estimate = _clean(data["revenueEstimate"])
        revenue = _clean(data["revenue"])
        ocf = _clean(data["operatingCashFlow"])
        receivables = _clean(data["receivables"])
        inventory = _clean(data["inventory"])
        ccc = _clean(data["cashConversionCycle"])

        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        has_industry = labels.notna()

        eps_lag = eps_estimate.shift(63)
        revenue_estimate_lag = revenue_estimate.shift(63)
        eps_revision = (eps_estimate - eps_lag) / eps_lag.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        revenue_revision = (
            (revenue_estimate - revenue_estimate_lag)
            / revenue_estimate_lag.abs().clip(lower=1.0)
        )
        revision_valid = (
            eps_estimate.notna()
            & eps_lag.notna()
            & revenue_estimate.notna()
            & revenue_estimate_lag.notna()
            & has_industry
        )
        coherent_upgrade = (
            revision_valid
            & eps_revision.gt(0.0)
            & revenue_revision.gt(0.0)
        )
        revision_strength = (
            0.5 * rank(eps_revision.where(revision_valid))
            + 0.5 * rank(revenue_revision.where(revision_valid))
        ).where(coherent_upgrade)

        close_lag = close.shift(5)
        valid_return = close.gt(0.0) & close_lag.gt(0.0)
        return_5 = close / close_lag - 1.0
        relative_return = _industry_relative_return(
            return_5,
            labels,
            valid_return & has_industry,
        )
        unassimilated_discount = (-relative_return).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.20)

        cash_state = _cash_conversion_state(
            revenue,
            ocf,
            receivables,
            inventory,
            ccc,
        )
        cash_support = cash_state.clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.20)

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume.gt(0.0)))
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(2).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        volume_std = log_volume.shift(2).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
        prior_volume_z = (
            (log_volume.shift(1) - volume_mean)
            / volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )

        valid_range = high.gt(low) & low.gt(0.0) & close.notna()
        clv = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / (high - low)).where(valid_range)
        prior_clv = clv.shift(1)
        prior_body = np.log(
            (close.shift(1) / open_.shift(1)).where(
                close.shift(1).gt(0.0) & open_.shift(1).gt(0.0)
            )
        ).abs()
        prior_range = np.log(
            (high.shift(1) / low.shift(1)).where(
                high.shift(1).gt(low.shift(1)) & low.shift(1).gt(0.0)
        ))
        current_range = np.log((high / low).where(valid_range))
        normal_range = current_range.le(
            2.0 * current_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        )
        neutral_prior = prior_clv.abs().le(0.10) & prior_body.le(
            np.minimum(0.005, 0.25 * prior_range)
        )
        inventory_discount = (
            prior_volume_z.ge(1.5)
            & neutral_prior
            & normal_range
            & clv.lt(0.0)
        )

        raw = (
            revision_strength
            * cash_support
            * unassimilated_discount
            * prior_volume_z.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
            * (-clv).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        )
        active = (
            coherent_upgrade
            & cash_state.gt(0.0)
            & relative_return.lt(0.0)
            & inventory_discount
            & raw.notna()
            & raw.gt(0.0)
        )
        score = rank(raw.where(active))
        return score.where(active, 0.0).fillna(0.0).reindex_like(close)

It then requires a high-volume neutral session followed by a close near the low, interpreting the adverse endpoint as a temporary inventory discount rather than informed selling. The interaction creates edge because revisions alone may already be accepted by the market, while a liquidity discount alone cannot distinguish a fundamentally justified dip from genuine deterioration.

Cash quality is computed on filing transitions and carried forward only for a limited post-filing validation window.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_zscore(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Datewise winsorised cross-sectional z-score."""
    lower = df.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
    upper = df.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
    clipped = df.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    std = clipped.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(std, axis=0).clip(-4.0, 4.0)


def _slow_zscore(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal standardisation appropriate for quarterly estimate step functions."""
    mean = df.rolling(84, min_periods=30).mean()
    std = df.rolling(84, min_periods=30).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return ((df - mean) / std).clip(-4.0, 4.0)


def _industry_median(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Contemporaneous industry medians, copied back to each member column."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns, dtype=float)
    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels, sort=False).groups.items():
        cols = list(members)
        block = values.loc[:, cols]
        valid_count = block.notna().sum(axis=1)
        med = block.median(axis=1).where(valid_count >= minimum)
        out.loc[:, cols] = np.repeat(med.to_numpy()[:, None], len(cols), axis=1)
    return out


def _report_event(fields: list[pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """True at a point-in-time fundamental update, including first availability."""
    event = pd.DataFrame(False, index=fields[0].index, columns=fields[0].columns)
    for field in fields:
        prior = field.shift(1)
        event = event | (field.notna() & (prior.isna() | field.ne(prior)))
    return event


@register_factor
class ConfirmedRevisionPeerAssimilationLag(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "confirmed_revision_peer_assimilation_lag"
    name = "Confirmed Revision Peer-Assimilation Lag"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks fresh multi-channel earnings delivery when a stock-specific, industry-opposed "
        "estimate revision agrees with delivery and the stock has lagged its industry's six-bar response."
    )
    window_length = 90
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "marketCap",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "operatingMargin",
        "operatingCashFlow",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        eps_est = data["epsEstimate"]
        rev_est = data["revenueEstimate"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        margin = data["operatingMargin"]
        cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"]

        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].astype(object).copy()
        missing = labels.isna()
        if missing.any():
            labels.loc[missing] = ["__single_" + str(col) for col in labels.index[missing]]

        prior_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_cap = market_cap.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        eps_yield = eps_est / prior_close
        revenue_yield = rev_est / prior_cap
        eps_revision = _slow_zscore(eps_yield - eps_yield.shift(21))
        revenue_revision = _slow_zscore(revenue_yield - revenue_yield.shift(21))
        revision = (0.65 * eps_revision.fillna(0.0) + 0.35 * revenue_revision.fillna(0.0))
        revision = revision.where(eps_revision.notna() | revenue_revision.notna())

        peer_revision = _industry_median(revision, labels, 4)
        displacement = revision - peer_revision
        industry_opposed = revision.mul(peer_revision).lt(0.0)

        eps_pct = eps_surprise / eps_est.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        revenue_pct = revenue_surprise / rev_est.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        margin_change = margin - margin.shift(63)
        prior_cash = cash_flow.shift(63)
        cash_growth = (cash_flow - prior_cash) / prior_cash.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)

        delivery_parts = [
            _cs_zscore(eps_pct),
            _cs_zscore(revenue_pct),
            _cs_zscore(margin_change),
            _cs_zscore(cash_growth),
        ]
        weights = [0.40, 0.25, 0.20, 0.15]
        numerator = sum(weight * part.fillna(0.0) for weight, part in zip(weights, delivery_parts))
        denominator = sum(weight * part.notna().astype(float) for weight, part in zip(weights, delivery_parts))
        delivery = (numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(denominator >= 0.40)

        event = _report_event([eps_surprise, revenue_surprise, margin, cash_flow])
        active_delivery = delivery.where(event).ffill(limit=10)

        six_bar_return = close / close.shift(6).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        peer_return = _industry_median(six_bar_return, labels, 4)
        directional_lag = (
            np.sign(active_delivery) * (peer_return - six_bar_return)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.30)

        agreement = active_delivery.mul(displacement).gt(0.0)
        score = (
            np.sign(active_delivery)
            * active_delivery.abs().clip(0.0, 4.0)
            * displacement.abs().clip(0.0, 4.0)
            * directional_lag
        ).where(industry_opposed & agreement)

        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).reindex(
            index=close.index, columns=close.columns
        ).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: A multi-channel earnings delivery makes a stock-specific estimate revision more credible, while an estimate move opposed to its industry identifies information that is unlikely to be merely a sector-wide repricing. The child trades only when that confirmed idiosyncratic revision agrees with the delivery direction but the stock has underperformed its industry's trailing response in that direction. This interaction captures delayed assimilation of firm-specific fundamental news relative to peers: delivery alone does not identify whether news is already priced, and revision displacement alone does not distinguish credible information from noisy analyst disagreement.

"""Correlation-squeeze pressure repair conditioned on financial resilience.

Common basket-flow regimes temporarily suppress idiosyncratic discovery.  A relative
lag that also arrives with abnormal participation, range, and an endpoint close is
more likely a liquidity-pressure displacement; resilient firms are better able to
repair that displacement after the common shock subsides.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _peer_mean(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.DataFrame, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal contemporaneous leave-one-out group mean, with valid-observation checks."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=frame.index, columns=frame.columns, dtype=float)
    group_labels = labels.iloc[0].reindex(frame.columns)
    for _, members in group_labels.dropna().groupby(group_labels.dropna(), sort=False).groups.items():
        if len(members) < minimum:
            continue
        values = frame.loc[:, members]
        valid = values.notna()
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        total = values.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        peer = total.to_frame().sub(values).div((count - 1).replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
        result.loc[:, members] = peer.where(valid & (count >= minimum).to_numpy()[:, None])
    return result


def _within_group_rank(frame: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.DataFrame, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile ranks within static groups at each bar."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=frame.index, columns=frame.columns, dtype=float)
    group_labels = labels.iloc[0].reindex(frame.columns)
    for _, members in group_labels.dropna().groupby(group_labels.dropna(), sort=False).groups.items():
        if len(members) < minimum:
            continue
        result.loc[:, members] = frame.loc[:, members].rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    return result


def _group_breadth(ret: pd.DataFrame, peer: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.DataFrame, minimum: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fraction of valid peers moving in the leave-one-out peer direction."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns, dtype=float)
    group_labels = labels.iloc[0].reindex(ret.columns)
    for _, members in group_labels.dropna().groupby(group_labels.dropna(), sort=False).groups.items():
        if len(members) < minimum:
            continue
        values = ret.loc[:, members]
        valid = values.notna()
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        positive = ((values > 0.0) & valid).sum(axis=1)
        negative = ((values < 0.0) & valid).sum(axis=1)
        peer_positive = positive.to_frame().sub(((values > 0.0) & valid).astype(float))
        peer_negative = negative.to_frame().sub(((values < 0.0) & valid).astype(float))
        same = peer_positive.where(peer.loc[:, members] > 0.0, peer_negative)
        breadth = same.div((count - 1).replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
        result.loc[:, members] = breadth.where(valid & (count >= minimum).to_numpy()[:, None])
    return result


@register_factor
class CorrelationPressureResilienceRepairGate(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "correlation_pressure_resilience_repair_gate"
    name = "Correlation Pressure Resilience Repair"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "During sector correlation squeezes and broad industry shocks, favors "
        "resilient names with abnormal liquidity-pressure bars and the largest "
        "shock-direction-adjusted sector-relative five-day response deficit."
    )
    window_length = 90
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "industry",
        "grossMargin",
        "sgaToRevenue",
        "currentRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        previous = close.shift(1)
        ret = (close / previous - 1.0).where((close > 0.0) & (previous > 0.0))

        sector_peer = _peer_mean(ret, data["sector"], 8)
        industry_peer = _peer_mean(ret, data["industry"], 6)
        industry_breadth = _group_breadth(ret, industry_peer, data["industry"], 6)

        corr_now = ret.rolling(15, min_periods=12).corr(sector_peer)
        corr_base = corr_now.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=35).mean()
        correlation_squeeze = (corr_now >= 0.50) & ((corr_now - corr_base) >= 0.15)

        shock_cutoff = industry_peer.abs().shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=35).quantile(0.75)
        broad_industry_shock = (
            industry_peer.notna()
            & (industry_peer.abs() >= shock_cutoff)
            & (industry_breadth >= 0.65)
        )

        prior_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=12).median()
        volume_multiple = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        raw_range = high - low
        valid_range = (high > 0.0) & (low > 0.0) & (close > 0.0) & (raw_range > 0.0)
        normalized_range = (raw_range / close).where(valid_range)
        prior_range = normalized_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=12).median()
        range_multiple = normalized_range / prior_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = (2.0 * (close - low) / raw_range - 1.0).where(valid_range)
        residual_today = ret - industry_peer
        directional_endpoint = np.sign(residual_today) * close_location >= 0.65
        pressure = (
            valid_range
            & (volume_multiple >= 1.30)
            & (range_multiple >= 1.25)
            & directional_endpoint
        )

        sector_relative_five_day = (ret - sector_peer).rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
        relative_rank = _within_group_rank(sector_relative_five_day, data["sector"], 8)
        response_deficit = (
            0.5 - np.sign(industry_peer) * (relative_rank - 0.5)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        gm = data["grossMargin"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sga = data["sgaToRevenue"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        current = data["currentRatio"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        leverage = data["debtToEquity"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        fundamental_valid = gm.notna() & sga.notna() & current.notna() & leverage.notna()
        resilience = (
            (_within_group_rank(gm.where(fundamental_valid), data["industry"], 6) - 0.5)
            + (0.5 - _within_group_rank(sga.where(fundamental_valid), data["industry"], 6))
            + (_within_group_rank(current.where(fundamental_valid), data["industry"], 6) - 0.5)
            + (0.5 - _within_group_rank(leverage.where(fundamental_valid), data["industry"], 6))
        ) / 4.0
        resilience_weight = (resilience + 0.5).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        active = (
            correlation_squeeze
            & broad_industry_shock
            & pressure
            & fundamental_valid
            & response_deficit.notna()
            & resilience_weight.notna()
        )
        score = resilience_weight * response_deficit
        return score.where(active, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Correlation Pressure Resilience Repair
programs.trading_idea: Sector correlation squeezes identify periods when basket trading suppresses firm-specific price discovery, while abnormal volume, range, and close-location identify the subset of relative moves most likely caused by urgent liquidity demand rather than information. The child buys financially resilient names that both lagged their sector basket over the squeeze and exhibit a shock-direction-adjusted relative-response deficit during an industry pressure event. The interaction has edge because correlation alone cannot distinguish genuine differentiation from forced flow, and pressure alone cannot establish that the move occurred in a common-flow regime where resilient relative laggards are likely to repair over the next six bars.
programs.description: The signal requires a sector-level rise in trailing leave-one-out return correlation, an industry-wide broad shock, and a name-level abnormal-volume/range directional pressure bar. Among active names it favors high-resilience stocks with the largest shock-direction-adjusted five-day sector-relative lag.

"""Late-report revision relays through unfinished peer event cascades."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank


def _leave_one_out(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
    minimum_peers: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Same-date leave-one-out industry mean and available peer count."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    counts_out = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels == label]
        if len(cols) <= minimum_peers:
            continue
        group = values.loc[:, cols]
        observed = group.notna().astype(float)
        total = group.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1)
        count = observed.sum(axis=1)
        peer_total = group.fillna(0.0).rsub(total, axis=0)
        peer_count = observed.rsub(count, axis=0)
        output.loc[:, cols] = peer_total.div(peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(peer_count >= minimum_peers)
        counts_out.loc[:, cols] = peer_count
    return output, counts_out


def _report_age(eps_actual: pd.DataFrame, revenue_actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bars since the latest observable earnings or revenue report update."""
    eps_previous = eps_actual.ffill().shift(1)
    revenue_previous = revenue_actual.ffill().shift(1)
    update = (
        (eps_actual.notna() & eps_previous.notna() & eps_actual.ne(eps_previous))
        | (revenue_actual.notna() & revenue_previous.notna() & revenue_actual.ne(revenue_previous))
    )
    row_number = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(np.arange(len(eps_actual), dtype=float)[:, None], eps_actual.shape),
        index=eps_actual.index,
        columns=eps_actual.columns,
    )
    latest_update = row_number.where(update).ffill()
    return row_number - latest_update


def _relative_revision(estimate: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Twenty-one-bar estimate change with a cross-sectional scale floor."""
    previous = estimate.shift(21)
    scale_floor = previous.abs().median(axis=1).mul(0.02)
    denominator = previous.abs().where(previous.abs().ge(scale_floor, axis=0), scale_floor, axis=0)
    valid = eligible & estimate.notna() & previous.notna() & denominator.gt(0.0)
    return estimate.sub(previous).div(denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0).where(valid)


@register_factor
class ReportLagPeerDeficitRevisionRelay(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "report_lag_peer_deficit_revision_relay"
    name = "Report-Lag Peer Deficit Relay"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Late-quarter estimate revisions are ranked only when an aligned, signed "
        "industry return-volume cascade exceeds the receiver's own marked response."
    )
    window_length = 90
    inputs = [
        "close", "volume", "industry", "epsActual", "revenueActual",
        "epsEstimate", "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        labels = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)

        age = _report_age(data["epsActual"], data["revenueActual"])
        report_window = age.ge(30.0) & age.le(75.0)
        eps_revision = _relative_revision(data["epsEstimate"], report_window)
        revenue_revision = _relative_revision(data["revenueEstimate"], report_window)
        revision = (0.60 * eps_revision + 0.40 * revenue_revision).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        log_return = np.log(safe_close.div(safe_close.shift(1)))
        industry_return, peer_return_count = _leave_one_out(log_return, labels, 4)
        abnormal_return = log_return - industry_return

        prior_abnormal = abnormal_return.shift(1)
        abnormal_scale = prior_abnormal.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        abnormal_z = abnormal_return.div(abnormal_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume.ge(0.0)))
        prior_volume = log_volume.shift(1)
        volume_mean = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        volume_scale = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        volume_z = log_volume.sub(volume_mean).div(volume_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        event_valid = abnormal_z.notna() & volume_z.notna() & peer_return_count.ge(4.0)
        marked_event = (
            np.sign(abnormal_z)
            * abnormal_z.abs().clip(upper=3.0)
            * (volume_z - 0.5).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        ).where(event_valid)

        history = event_valid.astype(float).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum().ge(15.0)
        own_intensity = marked_event.fillna(0.0).ewm(alpha=0.18, adjust=False).mean().where(history)
        peer_intensity, peer_count = _leave_one_out(own_intensity, labels, 4)

        directed_backlog = np.sign(revision) * (peer_intensity - own_intensity)
        aligned_cascade = revision.mul(peer_intensity).gt(0.0)
        own_saturation = own_intensity.abs().clip(lower=0.0)
        raw_signal = revision * directed_backlog.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).div(1.0 + own_saturation)

        valid = (
            report_window
            & revision.notna()
            & peer_intensity.notna()
            & peer_count.ge(4.0)
            & history
            & aligned_cascade
            & directed_backlog.gt(0.0)
        )
        return rank(raw_signal.where(valid)).where(valid, 0.0).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Report-Lag Peer Deficit Relay
programs.trading_idea: A late-quarter estimate revision supplies a slow-moving, stock-specific fundamental direction, while signed abnormal return-volume events from industry peers indicate that the same information is being actively transmitted through a peer cascade. The child trades only receivers whose own marked response remains behind the signed peer intensity, so it targets the unfinished transmission stage rather than revisions with no external validation or peer events that have already been absorbed. The interaction carries edge because the revision resolves the direction of the cascade and the peer-response deficit resolves its timing; either component alone cannot distinguish a validated but unpriced receiver from a stale revision or a purely technical industry shock.

The signal is largest when the receiver's own event intensity is below the signed peer cascade, indicating an unabsorbed revision-supported information relay.

"""Buffered industry activity acceleration as an information-relay signal.

Mechanism: a focal return-volume innovation is more likely to represent informed
cross-excitation when independent industry peers exhibit the same residual
activity and the focal activity is still accelerating.  Financial buffers select
names able to accommodate institutional repositioning, separating durable
information diffusion from fragile forced-flow episodes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _group_sum(values: pd.DataFrame, groups: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast same-industry column sums back to constituent tickers."""
    return values.T.groupby(groups, sort=False).transform("sum").T


def _peer_residual_returns(
    ret: pd.DataFrame, groups: pd.Series
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Leave-one-out contemporaneous industry residuals and peer counts."""
    valid = ret.notna()
    total = _group_sum(ret.fillna(0.0), groups)
    count = _group_sum(valid.astype(float), groups)
    peers = count - valid.astype(float)
    peer_mean = (total - ret.fillna(0.0)) / peers.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    residual = (ret - peer_mean).where(valid & peers.ge(5.0))
    return residual, peers


def _financial_buffer(
    cash_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    current_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_to_equity: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time cross-sectional liquid-capacity score in [0, 1]."""
    valid = (
        cash_ratio.notna()
        & current_ratio.notna()
        & debt_to_equity.notna()
        & cash_ratio.ge(0.0)
        & current_ratio.ge(0.0)
        & debt_to_equity.ge(0.0)
    )
    cash = cash_ratio.clip(0.0, 10.0).where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    current = current_ratio.clip(0.0, 10.0).where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    debt = debt_to_equity.clip(0.0, 10.0).where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    score = (cash + current + (1.0 - debt)) / 3.0
    enough_names = valid.sum(axis=1).ge(30)
    return score.where(enough_names, axis=0)


@register_factor
class BufferedPeerAccelerationInformationRelay(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "buffered_peer_acceleration_information_relay"
    name = "Buffered Peer-Acceleration Relay"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Directional industry residual return-volume co-excitation, retained only "
        "when focal activity accelerates concordantly and weighted by a PIT "
        "liquidity-minus-leverage buffer score."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "cashRatio",
        "currentRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        if close.empty:
            return output

        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(close).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        groups = data["industry"].reindex_like(close).iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        ret = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0
        residual, peer_count = _peer_residual_returns(ret, groups)

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        relative_volume = (volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 4.0)
        activity = residual * np.log1p(relative_volume)

        activity_mean = activity.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        activity_std = activity.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
        own_z = ((activity - activity_mean) / activity_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        valid_z = own_z.notna()
        peer_sum = _group_sum(own_z.fillna(0.0), groups) - own_z.fillna(0.0)
        peer_n = _group_sum(valid_z.astype(float), groups) - valid_z.astype(float)
        peer_z = peer_sum / peer_n.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        fast = own_z.ewm(halflife=3.0, adjust=False, min_periods=40).mean()
        slow = own_z.ewm(halflife=15.0, adjust=False, min_periods=40).mean()
        magnitude = own_z.abs().ewm(halflife=15.0, adjust=False, min_periods=40).mean()
        acceleration = ((fast - slow) / magnitude.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        buffer = _financial_buffer(
            data["cashRatio"].reindex_like(close).astype(float),
            data["currentRatio"].reindex_like(close).astype(float),
            data["debtToEquity"].reindex_like(close).astype(float),
        )

        concordant_peer = own_z.mul(peer_z).gt(0.0)
        accelerating_in_peer_direction = acceleration.mul(peer_z).gt(0.0)
        strength = (
            own_z.abs().clip(upper=3.0)
            * peer_z.abs().clip(upper=3.0)
            * acceleration.abs().clip(upper=2.0)
        )
        eligible = (
            concordant_peer
            & accelerating_in_peer_direction
            & peer_count.ge(5.0)
            & peer_n.ge(5.0)
            & buffer.notna()
            & own_z.abs().ge(0.5)
            & peer_z.abs().ge(0.25)
        )
        signal = np.sign(peer_z) * strength * buffer
        return signal.where(eligible, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)

"""Balance-sheet capacity determines whether a concentrated earnings burst is absorbed or propagates."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _fresh_release(actual: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """True only when a point-in-time reported field newly becomes available."""
    previous = actual.shift(1)
    return actual.notna() & (previous.isna() | actual.ne(previous))


def _pre_event_transition_entropy(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing entropy of prior return-volume state transitions.

    Four states combine return sign and volume above its own trailing median.
    The shift makes the latest transition end at t-1, so an event-day value
    contains no event-day order-flow information.
    """
    volume_reference = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
    valid_state = ret.notna() & volume.gt(0.0) & volume_reference.gt(0.0)
    up = ret.gt(0.0)
    high = volume.ge(volume_reference)
    state = pd.DataFrame(
        np.where(up.to_numpy(), np.where(high.to_numpy(), 0.0, 1.0), np.where(high.to_numpy(), 2.0, 3.0)),
        index=ret.index,
        columns=ret.columns,
    ).where(valid_state)

    # A transition observed at t is formed entirely from states at t-1 and t-2.
    transition = state.shift(1) * 4.0 + state.shift(2)
    valid_count = transition.notna().rolling(15, min_periods=15).sum()
    entropy = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    for code in range(16):
        count = transition.eq(float(code)).rolling(15, min_periods=15).sum()
        probability = count / valid_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        entropy = entropy - probability.where(probability.gt(0.0), 1.0) * np.log(
            probability.where(probability.gt(0.0), 1.0)
        )
    return (entropy / np.log(16.0)).where(valid_count.ge(15.0))


@register_factor
class BufferedEventCompletionPolarity(BaseFactor):
    """Trade completion reversals only where balance-sheet absorption is feasible."""

    factor_id = "buffered_event_completion_polarity"

    description = (

        "firms but continue in financially fragile firms, reflecting whether concentrated "
        "event pressure can be absorbed by incremental risk-bearing capital."
    )
    window_length = 45
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "cashRatio",

        "netDebtToEbitda",
    ]

    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        ret = close.pct_change(fill_method=None)

        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        eps_valid = eps_surprise.notna() & eps_estimate.abs().gt(0.0)
        revenue_valid = revenue_surprise.notna() & revenue_estimate.abs().gt(0.0)
        eps_scaled = (eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs()).where(eps_valid)
        revenue_scaled = (revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs()).where(revenue_valid)
        component_count = eps_valid.astype(float) + revenue_valid.astype(float)
        signed_surprise = (
            eps_scaled.fillna(0.0) + revenue_scaled.fillna(0.0)
        ) / component_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        volume_base = volume.shift(1).rolling(30, min_periods=30).median()
        return_q90 = ret.abs().shift(1).rolling(30, min_periods=30).quantile(0.90)
        transition_entropy = _pre_event_transition_entropy(ret, volume)

        cash_ratio = data["cashRatio"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        current_ratio = data["currentRatio"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        debt_to_equity = data["debtToEquity"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        net_debt_to_ebitda = data["netDebtToEbitda"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eligible_buffer = (
            cash_ratio.notna()
            & current_ratio.notna()
            & debt_to_equity.notna()
            & net_debt_to_ebitda.notna()
            & debt_to_equity.ge(0.0)
        )
        buffer_score = (
            0.30 * rank(cash_ratio.clip(0.0, 10.0).where(eligible_buffer))
            + 0.25 * rank(current_ratio.clip(0.0, 10.0).where(eligible_buffer))
            + 0.25 * (1.0 - rank(debt_to_equity.clip(0.0, 10.0).where(eligible_buffer)))
            + 0.20 * (1.0 - rank(net_debt_to_ebitda.clip(-5.0, 15.0).where(eligible_buffer)))
            - 0.5
        ) * 2.0
        buffer_score = buffer_score.where(eligible_buffer).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        fresh_event = _fresh_release(eps_actual) | _fresh_release(revenue_actual)
        surprise_aligned = (
            signed_surprise.abs().ge(0.01)
            & ret.ne(0.0)
            & np.sign(ret).eq(np.sign(signed_surprise))
        )
        valid_market_state = (
            close.gt(0.0)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & volume_base.gt(0.0)
            & return_q90.gt(0.0)
            & transition_entropy.notna()
        )
        event_mask = (
            fresh_event
            & (eps_valid | revenue_valid)
            & surprise_aligned
            & valid_market_state
            & ret.abs().ge(return_q90)
            & volume.ge(volume_base)
        )

        impact_strength = (ret.abs() / return_q90).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        participation_strength = np.sqrt((volume / volume_base).clip(0.0, 4.0))
        completion_strength = (1.0 - transition_entropy).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        # High buffers imply absorption and reversal; low buffers imply propagation.
        signal = -np.sign(ret) * buffer_score * impact_strength * participation_strength * completion_strength
        return signal.where(event_mask & eligible_buffer, 0.0).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Buffer-Conditioned Event Completion Polarity
programs.trading_idea: A surprise-aligned earnings burst following a low-entropy return-volume state is evidence of concentrated, nearly completed directional participation, but its six-day markout depends on the issuer's capacity to attract offsetting risk capital. Well-buffered firms can absorb the completed burst through balance-sheet-supported liquidity and fundamental dip buying, so the event-day move tends to mean-revert; financially fragile firms instead face adverse-selection and financing-risk amplification, so the same concentrated shock is more likely to propagate in its original direction. This interaction improves on Parent B's unconditional fade by identifying when completion is actually absorbed, and on Parent A by using the pre-event concentration state to distinguish a transient burst from an informationally persistent pressure episode.
programs.description: On fresh surprise-aligned earnings releases, the factor measures return-volume impact strength and low pre-event four-state transition entropy. It fades the event return for firms with strong liquidity and low leverage, while following it for weak-buffer firms, with exposure increasing in concentrated-event intensity.

programs.code:
"""Fundamental catalyst release through sector-synchronous gap-repair execution state.

Mechanism: fresh earnings and revenue information is assimilated most cleanly after
an opposite liquidity-impact impulse has relaxed.  Sector-wide stressed gap repairs
then identify whether lagged volume-price phase validates renewed execution in the
fundamental direction, rather than a generic endpoint rebound.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_peer_fraction(
    stressed: pd.DataFrame,
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    labels: pd.Series,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Contemporaneous but excluding-self sector stress breadth."""
    fraction = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=stressed.index, columns=stressed.columns)
    count = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=stressed.index, columns=stressed.columns)
    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        cols = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(cols) == 0:
            continue
        group_valid = valid.loc[:, cols].astype(float)
        group_stress = stressed.loc[:, cols].astype(float)
        total_valid = group_valid.sum(axis=1)
        total_stress = group_stress.sum(axis=1)
        peer_valid = group_valid.rsub(total_valid, axis=0)
        peer_stress = group_stress.rsub(total_stress, axis=0)
        count.loc[:, cols] = peer_valid
        fraction.loc[:, cols] = peer_stress.div(peer_valid.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
    return fraction, count


def _fresh_joint_catalyst(
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Marks the disclosure bar and the following five bars, causally."""
    available = eps_surprise.notna() & revenue_surprise.notna()
    eps_update = eps_surprise.ne(eps_surprise.shift(1)) | eps_surprise.shift(1).isna()
    revenue_update = revenue_surprise.ne(revenue_surprise.shift(1)) | revenue_surprise.shift(1).isna()
    update = available & (eps_update | revenue_update)
    return update.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).max().gt(0.0)


def _joint_surprise_polarity(
    eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
    revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Scale-free cross-sectional joint surprise direction."""
    valid = eps_surprise.notna() & revenue_surprise.notna()
    eps_score = 2.0 * eps_surprise.where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
    revenue_score = 2.0 * revenue_surprise.where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
    return ((eps_score + revenue_score) / 2.0).where(valid)


def _lagged_phase_support(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    gap_sign: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Volume-first directional path support, using only prior bars."""
    bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    displacement = ((close - open_) / bar_range).clip(-2.0, 2.0)
    log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume >= 0.0))
    prior_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=15).mean()
    prior_std = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(15, min_periods=15).std(ddof=0)
    volume_z = ((log_volume - prior_mean) / prior_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
    path = (volume_z.shift(1) * displacement.shift(1)).rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
    return path * gap_sign


@register_factor
class CatalystSectorGapPhaseRelease(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "catalyst_sector_gap_phase_release"
    name = "Catalyst Sector Gap-Phase Release"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Trades fresh joint earnings and revenue surprise polarity after an opposite "
        "impact shock has recovered, but only when a sector-synchronous stressed gap "
        "repair has lagged volume-price phase confirmation in that same direction."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        close = data["close"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        midpoint = ((high + low) / 2.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        stress = (bar_range / midpoint) * (prior_volume / volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        stress = stress.where((close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0) & (bar_range > 0.0))
        stress_mean = stress.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=45).mean()
        stress_std = stress.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=45).std(ddof=0)
        stress_z = ((stress - stress_mean) / stress_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        stressed = stress_z.ge(1.5) & stress_z.notna()

        labels = data["sector"].iloc[0]
        peer_fraction, peer_count = _sector_peer_fraction(stressed, stress_z.notna(), labels)
        synchrony = peer_fraction.ge(0.40) & peer_count.ge(6.0)

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        gap = open_ / previous_close - 1.0
        gap_sign = np.sign(gap)
        intraday_return = close / open_.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        repair = (-intraday_return / gap.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        phase = _lagged_phase_support(open_, high, low, close, volume, gap_sign)
        phase_rank = phase.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        phase_confirmed = phase_rank.ge(0.65)

        valid_price = close.gt(0.0) & close.shift(1).gt(0.0)
        log_return = np.log(close.where(valid_price) / close.shift(1).where(valid_price))
        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(valid_price & volume.gt(0.0))
        impact = log_return.abs() / (dollar_volume + 1.0)
        impact_base = impact.shift(1).rolling(40, min_periods=30).mean()
        impact_multiple = impact / impact_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        prior_pressure = (
            impact_multiple.shift(1).ge(2.0)
            & close_location.shift(1).abs().ge(0.60)
            & log_return.abs().shift(1).ge(log_return.abs().shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median())
        )
        capacity = dollar_volume.ge(0.80 * dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median())
        muted = log_return.abs().le(0.60 * log_return.abs().shift(1))
        recovered = capacity & muted

        polarity = _joint_surprise_polarity(eps_surprise, revenue_surprise)
        catalyst = _fresh_joint_catalyst(eps_surprise, revenue_surprise)
        opposed = polarity * (-np.sign(close_location.shift(1)))
        aligned_gap_execution = polarity * gap_sign
        active = (
            catalyst
            & prior_pressure
            & recovered
            & synchrony
            & phase_confirmed
            & repair.ge(0.35)
            & opposed.gt(0.0)
            & aligned_gap_execution.gt(0.0)
            & polarity.notna()
        )
        confidence = (2.0 * phase_rank - 1.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        raw = (polarity * peer_fraction * repair * confidence).where(active)

        score = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
            cols = labels.index[labels == group]
            if len(cols) == 0:
                continue
            group_raw = raw.loc[:, cols]
            group_active = active.loc[:, cols]
            group_mean = group_raw.where(group_active).mean(axis=1)
            score.loc[:, cols] = group_raw.sub(group_mean, axis=0).where(group_active, 0.0)
        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Catalyst Sector Gap-Phase Release
programs.trading_idea: Fresh joint earnings and revenue surprises are most informative when they arrive after an opposite name-specific impact shock has visibly relaxed, because the earlier move is then more likely forced inventory transfer than durable information. The child additionally requires a sector-synchronous liquidity-stress gap repair whose lagged volume-price phase supports the catalyst direction: phase-confirmed repairs reveal unfinished execution in the surprise direction, whereas unsupported repairs are excluded rather than mechanically faded. This interaction distinguishes fundamental assimilation released from temporary inventory pressure from either a standalone surprise or a generic sector stress repair.
programs.description: Ranks active combined earnings and revenue surprise polarity only after opposite high-impact pressure has recovered and a repaired opening gap in a sector-wide stress episode has phase-confirmed the same direction. Scores are sector demeaned to retain the idiosyncratic catalyst-release component.

programs.code:
"""A newly reported EPS surprise corroborated by a same-direction revenue surprise is a higher-information event than a price-and-volume pattern alone. When the close-to-close response on the release day is directionally consistent but small relative to the stock's recent daily volatility, the market has only partially incorporated that public information, creating a testable six-bar post-event drift proxy. This does not infer institutional flow, dealer inventory, or hidden metaorders; it tests whether public fundamental news receives a muted initial price response."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cross_sectional_winsorize(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize each timestamp's available cross-section at 2.5% and 97.5%."""
    lower = df.quantile(0.025, axis=1)
    upper = df.quantile(0.975, axis=1)
    return df.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)


def _cross_sectional_zscore(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Population cross-sectional z-score, preserving unavailable observations."""
    mean = df.mean(axis=1)
    std = df.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return df.sub(mean, axis=0).div(std, axis=0)


@register_factor
class ConcordantSurpriseUnderreactionDriftH6(BaseFactor):
    """Concordant accounting surprises gated by muted same-day price absorption."""

    factor_id = "concordant_surprise_underreaction_drift_h6"
    name = "Concordant Surprise Underreaction Drift"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks newly available, same-direction EPS and revenue surprises when "
        "the directionally consistent release-day return is small relative to "
        "trailing daily volatility, identifying potentially underreacted public news."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        daily_return = close.div(prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)).sub(1.0)
        trailing_sigma = daily_return.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
        trailing_sigma = trailing_sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        valid_scale = (close > 0.0) & (market_cap > 0.0)
        eps_scaled = eps_surprise.div(close.where(close > 0.0))
        revenue_scaled = revenue_surprise.div(market_cap.where(market_cap > 0.0))
        eps_scaled = eps_scaled.where(valid_scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_scaled = revenue_scaled.where(valid_scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        eps_z = _cross_sectional_zscore(_cross_sectional_winsorize(eps_scaled))
        revenue_z = _cross_sectional_zscore(
            _cross_sectional_winsorize(revenue_scaled)
        )
        event_strength = 0.5 * (eps_z + revenue_z)

        eps_changed = eps_surprise.ne(eps_surprise.shift(1))
        revenue_changed = revenue_surprise.ne(revenue_surprise.shift(1))
        concordant_sign = (
            ((eps_surprise > 0.0) & (revenue_surprise > 0.0))
            | ((eps_surprise < 0.0) & (revenue_surprise < 0.0))
        )

        response_ratio = (
            np.sign(event_strength)
            * daily_return.div(trailing_sigma)
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        eligible = (
            valid_scale
            & eps_surprise.notna()
            & revenue_surprise.notna()
            & eps_changed
            & revenue_changed
            & concordant_sign
            & event_strength.notna()
            & daily_return.notna()
            & trailing_sigma.notna()
            & (response_ratio >= 0.0)
            & (response_ratio <= 0.75)
        )

        raw_score = event_strength * (1.0 - response_ratio / 0.75)
        eligible_raw = raw_score.where(eligible).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eligible = eligible & eligible_raw.notna()
        winsorized_raw = _cross_sectional_winsorize(eligible_raw.where(eligible))
        percentile_rank = winsorized_raw.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        signal = (2.0 * percentile_rank - 1.0).where(eligible, 0.0)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Concordant Surprise Underreaction Drift
programs.trading_idea: A newly reported EPS surprise corroborated by a same-direction revenue surprise is a higher-information event than a price-and-volume pattern alone. When the close-to-close response on the release day is directionally consistent but small relative to the stock's recent daily volatility, the market has only partially incorporated that public information, creating a testable six-bar post-event drift proxy. This does not infer institutional flow, dealer inventory, or hidden metaorders; it tests whether public fundamental news receives a muted initial price response.
programs.description: At close t, compute daily return r_t = close_t / close_{t-1} - 1 and trailing volatility sigma_t as the sample standard deviation of the 20 returns from t-20 through t-1, requiring 20 valid observations. Define scaled current-quarter surprises a_t = epsSurprise_t / close_t and b_t = revenueSurprise_t / marketCap_t; require positive close and marketCap. Winsorize a_t and b_t independently each day at their cross-sectional 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles, then cross-sectionally standardize each to z_a and z_b and set E_t = 0.5 * (z_a + z_b). A name is eligible only if both surprise fields are nonmissing, both changed from t-1 to t (identifying the newly available report), epsSurprise_t and revenueSurprise_t have the same nonzero sign, and q_t = sign(E_t) * r_t / sigma_t lies in [0, 0.75]. For eligible names, raw score is E_t * (1 - q_t / 0.75); all other names receive zero. Winsorize eligible raw scores cross-sectionally at 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles and convert their eligible-only cross-sectional percentile rank to 2 * rank - 1, leaving ineligible names at zero. The signal is formed solely with fields available through close t and may be traded no earlier than t+1. Unlike the existing concealed-flow and arrival-curvature family, this factor uses no volume, return-signed volume, range, impact-per-volume, participation persistence, or curvature feature: its primary observable is the cross-confirmation of two point-in-time accounting surprises, with price response used only as an underreaction filter.

programs.code:
"""The signal does not attempt to identify dealer inventory relief from daily bars. Instead, it treats a failed partial recovery as an observable price-pressure continuation state: during a synchronized peer liquidity-impact episode, a stock that gaps down, recovers only partway, and closes near its low has not demonstrated sufficient clearing demand by the close. The proposed six-bar effect is slow completion of correlated de-risking and execution flows, rather than an assertion that any single intraday bounce uniquely reveals institutional supply."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_peer_breadth(
    stress: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causally compute same-date leave-one-out peer stress breadth.

    Industry is preferred when it has at least five other valid stress
    observations; otherwise the sector breadth is used when available.
    """
    breadth = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=stress.index, columns=stress.columns)

    for timestamp in stress.index:
        values = stress.loc[timestamp]
        industry_labels = industry.loc[timestamp]
        sector_labels = sector.loc[timestamp]

        def grouped_peer_stats(labels: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series]:
            valid = values.notna() & labels.notna()
            observed_values = values.where(valid, 0.0)
            observed_labels = labels[valid]
            grouped_values = observed_values[valid]

            if grouped_values.empty:
                empty = pd.Series(np.nan, index=values.index, dtype=float)
                return empty, empty

            sums = grouped_values.groupby(observed_labels).sum()
            counts = grouped_values.groupby(observed_labels).count()

            group_sum = labels.map(sums)
            group_count = labels.map(counts)
            peer_sum = group_sum - observed_values
            peer_count = group_count - valid.astype(float)
            return peer_sum, peer_count

        industry_sum, industry_count = grouped_peer_stats(industry_labels)
        sector_sum, sector_count = grouped_peer_stats(sector_labels)

        industry_breadth = industry_sum / industry_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        sector_breadth = sector_sum / sector_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        use_industry = industry_count >= 5.0
        use_sector = (~use_industry) & (sector_count >= 5.0)

        row_breadth = pd.Series(np.nan, index=values.index, dtype=float)
        row_breadth = row_breadth.where(~use_industry, industry_breadth)
        row_breadth = row_breadth.where(~use_sector, sector_breadth)
        breadth.loc[timestamp] = row_breadth

    return breadth


@register_factor
class PeerLiquidityReliefDistributionCarry(BaseFactor):
    """Short failed refills during broad peer liquidity-impact stress."""

    factor_id = "peer_liquidity_relief_distribution_carry"
    name = "Peer-Stress Failed-Refill Continuation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks stocks with abnormal own price impact, a downside gap that only "
        "partially refills, a weak close location, and persistent leave-one-out "
        "peer impact-stress breadth. Higher values are short signals."
    )
    window_length = 62
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "industry", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_price = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry = data["industry"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        bar_range = high - low
        true_range = np.maximum(
            np.maximum(bar_range, (high - prior_close).abs()),
            (low - prior_close).abs(),
        )

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where((close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0))
        impact = (true_range / dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(true_range > 0.0)
        log_impact = np.log(impact.where(impact > 0.0))

        historical_impact = log_impact.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=60)
        impact_threshold = historical_impact.quantile(0.80)
        historical_median = historical_impact.median()

        valid_stress = log_impact.notna() & impact_threshold.notna()
        own_stress = (log_impact > impact_threshold).astype(float).where(valid_stress)

        peer_breadth = _leave_one_out_peer_breadth(own_stress, industry, sector)
        peer_episode = (peer_breadth >= 0.60) & (peer_breadth.shift(1) >= 0.60)

        gap = open_price / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        refill = (close - open_price) / (prior_close - open_price).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        clv = (close - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        impact_deviation = log_impact - historical_median
        cross_sectional_rank = impact_deviation.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        qualifying = (
            peer_episode
            & (gap <= -0.01)
            & (refill >= 0.25)
            & (refill <= 0.95)
            & (close < prior_close)
            & (clv <= 0.35)
            & (bar_range > 0.0)
            & (own_stress == 1.0)
            & log_impact.notna()
            & historical_median.notna()
            & cross_sectional_rank.notna()
        )

        gap_severity = ((-gap - 0.01) / 0.04).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        raw_severity = (
            peer_breadth
            * gap_severity
            * (1.0 - clv)
            * (0.5 + 0.5 * cross_sectional_rank)
        ).where(qualifying)

        lower = raw_severity.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = raw_severity.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        winsorized = raw_severity.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
        scored = winsorized.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        return scored.where(qualifying, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Peer-Stress Failed-Refill Continuation
programs.trading_idea: The signal does not attempt to identify dealer inventory relief from daily bars. Instead, it treats a failed partial recovery as an observable price-pressure continuation state: during a synchronized peer liquidity-impact episode, a stock that gaps down, recovers only partway, and closes near its low has not demonstrated sufficient clearing demand by the close. The proposed six-bar effect is slow completion of correlated de-risking and execution flows, rather than an assertion that any single intraday bounce uniquely reveals institutional supply.
programs.description: All quantities are formed after the close of day t and are first traded at open(t+1). Define prior close P_i,t=close_i,t-1, true range TR_i,t=max(high_i,t-low_i,t,abs(high_i,t-P_i,t),abs(low_i,t-P_i,t)), dollar volume DV_i,t=close_i,t*volume_i,t, and impact I_i,t=TR_i,t/DV_i,t for positive-price, positive-volume observations. A stock has an own impact-stress flag H_i,t=1 when log(I_i,t) exceeds its own trailing 60-observation 80th percentile computed from t-60 through t-1; no future values are used. For each stock, peers are all other valid names in its industry; if fewer than five valid industry peers exist, use its sector instead, provided there are at least five valid sector peers. The leave-one-out peer-stress breadth is B_i,t=mean(H_j,t) across those peers. A peer-stress episode requires B_i,t>=0.60 both on t and t-1. The stock must additionally satisfy: downside opening gap g_i,t=open_i,t/P_i,t-1<=-0.01; partial refill r_i,t=(close_i,t-open_i,t)/(P_i,t-open_i,t) in [0.25,0.95]; failed prior-close reclaim close_i,t<P_i,t; close-location value CLV_i,t=(close_i,t-low_i,t)/(high_i,t-low_i,t)<=0.35; and own impact stress H_i,t=1. Zero-range bars, missing prior closes, missing peer classifications, and insufficient-peer observations are excluded. For qualifying names, raw severity is S_i,t=B_i,t*clip((-g_i,t-0.01)/0.04,0,1)*(1-CLV_i,t)*[0.5+0.5*CSRank(log(I_i,t)-median(log(I_i,t-60:t-1)))], where CSRank is the same-day cross-sectional percentile rank among valid stocks. S is winsorized cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th percentiles and converted to a [0,1] percentile rank; non-qualifiers receive zero. Higher scores are short signals, so the expected forward-return sign is negative. This differs from standalone gap continuation or own-impact factors because the signal requires the interaction of leave-one-out two-day peer breadth, own abnormal impact, and an incomplete recovery; any incremental test should externally residualize this score against the named parent-factor exposures when those book-level exposures are available.

"""This is a single-sided short signal, not a symmetric leader/laggard composite. A prior sector leader that experiences a high-participation, wide-range selloff closing near its low while an independently measured leave-one-out peer basket continues to advance is treated as a non-receiver of an ongoing sector demand impulse. The mandatory peer-impulse condition is intended to separate stock-specific adverse reassessment or distribution from a sector-wide reversal; the factor forecasts negative six-bar returns for selected names and is executed no earlier than the next bar."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_transform(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, operation: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Apply a cross-sectional transform independently within static sectors."""
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform(operation).T


def _sector_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Ascending average-tie ranks within each date-sector cross-section."""
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(method="average", ascending=True).T


@register_factor
class SectorImpulseNonreceiverDistribution(BaseFactor):
    """Short prior leaders suffering idiosyncratic distribution despite sector demand."""

    factor_id = "sector_impulse_nonreceiver_distribution"
    name = "Leave-One-Out Sector Impulse Non-Receiver"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Binary short-selection signal for prior sector leaders whose severe, "
        "high-participation distribution day contrasts with positive leave-one-out "
        "sector peer returns and breadth."
    )
    window_length = 66
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector_frame = data["sector"]

        # Sector is explicitly static. Filling labels only resolves sparse feed
        # representation and does not introduce a time-varying market datum.
        sector_labels = sector_frame.ffill().bfill().iloc[0]

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        daily_range = (high - low) / close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_range = daily_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()

        close_recent_positive = (
            close.rolling(21, min_periods=21).min() > 0.0
        )
        volume_recent_positive = (
            volume.rolling(21, min_periods=21).min() > 0.0
        )

        eligible = (
            close_recent_positive
            & volume_recent_positive
            & (close.shift(65) > 0.0)
            & (close.shift(5) > 0.0)
            & close.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & (high > low)
            & (prior_volume > 0.0)
            & (prior_range > 0.0)
            & sector_labels.notna()
        )

        leadership_return = close.shift(5) / close.shift(65).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        interruption_return = close / close.shift(5).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        abnormal_volume = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        range_ratio = daily_range / prior_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = (close - low) / (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        eligible_float = eligible.astype(float)
        sector_count = _sector_transform(eligible_float, sector_labels, "sum")
        peer_count = sector_count - eligible_float

        eligible_leadership = leadership_return.where(eligible)
        sector_leadership_sum = _sector_transform(
            eligible_leadership, sector_labels, "sum"
        )
        peer_leadership = (
            sector_leadership_sum - eligible_leadership
        ) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relative_leadership = leadership_return - peer_leadership

        leadership_rank = _sector_rank(eligible_leadership, sector_labels)
        leadership_percentile = leadership_rank / sector_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        eligible_interruption = interruption_return.where(eligible)
        sector_interruption_sum = _sector_transform(
            eligible_interruption, sector_labels, "sum"
        )
        peer_return = (
            sector_interruption_sum - eligible_interruption
        ) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        positive_interruption = (
            (interruption_return > 0.0) & eligible
        ).astype(float)
        sector_positive_count = _sector_transform(
            positive_interruption, sector_labels, "sum"
        )
        peer_breadth = (
            sector_positive_count - positive_interruption
        ) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        valid_peer_set = eligible & (peer_count >= 8.0)
        selected = (
            valid_peer_set
            & (leadership_percentile >= 0.70)
            & (relative_leadership > 0.0)
            & (interruption_return <= -0.05)
            & (abnormal_volume >= 1.50)
            & (range_ratio >= 1.50)
            & (close_location <= 0.25)
            & (peer_return >= 0.01)
            & (peer_breadth >= 0.60)
        )

        # Ineligible names and sectors without eight leave-one-out peers are
        # outside the signal universe; valid eligible names receive binary D.
        return selected.astype(float).where(valid_peer_set)
programs.name: Leave-One-Out Sector Impulse Non-Receiver
programs.trading_idea: This is a single-sided short signal, not a symmetric leader/laggard composite. A prior sector leader that experiences a high-participation, wide-range selloff closing near its low while an independently measured leave-one-out peer basket continues to advance is treated as a non-receiver of an ongoing sector demand impulse. The mandatory peer-impulse condition is intended to separate stock-specific adverse reassessment or distribution from a sector-wide reversal; the factor forecasts negative six-bar returns for selected names and is executed no earlier than the next bar.
programs.description: At the close of bar t, form the signal using only bars dated t or earlier; earliest execution is at t+1. A stock i is eligible only if close is positive and non-missing at t-65, t-20 through t, and t-5; volume is positive and non-missing at t-20 through t; high, low, and close are non-missing at t; high_t > low_t; and the following prior-20-bar averages are positive: mean(volume[t-20:t-1]) and mean((high-low)/close[t-1] over bars t-20:t-1). Define E_t as all eligible stocks. For stock i, define P_i,t as eligible stocks in E_t with the same static sector label as i, excluding i. Require at least 8 leave-one-out peers, |P_i,t| >= 8; otherwise i receives NaN. Define prior leadership return LRet_i,t = close_i,t-5 / close_i,t-65 - 1. For every j in the same eligible sector, compute LRet_j,t identically. Define leadership percentile LPct_i,t as the ascending fractional rank of LRet_i,t among all eligible stocks in i's sector, using average ranks for ties divided by the sector eligible count. Define relative prior leadership RelLead_i,t = LRet_i,t - mean(LRet_j,t for j in P_i,t). A stock is a prior leader only if LPct_i,t >= 0.70 and RelLead_i,t > 0. Define interruption return IR_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-5 - 1. Define abnormal-volume ratio AV_i,t = volume_i,t / mean(volume_i,t-20:t-1). Define daily range ratio Range_i,t = ((high_i,t-low_i,t)/close_i,t-1) / mean((high_i,s-low_i,s)/close_i,s-1 for s=t-20,...,t-1). Define close location CL_i,t = (close_i,t-low_i,t)/(high_i,t-low_i,t). For each peer j, define peer interruption return IR_j,t = close_j,t / close_j,t-5 - 1. Define leave-one-out peer return PeerRet_i,t = mean(IR_j,t for j in P_i,t) and peer breadth PeerBreadth_i,t = count(IR_j,t > 0 for j in P_i,t)/|P_i,t|. The binary factor is D_i,t = 1 if, jointly: prior-leader conditions hold; IR_i,t <= -0.05; AV_i,t >= 1.50; Range_i,t >= 1.50; CL_i,t <= 0.25; PeerRet_i,t >= 0.01; and PeerBreadth_i,t >= 0.60. Otherwise D_i,t = 0 for eligible stocks. No laggard-rebound counterpart is included. Aggregation is a strict logical AND rather than a tunable weighted composite: selected stocks are the D=1 cross-section and are the short side. The concrete distinction from sector_rank_interrupt_distribution_unwind is that this construction requires a quantitatively positive, leave-one-out sector impulse simultaneously in both equal-weight peer return and peer breadth, while defining leadership exclusively from the completed t-65 to t-5 interval and the interruption exclusively from t-5 to t; it does not infer sector support from a broad sector rank or use a symmetric reversal leg.
