"""The signal isolates a mechanically defined form of temporary selling-pressure absorption: a stock experiences an unusually poor intraday downside excursion during an industry-wide downside-stress day, yet closes relatively high in its own range while trading unusually high dollar volume with unusually low range-per-dollar-volume impact. The interpretation is deliberately limited to a conditional short-run reversal hypothesis rather than an inference about informed versus uninformed trading: conditional on common peer stress, recovery and low impact may indicate that end-of-day price pressure exceeded the permanent information component. The trade is formed after the completed daily bar and entered no earlier than the next tradable bar under the harness execution convention."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_window_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame, window: int, min_obs: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Standardize each value against its own strictly prior trailing history."""
    prior = values.shift(1)
    mean = prior.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    std = prior.rolling(window, min_periods=min_obs).std()
    return (values - mean) / std.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _peer_stress_breadth(
    downside_excursion: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute same-day leave-one-out stress using industry then sector fallback."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=downside_excursion.index, columns=downside_excursion.columns)

    for timestamp in downside_excursion.index:
        excursions = downside_excursion.loc[timestamp]
        industries = industry.loc[timestamp]
        sectors = sector.loc[timestamp]
        valid = excursions.notna()

        industry_count = valid.groupby(industries).transform("sum")
        industry_sum = excursions.where(valid).groupby(industries).transform("sum")
        sector_count = valid.groupby(sectors).transform("sum")
        sector_sum = excursions.where(valid).groupby(sectors).transform("sum")

        use_industry = industries.notna() & industry_count.ge(5)
        use_sector = (~use_industry) & sectors.notna() & sector_count.ge(5)

        selected_count = industry_count.where(use_industry, sector_count.where(use_sector))
        selected_sum = industry_sum.where(use_industry, sector_sum.where(use_sector))

        own_value = excursions.where(valid, 0.0)
        own_count = valid.astype(float)
        peer_count = selected_count - own_count
        peer_sum = selected_sum - own_value
        result.loc[timestamp] = peer_sum / peer_count.where(peer_count.gt(0.0))

    return result


@register_factor
class PeerStressResilienceImpactResidual(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks resilient, low-impact absorption during common peer downside stress."""

    factor_id = "peer_stress_resilience_impact_residual"
    name = "Peer-Stress Absorption Residual"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional composite of abnormal downside excursion, close-range "
        "recovery, dollar-volume innovation, low impact innovation, and "
        "leave-one-out industry or sector peer stress."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "industry", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        daily_return = close.pct_change()
        trailing_volatility = daily_return.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()

        downside_excursion = (previous_close - low) / previous_close
        downside_excursion = downside_excursion / trailing_volatility.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        intraday_range = high - low
        close_recovery = (close - low) / intraday_range.where(intraday_range.ne(0.0))

        dollar_volume = (close * volume.clip(lower=0.0)).where(close.notna())
        log_dollar_volume = np.log1p(dollar_volume.clip(lower=0.0))
        turnover_innovation = _prior_window_zscore(log_dollar_volume, 20, 15)

        impact = (intraday_range / previous_close) / log_dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        impact_innovation = _prior_window_zscore(impact, 20, 15)

        peer_stress = _peer_stress_breadth(
            downside_excursion,
            data["industry"],
            data["sector"],
        )

        score = (
            0.25 * rank(downside_excursion)
            + 0.25 * rank(close_recovery)
            + 0.20 * rank(turnover_innovation)
            + 0.20 * rank(-impact_innovation)
            + 0.10 * rank(peer_stress)
        )
        return rank(score).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.trading_idea: The signal isolates a mechanically defined form of temporary selling-pressure absorption: a stock experiences an unusually poor intraday downside excursion during an industry-wide downside-stress day, yet closes relatively high in its own range while trading unusually high dollar volume with unusually low range-per-dollar-volume impact. The interpretation is deliberately limited to a conditional short-run reversal hypothesis rather than an inference about informed versus uninformed trading: conditional on common peer stress, recovery and low impact may indicate that end-of-day price pressure exceeded the permanent information component. The trade is formed after the completed daily bar and entered no earlier than the next tradable bar under the harness execution convention.
programs.description: For each ticker i on day t, define dollar volume DV_i,t = close_i,t × volume_i,t. Define the 20-day trailing return volatility as SD of daily close-to-close returns over t-20 through t-1, requiring at least 15 valid observations. Define downside excursion DE_i,t = (close_i,t-1 − low_i,t) / close_i,t-1, divided by that trailing volatility. Define close recovery CR_i,t = (close_i,t − low_i,t) / (high_i,t − low_i,t), with CR set to NaN when high equals low. Define turnover innovation TV_i,t as log(1 + DV_i,t) minus its trailing 20-day mean over t-20 through t-1, divided by its trailing 20-day standard deviation, requiring at least 15 observations. Define impact I_i,t = (high_i,t − low_i,t) / close_i,t-1 divided by log(1 + DV_i,t), and define impact innovation II_i,t as I_i,t minus its trailing 20-day mean, divided by its trailing 20-day standard deviation, again requiring at least 15 observations. Peer groups are industry labels when at least five valid names, otherwise sector labels when at least five valid names; groups with fewer than five valid names produce NaN. Peer stress breadth PS_i,t is the mean of DE_j,t across eligible peers j in i's selected group excluding i. Within the full eligible cross-section each day, rank DE, CR, TV, negative II, and PS into ascending percentile ranks. The final signal is the cross-sectional percentile rank of 0.25×rank(DE) + 0.25×rank(CR) + 0.20×rank(TV) + 0.20×rank(−II) + 0.10×rank(PS). Higher values predict positive six-bar returns. No same-close execution is assumed.

"""Cash-backed quality latency amplified by temporary forced-flow stress."""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_relative_return(ret: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal same-day sector residual return with a minimum peer count."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(sector.dropna()):
        cols = sector.index[sector.eq(label)].tolist()
        sample = ret.loc[:, cols]
        count = sample.notna().sum(axis=1)
        mean = sample.mean(axis=1)
        out.loc[:, cols] = sample.sub(mean, axis=0).where(count.ge(4), np.nan)
    return out


def _row_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, neutral: float = 0.5) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Finite cross-sectional percentile rank with neutral sparse fallback."""
    clean = values.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return clean.rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(neutral)


@register_factor
class CashQualityForcedflowLatencyRelease(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_quality_forcedflow_latency_release"
    name = "Cash Quality Forced-Flow Release"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Muted positive cash-backed quality updates are carried for several bars "
        "and amplified when a post-selloff persistent-range stress state indicates "
        "temporary forced-flow suppression of fundamental assimilation."
    )
    window_length = 25
    inputs = [
        "close", "high", "low", "sector", "roic", "incomeQuality",
        "freeCashFlowYield", "totalDebt", "cash", "ebitda"
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        sector = data["sector"].iloc[0]

        quality_fields = [
            data["roic"].astype(float),
            data["incomeQuality"].astype(float),
            data["freeCashFlowYield"].astype(float),
        ]
        ranked_updates = []
        valid_updates = []
        for field in quality_fields:
            prior = field.ffill().shift(1)
            changed = field.notna() & prior.notna() & field.ne(prior)
            innovation = field.sub(prior).where(changed)
            ranked_updates.append(_row_rank(innovation) - 0.5)
            valid_updates.append(changed.astype(float))

        update_count = valid_updates[0] + valid_updates[1] + valid_updates[2]
        quality_update = (
            ranked_updates[0] + ranked_updates[1] + ranked_updates[2]
        ).div(update_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        positive_quality = quality_update.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)

        ret = close.pct_change()
        sector_ret = _sector_relative_return(ret, sector)
        response_rank = _row_rank(sector_ret)
        muted_response = ((0.65 - response_rank) / 0.65).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        event_latency = positive_quality * muted_response

        latency_memory = (
            event_latency
            + 0.75 * event_latency.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
            + 0.50 * event_latency.shift(2).fillna(0.0)
            + 0.30 * event_latency.shift(3).fillna(0.0)
        )

        valid_range = (high > 0.0) & (low > 0.0)
        log_range = np.log((high / low).where(valid_range)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        range_var = log_range.pow(2)
        fast_var = range_var.ewm(alpha=0.30, adjust=False, ignore_na=True).mean()
        slow_var = range_var.ewm(alpha=0.07, adjust=False, ignore_na=True).mean()
        range_autocorr = log_range.rolling(12, min_periods=8).corr(log_range.shift(1))
        persistence_ratio = np.log(
            slow_var.div(fast_var.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        persistence = (
            0.40 * _row_rank(range_autocorr)
            + 0.35 * _row_rank(persistence_ratio)
            + 0.25 * _row_rank(np.log(fast_var.replace(0.0, np.nan)))
        )

        debt = data["totalDebt"].astype(float)
        cash = data["cash"].astype(float)
        ebitda = data["ebitda"].astype(float)
        net_debt_multiple = (debt - cash).div(ebitda.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        positive_multiple = net_debt_multiple.where(ebitda > 0.0)
        fallback = positive_multiple.quantile(0.90, axis=1).fillna(0.0)
        fragility = positive_multiple.where(ebitda > 0.0, fallback, axis=0)
        fragility_rank = _row_rank(fragility)

        five_day_return = close.div(close.shift(5).replace(0.0, np.nan)).sub(1.0)
        selloff = (-five_day_return / 0.08).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)
        stress = (selloff * persistence * fragility_rank).fillna(0.0)

        raw = latency_memory * stress
        return raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).astype(float)
programs.name: Cash Quality Forced-Flow Release
programs.trading_idea: A positive, cash-backed quality update that receives little immediate relative-price recognition is normally an information-latency opportunity. The interaction is strongest after a downside range-volatility shock: Parent B's realized positive sign suggests persistent stressed trading often reflects temporary forced-flow exhaustion rather than reliable continuation, so this state mechanically suppresses initial assimilation of credible good news and creates a sharper subsequent rebound. Neither parent alone distinguishes ordinary disclosure underreaction from an update temporarily hidden by deleveraging and liquidity stress.
programs.description: The factor carries forward muted positive cross-sectional updates in ROIC, income quality, and free-cash-flow yield, then weights them by a post-selloff stress state built from persistent intrabar range variance, range autocorrelation, and net-debt fragility. Higher values identify credible positive fundamental revisions whose price response is temporarily obscured by forced selling.

"""Fundamental peer impulses identify temporary contrary-flow receiver dislocations."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_transform(
    values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, operation: str
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Apply a same-date transform inside static industry groups."""
    return values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform(operation).T


@register_factor
class IndustrySurpriseContraryFlowRecoil(BaseFactor):
    """Trade temporary idiosyncratic flow against a confirmed peer-news impulse."""

    factor_id = "industry_surprise_contrary_flow_recoil"
    name = "Industry Surprise Contrary-Flow Recoil"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Signed coherent industry earnings surprises are combined with a "
        "leave-one-out peer impulse and an own-stock high-participation move "
        "in the opposite direction."
    )
    window_length = 26
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"].reindex_like(close)
        low = data["low"].reindex_like(close)
        volume = data["volume"].reindex_like(close)
        industry_frame = data["industry"].reindex_like(close)
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"].reindex_like(close)
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"].reindex_like(close)
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"].reindex_like(close)

        industry_labels = industry_frame.ffill().bfill().iloc[0]
        valid_label = industry_labels.notna()

        eps_new = eps_surprise.notna() & (
            eps_surprise.shift(1).isna()
            | eps_surprise.ne(eps_surprise.shift(1))
        )
        revenue_new = revenue_surprise.notna() & (
            revenue_surprise.shift(1).isna()
            | revenue_surprise.ne(revenue_surprise.shift(1))
        )
        report_flag = eps_new | revenue_new

        eps_component = (
            eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        revenue_component = (
            revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(-0.25, 0.25)
        component_count = eps_component.notna().astype(float) + revenue_component.notna().astype(float)
        report_quality = (
            eps_component.fillna(0.0) + revenue_component.fillna(0.0)
        ) / component_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        reporter_score = report_quality.where(report_flag)

        reporter_count = _industry_transform(
            reporter_score.notna().astype(float), industry_labels, "sum"
        )
        industry_mean = _industry_transform(reporter_score, industry_labels, "mean")
        positive_share = _industry_transform(
            (reporter_score > 0.0).astype(float).where(reporter_score.notna()),
            industry_labels,
            "mean",
        )
        consensus = (positive_share >= 2.0 / 3.0) | (positive_share <= 1.0 / 3.0)
        coherent_event = industry_mean.where(
            (reporter_count >= 2.0)
            & consensus
            & (industry_mean.abs() >= 0.04)
            & valid_label
        )

        own_report_blackout = report_flag.astype(float).rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum().eq(0.0)
        daily_return = close / close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        return_count = _industry_transform(
            daily_return.notna().astype(float), industry_labels, "sum"
        )
        industry_return_sum = _industry_transform(daily_return, industry_labels, "sum")
        peer_count = return_count - daily_return.notna().astype(float)
        peer_return = (
            industry_return_sum - daily_return.fillna(0.0)
        ) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        event_sign = np.sign(coherent_event)
        aligned_return = (daily_return * event_sign > 0.0).astype(float).where(daily_return.notna())
        aligned_sum = _industry_transform(aligned_return, industry_labels, "sum")
        peer_breadth = (
            aligned_sum - aligned_return.fillna(0.0)
        ) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        prior_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        daily_range = (high - low) / close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_range = daily_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        volume_excess = (volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(0.0, 4.0)
        range_excess = (daily_range / prior_range.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(0.0, 4.0)
        close_location = (close - low) / (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        adverse_close = (event_sign * (0.5 - close_location)).clip(0.0, 0.5) * 2.0

        response_gap = (event_sign * (peer_return - daily_return)).clip(0.0, 0.20)
        peer_confirmation = (event_sign * peer_return > 0.0) & (peer_breadth >= 0.55)
        valid_market_data = (
            close.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & volume.notna()
            & (high > low)
            & (prior_volume > 0.0)
            & (prior_range > 0.0)
        )
        eligible = (
            coherent_event.notna()
            & own_report_blackout
            & valid_market_data
            & (peer_count >= 4.0)
            & peer_confirmation
        )

        raw_score = coherent_event * response_gap * (1.0 + volume_excess) * (1.0 + range_excess) * adverse_close
        ranked = 2.0 * raw_score.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        return ranked.where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0).astype(float)

The child trades receivers whose own high-volume, wide-range bar moves sharply against that verified impulse and closes at the adverse end of its range: this is more plausibly a temporary inventory/distribution shock than a revision of the shared fundamental signal. Neither parent has this edge alone because peer news without a price-response state cannot distinguish already-assimilated receivers, while an idiosyncratic distribution bar without a signed fundamental peer impulse cannot distinguish capitulation from genuinely adverse stock-specific information.

Positive-surprise names sold aggressively despite advancing peers receive positive scores; the symmetric negative-surprise case receives negative scores.

"""A large downside-semivariance innovation is interpreted as a transient order-imbalance candidate only when trading conditions subsequently normalize using information available by formation. The economic mechanism is not that a slow volatility estimate mechanically creates underpricing; rather, a downside shock that is large relative to the stock's own slow risk baseline but is followed by quickly declining range and participation is more consistent with exhausted forced selling and temporary dealer/inventory pressure than with an ongoing adverse-information cascade. Once the pressure state extinguishes, passive allocation demand and liquidity-provider inventory rebalancing can produce a short-horizon rebound; the signal is explicitly conditional because quiet trading after a selloff can otherwise indicate latent bad news."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _finite(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Replace non-finite numerical observations with missing values."""
    return frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _positive_cross_sectional_floor(
    first: pd.DataFrame, second: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.Series:
    """Small same-date scale-aware floor based on positive panel observations."""
    values = pd.concat([_finite(first), _finite(second)], axis=1)
    positive_values = values.where(values > 0.0)
    scale = positive_values.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    return scale.mul(1.0e-6).fillna(1.0e-12).clip(lower=1.0e-12)


def _industry_residual(
    values: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract each ticker's same-date static-industry median."""
    if values.empty or industry.empty:
        return values.astype(float) * np.nan

    labels = industry.iloc[0].reindex(values.columns)
    grouped_medians = values.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).median().T
    mapped_medians = grouped_medians.reindex(columns=labels.to_numpy())
    mapped_medians.columns = values.columns
    return values - mapped_medians


@register_factor
class DownsideVarianceMemoryMismatchRebound(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks exhausted downside shocks whose range and participation have normalized."""

    factor_id = "downside_variance_memory_mismatch_rebound"
    name = "Downside Shock Extinction Mismatch"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Industry-relative downside-semivariance shocks are rewarded only when "
        "the strictly subsequent trailing range and volume have compressed, "
        "indicating extinction of temporary forced-selling pressure."
    )
    window_length = 68
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _finite(data["close"])
        high = _finite(data["high"])
        low = _finite(data["low"])
        volume = _finite(data["volume"])
        industry = data["industry"]

        valid_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        ret = _finite(valid_close / valid_close.shift(1) - 1.0)
        downside_variance = ret.pow(2).where(ret < 0.0, 0.0)
        downside_variance = downside_variance.where(ret.notna())

        shock_mean = downside_variance.shift(3).rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        baseline_mean = downside_variance.shift(8).rolling(60, min_periods=60).mean()
        downside_floor = _positive_cross_sectional_floor(shock_mean, baseline_mean)
        shock = np.log(
            shock_mean.add(downside_floor, axis=0)
            / baseline_mean.add(downside_floor, axis=0)
        )
        shock = _finite(shock)

        valid_range = high.notna() & low.notna() & valid_close.notna()
        normalized_range = ((high - low) / valid_close).clip(lower=0.0)
        normalized_range = _finite(normalized_range.where(valid_range))

        recent_range = normalized_range.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        prior_range = normalized_range.shift(8).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        range_floor = _positive_cross_sectional_floor(recent_range, prior_range)
        range_change = np.log(
            recent_range.add(range_floor, axis=0)
            / prior_range.add(range_floor, axis=0)
        )
        range_change = _finite(range_change)

        valid_volume = volume.where(volume >= 0.0)
        recent_volume = valid_volume.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        prior_volume = valid_volume.shift(8).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        volume_floor = _positive_cross_sectional_floor(recent_volume, prior_volume)
        volume_change = np.log(
            recent_volume.add(volume_floor, axis=0)
            / prior_volume.add(volume_floor, axis=0)
        )
        volume_change = _finite(volume_change)

        shock_residual = _finite(_industry_residual(shock, industry))
        range_residual = _finite(_industry_residual(range_change, industry))
        volume_residual = _finite(_industry_residual(volume_change, industry))
        normalization = _finite(-0.5 * (range_residual + volume_residual))

        valid_signal = (
            shock_residual.notna()
            & normalization.notna()
            & np.isfinite(shock_residual)
            & np.isfinite(normalization)
        )
        shock_rank = rank(shock_residual.where(valid_signal))
        normalization_rank = rank(normalization.where(valid_signal))
        signal = _finite(shock_rank * normalization_rank)

        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: A large downside-semivariance innovation is interpreted as a transient order-imbalance candidate only when trading conditions subsequently normalize using information available by formation. The economic mechanism is not that a slow volatility estimate mechanically creates underpricing; rather, a downside shock that is large relative to the stock's own slow risk baseline but is followed by quickly declining range and participation is more consistent with exhausted forced selling and temporary dealer/inventory pressure than with an ongoing adverse-information cascade. Once the pressure state extinguishes, passive allocation demand and liquidity-provider inventory rebalancing can produce a short-horizon rebound; the signal is explicitly conditional because quiet trading after a selloff can otherwise indicate latent bad news.
programs.description: At formation close t, define daily close return r_u = close_u / close_{u-1} - 1 and downside variance d_u = r_u^2 * 1[r_u < 0]. Define the completed shock window as u = t-7 through t-3 and the non-overlapping slow baseline as u = t-67 through t-8. The downside-shock innovation is S_i,t = log((mean(d_i,u, u=t-7..t-3)+epsilon) / (mean(d_i,u, u=t-67..t-8)+epsilon)), with epsilon a small positive cross-sectional floor to avoid division by zero. Industry residualize S by subtracting the same-date median S among stocks in the same industry: Sres_i,t = S_i,t - median_industry(S_t). Define daily normalized range q_u = (high_u-low_u)/close_u. Measure post-shock normalization only from completed trailing bars: R_i,t = log((mean(q_i,u, u=t-2..t)+epsilon) / (mean(q_i,u, u=t-27..t-8)+epsilon)) and V_i,t = log((mean(volume_i,u, u=t-2..t)+epsilon) / (mean(volume_i,u, u=t-27..t-8)+epsilon)). Industry residualize both R and V using same-date industry medians. Define the normalization score N_i,t = -0.5*(Rres_i,t + Vres_i,t), so higher N means both recent range and volume are compressed relative to their pre-shock levels. Convert Sres and N to same-date cross-sectional percentile ranks after excluding missing or non-finite observations, and form M_i,t = rank(Sres_i,t) * rank(N_i,t). Go long the highest M ranks and short the lowest M ranks, subject to ordinary liquidity and universe controls in the harness. Every input, including the t bar close, high, low, and volume, is observed no later than formation close t; no post-formation observation is used. Portfolio trading begins at the next bar's open, after formation, and the return is evaluated over the fixed subsequent six-bar horizon. The construction can be exposure-tested directly against existing downside-pressure, range-repair, and liquidity-resilience factors because its distinctive component is the non-overlapping slow downside-semivariance innovation multiplied by strictly subsequent-but-still-trailing normalization.

"""This is a narrowly defined short-horizon reversal signal, not a direct measure of liquidity-provider inventory or forced selling. A stock that experiences an unusually high-volume negative daily return but closes materially above its intraday low has partially reversed its same-day downside move; conditional on the selloff and abnormal participation, this geometry may identify temporary price pressure whose residual component mean-reverts over the next six sessions. The factor uses only the downside-rejection leg because upside fades need not be economically symmetric under short-sale constraints and asymmetric incorporation of bad news."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _winsorized_cross_sectional_rank(
    raw_signal: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorize each date at valid 2nd/98th-percentile values, then rank."""
    lower = raw_signal.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
    upper = raw_signal.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
    winsorized = raw_signal.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    return rank(winsorized)


@register_factor
class DownsideTailAbsorptionReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks high-volume downside bars that reject their intraday lows."""

    factor_id = "downside_tail_absorption_reversal"
    name = "High-Volume Downside Rejection Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of abnormal-volume negative-return bars that "
        "close well above their intraday lows, identifying temporary downside "
        "price pressure expected to reverse over the next six sessions."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        daily_return = close / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0

        bar_range = high - low
        lower_tail_rejection = (close - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # Shift first so the current bar's participation cannot enter its own
        # abnormal-volume benchmark.
        prior_mean_volume = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        relative_volume = volume / prior_mean_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        required_valid = (
            close.notna()
            & previous_close.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & volume.notna()
            & (bar_range > 0.0)
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & prior_mean_volume.notna()
            & (prior_mean_volume > 0.0)
        )

        downside_pressure = (-daily_return).clip(lower=0.0)
        raw_downside = (
            downside_pressure
            * lower_tail_rejection
            * np.log1p(relative_volume)
        )

        # Non-negative-return bars are valid observations but carry no
        # downside-pressure signal; malformed or unavailable observations are
        # retained as NaN and therefore excluded from the cross section.
        raw_signal = raw_downside.where(daily_return < 0.0, 0.0)
        raw_signal = raw_signal.where(required_valid)

        return _winsorized_cross_sectional_rank(raw_signal)

A stock that experiences an unusually high-volume negative daily return but closes materially above its intraday low has partially reversed its same-day downside move; conditional on the selloff and abnormal participation, this geometry may identify temporary price pressure whose residual component mean-reverts over the next six sessions. The factor uses only the downside-rejection leg because upside fades need not be economically symmetric under short-sale constraints and asymmetric incorporation of bad news.
programs.description: At the close of day t, compute daily return r_t = close_t / close_{t-1} - 1 and lower-tail rejection L_t = (close_t - low_t) / (high_t - low_t) for bars with high_t > low_t; set L_t to NaN for zero-range bars. Compute relative volume RV_t = volume_t / mean(volume_{t-20:t-1}), requiring a strictly positive 20-prior-bar mean volume and setting the observation to NaN otherwise; current-day volume is excluded from the denominator. Define downside pressure D_t = max(-r_t, 0). The raw signal is S_t = D_t * L_t * log(1 + RV_t), with S_t set to zero when r_t >= 0, volume_t <= 0, or any required input is missing. Each day, winsorize valid raw signals cross-sectionally at the 2nd and 98th percentiles, then convert them to a cross-sectional percentile rank on [0,1]; missing or invalid observations remain NaN and are not traded. Higher ranks are expected to predict higher six-bar forward returns. The signal is finalized after the t close and is executed no earlier than the next tradable bar's open. No discretionary news or fundamental-disclosure exclusion is applied because no comprehensive news field is available in scope.

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _joint_transition_entropy(states: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal entropy of 9-state return-volume transitions over 20 bars."""
    values = states.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n_rows, n_cols = values.shape
    output = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    col_ids = np.arange(n_cols)
    normalizer = np.log(81.0)

    for end in range(19, n_rows):
        window = values[end - 19:end + 1]
        counts = np.full((n_cols, 81), 0.25, dtype=float)
        retained = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=int)
        for offset in range(19):
            previous = window[offset]
            current = window[offset + 1]
            valid = np.isfinite(previous) & np.isfinite(current)
            if valid.any():
                transition = previous[valid].astype(int) * 9 + current[valid].astype(int)
                np.add.at(counts, (col_ids[valid], transition), 1.0)
                retained[valid] += 1
        eligible = retained >= 12
        if eligible.any():
            probs = counts[eligible] / counts[eligible].sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
            output[end, eligible] = -(probs * np.log(probs)).sum(axis=1) / normalizer

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=states.index, columns=states.columns)


def _cross_sectional_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorized daily z-score with a stable zero fallback."""
    lower = values.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = values.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    clipped = values.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    std = clipped.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(std, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class AuctionGapVarianceRepairPolarity(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "auction_gap_variance_repair_polarity"
    name = "Auction Variance Repair Polarity"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectionally standardizes the polarity of abnormal downside opening "
        "auctions: long repaired variance-dislocation shocks and short failed ones, "
        "only after regular low-entropy sell pressure."
    )
    window_length = 45
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        open_ = data["open"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)

        prior_close = close.shift(1).where(close.shift(1) > 0.0)
        valid_return = close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.notna()
        log_return = np.log(close.where(valid_return) / prior_close.where(valid_return))

        positive_volume = volume.where(volume > 0.0)
        volume_base = positive_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        relative_volume = volume / volume_base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        state_valid = valid_return & relative_volume.notna() & volume.gt(0.0)

        return_state = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(log_return.to_numpy() < 0.0, 0.0,
                     np.where(log_return.to_numpy() > 0.0, 2.0, 1.0)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        volume_state = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(relative_volume.to_numpy() <= 0.80, 0.0,
                     np.where(relative_volume.to_numpy() <= 1.20, 1.0, 2.0)),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        entropy = _joint_transition_entropy((return_state * 3.0 + volume_state).where(state_valid))
        regularity = (1.0 - entropy.shift(1)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        signed_pressure = (
            log_return * relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        ).where(state_valid).rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
        prior_sell_pressure = (-signed_pressure.shift(1)).clip(lower=0.0)
        sell_scale = prior_sell_pressure.rolling(20, min_periods=12).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        cadence_gate = regularity * (prior_sell_pressure / sell_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

        valid_range = high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0) & high.ge(low)
        log_range = np.log(high.where(valid_range) / low.where(valid_range))
        range_variance = log_range.pow(2) / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))
        close_variance = log_return.pow(2)
        downside = log_return.lt(0.0)
        down_close = close_variance.where(downside, 0.0).ewm(halflife=10, adjust=False).mean()
        down_range = range_variance.where(downside, 0.0).ewm(halflife=10, adjust=False).mean()
        variance_dislocation = (
            (down_close - down_range) / (down_close + down_range).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        gap = np.log(open_.where(open_ > 0.0) / prior_close)
        prior_range_sigma = (
            log_range.pow(2).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean().pow(0.5)
        ).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        downside_gap = (-gap / prior_range_sigma).clip(lower=0.0, upper=5.0)
        abnormal_volume = (relative_volume - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        auction_stress = downside_gap * abnormal_volume

        width = (high - low).where(valid_range)
        close_location = ((close - low) / width.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        repair_polarity = 2.0 * close_location - 1.0

        valid = (
            gap.lt(0.0)
            & auction_stress.notna()
            & variance_dislocation.notna()
            & cadence_gate.notna()
            & repair_polarity.notna()
        )
        raw = (
            auction_stress
            * variance_dislocation
            * cadence_gate
            * repair_polarity
        ).where(valid, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        return _cross_sectional_zscore(raw).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Auction Variance Repair Polarity
programs.trading_idea: A downside gap with abnormal participation is ambiguous: a close near the low indicates an unrepaired auction failure and continuing inventory overhang, while a close near the high indicates that buyers absorbed the same forced-flow shock. The child conditions this auction polarity on Parent A's low-entropy negative selling cadence and Parent B's downside close-versus-range variance disagreement, identifying shocks likely caused by mechanical execution rather than fresh information. Neither parent alone jointly distinguishes whether a cadenced volatility shock is still propagating or has already been absorbed, so the interaction supports shorting failed repairs and buying genuine repairs.
programs.description: Computes a signed repaired-versus-failed downside-auction score from normalized opening-gap stress, abnormal volume, intrabar close location, and an exponentially weighted downside close/range variance dislocation. The signal is active only after persistent low-entropy, negative return-volume pressure and is cross-sectionally standardized.

"""A sharp selloff immediately following a newly available non-negative earnings and revenue surprise is more plausibly a temporary liquidity dislocation than a pure bad-news discovery event, particularly when the firm is not financially fragile. Elevated downside range volatility and unusual trading activity identify a state in which adverse-order-flow amplification can temporarily dominate the contemporaneous fundamental disclosure. The signal buys the names where intraday closes are beginning to move away from the lows, consistent with same-day absorption rather than a fully persistent downward-information state."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _finite_frame(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Replace non-finite panel values with NaN."""
    return frame.where(np.isfinite(frame))


def _winsorized_percentile(
    frame: pd.DataFrame, missing_rank: float = 0.5
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectionally winsorize finite observations and average-rank ties."""
    clean = _finite_frame(frame)
    lower = clean.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    upper = clean.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    clipped = clean.where(clean.ge(lower, axis=0), lower, axis=0)
    clipped = clipped.where(clipped.le(upper, axis=0), upper, axis=0)
    ranked = clipped.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True)
    return ranked.fillna(missing_rank)


def _cross_sectional_liquidity_gate(adv: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return one for available names at or above the daily 60th ADV percentile."""
    clean = _finite_frame(adv)
    available = clean.notna() & clean.gt(0.0)
    threshold = clean.where(available).quantile(0.60, axis=1)
    return available & clean.ge(threshold, axis=0)


@register_factor
class SolventPositiveEventDislocationReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Positive-surprise selloff reversal conditioned on liquidity and solvency."""

    factor_id = "solvent_positive_event_dislocation_reversal"
    name = "Solvent Positive-Event Dislocation Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Ranks temporary downside dislocations after fresh positive EPS and "
        "non-negative revenue surprises, requiring top-quintile liquidity and "
        "discounting financially fragile firms."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "debtToEquity",
        "interestCoverage",
        "currentRatio",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _finite_frame(data["close"])
        high = _finite_frame(data["high"])
        low = _finite_frame(data["low"])
        volume = _finite_frame(data["volume"])

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        three_bar_return = close / close.shift(3).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        downside = (-three_bar_return).clip(lower=0.0)
        downside_valid = (
            close.notna()
            & close.shift(3).notna()
            & close.shift(3).ne(0.0)
        )
        downside_rank = _winsorized_percentile(
            downside.where(downside_valid), missing_rank=0.5
        )

        range_a = high - low
        range_b = (high - previous_close).abs()
        range_c = (low - previous_close).abs()
        true_range = pd.concat([range_a, range_b, range_c], axis=0).groupby(level=0).max()
        normalized_tr = true_range / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tr_valid = (
            high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & previous_close.notna()
            & previous_close.gt(0.0)
            & normalized_tr.notna()
        )
        normalized_tr = normalized_tr.where(tr_valid)
        fast_vol = normalized_tr.pow(2).rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean().pow(0.5)
        slow_vol = normalized_tr.pow(2).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().pow(0.5)
        volatility_stress = (fast_vol / slow_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        volatility_rank = _winsorized_percentile(volatility_stress, missing_rank=0.5)

        bar_range = (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = (close - low) / bar_range
        flat_bar = high.eq(low) & high.notna() & low.notna() & close.notna()
        close_location = close_location.where(~flat_bar, 0.5)
        close_location = close_location.where(
            high.notna() & low.notna() & close.notna()
        )
        recent_location = close_location.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        prior_location = close_location.shift(3).rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        low_repair = (recent_location - prior_location).clip(lower=0.0)
        repair_rank = _winsorized_percentile(low_repair, missing_rank=0.5)

        prior_volume_mean = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        activity = volume / prior_volume_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        activity_valid = volume.notna() & prior_volume_mean.gt(0.0)
        activity_rank = _winsorized_percentile(
            activity.where(activity_valid), missing_rank=0.5
        )

        dollar_volume = close * volume
        adv = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        liquidity_gate = _cross_sectional_liquidity_gate(adv).astype(float)

        eps_surprise = _finite_frame(data["epsSurprise"])
        revenue_surprise = _finite_frame(data["revenueSurprise"])
        eps_previous = eps_surprise.shift(1)
        revenue_previous = revenue_surprise.shift(1)
        event_gate = (
            eps_surprise.notna()
            & eps_previous.notna()
            & revenue_surprise.notna()
            & revenue_previous.notna()
            & eps_surprise.ne(eps_previous)
            & revenue_surprise.ne(revenue_previous)
            & eps_surprise.gt(0.0)
            & revenue_surprise.ge(0.0)
        ).astype(float)

        leverage_rank = _winsorized_percentile(_finite_frame(data["debtToEquity"]))
        coverage_rank = _winsorized_percentile(-_finite_frame(data["interestCoverage"]))
        liquidity_rank = _winsorized_percentile(-_finite_frame(data["currentRatio"]))
        fragility = (leverage_rank + coverage_rank + liquidity_rank) / 3.0

        dislocation = (
            0.30 * downside_rank
            + 0.25 * volatility_rank
            + 0.20 * activity_rank
            + 0.25 * repair_rank
        )
        raw_score = event_gate * liquidity_gate * (1.0 - fragility) * dislocation
        return _winsorized_percentile(raw_score, missing_rank=0.5)

Elevated downside range volatility and unusual trading activity identify a state in which adverse-order-flow amplification can temporarily dominate the contemporaneous fundamental disclosure. The signal buys the names where intraday closes are beginning to move away from the lows, consistent with same-day absorption rather than a fully persistent downward-information state.
programs.description: All quantities are computed separately for each ticker at signal-date close t, using only bars dated t or earlier and point-in-time fundamental fields available at t. Define one-bar return r_t = close_t / close_(t-1) - 1. Define downside shock D_t = max(0, -(close_t / close_(t-3) - 1)). Define normalized true range TR_t = max(high_t-low_t, abs(high_t-close_(t-1)), abs(low_t-close_(t-1))) / close_(t-1). Fast range volatility is VF_t = sqrt(mean(TR^2 over t-2 through t)); slow range volatility is VS_t = sqrt(mean(TR^2 over t-19 through t)); volatility stress is V_t = max(0, VF_t / VS_t - 1). Define close location CL_t = (close_t-low_t)/(high_t-low_t), with CL_t = 0.5 when high_t equals low_t. Define away-from-low repair L_t = max(0, mean(CL over t-2 through t) - mean(CL over t-5 through t-3)). Define activity A_t = volume_t / mean(volume over t-20 through t-1), provided the denominator is positive. Define 20-day dollar-volume liquidity ADV_t = mean(close*volume over t-19 through t), and let Q_t equal 1 only when ADV_t is at or above that date's cross-sectional 60th percentile among available names; otherwise Q_t = 0. Define a hard contemporaneous disclosure gate E_t = 1 only if epsSurprise_t differs from epsSurprise_(t-1), revenueSurprise_t differs from revenueSurprise_(t-1), epsSurprise_t > 0, and revenueSurprise_t >= 0; otherwise E_t = 0. This gate uses the point-in-time availability-date steps of the surprise fields and does not infer a later confirmation. Financial fragility is F_t = [R(debtToEquity_t) + R(-interestCoverage_t) + R(-currentRatio_t)]/3, where R(x) is the cross-sectional percentile rank after winsorizing finite observations of x at the 1st and 99th percentiles; a missing fundamental component receives rank 0.5. Thus high F means high leverage, weak interest coverage, and weak liquidity. For each date, winsorize finite values of D, V, A, and L at the cross-sectional 1st and 99th percentiles, then convert each to percentile ranks RD, RV, RA, and RL using average ranks for ties. If a required OHLCV history is unavailable, or if volume history is invalid, set that component rank to 0.5; if ADV is unavailable, set Q to 0. The raw score is S_t = E_t * Q_t * (1-F_t) * (0.30*RD_t + 0.25*RV_t + 0.20*RA_t + 0.25*RL_t). The factor value is the cross-sectional percentile rank of winsorized S_t; names with no qualifying fresh positive event or insufficient liquidity receive S_t = 0. Rebalance once per day after the signal-date close, enter eligible high-score names at the next bar's open, and hold for six daily bars before exit; no centered window, future-bar confirmation, or future return-derived state is used. The explicit differentiator from the named pressure/repair factors is the mandatory E_t hard gate and the solvency penalty (1-F_t): this is not a standalone selloff, range-stress, turnover, or close-repair score. Exact duplication would require another factor to use the same jointly necessary condition of a newly updated positive EPS surprise, newly updated non-negative revenue surprise, top-40-percent dollar-volume eligibility, and the specified three-component point-in-time fragility penalty.

programs.code:
"""This is a reduced-form indicator of persistent adverse trading pressure, not a claim that daily bars identify a specific latent sell queue or liquidity-provider inventory. A stock is vulnerable when abnormal participation repeatedly coincides with closes near the low of the bar while its realized range remains below its own recent range regime; this distinguishes sustained directional imbalance from a single large-range news shock. The hypothesis is that, conditional on sector-relative comparison and adequate liquidity, this state predicts negative six-bar returns because the adverse order-flow or information-adjustment state has not yet dissipated."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _weighted_recent_sum(values: pd.DataFrame, length: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal linearly weighted sum, with the newest observation largest."""
    terms = []
    normalizer = float(length * (length + 1) // 2)
    for age in range(length - 1, -1, -1):
        weight = float(length - age) / normalizer
        terms.append(values.shift(age) * weight)
    return pd.concat(terms, axis=1).T.groupby(level=0).sum()


def _weighted_recent_sum_complete(values: pd.DataFrame, length: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal weighted sum that is NaN unless every required observation exists."""
    normalizer = float(length * (length + 1) // 2)
    result = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    valid_count = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for age in range(length - 1, -1, -1):
        shifted = values.shift(age)
        weight = float(length - age) / normalizer
        result = result + shifted.fillna(0.0) * weight
        valid_count = valid_count + shifted.notna().astype(float)
    return result.where(valid_count == float(length))


def _sector_or_universe_rank(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rank eligible names by sector, reverting small sectors to universe rank."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)

    for row_number, timestamp in enumerate(values.index):
        row_values = values.loc[timestamp]
        row_eligible = eligible.loc[timestamp].fillna(False).astype(bool)
        if not row_eligible.any():
            continue

        universe_rank = row_values.where(row_eligible).rank(pct=True)
        row_output = universe_rank.copy()
        labels = sector.loc[timestamp]

        valid_labels = labels.where(row_eligible).dropna().unique()
        for label in valid_labels:
            in_sector = row_eligible & (labels == label)
            if int(in_sector.sum()) >= 5:
                row_output.loc[in_sector] = row_values.where(in_sector).rank(pct=True).loc[in_sector]

        output.loc[timestamp] = row_output

    return output


@register_factor
class DownsideEndpointVolumeClockDivergence(BaseFactor):
    """Persistent downside endpoint participation under compressed realized range."""

    factor_id = "downside_endpoint_volume_clock_divergence"
    name = "Persistent Downside Participation Compression"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-relative rank of repeated low-close, abnormal-volume participation "
        "when recent realized range remains contained versus its trailing regime; "
        "higher values identify a six-bar short signal."
    )
    window_length = 25
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sector = data["sector"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        bar_range = high - low
        clv = (2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        clv = clv.fillna(0.0)
        endpoint = (-clv).clip(lower=0.0)

        prior_volume_mean = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        abnormal_volume = (volume / prior_volume_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(
            lower=0.0,
            upper=3.0,
        )

        normalized_range = bar_range / close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        pressure = _weighted_recent_sum_complete(endpoint * abnormal_volume, 5)
        recent_range = _weighted_recent_sum_complete(normalized_range, 5)
        baseline_range = normalized_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        containment = (1.0 - recent_range / baseline_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(
            lower=0.0,
            upper=1.0,
        )
        raw_score = pressure * containment

        close_valid = (close > 0.0).rolling(21, min_periods=21).sum() == 21.0
        volume_valid = (volume > 0.0).rolling(25, min_periods=25).sum() == 25.0
        range_valid = (
            high.notna() & low.notna() & (high >= low)
        ).rolling(21, min_periods=21).sum() == 21.0

        trailing_volume_mean = volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        dollar_volume_mean = (close * volume).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        basic_eligible = (
            close_valid
            & volume_valid
            & range_valid
            & (trailing_volume_mean > 0.0)
            & (prior_volume_mean > 0.0)
            & (baseline_range > 0.0)
            & raw_score.notna()
        )

        candidate_dollar_volume = dollar_volume_mean.where(basic_eligible)
        dollar_volume_cutoff = candidate_dollar_volume.quantile(0.30, axis=1)
        eligible = basic_eligible & dollar_volume_mean.ge(dollar_volume_cutoff, axis=0)

        eligible_score = raw_score.where(eligible)
        lower = eligible_score.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
        upper = eligible_score.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
        winsorized = eligible_score.clip(lower=lower, upper=upper, axis=0)

        return _sector_or_universe_rank(winsorized, eligible, sector)

A stock is vulnerable when abnormal participation repeatedly coincides with closes near the low of the bar while its realized range remains below its own recent range regime; this distinguishes sustained directional imbalance from a single large-range news shock. The hypothesis is that, conditional on sector-relative comparison and adequate liquidity, this state predicts negative six-bar returns because the adverse order-flow or information-adjustment state has not yet dissipated.
programs.description: At the close of day t, use only OHLCV observations through t. Eligible names must have positive close and volume on each required day, a positive 20-day trailing mean volume, and 20-day average dollar volume mean(close[s]*volume[s], s=t-19,...,t) at or above the cross-sectional 30th percentile. Define close location CLV[s]=(2*close[s]-high[s]-low[s])/(high[s]-low[s]) when high[s]>low[s], and CLV[s]=0 otherwise. Define downside endpoint E[s]=max(0,-CLV[s]). Define abnormal-volume excess A[s]=min(3,max(0,volume[s]/mean(volume[u],u=s-20,...,s-1)-1)); names with a nonpositive or unavailable denominator are ineligible. Define daily normalized range R[s]=(high[s]-low[s])/close[s]. Compute endpoint-participation pressure P[t]=sum_{j=0}^4 ((j+1)/15)*E[t-4+j]*A[t-4+j]. Compute recent range Rrecent[t]=sum_{j=0}^4 ((j+1)/15)*R[t-4+j] and baseline range Rbase[t]=mean(R[u],u=t-20,...,t-1). Define containment C[t]=min(1,max(0,1-Rrecent[t]/Rbase[t])); names lacking a positive baseline are ineligible. The raw score is D[t]=P[t]*C[t], so high scores require repeated downside endpoint pressure, above-normal volume, and range compression rather than merely a low close or a volatility shock. Winsorize D[t] cross-sectionally at the 1st and 99th percentiles among eligible names, then convert it to a percentile rank within sector; use the all-eligible-universe rank when a sector has fewer than five eligible names. Higher rank is the short signal. Compute after the close at t, enter no earlier than the next bar's open, and evaluate/hold the position through t+6; implementation should use six-bar rebalancing or non-overlapping six-bar cohorts to limit turnover.

programs.code:
"""The signal targets a specific temporal state rather than merely high signed volume in a compressed range: repeated, directionally consistent close-location pressure must be accompanied by unusually regular abnormal participation, followed by a measurable break in that participation cadence. A taper after regular one-sided pressure is interpreted as the completion of a predictable execution sequence, for which temporary price pressure can partially reverse over the following six trading days. The reversal interpretation is empirical rather than identified from OHLCV alone; the signal is therefore intended for incremental testing against existing volume-range-pressure factors."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cadence_state(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Construct the causal pressure, cadence regularity, and taper state."""
    bar_range = high - low
    current_valid = (
        np.isfinite(high)
        & np.isfinite(low)
        & np.isfinite(close)
        & np.isfinite(volume)
        & (close > 0.0)
        & (volume > 0.0)
        & (bar_range >= 0.0)
    )

    relative_range = (bar_range / close).where(current_valid)
    prior_valid_count = current_valid.astype(float).shift(1).rolling(
        20, min_periods=20
    ).sum()
    baseline_complete = prior_valid_count == 20.0

    volume_base = volume.where(current_valid).shift(1).rolling(
        20, min_periods=20
    ).median()
    range_base = relative_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
    baseline_valid = baseline_complete & (volume_base > 0.0) & (range_base > 0.0)

    abnormal_participation = np.log(volume / volume_base).where(
        current_valid & baseline_valid
    )

    close_location = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    nontrivial_range = current_valid & (relative_range > 0.0001)
    close_location = close_location.where(
        ~nontrivial_range,
        (2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan),
    )
    close_location = close_location.where(current_valid)

    compression = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    compression_mask = current_valid & baseline_valid & (relative_range > 0.0001)
    compression_value = np.log(range_base / relative_range).clip(lower=0.0)
    compression = compression.where(~compression_mask, compression_value)

    positive_abnormal = abnormal_participation.clip(lower=0.0)
    pressure = (close_location * positive_abnormal * compression).where(
        current_valid & baseline_valid
    )

    prior_pressure = pressure.shift(1).rolling(10, min_periods=10).mean()

    lag_pair_corr = (
        abnormal_participation.shift(1)
        .rolling(9, min_periods=9)
        .corr(abnormal_participation)
        .shift(1)
    )
    lag_pair_corr = lag_pair_corr.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
    prior_dispersion = abnormal_participation.shift(1).rolling(
        10, min_periods=10
    ).std()
    cadence = ((1.0 + lag_pair_corr) / 2.0) / (1.0 + prior_dispersion)

    early_participation = abnormal_participation.shift(6).rolling(
        5, min_periods=5
    ).mean()
    current_participation = abnormal_participation.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
    taper = early_participation - current_participation

    state = prior_pressure * cadence * taper

    # Each day in t-30 through t must itself have valid current data and a
    # complete valid 20-bar baseline, preventing implicit imputation.
    daily_observable = current_valid & baseline_valid
    complete_history = daily_observable.astype(float).rolling(
        31, min_periods=31
    ).sum() == 31.0
    return state.where(complete_history)


def _industry_median_residual(
    state: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract same-day industry median, falling back for small industries."""
    valid_state = state.where(np.isfinite(state))
    universe_median = valid_state.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
    benchmark = pd.DataFrame(
        {column: universe_median for column in state.columns}, index=state.index
    )

    labels = industry.iloc[0].copy()
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "__UNKNOWN_INDUSTRY__")

    for label in pd.unique(labels):
        group_columns = labels.index[labels == label]
        group_state = valid_state.loc[:, group_columns]
        group_median = group_state.median(axis=1, skipna=True)
        group_count = group_state.notna().sum(axis=1)
        chosen_median = group_median.where(group_count >= 5, universe_median)
        benchmark.loc[:, group_columns] = pd.DataFrame(
            {column: chosen_median for column in group_columns}, index=state.index
        )

    return valid_state - benchmark


@register_factor
class CadenceBreakAbsorptionInventoryReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Regular participation pressure that tapers after a predictable execution cadence."""

    factor_id = "cadence_break_absorption_inventory_reversal"
    name = "Cadence-Break Pressure Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Industry-residualized compressed close-location pressure whose abnormal "
        "volume participation was regular over nine lag pairs and has now tapered."
    )
    window_length = 51
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        state = _cadence_state(
            data["high"],
            data["low"],
            data["close"],
            data["volume"],
        )
        result = _industry_median_residual(state, data["industry"])
        return result.reindex(index=data["close"].index, columns=data["close"].columns)

programs.description: All quantities are computed using bars through close t only, and the portfolio may execute no earlier than the next bar open, t+1. For each ticker and day s, define relative range r_s=(high_s-low_s)/close_s when close_s>0; otherwise r_s is missing. Define close-location l_s=(2*close_s-high_s-low_s)/(high_s-low_s) when r_s>0.0001, and l_s=0 when 0<=r_s<=0.0001; invalid or nonpositive close/volume observations are missing. Let vbase_s be the median of volume over s-20 through s-1 and rbase_s be the median of r over s-20 through s-1. Require all 20 baseline observations to be valid and vbase_s>0 and rbase_s>0. Define abnormal participation a_s=log(volume_s/vbase_s), compression k_s=max(log(rbase_s/r_s),0), and signed compressed-pressure p_s=l_s*max(a_s,0)*k_s. At date t require valid observations for every day from t-30 through t, so that every stated rolling input is observable without imputation. Define prior directional pressure D_t=mean(p_{t-10},...,p_{t-1}). Define cadence regularity C_t=((1+corr(a_{t-10},...,a_{t-2}; a_{t-9},...,a_{t-1}))/2)/(1+stdev(a_{t-10},...,a_{t-1})), using sample correlation and sample standard deviation; if the correlation is undefined, the signal is missing. Define the participation taper T_t=mean(a_{t-10},...,a_{t-6})-mean(a_{t-2},...,a_t), so T_t>0 means current abnormal participation is below the earlier recurring-pressure segment. The raw state is S_t=D_t*C_t*T_t. On each date, residualize S_t by subtracting the contemporaneous median S_t of its industry, using only valid tickers on that date; an industry must have at least five valid names, otherwise subtract the all-universe contemporaneous median of valid S_t. The resulting residual is the factor value. Positive values represent regular prior buy-side compressed pressure followed by tapering participation and are expected to predict negative subsequent returns; negative values analogously represent sell-side pressure and expected positive returns. Unlike the cited compressed-range participation, escape-carry, tail-markout-release, and concealed-flow-drift signals, this construction is not a level or threshold on current signed volume-range pressure: its distinctive required inputs are the nine-pair lag-one autocorrelation of abnormal participation, its ten-bar dispersion penalty, and the explicitly dated early-window versus current-window cadence-break taper.
