The interpretation is deliberately limited to a conditional short-run reversal hypothesis rather than an inference about informed versus uninformed trading: conditional on common peer stress, recovery and low impact may indicate that end-of-day price pressure exceeded the permanent information component. The trade is formed after the completed daily bar and entered no earlier than the next tradable bar under the harness execution convention.
programs.description: For each ticker i on day t, define dollar volume DV_i,t = close_i,t × volume_i,t. Define the 20-day trailing return volatility as SD of daily close-to-close returns over t-20 through t-1, requiring at least 15 valid observations. Define downside excursion DE_i,t = (close_i,t-1 − low_i,t) / close_i,t-1, divided by that trailing volatility. Define close recovery CR_i,t = (close_i,t − low_i,t) / (high_i,t − low_i,t), with CR set to NaN when high equals low. Define turnover innovation TV_i,t as log(1 + DV_i,t) minus its trailing 20-day mean over t-20 through t-1, divided by its trailing 20-day standard deviation, requiring at least 15 observations. Define impact I_i,t = (high_i,t − low_i,t) / close_i,t-1 divided by log(1 + DV_i,t), and define impact innovation II_i,t as I_i,t minus its trailing 20-day mean, divided by its trailing 20-day standard deviation, again requiring at least 15 observations. Peer groups are industry labels when at least five valid names, otherwise sector labels when at least five valid names; groups with fewer than five valid names produce NaN. Peer stress breadth PS_i,t is the mean of DE_j,t across eligible peers j in i's selected group excluding i. Within the full eligible cross-section each day, rank DE, CR, TV, negative II, and PS into ascending percentile ranks. The final signal is the cross-sectional percentile rank of 0.25×rank(DE) + 0.25×rank(CR) + 0.20×rank(TV) + 0.20×rank(−II) + 0.10×rank(PS). Higher values predict positive six-bar returns. No same-close execution is assumed.

programs.code:
"""Sector-relative price/fundamental disagreement catch-up factor.

Mechanism: peer-relative price trends that conflict with a firm's cash-realization
and revenue-expectation state are more likely to be temporary extrapolation than
information. Improving cash fundamentals in a sector laggard support catch-up,
while deteriorating cash fundamentals in a sector leader support repricing down.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_rank(value: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank within static sector groups."""
    labels = sector.ffill().bfill().iloc[0]
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=value.index, columns=value.columns)
    valid_labels = labels.dropna()

    for label in pd.unique(valid_labels):
        members = labels.index[labels == label]
        group = value.loc[:, members]
        count = group.notna().sum(axis=1)
        ranked = group.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        result.loc[:, members] = ranked.where(count >= 5)

    return result


def _finite(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return df.astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class SectorCashDisagreementCatchup(BaseFactor):
    """Trade price/fundamental disagreement among sector peers."""

    factor_id = "sector_cash_disagreement_catchup"
    name = "Sector Cash-Disagreement Catch-Up"
    category = "momentum"
    description = (
        "Ranks sector-relative cash and revenue-state improvement among stocks whose "
        "lagged sector-relative momentum disagrees with that fundamental state; long "
        "improving laggards and short deteriorating leaders."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "sector",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "netIncome",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _finite(data["close"])
        volume = _finite(data["volume"])
        market_cap = _finite(data["marketCap"])
        cash_flow = _finite(data["operatingCashFlow"])
        net_income = _finite(data["netIncome"])
        revenue_estimate = _finite(data["revenueEstimate"])
        sector = data["sector"]

        valid_close = close.gt(0.0)
        log_close = np.log(close.where(valid_close))
        lagged_return = log_close.shift(2) - log_close.shift(12)
        return_vol = log_close.diff().rolling(10, min_periods=10).std().shift(2)
        risk_adjusted_momentum = lagged_return / return_vol.clip(lower=0.005)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(valid_close & volume.gt(0.0))
        mean_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(21, min_periods=15).mean()
        liquid = mean_dollar_volume.ge(1_000_000.0)

        prior_cash_flow = cash_flow.shift(63)
        prior_income = net_income.shift(63)
        prior_revenue_estimate = revenue_estimate.shift(63)
        cash_conversion = cash_flow / net_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_conversion = prior_cash_flow / prior_income.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        cash_change = cash_conversion - prior_conversion
        revenue_revision = (
            revenue_estimate - prior_revenue_estimate
        ) / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        eligible = (
            valid_close
            & market_cap.ge(100_000_000.0)
            & liquid
            & risk_adjusted_momentum.notna()
            & cash_change.notna()
            & revenue_revision.notna()
        )

        momentum_rank = _sector_rank(risk_adjusted_momentum.where(eligible), sector)
        cash_rank = _sector_rank(cash_change.where(eligible), sector)
        revenue_rank = _sector_rank(revenue_revision.where(eligible), sector)

        momentum_state = momentum_rank - 0.5
        fundamental_state = ((cash_rank - 0.5) + (revenue_rank - 0.5)) / 2.0
        disagreement = momentum_state * fundamental_state < 0.0

        raw_score = (
            fundamental_state * momentum_state.abs()
        ).where(disagreement & fundamental_state.notna() & momentum_state.notna())

        output = raw_score.rank(axis=1, pct=True).sub(0.5)
        return output.where(raw_score.notna(), 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Sector Cash-Disagreement Catch-Up
programs.trading_idea: Sector-relative intermediate winners are not automatically continuation candidates at a six-bar horizon: the parent evidence suggests that recently successful relative-price narratives can become extrapolated when operating cash evidence fails to validate them. This child trades the interaction rather than either signal alone: it buys sector-relative laggards whose cash conversion and revenue-estimate state are improving, and shorts sector-relative leaders whose cash conversion and revenue-estimate state are deteriorating. The edge comes from identifying a temporary disagreement between slowly updated fundamental evidence and already-extended peer-relative prices, creating a catch-up/repricing channel that pure momentum and cash-state signals cannot isolate.
programs.description: Computes sector-relative lagged, volatility-normalized momentum and a sector-relative cash-conversion plus revenue-estimate state. It activates only when the price trend and fundamental state disagree, ranking fundamentally improving laggards above fundamentally weakening leaders.

programs.code:
"""Peer earnings disclosures can provide economically relevant, directionally signed information about near-term demand and operating conditions for firms with the same industry exposure that have not yet reported. The revised mechanism does not assume that peer news creates a separate valuation, cash-flow, anchoring, or overhead-supply unwind; it predicts that non-reporting peers move in the direction of a coherent, public industry-level earnings-and-revenue surprise. This shortens the causal chain to information propagation and avoids imposing an unsupported universally negative sign."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _industry_event_scores(industry: pd.DataFrame, reporter_quality: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute causal daily industry mean-surprise events and broadcast them.

    A valid event has at least three usable reporters, a two-thirds directional
    sign consensus, and an absolute mean quality-adjusted surprise of 0.15.
    Each row is independent and only contains information available on that bar.
    """
    output = np.full(reporter_quality.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)
    for row_number in range(len(reporter_quality.index)):
        industry_row = industry.iloc[row_number]
        quality_row = reporter_quality.iloc[row_number]
        observations = pd.DataFrame({'industry': industry_row, 'quality': quality_row}).dropna(subset=['industry', 'quality'])
        if observations.empty:
            continue
        observations['positive'] = (observations['quality'] > 0.0).astype(float)
        observations['negative'] = (observations['quality'] < 0.0).astype(float)
        grouped = observations.groupby('industry').agg(count=('quality', 'count'), mean_quality=('quality', 'mean'), positive=('positive', 'sum'), negative=('negative', 'sum'))
        consensus = (grouped['positive'] / grouped['count'] >= 2.0 / 3.0) | (grouped['negative'] / grouped['count'] >= 2.0 / 3.0)
        valid = (grouped['count'] >= 3.0) & consensus & (grouped['mean_quality'].abs() >= 0.15)
        valid_means = grouped.loc[valid, 'mean_quality']
        if not valid_means.empty:
            output[row_number, :] = industry_row.map(valid_means).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=reporter_quality.index, columns=reporter_quality.columns)

@register_factor
class DirectionalPeerFundamentalReadthrough(BaseFactor):
    """Signed industry earnings-surprise propagation to non-reporting peers."""
    factor_id = 'peer_readthrough_model_risk_supply_unwind_j'
    name = 'Directional Peer Fundamental Readthrough'
    category = 'momentum'
    description = 'Ranks non-reporting firms by the signed mean earnings and revenue surprise of a coherent same-industry reporter group, subject to a five-bar own-report blackout.'
    window_length = 6
    inputs = ['close', 'industry', 'epsEstimate', 'revenueEstimate', 'epsSurprise', 'revenueSurprise']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        industry = data['industry'].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        eps_estimate = data['epsEstimate'].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        revenue_estimate = data['revenueEstimate'].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        eps_surprise = data['epsSurprise'].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        revenue_surprise = data['revenueSurprise'].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        prior_eps_surprise = eps_surprise.shift(1)
        prior_revenue_surprise = revenue_surprise.shift(1)
        eps_report = eps_surprise.notna() & (prior_eps_surprise.isna() | eps_surprise.ne(prior_eps_surprise))
        revenue_report = revenue_surprise.notna() & (prior_revenue_surprise.isna() | revenue_surprise.ne(prior_revenue_surprise))
        reporter_flag = eps_report | revenue_report
        usable = np.isfinite(eps_estimate) & np.isfinite(revenue_estimate) & np.isfinite(eps_surprise) & np.isfinite(revenue_surprise) & (eps_estimate.abs() > 0.0) & (revenue_estimate.abs() > 0.0) & reporter_flag
        normalized_eps = (eps_surprise / eps_estimate.abs()).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        normalized_revenue = (revenue_surprise / revenue_estimate.abs()).clip(-0.25, 0.25)
        eps_percentile = normalized_eps.where(usable).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        revenue_percentile = normalized_revenue.where(usable).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        reporter_quality = 0.5 * eps_percentile + 0.5 * revenue_percentile - 0.5
        industry_score = _industry_event_scores(industry, reporter_quality)
        recent_own_reports = reporter_flag.astype(float).rolling(5, min_periods=1).sum().eq(0.0)
        eligible = recent_own_reports & industry_score.notna()
        raw_receiver_score = industry_score.where(eligible)
        ranked = 2.0 * raw_receiver_score.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        return ranked.where(eligible, 0.0).fillna(0.0).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: Peer earnings disclosures can provide economically relevant, directionally signed information about near-term demand and operating conditions for firms with the same industry exposure that have not yet reported. The revised mechanism does not assume that peer news creates a separate valuation, cash-flow, anchoring, or overhead-supply unwind; it predicts that non-reporting peers move in the direction of a coherent, public industry-level earnings-and-revenue surprise. This shortens the causal chain to information propagation and avoids imposing an unsupported universally negative sign.
programs.description: At each daily bar t after the close, define a reporter as a ticker for which either epsSurprise or revenueSurprise newly becomes non-null or changes from its value at t-1; this uses the point-in-time availability timestamps already supplied by the feed. A reporter is usable only when epsEstimate, revenueEstimate, epsSurprise, and revenueSurprise are finite and abs(epsEstimate)>0 and abs(revenueEstimate)>0. For each usable reporter, compute e=(epsSurprise/abs(epsEstimate)).clip(-1,1) and r=(revenueSurprise/abs(revenueEstimate)).clip(-0.25,0.25), then compute q=0.5*rank_pct(e)+0.5*rank_pct(r)-0.5, where each percentile rank is calculated cross-sectionally among that day's usable reporters and mapped to [-0.5,0.5]. The peer universe for a receiver is all usable reporters with the same non-null industry label. An industry event is valid only when at least three usable reporters exist, at least two-thirds have the same sign of q, and abs(mean(q))>=0.15. Its signed readthrough statistic is I=mean(q) across those reporters; direction is explicitly used, unlike the original absolute-informativeness trigger. Eligible receivers are tickers in a valid-event industry that are not reporters on t and had no reporter flag during t-1 through t-5, a fixed five-bar own-report blackout. The receiver score is I, cross-sectionally percentile-ranked among eligible receivers and mapped to [-1,1]; higher scores predict higher six-bar returns. Orders are formed only after bar t has closed and entered at the next tradable bar's open, t+1, so same-day close, volume, and after-close report information is never used for same-day execution. The original EPS-optimism, revenue-growth, cash-realization, valuation, and volume-cost-basis/overhead-inventory gates are intentionally removed: no epsEstimate revision, revenueGrowth, incomeQuality/freeCashFlow proxy, peRatio/earningsYield valuation metric, or price-volume inventory measure enters the score. This implementation fingerprint is therefore a signed, minimum-three-reporter, industry-mean surprise propagation signal with a fixed own-report blackout, rather than an interaction of peer shocks with receiver revisions, cash quality, valuation, or reference-price overhang.

programs.code:
"""Peer earnings catalysts release receiver-specific narrative and inventory pressure.

Mechanism: an industry earnings event creates attention and liquidity for
non-reporting peers.  At a six-bar horizon, its sign is chiefly a catalyst:
expensive EPS-led narratives with deteriorating cash realization and overhead
cost-basis supply unwind, while cash-confirmed supported peers recover from the
same attention shock.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _finite(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Preserve alignment while removing unusable numeric observations."""
    return df.astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _costbasis_skew(high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, close: pd.DataFrame, volume: pd.DataFrame, lookback: int=35) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponentially decayed volume imbalance above today's price."""
    above = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    below = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    decay = np.log(2.0) / 12.0
    current_valid = close.gt(0.0) & close.notna()
    for lag in range(lookback):
        reference = (high.shift(lag) + low.shift(lag) + close.shift(lag)) / 3.0
        traded = volume.shift(lag)
        valid = current_valid & reference.gt(0.0) & traded.gt(0.0) & reference.notna() & traded.notna()
        weighted = traded * np.exp(-decay * lag)
        above = above + weighted.where(valid & reference.gt(close), 0.0)
        below = below + weighted.where(valid & reference.lt(close), 0.0)
    total = above + below
    return ((above - below) / total.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(total.gt(0.0))

def _coherent_peer_catalyst(close: pd.DataFrame, eps_actual: pd.DataFrame, eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Transfer coherent same-day reporter reactions to non-reporting peers.

    A group needs two fresh reporters and agreement between surprise signs and
    realized reporter-return signs.  All information is observed at the current
    bar close, and recipients explicitly exclude firms updating EPS themselves.
    """
    ret = close.pct_change()
    prior_actual = eps_actual.shift(1)
    update = eps_actual.notna() & (prior_actual.isna() | eps_actual.ne(prior_actual))
    fresh = update & eps_surprise.notna() & ret.notna() & industry.notna()
    impulse = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    recipient = pd.DataFrame(False, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    for timestamp in close.index:
        labels = industry.loc[timestamp]
        valid_labels = labels.dropna()
        if valid_labels.empty:
            continue
        row_ret = ret.loc[timestamp]
        row_surprise = eps_surprise.loc[timestamp]
        row_fresh = fresh.loc[timestamp]
        row_update = update.loc[timestamp]
        for label, members_index in valid_labels.groupby(valid_labels).groups.items():
            members = list(members_index)
            reporters = [ticker for ticker in members if bool(row_fresh.loc[ticker])]
            if len(reporters) < 2:
                continue
            reporter_ret = row_ret.loc[reporters].dropna()
            reporter_surprise = row_surprise.loc[reporters].dropna()
            common = reporter_ret.index.intersection(reporter_surprise.index)
            if len(common) < 2:
                continue
            reporter_ret = reporter_ret.loc[common]
            reporter_surprise = reporter_surprise.loc[common]
            mean_ret = reporter_ret.mean()
            if not np.isfinite(mean_ret) or mean_ret == 0.0:
                continue
            direction = float(np.sign(mean_ret))
            return_agreement = (np.sign(reporter_ret) == direction).mean()
            surprise_agreement = (np.sign(reporter_surprise) == direction).mean()
            if return_agreement < 0.67 or surprise_agreement < 0.67:
                continue
            non_reporters = labels.index[(labels == label) & ~row_update]
            if len(non_reporters) > 0:
                impulse.loc[timestamp, non_reporters] = mean_ret
                recipient.loc[timestamp, non_reporters] = True
    return (impulse, recipient)

def _narrative_fragility(close: pd.DataFrame, market_cap: pd.DataFrame, ev_to_sales: pd.DataFrame, eps_estimate: pd.DataFrame, revenue_estimate: pd.DataFrame, net_income: pd.DataFrame, operating_cash_flow: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Cross-sectional EPS optimism minus revenue/cash confirmation quality."""
    price_lag = close.shift(1).where(close.shift(1).gt(0.0))
    eps_lag = eps_estimate.shift(59)
    revenue_lag = revenue_estimate.shift(60)
    income_lag = net_income.shift(66)
    cash_lag = operating_cash_flow.shift(66)
    eligible = market_cap.gt(0.0) & ev_to_sales.gt(0.0) & eps_estimate.notna() & eps_lag.notna() & revenue_estimate.notna() & revenue_lag.notna() & net_income.gt(0.0) & income_lag.gt(0.0) & operating_cash_flow.notna() & cash_lag.notna() & price_lag.notna()
    eps_revision = (eps_estimate - eps_lag) / price_lag
    revenue_revision = (revenue_estimate - revenue_lag) / market_cap.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    cash_change = operating_cash_flow / net_income.replace(0.0, np.nan) - cash_lag / income_lag.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    valuation = np.log(ev_to_sales.where(ev_to_sales.gt(0.0)))

    def centered_rank(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        masked = value.where(eligible).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        return masked.rank(axis=1, pct=True).sub(0.5).mul(2.0)
    fragility = 0.3 * centered_rank(eps_revision) - 0.25 * centered_rank(revenue_revision) - 0.25 * centered_rank(cash_change) + 0.2 * centered_rank(valuation)
    return (fragility.where(eligible), eligible)

@register_factor
class PeerCatalystCashNarrativeInventoryUnwind(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'peer_catalyst_cash_narrative_inventory_unwind_j'
    name = 'Peer Catalyst Narrative-Inventory Unwind'
    category = 'mean_reversion'
    description = 'Uses coherent industry earnings impulses as attention catalysts and ranks the subsequent correction predicted by receiver cash-unconfirmed EPS narratives, expensive valuation, and decayed cost-basis supply imbalance.'
    window_length = 63
    inputs = ['high', 'low', 'close', 'volume', 'industry', 'epsActual', 'epsSurprise', 'marketCap', 'evToSales', 'epsEstimate', 'revenueEstimate', 'netIncome', 'operatingCashFlow']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _finite(data['close'])
        high = _finite(data['high'])
        low = _finite(data['low'])
        volume = _finite(data['volume'])
        eps_actual = _finite(data['epsActual'])
        eps_surprise = _finite(data['epsSurprise'])
        market_cap = _finite(data['marketCap'])
        ev_to_sales = _finite(data['evToSales'])
        eps_estimate = _finite(data['epsEstimate'])
        revenue_estimate = _finite(data['revenueEstimate'])
        net_income = _finite(data['netIncome'])
        operating_cash_flow = _finite(data['operatingCashFlow'])
        impulse, recipient = _coherent_peer_catalyst(close, eps_actual, eps_surprise, data['industry'])
        fragility, fundamental_eligible = _narrative_fragility(close, market_cap, ev_to_sales, eps_estimate, revenue_estimate, net_income, operating_cash_flow)
        inventory = _costbasis_skew(high, low, close, volume)
        receiver_state = 0.65 * fragility + 0.35 * inventory.clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        raw = (-impulse.abs() * receiver_state).where(recipient & fundamental_eligible & inventory.notna())
        score = raw.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return score.where(raw.notna(), 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A coherent industry earnings event attracts attention and liquidity to non-reporting peers, but at a six-bar horizon the event sign is better viewed as a catalyst than as the return direction itself. Peers with expensive, EPS-led but revenue- and cash-unconfirmed narratives and heavy overhead cost-basis supply use either favorable or unfavorable peer news as an opportunity for marginal holders to exit, producing a subsequent unwind; cash-confirmed, cheaper peers with support-side inventory instead tend to rebound after the same attention shock. This resolves Parent B's sign failure: peer-news direction alone is not reliably persistent at six bars, whereas the interaction between transferable attention, receiver narrative fragility, and inventory location identifies whether the event releases trapped supply or exhausts weak selling.
programs.description: The factor detects coherent same-industry EPS-surprise events among reporting firms and assigns their absolute impulse to non-reporting peers. It ranks the expected correction implied by each receiver's cash-unconfirmed EPS narrative, valuation, and decayed above-versus-below-price volume imbalance.

programs.code:
"""The hypothesis is conditional: repeated closes near one side of a stock's daily range are informative only when they persist across several completed sessions, occur with relatively elevated participation, and have not already been converted into a same-direction price move. This distinguishes a gradual, incompletely repriced demand or supply imbalance from a late-stage chase, because occupancy accompanied by substantial prior same-direction repricing is explicitly discounted rather than treated as fresh continuation evidence. The signal is not intended to identify informed trading from a single close; it tests whether persistent, volume-emphasized range positioning contains residual cross-sectional drift after controlling for sector-level effects."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _strict_trailing_dollar_volume_median(
    dollar_volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """20-bar median excluding the current bar, requiring 15 positive bars."""
    positive_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.where(dollar_volume > 0.0)
    return positive_dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()


def _decayed_occupancy_score(
    occupancy: pd.DataFrame,
    weight: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Five-bar causal weighted occupancy score and usable-bar count."""
    numerator = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=occupancy.index, columns=occupancy.columns)
    denominator = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=occupancy.index, columns=occupancy.columns)
    usable_count = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=occupancy.index, columns=occupancy.columns)

    for lag in range(5):
        decay = 0.75 ** lag
        lagged_occupancy = occupancy.shift(lag)
        lagged_weight = weight.shift(lag)
        usable = lagged_occupancy.notna() & lagged_weight.notna()
        numerator = numerator + decay * (lagged_occupancy * lagged_weight).where(usable, 0.0)
        denominator = denominator + decay * lagged_weight.where(usable, 0.0)
        usable_count = usable_count + usable.astype(float)

    score = numerator / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    score = score.where(usable_count >= 4.0)
    return score, usable_count


def _persistent_sign_count(
    occupancy: pd.DataFrame,
    score: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Count trailing occupancy signs agreeing with the final decayed score."""
    agreement_count = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=occupancy.index, columns=occupancy.columns)
    positive_score = score > 0.0
    negative_score = score < 0.0

    for lag in range(5):
        lagged = occupancy.shift(lag)
        agrees = ((positive_score & (lagged > 0.0)) | (negative_score & (lagged < 0.0)))
        agreement_count = agreement_count + agrees.astype(float)

    return agreement_count


def _sector_relative_percentile(
    score: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Sector demean and percentile-rank sectors having at least ten names."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=score.index, columns=score.columns, dtype=float)

    for timestamp in score.index:
        sector_row = sector.loc[timestamp]
        score_row = score.loc[timestamp]
        eligible_row = eligible.loc[timestamp] & sector_row.notna() & score_row.notna()

        if not eligible_row.any():
            continue

        frame = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "sector": sector_row[eligible_row],
                "score": score_row[eligible_row],
            }
        )
        counts = frame.groupby("sector")["score"].transform("count")
        valid = counts >= 10
        if not valid.any():
            continue

        valid_frame = frame.loc[valid].copy()
        residual = valid_frame["score"] - valid_frame.groupby("sector")["score"].transform("mean")
        percentile = residual.groupby(valid_frame["sector"]).rank(pct=True)
        result.loc[timestamp, valid_frame.index] = percentile.to_numpy(dtype=float)

    return result


@register_factor
class SequentialRangeOccupancyEvidenceDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-relative rank of persistent volume-weighted range occupancy."""

    factor_id = "sequential_range_occupancy_evidence_drift"
    name = "Persistent Range-Occupancy Drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-relative percentile rank of a five-bar, volume-emphasized "
        "range-occupancy signal, requiring sign persistence and discounting "
        "occupancy already reflected in same-direction five-bar repricing."
    )
    window_length = 25
    inputs = ["high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where((close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0))
        baseline = _strict_trailing_dollar_volume_median(dollar_volume)

        price_range = high - low
        usable_bar = (
            (price_range > 0.0)
            & (dollar_volume > 0.0)
            & baseline.notna()
            & (baseline > 0.0)
        )
        occupancy = (2.0 * (close - low) / price_range.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).where(usable_bar)
        weight = (dollar_volume / baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.5, upper=2.0).where(usable_bar)

        evidence, _ = _decayed_occupancy_score(occupancy, weight)
        sign_agreement = _persistent_sign_count(occupancy, evidence)
        persistent = sign_agreement >= 3.0

        prior_close = close.shift(5)
        repricing = close / prior_close.where(prior_close > 0.0) - 1.0
        same_direction_move = (evidence * repricing).clip(lower=0.0)
        discount = 1.0 / (1.0 + same_direction_move / 0.03)
        raw_score = (evidence * discount).where(persistent, 0.0)

        eligible = (baseline >= 5_000_000.0) & evidence.notna() & persistent
        return _sector_relative_percentile(raw_score, sector, eligible)
programs.name: Persistent Range-Occupancy Drift
programs.trading_idea: The hypothesis is conditional: repeated closes near one side of a stock's daily range are informative only when they persist across several completed sessions, occur with relatively elevated participation, and have not already been converted into a same-direction price move. This distinguishes a gradual, incompletely repriced demand or supply imbalance from a late-stage chase, because occupancy accompanied by substantial prior same-direction repricing is explicitly discounted rather than treated as fresh continuation evidence. The signal is not intended to identify informed trading from a single close; it tests whether persistent, volume-emphasized range positioning contains residual cross-sectional drift after controlling for sector-level effects.
programs.description: At the close of day t, use only completed OHLCV bars through t. Define dollar volume D_i,s = close_i,s × volume_i,s. For every stock and day s, define range occupancy x_i,s = 2 × (close_i,s − low_i,s) / (high_i,s − low_i,s) − 1 when high_i,s > low_i,s and D_i,s > 0; otherwise x_i,s is missing, so zero-range and zero-volume bars contribute no directional evidence. Define the strictly trailing abnormal-dollar-volume baseline M_i,s as the median of D_i over days s−20 through s−1, requiring at least 15 positive observations; the current bar is excluded from its own baseline. A stock is eligible at t only if M_i,t is at least USD 5,000,000. For each usable bar, set volume weight w_i,s = min(2.0, max(0.5, D_i,s / M_i,s)); this is the fixed winsorization of abnormal participation. Form the five-bar exponentially decayed occupancy score E_i,t = [sum from k=0 to 4 of 0.75^k × w_i,t−k × x_i,t−k] / [sum from k=0 to 4 of 0.75^k × w_i,t−k], requiring at least four usable bars. Require persistence: at least three of the usable x observations must have the same sign as E_i,t; otherwise set the raw score to zero. Define strictly trailing five-bar cumulative repricing r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t−5 − 1, requiring positive closes at both dates. Apply the fixed same-direction repricing discount Q_i,t = 1 / [1 + max(0, E_i,t × r_i,t) / 0.03], and set S_i,t = E_i,t × Q_i,t. Thus, a positive occupancy score is attenuated only when positive prior returns have already repriced it, and analogously for negative occupancy and negative returns; opposite-direction prior returns receive no discount. Within each sector at t, retain sectors with at least 10 eligible stocks, subtract that sector's cross-sectional mean S from each stock's S, and convert the residuals to percentile ranks within sector. The final factor is that sector-relative percentile rank, with high-ranked names expected to outperform and low-ranked names expected to underperform. No centered windows, future observations, or forecast-period returns are used: the forecast return is from t+1 through t+6.

"""This is a reduced-form bad-news-amplification and asymmetric-liquidity hypothesis, not an identification of specific forced sellers. A sharp idiosyncratic downside move with range expansion and a low close, but without commensurately exceptional trading participation, is interpreted as a temporary liquidity vacuum: limited bid depth allows pessimistic orders to produce disproportionate price impact. Conditioning on no contemporaneous reported earnings update and on stronger fundamental quality is intended to reduce exposure to readily observable firm-specific deterioration; the predicted outcome is partial reversal over the next six daily bars."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_peer_mean(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Leave-one-out same-sector means, requiring at least five peers."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)

    for row_num in range(len(values.index)):
        row = values.iloc[row_num]
        labels = sector.iloc[row_num]
        active = valid.iloc[row_num] & row.notna() & labels.notna()
        grouped_values = row.where(active)
        counts = grouped_values.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("count")
        totals = grouped_values.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("sum")
        peer_count = counts - 1.0
        peer_mean = (totals - grouped_values) / peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        result.iloc[row_num] = peer_mean.where(active & (peer_count >= 5.0))

    return result


def _sector_quality_rank(
    roic: pd.DataFrame,
    fcf_yield: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Average-tie percentile quality ranks within sectors of at least five."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=roic.index, columns=roic.columns)

    for row_num in range(len(roic.index)):
        labels = sector.iloc[row_num]
        active = (
            eligible.iloc[row_num]
            & labels.notna()
            & roic.iloc[row_num].notna()
            & fcf_yield.iloc[row_num].notna()
        )
        roic_row = roic.iloc[row_num].where(active)
        fcf_row = fcf_yield.iloc[row_num].where(active)
        counts = roic_row.groupby(labels, sort=False).transform("count")
        roic_rank = roic_row.groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(
            method="average", pct=True
        )
        fcf_rank = fcf_row.groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(
            method="average", pct=True
        )
        quality = 0.5 * (roic_rank + fcf_rank)
        result.iloc[row_num] = quality.where(active & (counts >= 5.0))

    return result


@register_factor
class IdiosyncraticDownsideLiquidityVacuum(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-residual downside liquidity-vacuum reversal signal."""

    factor_id = "sector_residual_downside_liquidity_vacuum"
    name = "Idiosyncratic Downside Liquidity-Vacuum Reversal"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Ranks sector-residual downside price-impact episodes with abnormal "
        "range, weak closes, and muted volume participation, conditioned on "
        "no earnings update and stronger sector-relative fundamentals."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "roic",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sector = data["sector"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        valid_ohlc = (
            (open_ > 0.0)
            & (high > 0.0)
            & (low > 0.0)
            & (close > 0.0)
            & (low <= open_)
            & (low <= close)
            & (open_ <= high)
            & (close <= high)
        )
        valid_price_bar = valid_ohlc & (prior_close > 0.0)
        valid_volume = volume.notna() & (volume >= 0.0)

        bar_range = ((high - low) / prior_close).where(valid_price_bar)
        log_return = np.log(close / prior_close).where(valid_price_bar)

        positive_ranges = bar_range.where(bar_range > 0.0)
        prior_range_count = positive_ranges.rolling(20, min_periods=1).count().shift(1)
        median_range = positive_ranges.rolling(20, min_periods=1).median().shift(1)

        volume_measure = (1.0 + volume).where(valid_price_bar & valid_volume)
        prior_volume_count = volume_measure.rolling(20, min_periods=1).count().shift(1)
        median_volume = volume_measure.rolling(20, min_periods=1).median().shift(1)

        sufficient_history = (
            (prior_range_count >= 15.0)
            & (prior_volume_count >= 15.0)
            & (median_range > 0.0)
            & (median_volume > 0.0)
        )
        score_valid = (
            valid_price_bar
            & valid_volume
            & sufficient_history
            & (bar_range > 0.0)
        )

        range_ratio = (bar_range / median_range).where(score_valid)
        volume_ratio = ((1.0 + volume) / median_volume).where(score_valid)
        z_range = np.log(range_ratio).clip(lower=0.0)
        z_volume = np.log(volume_ratio).clip(lower=0.0)

        close_location = pd.DataFrame(
            0.5, index=close.index, columns=close.columns, dtype=float
        )
        nonzero_span = (high - low) > 0.0
        close_location = close_location.where(
            ~nonzero_span,
            1.0 - (close - low) / (high - low),
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        downside = (-log_return).clip(lower=0.0)
        vacuum_score = (downside * z_range * close_location / (1.0 + z_volume)).where(
            score_valid
        )
        vacuum_score = vacuum_score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        score_valid = score_valid & vacuum_score.notna()

        peer_mean = _sector_peer_mean(vacuum_score, score_valid, sector)
        residual_score = (vacuum_score - peer_mean).where(peer_mean.notna())

        eps_actual = data["epsActual"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        eps_update = eps_actual.notna() & (
            eps_actual.shift(1).isna() | eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1))
        )
        revenue_update = revenue_actual.notna() & (
            revenue_actual.shift(1).isna()
            | revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1))
        )
        no_earnings_update = ~(eps_update | revenue_update)

        roic = data["roic"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        fcf_yield = data["freeCashFlowYield"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        quality_eligible = (
            no_earnings_update & roic.notna() & fcf_yield.notna()
        )
        quality = _sector_quality_rank(roic, fcf_yield, quality_eligible, sector)

        final_eligible = (
            score_valid
            & peer_mean.notna()
            & no_earnings_update
            & quality.notna()
        )
        raw_signal = (residual_score * quality).where(final_eligible)
        return raw_signal.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True).sub(0.5)
programs.name: Idiosyncratic Downside Liquidity-Vacuum Reversal
programs.trading_idea: This is a reduced-form bad-news-amplification and asymmetric-liquidity hypothesis, not an identification of specific forced sellers. A sharp idiosyncratic downside move with range expansion and a low close, but without commensurately exceptional trading participation, is interpreted as a temporary liquidity vacuum: limited bid depth allows pessimistic orders to produce disproportionate price impact. Conditioning on no contemporaneous reported earnings update and on stronger fundamental quality is intended to reduce exposure to readily observable firm-specific deterioration; the predicted outcome is partial reversal over the next six daily bars.
programs.description: Use supplied OHLCV values without independently adjusting for corporate actions; a bar is valid only when open, high, low, close are positive and low <= min(open, close) <= max(open, close) <= high, with positive prior close. Let r_i,t = ln(close_i,t / close_i,t-1), R_i,t = (high_i,t - low_i,t) / close_i,t-1, A_i,t = 1 - (close_i,t - low_i,t) / (high_i,t - low_i,t) when high > low, and A_i,t = 0.5 when high = low. For each stock, calculate trailing medians using only bars t-20 through t-1 and require at least 15 valid observations: MR_i,t = median(R_i,t-20:t-1) over positive ranges and MV_i,t = median(1 + max(volume_i,t-20:t-1, 0)). Zero volume is retained as 1 + volume = 1; missing or negative volume is invalid. Define zR_i,t = max(ln(R_i,t / MR_i,t), 0) when R_i,t and MR_i,t are positive, and zV_i,t = max(ln((1 + max(volume_i,t, 0)) / MV_i,t), 0). The daily liquidity-vacuum score is X_i,t = max(-r_i,t, 0) * zR_i,t * A_i,t / (1 + zV_i,t). Thus, unusually high-volume downside moves are explicitly damped rather than treated as confirmation of persistent selling. For each date and static sector label, compute the equal-weight mean of X among all other valid stocks in the same sector, excluding the focal stock and requiring at least five such peers; set XR_i,t = X_i,t - mean_peer(X_t). Define an earnings-update flag equal to one if either epsActual or revenueActual becomes newly non-missing or changes from t-1 to t, and zero otherwise; names with an update flag of one are excluded for that date. Among remaining names in each sector with at least five observations, compute average-tie percentile ranks of roic and freeCashFlowYield, each scaled to [0,1], and define Q_i,t as their equal-weight average. The raw signal is Y_i,t = XR_i,t * Q_i,t. Emit the same-date cross-sectional average-tie percentile rank of Y among eligible names, minus 0.5; higher values predict higher subsequent returns. All rolling calculations are strictly trailing, and all sector aggregates and ranks use only date-t point-in-time data.

"""Narrative overhang activation: fragile earnings optimism meets loss-triggered supply.

Mechanism: an EPS-revision narrative with weak cash and revenue confirmation is
most vulnerable when decayed traded volume lies above the current price.  That
reference-price overhang supplies a nonlinear selling channel, making the
fundamental-attention correction faster than either signal alone.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _numeric(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Preserve panel alignment while making invalid numeric observations missing."""
    return df.astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _centered_rank(value: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional robust percentile rank, centered at zero."""
    masked = value.where(eligible).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lo = masked.quantile(0.05, axis=1)
    hi = masked.quantile(0.95, axis=1)
    clipped = masked.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)
    return clipped.rank(axis=1, pct=True).sub(0.5)


def _decayed_above_price_overhang(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    lookback: int = 45,
    half_life: float = 15.0,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal fraction of decayed reference-price volume above today's close."""
    above = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    below = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    valid_now = close.notna() & np.isfinite(close) & close.gt(0.0)
    decay = np.log(2.0) / half_life

    for lag in range(lookback):
        ref = (high.shift(lag) + low.shift(lag) + close.shift(lag)) / 3.0
        vol = volume.shift(lag)
        valid = (
            valid_now
            & ref.notna()
            & np.isfinite(ref)
            & ref.gt(0.0)
            & vol.notna()
            & np.isfinite(vol)
            & vol.gt(0.0)
        )
        weighted = vol * np.exp(-decay * lag)
        above = above + weighted.where(valid & ref.gt(close), 0.0)
        below = below + weighted.where(valid & ref.lt(close), 0.0)

    total = above + below
    return ((above - below) / total.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(total.gt(0.0))


@register_factor
class NarrativeCostbasisOverhangActivation(BaseFactor):
    """Short fragile EPS narratives only when loss-triggered supply is available."""

    factor_id = "narrative_costbasis_overhang_activation"
    name = "Narrative Cost-Basis Overhang Activation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks cash-unconfirmed and expensive EPS extrapolation, then activates "
        "that bearish narrative only for stocks with decayed traded-volume "
        "reference prices concentrated above the current close."
    )
    window_length = 108
    inputs = [
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "evToSales",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "netIncome",
        "operatingCashFlow",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = _numeric(data["close"])
        high = _numeric(data["high"])
        low = _numeric(data["low"])
        volume = _numeric(data["volume"])
        market_cap = _numeric(data["marketCap"])
        ev_sales = _numeric(data["evToSales"])
        eps_est = _numeric(data["epsEstimate"])
        revenue_est = _numeric(data["revenueEstimate"])
        income = _numeric(data["netIncome"])
        cash_flow = _numeric(data["operatingCashFlow"])

        close_1 = close.shift(1)
        close_5 = close.shift(5)
        eps_63 = eps_est.shift(63)
        revenue_63 = revenue_est.shift(63)
        income_63 = income.shift(63)
        cash_63 = cash_flow.shift(63)

        eligible = (
            close.gt(5.0)
            & close_1.gt(0.0)
            & close_5.gt(0.0)
            & market_cap.gt(0.0)
            & ev_sales.gt(0.0)
            & eps_est.notna()
            & eps_63.notna()
            & revenue_est.notna()
            & revenue_63.notna()
            & income.gt(0.0)
            & income_63.gt(0.0)
            & cash_flow.notna()
            & cash_63.notna()
        )

        eps_revision = (eps_est - eps_63) / close_1.where(close_1.gt(0.0))
        revenue_revision = (revenue_est - revenue_63) / market_cap
        cash_conversion_change = cash_flow / income - cash_63 / income_63
        recent_reaction = np.log(close / close_5.where(close_5.gt(0.0)))
        valuation = np.log(ev_sales)

        narrative = (
            _centered_rank(eps_revision, eligible)
            - _centered_rank(revenue_revision, eligible)
            - _centered_rank(cash_conversion_change, eligible)
            + _centered_rank(recent_reaction, eligible)
            + _centered_rank(valuation, eligible)
        ) / 5.0

        overhang_raw = _decayed_above_price_overhang(high, low, close, volume)
        overhang = _centered_rank(overhang_raw, eligible)

        activation = narrative.clip(lower=0.0) * overhang.clip(lower=0.0)
        return activation.where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Narrative Cost-Basis Overhang Activation
programs.trading_idea: Cash-unconfirmed EPS optimism is normally corrected gradually because investors overweight the salient earnings-revision narrative relative to weak revenue confirmation and deteriorating cash conversion. The correction becomes faster when recent volume is concentrated above the current price: these optimistic holders are simultaneously sitting on losses, so a modest decline can activate stop-loss and adverse-selection selling. Neither parent alone identifies this state-dependent acceleration: the narrative signal identifies vulnerable beliefs, while the volume-reference skew identifies the mechanical supply channel that converts vulnerability into a six-bar repricing.
programs.description: Computes a cross-sectional cash-unconfirmed EPS-extrapolation score and multiplies its positive tail by a decayed volume-reference-price overhang score. High values identify expensive, recently appreciated EPS-upgrade narratives with weak cash/revenue confirmation whose recent buyers are predominantly above water only at higher prices.

"""Barrier-conditioned failed-reclaim downside continuation.

Mechanism: a heavy downward traversal through prior turnover-weighted price
levels becomes informative when subsequent reclaim attempts fail and each unit
of participation produces progressively larger downside displacement.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _decayed_barrier_activation(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    history: int,
    half_life: float,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal fraction of decayed historical turnover crossed by a down bar.

    Historical typical prices and volume are strictly before the current bar.
    The activation additionally requires unusual current participation and a
    close near the daily low, making it a coarse but robust supply-wall breach.
    """
    c = close.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    h = high.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    l = low.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    v = volume.to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
    n_rows, n_cols = c.shape
    out = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
    typical = (h + l + c) / 3.0

    ages = np.arange(history, 0, -1, dtype=float)
    decay = np.exp(-np.log(2.0) * ages / half_life)[:, None]
    prior_average = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().to_numpy(
        dtype=float, copy=False
    )

    for t in range(history, n_rows):
        previous = c[t - 1]
        current = c[t]
        current_volume = v[t]
        average_volume = prior_average[t]
        hist_price = typical[t - history : t]
        hist_volume = v[t - history : t]

        valid_hist = (
            np.isfinite(hist_price)
            & np.isfinite(hist_volume)
            & (hist_volume >= 0.0)
        )
        weighted_volume = np.where(valid_hist, hist_volume * decay, 0.0)
        total_mass = weighted_volume.sum(axis=0)

        down_move = (
            np.isfinite(current)
            & np.isfinite(previous)
            & (current < previous)
        )
        crossed = (
            valid_hist
            & (hist_price >= current[None, :])
            & (hist_price < previous[None, :])
            & down_move[None, :]
        )
        crossed_mass = np.where(crossed, weighted_volume, 0.0).sum(axis=0)

        bar_range = h[t] - l[t]
        close_lowness = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
        valid_range = np.isfinite(bar_range) & (bar_range > 0.0)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            np.divide(
                h[t] - current,
                bar_range,
                out=close_lowness,
                where=valid_range,
            )
        close_lowness = np.clip(close_lowness, 0.0, 1.0)

        relative_volume = np.zeros(n_cols, dtype=float)
        valid_average = np.isfinite(average_volume) & (average_volume > 0.0)
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            np.divide(
                current_volume,
                average_volume,
                out=relative_volume,
                where=np.isfinite(current_volume) & valid_average,
            )
        relative_volume = np.clip(relative_volume, 0.0, 4.0)

        eligible = (
            down_move
            & valid_average
            & np.isfinite(current_volume)
            & (total_mass > 0.0)
        )
        activation = np.full(n_cols, np.nan, dtype=float)
        activation[eligible] = (
            crossed_mass[eligible] / total_mass[eligible]
            * relative_volume[eligible]
            * close_lowness[eligible]
        )
        out[t] = activation

    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)


@register_factor
class BarrierConditionedReclaimConvexity(BaseFactor):
    """Short barrier breaches whose failed reclaim reveals convex sell impact."""

    factor_id = "barrier_conditioned_reclaim_convexity"
    name = "Barrier-Conditioned Reclaim Convexity"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Negative rank of decayed turnover-barrier activation on a breach bar, "
        "but only after a turnover-anchor reclaim failure with accelerating "
        "participation-adjusted downside impact."
    )
    window_length = 90
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        barrier_now = _decayed_barrier_activation(
            close, high, low, volume, 84, 21.0
        )
        barrier_at_breach = barrier_now.shift(3)

        prior_dollar = (close * volume).shift(1)
        prior_volume = volume.shift(1)
        anchor_at_breach = (
            prior_dollar.rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
            / prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        baseline_at_breach = prior_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        anchor = anchor_at_breach.shift(3)
        baseline = baseline_at_breach.shift(3)

        close_b = close.shift(3)
        close_before_b = close.shift(4)
        valid = (
            close.gt(0.0)
            & close.shift(1).gt(0.0)
            & close.shift(2).gt(0.0)
            & close.shift(3).gt(0.0)
            & close.shift(4).gt(0.0)
            & high.shift(1).gt(0.0)
            & high.shift(2).gt(0.0)
            & anchor.gt(0.0)
            & baseline.gt(0.0)
            & barrier_at_breach.notna()
        )
        failed_reclaim = (
            valid
            & close_b.lt(close_before_b)
            & close_b.le(0.985 * anchor)
            & high.shift(2).lt(anchor)
            & high.shift(1).lt(anchor)
            & high.lt(anchor)
            & close.le(close_b)
        )

        def _impact(now: pd.DataFrame, previous: pd.DataFrame, vol: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
            downside = (-np.log(now / previous)).clip(lower=0.0)
            participation = (vol / baseline).clip(lower=0.25)
            return downside / participation.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        impact_b = _impact(close.shift(3), close.shift(4), volume.shift(3))
        impact_probe_1 = _impact(close.shift(2), close.shift(3), volume.shift(2))
        impact_probe_2 = _impact(close.shift(1), close.shift(2), volume.shift(1))
        impact_now = _impact(close, close.shift(1), volume)
        acceleration = 0.5 * (impact_probe_2 + impact_now) - 0.5 * (
            impact_b + impact_probe_1
        )

        strength = barrier_at_breach.clip(lower=0.0) * acceleration.clip(lower=0.0)
        active = failed_reclaim & acceleration.gt(0.0) & barrier_at_breach.gt(0.0)
        scored = -rank(strength.where(active))
        return scored.where(active, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Barrier-Conditioned Reclaim Convexity
programs.trading_idea: A high-turnover volume-at-price region crossed on a heavy, low-close sell bar identifies a meaningful public reference-price failure, but such breaches alone can also be exhaustion events. The child only shorts these barrier activations when price subsequently fails to reclaim a shorter turnover-weighted anchor and downside impact accelerates across the failed probes. This interaction distinguishes persistent adverse-liquidity cascades, where trapped inventory and declining resilience reinforce each other, from isolated high-volume capitulation that either parent can misclassify alone.
programs.description: Computes a causal decayed volume-at-price barrier-crossing activation on the breach bar, then conditions it on a three-bar failed reclaim of a 20-bar turnover anchor and accelerating participation-adjusted downside impact. The output is the negative cross-sectional rank of the interacted continuation state.

"""Cadenced absorbed pressure converted into a directional escape.

Mechanism: repeated compressed-range, high-participation directional closes can be
an execution schedule whose impact is initially absorbed.  When a regular,
industry-idiosyncratic absorbed state converts into an aligned range and return
escape, the conversion indicates depleted passive liquidity and remaining
metaorder demand, favoring six-bar continuation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_industry_labels(field: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Return one static issuer label per column without using future bar values."""
    labels = pd.Series(index=field.columns, dtype=object)
    for column in field.columns:
        observed = field[column].dropna()
        if not observed.empty:
            labels.loc[column] = observed.iloc[0]
    return labels


def _industry_residual(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectionally remove same-industry common flow where groups are usable."""
    output = values.copy()
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        columns = labels.index[labels == label]
        if len(columns) >= 3:
            group = values.loc[:, columns]
            output.loc[:, columns] = group.sub(group.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    return output


@register_factor
class CadencedAbsorptionConversionEscape(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cadenced_absorption_conversion_escape"
    name = "Cadenced Absorption Conversion Escape"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks aligned range-and-return escapes only after persistent, "
        "industry-idiosyncratic, directionally regular absorbed participation pressure."
    )
    window_length = 24
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        valid = (
            close.gt(0.0)
            & high.gt(low)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & close.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & volume.notna()
        )
        bar_range = (high - low).where(valid)
        prop_range = (bar_range / close.where(close.gt(0.0))).where(valid)

        # References end at t-1, preventing the escape bar from redefining the state.
        volume_ref = volume.where(valid).rolling(16, min_periods=12).median().shift(1)
        range_ref = prop_range.rolling(16, min_periods=12).median().shift(1)
        rel_volume = (volume / volume_ref.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(valid)
        rel_range = (prop_range / range_ref.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(valid)

        close_location = (
            (2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).where(valid).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
        compression = (1.0 - rel_range).clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.85)
        absorbed = (
            close_location
            * rel_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
            * compression
        ).where(valid & volume_ref.gt(0.0) & range_ref.gt(0.0))

        # The state is entirely prior to the candidate conversion/escape bar.
        prior_absorbed = absorbed.shift(1)
        persistent = prior_absorbed.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        cadence_mean = prior_absorbed.rolling(5, min_periods=4).mean()
        cadence_abs = prior_absorbed.abs().rolling(5, min_periods=4).mean()
        cadence = (cadence_mean.abs() / cadence_abs.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(
            lower=0.0, upper=1.0
        )

        labels = _static_industry_labels(data["industry"])
        idio_persistent = _industry_residual(persistent, labels)
        direction = np.sign(idio_persistent)
        state_strength = idio_persistent.abs() * cadence

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        signed_return = (close / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).where(valid)
        return_scale = prop_range.rolling(16, min_periods=12).median().shift(1)
        impact_conversion = (
            direction * signed_return / return_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=4.0)
        range_escape = (rel_range - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        endpoint_alignment = (direction * close_location).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        score = direction * state_strength * impact_conversion * range_escape * endpoint_alignment
        active = (
            valid
            & state_strength.gt(0.0)
            & impact_conversion.gt(0.0)
            & range_escape.gt(0.0)
            & endpoint_alignment.gt(0.0)
        )
        output = 2.0 * rank(score.where(active)) - 1.0
        return output.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Cadenced Absorption Conversion Escape
programs.trading_idea: Persistent high-participation, compressed-range closes are ambiguous alone: they can reflect temporary dealer inventory pressure or informed execution that is being absorbed without immediate displacement. This child requires that absorbed pressure be both directionally regular and idiosyncratic to the industry, then enters only when a same-direction expansion converts the previously muted flow into realized price displacement. The interaction carries edge because cadence identifies a likely continuing metaorder while the conversion escape distinguishes informed liquidity depletion from an isolated, reversible high-volume close.
programs.description: Computes a prior three-bar absorbed-pressure state from close location, relative volume, and range compression; gates it by five-bar directional cadence and industry residualization. It ranks aligned current range-and-return escapes from that state as continuation signals.

programs.code:
"""The signal is a reduced-form temporary-price-pressure reversal measure, not an identification of metaorders or dealer inventory. A stock whose prior close-to-close intraday residual moves repeatedly reverse across the already observed following overnight interval has historically exhibited weak retention of daytime price pressure; a fresh same-direction residual displacement is therefore more likely to mean-revert over the next six trading days. The construction is deliberately restricted to liquid, non-event-like states and uses only transfer outcomes completed before the decision close."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_demean(values: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract same-day sector means using static, point-in-time sector labels."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    if sector.empty:
        return result

    # Sector is static by contract. Reading the first available bar avoids any
    # use of future labels while retaining an aligned column-level grouping.
    labels = sector.iloc[0]
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels == label]
        if len(members) == 0:
            continue
        group_values = values.loc[:, members]
        group_mean = group_values.mean(axis=1)
        result.loc[:, members] = group_values.sub(group_mean, axis=0)
    return result


def _fresh_nonzero_event(event: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag a nonzero surprise only on the bar where its PIT value changes."""
    changed = event.ne(event.shift(1))
    return event.notna() & event.ne(0.0) & changed


@register_factor
class ScheduledImpactTransferFailure(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-relative overnight transfer-failure reversal signal."""

    factor_id = "scheduled_impact_transfer_failure"
    name = "Historical Overnight Transfer Failure"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-relative intraday pressure is faded when its prior ten-day "
        "transfer into the following overnight return was persistently negative, "
        "participation is tapering, and the current bar is liquid and non-event-like."
    )
    window_length = 17
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "marketCap",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]

        valid_prices = (
            open_.gt(0.0)
            & high.gt(0.0)
            & low.gt(0.0)
            & close.gt(0.0)
            & high.ge(low)
        )
        valid_volume = volume.gt(0.0)

        safe_open = open_.where(open_.gt(0.0))
        safe_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        prior_close = safe_close.shift(1)

        intraday = close / safe_open - 1.0
        overnight = open_ / prior_close - 1.0
        intraday = intraday.where(valid_prices)
        overnight = overnight.where(valid_prices & prior_close.gt(0.0))

        x = _sector_demean(intraday, sector)
        overnight_residual = _sector_demean(overnight, sector)

        # At date t, this pairs x(s) with y(s + 1) for s through t - 1.
        # The product indexed t is x(t - 1) times the overnight move ending t.
        completed_transfer = x.shift(1) * overnight_residual
        transfer = completed_transfer.rolling(10, min_periods=7).mean()

        positive_volume = volume.where(valid_volume)
        prior_volume_mean = positive_volume.shift(1).rolling(10, min_periods=7).mean()
        participation = positive_volume / prior_volume_mean.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        recent_participation = participation.shift(1).rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        earlier_participation = participation.shift(4).rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        taper = recent_participation - earlier_participation

        true_range = (high - low) / safe_open
        true_range = true_range.where(valid_prices)
        prior_range_mean = true_range.shift(1).rolling(10, min_periods=7).mean()
        quiet_range = (
            true_range.ge(0.0)
            & prior_range_mean.gt(0.0)
            & true_range.le(1.5 * prior_range_mean)
        )

        fresh_event = (
            _fresh_nonzero_event(eps_surprise)
            | _fresh_nonzero_event(revenue_surprise)
        )
        # PIT fields become NaN after a staleness gap; requiring a current
        # capitalization and at least one available surprise field removes such states.
        fundamental_ok = market_cap.gt(0.0) & (
            eps_surprise.notna() | revenue_surprise.notna()
        )

        eligible = (
            valid_prices
            & valid_volume
            & fundamental_ok
            & ~fresh_event
            & transfer.lt(0.0)
            & x.notna()
            & x.ne(0.0)
            & taper.lt(0.0)
            & participation.ge(0.75)
            & participation.le(1.50)
            & quiet_range
        )

        transfer_strength = (-transfer).where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        taper_strength = (-taper).where(eligible).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        raw_score = (-x * transfer_strength * taper_strength).where(eligible)

        sector_neutral_score = _sector_demean(raw_score, sector)
        return sector_neutral_score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
