from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _labels(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
    values = frame.ffill().iloc[-1].astype(object).to_numpy(copy=True)
    for i, ticker in enumerate(frame.columns):
        if pd.isna(values[i]):
            values[i] = "__single_" + str(ticker)
        else:
            values[i] = str(values[i])
    return values


def _leave_one_out(values: pd.DataFrame, labels: np.ndarray, minimum: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    counts = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    for label in np.unique(labels):
        positions = np.flatnonzero(labels == label)
        if len(positions) <= minimum:
            continue
        group = values.iloc[:, positions]
        observed = group.notna().astype(float)
        total = group.fillna(0.0).sum(axis=1)
        count = observed.sum(axis=1)
        peer_total = group.rsub(total, axis=0)
        peer_count = observed.rsub(count, axis=0)
        peer_mean = peer_total.div(peer_count.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
        result.iloc[:, positions] = peer_mean.where(peer_count >= minimum)
        counts.iloc[:, positions] = peer_count
    return result, counts


def _fresh(value: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    previous = value.shift(1)
    return value.notna() & (previous.isna() | value.ne(previous))


def _relative_revision(estimate: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    prior = estimate.shift(lag)
    row_floor = prior.abs().median(axis=1).mul(0.02)
    denominator = prior.abs().where(prior.abs().ge(row_floor, axis=0), row_floor, axis=0)
    return estimate.sub(prior).div(denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)


@register_factor
class CalmFlowDisclosureCascadeReceiver(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "calm_flow_disclosure_cascade_receiver"
    name = "Calm-Flow Disclosure Cascade Receiver"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Late estimate-revision receivers aligned with a price-confirmed "
        "industry disclosure cascade, conditional on an unpaid relative-price "
        "gap and ordinary local flow and range states."
    )
    window_length = 90
    inputs = [
        "close", "high", "low", "volume", "industry", "epsActual",
        "revenueActual", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise", "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)
        labels = _labels(data["industry"])

        log_return = np.log(close.where(close.gt(0.0)).div(close.shift(1)))
        industry_return, industry_count = _leave_one_out(log_return, labels, 4)
        abnormal_return = log_return - industry_return
        abnormal_scale = abnormal_return.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        abnormal_z = abnormal_return.div(abnormal_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume.ge(0.0)))
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        volume_scale = log_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).std()
        volume_z = log_volume.sub(volume_mean).div(volume_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        eps_fresh = _fresh(data["epsActual"])
        revenue_fresh = _fresh(data["revenueActual"])
        eps_scaled = data["epsSurprise"].div(close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        revenue_scaled = data["revenueSurprise"].div(data["revenueEstimate"].abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        eps_rank = 2.0 * eps_scaled.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        revenue_rank = 2.0 * revenue_scaled.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        event_count = (eps_fresh & eps_rank.notna()).astype(float) + (revenue_fresh & revenue_rank.notna()).astype(float)
        surprise = eps_rank.where(eps_fresh).fillna(0.0).add(revenue_rank.where(revenue_fresh).fillna(0.0))
        surprise = surprise.div(event_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        confirmed = (
            surprise.notna()
            & abnormal_z.notna()
            & volume_z.notna()
            & industry_count.ge(4.0)
            & np.sign(surprise).eq(np.sign(abnormal_z))
            & volume_z.gt(0.25)
        )
        disclosure_mark = (
            surprise.abs().clip(upper=1.0)
            * abnormal_z.abs().clip(upper=3.0)
            * volume_z.sub(0.25).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
            * np.sign(surprise)
        ).where(confirmed)
        intensity_history = abnormal_z.notna().astype(float).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum().ge(15.0)
        own_intensity = disclosure_mark.fillna(0.0).ewm(alpha=0.20, adjust=False).mean().where(intensity_history)
        peer_intensity, peer_count = _leave_one_out(own_intensity, labels, 4)

        eps_revision = _relative_revision(data["epsEstimate"], 21)
        revenue_revision = _relative_revision(data["revenueEstimate"], 21)
        revision_count = eps_revision.notna().astype(float) + revenue_revision.notna().astype(float)
        revision = (0.60 * eps_revision.fillna(0.0) + 0.40 * revenue_revision.fillna(0.0)).div(revision_count.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        receiver_return = close.div(close.shift(3)).sub(1.0)
        peer_receiver_return, _ = _leave_one_out(receiver_return, labels, 4)
        own_gap = receiver_return - peer_receiver_return

        bar_range = high - low
        valid_bar = close.gt(0.0) & high.gt(low) & volume.ge(0.0)
        clv = (2.0 * close.sub(low).div(bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)) - 1.0).where(valid_bar)
        pressure = clv * np.log1p(volume.where(volume.ge(0.0)))
        pressure_mean = pressure.rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean()
        pressure_scale = pressure.rolling(60, min_periods=40).std()
        flow_z = pressure.sub(pressure_mean).div(pressure_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        range_ratio = bar_range.div(close.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(valid_bar)
        range_mean = range_ratio.rolling(60, min_periods=40).mean()
        range_scale = range_ratio.rolling(60, min_periods=40).std()
        range_z = range_ratio.sub(range_mean).div(range_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        calm_local_state = flow_z.abs().le(1.0) & range_z.le(1.0)

        direction = np.sign(revision)
        aligned = revision.mul(peer_intensity).gt(0.0)
        unpaid = direction.mul(own_gap).le(0.0)
        valid = (
            revision.notna()
            & peer_intensity.notna()
            & peer_count.ge(4.0)
            & intensity_history
            & calm_local_state
            & aligned
            & unpaid
        )
        raw = revision * peer_intensity.abs().clip(upper=3.0)
        signal = 2.0 * raw.where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        return signal.where(valid, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: Industry disclosure cascades transmit fundamental information gradually, but a receiver's lagged relative price is only actionable when its own estimate revision agrees with the peer-news direction. The parent-B cascade identifies the informational impulse, while the parent-A close-location, volume, and range state filters out receivers undergoing exceptional local execution pressure, where a price gap is more likely a temporary liquidity dislocation than delayed assimilation. This interaction isolates calm, under-reacting receivers whose remaining move should occur over the fixed six-bar horizon rather than fading mechanically.
programs.description: Constructs a leave-one-out industry intensity from fresh, price- and volume-confirmed earnings disclosures, then trades late estimate-revision receivers aligned with that cascade whose industry-relative return remains unpaid. The signal is admitted only when directional-pressure and intrabar-range proxies are ordinary.

"""Opening-repair direction conditional on phase pressure and liquidity exhaustion.

Mechanism: an aligned price-volume phase loop reveals residual directional
execution after an opening-gap repair.  Accelerating inverse range-volume
elasticity plus repeated repair-side endpoint closes identifies the separate
terminal regime in which that same execution pressure has depleted available
depth and should reverse rather than continue.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _phase_pressure(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal oriented price-volume area; positive values denote sell markout."""
    valid = (
        open_.notna()
        & high.notna()
        & low.notna()
        & close.notna()
        & volume.notna()
        & volume.ge(0.0)
    )
    bar_range = high - low
    displacement = ((close - open_) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-2.0, 2.0)
    displacement = displacement.where(valid)
    displacement = displacement.where(~(valid & bar_range.eq(0.0)), 0.0)

    log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(valid))
    prior_mean = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().shift(1)
    prior_std = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std(ddof=0).shift(1)
    complete = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).count().shift(1).eq(20)
    volume_surprise = ((log_volume - prior_mean) / prior_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
    volume_surprise = volume_surprise.where(valid & complete)

    area_increment = (
        displacement.shift(1) * volume_surprise
        - volume_surprise.shift(1) * displacement
    )
    oriented_area = area_increment.rolling(9, min_periods=9).sum() / 54.0
    endpoints_complete = (
        (displacement.notna() & volume_surprise.notna())
        .rolling(10, min_periods=10)
        .sum()
        .eq(10)
    )
    return (-oriented_area * displacement).where(endpoints_complete)


def _inverse_elasticity_acceleration(
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing acceleration in inverse range-volume elasticity, causally scaled."""
    prior_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    normalized_range = (high - low) / prior_close
    prior_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0)).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
    prior_range = normalized_range.where(normalized_range.gt(0.0)).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()

    volume_ratio = volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    range_ratio = normalized_range / prior_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    log_volume = np.log(volume_ratio.where(volume_ratio.gt(0.0)))
    log_range = np.log(range_ratio.where(range_ratio.gt(0.0)))

    covariance = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).cov(log_range)
    variance = log_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).var()
    inverse_elasticity = -covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return inverse_elasticity - inverse_elasticity.shift(5)


@register_factor
class PhaseElasticityRepairRegimeBifurcation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "phase_elasticity_repair_regime_bifurcation"
    name = "Phase-Elasticity Repair Bifurcation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Uses price-volume phase alignment to identify residual gap-direction "
        "execution, then switches from continuation to reversal when accelerating "
        "inverse range-volume elasticity and repeated repair-side closes imply "
        "terminal liquidity depletion."
    )
    window_length = 45
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        close = data["close"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        previous_close = close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        gap = open_ / previous_close - 1.0
        intraday_return = close / open_.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        repair = (-intraday_return / gap.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        gap_sign = np.sign(gap)

        prior_volume = volume.where(volume.gt(0.0)).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        participation = (volume / prior_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)).rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        phase = _phase_pressure(open_, high, low, close, volume)
        alignment = -gap_sign * phase
        alignment_rank = alignment.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        elasticity_acceleration = _inverse_elasticity_acceleration(high, low, close, volume)
        depletion_rank = elasticity_acceleration.rank(axis=1, pct=True)

        bar_range = high - low
        close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        repair_direction = -gap_sign
        repair_edge = (
            close_location.abs().ge(0.8)
            & np.sign(close_location).eq(repair_direction)
            & np.sign(close_location.shift(1)).eq(repair_direction)
            & np.sign(close_location.shift(2)).eq(repair_direction)
        )
        depleted_terminal = (
            elasticity_acceleration.gt(0.0)
            & depletion_rank.ge(0.60)
            & repair_edge
        )

        direction = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(depleted_terminal.to_numpy(), -gap_sign.to_numpy(), gap_sign.to_numpy()),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )
        regime_conviction = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(
                depleted_terminal.to_numpy(),
                depletion_rank.to_numpy(),
                1.0 - depletion_rank.to_numpy(),
            ),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        )

        raw = direction * gap.abs() * repair * participation * alignment_rank * regime_conviction
        valid = (
            gap.ne(0.0)
            & repair.notna()
            & participation.notna()
            & phase.notna()
            & alignment_rank.notna()
            & depletion_rank.notna()
            & raw.notna()
        )
        percentile = raw.where(valid).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return (2.0 * percentile - 1.0).where(valid).astype(float)
programs.name: Phase-Elasticity Repair Bifurcation
programs.trading_idea: An opening-gap repair has different implications depending on whether the recent price-volume phase loop reflects a still-active directional execution program and whether range-volume elasticity indicates that liquidity is replenishing or being depleted. When phase pressure remains aligned with the original gap but elasticity is not in a depleted, accelerating state, the repair is treated as temporary and the original gap direction should continue; when the same aligned pressure ends at repeated repair-side closes under accelerating inverse elasticity, the program is likely terminal and the signal flips to fade the original gap. Neither parent alone identifies this regime bifurcation: phase alignment identifies directional execution pressure, while elasticity and endpoint persistence identify whether that pressure still has available depth or has exhausted the book.
programs.description: Computes a causal price-volume oriented-area phase state for repaired opening gaps, then conditionally switches between continuation and reversal according to trailing range-volume elasticity acceleration and repeated repair-side endpoint closes. The output is a cross-sectional signed rank of gap magnitude, repair intensity, abnormal participation, phase alignment, and the selected liquidity regime.

"""A large, high-participation excursion away from the prior close followed by a strong intrabar retracement can reflect temporary end-of-day price compression rather than completed absorption. The factor deliberately assigns continuation signs to rejected extremes: an upside probe that closes near the low is positive, while a downside probe that closes near the high is negative. This is a falsifiable alternative to the conventional reversal interpretation, restricted to liquid names and non-dislocation days where next-bar execution is more feasible."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _prior_completed_median(df: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing median excluding the current bar, using only completed bars."""
    return df.shift(1).rolling(window, min_periods=window).median()


@register_factor
class IntrabarExtremeInformationDominance(BaseFactor):
    """Volume-backed rejected intrabar extremes with continuation-oriented signs."""

    factor_id = "intrabar_extreme_information_dominance"
    name = "Volume-Backed Rejected-Extreme Continuation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks volume-backed rejected intrabar extremes among liquid names, "
        "assigning positive signs to upside probes that fade and negative signs "
        "to downside probes that recover, while excluding market discontinuities."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        bar_range = high - low

        valid_bar = (
            open_.notna()
            & high.notna()
            & low.notna()
            & close.notna()
            & volume.notna()
            & (bar_range > 0.0)
            & (prior_close > 0.0)
            & (volume > 0.0)
        )

        clv = (close - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        downside_probe = ((prior_close - low) / prior_close).clip(lower=0.0) * clv
        upside_probe = ((high - prior_close) / prior_close).clip(lower=0.0) * (1.0 - clv)

        prior_volume_median = _prior_completed_median(volume, 20)
        abnormal_volume = (volume / prior_volume_median.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(upper=3.0)
        raw_pressure = abnormal_volume * (upside_probe - downside_probe)

        dollar_volume = close * volume
        prior_dollar_volume_median = _prior_completed_median(dollar_volume, 20)
        liquidity_rank = rank(prior_dollar_volume_median)
        liquid = liquidity_rank >= 0.30

        same_day_return = (close / prior_close) - 1.0
        valid_market_return = close.notna() & (prior_close > 0.0)
        market_return = same_day_return.where(valid_market_return).mean(axis=1)
        normal_market_day = market_return.abs() <= 0.03

        eligible = valid_bar & prior_volume_median.gt(0.0) & liquid
        eligible = eligible & normal_market_day.reindex(close.index).to_numpy()[:, None]

        ranked_pressure = rank(raw_pressure.where(eligible))
        return (2.0 * ranked_pressure - 1.0).where(eligible)
programs.name: Volume-Backed Rejected-Extreme Continuation
programs.trading_idea: A large, high-participation excursion away from the prior close followed by a strong intrabar retracement can reflect temporary end-of-day price compression rather than completed absorption. The factor deliberately assigns continuation signs to rejected extremes: an upside probe that closes near the low is positive, while a downside probe that closes near the high is negative. This is a falsifiable alternative to the conventional reversal interpretation, restricted to liquid names and non-dislocation days where next-bar execution is more feasible.
programs.description: The signal is formed only after each daily bar has closed and is entered no earlier than the next tradable bar/open; forward returns are measured from that feasible next-bar execution point for the fixed 6-bar horizon. Let P be the prior bar close, R = high - low, and CLV = (close - low) / R. Names with R <= 0, P <= 0, missing OHLCV, or nonpositive volume are excluded. Define downside_probe = max((P - low) / P, 0) * CLV and upside_probe = max((high - P) / P, 0) * (1 - CLV), so a downside probe receives high weight only when the close recovers toward the high and an upside probe receives high weight only when the close fades toward the low. Abnormal participation is AV = min(volume / median(volume over the preceding 20 completed bars), 3); the current bar is excluded from that median. Raw signed pressure is AV * (upside_probe - downside_probe): positive values correspond to an upside probe/fade and are intended to predict positive future return, while negative values correspond to a downside probe/recovery and are intended to predict negative future return. Eligibility is limited each day to names in the top 70% of cross-sectional 20-bar median dollar volume, where dollar volume is close * volume and the 20-bar median uses only preceding completed bars. A market-discontinuity filter sets the signal to missing when the absolute equal-weight universe return from prior close to current close exceeds 3%; this return is computed only from valid same-day close/prior-close observations. Among remaining eligible names, rank raw signed pressure cross-sectionally and map percentile ranks to [-1, 1], with missing or filtered names left missing rather than imputed.

programs.code:
"""Reversal after resilient absorption confirms pressure completion.

Mechanism: a prior high-impact directional impulse is likely inventory pressure only
when subsequent high participation is absorbed with little incremental impact and
normal trading capacity returns.  This separates completed dealer inventory transfer
from persistent informed execution, so the original displacement is reversed."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


@register_factor
class ResilientAbsorptionDeficitCompletionReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Reverses an impact shock only after absorbed-flow completion is verified."""

    factor_id = "resilient_absorption_deficit_completion_reversal"
    name = "Resilient Absorption Completion Reversal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Detects a prior directional price-impact innovation and reverses it only "
        "when a current high-participation impact deficit, restored capacity, and "
        "muted non-continuation indicate that residual flow has been absorbed."
    )
    window_length = 140
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)

        valid_price = close.gt(0.0) & close.shift(1).gt(0.0)
        valid_volume = volume.gt(0.0)
        valid = valid_price & valid_volume

        log_return = np.log(close.where(valid_price) / close.shift(1).where(valid_price))
        abs_return = log_return.abs()
        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(valid)

        # Parent-A state: an unusually large price displacement per dollar traded,
        # measured relative to the strictly preceding liquidity-impact history.
        log_impact = np.log((abs_return + 1.0e-6) / (dollar_volume + 1.0))
        prior_impact = log_impact.shift(1)
        impact_mean = prior_impact.rolling(60, min_periods=45).mean()
        impact_std = prior_impact.rolling(60, min_periods=45).std()
        impact_innovation = (log_impact - impact_mean) / impact_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_innovation_q80 = prior_impact.rolling(60, min_periods=45).quantile(0.80)

        bar_range = high - low
        close_location = (
            ((close - low) - (high - close)) / (bar_range + 1.0e-6)
        ).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        prior_return_median = abs_return.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()

        impulse = (
            impact_innovation.shift(1).gt(
                ((prior_innovation_q80 - impact_mean) / impact_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)).shift(1)
            )
            & close_location.shift(1).abs().ge(0.60)
            & abs_return.shift(1).ge(prior_return_median)
        )

        # Parent-B state: fit a causal, stock-specific sublinear volume-impact curve
        # on prior observations only.  A positive residual is quiet price response
        # despite unusually high participation.
        prior_volume_median = volume.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=40).median()
        relative_volume = np.log(volume / prior_volume_median.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        prior_x = relative_volume.shift(1)
        prior_y = abs_return.shift(1)
        mean_x = prior_x.rolling(120, min_periods=80).mean()
        mean_y = prior_y.rolling(120, min_periods=80).mean()
        cov_xy = prior_x.rolling(120, min_periods=80).cov(prior_y)
        var_x = prior_x.rolling(120, min_periods=80).var()
        beta = (cov_xy / var_x.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        predicted_impact = (mean_y + beta * (relative_volume - mean_x)).clip(lower=0.0)
        deficit_ratio = (
            (predicted_impact - abs_return).clip(lower=0.0)
            / (predicted_impact + 1.0e-6)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        participation = relative_volume.clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
        absorption_strength = participation * deficit_ratio

        # Capacity recovery makes the deficit a completion signal rather than an
        # ongoing thin-market continuation.  Same-direction residual flow must be
        # too small to extend the original displacement.
        prior_dollar_median = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).median()
        capacity_recovered = dollar_volume.ge(0.80 * prior_dollar_median)
        muted_return = abs_return.le(0.25 * abs_return.shift(1))
        same_direction = np.sign(log_return).eq(np.sign(log_return.shift(1)))
        aligned_absorption = same_direction & participation.gt(0.0) & deficit_ratio.gt(0.0)

        active = (
            impulse
            & capacity_recovered
            & muted_return
            & aligned_absorption
            & valid
            & absorption_strength.notna()
        )

        magnitude = rank(absorption_strength.fillna(0.0)).fillna(0.0)
        score = -np.sign(log_return.shift(1)) * magnitude
        return score.where(active, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Resilient Absorption Completion Reversal
programs.trading_idea: A high-impact directional impulse identifies a likely inventory-displacing trade, while a subsequent high-participation but low-realized-impact session indicates that remaining same-direction flow is being absorbed without further price concession. The child only reverses the original impulse when trading capacity has recovered and the current volume-impact deficit is aligned with the original direction, distinguishing completed dealer inventory transfer from a still-propagating information-driven move. Parent A alone cannot tell whether recovered capacity is absorbing residual directional flow, while Parent B alone mixes persistent concealed execution with completed, absorbed execution; their interaction isolates the completion state that should mean-revert over the fixed six-bar horizon.
programs.description: The factor detects a prior directional price-impact innovation, then requires current volume recovery, muted non-continuing returns, and a causal trailing volume-impact deficit consistent with same-direction flow being absorbed. It ranks the deficit magnitude and takes the opposite side of the original impulse only in this verified completion regime.

programs.code:
"""Positive EPS-consensus updates can generate short-horizon drift when the revised expectation and recently reported cash evidence jointly improve, but the stock has shown only a muted sector-relative response. The cash and working-capital conditions are intended to exclude upgrades that are more likely to reflect accruals, weak cash realization, or deteriorating operating efficiency. The signal does not assume a particular investor class; it tests whether public estimate and filing information is incorporated with a short delay when their joint implication has not yet been reflected in relative price performance."""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _sector_median_return(daily_return: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the same-day, equal-weighted sector median for each stock.

    Grouping is performed independently at each timestamp, using only returns
    observed on that timestamp.  The output preserves the original panel shape.
    """
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=daily_return.index, columns=daily_return.columns)
    sector_aligned = sector.reindex(index=daily_return.index, columns=daily_return.columns)
    for timestamp in daily_return.index:
        row_return = daily_return.loc[timestamp]
        row_sector = sector_aligned.loc[timestamp]
        valid = row_return.notna() & row_sector.notna()
        if valid.any():
            medians = row_return.loc[valid].groupby(row_sector.loc[valid]).median()
            result.loc[timestamp, valid] = row_sector.loc[valid].map(medians).astype(float)
    return result

def _cross_sectional_rank(values: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Ascending percentile ranks restricted to the eligible universe each day."""
    masked = values.where(eligible)
    return masked.rank(axis=1, pct=True, ascending=True)

@register_factor
class CashValidatedRevisionAssimilationGap(BaseFactor):
    """Cash-validated positive revisions with muted sector-relative reactions."""
    factor_id = 'cash_validated_revision_assimilation_gap_j'
    name = 'Cash-Validated Revision Assimilation Gap'
    category = 'sentiment'
    description = 'Ranks positive, fresh EPS-consensus revisions whose five-day sector-relative price reaction remains muted, retaining only filing updates with improving operating-cash-flow margins and faster cash conversion cycles.'
    window_length = 63
    inputs = ['close', 'sector', 'epsEstimate', 'operatingCashFlow', 'revenue', 'cashConversionCycle']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        eps_estimate = data['epsEstimate'].reindex_like(close)
        operating_cash_flow = data['operatingCashFlow'].reindex_like(close)
        revenue = data['revenue'].reindex_like(close)
        cash_conversion_cycle = data['cashConversionCycle'].reindex_like(close)
        sector = data['sector'].reindex_like(close)
        prior_estimate = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        revision_denominator = prior_estimate.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        revision = (eps_estimate - prior_estimate) / revision_denominator
        estimate_changed = eps_estimate.ne(eps_estimate.shift(1)) & eps_estimate.notna() & eps_estimate.shift(1).notna()
        fresh_revision = estimate_changed.rolling(6, min_periods=1).max().fillna(0.0).astype(bool)
        daily_return = close.pct_change()
        sector_median = _sector_median_return(daily_return, sector)
        relative_reaction = (daily_return - sector_median).rolling(6, min_periods=5).sum()
        base_eligible = revision.notna() & fresh_revision & (revision > 0.0) & relative_reaction.notna() & (relative_reaction >= -0.02) & (relative_reaction <= 0.02)
        revision_rank = _cross_sectional_rank(revision, base_eligible)
        reaction_rank = _cross_sectional_rank(relative_reaction, base_eligible)
        gap = revision_rank - reaction_rank
        pre_quality = (revision_rank * (1.0 - reaction_rank)).where(gap > 0.0, 0.0)
        prior_ocf = operating_cash_flow.shift(58)
        prior_revenue = revenue.shift(62)
        prior_ccc = cash_conversion_cycle.shift(69)
        ocf_margin = operating_cash_flow / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_ocf_margin = prior_ocf / prior_revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        margin_improved = ocf_margin - prior_ocf_margin >= 0.01
        ccc_improved = cash_conversion_cycle - prior_ccc <= -5.0
        filing_updated = operating_cash_flow.notna() & prior_ocf.notna() & revenue.notna() & prior_revenue.notna() & cash_conversion_cycle.notna() & prior_ccc.notna() & operating_cash_flow.ne(prior_ocf) & revenue.ne(prior_revenue) & cash_conversion_cycle.ne(prior_ccc)
        quality_pass = margin_improved & ccc_improved & filing_updated
        signal = pre_quality.where(quality_pass, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: Positive EPS-consensus updates can generate short-horizon drift when the revised expectation and recently reported cash evidence jointly improve, but the stock has shown only a muted sector-relative response. The cash and working-capital conditions are intended to exclude upgrades that are more likely to reflect accruals, weak cash realization, or deteriorating operating efficiency. The signal does not assume a particular investor class; it tests whether public estimate and filing information is incorporated with a short delay when their joint implication has not yet been reflected in relative price performance.
programs.description: Form the signal after the close of day t and trade no earlier than the open of t+1. Let E_t be the point-in-time epsEstimate available by the close of t, and define the 20-trading-day normalized EPS revision as Rev_t = (E_t - E_(t-20)) / max(abs(E_(t-20)), 0.01). A name is revision-fresh only if at least one daily change in epsEstimate occurred during t-4 through t; it is eligible only when Rev_t > 0. Define daily stock return as close/close.shift(1)-1. For each sector and day, compute the equal-weighted median daily return across available member stocks. Define the five-day sector-relative reaction IR_t as the sum from t-4 through t of stock daily return minus that day's sector-median return. Retain only names with -0.02 <= IR_t <= 0.02, explicitly targeting muted rather than strongly negative reactions. Across all eligible finite observations on t, compute ascending percentile ranks RRev_t of Rev_t and RIR_t of IR_t. The revision-versus-price-response gap is Gap_t = RRev_t - RIR_t, and the pre-quality score is RRev_t * (1 - RIR_t); names with Gap_t <= 0 receive zero score. Cash validation uses only point-in-time filing fields available at t: OCFMargin_t = operatingCashFlow_t / revenue_t and OCFMargin_(t-63) = operatingCashFlow_(t-63) / revenue_(t-63); require OCFMargin_t - OCFMargin_(t-63) >= 0.01. Working-capital efficiency is measured by cashConversionCycle; require cashConversionCycle_t - cashConversionCycle_(t-63) <= -5. Both current and 63-day-lagged values must be finite, and the current operatingCashFlow, revenue, and cashConversionCycle values must differ from their t-63 values, ensuring that the comparison incorporates a filing update rather than two copies of the same quarterly step value. The final factor is the pre-quality score for names passing both quality gates and zero otherwise. All inputs, including the t-close reaction, are observed only after t closes; execution is deferred to t+1 open.

"""Cash-credible upgrades entered through a peer-confirmed inventory discount.

Mechanism: positive industry revisions validate that a firm's upgrade belongs to a
shared cash-flow regime, while a non-muted relative response rejects the hidden
idiosyncratic-warning state found in peer-response backlogs.  A subsequent
high-volume-neutral-to-low-close pattern is then interpreted as transient
inventory pressure rather than adverse information.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _clean(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _report_updates(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """True when a point-in-time quarterly value newly becomes available."""
    x = _clean(values)
    previous = x.ffill().shift(1)
    return x.notna() & (previous.isna() | x.ne(previous))


def _prior_report_value(values: pd.DataFrame, updates: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Most recent preceding disclosed observation, available at this bar."""
    return _clean(values).where(updates).ffill().shift(1)


def _loo_industry_mean(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    groups: pd.Series,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Row-wise leave-one-out industry mean, requiring five valid peers."""
    labels = groups.reindex(values.columns)
    has_label = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(labels.notna().to_numpy(), values.shape),
        index=values.index,
        columns=values.columns,
    )
    usable = valid & has_label
    masked = values.where(usable)
    group_sum = masked.T.groupby(labels, sort=False).sum(min_count=1).T
    group_count = masked.notna().astype(float).T.groupby(labels, sort=False).sum().T

    mapped_sum = group_sum.reindex(columns=labels.to_numpy())
    mapped_count = group_count.reindex(columns=labels.to_numpy())
    mapped_sum.columns = values.columns
    mapped_count.columns = values.columns

    peers = mapped_count - usable.astype(float)
    peer_mean = (mapped_sum - values.where(usable)) / peers.where(peers > 0.0)
    eligible = usable & peers.ge(5.0) & peer_mean.notna()
    return peer_mean, eligible


@register_factor
class CashCrediblePeerAssimilationInventoryEntry(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "cash_credible_peer_assimilation_inventory_entry"
    name = "Cash-Credible Peer Assimilation Entry"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks cash-conversion-confirmed EPS and revenue upgrades after a "
        "bearish inventory-style close, but only where positive leave-one-out "
        "industry revisions have received a non-muted relative price response."
    )
    window_length = 252
    inputs = [
        "open",
        "high",
        "low",
        "close",
        "volume",
        "industry",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "revenue",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "cashConversionCycle",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        template = data["close"]
        close = _clean(data["close"])
        open_ = _clean(data["open"])
        high = _clean(data["high"])
        low = _clean(data["low"])
        volume = _clean(data["volume"])
        eps_est = _clean(data["epsEstimate"])
        rev_est = _clean(data["revenueEstimate"])
        revenue = _clean(data["revenue"])
        ocf = _clean(data["operatingCashFlow"])
        ccc = _clean(data["cashConversionCycle"])

        # Estimate-revision channel, standardized cross-sectionally before
        # constructing leave-one-out industry information.
        eps_lag = eps_est.shift(20)
        rev_lag = rev_est.shift(20)
        eps_ok = eps_est.notna() & eps_lag.notna() & eps_lag.ne(0.0)
        rev_ok = rev_est.notna() & rev_lag.notna() & rev_lag.ne(0.0)
        revision_ok = eps_ok & rev_ok
        eps_rev = (eps_est / eps_lag.abs() - 1.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        sales_rev = (rev_est / rev_lag.abs() - 1.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        revision = (0.65 * eps_rev + 0.35 * sales_rev).where(revision_ok)
        revision_rank = revision.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        own_revision = (2.0 * revision_rank - 1.0).where(revision_ok)

        industry = data["industry"].iloc[0].reindex(close.columns)
        peer_revision, peer_ok = _loo_industry_mean(
            own_revision, revision_ok & own_revision.notna(), industry
        )

        # A positive peer regime is useful only if the stock has not displayed
        # the strongly muted relative response associated with hidden bad news.
        lag5 = close.shift(5)
        ret_ok = close.notna() & lag5.notna() & lag5.ne(0.0)
        ret5 = (close / lag5 - 1.0).where(ret_ok)
        peer_ret, peer_ret_ok = _loo_industry_mean(ret5, ret_ok, industry)
        relative_response = (ret5 - peer_ret).where(ret_ok & peer_ret_ok)
        response_rank = relative_response.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        peer_supported = (
            peer_revision.gt(0.0)
            & (peer_revision - own_revision).ge(-0.50)
            & response_rank.ge(0.30)
        )

        # Cash-conversion confirmation is computed only on a newly disclosed
        # quarterly report, avoiding stale step-function fundamentals.
        updates = _report_updates(revenue)
        prior_revenue = _prior_report_value(revenue, updates)
        prior_ocf = _prior_report_value(ocf, updates)
        prior_ccc = _prior_report_value(ccc, updates)
        margin = ocf / revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        prior_margin = prior_ocf / prior_revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        filing_ok = (
            updates
            & revenue.gt(0.0)
            & prior_revenue.gt(0.0)
            & ocf.notna()
            & prior_ocf.notna()
            & ccc.notna()
            & prior_ccc.notna()
        )
        margin_change = (margin - prior_margin).where(filing_ok)
        ccc_change = (ccc - prior_ccc).where(filing_ok)
        cash_quality = (
            0.65 * margin_change.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
            + 0.35 * (-ccc_change).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        ).where(filing_ok)

        # Inventory-discount entry: an unusually active but directionless prior
        # session followed by today's close in the lower part of a normal range.
        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume.gt(0.0)))
        vol_mean = log_volume.shift(2).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        vol_std = log_volume.shift(2).rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
        prior_vol_z = (log_volume.shift(1) - vol_mean) / vol_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        valid_range = high.gt(low) & low.gt(0.0) & close.notna()
        bar_range = high - low
        clv = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / bar_range).where(valid_range)
        prior_clv = clv.shift(1)
        prior_body = np.log(
            (close.shift(1) / open_.shift(1)).where(
                close.shift(1).gt(0.0) & open_.shift(1).gt(0.0)
            )
        ).abs()
        prior_range = np.log(
            (high.shift(1) / low.shift(1)).where(
                high.shift(1).gt(low.shift(1)) & low.shift(1).gt(0.0)
        ))
        current_range = np.log((high / low).where(valid_range))
        normal_range = current_range.le(
            1.75 * current_range.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        )
        inventory_discount = (
            prior_vol_z.ge(1.25)
            & prior_clv.abs().le(0.15)
            & prior_body.le(np.minimum(0.006, 0.30 * prior_range))
            & clv.le(-0.25)
            & normal_range
        )

        active = (
            filing_ok
            & revision_ok
            & own_revision.gt(0.0)
            & cash_quality.ge(0.60)
            & peer_ok
            & peer_ret_ok
            & peer_supported
            & inventory_discount
        )
        raw = (
            own_revision.clip(lower=0.0)
            * cash_quality
            * peer_revision.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
            * (-clv).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
            * prior_vol_z.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        )
        score = raw.where(active & raw.gt(0.0)).rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        return score.where(active, 0.0).fillna(0.0).reindex_like(template)

programs.trading_idea: A cash-backed upgrade is most attractive after a bearish inventory-style close when the firm is participating in, rather than resisting, a positive industry revision regime. Parent B's negative realized sign is interpreted as evidence that a severe peer-information/price-response deficit is a hidden idiosyncratic warning, not an unpriced catch-up opportunity; this child therefore uses that deficit as a veto rather than simply reversing Parent B. The interaction isolates temporary dealer or investor inventory pressure in fundamentally credible firms whose sector information has already been accepted, a distinction neither the standalone cash-quality dip nor the standalone peer-response gap can make.

"""Novel consensus shocks whose delayed price catch-up exhausts inventory.

Mechanism: a discrete industry-unusual consensus revision is informative, but a
high-volume neutral inventory transfer followed by an endpoint close after price
has lagged the revision identifies a terminal catch-up rather than fresh drift.
The factor therefore trades against the signed revision in that completion state.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_percentile(
    values: pd.DataFrame,
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
    minimum: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-industry row-wise percentile, retained only with enough peers."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    if industry.empty:
        return output
    labels = industry.iloc[0].reindex(values.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels):
        if pd.isna(label):
            continue
        members = labels.index[labels == label]
        if len(members) == 0:
            continue
        panel = values.loc[:, members].where(valid.loc[:, members])
        counts = panel.notna().sum(axis=1)
        pct = panel.rank(axis=1, pct=True).where(counts.ge(minimum), 0.0)
        output.loc[:, members] = pct.fillna(0.0)
    return output


def _industry_relative_return(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal cross-sectional industry-relative return with five valid peers."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    if industry.empty:
        return output
    labels = industry.iloc[0].reindex(ret.columns)
    for label in pd.unique(labels):
        if pd.isna(label):
            continue
        members = labels.index[labels == label]
        panel = ret.loc[:, members].where(valid.loc[:, members])
        count = panel.notna().sum(axis=1)
        relative = ret.loc[:, members].sub(panel.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        output.loc[:, members] = relative.where(valid.loc[:, members] & count.ge(5), np.nan)
    return output


@register_factor
class NovelRevisionTerminalInventoryReversal(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "novel_revision_terminal_inventory_reversal"
    name = "Novel Revision Terminal Inventory Reversal"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Opposes a signed, industry-novel EPS consensus break only when a prior "
        "neutral volume transfer and revision-aligned endpoint close indicate "
        "terminal catch-up after industry-relative underassimilation."
    )
    window_length = 63
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "epsEstimate", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        eps = data["epsEstimate"].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
        eps = eps.where(np.isfinite(eps))

        previous = eps.shift(1)
        denominator = previous.abs().clip(lower=0.05)
        revision = (eps - previous) / denominator
        finite = eps.notna()
        complete = finite.astype(float).rolling(22, min_periods=22).sum().eq(22)
        prior_change = eps.sub(previous).abs().div(denominator)
        stable = prior_change.shift(1).rolling(21, min_periods=21).max().le(0.01)

        revision_valid = finite & previous.notna() & np.isfinite(revision)
        novelty = _industry_percentile(revision.abs(), revision_valid, data["industry"], 8)
        novel_break = complete & stable & revision_valid & revision.abs().ge(0.05) & novelty.ge(0.90)

        close_lag = close.shift(5)
        price_valid = close.gt(0.0) & close_lag.gt(0.0)
        return_5d = close.div(close_lag).sub(1.0)
        relative_return = _industry_relative_return(return_5d, price_valid, data["industry"])
        unassimilated = relative_return.mul(revision).lt(0.0)

        width = high.sub(low)
        valid_range = high.gt(low) & low.gt(0.0) & close.notna()
        clv = close.mul(2.0).sub(high).sub(low).div(width).where(valid_range)
        prior_clv = clv.shift(1)
        prior_body = np.log(close.shift(1).div(open_ .shift(1)).where(
            close.shift(1).gt(0.0) & open_.shift(1).gt(0.0)
        )).abs()
        prior_range = np.log(high.shift(1).div(low.shift(1)).where(
            high.shift(1).gt(low.shift(1)) & low.shift(1).gt(0.0)
        ))
        neutral_prior = prior_clv.abs().le(0.20) & prior_body.le(
            0.35 * prior_range.clip(lower=0.003)
        )

        log_volume = np.log1p(volume.where(volume.gt(0.0)))
        prior_volume = log_volume.shift(1)
        volume_mean = log_volume.shift(2).rolling(20, min_periods=12).mean()
        volume_std = log_volume.shift(2).rolling(20, min_periods=12).std()
        volume_z = prior_volume.sub(volume_mean).div(volume_std.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        revision_sign = np.sign(revision)
        endpoint_confirmation = clv.mul(revision_sign).ge(0.35)
        active = (
            novel_break
            & unassimilated
            & neutral_prior
            & volume_z.ge(1.0)
            & endpoint_confirmation
            & valid_range
        )

        raw = (-revision_sign * novelty * volume_z.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)).where(active)
        signal = (rank(raw) * 2.0 - 1.0).where(active, 0.0)
        return signal.fillna(0.0).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns, fill_value=0.0)
programs.name: Novel Revision Terminal Inventory Reversal
programs.trading_idea: A large, industry-unusual EPS-consensus break after a stable estimate plateau identifies a genuine discrete reassessment rather than routine analyst drift. If the stock has remained directionally behind its industry and then prints a high-volume neutral transfer followed by a close at the revision-direction range endpoint, the delayed repricing is more likely the terminal release of accumulated inventory than the beginning of a fresh diffusion leg. Parent A alone cannot distinguish a durable novelty-driven update from its late, crowded price catch-up, while Parent B's inventory state lacks a high-information anchor; their interaction isolates the endpoint state, for which the observed reversal sign is economically consistent with one-shot inventory completion.
programs.description: Detects signed EPS-estimate novelty relative to industry peers after a 21-bar stable-consensus plateau, then requires an unassimilated industry-relative return and a high-volume neutral-session-to-endpoint-close sequence. The factor takes the opposite side of the revision direction because this specific microstructural confirmation is treated as terminal catch-up rather than continuation.

"""Resolution of EPS-only revisions by cash-confirmed delivered revenue news.

Mechanism: an EPS revision that outruns its revenue revision is often discounted as a
possibly temporary margin/accounting improvement.  When the subsequent reported
release supplies aligned revenue and EPS delivery while operating cash conversion and
the cash cycle corroborate it, investors must rapidly resolve that skepticism into a
more durable earnings path; the symmetric negative resolution is bearish.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cs_zscore(values: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robust date-wise standardization, with unavailable observations left at zero."""
    clean = values.where(np.isfinite(values))
    lo = clean.quantile(0.02, axis=1)
    hi = clean.quantile(0.98, axis=1)
    clipped = clean.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)
    mean = clipped.mean(axis=1)
    std = clipped.std(axis=1, ddof=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return clipped.sub(mean, axis=0).div(std, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


def _disclosure_event(eps_surprise: pd.DataFrame, revenue_surprise: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Identify a newly available surprise observation without firing on carried values."""
    eps = eps_surprise.where(np.isfinite(eps_surprise))
    rev = revenue_surprise.where(np.isfinite(revenue_surprise))
    eps_new = eps.notna() & (eps.shift(1).isna() | eps.ne(eps.shift(1)))
    rev_new = rev.notna() & (rev.shift(1).isna() | rev.ne(rev.shift(1)))
    return eps_new | rev_new


@register_factor
class TranslationResolutionDeliveryImpulse(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "translation_resolution_delivery_impulse"
    name = "Translation-Resolution Delivery Impulse"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Trades earnings delivery only when a pre-existing EPS-versus-revenue "
        "revision wedge is resolved in the same direction by cash-confirmed "
        "revenue and EPS surprise news."
    )
    window_length = 70
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "operatingCashFlow",
        "revenue",
        "cashConversionCycle",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_est = data["epsEstimate"]
        rev_est = data["revenueEstimate"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        rev_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        operating_cash_flow = data["operatingCashFlow"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]
        cash_cycle = data["cashConversionCycle"]

        prior_eps_est = eps_est.shift(21)
        prior_rev_est = rev_est.shift(21)
        eps_revision = (eps_est - prior_eps_est).div(prior_eps_est.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        rev_revision = (rev_est - prior_rev_est).div(prior_rev_est.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))

        # Parent-A state: EPS forecasts have moved ahead of sales forecasts.
        translation_wedge = _cs_zscore(eps_revision) - _cs_zscore(rev_revision)

        cash_margin = operating_cash_flow.div(revenue.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        cash_margin_change = cash_margin - cash_margin.shift(63)
        cycle_change = cash_cycle - cash_cycle.shift(63)
        cash_confirmation = 0.55 * _cs_zscore(cash_margin_change) - 0.45 * _cs_zscore(cycle_change)
        resolution_state = 0.60 * translation_wedge + 0.40 * cash_confirmation

        eps_delivery_raw = eps_surprise.div(eps_est.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        rev_delivery_raw = rev_surprise.div(rev_est.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        eps_delivery = _cs_zscore(eps_delivery_raw)
        rev_delivery = _cs_zscore(rev_delivery_raw)
        delivery = 0.40 * eps_delivery + 0.60 * rev_delivery

        # Agreement is an interaction, not a blend: delivery gets amplified only
        # when it resolves the pre-report translation/cash state in its own direction.
        agreement = (delivery * resolution_state).clip(-10.0, 10.0)
        multiplier = 0.35 + 1.15 / (1.0 + np.exp(-agreement))

        one_bar_return = close.div(close.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)) - 1.0
        reaction_penalty = _cs_zscore(one_bar_return)
        event = _disclosure_event(eps_surprise, rev_surprise)

        event_signal = (delivery * multiplier - 0.15 * reaction_penalty).where(event, 0.0)
        carried = event_signal.fillna(0.0).ewm(halflife=2.5, adjust=False).mean()
        output = rank(carried).fillna(0.5)
        return output.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)
programs.name: Translation-Resolution Delivery Impulse
programs.trading_idea: EPS-only estimate upgrades are normally ambiguous: Parent A's negative realized sign suggests the market often interprets them as unsustainable cost, tax, or accounting improvements when revenue expectations have not moved. The child treats that wedge as a latent skepticism state and trades only when a subsequent earnings release delivers a same-signed revenue/EPS surprise together with improving cash conversion and a shortening cash cycle. This interaction captures the rapid repricing when a previously untrusted margin-led forecast is converted into verified top-line-and-cash evidence, an informational resolution neither an estimate wedge nor a delivered surprise identifies alone.
programs.description: On earnings-update dates, the factor combines standardized delivery surprise with an EPS-versus-revenue consensus translation wedge and a cash-conversion confirmation state. It retains the signal briefly with exponential decay and discounts announcements whose directional price reaction has already occurred.

"""Revision drift released after transient downside-pressure extinction.

Mechanism: a positive analyst revision has the strongest near-term continuation
when its price has not yet caught up and an earlier downside shock has cooled in
both range and participation, consistent with exhausted inventory pressure.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _relative_change(values: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal estimate revision scaled by the prior public estimate."""
    prior = values.shift(lag)
    valid = values.notna() & prior.notna() & np.isfinite(values) & np.isfinite(prior)
    denominator = prior.abs().where(prior.abs().gt(1e-8))
    return ((values - prior) / denominator).where(valid).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _industry_residual(values: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same-date industry demeaning with an all-universe fallback."""
    if values.empty:
        return values.astype(float)
    labels = industry.ffill().iloc[-1].reindex(values.columns).astype(object)
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), "__UNKNOWN__")
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns, dtype=float)
    universe = values.median(axis=1)
    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels, sort=False).groups.items():
        group = values.loc[:, members]
        group_median = group.median(axis=1)
        sufficient = group.notna().sum(axis=1).ge(4)
        location = group_median.where(sufficient, universe)
        result.loc[:, members] = group.sub(location, axis=0)
    return result


@register_factor
class RevisionExtinguishedDownsideResponseGap(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "revision_extinguished_downside_response_gap"
    name = "Revision Extinction Response Gap"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Positive consensus revisions with incomplete price assimilation, weighted "
        "by an extinguishing industry-relative downside-liquidity shock."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "epsEstimate", "revenueEstimate", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = data["high"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        low = data["low"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        eps_revision = _relative_change(data["epsEstimate"].astype(float), 20)
        revenue_revision = _relative_change(data["revenueEstimate"].astype(float), 20)
        eps_score = 2.0 * eps_revision.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        revenue_score = 2.0 * revenue_revision.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        available = 0.65 * eps_score.notna().astype(float) + 0.35 * revenue_score.notna().astype(float)
        revision = (0.65 * eps_score.fillna(0.0) + 0.35 * revenue_score.fillna(0.0)).div(
            available.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        positive_revision = revision.clip(lower=0.0)

        valid_close = close.where(close.gt(0.0))
        log_return = np.log(valid_close / valid_close.shift(1))
        downside = log_return.pow(2).where(log_return.lt(0.0), 0.0).where(log_return.notna())
        shock_recent = downside.shift(5).rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        shock_base = downside.shift(10).rolling(40, min_periods=30).mean()
        shock = np.log((shock_recent + 1e-10) / (shock_base + 1e-10))

        valid_range = high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0) & high.ge(low) & valid_close.notna()
        bar_range = ((high - low) / valid_close).where(valid_range)
        recent_range = bar_range.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        prior_range = bar_range.shift(5).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        range_cooling = -np.log((recent_range + 1e-10) / (prior_range + 1e-10))

        valid_volume = volume.where(volume.ge(0.0))
        recent_volume = valid_volume.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        prior_volume = valid_volume.shift(5).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        volume_cooling = -np.log((recent_volume + 1e-10) / (prior_volume + 1e-10))

        shock_residual = _industry_residual(shock, data["industry"])
        cooling_residual = _industry_residual(0.5 * (range_cooling + volume_cooling), data["industry"])
        extinction = rank(shock_residual) * rank(cooling_residual)

        price_response = np.log(valid_close / valid_close.shift(10))
        price_score = 2.0 * price_response.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0
        response_deficit = (positive_revision - price_score).clip(lower=0.0)

        valid = positive_revision.notna() & response_deficit.notna() & extinction.notna()
        signal = positive_revision * response_deficit * (0.25 + 0.75 * extinction)
        return rank(signal.where(valid)).fillna(0.0).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).astype(float)
programs.name: Revision Extinction Response Gap
programs.trading_idea: Positive estimate revisions are most likely to retain a six-bar drift when their price response is still incomplete but a preceding downside-liquidity episode has visibly extinguished. The revision supplies directional fundamental information from Parent A, while Parent B identifies that recent selling was more likely transient inventory pressure because range and participation have cooled after the shock. Neither condition alone is sufficient: an unpriced upgrade can be stale or ignored, while a cooling selloff can simply be a technical bounce; their interaction identifies fundamentally supported demand released from a temporary adverse-selection state.
programs.description: Ranks positive EPS and revenue estimate revisions by their residual price-response deficit, then weights them by an industry-relative downside-semivariance shock whose range and volume have subsequently normalized. The signal is zero when estimates are unavailable or the revision is non-positive.

"""The signal targets short-lived common price-pressure episodes rather than attempting to infer a specific ETF, dealer, or rebalancing counterparty. A sector-wide volume-participation surge followed by an immediately observable collapse in participation, while return commonality remains elevated rather than releasing, is interpreted as exhaustion of urgent basket-like trading demand. The payoff is a narrowly defined cross-sectional reversal within the affected sector: recent residual losers are bought and residual leaders are shorted after the participation shock has already cooled."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_labels(sector: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Return static sector-to-column-position mapping, ignoring unlabeled names."""
    groups: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
    for column_number, column in enumerate(sector.columns):
        observed = sector.iloc[:, column_number].dropna()
        if not observed.empty:
            # Sector is documented as static, so its first observed label is safe.
            label = str(observed.iloc[0])
            groups.setdefault(label, []).append(column_number)
    return {
        label: np.asarray(positions, dtype=int)
        for label, positions in groups.items()
    }


def _observable_basket_flow_signal(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Construct causal, sector-neutral six-bar basket-flow exhaustion sleeves."""
    positive_bar = (close > 0.0) & (volume > 0.0)
    dollar_volume = (close * volume).where(positive_bar)

    # The 18-observation minimum respects the explicit eligible-universe rule
    # while never treating a missing or nonpositive bar as a valid observation.
    valid_count = positive_bar.astype(float).rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
    adv20 = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=18).mean()
    eligible = (valid_count >= 18.0) & (adv20 >= 5_000_000.0)

    # Current dollar participation relative to the trailing, strictly prior
    # twenty bars.  A median based on fewer than 18 valid observations is not
    # considered observable enough to define a participation shock.
    prior_median = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=18).median()
    q = dollar_volume / prior_median.where(prior_median > 0.0)

    safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
    ret = safe_close / safe_close.shift(1) - 1.0
    ret3 = ret.rolling(3, min_periods=3).sum()

    group_positions = _sector_labels(sector)
    n_rows, n_columns = close.shape
    output = np.zeros((n_rows, n_columns), dtype=float)

    eligible_array = eligible.to_numpy(dtype=bool)
    q_array = q.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    ret3_array = ret3.to_numpy(dtype=float)

    previous_b: dict[str, float] = {label: np.nan for label in group_positions}
    previous_c: dict[str, float] = {label: np.nan for label in group_positions}

    # Each item is (sector, final formation-row index, long columns, short columns).
    # A sleeve formed after close t is represented from row t through t+5; a
    # next-open execution engine consequently holds it for exactly six bars.
    active: list[tuple[str, int, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]] = []

    for row in range(n_rows):
        active = [sleeve for sleeve in active if sleeve[1] >= row]
        occupied_sectors = {sleeve[0] for sleeve in active}

        current_b: dict[str, float] = {}
        current_c: dict[str, float] = {}
        current_members: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

        for label, sector_columns in group_positions.items():
            members = sector_columns[eligible_array[row, sector_columns]]
            if members.size < 15:
                continue

            # Invalid q observations are excluded rather than forward-filled.
            q_values = q_array[row, members]
            q_valid = np.isfinite(q_values)
            q_members = members[q_valid]
            if q_members.size < 15:
                continue
            current_b[label] = float(np.mean(q_array[row, q_members] >= 1.5))

            # Pairwise complete 10-bar correlations among eligible members.
            # A pair is valid only when all ten return observations are present;
            # constant-return pairs naturally produce NaN and are excluded.
            correlation_window = ret.iloc[row - 9 : row + 1, members] if row >= 9 else None
            if correlation_window is None or correlation_window.shape[0] != 10:
                continue
            corr = correlation_window.corr(min_periods=10).to_numpy(dtype=float)
            upper = np.triu(np.ones((members.size, members.size), dtype=bool), k=1)
            pair_values = corr[upper]
            valid_pairs = pair_values[np.isfinite(pair_values)]
            possible_pairs = members.size * (members.size - 1) // 2
            required_pairs = int(np.ceil(0.80 * possible_pairs))
            if valid_pairs.size < required_pairs:
                continue

            current_c[label] = float(np.mean(valid_pairs))
            current_members[label] = members

        # The correlation quintile is evaluated only across sectors that have
        # both an eligible membership and sufficiently observed correlations.
        if current_c:
            c_rank = pd.Series(current_c, dtype=float).rank(pct=True)
            high_commonality = {
                label for label, value in c_rank.items() if value >= 0.80
            }
        else:
            high_commonality = set()

        for label in high_commonality:
            if label in occupied_sectors:
                continue
            if label not in current_b or label not in current_members:
                continue

            b_now = current_b[label]
            b_previous = previous_b.get(label, np.nan)
            c_now = current_c[label]
            c_previous = previous_c.get(label, np.nan)
            cooling = (
                np.isfinite(b_previous)
                and b_previous >= 0.60
                and b_now <= 0.35
                and b_now <= b_previous - 0.20
            )
            commonality_persistent = (
                np.isfinite(c_previous) and c_now >= c_previous - 0.01
            )
            if not (cooling and commonality_persistent):
                continue

            members = current_members[label]
            three_bar = ret3_array[row, members]
            valid_return = np.isfinite(three_bar)
            candidates = members[valid_return]
            candidate_returns = three_bar[valid_return]
            if candidates.size < 15:
                continue

            sector_mean = float(np.mean(candidate_returns))
            residual = candidate_returns - sector_mean
            side_size = candidates.size // 5
            if side_size < 3:
                continue

            order = np.argsort(residual, kind="mergesort")
            longs = candidates[order[:side_size]]
            shorts = candidates[order[-side_size:]]
            if longs.size < 3 or shorts.size < 3:
                continue

            active.append((label, row + 5, longs, shorts))
            occupied_sectors.add(label)

        # Update state only after all current-t entry tests have used t-1 state.
        for label in group_positions:
            previous_b[label] = current_b.get(label, np.nan)
            previous_c[label] = current_c.get(label, np.nan)

        # Equal gross allocation across simultaneously active sector sleeves;
        # every sleeve has equal long and short dollar exposure.
        if active:
            sleeve_scale = 1.0 / len(active)
            for _, _, longs, shorts in active:
                output[row, longs] += 0.5 * sleeve_scale / longs.size
                output[row, shorts] -= 0.5 * sleeve_scale / shorts.size

    return pd.DataFrame(output, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)


@register_factor
class CorrelationSqueezeTurnoverCoolingRepair(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-neutral reversal after correlated basket-flow participation cools."""

    factor_id = "correlation_squeeze_turnover_cooling_repair"
    name = "Observable Basket-Flow Exhaustion"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-neutral six-bar reversal sleeves triggered when broad sector "
        "dollar-volume participation abruptly cools after a surge while "
        "10-bar return commonality remains in the cross-sector top quintile."
    )
    window_length = 20
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return _observable_basket_flow_signal(
            data["close"],
            data["volume"],
            data["sector"],
        )

Sector participation B_s,t is the fraction of eligible constituents with q_i,t >= 1.5. A sector enters the exhaustion state at t only when all conditions are known at t: (1) B_s,t-1 >= 0.60, showing broad participation on the preceding bar; (2) B_s,t <= 0.35 and B_s,t <= B_s,t-1 - 0.20, an observable one-bar cooling event; (3) C_s,t is in the cross-sector top quintile among eligible sectors at t; and (4) C_s,t >= C_s,t-1 - 0.01, so correlation has not materially released. Each active sector receives equal gross exposure, with equal long and short dollar exposure, so every sector sleeve is dollar neutral and the aggregate portfolio is sector neutral. Signals are formed after the close t, entered at the next bar's open, and held for exactly 6 daily bars before exit; do not open another sleeve in the same sector while its prior 6-bar sleeve remains active. The factor uses no fundamental quality or valuation overlay, avoiding the prior factor's fundamental-dispersion payoff construction; turnover cooling is the indispensable, independently measured entry condition.
