"""The hypothesis is not that OHLCV identifies latent dealer capacity directly. Instead, a positive-return stock that absorbs unusually high trading activity with less realized range-per-dollar-volume than its own recent norm may be experiencing persistent, gradually executed demand rather than a one-bar information shock. The signal is used only when its industry simultaneously shows broad liquidity stress and heterogeneous price-response outcomes, conditions under which relatively low-displacement names may continue to attract incremental sector flow over the following week."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_candidate_scores(
    impact_residual: pd.DataFrame,
    abnormal_volume: pd.DataFrame,
    base_eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    directional_return: pd.DataFrame,
    industry: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return raw refuge scores only for stocks passing their industry's stress regime."""
    scores = pd.DataFrame(
        np.nan,
        index=impact_residual.index,
        columns=impact_residual.columns,
        dtype=float,
    )

    for row_num, timestamp in enumerate(impact_residual.index):
        eligible = base_eligible.iloc[row_num]
        labels = industry.iloc[row_num]
        active = eligible & labels.notna()

        if int(active.sum()) < 10:
            continue

        tickers = active.index[active]
        group_data = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "industry": labels.loc[tickers].to_numpy(),
                "impact": impact_residual.loc[timestamp, tickers].to_numpy(),
                "volume": abnormal_volume.loc[timestamp, tickers].to_numpy(),
                "direction": directional_return.loc[timestamp, tickers].to_numpy(),
            },
            index=tickers,
        )

        for _, group in group_data.groupby("industry", sort=False):
            if len(group) < 10:
                continue

            industry_impact_stress = group["impact"].median()
            industry_volume_stress = group["volume"].median()
            impact_dispersion = group["impact"].quantile(0.75) - group["impact"].quantile(0.25)

            if not (
                np.isfinite(industry_impact_stress)
                and np.isfinite(industry_volume_stress)
                and np.isfinite(impact_dispersion)
                and industry_impact_stress > 0.0
                and industry_volume_stress > 0.0
                and impact_dispersion > 0.0
            ):
                continue

            candidate = (
                (group["volume"] > 0.0)
                & (group["impact"] < 0.0)
                & (group["direction"] > 0.0)
            )
            if candidate.any():
                candidate_tickers = group.index[candidate]
                scores.loc[timestamp, candidate_tickers] = -group.loc[candidate, "impact"].to_numpy()

    return scores


@register_factor
class SectorLiquidityRefugeRotation(BaseFactor):
    """Long low-displacement demand absorbers during industry-wide liquidity stress."""

    factor_id = "sector_liquidity_refuge_rotation"
    name = "Directional Liquidity-Resilience Continuation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Long-only cross-sectional score for positive-direction stocks absorbing "
        "abnormal activity with below-normal range-per-dollar impact while their "
        "industry exhibits broad impact, volume, and response-dispersion stress."
    )
    window_length = 21
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        finite_inputs = (
            np.isfinite(close)
            & np.isfinite(open_)
            & np.isfinite(high)
            & np.isfinite(low)
            & np.isfinite(volume)
        )
        dollar_volume = close * volume
        valid_bar = (
            finite_inputs
            & (close > 0.0)
            & (volume > 0.0)
            & (high >= low)
            & np.isfinite(dollar_volume)
            & (dollar_volume > 0.0)
        )

        impact = ((high - low) / dollar_volume.where(valid_bar)).where(valid_bar)
        prior_valid_count = (
            valid_bar.astype(float)
            .shift(1)
            .rolling(20, min_periods=18)
            .sum()
        )
        median_impact = impact.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=18).median()
        median_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.where(valid_bar).shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=18).median()

        sufficient_history = prior_valid_count >= 18.0
        valid_baseline = (
            sufficient_history
            & (median_impact > 0.0)
            & (median_dollar_volume > 0.0)
            & np.isfinite(median_impact)
            & np.isfinite(median_dollar_volume)
        )

        impact_residual = impact / median_impact - 1.0
        abnormal_volume = dollar_volume / median_dollar_volume - 1.0
        directional_return = close / open_ - 1.0

        positive_median_dv = median_dollar_volume.where(median_dollar_volume > 0.0)
        liquidity_cutoff = positive_median_dv.quantile(0.30, axis=1)
        liquid_enough = median_dollar_volume.ge(liquidity_cutoff, axis=0)

        base_eligible = (
            valid_bar
            & valid_baseline
            & liquid_enough
            & np.isfinite(impact_residual)
            & np.isfinite(abnormal_volume)
        )

        raw_scores = _industry_candidate_scores(
            impact_residual=impact_residual,
            abnormal_volume=abnormal_volume,
            base_eligible=base_eligible,
            directional_return=directional_return,
            industry=industry,
        )
        ranked_candidates = raw_scores.rank(axis=1, pct=True, ascending=True)
        return ranked_candidates.where(raw_scores.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)

programs.description: Form the signal only after daily bar t is complete, and execute no earlier than the next tradable bar. For each stock, define dollar volume DV_t = close_t * volume_t and daily impact I_t = (high_t - low_t) / DV_t. An observation is valid only when close_t > 0, volume_t > 0, high_t >= low_t, and DV_t > 0; zero-range valid bars have I_t = 0. Using only the preceding 20 completed bars t-20 through t-1, compute each stock's median impact MImpact_t and median dollar volume MDV_t, requiring at least 18 valid observations and MImpact_t > 0 and MDV_t > 0. Define own impact residual RImpact_t = I_t / MImpact_t - 1 and abnormal dollar volume AVol_t = DV_t / MDV_t - 1. Base eligibility additionally requires the stock's MDV_t to be at or above the 30th percentile of positive MDV_t values across the date-t universe. Group eligible stocks by the static industry field; an industry is usable only if it has at least 10 eligible stocks. For each usable industry, compute industry stress as the cross-sectional median of RImpact_t, industry volume stress as the cross-sectional median of AVol_t, and impact dispersion as the cross-sectional 75th percentile of RImpact_t minus its 25th percentile. A stock is a candidate only when: its industry stress is greater than 0, industry volume stress is greater than 0, industry impact dispersion is greater than 0, its own AVol_t is greater than 0, its own RImpact_t is less than 0, and its intraday directional return close_t / open_t - 1 is greater than 0. The raw candidate score is -RImpact_t. The final factor is the ascending cross-sectional percentile rank of raw candidate scores among candidates on date t, with non-candidates assigned 0. This is a long-only score: no short position is taken in high-impact or fragile names, avoiding reliance on an expensive-to-trade short leg. The prediction target is the return over the fixed next 6 daily bars following next-bar execution.

programs.code:
"""This is an observational latent-liquidity-adjustment signal, not an identification of dealer inventory or metaorder identity. A large-volume bar with unusually small contemporaneous close-to-close impact can indicate that traded interest was initially absorbed; a directionally efficient endpoint displacement exactly two completed daily bars later may indicate that this absorption state has changed. The factor trades in the direction of that completed delayed displacement, with all information known at the decision close."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _finite_positive(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the panel mask for finite, strictly positive observations."""
    return np.isfinite(df) & (df > 0.0)


@register_factor
class FixedLagLowImpactVolumeRelease(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks delayed efficient displacement following low-impact volume absorption."""

    factor_id = "lagged_capacity_release_transfer"
    name = "Fixed-Lag Low-Impact Volume Release"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks the signed, range-efficient confirmation-bar displacement after "
        "a fixed two-bar-old high-dollar-volume event with muted contemporaneous "
        "price impact, retaining only sufficiently liquid eligible names."
    )
    window_length = 24
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        open_ = data["open"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        valid_close = _finite_positive(close)
        valid_open = _finite_positive(open_)
        valid_high = _finite_positive(high)
        valid_low = _finite_positive(low)
        valid_volume = _finite_positive(volume)

        safe_close = close.where(valid_close)
        safe_volume = volume.where(valid_volume)
        dollar_volume = (safe_close * safe_volume).where(valid_close & valid_volume)
        valid_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.notna() & np.isfinite(dollar_volume)

        prior_close_valid = valid_close.shift(1).fillna(False)
        log_return = np.log(safe_close / safe_close.shift(1))
        valid_return = (
            valid_close
            & prior_close_valid
            & log_return.notna()
            & np.isfinite(log_return)
        )
        log_return = log_return.where(valid_return)

        # Both reference scales use exactly the twenty observations completed
        # before the bar being evaluated; rolling non-null requirements enforce
        # the stated valid-history condition without imputation.
        adv = dollar_volume.where(valid_dollar_volume).shift(1).rolling(
            20, min_periods=20
        ).mean()
        abs_return_scale = log_return.abs().shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
        abs_return_scale = abs_return_scale.where(abs_return_scale > 0.0)

        abnormal_volume = dollar_volume / adv.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        normalized_impact = log_return.abs() / abs_return_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        impulse_valid = (
            valid_dollar_volume
            & valid_return
            & adv.notna()
            & abs_return_scale.notna()
            & np.isfinite(abnormal_volume)
            & np.isfinite(normalized_impact)
        )
        impulse_gate = (
            impulse_valid
            & abnormal_volume.ge(2.0)
            & normalized_impact.le(1.0)
        ).shift(2).fillna(False)

        bar_range = high - low
        current_ohlcv_valid = valid_open & valid_high & valid_low & valid_close & valid_volume
        confirmation_valid = (
            current_ohlcv_valid
            & valid_return
            & (bar_range > 0.0)
            & np.isfinite(bar_range)
            & abs_return_scale.notna()
        )

        close_location = 2.0 * (close - low) / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        body_efficiency = (close - open_).abs() / bar_range.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        endpoint_alignment = (np.sign(log_return) * close_location).clip(lower=0.0)
        delayed_displacement = (
            np.sign(log_return)
            * (log_return.abs() / abs_return_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan))
            * body_efficiency
            * endpoint_alignment
        )

        # The trailing liquidity screen is calculated only from valid dollar
        # volume observations and is applied within the otherwise eligible set.
        trailing_median_dv = dollar_volume.where(valid_dollar_volume).rolling(
            20, min_periods=20
        ).median()
        eligible = (
            confirmation_valid
            & adv.shift(2).notna()
            & abs_return_scale.shift(2).notna()
            & trailing_median_dv.notna()
            & np.isfinite(delayed_displacement)
        )

        eligible_median_dv = trailing_median_dv.where(eligible)
        liquidity_cutoff = eligible_median_dv.quantile(0.20, axis=1)
        retained = eligible & trailing_median_dv.ge(liquidity_cutoff, axis=0)

        raw_score = (impulse_gate.astype(float) * delayed_displacement).where(retained)
        return rank(raw_score) - 0.5
programs.name: Fixed-Lag Low-Impact Volume Release
programs.trading_idea: This is an observational latent-liquidity-adjustment signal, not an identification of dealer inventory or metaorder identity. A large-volume bar with unusually small contemporaneous close-to-close impact can indicate that traded interest was initially absorbed; a directionally efficient endpoint displacement exactly two completed daily bars later may indicate that this absorption state has changed. The factor trades in the direction of that completed delayed displacement, with all information known at the decision close.
programs.description: For stock i at completed bar t, define dollar volume DV_i,s = close_i,s × volume_i,s and return r_i,s = log(close_i,s / close_i,s-1). Let ADV_i,s = mean(DV_i,s-20,...,DV_i,s-1) and AR_i,s = mean(abs(r_i,s-20),...,abs(r_i,s-1)); both require 20 prior valid observations. The fixed impulse bar is t-2, with abnormal-volume ratio A_i,t-2 = DV_i,t-2 / ADV_i,t-2 and normalized contemporaneous impact I_i,t-2 = abs(r_i,t-2) / AR_i,t-2. The impulse condition is G_i,t = 1 only when A_i,t-2 >= 2.0 and I_i,t-2 <= 1.0; otherwise G_i,t = 0. No lag is selected or optimized: the confirmation lag is always exactly two daily bars. On the confirmation bar t, define close-location CL_i,t = 2 × (close_i,t - low_i,t) / (high_i,t - low_i,t) - 1, intrabar body efficiency B_i,t = abs(close_i,t - open_i,t) / (high_i,t - low_i,t), and endpoint alignment Q_i,t = max(0, sign(r_i,t) × CL_i,t). Define delayed signed displacement D_i,t = sign(r_i,t) × (abs(r_i,t) / AR_i,t) × B_i,t × Q_i,t. The raw factor is S_i,t = G_i,t × D_i,t. Thus a positive score requires a high-volume, low-impact event two bars earlier and a positive, range-efficient close near the high at t; a negative score analogously requires a close near the low. A name is eligible only if all required OHLCV observations are positive and finite, high > low on t, and it has 20 valid prior bars for ADV and AR; zero-range, missing, zero-volume, or otherwise invalid observations receive NaN rather than being imputed. To avoid the least tradable names, retain only eligible names whose trailing-20-bar median dollar volume is at or above the cross-sectional 20th percentile among eligible names at t. Cross-sectionally rank S_i,t among retained names at t, map percentile ranks to [-0.5, 0.5], and use that signed rank as the portfolio signal. The score is timestamped after the close of t and may only be traded from the next bar onward; its target is return over the subsequent six daily bars, not any return through t.

programs.code:
"""The signal does not assume that a retained daily-bar shock proves informed trading. Instead, it tests a narrower reduced-form condition: an idiosyncratic high-impact move occurring during temporarily impaired trading capacity, followed by restoration of ordinary capacity without a meaningful price repair or intrabar rejection. The proposed continuation mechanism is that the shock has not been fully absorbed by the restored trading environment; the factor is explicitly a conditional price-pressure persistence screen rather than an attribution of the move to informed metaorders."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_robust_zscore(
    impact: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compute same-date sector median/MAD standardized impacts causally."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=impact.index, columns=impact.columns)

    # Sector is static by construction.  Each group calculation remains strictly
    # cross-sectional at each timestamp and never pools impact observations over time.
    labels = pd.unique(sector.to_numpy().ravel())
    for label in labels:
        if pd.isna(label):
            continue
        member_mask = sector.eq(label)
        group_impact = impact.where(member_mask)
        group_median = group_impact.median(axis=1)
        group_mad = group_impact.sub(group_median, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1)
        group_z = group_impact.sub(group_median, axis=0).div(
            1.4826 * group_mad + 0.0001,
            axis=0,
        )
        result = result.where(~member_mask, group_z)

    return result


@register_factor
class IdiosyncraticImpactRecoveryAcceptanceDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Ranks accepted idiosyncratic impact shocks after capacity restoration."""

    factor_id = "idiosyncratic_impact_recovery_acceptance_drift"
    name = "Restored-Capacity Accepted Impact"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Conditional continuation screen for sector-idiosyncratic price impacts "
        "that occurred under subnormal dollar-volume capacity, then retained "
        "their directional endpoint and intrabar acceptance after normal "
        "capacity returned."
    )
    window_length = 24
    inputs = ["close", "high", "low", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).where((close * volume) > 0.0)
        normal_dollar_volume = dollar_volume.rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        capacity_ratio = dollar_volume.div(normal_dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        daily_return = close.div(close.shift(1)).sub(1.0)
        volatility = daily_return.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std()
        standardized_return = daily_return.div(volatility.clip(lower=0.0001))
        impact = standardized_return.div(
            np.sqrt(capacity_ratio.clip(lower=0.10))
        )

        impact_z = _sector_robust_zscore(impact, sector)

        # At date t the shock date is s=t-3.  These shifts ensure the full
        # three-bar confirmation interval has completed before scoring.
        shock_z = impact_z.shift(3)
        shock_capacity = capacity_ratio.shift(3)
        shock_normal_dv = normal_dollar_volume.shift(3)
        shock_return = daily_return.shift(3)
        shock_close = close.shift(3)
        pre_shock_close = close.shift(4)

        confirmation_capacity = capacity_ratio.rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        restoration = (
            1.0
            - np.log(confirmation_capacity).abs().div(np.log(1.25))
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        direction = np.sign(shock_z)
        endpoint_move = close.div(pre_shock_close).sub(1.0)
        retention_ratio = direction * endpoint_move.div(
            shock_return.abs().clip(lower=0.0001)
        )
        endpoint_retention = (
            retention_ratio.sub(0.50).div(0.50)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        confirmation_low = low.rolling(3, min_periods=3).min()
        confirmation_high = high.rolling(3, min_periods=3).max()
        positive_adverse = (
            1.0 - confirmation_low.div(shock_close.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        ).clip(lower=0.0)
        negative_adverse = (
            confirmation_high.div(pre_shock_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)) - 1.0
        ).clip(lower=0.0)
        adverse_retracement = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(direction > 0.0, positive_adverse, negative_adverse),
            index=close.index,
            columns=close.columns,
        ).div(shock_return.abs().clip(lower=0.0001))
        path_acceptance = (
            1.0 - adverse_retracement.div(0.50)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        bar_range = (high - low).clip(lower=0.0001)
        close_location = (2.0 * close - high - low).div(bar_range)
        directional_location = (
            close_location.mul(direction).rolling(3, min_periods=3).mean()
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

        dv_floor = shock_normal_dv.quantile(0.30, axis=1)
        eligible = (
            shock_z.abs().ge(1.5)
            & shock_capacity.le(0.75)
            & shock_normal_dv.gt(dv_floor, axis=0)
            & shock_normal_dv.notna()
            & shock_capacity.notna()
        )

        raw_signal = (
            direction
            * shock_z.abs().sub(1.5).clip(lower=0.0)
            * restoration
            * endpoint_retention
            * path_acceptance
            * directional_location
        )
        raw_signal = raw_signal.where(eligible)

        ranked = raw_signal.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        centered_rank = (2.0 * ranked - 1.0).where(eligible, 0.0)
        return centered_rank.fillna(0.0).astype(float)

programs.trading_idea: The signal does not assume that a retained daily-bar shock proves informed trading. Instead, it tests a narrower reduced-form condition: an idiosyncratic high-impact move occurring during temporarily impaired trading capacity, followed by restoration of ordinary capacity without a meaningful price repair or intrabar rejection. The proposed continuation mechanism is that the shock has not been fully absorbed by the restored trading environment; the factor is explicitly a conditional price-pressure persistence screen rather than an attribution of the move to informed metaorders.
programs.description: At the close of date t, define the shock date s=t-3, so all three confirmation bars s+1, s+2, and s+3=t are completed before the score exists. Let r_i,u=close_i,u/close_i,u-1-1, sigma_i,s be the rolling 20-bar standard deviation of r through s, and DV_i,u=close_i,u*volume_i,u. Let a_i,u=DV_i,u/median(DV_i,s-19:s), requiring 20 valid prior bars. Define signed impact I_i,s=(r_i,s/max(sigma_i,s,0.0001))/sqrt(max(a_i,s,0.10)). Sector-relative idiosyncratic impact is J_i,s=(I_i,s-median_sector(I_s))/(1.4826*MAD_sector(I_s)+0.0001), where the sector median and MAD are calculated cross-sectionally on date s. A name is eligible only when abs(J_i,s)>=1.5, a_i,s<=0.75, and its 20-bar median dollar volume is above the cross-sectional 30th percentile, limiting the signal to names with a minimum practical trading-capacity floor. Capacity restoration is H_i=clip(1-abs(log(mean(a_i,s+1:s+3)))/log(1.25),0,1), which is one only when average confirmation-window dollar volume equals its own trailing normal level and reaches zero outside approximately 0.8x to 1.25x normal capacity. Directional endpoint retention is R_i=sign(J_i,s)*(close_i,t/close_i,s-1)/max(abs(r_i,s),0.0001), with retention score E_i=clip((R_i-0.50)/0.50,0,1). Pathwise adverse retracement is A_i=max(0,1-min(low_i,s+1:s+3)/close_i,s) / max(abs(r_i,s),0.0001) for positive J, and max(0,max(high_i,s+1:s+3)/close_i,s-1) / max(abs(r_i,s),0.0001) for negative J; its penalty-adjusted score is P_i=clip(1-A_i/0.50,0,1). Close-location acceptance is L_i=clip(mean(sign(J_i,s)*(2*close_i,u-high_i,u-low_i,u)/max(high_i,u-low_i,u,0.0001), u=s+1:s+3),0,1). The raw signal is X_i,t=sign(J_i,s)*max(abs(J_i,s)-1.5,0)*H_i*E_i*P_i*L_i, and the implemented factor is the cross-sectional rank of X among eligible names, centered to be negative for short candidates and positive for long candidates. The differentiating construction is the required contrast between initially subnormal shock-day capacity and subsequently normalized capacity, jointly with pathwise endpoint acceptance; it excludes both persistent abnormal-participation continuation and simple one-bar return-retention cases. The score is formed only after bar t closes, and its six-bar forecast begins on the next tradable bar, t+1.

programs.code:
"""The revised mechanism is not that raw EPS-to-revenue surprise elasticity is itself a durable operating-leverage estimate. Instead, it isolates the residual between delivered EPS news and the EPS implication of pre-release consensus co-revisions, then trades it only when contemporaneous operating-margin, cash-conversion, and working-capital evidence support the residual's sign. The expected continuation arises when analysts must revise profitability and cash-realization assumptions after a report, while the completed report-day return indicates that the directional implication was not already fully absorbed."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _finite_mask(*frames: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the aligned mask on which every supplied numeric frame is finite."""
    mask = pd.DataFrame(True, index=frames[0].index, columns=frames[0].columns)
    for frame in frames:
        mask = mask & frame.notna() & np.isfinite(frame)
    return mask


def _carry_post_close_events(event_score: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Carry a report-day score from the next bar through the sixth bar."""
    carried = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=event_score.index, columns=event_score.columns)
    for lag in range(1, 7):
        decay = 1.0 - (lag - 1) / 6.0
        carried = carried + event_score.shift(lag).fillna(0.0) * decay
    return carried


@register_factor
class DeliveredElasticityCalibrationResponseGap(BaseFactor):
    """Post-close residual earnings-news drift confirmed by cash and margins."""

    factor_id = "delivered_elasticity_calibration_response_gap"
    name = "Cash-Confirmed Delivery Residual Drift"
    category = "sentiment"
    description = (
        "Ranks post-close EPS delivery residuals versus pre-report consensus "
        "elasticity only when margin, cash-conversion, and working-capital "
        "evidence confirm the residual and report-day absorption is incomplete."
    )
    window_length = 84
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
        "operatingMargin",
        "incomeQuality",
        "workingCapital",
        "revenue",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        eps_actual = data["epsActual"]
        revenue_actual = data["revenueActual"]
        eps_surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        revenue_surprise = data["revenueSurprise"]
        eps_estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        revenue_estimate = data["revenueEstimate"]
        operating_margin = data["operatingMargin"]
        income_quality = data["incomeQuality"]
        working_capital = data["workingCapital"]
        revenue = data["revenue"]

        eps_est_t1 = eps_estimate.shift(1)
        eps_est_t21 = eps_estimate.shift(21)
        revenue_est_t1 = revenue_estimate.shift(1)
        revenue_est_t21 = revenue_estimate.shift(21)

        eps_revision = (eps_est_t1 - eps_est_t21) / eps_est_t21.abs().clip(lower=0.01)
        revenue_revision = (revenue_est_t1 - revenue_est_t21) / revenue_est_t21.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        beta = (eps_revision / revenue_revision.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        standardized_eps = (eps_surprise / eps_est_t1.abs().clip(lower=0.01)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        standardized_revenue = (
            revenue_surprise / revenue_est_t1.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        ).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        delivery_residual = (standardized_eps - beta * standardized_revenue).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        operating_margin_lag = operating_margin.shift(63)
        income_quality_lag = income_quality.shift(63)
        working_capital_lag = working_capital.shift(63)
        revenue_lag = revenue.shift(63)

        delta_margin = operating_margin - operating_margin_lag
        delta_income_quality = income_quality - income_quality_lag
        normalized_wc = working_capital / revenue.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        normalized_wc_lag = working_capital_lag / revenue_lag.abs().clip(lower=1000000.0)
        delta_working_capital = normalized_wc - normalized_wc_lag

        confirmation = (
            (delta_margin / 0.02).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
            + 0.5 * delta_income_quality.clip(-1.0, 1.0)
            - 0.5 * (delta_working_capital / 0.05).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        )

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        report_return = close / prior_close.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0
        absorption = 1.0 - (
            (np.sign(delivery_residual) * report_return)
            .clip(lower=0.0)
            .clip(upper=0.10)
            / 0.10
        )

        eps_changed = eps_actual.notna() & (
            eps_actual.shift(1).isna() | eps_actual.ne(eps_actual.shift(1))
        )
        revenue_changed = revenue_actual.notna() & (
            revenue_actual.shift(1).isna() | revenue_actual.ne(revenue_actual.shift(1))
        )
        fresh_report = eps_changed | revenue_changed

        revision_valid = _finite_mask(
            eps_est_t1,
            eps_est_t21,
            revenue_est_t1,
            revenue_est_t21,
            eps_revision,
            revenue_revision,
            beta,
        ) & revenue_revision.abs().ge(0.01)
        surprise_valid = _finite_mask(
            eps_surprise,
            revenue_surprise,
            standardized_eps,
            standardized_revenue,
            delivery_residual,
        ) & standardized_revenue.abs().ge(0.01)
        confirmation_valid = _finite_mask(
            operating_margin,
            operating_margin_lag,
            income_quality,
            income_quality_lag,
            working_capital,
            working_capital_lag,
            revenue,
            revenue_lag,
            delta_margin,
            delta_income_quality,
            delta_working_capital,
            confirmation,
        )
        absorption_valid = _finite_mask(close, prior_close, report_return, absorption)
        report_fields_valid = _finite_mask(
            eps_actual,
            revenue_actual,
            eps_surprise,
            revenue_surprise,
        )

        eligible = (
            fresh_report
            & report_fields_valid
            & revision_valid
            & surprise_valid
            & confirmation_valid
            & absorption_valid
            & confirmation.abs().ge(0.25)
            & np.sign(delivery_residual).eq(np.sign(confirmation))
            & np.sign(delivery_residual).eq(np.sign(delta_margin))
        )

        event_score = (
            delivery_residual * confirmation.abs() * absorption
        ).where(eligible, 0.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        carried_score = _carry_post_close_events(event_score)

        ranked = rank(carried_score)
        return ranked.where(carried_score.ne(0.0), 0.0).fillna(0.0)

The expected continuation arises when analysts must revise profitability and cash-realization assumptions after a report, while the completed report-day return indicates that the directional implication was not already fully absorbed.
programs.description: Let t be a fresh report date: epsActual[t] and revenueActual[t] must be non-null, epsSurprise[t] and revenueSurprise[t] must be non-null, and at least one of epsActual[t] or revenueActual[t] must differ from its value at t-1. All report-date quantities are used only after close[t] is known. Pre-report consensus revisions use only the 20-bar window ending at t-1: rE = (epsEstimate[t-1]-epsEstimate[t-21]) / max(abs(epsEstimate[t-21]), 0.01), and rR = (revenueEstimate[t-1]-revenueEstimate[t-21]) / max(abs(revenueEstimate[t-21]), 1000000). The pre-report calibration coefficient is beta = winsorize(rE / rR, -5, 5), but the event is discarded unless abs(rR) >= 0.01. Delivered standardized surprises are sE = winsorize(epsSurprise[t] / max(abs(epsEstimate[t-1]), 0.01), -3, 3) and sR = winsorize(revenueSurprise[t] / max(abs(revenueEstimate[t-1]), 1000000), -3, 3); discard the event unless abs(sR) >= 0.01. The economically scaled delivery residual is D = winsorize(sE - beta*sR, -3, 3), rather than an unbounded ratio of EPS and revenue surprises. Cash-and-operations confirmation is measured over the prior approximately quarterly 63-bar lookback: dOM = operatingMargin[t]-operatingMargin[t-63], dIQ = incomeQuality[t]-incomeQuality[t-63], and dWC = workingCapital[t]/max(abs(revenue[t]), 1000000) - workingCapital[t-63]/max(abs(revenue[t-63]), 1000000). Define Q = clip(dOM/0.02, -1, 1) + 0.5*clip(dIQ, -1, 1) - 0.5*clip(dWC/0.05, -1, 1). Retain an event only when sign(D)=sign(Q), abs(Q)>=0.25, and sign(D)=sign(dOM); otherwise assign zero. This requires positive residuals to coincide with improving operating margin, improving cash conversion, and/or reduced working-capital cash consumption, while negative residuals require deterioration on those dimensions. Any missing input to the event, revision, confirmation, or absorption calculation produces no trade. Report-day absorption is based on the completed close-to-close return R0 = close[t]/close[t-1]-1: A = 1 - clip(max(0, sign(D)*R0)/0.10, 0, 1). The post-close event score is S_t = D*abs(Q)*A. It is first executable at the next bar, t+1, never on report date t. At each bar u from t+1 through t+6, carry S_t with linear decay S_t*(1-(u-t-1)/6); exit after the sixth executable bar. If multiple eligible report events remain active, sum their decayed scores before cross-sectionally ranking the resulting signal.

"""Sector-shock differentiation confirmed by revisions and absorbed flow.

A sector-wide shock initially transmits through correlated baskets.  Firm-specific
late-quarter estimate changes should separate resilient firms from fragile peers,
but only when aligned volume is being absorbed rather than immediately exhausting
in a high-volatility price-discovery episode.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _winsorize(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    clean = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    lo = clean.quantile(0.01, axis=1)
    hi = clean.quantile(0.99, axis=1)
    return clean.clip(lower=lo, upper=hi, axis=0)


def _update_flag(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    prior = frame.ffill().shift(1)
    valid = frame.notna() & ~frame.isin([np.inf, -np.inf])
    return valid & prior.notna() & frame.ne(prior)


def _report_age(reset: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    rows, cols = reset.shape
    positions = pd.DataFrame(
        np.broadcast_to(np.arange(rows, dtype=float)[:, None], (rows, cols)),
        index=reset.index,
        columns=reset.columns,
    )
    return positions - positions.where(reset).ffill()


def _revision(frame: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame, lag: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    prior = frame.shift(lag)
    valid = eligible & frame.notna() & prior.notna() & prior.ne(0.0)
    scale = prior.abs()
    floor = 0.01 * scale.median(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    denom = scale.where(scale.ge(floor, axis=0), floor, axis=0)
    return ((frame - prior) / denom.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(valid).replace(
        [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
    )


def _sector_resilience_response(
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
    gross_margin: pd.DataFrame,
    sga_to_revenue: pd.DataFrame,
    current_ratio: pd.DataFrame,
    debt_to_equity: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal sector-shock differentiation score using date-t public fields."""
    ret5 = close / close.shift(5) - 1.0
    ret5 = ret5.where(close.gt(0.0) & close.shift(5).gt(0.0))
    gm = _winsorize(gross_margin)
    sga = _winsorize(sga_to_revenue)
    liquidity = _winsorize(current_ratio)
    leverage = _winsorize(debt_to_equity)
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns, dtype=float)

    for i in range(len(close.index)):
        labels = sector.iloc[i]
        stock_ret = ret5.iloc[i]
        eligible = (
            labels.notna()
            & stock_ret.notna()
            & gm.iloc[i].notna()
            & sga.iloc[i].notna()
            & liquidity.iloc[i].notna()
            & leverage.iloc[i].notna()
        )
        score = pd.Series(np.nan, index=close.columns, dtype=float)
        if not eligible.any():
            out.iloc[i] = score
            continue

        group_ret = stock_ret.loc[eligible].groupby(labels.loc[eligible], sort=False).agg(["mean", "count"])
        group_ret = group_ret.loc[group_ret["count"].ge(5), "mean"]
        if group_ret.empty:
            out.iloc[i] = score
            continue
        shocked = group_ret.loc[group_ret.abs().rank(pct=True).ge(2.0 / 3.0)]
        if shocked.empty:
            out.iloc[i] = score
            continue

        sector_ret = labels.map(group_ret)
        abnormal = stock_ret - sector_ret
        abnormal_rank = abnormal.groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True) - 0.5
        gm_rank = gm.iloc[i].where(eligible).groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True) - 0.5
        sga_rank = (-sga.iloc[i]).where(eligible).groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True) - 0.5
        liq_rank = liquidity.iloc[i].where(eligible).groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True) - 0.5
        lev_rank = (-leverage.iloc[i]).where(eligible).groupby(labels, sort=False).rank(pct=True) - 0.5
        resilience = (gm_rank + sga_rank + liq_rank + lev_rank) / 4.0

        direction = labels.map(np.sign(shocked))
        active = labels.isin(shocked.index) & eligible & abnormal_rank.notna()
        score.loc[active] = resilience.loc[active] - direction.loc[active] * abnormal_rank.loc[active]
        out.iloc[i] = score

    return out


@register_factor
class SectorResilienceRevisionAbsorptionSeparation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sector_resilience_revision_absorption_separation"
    name = "Sector Resilience Revision Absorption"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks resilience-adjusted relative sector-shock responses only when "
        "late-quarter estimate revisions are supported by absorbed directional flow."
    )
    window_length = 65
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "grossMargin",
        "sgaToRevenue",
        "currentRatio",
        "debtToEquity",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsEstimate",
        "revenueEstimate",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        if close.empty:
            return close.astype(float)

        sector_score = _sector_resilience_response(
            close,
            data["sector"],
            data["grossMargin"],
            data["sgaToRevenue"],
            data["currentRatio"],
            data["debtToEquity"],
        )

        reset = _update_flag(data["epsActual"]) | _update_flag(data["revenueActual"])
        age = _report_age(reset)
        late_clock = age.ge(35.0) & age.le(65.0)
        eps_rev = _revision(data["epsEstimate"], late_clock, 21)
        revenue_rev = _revision(data["revenueEstimate"], late_clock, 21)
        revision = (
            0.60 * (2.0 * eps_rev.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0)
            + 0.40 * (2.0 * revenue_rev.rank(axis=1, pct=True) - 1.0)
        )

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        valid = (
            close.gt(0.0) & prior_close.gt(0.0) & high.gt(0.0) & low.gt(0.0)
            & high.ge(low) & volume.gt(0.0)
        )
        ret = (close / prior_close - 1.0).where(valid)
        bar_range = ((high - low) / prior_close).where(valid)
        rel_volume = volume / volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=12).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        close_location = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / (high - low).replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(valid)
        signed_flow = np.sign(ret) * close_location * rel_volume.clip(lower=0.25, upper=4.0)

        impact = ret.abs() / rel_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        normal_impact = impact.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=12).median()
        absorbed = impact.le(normal_impact) & rel_volume.ge(1.0)
        aligned = revision.mul(signed_flow).gt(0.0)

        range_var = (np.log(high / low).pow(2) / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))).where(valid)
        short_var = range_var.rolling(5, min_periods=5).mean()
        long_var = range_var.rolling(20, min_periods=12).mean()
        calm = short_var.le(1.5 * long_var.replace(0.0, np.nan))

        eligible = late_clock & sector_score.notna() & revision.notna() & absorbed & aligned & calm
        raw = sector_score + 0.50 * revision
        scored = raw.rank(axis=1, pct=True).where(eligible, 0.0)
        return scored.fillna(0.0).astype(float).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

"""A broad industry-consensus revision is treated as a candidate common-information event only when the leave-one-out peer basket has already moved in the same direction. Conditional on that confirmation and the absence of a newly released contradictory firm-specific earnings surprise or own-consensus revision, stocks whose five-day response is weak relative to their historically estimated industry-return sensitivity should subsequently outperform their industry peers. The mechanism is delayed cross-sectional incorporation of a confirmed common shock, rather than an unconditional inference that analyst revision breadth itself is new fundamental information."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_median(
    values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, minimum_peers: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Exact row-wise leave-one-out group medians with a peer-count gate."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    valid_labels = labels.dropna()

    for group in pd.unique(valid_labels):
        columns = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(columns) <= minimum_peers:
            continue

        array = values.loc[:, columns].to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
        valid = np.isfinite(array)
        counts = valid.sum(axis=1)
        group_result = np.full(array.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)

        for column_number in range(array.shape[1]):
            peer_count = counts - valid[:, column_number].astype(int)
            eligible_rows = peer_count >= minimum_peers
            if not eligible_rows.any():
                continue

            peer_values = array[eligible_rows].copy()
            peer_values[:, column_number] = np.nan
            group_result[eligible_rows, column_number] = np.nanmedian(
                peer_values, axis=1
            )

        result.loc[:, columns] = group_result

    return result


def _leave_one_out_mean(
    values: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, minimum_peers: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise leave-one-out equal-weighted group means with a peer-count gate."""
    result = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=values.index, columns=values.columns)
    valid_labels = labels.dropna()

    for group in pd.unique(valid_labels):
        columns = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(columns) <= minimum_peers:
            continue

        array = values.loc[:, columns].to_numpy(dtype=float, copy=False)
        valid = np.isfinite(array)
        clean = np.where(valid, array, 0.0)
        total = clean.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
        counts = valid.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
        peer_counts = counts - valid.astype(int)
        peer_sums = total - clean

        group_result = np.divide(
            peer_sums,
            peer_counts,
            out=np.full(array.shape, np.nan, dtype=float),
            where=peer_counts >= minimum_peers,
        )
        result.loc[:, columns] = group_result

    return result


def _lagged_rolling_beta(
    stock_return: pd.DataFrame,
    peer_return: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
    lag: int,
    minimum_pairs: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal beta over t-window-lag+1 through t-lag using paired observations."""
    y = stock_return.shift(lag)
    x = peer_return.shift(lag)
    paired = y.notna() & x.notna()

    x_clean = x.where(paired, 0.0)
    y_clean = y.where(paired, 0.0)
    count = paired.astype(float).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_x = x_clean.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_y = y_clean.rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_xx = (x_clean * x_clean).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()
    sum_xy = (x_clean * y_clean).rolling(window, min_periods=window).sum()

    covariance_numerator = sum_xy - (sum_x * sum_y) / count
    variance_numerator = sum_xx - (sum_x * sum_x) / count
    beta = covariance_numerator / variance_numerator.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return beta.where((count >= minimum_pairs) & (variance_numerator != 0.0))


def _industry_neutral_equal_gross_weights(
    deficit: pd.DataFrame, eligible: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Demean within-industry percentile ranks and equalize gross exposure by industry."""
    output = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=deficit.index, columns=deficit.columns)
    included_industries = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=deficit.index, columns=["count"])
    normalized_by_group: list[pd.DataFrame] = []

    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        columns = labels.index[labels == group]
        group_deficit = deficit.loc[:, columns].where(eligible.loc[:, columns])
        eligible_count = group_deficit.notna().sum(axis=1)
        group_valid = eligible_count >= 4

        percentile = group_deficit.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        demeaned = percentile.sub(percentile.mean(axis=1), axis=0).where(
            group_valid, 0.0
        )
        gross = demeaned.abs().sum(axis=1)
        normalized = demeaned.div(gross.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0).fillna(0.0)
        normalized_by_group.append(normalized)
        included_industries["count"] += (gross > 0.0).astype(float)

    group_count = included_industries["count"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
    for normalized in normalized_by_group:
        output.loc[:, normalized.columns] = normalized.div(group_count, axis=0).fillna(0.0)

    return output


@register_factor
class IndustryRevisionCovarianceMaskedCatchup(BaseFactor):
    """Industry-neutral catch-up after confirmed common estimate-revision shocks."""

    factor_id = "industry_revision_covariance_masked_catchup"
    name = "Confirmed Revision-Response Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Industry-neutral long-short catch-up signal for stocks whose five-day "
        "return underreacted to a confirmed leave-one-out industry EPS-consensus "
        "revision and peer-basket move, excluding contradictory fresh earnings news."
    )
    window_length = 86
    inputs = ["close", "epsEstimate", "epsSurprise", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        estimate = data["epsEstimate"]
        surprise = data["epsSurprise"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        labels = industry.iloc[0].copy()
        labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), np.nan)

        prior_estimate = estimate.shift(21)
        valid_revision = (
            estimate.notna()
            & prior_estimate.notna()
            & close.notna()
            & (close > 0.0)
        )
        revision = ((estimate - prior_estimate) / close).where(valid_revision)

        breadth = _leave_one_out_median(revision, labels, 10)

        prior_close = close.shift(1)
        daily_return = (close / prior_close - 1.0).where(
            close.notna() & prior_close.notna() & (prior_close > 0.0)
        )
        peer_return = _leave_one_out_mean(daily_return, labels, 10)

        beta = _lagged_rolling_beta(
            daily_return, peer_return, window=60, lag=6, minimum_pairs=40
        )

        stock_response = (close / close.shift(5) - 1.0).where(
            close.notna() & close.shift(5).notna() & (close.shift(5) > 0.0)
        )
        peer_response = (
            (1.0 + peer_return).rolling(5, min_periods=5).apply(np.prod, raw=True)
            - 1.0
        )
        deficit = beta * peer_response - stock_response

        previous_surprise = surprise.shift(1)
        new_surprise = surprise.notna() & (
            previous_surprise.isna() | surprise.ne(previous_surprise)
        )
        positive_event = (new_surprise & (surprise > 0.0)).astype(float)
        negative_event = (new_surprise & (surprise < 0.0)).astype(float)
        recent_positive = positive_event.rolling(21, min_periods=1).max() > 0.0
        recent_negative = negative_event.rolling(21, min_periods=1).max() > 0.0

        contradictory_surprise = ((breadth > 0.0) & recent_negative) | (
            (breadth < 0.0) & recent_positive
        )
        opposite_own_revision = (revision * breadth) < 0.0
        confirmed = (peer_response * breadth) > 0.0

        eligible = (
            revision.notna()
            & breadth.notna()
            & (breadth != 0.0)
            & beta.notna()
            & stock_response.notna()
            & peer_response.notna()
            & confirmed
            & ~opposite_own_revision
            & ~contradictory_surprise
            & deficit.notna()
        )

        return _industry_neutral_equal_gross_weights(deficit, eligible, labels)
programs.name: Confirmed Revision-Response Catch-Up
programs.trading_idea: A broad industry-consensus revision is treated as a candidate common-information event only when the leave-one-out peer basket has already moved in the same direction. Conditional on that confirmation and the absence of a newly released contradictory firm-specific earnings surprise or own-consensus revision, stocks whose five-day response is weak relative to their historically estimated industry-return sensitivity should subsequently outperform their industry peers. The mechanism is delayed cross-sectional incorporation of a confirmed common shock, rather than an unconditional inference that analyst revision breadth itself is new fundamental information.
programs.description: Formation occurs after the close of day t, using only point-in-time fields available at that close; trading starts at the next-bar open, t+1. Define each stock's 21-bar EPS-consensus revision as q_i,t = (epsEstimate_i,t - epsEstimate_i,t-21) / close_i,t, requiring both estimates and close_i,t to be non-null and close_i,t > 0. Industry is the static industry field. For stock i, define its leave-one-out industry revision breadth B_i,t as the cross-sectional median of q_j,t over all j != i in i's industry, requiring at least 10 valid peers; stocks with B_i,t = 0 or missing are ineligible. Define daily close return r_i,s = close_i,s / close_i,s-1 - 1. For every date s, construct the leave-one-out industry return I_i,s as the equal-weighted mean r_j,s of valid peers j != i in the same industry, requiring at least 10 valid peer returns. Estimate beta_i,t as Cov(r_i,s, I_i,s) / Var(I_i,s) over the 60 daily observations s = t-65 through t-6, requiring at least 40 paired valid observations and nonzero benchmark variance. The pre-event stock response is R_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-5 - 1 and the corresponding peer-basket response is J_i,t = product from s=t-4 through t of (1 + I_i,s) minus 1; both end at formation-date close t. Retain an observation only when sign(J_i,t) equals sign(B_i,t), so the peer price basket confirms the revision direction. Define the response-deficit score D_i,t = beta_i,t * J_i,t - R_i,t; a high score means the stock underresponded to its beta-implied peer-basket move. Exclude a stock if its own q_i,t has the opposite sign from B_i,t. Also exclude it if epsSurprise changed from its value on t-1 on any day from t-20 through t, the newly observed epsSurprise is nonzero, and its sign is opposite B_i,t; this identifies a fresh, contradictory firm-specific reported-earnings surprise using its point-in-time availability date. Within each eligible industry having at least four eligible names, percentile-rank D_i,t, subtract that industry's mean percentile rank, and use the demeaned ranks as dollar weights after scaling each industry's long-plus-short gross exposure equally. This produces zero net dollar exposure within every included industry: high-deficit stocks are long and low-deficit stocks are short. Enter at open t+1 and exit at close t+6, so the six-bar holding return begins strictly after all signal inputs. Mechanically, this differs from sector-relative momentum because it requires a leave-one-out EPS-estimate revision event, confirmation that peer returns agree with that revision, a pre-event beta-implied response deficit, and explicit exclusion of opposite-signed fresh firm earnings news; it is not a standalone sector-return or residual-momentum sort.

"""This is a reduced-form common-shock diffusion hypothesis, not a claim that daily OHLCV identifies specific allocator or market-maker behavior. After a broad, statistically unusual sector move, stocks whose intraday price action confirms the sector direction but whose close only partially settles in that direction may retain a short-lived directional residual. To avoid treating a full end-of-day rejection as continuation, the signal uses a bounded settlement deficit: it follows only partial, rather than extreme, directional failure to settle."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sector_leave_one_out(
    returns_df: pd.DataFrame,
    eligible: pd.DataFrame,
    sector: pd.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute causal daily leave-one-out sector returns, peer counts, and breadth."""
    index = returns_df.index
    columns = returns_df.columns
    loo_return = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    peer_count = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    breadth = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)

    if len(index) == 0:
        return loo_return, peer_count, breadth

    # Sector is static by construction. The first row is used only to assign
    # permanent group membership; contemporaneous nonmissing-sector eligibility
    # below still prevents trading before a sector label is available.
    labels = sector.iloc[0]
    for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        members = labels.index[labels.eq(label)]
        if len(members) == 0:
            continue

        group_ret = returns_df.loc[:, members]
        valid = eligible.loc[:, members] & group_ret.notna()
        valid_ret = group_ret.where(valid)
        total_return = valid_ret.sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        total_count = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float)

        group_sign = np.sign(group_ret)
        positive_count = ((group_sign > 0.0) & valid).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        negative_count = ((group_sign < 0.0) & valid).sum(axis=1).astype(float)

        for ticker in members:
            own_valid = valid[ticker]
            own_return = group_ret[ticker].where(own_valid, 0.0)
            count_ex_self = total_count - own_valid.astype(float)
            return_ex_self = total_return - own_return
            loo = return_ex_self / count_ex_self.where(count_ex_self >= 8.0)
            direction = np.sign(loo)

            own_positive = ((group_sign[ticker] > 0.0) & own_valid).astype(float)
            own_negative = ((group_sign[ticker] < 0.0) & own_valid).astype(float)
            matching_peers = pd.Series(
                np.where(
                    direction > 0.0,
                    positive_count - own_positive,
                    np.where(direction < 0.0, negative_count - own_negative, np.nan),
                ),
                index=index,
                dtype=float,
            )

            loo_return[ticker] = loo
            peer_count[ticker] = count_ex_self
            breadth[ticker] = matching_peers / count_ex_self.where(count_ex_self >= 8.0)

    return loo_return, peer_count, breadth


def _fresh_fundamental_event(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Flag new or revised point-in-time earnings and revenue observations."""
    fields = ["epsActual", "revenueActual", "epsSurprise", "revenueSurprise"]
    event = pd.DataFrame(False, index=data[fields[0]].index, columns=data[fields[0]].columns)

    for field in fields:
        values = data[field]
        previous = values.shift(1)
        changed = values.notna() & (previous.isna() | values.ne(previous))
        event = event | changed.fillna(False)

    return event


@register_factor
class SectorAuctionSettlementDeficitCarry(BaseFactor):
    """Sector-shock continuation from bounded directional auction settlement deficits."""

    factor_id = "sector_auction_settlement_deficit_carry"
    name = "Bounded Sector Settlement-Deficit Carry"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "After an unusually broad leave-one-out sector shock, rank within-sector "
        "partial directional closing deficits while excluding extreme rejection, "
        "fresh fundamental events, and unusually high-volume moves."
    )
    window_length = 61
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "marketCap",
        "epsActual",
        "revenueActual",
        "epsSurprise",
        "revenueSurprise",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        high = data["high"]
        low = data["low"]
        volume = data["volume"]
        sector = data["sector"]
        market_cap = data["marketCap"]

        if close.empty:
            return close.astype(float)

        previous_close = close.shift(1)
        returns_df = (close / previous_close - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        eligible = (
            sector.notna()
            & close.gt(0.0)
            & previous_close.gt(0.0)
            & volume.gt(0.0)
            & market_cap.gt(0.0)
        )

        loo_return, _, breadth = _sector_leave_one_out(returns_df, eligible, sector)
        sector_sigma = loo_return.shift(1).rolling(60, min_periods=40).std()
        direction = np.sign(loo_return)
        shock = loo_return.abs().ge(1.50 * sector_sigma)
        broad = breadth.ge(0.65)

        upside_excursion = high / previous_close - 1.0
        downside_excursion = 1.0 - low / previous_close
        excursion = upside_excursion.where(direction > 0.0, downside_excursion)
        confirms_intraday = excursion.ge(0.50 * loo_return.abs())

        trading_range = high - low
        clv = (2.0 * close - high - low) / trading_range.where(trading_range > 0.0)
        clv = clv.where(trading_range > 0.0, 0.0)
        deficit = 1.0 - direction * clv
        bounded_deficit = deficit.ge(0.50) & deficit.le(1.25)

        volume_baseline = volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        relative_volume = volume / volume_baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        quiet_volume = relative_volume.le(0.80)

        dollar_volume = (close * volume).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        dollar_baseline = dollar_volume.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=15).mean()
        dollar_cutoff = dollar_baseline.where(eligible).quantile(0.30, axis=1)
        sufficient_dollar_volume = dollar_baseline.ge(dollar_cutoff, axis=0)

        event = _fresh_fundamental_event(data)
        no_recent_event = event.rolling(6, min_periods=1).max().eq(0.0)

        qualifying = (
            eligible
            & shock.fillna(False)
            & broad.fillna(False)
            & confirms_intraday.fillna(False)
            & bounded_deficit.fillna(False)
            & quiet_volume.fillna(False)
            & sufficient_dollar_volume.fillna(False)
            & no_recent_event.fillna(False)
        )

        score = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        labels = sector.iloc[0]
        for label in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
            members = labels.index[labels.eq(label)]
            if len(members) == 0:
                continue

            group_deficit = deficit.loc[:, members].where(qualifying.loc[:, members])
            group_count = qualifying.loc[:, members].sum(axis=1)
            sector_rank = group_deficit.rank(axis=1, method="average", pct=True)
            group_score = direction.loc[:, members] * (sector_rank - 0.5)
            group_score = group_score.where(group_count.ge(5), 0.0)
            score.loc[:, members] = group_score.fillna(0.0)

        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Bounded Sector Settlement-Deficit Carry
programs.trading_idea: This is a reduced-form common-shock diffusion hypothesis, not a claim that daily OHLCV identifies specific allocator or market-maker behavior. After a broad, statistically unusual sector move, stocks whose intraday price action confirms the sector direction but whose close only partially settles in that direction may retain a short-lived directional residual. To avoid treating a full end-of-day rejection as continuation, the signal uses a bounded settlement deficit: it follows only partial, rather than extreme, directional failure to settle.
programs.description: All signals are formed after close t and are entered no earlier than open t+1; the six-bar return is measured from that executable t+1 open. Define the point-in-time eligible universe U_t as stocks with a nonmissing static sector label, positive close at t and t-1, positive volume at t, and positive point-in-time marketCap at t. For stock i in sector s, define daily return r_i,t = close_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1. Define the leave-one-out equal-weight sector return R_-i,t as the mean of r_j,t over j in U_t with sector_j = s and j != i; require at least 8 such peers. Let sigma_-i,t be the rolling 60-trading-day standard deviation of the historical leave-one-out sector-return series through t-1, requiring at least 40 valid observations. A sector-shock trigger requires |R_-i,t| >= 1.5 * sigma_-i,t, with direction d_i,t = sign(R_-i,t). Breadth B_-i,t is the fraction of the same leave-one-out peers whose return sign equals d_i,t; require B_-i,t >= 0.65. This trigger and breadth use all valid sector peers, not merely candidate stocks, and the leave-one-out construction prevents i from mechanically generating its own sector shock. Define directional intraday excursion E_i,t = high_i,t / close_i,t-1 - 1 when d_i,t = +1, and E_i,t = 1 - low_i,t / close_i,t-1 when d_i,t = -1; require E_i,t >= 0.50 * |R_-i,t|. Define CLV_i,t = (2*close_i,t - high_i,t - low_i,t)/(high_i,t - low_i,t) when high_i,t > low_i,t, and CLV_i,t = 0 when high_i,t = low_i,t. The signed settlement deficit is D_i,t = 1 - d_i,t * CLV_i,t. Retain only partial deficits 0.50 <= D_i,t <= 1.25, explicitly excluding both nearly complete directional settlement and severe close-direction rejection. Relative volume is RV_i,t = volume_i,t / mean(volume_i,t-20 through t-1); require RV_i,t <= 0.80 and at least 15 valid baseline observations. To limit implementation in structurally illiquid names, also require trailing 20-day dollar volume mean(close*volume, t-20 through t-1) to be at or above the cross-sectional 30th percentile within U_t. A point-in-time event flag A_i,k equals one when any of epsActual, revenueActual, epsSurprise, or revenueSurprise is nonmissing at k and is either nonmissing after being missing at k-1 or differs from its value at k-1. Exclude stock i if any A_i,k = 1 for k from t-5 through t, so no fresh earnings or revenue update is used. Among stocks passing every condition, rank D_i,t ascending within sector at t, requiring at least 5 qualifying stocks in that sector, and define the tradable score as S_i,t = d_i,t * (rank_sector(D_i,t) - 0.5). Buy positive scores and short negative scores, with larger absolute scores receiving larger weights. The precommitted robustness grid is sector-shock multipliers {1.25, 1.50, 2.00}, breadth thresholds {0.60, 0.65}, relative-volume caps {0.70, 0.80}, and bounded-deficit intervals {[0.50, 1.25], [0.50, 1.00]}; 1.50, 0.65, 0.80, and [0.50, 1.25] are the primary specification.

programs.code:
"""A large, broad, low-residual-dispersion industry move can temporarily dominate stock-specific price formation even without proving a particular ETF or dealer-flow counterparty. When a stock's completed-day industry-relative move is opposite to its established 21-day industry-relative direction, the move is treated as a conditional relative-price dislocation rather than as a post-event \"release\" signal. The hypothesis is that the prior relative-price direction contains slower-moving idiosyncratic information that reasserts itself over the next six daily bars after contemporaneous common-mode compression."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _industry_common_mode_components(
    returns: pd.DataFrame, industry: pd.DataFrame
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Compute causal daily industry medians, residuals, dispersion, and breadth."""
    index = returns.index
    columns = returns.columns
    median_panel = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    residual_panel = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    dispersion_panel = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)
    breadth_panel = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns, dtype=float)

    if not isinstance(industry, pd.DataFrame) or industry.empty:
        return median_panel, residual_panel, dispersion_panel, breadth_panel

    # Industry is static by contract.  Taking its last supplied observation is
    # robust to sparse synthetic panels while not changing a static classification.
    labels = industry.reindex(index=index, columns=columns).ffill().iloc[-1]
    labels = labels.where(labels.notna() & (labels.astype(str) != ""))

    for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
        group_columns = labels.index[labels == group]
        if len(group_columns) == 0:
            continue

        group_returns = returns.loc[:, group_columns]
        valid = np.isfinite(group_returns)
        count = valid.sum(axis=1)
        group_median = group_returns.where(valid).median(axis=1).where(count >= 10)
        group_residual = group_returns.sub(group_median, axis=0).where(valid)
        group_dispersion = group_residual.std(axis=1, ddof=0).where(count >= 10)

        direction = np.sign(group_median)
        same_sign = group_returns.mul(direction, axis=0).gt(0.0).astype(float)
        group_breadth = same_sign.where(valid).sum(axis=1).div(count).where(count >= 10)

        repeated_median = np.repeat(group_median.to_numpy()[:, None], len(group_columns), axis=1)
        repeated_dispersion = np.repeat(group_dispersion.to_numpy()[:, None], len(group_columns), axis=1)
        repeated_breadth = np.repeat(group_breadth.to_numpy()[:, None], len(group_columns), axis=1)

        median_panel.loc[:, group_columns] = repeated_median
        residual_panel.loc[:, group_columns] = group_residual
        dispersion_panel.loc[:, group_columns] = repeated_dispersion
        breadth_panel.loc[:, group_columns] = repeated_breadth

    return median_panel, residual_panel, dispersion_panel, breadth_panel


@register_factor
class ContemporaneousCommonModeAnchorOpposition(BaseFactor):
    """Industry-compression residual reversal against a prior relative-price anchor."""

    factor_id = "common_mode_compression_anchor_release"
    name = "Contemporaneous Common-Mode Anchor Opposition"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Scores stocks whose 21-day industry-relative anchor is opposed by a "
        "same-day high-breadth, low-residual-dispersion industry shock."
    )
    window_length = 42
    inputs = ["close", "industry"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        industry = data["industry"]

        if not isinstance(close, pd.DataFrame):
            return pd.DataFrame()

        safe_close = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        daily_returns = safe_close.pct_change(fill_method=None)
        daily_returns = daily_returns.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        industry_move, residual, dispersion, breadth = _industry_common_mode_components(
            daily_returns, industry
        )

        # All anchor and baseline quantities explicitly stop at t-1.
        anchor = residual.shift(1).rolling(21, min_periods=21).sum()
        move_baseline = industry_move.abs().shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()
        dispersion_baseline = dispersion.shift(1).rolling(20, min_periods=20).median()

        score = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns, dtype=float)

        if not isinstance(industry, pd.DataFrame) or industry.empty:
            return score

        labels = industry.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).ffill().iloc[-1]
        labels = labels.where(labels.notna() & (labels.astype(str) != ""))

        for group in pd.unique(labels.dropna()):
            group_columns = labels.index[labels == group]
            if len(group_columns) == 0:
                continue

            group_anchor = anchor.loc[:, group_columns]
            anchor_scale = group_anchor.abs().median(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

            group_move = industry_move.loc[:, group_columns[0]]
            group_dispersion = dispersion.loc[:, group_columns[0]]
            group_breadth = breadth.loc[:, group_columns[0]]
            group_move_baseline = move_baseline.loc[:, group_columns[0]]
            group_dispersion_baseline = dispersion_baseline.loc[:, group_columns[0]]

            eligible = (
                group_move_baseline.gt(0.0)
                & group_dispersion_baseline.gt(0.0)
                & group_move.abs().ge(1.5 * group_move_baseline)
                & group_breadth.ge(0.75)
                & group_dispersion.gt(0.0)
                & group_dispersion.le(0.60 * group_dispersion_baseline)
            )

            group_residual = residual.loc[:, group_columns]
            anchor_magnitude = group_anchor.abs().div(anchor_scale, axis=0).clip(upper=3.0)
            residual_magnitude = group_residual.abs().div(group_dispersion, axis=0).clip(upper=3.0)
            raw_score = np.sign(group_anchor) * anchor_magnitude * residual_magnitude

            opposition = group_anchor.mul(group_residual).lt(0.0)
            valid_event = opposition & eligible.to_numpy()[:, None]
            score.loc[:, group_columns] = raw_score.where(valid_event, 0.0)

        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
